rows.raw: " Right. Kiyoko. Of course you wouldn't have forgotten in all this... can she be helped? Grabbing her cane, Komari rises from her seat and beckons you to follow her. The elderly kitsune sets off down the garden path back to the shrine, and speaks as she walks: "This amulet used to be mine; it was the keepsake of my family. Even my name... it means 'little ball' in your tongue, northerner; I suppose my parents thought it funny. A family treasure... I lost it about two hundred and fifty years ago, not long after I arrived in this part of the world on divine orders to aid in this front of the Godswar... "I remember that day, I had been out with the harpies... Sorra's creatures were more civilized back in the day, but they were still insufferable. Me and mine returned to find the den utterly ruined; the wraiths' minions had struck while we were out, and my liege was presumably dead. Try as I might, I couldn't find the amulet of transference any more, one of the keys to our Lord's Dream." A dream...? "You know it better as the Astral Plane. The Living Gods each have dreams, realms formed from... well, I'm not sure myself. But we do know that they are sovereign in that domain; it is where their presence is most real, for lack of a better word to describe it." [flags.ARCHWAY_WAKEUP| You know this to be true — after all, Nareva herself explained it to you, though the explanation was no less cryptic than anything else the serpent goddess said. |Interesting... ] Kiyoko must have escaped into the orb then, and it had lain buried in the debris for centuries until you came along. "With the family heirloom lost, I could not return to the Old Country to face my relatives. As the Lady Otomo's retainer, allowing her to die from my negligence meant I deserved death. The shame was too great... but my Divine Lord had other ideas. It would be a waste, he said, for my talents to be lost in such a manner... I would remain here with those who would stay alongside me, and keep a foothold for his influence in these foreign lands. By all rights I should have paid for my mistake with my life, but my Lord has seen fit to be magnanimous and give me a second chance. Perhaps this exile was the cowardly option, but today, I think I would have preferred death. Turning me into a yasha and forcing me to watch generations of my descendants age, wither and die while I remain unchanging... each time I perform the funerary rites, I desire more and more to simply be one with the land." The two of you have approached the fox shrine at this point, the amulet and its amber orb in Komari's hands. For the first time since you've met her, the Shrine Mother looks a little uncertain. "I will attempt to contact my Lord and ask him for aid. The amulet is a gift from the divine, after all; truth be told, I know little of its actual workings. But he should be able to help." You nod. If it means Kiyoko's freedom... you've done so much already, this is nothing by comparison. Standing in front of the fox statue, Komari clasps her hands about the amulet and its orb and bows her head. You'd expected... well, maybe some chanting, maybe some gesticulating, perhaps some kind of ritual or offerings to be made. Still, you wait by the Shrine Mother's side, trusting that she knows what she's doing — "Hey." The voice that emerges from the fox statue is high, almost nasal, and definitely doesn't sound like anything stereotypically deific. Definitely vulpine, though, no doubt about that — it's almost as if it's just a fox barking and your mind's rearranging the animal noises into actual words, as crazy as that sounds. "My Lord, I —" "Sorry, can't talk now. In an emergency meeting with the others. We've found an invader lurking around, and need to discuss what's to be done. Why don't you catch me later, sweetheart?" The tension in the air dispels with a snap, leaving a rather sheepish Komari standing in the shrine. Slowly, she turns to you and hands back the amulet. "Well, did you hear that?" You did. Perhaps you ought to come back later when her god isn't as occupied? "Deal with Evergreen first — let her have her bag back and the victory that comes with it. I can't speak for my patron deity, but I'll try to get you a proper audience with him when you return; he'll get the orb sorted out. Is this fine?" It will work, you suppose. "Right. I... truth be told, I don't know how to feel about a piece of my past just showing up like that. Not just the amulet, but Kiyoko as well... it'll be nice to actually be able to speak with someone I knew back then. Everyone else, I buried with my own two hands. The price of a long life, as it were." Oh. "There's something else I want you to have as an apology for you going to all this trouble to return someone very important to us." Someone important? Kiyoko? "Just how much of her history do you know?" Not more than you've ever needed to. You trust her, [kiyoko.numKits 1|enough to have given of your bodily life-force — or chi, as she calls it — and she's borne your child[kiyoko.numKits 2|ren]|enough for you to have gone all this way and braved these dangers for her sake]. She's told you something of her past in coming to this part of the world and bits and pieces of her childhood, but nothing that would pin down specifics. Why, is she some kind of celebrity in the country where kitsune come from? Komari thinks a moment, then shakes her head. "Never mind. If the two of you are content together like this, it's for the better. It's not as if it means anything, not this far from the Old Country. Kiyoko was — I mean, is my friend, and after all these years, I can only wish the best for her if she's found happiness. "In any case, please have this." As you watch, Komari reaches into her colorful priestess garb and draws out what looks like a small orange fox tail on a length of red cord. It looks pretty nondescript, but you can feel a faint sense of power radiating from it. "It's unlikely you'll be able to keep the amulet once our friend is freed from her imprisonment. The law demands that if we take something from you, something of equal value must be exchanged... and so here it is." You nod reluctantly, and pocket the little charm. Obtained the Fox-Tail Charm. "That'll be all for now. Allow me to walk you out, so that at least no one will accost you during your egress. Coming this far, even with most out for the festival, must have been harrowing." To be honest, with the way things had been going, you didn't expect it to end this way. Ever since all this business began, the number of shenanigans you've been wrapped up in have mostly resulted in violence and yet more violence... Nevertheless, you eventually return [party.hasCompanions|to [party.compNames] ]and begin the long trek out through the tree, quite literally tailing along behind Komari herself. While you feel several pairs of curious eyes on you through your walk out, none of the kitsune deign to reveal themselves, and you've but walked a surprisingly short distance — and definitely not the way you came in by — before you're at the entrance once more. Komari claps her hands twice, and the door in the wooden wall materializes, parting to reveal the welcome sight of the Frostwood beyond. "And this is where we part ways for now. Just give Evergreen her due, and tell her to keep things between us in the future, instead of hiring idiots to do her dirty work for her, else I might very well think up a particularly nasty prank or two to send her way." With that, the door slams behind you, and melds into the tree once more. Now that was something... [party.comp brint cait etheryn |"I'm just glad we're out of there," Brint muses as you set off into the woods. "Those fox-people are just so small, I was getting tired of having to duck all the time to avoid hitting my head on things." You give Brint a weak grin. He just emerged unscathed from a series of fights for what might very well have been for his life, and his greatest relief is not having to hunch over a little? "You don't understand," Brint replies with a playful snort. "[pc.ra minotaur cowgirl|You have to be born a minotaur to get it, not just look like one. It's about the life you've led.|It's a minotaur thing. You wouldn't understand even if I tried to explain. ]To make things worse, the place was an ever-changing maze. Why do you think the tunnels bored into the Undermountain are so wide?" |"I'm just glad this is all over without us starting a religious war!" Yeah, huh... now that she brought it up, maybe you ought to have had Cait sit out this one. This would be more or less the equivalent to invading a temple of Keros, wouldn't it? Cait's superiors in Jassira really wouldn't be appreciative of her doing such a thing in her priestess garb and all... Cait just gives you a cheery smile. "All's well that ends well, [pc.name]. The healing power of Mallach's love brought people of different faiths and beliefs to a peaceful resolution!" You like her unshakable optimism and enthusiasm, if nothing else. |"There were always stories about this part of the woods, mostly from the few druids of the Old Wyld who remained in touch with the Winter City," Etheryn muses as you depart. "Strange blue flames leading those on patrol astray, laughter in the trees, that sort of thing. Alissa always dismissed such talk as nonsense — for a full-fledged warrioress of the boer'alvar to be taken in by the glamours of fox-eared midgets, even the notion was preposterous. It didn't change the fact that for so many years, there was no end of women willing to volunteer for duty in this neck of the woods." Sounds like her sister really should have been open to more possibilities instead of dismissing them outright. Now that Ryn's seen a lot more of the world outside of the Winter City, you're sure her perspective on things has changed. "One of my tutors mentioned that reality often was allowed to be more bizarre than fiction, because fiction had to be believable while reality did not. I didn't understand it at the time, but I'm beginning to understand what he meant by it." ]"

rows.original: Again, you'll reiterate: you're being entirely straight with her here. Yes, you've been hired by Evergreen, but it's not to finish off her rival or whatever she thinks it is you're here to do — you know better than to involve yourself in the squabbles of woodland witches. You just want to know if the bag she wanted is here, that's all, and no, you didn't know of all this before you came here. No doubt you'll be more careful in accepting work from Evergreen in the future. Still, you can't say that Evergreen was completely in the wrong here — she was paid for what sounded like quite the potent magical treasure with a pile of leaves. No matter how one spins it, that's not an equivalent exchange. "Well, I can't tell you what I don't know, young [pc.mf|man|lady]. Are you really that determined to comb the entirety of my home for her sake?" It's then that Mai stops sniffling long enough to speak up. "Eh, granny..." "What?" "I think I know something of what th' barbarian's speakin' of... ya see, I didn't think much of it at the time, but Miko's ain't been askin' to borrow my piercin' for a little while now, an' —" That's about as far as Mai gets before her sister leaps up and clamps her hands over Mai's lips, the two bowling over backwards onto the grass. Komari rounds on her great-great-granddaughters, waving her walking stick threateningly. "Mikoto, you're not helping your situation right now. Miyuki, speak." "Like I was sayin', granny, I was wonderin' why, since she's usually pesterin' me to no end askin' to let her have a go. Couple days ago, I saw —" "Look, it was jus' a prank, okay? If the stupid witch had wanted a better price for her bag she oughta not make it look like some ratty ol' thing! As it stood, a pile of leaves was just about right an' by the time I found out, it was too late —" Komari's lips set into a thin line, and without hesitation or mercy she raises her cane and gives Miko a good smack on the head with its handle, leaving a nasty bruise in its wake. "In that case, why didn't you say anything after the first of Oxana's mercenaries arrived? You've not just caused me no end of trouble, you've flouted divine law to boot, and — no, I'll deal with you later. Miyuki, get your sister to tell you where she's put the damned thing, and bring it here. "I can't believe I'm actually siding with Oxana on this..." As you watch, Mai drags her sister upright, and together they limp down the garden path, disappearing down the steps. Awkward silence hangs in the air as Komari turns back to you and levels her gaze to meet yours. "Well. This is quite embarrassing. It appears I owe you an apology, northerner. It looks like you'll have your bag back, and I'll even add a token of my own to make up for their mistake." [pc.isDK|She'd better. After all the trouble you've been through, it's a small miracle you aren't wrecking this place any more than you have already|Considering everything you've been through to get here, you don't think that whatever payment Oxana is going to have waiting for you will feel sufficient. Very generous and astute of her]. "If that's the way you see it." Fumbling about in her robes for a bit, Komari draws out a small charm, orange and white; it's clearly made to resemble a fox's tail. "Here. Take it, if it means you'll leave us alone when it comes to your line of work." Obtained the Fox-Tail Charm. Many people bother her kind? "When you're monsters, you're fair game for anyone, and there's not much course to appeal to the so-called civilized peoples." You'd press the point further, but it's then that Miko and Mai reappear on the garden path. Wordlessly, Miko presses a plain brown linen pouch into Komari's hands, then turns and breaks into a run; you've never quite seen someone that curvaceous move quite that quickly. Sniffing, Komari picks up the worn little thing, turning it over in her hands as she draws back the strings. "Stupid girl, that Mikoto. Wonder what's it about this that's got Oxana in a tizzy over losing it... oh." As Komari upends the pouch, all sorts of sex toys flow out of its open mouth — everything from the more common dildoes and onaholes in various shapes and sizes to more esoteric devices, possibly enchanted, that you have no idea how they might be used or whatever for in the first place. For the first time since you've met her, Komari's stern countenance breaks into a little grin, and the Shrine Mother rolls her eyes and shakes her head as she packs the lewd mess back into the little bag. "Oh, Oxana. It's been more than a century, and you never change. Right, [pc.name], I understand perfectly well why Evergreen's so desperate to have this bag of hers back now. If she wants it that badly, she can have it for all I care. I'll just be all the merrier knowing the old bitch needs her toys that badly that she can't go a week without them." "Fine, you've what you came to get. Will you now please just get out of my house and leave me alone? There's been enough trouble for one day, and there's only going to be more when I deal with the stupid girls. Come, I'll even see you out so that no one harasses you during your egress. Is that fine?" Sure. You've no personal beef with these people; now that you've the goods, you might as well get back to Evergreen and deliver on your side of the bargain. "Let me see you out, then." At long last, you begin the long trek out through the tree, quite literally tailing along behind Komari herself. While you feel several pairs of curious eyes on you through your walk out, none of the kitsune deign to reveal themselves, and you've but walked a surprisingly short distance — and definitely not the way you came in by — before you're at the entrance once more. Komari claps her hands twice, and the door in the wooden wall materializes, parting to reveal the welcome sight of the Frostwood beyond. "And this is where we part ways for now. Give Evergreen her due, and tell her to keep things between us in the future instead of hiring idiots to do her dirty work for her, else I might very well consider giving her a taste of her own medicine. Two can play at that game, if she's determined to keep at it. "As for you, if you're going to come around these parts again, don't do it on business. Strictly pleasure, you understand me?" With that, the door slams behind you and melds into the tree once more, leaving you in the forest. Now that was something... [party.comp cait arona berwyn einin |"Well, that could've been worse," Cait says as she dusts herself off and falls in line behind you. "Given how I was here, we could've touched off a holy war." Wait, is she for real? "Naw, just kidding! Or am I?" She really shouldn't joke about things like that. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte|You've read your share of histories in your time, and all-out holy wars never end well. Considering where Cait's from, surely she remembers the disastrous jihad launched by the Jassiran sultan about four hundred and twenty years ago?|You don't know much about these things, never really had the chance to study them in depth, but everything you've heard in your time points to such conflicts never ending well for everyone involved.] "Seriously, though, while I probably wouldn't have caused an all-out holy war, things could've gotten hairy for the Temple if the foxes had decided to make a fuss. Even if I am an apostate, who's to say they'd believe that? I'm just glad things turned out well for everyone involved." You get the feeling Komari and hers might disagree with that. |"I'm just glad to be out of that place," Arona mumbles. "Most boring place I've ever been to, and most unsettling too." Oh? You wouldn't call what you just went through boring; at the very least, didn't she get a good workout with all that fighting? "Those ginger-tailed soul-suckers, they're all so small, their den's practically crushing for a big girl like me. Gotta bend and scrape just to get through the damn doors! They're all smoke and mirrors, and that's a job for Hretha, not a real warrior-babe like me. Save for that one actual warrior they had, none of them were fun to fight, either! Every last one of them would've made good cocksleeves, I didn't get to do that either. Take me out somewhere more interesting in the future, won't you?" You'll give it some deep consideration. |Berwyn's been quiet all this while, holding his hat in his hands as he tails along in line. He doesn't look sad or anything, just... thoughtful. Something the matter? Two coppers for his thoughts? "Oh! It's... nothing. Well, it's something, but it's more my problem than yours." Come now. [pc.isDK|You don't want him being a drag on the party if something's bothering him to the point of keeping him from performing|His problems are your problems, and you've known each other long enough for him to feel comfortable sharing]. Now, what's the matter? "Well, the way that fox just snapped her fingers and dismissed my elemental just like that..." Ah, you see. Having his signature spell negated like that must've left him feeling quite inadequate. "I-it's not like I'm worried or anything. It's just that a lot of my strategies do assume that I can have it by my side, and I've got to rethink things if there are people out there who can just snap their fingers and override my control!" That's a perfectly reasonable thing to do. "You're not teasing me, are you?" You? Of course not. |"Ouch..." Einin says as she turns to look back at the cherry blossom tree. "Considering the number of places I've been thrown out of in my time, that went far better than it could otherwise have. Here's to hoping we're not actually barred from the place." Why, does she want to go back? A nod. "The people we fought in there... I saw a few tricks I'd like to ask about. Not copy wholesale, of course, but there're some things I could learn. Think we'll ever have reason to return?" Not on business, at least. Hopefully for pleasure. Either way, it's best to let things cool down a little before showing your face around these parts again; at the very least, you should settle accounts with Oxana before anything else. ] One way or the other, there's nothing left for you here for the moment. Back to Evergreen's it is then, right?
rows.translation: 你还是要再次强调：你对她来说，完全是坦诚相待的。没错，你确实是被常青女士雇佣来的，但你的目的并不是为了击败她的竞争对手部，或者满足她所认为的你的任何其他目的——你心里很清楚，不应该卷入这些森林女巫之间的争斗之中。 你只是想确认她想要的那个袋子是否在这里，仅此而已。而且，在你来之前，你根本不知道这些事情。毫无疑问，以后在接受常青女士的工作时，你会更加谨慎了。不过，也不能说常青女士在这件事上完全有过错——毕竟，她是用一堆树叶换来了看似价值不菲的魔法宝物，因此她也得到了相应的报酬。 无论从哪个角度来看，这种交换都并不公平。 嗯，那些我也不知道的事情，年轻人，我也无从告诉你。 [pc.mf|男人|女士]你真的那么坚决，要为了她而搜遍我的整个家吗？ 就在这时，舞终于停止了抽泣，终于能够开口说话了。 呃，奶奶…… 什么？ 我想我大概明白那些野蛮人在说什么了……当时我并没有太在意，但米科已经有一段时间没有来借我的穿孔饰品了，而且…… 就在这时，舞的姐姐突然跳起来，用手部捂住了舞的嘴，两人一起摔倒在草地上。小栗则转过身来，挥舞着她的拐杖，威胁地瞪着她的曾孙女们。 美琴，你现在这样的做法并没有帮助到自己。美雪，你说吧。 就像我刚才说的，奶奶，我在想，既然她平时总是缠着我，不停地请求让我让她试试看，那为什么前几天我看到的…… 听着，这只是个恶作剧而已，好吗？如果那个愚蠢的女巫真的想要更高的价钱来买她的包，她应该 不是 把它弄得看起来像什么破旧的东西吧！就它现在的样子，用一堆树叶来装饰简直再合适不过了，可等我发现的时候，已经太晚了—— 小麻的嘴唇紧抿成一条细线，她没有丝毫犹豫或留情，举起手部杖，用它的把手部狠狠地敲在了美子的头上，留下了一个明显的淤青。 那样的话，为什么在奥克萨娜的雇佣兵刚到的时候你什么都没说呢？你不仅给我带来了无尽的麻烦，还违背了神的法律——不，这件事我稍后再处理。美雪，让你妹妹告诉你把那该死的东西放在哪里了，然后把它拿过来。 真不敢相信，在这件事上我竟然站在奥克萨娜这一边…… 你看到，舞将她的妹妹扶了起来，两人一起一瘸一拐地沿着花园的小路走去，最终消失在台阶后面。一阵尴尬的沉默笼罩在空气中，这时科玛丽转过身来，与你的目光相对。 嗯，这确实挺尴尬的。看来我应该向你道歉，北方人。你的包应该可以拿回来了，而且我还会再额外赠送一些东西，来弥补他们的失误。 [pc.isDK|她最好这么做。经历了这么多麻烦之后，你居然还没有把这个地方弄得更糟，已经算是小小的奇迹了。|考虑到你为达到今天这个地步所经历的一切，你肯定认为，无论奥克萨娜准备给你什么报酬，都远远不够。她真是既慷慨又精明啊。]. 如果你是这么看的的话。 小毬在长袍中摸索了一会儿，最终取出一枚橙白相间的小饰品——它显然被设计成狐妖尾巴的形状。 拿着吧。如果你接受这个，就意味着在你们工作方面，你们会不再打扰我们。 获得了狐尾护身符。 为什么会有这么多人去打扰她呢？ 当你成为怪物时，你就成了任何人的攻击目标，而那些所谓的文明民族也根本没有理由去同情你。 你本想进一步追问，就在这时，美子和小舞再次出现在花园的小路上。美子一言不发地将一个普通的棕色亚麻布袋塞到小麻里的手部中，然后转身飞快地跑开了——你从未见过有人能以如此优雅的姿态奔跑。 那个 迅速地。科玛丽闻了闻，捡起了那个破旧的小东西，把它在手部中翻来覆去，同时拉紧了那些绳子。 蠢女孩，那个美琴……真不知道她到底有什么魅力，能让奥克萨娜如此抓狂……哦。 当小樱将那个袋子翻过来时，各种各样的人体玩具从袋口流了出来——有各种形状和大小的普通假阳具和阴具，也有一些更为奇特、可能还被施了魔法的装置，你根本不知道这些东西到底是用来做什么的。自从你认识她以来，小樱严肃的表情第一次露出了丝丝笑意，而那位神殿女祭司则翻了个白眼，摇着头，把这些淫秽的物品重新装回了那个小袋子里。 哦，奥克萨娜。一个多世纪过去了，你依然一点都没变，对吧？ [pc.name]我完全理解为什么常青女士现在如此迫切地想要拿回她的那个包。如果她那么想要，那我完全没意见让她拿去。相反，想到那个老女人如此离不开她的那些“玩具”，以至于一周都离不开它们，我会觉得更加开心。 好吧，你们已经得到了想要的东西。现在请离开我的房子，让我安静一会儿吧。今天已经够麻烦的了，等我去处理那些愚蠢的女孩们，麻烦只会更多。来，我甚至会送你们出去，这样你们离开的时候就不会有人打扰你们了。这样可以吗？ 当然。你与这些人并没有私人恩怨；既然你已经掌握了证据，那么不妨回到常青女士，履行你应尽的责任吧。 那我就送你出去吧。 终于，你开始沿着小路穿过树林，一路上紧跟着小毬的脚步。在行走的过程中，你感觉到有几双好奇的目光在注视着你，但那些狐妖们始终没有现身。出乎意料的是，你走过的距离其实很短——而且肯定不是你进来时走的那条路——很快就又回到了入口处。 小毬拍了两下手部，木墙上的门应声而开，将你引入了那片冰冷的霜林之中。 在这里，我们暂时分道扬镳了。要给常青女士应有的尊重，告诉她以后要把我们之间的事情保密，不要雇些蠢货来替她干这种卑鄙的事；否则，我很可能会让她自己尝到同样的滋味。如果她坚持要这么做的话，我们也可以互相报复的。 至于你，如果以后再来到这些地方，千万不要以公事为由，一定要纯粹是为了休闲娱乐，明白我的意思吗？ 随着门在你身后猛地关上，它再次融入了树木之中，将你留在了森林里。这一下可真是…… [party.comp cait arona berwyn einin |嗯，情况本可能更糟的。 凯特一边拍掉身上的灰尘，一边排在你身后站好了队。 考虑到我当时的处境，我们本可能引发一场圣战。 等等，她是认真的吗？ 哈哈，只是开个玩笑而已！还是说，我真的是认真的？ 她真的不应该拿那样的事情开玩笑。 [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte|你在这段时间里读过很多关于历史的故事，而那些全面爆发的圣战从来都没有好的结局。考虑到凯特的身世，她肯定还记得大约四百二十年前贾西兰苏丹发动的那场灾难性的圣战吧？|你对这些事情了解得并不多，也从未真正有机会深入研究它们，但你所听到的所有信息都表明，这类冲突从来都不会以所有相关方的满意结局收场。] 说真的，虽然我可能不会引发一场全面的大战，但如果那些狐妖决定大吵大闹的话，对神庙来说情况也会变得很棘手部。即便我 是 一个叛教者，谁会相信他们的话呢？我只是很高兴所有相关人员最终都得到了好的结果。 你有种感觉，小牧和她的人可能会不同意这个观点。 |能离开那个地方，我真是太高兴了。 阿罗娜低声嘟囔着。 这是我去过最无聊的地方，同时也是最让人感到不安的地方。 哦？你不会认为自己刚才经历的一切很无聊吧？至少，通过那些打斗，她应该得到了很好的锻炼吧？ 那些红尾巴的吸血鬼，他们全都 小对他们这样的小女孩来说，他们的洞穴简直小得可怜。要想穿过那些该死的门，真的得费九牛二虎之力才行！那些地方全都是障眼法，这种工作应该交给赫蕾莎来干，而不是像我这样的真正的女战士。除了他们那个真正的战士之外，其他人都根本不是什么好对手部——他们一个个都适合被当袖子来用，我根本没机会动手部战斗呢。 那个 要么这样吧。以后带我去一些更有趣的地方吧，好吗？ 你会认真考虑这个问题的。 |整个过程中，贝尔温一直保持着沉默，双手部捧着帽子，默默地跟在队伍后面。他看起来既不悲伤，也没有其他什么情绪，只是……显得若有所思。是不是出了什么问题？他的这些思绪，值两个铜币吗？ 哦！其实……没什么。好吧，其实是有点事，但这个问题更多出在我自己身上，而不是你。 快来吧。 [pc.isDK|你肯定不希望他因为某些事情而影响自己的表现，进而成为派对上的负担吧。|他的问题也是你的问题，而且你们相识已久，他已经足够信任你，愿意与你分享这些困扰。]现在，怎么了？ 哎呀，那只狐妖只是打了个响指，就把我的元素力量给消除了…… 啊，你懂的。他的招牌技能被那样削弱，肯定让他觉得自己很无能。 我并不是说我很担心什么。只是我的很多策略都是建立在假设这个人会一直在我身边的前提之上的，如果真的有人能够随随便便就推翻我的控制，那我就必须重新考虑这些策略了！ 这样做完全合情合理。 你不会是在开玩笑吧？ 你？当然不会。 |哎哟…… 艾宁一边说着，一边转身望向那棵樱花树。 考虑到这些年来我被赶出去过多少次，这次的情况已经好得多了。希望我们真的不会被禁止再进入那个地方。 为什么，她想回去吗？ 点头表示同意。 我们在那里战斗过的那些人……我看到了一些技巧，想请教一下。当然，不是要完全照搬，但有些东西确实值得学习。你觉得我们还有机会再回到那里吗？ 至少不是出于工作原因。希望是出于娱乐目的吧。不管怎样，在再次出现在这个地方之前，最好先让事情平息一下；至少，你应该先和奥克萨娜把账算清楚。 ] 不管怎样，目前你在这里已经无事可做了。那么，是时候回到常青女士之地去了，对吧？
rows.raw: " Again, you'll reiterate: you're being entirely straight with her here. Yes, you've been hired by Evergreen, but it's not to finish off her rival or whatever she thinks it is you're here to do — you know better than to involve yourself in the squabbles of woodland witches. You just want to know if the bag she wanted is here, that's all, and no, you didn't know of all this before you came here. No doubt you'll be more careful in accepting work from Evergreen in the future. Still, you can't say that Evergreen was completely in the wrong here — she was paid for what sounded like quite the potent magical treasure with a pile of leaves. No matter how one spins it, that's not an equivalent exchange. "Well, I can't tell you what I don't know, young [pc.mf|man|lady]. Are you really that determined to comb the entirety of my home for her sake?" It's then that Mai stops sniffling long enough to speak up. "Eh, granny..." "What?" "I think I know something of what th' barbarian's speakin' of... ya see, I didn't think much of it at the time, but Miko's ain't been askin' to borrow my piercin' for a little while now, an' —" That's about as far as Mai gets before her sister leaps up and clamps her hands over Mai's lips, the two bowling over backwards onto the grass. Komari rounds on her great-great-granddaughters, waving her walking stick threateningly. "Mikoto, you're not helping your situation right now. Miyuki, speak." "Like I was sayin', granny, I was wonderin' why, since she's usually pesterin' me to no end askin' to let her have a go. Couple days ago, I saw —" "Look, it was jus' a prank, okay? If the stupid witch had wanted a better price for her bag she oughta not make it look like some ratty ol' thing! As it stood, a pile of leaves was just about right an' by the time I found out, it was too late —" Komari's lips set into a thin line, and without hesitation or mercy she raises her cane and gives Miko a good smack on the head with its handle, leaving a nasty bruise in its wake. "In that case, why didn't you say anything after the first of Oxana's mercenaries arrived? You've not just caused me no end of trouble, you've flouted divine law to boot, and — no, I'll deal with you later. Miyuki, get your sister to tell you where she's put the damned thing, and bring it here. "I can't believe I'm actually siding with Oxana on this..." As you watch, Mai drags her sister upright, and together they limp down the garden path, disappearing down the steps. Awkward silence hangs in the air as Komari turns back to you and levels her gaze to meet yours. "Well. This is quite embarrassing. It appears I owe you an apology, northerner. It looks like you'll have your bag back, and I'll even add a token of my own to make up for their mistake." [pc.isDK|She'd better. After all the trouble you've been through, it's a small miracle you aren't wrecking this place any more than you have already|Considering everything you've been through to get here, you don't think that whatever payment Oxana is going to have waiting for you will feel sufficient. Very generous and astute of her]. "If that's the way you see it." Fumbling about in her robes for a bit, Komari draws out a small charm, orange and white; it's clearly made to resemble a fox's tail. "Here. Take it, if it means you'll leave us alone when it comes to your line of work." Obtained the Fox-Tail Charm. Many people bother her kind? "When you're monsters, you're fair game for anyone, and there's not much course to appeal to the so-called civilized peoples." You'd press the point further, but it's then that Miko and Mai reappear on the garden path. Wordlessly, Miko presses a plain brown linen pouch into Komari's hands, then turns and breaks into a run; you've never quite seen someone that curvaceous move quite that quickly. Sniffing, Komari picks up the worn little thing, turning it over in her hands as she draws back the strings. "Stupid girl, that Mikoto. Wonder what's it about this that's got Oxana in a tizzy over losing it... oh." As Komari upends the pouch, all sorts of sex toys flow out of its open mouth — everything from the more common dildoes and onaholes in various shapes and sizes to more esoteric devices, possibly enchanted, that you have no idea how they might be used or whatever for in the first place. For the first time since you've met her, Komari's stern countenance breaks into a little grin, and the Shrine Mother rolls her eyes and shakes her head as she packs the lewd mess back into the little bag. "Oh, Oxana. It's been more than a century, and you never change. Right, [pc.name], I understand perfectly well why Evergreen's so desperate to have this bag of hers back now. If she wants it that badly, she can have it for all I care. I'll just be all the merrier knowing the old bitch needs her toys that badly that she can't go a week without them." "Fine, you've what you came to get. Will you now please just get out of my house and leave me alone? There's been enough trouble for one day, and there's only going to be more when I deal with the stupid girls. Come, I'll even see you out so that no one harasses you during your egress. Is that fine?" Sure. You've no personal beef with these people; now that you've the goods, you might as well get back to Evergreen and deliver on your side of the bargain. "Let me see you out, then." At long last, you begin the long trek out through the tree, quite literally tailing along behind Komari herself. While you feel several pairs of curious eyes on you through your walk out, none of the kitsune deign to reveal themselves, and you've but walked a surprisingly short distance — and definitely not the way you came in by — before you're at the entrance once more. Komari claps her hands twice, and the door in the wooden wall materializes, parting to reveal the welcome sight of the Frostwood beyond. "And this is where we part ways for now. Give Evergreen her due, and tell her to keep things between us in the future instead of hiring idiots to do her dirty work for her, else I might very well consider giving her a taste of her own medicine. Two can play at that game, if she's determined to keep at it. "As for you, if you're going to come around these parts again, don't do it on business. Strictly pleasure, you understand me?" With that, the door slams behind you and melds into the tree once more, leaving you in the forest. Now that was something... [party.comp cait arona berwyn einin |"Well, that could've been worse," Cait says as she dusts herself off and falls in line behind you. "Given how I was here, we could've touched off a holy war." Wait, is she for real? "Naw, just kidding! Or am I?" She really shouldn't joke about things like that. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte|You've read your share of histories in your time, and all-out holy wars never end well. Considering where Cait's from, surely she remembers the disastrous jihad launched by the Jassiran sultan about four hundred and twenty years ago?|You don't know much about these things, never really had the chance to study them in depth, but everything you've heard in your time points to such conflicts never ending well for everyone involved.] "Seriously, though, while I probably wouldn't have caused an all-out holy war, things could've gotten hairy for the Temple if the foxes had decided to make a fuss. Even if I am an apostate, who's to say they'd believe that? I'm just glad things turned out well for everyone involved." You get the feeling Komari and hers might disagree with that. |"I'm just glad to be out of that place," Arona mumbles. "Most boring place I've ever been to, and most unsettling too." Oh? You wouldn't call what you just went through boring; at the very least, didn't she get a good workout with all that fighting? "Those ginger-tailed soul-suckers, they're all so small, their den's practically crushing for a big girl like me. Gotta bend and scrape just to get through the damn doors! They're all smoke and mirrors, and that's a job for Hretha, not a real warrior-babe like me. Save for that one actual warrior they had, none of them were fun to fight, either! Every last one of them would've made good cocksleeves, I didn't get to do that either. Take me out somewhere more interesting in the future, won't you?" You'll give it some deep consideration. |Berwyn's been quiet all this while, holding his hat in his hands as he tails along in line. He doesn't look sad or anything, just... thoughtful. Something the matter? Two coppers for his thoughts? "Oh! It's... nothing. Well, it's something, but it's more my problem than yours." Come now. [pc.isDK|You don't want him being a drag on the party if something's bothering him to the point of keeping him from performing|His problems are your problems, and you've known each other long enough for him to feel comfortable sharing]. Now, what's the matter? "Well, the way that fox just snapped her fingers and dismissed my elemental just like that..." Ah, you see. Having his signature spell negated like that must've left him feeling quite inadequate. "I-it's not like I'm worried or anything. It's just that a lot of my strategies do assume that I can have it by my side, and I've got to rethink things if there are people out there who can just snap their fingers and override my control!" That's a perfectly reasonable thing to do. "You're not teasing me, are you?" You? Of course not. |"Ouch..." Einin says as she turns to look back at the cherry blossom tree. "Considering the number of places I've been thrown out of in my time, that went far better than it could otherwise have. Here's to hoping we're not actually barred from the place." Why, does she want to go back? A nod. "The people we fought in there... I saw a few tricks I'd like to ask about. Not copy wholesale, of course, but there're some things I could learn. Think we'll ever have reason to return?" Not on business, at least. Hopefully for pleasure. Either way, it's best to let things cool down a little before showing your face around these parts again; at the very least, you should settle accounts with Oxana before anything else. ] One way or the other, there's nothing left for you here for the moment. Back to Evergreen's it is then, right? "

rows.original: There's a moment of silence as Komari lets the tension build in the air, clearly enjoying this far too much than she ought to. You can feel the eyes of every kitsune present on your new, barely clothed body, although the general mood of the crowd is strangely alien to you. These ginger-tailed soul-suckers can be hard to read when they want to be... "Nakano." A giant spike in... it's not quite killing intent, but is related to such, and it's coming from behind you. You remember that name; it was whoever who was holding that blade to your neck. Try as you might to suppress the motion, your traitorous body shivers at the memory of cold steel against soft flesh. "Great-great-grandmother." Komari swishes her nine golden tails idly. "Ah, yes... twenty summers, and still not seeking a consort, let alone betrothed. That is the way things stand, is it not?" By the way she's saying it, the question is clearly rhetorical. "That is... not incorrect. You know where my priorities lie, Great-great-grandmother. Surely I must accumulate more prestige for our house with the homeland before —" Komari waves off his concern — and with a jolt, you realize that you can understand them perfectly, despite them not speaking Belharan — or any of the continent's common trade languages, either. "And by that time, who knows what will have happened to you. Don't think I don't know that you've been putting off the eligible young women I've been throwing your way with your Seven-be-damned monomania, so you know what? I'm going to do something that I think will be highly interesting to watch you handle. "Nakano Kurokawa, you'll take this northerner as your wife-consort. And since you've studied the laws so thoroughly, you know perfectly well that I have the power to do this in my authority as Shrine Mother. Since you've kept putting off making the decision, you've forced your dear old granny's hand in doing just that for you." You hear a sharp, collective intake of breath from the watching kitsune, and while you don't know the details, you're pretty sure that something momentous — no, sacreligious — has happened here. You feel the form behind you take a step back, the emotional emanations abating — or perhaps intensifying. "Great-great-grandmother —" "What's the matter? I made sure to sculpt her into a very fetching form; quite like me when I was younger, really. She'll not lack any pleasures of the flesh, I'm sure. If anything, she'll be a little too eager for your cock." "Great-great-grandmother!" "She'll not stab you while you sleep or poison your food, I made sure of that. Or maybe you're worried that she won't know proper etiquette as befits a woman of her station? Your cousins will be overjoyed to have another warm body to toy with, so you can be assured that she won't shame you. Why, perhaps she'll even enjoy your poetry. What exactly is your problem, Nakano Kurokawa?" "She... she's not even a kitsune! You just transformed a barbarian into something that looks like one of us! And you're going to force me to marry... that? "It's an insult!" Komari just grins devilishly. "Is that disobedience I'm hearing from you? Don't imagine for a moment that you don't deserve it, my dear descendant. All the times you've shamed me with your incessant obsession and turning down girls from perfectly good families... a public rebuke and me exercising my lawful authority to correct the situation is the least of what's in my power to do. If you're that into the ways of our homeland, then you'd better follow them — even when they mean you have to do things you'd rather not. "As for her not being an actual kitsune... oh well. I could ask our Divine Lord and see if he could do something about that, but to be perfectly frank, I don't feel like it just yet. Like I said, it'll be interesting to see how you handle this situation. Maybe you'll actually make something of your life for once instead of wasting it away seeking war-glory in peacetime and writing mountains of bad choka poetry. Do you even realize that your doggerel has been making the rounds in certain circles and bringing shame upon your clan?" You listen to all this, slightly dazed from the entirety of the transformation you've just been put through. The implications of Komari's words is that she didn't just change you physically, but... no, the pressing matter is that you're being forcibly married off to one of her descendants — and not as any sort of gift, but as a punishment. Sure, it might be a better fate than having one's mind wiped and used as a shell of a body for a forest witch, but it's not very much so. Y-you should be indignant at this. No, furious. Perhaps show a little more concern at the prospect of being forced to stay here forever, considering what Kasyrra has promised to do to the entire world. [party.som||[party.compNames]... did [companion1.himHer] meet a similar fate to yours?|[party.compNames]... did they meet a fate like yours?] It's all so overwhelming. The tree, the masses of fluffy foxen, all the strange sights and sounds, this entire situation... everything comes together, crashing down and crushing you completely. There is no way you can escape from this, no way that you can avoid your fate. All you can do is latch on to the calm eye at the center of the storm, this presence behind you... some fading part of your mind screams that this is horribly wrong, that your mind's twisted out of existence by a cruel kitsune trick, but that's eventually drowned out by the constant baseline of low-key lust in the back of your head. It's just so much easier to go along with what Komari says... besides, it's your fault for invading her home on nothing more than the say-so of a forest witch. You deserve this, really. "Fine. I will accept my reprimand with dignity." "Excellent." Komari's expression is more smug than you'd think possible for one person. "Perhaps being responsible for someone else will actually teach you something for once, instead of frittering away your youth tilting at windmills. I'll get Mikoto and Miyuki to come up and help with the arrangements." Hard and cold gauntleted fingers take hold of yours from behind, and for the first time you turn to see your consort-to-be. Clad from head to toe in red lamellar armor with his helmet tucked under an arm, the young kitsune man that meets your eyes is shockingly handsome even by their standards. By Marches standards, he's perhaps a little shorter than average, which would put him at slightly taller than average for a kitsune; his hair and fur are in varying shades of black save for the very tips of his five tails, all immaculately groomed save for the slightly unkempt appearance of his hair. Most kitsune you've seen look as if they've trouble putting on mass, and he's no exception; he's a bit lanky, or if one were to be generous, wiry. But there's something about this man... a presence of sorts. It's not merely his appearance of the way he's dressed, though he's something of a prettyboy. There's something in the way he holds himself... something that is desperate for respect and acknowledgement. He radiates something; you feel a deep sense of... it's confusing. A mixture of love, fear and adoration, all bunched up in a confused ball. From the moment you lay eyes on him, you can see nothing else... and you feel small and humble. You ought to be aware of kitsune glamours, but this if anything is the exact opposite of a playful aura, a sensation which sucks out all the fun of everything, leaving a blank void to be filled. Besides, with how he's fuming coldly at the moment, you doubt he has the presence of mind to keep up any kind of glamour. "Yes, great-great-grandmother." "For once, you're actually taking the advice of your forebears, just not the bits you like and ignoring the rest — like filial piety. See? This was the right decision. You're learning something, after all."
rows.translation: 一阵沉默降临，小麻里故意让紧张的气氛在空气中逐渐累积，显然，她从中获得的乐趣远超她应该感受到的程度。你能感觉到在场的每一只狐妖都在注视着你那几乎一丝不挂的身体，然而人群的整体氛围却让你感到十分陌生。这些红尾巴的家伙，当他们想要隐藏自己的真实意图时，确实很难被看穿…… 中野。 某种巨大的能量冲击……虽然算不上真正的杀意，但与之密切相关，而且这种能量是从你背后袭来的。你应该还记得那个名字吧——就是那个曾经将刀刃抵在你脖子上的人。无论你如何努力抑制自己的反应，当你回想起冰冷钢铁触碰柔软肌肤的那一刻，你的身体还是会不由自主地颤抖起来。 高祖母。 小蚊子闲散地摆动着她那九条金色的尾巴。 啊，没错……二十个夏天过去了，却依然没有寻找伴侣，更别说订婚了。事情就是这样的，不是吗？ 从她说话的方式来看，这个问题显然只是出于习惯或形式而已，并非真正想要得到答案。 那个……也并非不对。您知道我的优先事项是什么的，曾曾祖母。在我为我们的家族和祖国赢得更多声望之前，这样做当然是必要的…… 科马里对他的担忧摆了摆手——就在这时，你突然意识到，尽管他们并没有使用贝尔哈兰语，也没有使用这片大陆上任何常见的贸易语言，你却能够完全理解他们的话。 到那时候，谁知道你会变成什么样子呢。别以为我不知道，你一直因为那该死的偏执症而拒绝我给你介绍的那些合适的女孩。所以，你知道吗？我打算做一件我觉得会很有意思的事情——就看你如何应对了。 中野黑川，你必须将这个北方人收为你的妻子。既然你如此精通各种法规，你肯定也清楚，作为神社的女祭司，我拥有这样的权力。因为你一直迟迟不肯做出决定，所以最终还是让你亲爱的奶奶出面替你做了这个决定。 你听到周围那些正在注视着的狐妖们同时发出了剧烈的吸气声。虽然你并不了解具体的情况，但你可以肯定，这里刚刚发生了一些极其重要——甚至可以说是神圣不可侵犯的事情。 你感觉到身后的那个身影向后退了一步，那些情绪波动似乎减弱了……又或许，反而变得更加强烈了。 高祖母—— 怎么了？我可是精心地将她塑造成了一个非常诱人的形象，真的和年轻时的我非常相像。她肯定不会缺少任何肉体上的享受……如果说有什么不同的话，那就是她可能会对你产生过分的渴望吧。 高祖母！ 她不会在你睡觉时刺伤你，也不会在你的食物里下毒，这一点我已经确保了。或者，你是在担心她不懂符合她身份的女子应该具备的礼仪吗？你的表亲们一定会很高兴有另一个可以戏弄的对象，所以你可以放心，她不会让你难堪的。说不定，她甚至会喜欢你的诗呢。 中野 Kurokawa，你到底在担心什么？ 她……她甚至都不是一只狐妖！你只不过是把一个野蛮人变成了别的什么东西罢了 看起来 简直就像我们中的一员！而你现在却要强迫我嫁给……那个东西？ 这是一种侮辱！ 小麻里只是露出一个邪恶的笑容。 我听到的这就是你的不服从吗？亲爱的后裔，千万不要以为你不应受到这样的惩罚。你那些无休止的固执行为，以及拒绝那些家世优良的女孩……这些行为已经让我蒙羞，而我公开斥责你、行使我的法定权力来纠正这种状况，其实只是我所能做的最轻的措施而已。如果你如此重视我们故乡的传统，那么你就应该遵守它们——即使这些传统意味着你必须去做那些你并不愿意做的事情。 至于她并不是真正的狐妖……唉，算了。我可以去问问我们的神君，看看他能否对此采取什么措施，但说实话，我现在还不想这么做。就像我之前说的，看看你将如何处理这个局面，会是一件很有趣的事情。 也许这次你终于能够真正利用好自己的生命，而不是在和平时期浪费时间去追求所谓的战争荣耀，还写出一大堆糟糕的诗歌。你难道没有意识到，你的那些拙劣诗作已经在某些圈子里流传，让你的家族蒙羞吗？" 你听着这一切，刚刚经历的种种变化让你有些恍惚。小毬的话意味着，她不仅仅在你的外貌上做出了改变，而且……不，更重要的是，你即将被强行嫁给她的一个后代——而且这并非什么礼物，而是一种 惩罚当然，比起被彻底抹去记忆、沦为某个森林女巫的躯壳，这样的结局或许还算不错吧……但也不算好到哪里去。 你……你应该为此感到愤怒才对。不，应该是暴怒才对！考虑到卡希拉威胁要对整个世界做出什么，被强迫永远留在这里，你至少应该表现出更多的担忧才对啊。 [party.som||[party.compNames]…做了 [companion1.himHer] 遭遇与你相同的命运吗？|[party.compNames]…他们的命运也和你一样吗？] 这一切都让人感到难以承受。那棵树、那些成群的毛茸茸的狐妖、所有那些奇怪的景象和声音，整个这种环境……所有这些因素加在一起，仿佛一起压了下来，彻底将你压垮。你根本无法逃离这一切，也无法逃避自己的命运。 你所能做的，就是紧紧抓住暴风雨中心那股平静的力量，紧紧依靠你身后这个存在……你脑海中某个逐渐模糊的部分不断呐喊着：这一切都大错特错，你的思维被某个残忍的狐妖玩弄得面目全非……但最终，这些呐喊都被你脑海深处那股持续不断的欲望所淹没。 跟着小丸子的安排走其实要容易得多……而且，仅仅因为一个森林女巫的说法就闯进她的家，这确实是你的错。你确实活该这样。 好吧。我会以尊严的态度接受这个惩戒。 太棒了。 小麻里的表情之得意，简直超出了你的想象。 或许，承担起对别人的责任，真的会让你学到些什么，而不是把青春浪费在徒劳无功的事情上。我会让美琴和美雪过来帮忙安排这些事情。 冰冷而坚硬的护手从背后握住了你的手，这时你才第一次转过头，看到了你未来的伴侣。这个年轻的狐人男子从头到脚都穿着红色的层状铠甲，头盔则夹在手臂下。当他与你的目光相遇时，你会发现他竟然美得令人震惊——即使以他们的标准来看也是如此。而以马奇们的标准来看，他的身高或许略低于平均水平 更高 对于一只狐妖来说，他的体形算是偏瘦的；他的毛发呈现出深浅不一的黑色，只有五条尾巴的尖端是例外——那些尾巴都修剪得非常整齐，只是他的头发看起来有点凌乱。你见过的大多数狐妖都显得有些瘦弱，他也不例外；他的身材有点瘦高，或者说得委婉些，就是骨架比较明显。 但是这个男人身上有一种特别的气质……一种难以言喻的存在感。这不仅仅体现在他的外貌或穿着上，虽然他确实算是个英俊的男子。更重要的是他举止言谈的方式……那种迫切渴望得到尊重与认可的态度。 他身上散发着某种特殊的气质，让你感受到一种难以名状的情绪……这种感觉实在令人困惑。那是爱、恐惧与崇拜的混合体，全都凝聚成了一个复杂的情绪团。从你第一眼看到他的那一刻起，你就再也无法关注其他任何事物了……你会觉得自己如此渺小、如此卑微。 你应该了解狐妖的魅惑技巧，但这一次，他的行为完全违背了那种轻松愉悦的氛围——这种感觉会剥夺一切乐趣，只留下一个需要被填补的空虚。更何况，看他现在那副怒不可遏的样子，你根本怀疑他是否有心思去施展任何魅惑手段。 是的，曾曾祖母。 这一次，你终于听从了祖先们的建议，只不过你只选择了自己感兴趣的部分，而忽略了其他内容——比如孝道。看到了吗？这才是正确的决定。毕竟，你正在从中学习到一些东西。

All you can do is latch on to the calm eye at the center of the storm, this presence behind you... some fading part of your mind screams that this is horribly wrong, that your mind's twisted out of existence by a cruel kitsune trick, but that's eventually drowned out by the constant baseline of low-key lust in the back of your head. It's just so much easier to go along with what Komari says... besides, it's your fault for invading her home on nothing more than the say-so of a forest witch. You deserve this, really. "Fine. I will accept my reprimand with dignity." "Excellent." Komari's expression is more smug than you'd think possible for one person. "Perhaps being responsible for someone else will actually teach you something for once, instead of frittering away your youth tilting at windmills. I'll get Mikoto and Miyuki to come up and help with the arrangements." Hard and cold gauntleted fingers take hold of yours from behind, and for the first time you turn to see your consort-to-be. Clad from head to toe in red lamellar armor with his helmet tucked under an arm, the young kitsune man that meets your eyes is shockingly handsome even by their standards. By Marches standards, he's perhaps a little shorter than average, which would put him at slightly taller than average for a kitsune; his hair and fur are in varying shades of black save for the very tips of his five tails, all immaculately groomed save for the slightly unkempt appearance of his hair. Most kitsune you've seen look as if they've trouble putting on mass, and he's no exception; he's a bit lanky, or if one were to be generous, wiry. But there's something about this man... a presence of sorts. It's not merely his appearance of the way he's dressed, though he's something of a prettyboy. There's something in the way he holds himself... something that is desperate for respect and acknowledgement. He radiates something; you feel a deep sense of... it's confusing. A mixture of love, fear and adoration, all bunched up in a confused ball. From the moment you lay eyes on him, you can see nothing else... and you feel small and humble. You ought to be aware of kitsune glamours, but this if anything is the exact opposite of a playful aura, a sensation which sucks out all the fun of everything, leaving a blank void to be filled. Besides, with how he's fuming coldly at the moment, you doubt he has the presence of mind to keep up any kind of glamour. "Yes, great-great-grandmother." "For once, you're actually taking the advice of your forebears, just not the bits you like and ignoring the rest — like filial piety. See? This was the right decision. You're learning something, after all.""

rows.original: Nakano is quiet as he leads you to your new home, though the blankness of his emotional slate weighs on your mind; he isn't bothered by your nakedness in the slightest, or at least gives no sign of such. As you leave the sacred gardens and Komari's presence you gradually regain some of your senses; the fluff in your mind replaced with a nagging feeling of doubt. Did you do the right thing? What exactly have you gotten yourself into? Why can't you get angry about any of this? It's not as if you had any choice in the matter, anyway... The amber light of the cherry blossom tree's heart slowly fades, and the hallways are lit by lanterns once more. You get the impression that you've been heading up, yet you've climbed no stairs; your suspicions are confirmed when you emerge out into open air and the tree's massive branches, even more imposing than when you viewed them from the ground. "We're here." He speaks in the kitsunes' mother tongue, yet you understand him perfectly. Nakano's living arrangements are surprisingly unassuming for someone of his stature; a warrior of some renown like he is would be better lavished upon, for lack of a better way to put it. His chambers are sparsely decorated, the most lavish things around being his weaponry and armor, up on racks on the walls. There's a low table and cushions for meetings, a small study crammed with books and scrolls of all kinds, and a small open garden-cum-courtyard connecting the other rooms where you can look at the evening sky. Exploring further, you find his personal quarters, which are even more bare than the rest of his home — save for the scrollwork that hangs on the walls. There must be more than a dozen of them, poetry composed in careful calligraphy against a backdrop of a painting; all of them are by the same artist. "Did you compose all of these?" You realize these are the first words you've said to him. "...Great-great-grandmother says that my poetry has been incorrigibly bad for the last five years, and that I should try something that I actually have a talent for. At least my art isn't a complete failure." Before you can reply, though, the door bursts open and two kitsune burst in — the ones you saw at Komari's side in the garden. One orange, one gray, they draw close and start circling Nakano in a swish of fluffy fur. "Mikoto. Miyuki." "Eeeeeeh, congrats on yer betrothal, cus!" Nakano scowls. "You know full well great-great-grandmother meant to punish me with this forced marriage, Miyuki." A pout. "Really, cus, what happened to ya these last five years? I preferred it when you jus' called me Mai..." "To do so would be to not accord you the respect owed your station as great-great-grandmother's successors." The orange-furred kitsune cuts in. "Ya really think so, cus? Which is less respectful of us, callin' us by our beloved pet names or ignorin' our perfectly respectable requests?" "Just... just do the job you were sent here to do." An edge of exasperation in his voice. "Take her away and leave me alone for a moment. I need to review the situation and consider my options." "Yer jus' looking so glum all th' time. Ya gotta see the good in yer situation, 'else yer gonna be miserable th' rest of yer life. Fine, be stuck-up. We'll take yer bride-to-be an' make sure she ain't gonna embarrass ya." As the two lead you away, you realize that Nakano never asked for your name.
rows.translation: 中野沉默地带你前往新家，但他那毫无情绪波动的表情让你感到不安；他似乎完全不在意你的裸露，至少没有表现出任何在意的意思。当你离开那些神圣的花园，离开小麻莉的影响后，你的感官逐渐恢复了正常，但心中却开始涌现出一种挥之不去的疑虑。 你做得对吗？你究竟把自己卷入了什么麻烦之中？为什么对这些事情你却一点愤怒都没有？ 反正，在这件事上你本来也没有什么选择权…… 樱花树核心处的琥珀色轻型芒渐渐黯淡，走廊里再次被灯笼照亮。 你会有一种自己一直在向上攀登的错觉，但实际上你并没有爬上任何楼梯；当你走到户外，看到那棵树的巨大树枝时，你的怀疑得到了证实——那些树枝看起来比你从地面上看时还要雄伟壮观。 我们到了。 他用狐族的母语说话，但你却能完全理解他的意思。 对于像中野这样地位显赫的人来说，他的居住条件出奇地简朴；用另一种方式来说，像他这样颇有名望的战士，本应该享受更好的生活条件才对。 他的房间装饰极为简朴，墙上架子上摆放的最为奢华的物品，莫过于他的武器和盔甲。房间里有一张矮桌和几个靠垫，可供会面使用；还有一个堆满各类书籍和卷轴的小书房；此外，还有一个连接其他房间的小花园式庭院，在那里可以欣赏到晚间的天空。 进一步探索后，你发现了他的私人居所，那里比他家的其他地方更加简陋——唯有挂在墙上的那些卷轴例外。那些卷轴应该有十几幅，都是用精美的书法写成的诗篇，背景则是绘画作品；而这些作品全都出自同一位艺术家之手。 这些都是你自己创作的吗？ 你意识到，这些其实是你第一次对他说这些话。 ……我的高祖母说，过去五年里我的诗歌创作一直糟糕透顶，我应该尝试做一些自己真正有天赋的事情。至少我的绘画艺术还没有彻底失败。 然而，你还没来得及回答，门突然被撞开了，两只狐妖冲了进来——就是你在花园里看到跟小鞠在一起的那两只。一只橙色的，一只灰色的，它们凑近过来，蓬松的毛茸茸的尾巴在空中甩来甩去，开始绕着中野转圈。 美琴。美雪。 哎呀，恭喜你订婚啦，真的！ 中野皱起了眉头。 你心里很清楚，我的高祖母之所以安排这场强迫婚姻，就是为了惩罚我，美雪。 撅起嘴来。 说真的，你过去这五年到底发生了什么？我更喜欢你直接叫我‘舞’…… 这样做就等于没有给予你作为曾曾祖母后代应有的尊重。 那只毛色呈橙色的狐妖插话道。 你真这么认为吗？为什么？叫我们那些亲昵的昵称，和忽略我们那些完全合理的请求，哪一种才更不尊重我们呢？ 就…就去做你被派到这里来要做的事情吧。 他的声音里带着一丝恼怒。 把她带走，让我单独待一会儿。我需要仔细考虑当前的情况，思考一下该怎么做。 你整天都这么闷闷不乐的，得学会看到自己处境中的积极面，否则你这辈子都会过得很痛苦的。好吧，就算你高傲吧，但我们一定会照顾好你的未婚妻，确保她不会让你难堪。 当那两个人带你离开时，你突然意识到，中野从来都没有问过你的名字。

rows.original: The days meld into each other, a strange acceptance falling over you in your new role, far more coercive than the cruelest of slave collars in its own right. Maybe it's part of the transformation you were put through, or — perhaps more disquietingly — you're actually growing to like this situation. For all their playfulness and relaxed demeanour, Miko and Mai are well-schooled in etiquette and decorum; the more you learn about the kitsune, the more it makes sense why their society is intensely stringent on such things. When one crams enough hungry vampires together to form a civilization, conduct and following the pecking order is imperative. The only thing you've kept — or been allowed to keep — from your old life is your name, perhaps a reminder that you're not truly one of the denizens in this den of foxes, no matter how much you might look like them. When the day is done, you always return to Nakano's accommodations for dinner and bed; he is always unfailingly polite but distant, keeping you at arm's length in all your interactions. You don't even sleep in the same room, let alone the same futon; he always retires far later than you do, working on his poetry and scroll painting late into the night. You've spied on him once or twice, sitting at the floor desk while he works, completely motionless save for his brush and the twitching of his ears. He's always awake by the time you rouse yourself in the mornings, his polite, stony expression going against everything a kitsune stereotypically ought to be. Miko and Mai are experts in what the kitsune consider the feminine arts — which, although there is some overlap, are considerably different from what many Marches cultures would consider such. No matter which of the duo's little suggestions you do to try and get some kind of positive reaction out of Nakano, the man is stoic and serene as ever. "It's th' Zen thing, I'm tellin' ya," Miko complains to you when you bring up the matter of her cousin to her. "He goes with granny to th' Old Country for a small trip when he comes of age an' returns home five years later with a head full of ideas. Big an' grandiose ones. Our smilin' cus done turned into a samurai without a war to fight, an' it's eatin' him up inside." A handful of months tick by in this fashion, the appointed date of your forced marriage to Nakano as his wife-consort drawing closer. He's asked your name, but other than that not made any further advances; maybe he thinks that by ignoring the problem, it'll go away on its own. Fat chance of that. Guess you'll have to take matters into your own hands. While the idea of an arranged marriage isn't as offensive as it once might have been to you, as strange as that sounds, spending the rest of your life stuck in a loveless one is another thing. Miko and Mai are full of mischievous ideas as to how to rectify the situation, but it's easy to pitch ideas when one doesn't have to bear the brunt of carrying them out. It's a cool night when you decide to put your plan into action. You're supposed to have retired to bed some time ago, while Nakano's just starting to work on his artistic pursuits. Not that this situation is going to last, if you have any say in the matter. Resolutely, you let your kimono fall to the floor and step through the garden and into the study, naked as the day you were — well, sculpted. Your [pc.hasTails|tails stream|tail streams] out behind you in the evening breeze; time to see how long this stoic warrior will favor his art and poetry over his future bride. His muscles tense as you trail a soothing hand over his shoulder, coiled to spring, but they gradually relax when you press your bare bosom against his back, taking care not to step on his many tails. You discover something quite startling: Nakano's skin is hot to the touch, even through the fabric of his kimono — not scalding, but nevertheless much warmer than you'd expect from something so human-like, as if there's a fire burning within his body. Then again, what did you expect? You've never quite touched a kitsune like this before, especially not one so... tempered. "For all that the twins tell me you're adapting swimmingly, I see you're still more forward than most," Nakano murmurs, not looking up from his brush and ink. "Is all seduction in these lands so brazen?" Now then. You may not have the ability to feed as kitsune do, but you've seen them do it often enough to know that they can be quite exuberant in doing so. Come to think of it, you've never actually seen Nakano feed... would you be delicious to him? Peeking over his shoulder, you see what Nakano is working on: a stylised scenery of a mountain lake, trees and a grazing deer in the foreground. "Perhaps, it would certainly save me the trouble of having to join that rabble when they go seek benefactors in the forest. I merely have a few matters to attend to before I can join you, matters of artistic endeavor. Retire to bed and I'll come for you when I am done." Nice try. You kneel down and envelop him in an embrace, hands sensually trailing down his body. You tell him to not mind you, you'll just entertain yourself while your husband-to-be is busy with more important matters. Nakano has excellent control over his body, but his heartbeat nevertheless quickens — not readily apparent, but barely possible for you to detect in your intimate embrace. For all that he can empty his mind, his body is traitorous. "As you wish," he replies flatly, his brush putting the last of the details on the foreground. Other kitsune speak as a playful lilt or a soaring song; Nakano's words are iron poetry. "Humor yourself, if you think it'll get a rise out of me. It's good training at ignoring distractions, if nothing else." That's as much of an invitation as you'll ever get out of him. Your hands are everywhere, caressing his chest, his arms, his legs; your fingers find his ears amidst his pretty shock of hair, perky and triangular, and toy with them as they twitch and wiggle of their own accord. His tails are sleek and difficult to get a solid grasp on, the dark fur and white tips finely groomed as any other. You spend a good long while just running your fingers through the fine fluff, savouring the warmth that comes with it. Nakano has finished his painting now, the mountain lake and vista in all of its fine glory; he's left a space blank on the paper for him to attend to the poetry. While Komari's transformation did away with the spoken word, actually learning to be literate in the kitsunes' mother tongue has been a trying experience. This goes doubly so when the characters are so stylised; nevertheless, Nakano moves his brush with perfect grace and exaction. You're not giving up here. One more spot remains for you to explore; that secret place down between his legs. Kneeling on the flooring and reaching around your husband-to-be's waist, your hands dive beneath fabric and undergarments to seek his cock. Finding it isn't hard, an amply-sized rod of masculine flesh with a bulbous knot near the base. Already half-hard from your earlier ministrations, it throbs and pulses faintly against your fingers, and it's not too difficult to wrap your hand about it. Good contact is vital, after all. "A moment." Nakano shifts in his seat, his tails tickling your thighs as he leans his back into your hefty boobs. The warmth of his body heats your chest, making it feel all tingly inside, a roiling of liquid warmth. "I suppose I can give you a handicap to begin with." The arrogance of the man. As Nakano returns to his poetry, brush moving in smooth, delicate strokes, you start to stroke him off in earnest. The stoic warrior's facade is unflinching even as his canine cock bulges in his undergarments; what goes on down below stays there, apparently. You're not about to be discouraged so easily — if Nakano's skin is warm, his manhood is a veritable furnace, almost uncomfortably so, the key word here being almost. You employ every trick you know in stoking him off, palm and fingers moving furiously along the length of his engorged red rocket, but he calmly finishes yet another stanza in impeccable calligraphy. You even resort to toying with the bases of his tails with your other hand while you work his cock, but he just idly bats at your wrist with his tail-tips while you do so, acknowledging your efforts but not succumbing to them. Nakano's mind might be an impenetrable bulwark, but his flesh is as susceptible as anyone else's. His cock twitches in your hand, knot pressing against your palm as it inflates, and then you feel steaming hot semen explode outwards from the tapered tip, joining what pre you've already coaxed out of him in staining his garments. His ears fold flat against his hair, but he's otherwise poised as he finishes the last stanza and starts putting away ink, paints and brushes, leaving the unfurled scroll on the table to dry. Thick, heated kitsune semen coats your hand as you withdraw it from within his clothes, a foxy, musky smell filling the air as it oozes and rolls. At last, Nakano turns to you. "I'm sorry for your failure, yet the odds you were up against were nigh-impossible. Mikoto and Miyuki have been teasing me since the day I reached my majority and underwent the genpuku; I can see they've tried to teach you something of what they know, yet it's still insufficient." Nigh-impossible odds haven't deterred him any. At last, the faintest glimmer of a smile. "There is a lesson to be learned from a downpour of rain. If you get caught in a sudden cloudburst, you will still get a drenching even though you try to keep dry by hurrying along and taking cover under overhangs of roofs. If you are prepared to get wet from the start, the result is the same but there is no hardship. This attitude can be extended to all things." Silence. "I suppose you did help, though. The verses came to me far easier than they usually do, and I appear to be done well ahead of time. It would be remiss for me to not repay you with something of equivalent value as divine law commands... understand that this is merely fulfilment of an obligation, and is no sign of affection on my part." rows.translation: 日子一天天过去，渐渐融入彼此之中。在这种新的角色中，你会产生一种奇怪的接受感，这种感觉比最残酷的奴隶枷锁还要具有强制性。也许，这是你所经历的转变的一部分；又或者——更令人不安的是——你其实正在逐渐接受这种状态。 喜欢 在这种情况下。尽管米科和舞表现得十分活泼开朗、举止轻松随意，但她们其实非常懂得礼仪与规矩；当你越深入地了解这些狐族的相关知识，就越能理解为什么他们的社会会对这些方面要求如此严格。 当把足够多的饥饿吸血鬼聚集在一起形成一个文明时，遵守并维护等级制度就变得至关重要。在旧生活中，你唯一能够保留下来的——或者被允许保留下来的——就是你的名字。这个名字或许在提醒你：无论你看起来多么像他们，你其实并不属于这个群体。 一天结束之后，你总是会回到中野的住处吃晚餐并休息；他始终保持着礼貌，但却保持着一定的距离，在与你的所有互动中都保持着疏离的态度。你们甚至不会睡在同一个房间里，更不用说共用同一张榻榻米了；他总是比你晚很多才上床睡觉，会一直忙到深夜才去创作诗歌或绘制画卷。 你曾一两次观察到他：当他工作时，他会坐在地板上的书桌前，一动不动，只有画笔在手部中移动，耳朵偶尔会微微抽动。而每当你早上醒来时，他早已醒着了，他那礼貌而冷漠的表情，完全违背了人们对狐妖的一贯印象。 美子与真依是那些被狐族视为“女性艺术”领域的专家——尽管这些艺术形式之间存在某些重叠之处，但它们与许多人类文化所理解的“女性艺术”还是有着相当大的差异。无论你尝试采用这对姐妹提出的哪一种建议来试图引起中野的某种积极反应，这个男人始终都保持着冷静与沉着。 这就是所谓的‘禅意’，我跟你说的。 当你向米科提起她表妹的事情时，她会向你抱怨。 他成年后和奶奶一起去了乡下小住了一段时间，五年后回到家中时，脑子里充满了各种宏伟的计划。我们那个曾经总是面带微笑的孩子，如今已经变成了一名没有战斗可打的武士，而这些计划正在慢慢地吞噬他的内心。 几个月就这样匆匆过去了，你被迫与中野结婚的日期也越来越近了。他曾经问过你的名字，但除此之外并没有再采取任何进一步的行动；也许他觉得，只要忽视这个问题，它就会自行消失。 rows.original: In the days that follow, Nakano is a little less standoffish towards you. He still goes out with the other kitsune on their excursions to find benefactors to feed from — it's a social obligation as much as it is a necessity — but occasionally feeds from you perhaps once every fortnight. By day, he studies the blade, by night, he studies the brush; you continue to act as his muse when he's dissatisfied with his paintings or having trouble with verses, paying him back even if you're not truly a kitsune nor bound by their divine laws, strictly speaking. Kasyrra[party.som|...| and [party.compNames]...|, [party.compNames]...] the past slowly fades away as you gradually come to accept your new life. It's not a mindbreaking, or at least not that you're aware of, but a simple cessation of questioning one's situation. The other kitsune still point and whisper when you go about your business in the den, but whether it's Nakano, or perhaps Miko and Mai watching out for you, none of them actually do anything serious past the occasional minor prank. For better or for worse, you've become part of the scenery here — not someone in the foreground, as that would be beyond your station here, but as accepted as you might ever be in this society of vampiric vulpines. As promised, the two of you are married in the coming spring in a small, unassuming ceremony without the pomp that one might expect, given what you've learned of kitsune culture. Even so, Miko and Mai are practically overjoyed at dealing with the preparations, while even Komari herself appears mollified somewhat at the state of affairs and her great-great-grandson. There isn't much time for celebration, though. Barely a month has passed after your wedding when demons sweep out from the northeast beyond the mountains, no doubt Kasyrra's work now that you're no longer around to oppose her. After more than two centuries of peace, the Seven rally their faithful once more to meet the incursion from beyond this world, and glory-hungry Nakano eagerly volunteers to fight in the war he's dreamed of for so long. The campaign lasts years, and the entirety of the Marches is on the front lines. The den eventually sees more visitors, not just from the Old Country but from other allied armies of the Seven. Nakano is gone for weeks, months at a go; every time he leaves you can't help but worry about him, every time he returns with a few more fresh scars you make sure the bedchambers are ready for him. While he might claim that even dozens of demons are no match for one who has fully given himself over to shido — that paradoxically, by embracing death unflinchingly one stands the best chance of avoiding it — you have your own doubts, and work said doubts off with him in the night. With such a routine, the obvious outcome is inevitable — the second time he comes home from being on campaign, there's a fox kit in your arms when you come to greet him at the door. More follow as the second Godswar drags on, at least giving your husband-consort more of a reason to come home at the end of the day. As desperate as he is to prove himself as a diasporan, as much as he desires recognition from what he sees as his homeland, Nakano never fails to return on time to see his family, to retire to his study and practice the brush with you as his muse. Eventually, the war does end after years of struggle. Kasyrra is beaten back and her demons exterminated, though not without considerable losses for everyone involved. So long as Nakano isn't one of them, you couldn't care less. He's distinguished himself with zeal and fervor on the field multiple times, and is finally rewarded with the acknowledgement he's desired all his life — his entire family, Miko, Mai and even Komari herself included, take a small trip to the Old Country for him to receive a personal commendation from the Emperor for his dedication to divine war in the name of Keros. It is the crowning pinnacle of his life — and yours, too. Years fly by as the both of you savour your hard-won peace; as the wife of a war hero decorated by the Imperial Family, the other kitsune finally come to accept you even if you are a foreign bride. Even Komari wonders aloud if the two of you together has turned out better than she expected. The fight is not over; pockets of corruption still exist especially in the Marches, and Nakano has yet to hang up his sword. Yet the two of you are content to be together now and watch your kits grow into young foxes — and you couldn't be happier. Your adventure ends here.
rows.translation: 在接下来的几天里，中野对你不再那么冷淡了。他还是会和其他狐妖一起外出，去寻找可以吸食血液的施主——这既是一种社会义务，也是一种生存需要——但偶尔也会吸你的血，大概每两周一次。 白天他研究刀剑，夜晚则钻研笔墨；每当他对自己的画作不满意，或者在创作诗句时遇到困难时，你总会成为他的灵感源泉。即便严格来说，你并非真正的狐妖，也不受那些神圣法则的约束，但你依然在默默地帮助他。 卡希拉[party.som|...| 以及 [party.compNames]...|, [party.compNames]...] 随着你逐渐接受自己的新生活，过去的一切也会慢慢淡出你的记忆。这个过程并不会让人感到难以接受，至少你并没有察觉到这一点。其实，只是不再去质疑自己的处境罢了。当你在巢穴里忙自己的事情时，那些其他的狐妖们还是会指指点点、低声议论，但无论是中野，还是美子、舞子，她们其实都不会做出什么过分的事情，只是偶尔会开一些小玩笑而已。 无论好坏，你都已经成为了这里的一道风景线——虽然不是处于最显眼的位置，因为那超出了你的身份地位，但在这个由吸血鬼与女狼组成的社会中，你已经得到了人们应有的认可。 正如所承诺的那样，你们俩将在来年春天举行一场简单而低调的婚礼，不会有那些人们根据对狐族文化的了解所预想的盛大场面。即便如此，美子和小舞在筹备婚礼的过程中也显得无比开心，而就连小鞠本人，对于目前的状况以及她的曾曾孙似乎也感到相当满意。 然而，人们几乎没有时间庆祝。你的婚礼刚结束不到一个月，恶魔就从山脉东北方向涌了出来——毫无疑问，这是卡希拉在你不再阻碍她的情况下所为。经过两个多世纪的和平，七大势力再次集结他们的信徒，共同抵御这场来自异世界的入侵，而渴望荣耀的中野也迫不及待地志愿加入了这场他梦寐以求的战争。 这场战役持续了数年，整个边境地区都处于前线。最终，那个巢穴迎来了越来越多的访客——他们不仅来自旧国，还来自七国联盟的其他军队。中野常常会离开数周甚至数月；每次他离开时，你都会为他担心；而每次他回来时，身上又多了几道新的伤痕，你都会确保他的卧室已经准备好了。虽然他可能会声称，即使有几十只恶魔，也敌不过一个已经全身心投入战斗的人 志度 ——这种看似矛盾的现象其实说明：只有毫无畏惧地接受死亡，人才真正有可能避免它——你心中也有自己的疑虑，而你会在夜晚与他一起探讨这些疑虑。 在这样的日常生活中，结果自然是不可避免的——当他第二次从征战归来时，当你去门口迎接他时，你会看到他的怀里抱着一只狐妖幼崽。 随着第二次“神战”持续进行，越来越多的人加入了这场斗争。至少，这也给了你的丈夫更多的理由，在一天结束时回家与家人团聚。尽管他迫切地想要证明自己作为流亡者的价值，尽管他非常渴望得到他心目中旧国的认可，但中野始终会按时回家与家人团聚，然后回到书房，与你一起练习绘画，把你当作他的灵感源泉。 经过多年的斗争，这场战争最终还是结束了。卡希拉被击败了，她的那些恶魔也被消灭了，不过所有参与这场斗争的一方都付出了巨大的代价。只要中野不在那些受害者之中，你根本就不会在意这些事情。 他多次以满腔的热忱和坚定的决心在战场上表现出色，终于获得了他一生所追求的认可——他的全家，包括美子、舞以及小Mari，都专程前往古国，让他能够亲自接受皇帝的表彰，以表彰他为代表凯罗斯所进行的神圣战争所做出的贡献。 这是他一生中的巅峰时刻——对你来说也是如此。 岁月飞逝，你们俩共同享受着这份来之不易的安宁；作为一位被皇室授予荣誉的战争英雄的妻子，其他那些狐妖们终于开始接受你，即使你是一个外来的新娘。 就连小丸里也不禁暗自思忖：你们两个在一起，是否真的比她预想的还要幸福呢？这场斗争还没有结束，腐败现象依然存在，尤其是在边境地区；中野也尚未放下手中的剑。然而你们现在却很满足，一起守护着那些小家伙，看着它们渐渐长大成为年轻的狐妖——你们真的再幸福不过了。 你的冒险在这里结束。

rows.original: "I've got the bag," you say unenthusiastically. The tanuki witch sets down her teacup and beams at you. "What's with the gloom, dear? This is a happy moment!" "Well, I had to fight my way through their unwelcoming committee to get it for you." She raises one finger towards you, as if lecturing a child. "I didn't spring this on you, [pc.name]. You argued for different payment for the information in my possession, and I was kind enough to oblige. Now, the bag, please." You hand over the pouch and Evergreen unceremoniously flips it upside down and pulls the string holding it closed. A veritable smorgasbord of sex toys of all shapes and sizes spills out onto the floor. Once the cascade slows to a trickle, Evergreen peruses through the heap for a minute, making sure nothing is missing. Seemingly satisfied, the witch snaps her fingers which prompts a few of her daughters to enter the room and begin clearing out the pile. "All seems to be in order, [pc.name]," the witch says as she lays down onto the cushions. She makes herself comfortable and turns to Cait. "Now for your payment. Your father has made camp at an old caravanserai south of Hawkethorne, head west at the first junction and look around. The building is quite remarkable so you shouldn't have much trouble finding it. Merchant caravans used to run from there all the way to Tychris, and, from what I could glimpse of your father, I would presume that he has lost himself entirely to studying it." "He was there this whole time!?" Cait exclaims with understandable shock. She barely regains her composure and turns to you. "[pc.name]! We have to get to him! Please." "We will, Cait. Let's go." Before leaving you give a respectful bow to the witch. "Thank you for the information." You gather it's best to remain cautious and courteous around her. "Don't mention it. Oh, and [pc.name]." Evergreen tosses the bag at you. You snatch it from the air. The witch shifts, accentuating her curves and setting her eyes on yours with a sultry glint. "Think of it as hazard pay. I know firsthand how insufferable those foxes can be." You thank the tanuki for the extra and are about to put the purse in your bag before you remember what was inside it just a minute ago. Noticing your apprehension, Oxana chuckles. "It's clean, [pc.name]. It's not a physical space and as such doesn't retain any residue; all that was in it was removed along with the toys." "Right, thank you." With your concerns addressed, you put the bag into your bag. It will likely come in handy, and you're not one to shirk a witch's gift. At least not in her presence.

I do, but... oh, what the hell, I want my bag back more than I want anything you could give me. Your womb's as locked tight as an abbot's purse strings. Give me the bag, and I'll tell you what you want to know." You hand over the pouch and Evergreen unceremoniously flips it upside down and pulls the string holding it closed. A veritable smorgasbord of sex toys of all shapes and sizes spills out onto the floor. Once the cascade slows to a trickle, Evergreen peruses through the heap for a minute, making sure nothing is missing. Seemingly satisfied, the witch snaps her fingers which prompts a few of her daughters to enter the room and begin clearing out the pile. "All seems to be in order, [pc.name]," the witch says as she lays down onto the cushions. She makes herself comfortable and turns to Cait. "Now for your payment. Your father has made camp at an old caravanserai south of Hawkethorne, head west at the first junction and look around. The building is quite remarkable so you shouldn't have much trouble finding it. Merchant caravans used to run from there all the way to Tychris, and, from what I could glimpse of your father, I would presume that he has lost himself entirely to studying it." "He was there this whole time!?" Cait exclaims with understandable shock. She barely regains her composure and turns to you. "[pc.name]! We have to get to him! Please." "We will, Cait. Let's go." rows.translation: 我搞到了，”你兴致缺缺地说道。 那只狸猫女巫放下茶杯，朝你灿烂地一笑：“亲爱的，为什么这么闷闷不乐呢？现在应该是欢庆的时刻啊！” “嗯，我可是费了很大劲，才从他们那个不友好的委员会手中把东西弄到手的。” 她伸出一根手指，仿佛在训斥一个孩子：“我可没有突然把这个消息告诉你 [pc.name]你要求对我掌握的信息支付不同的报酬，我出于好意答应了你的要求。现在，请把那个袋子交给我。” 在你即将把袋子递过去之前，凯特走上前，握住了你的手腕。“等一下……在把这个交给你之前……我觉得我父亲在那场大暴风雪之前应该是从这边过来的。如果你知道他可能在哪里的话，我真的需要你的帮助……” 常青女士对她发出了一声轻哼，然后在沙发上换了一个姿势。“又来这一套 [pc.mf |男人 |女性 ]在最后一刻才来讨价还价？有点不地道啊，Caitriss Zethra。” “你知道我是谁吧？” 常青女士露出讥讽的笑容：“当然知道。感到惊讶吗？别这么觉得。你父亲曾经特别提到过他那迷人的女儿那漂亮的粉色头发，而且我无论在哪里都能认出一个Jassiran妓女会选择的服装。 在暴风雪来临前的几天，你的父亲来找你了。他说，他比他亲爱的女儿们先来到这片霜林，想要调查这里的废墟，但首先他想确认那些关于我存在的传闻是否属实——那些被普通民众用来吓唬孩子们的、关于森林女巫的传说。 他是个挺讨人喜欢的人，就是有点爱管闲事。他在房子周围转了半圈后，我几乎可以肯定他会把我的门垫用炭笔描下来。真奇怪你居然没能找到他——他这么显眼，很容易被注意到啊。" 凯特的尾巴兴奋地在她身后摆动着。“那么，你知道他在哪里吗？” “啊，问题就在这里。我知道，但是……哎呀，说实话，我比想要你给我的任何东西都更想要回我的包。你的嘴巴紧得就像修道院院长的钱袋一样。把包还给我，我就告诉你你想知道的事情。 你把袋子递过去，常青女士毫不客气地把它翻了个个儿，然后拉开了系住袋口的绳子。各种各样形状和大小的性玩具纷纷散落在地板上，简直就像一场丰富的“性玩具盛宴”。等这些玩具落下的速度慢了下来，常青女士仔细地检查了这一堆东西，确保没有遗漏任何东西。看起来很满意之后，这位女巫打了个响指，几名她的女儿立刻走进房间，开始清理这些玩具。 一切看起来都正常， [pc.name]这样吧，”女巫说着，躺到了垫子上，让自己舒服地躺好，然后转向凯特，“现在该支付你的报酬了。你父亲在鹰棘镇南边的一处旧商队旅馆安营了。你往西走，遇到第一个岔路口就往左转，然后四处看看吧。 这座建筑非常引人注目，所以你应该不会很难找到它。过去，商队就是从那里一路前往提克里斯的。从我对你父亲的观察来看，我敢推测，他应该已经完全沉浸在对这座建筑的研究之中了。他曾经是 那里 整个这段时间？！”凯特震惊地叫道。她好不容易才恢复镇定，然后转向你说道。[pc.name]我们必须找到他！求你了。” “我们一定会找到的，凯特。我们走吧。”在离开之前，你们向那位女巫恭敬地鞠了一躬：“感谢您提供的信息。”在她的面前，保持谨慎和礼貌总是最好的做法。 “不客气。哦，对了 [pc.name]常青女士将那个袋子扔向你，你迅速从空中接住了它。女巫的身姿微微一动，那曲线更加凸显出来，她用一种充满诱惑的眼神注视着你，说道：‘就把这当作是一种额外的补偿吧。我可是亲身体会过那些狐狸到底有多让人难以忍受。’” 你感谢了那只狸猫送来的这份额外礼物，正准备把钱包放进包里，突然想起刚才里面装着什么。 看到你脸上的犹豫，奥克萨娜轻笑了一声，说道：“里面什么都没有，是空的。 [pc.name]那并不是一个实体空间，因此也不会留下任何残留物；里面原本有的东西，连同那些玩具一起，都被清走了。” “好的，谢谢。”你的顾虑得到了解答，于是你把那个袋子放进了自己的包里。这个袋子很可能会在以后派上用场，而你也不是那种会拒绝女巫送的礼物的人。至少在她面前，你是不会这么做的。

rows.original: Evergreen greets you with a nod. "Ah, you're back. Did you have any luck getting my bag back from the foxes?" Why yes, you did. There were some circumstances that complicated matters in retrieving it, but you do have it on you. Which leads to some questions you'd like to ask before turning in the goods... "And those would be?" First of all, you definitely deserve some hazard pay for this. Her little errand turned out to be a lot more dangerous than she'd led you to expect. She could at least be a little more forthright about her jobs in the future. Sure, it's partly your own fault for not asking beforehand, but — "Hand it over, and let's see if the things inside are still intact. I'm sure those fuzzy good-for-nothings have their wet-fur stink all over my toys now." You do just that, and Evergreen pulls apart the strings, peering into the small brown bag. Standing, she crosses over to a nearby table and upends the linen pouch onto its surface, a veritable mountain of sex toys of various shapes and sizes spilling out into view. The tanuki witch picks up a few choice pieces, sniffs them, then nods. "Looks like all of my favorite pieces are still there, yes. Renegotiating price after the task is done is rather poor form, but I think I understand where you're coming from; at the same time, I'd rather not start a precedent by making an exception for you. Let's call it a bonus for a job well done, hmm?" You suppose that'll have to do — that, and being more careful while accepting jobs from her in the future. Evergreen smiles sweetly, then snaps her fingers. One of her daughters shuffles in to put away the mess on the table, and she turns her attention back to you. "Very well, then. Anything else?" You shake your head and stifle a sigh. Of course. Well, if she'd be so kind as to pay you for services rendered... "Ah, of course." Evergreen whistles sharply, and another daughter comes up with a tray, a bag of coin set on it. The tanuki witch takes it and shoves it into your hands; it feels appropriately heavy and clinks with a very satisfactory sound. So long as it doesn't disappear or turn into leaves in the morning, that'll do just fine. Evergreen chuckles. "I've long grown past simple glamours like that. Here, you wanted hazard pay? Take the bag as well. It'll be of more use in your hands than it is holding all my knick-knacks." You mean... after everything... well, you don't know what's been inside of it... "But you do. You saw it all come out, didn't you?" That was a rhetorical question. "Don't be such a prude, it's pretty clean inside. Extradimensional spaces don't come cheap, you know, and they don't get dirty." Would bad things happen if you turned it inside-out? "No, it just gets turned inside-out. Seriously, Estelore fixed that basic loophole a long time ago. Shame on you for not knowing your history, dear. Now that we've concluded business, perhaps we should have a little pleasure? My treat — if you're up for it, that is. Just ask."
rows.translation: 常青女士向你点头致意。 啊，你回来了。有没有成功把我的包从那些狐狸手部里夺回来呢？ 没错，你确实做到了。在取回它的过程中确实遇到了一些复杂的情况，但你现在确实把它带在身上了。因此，在上交这些物品之前，你有一些问题想要先问清楚…… 那么，这些是什么呢？ 首先，你确实应该因为这件事得到一些额外的补偿。她那个小小的差事，结果比她让你想象的要危险得多。以后她至少应该更坦诚地告诉你自己要去做什么。当然，你没有事先询问，这也是你自己的疏忽，但是—— 把东西交出来，让我们看看里面的东西还完好无损吗。我敢肯定，那些毛茸茸的家伙肯定把他们的湿漉漉的臭味弄得我的玩具到处都是。 你照做了，然后常青女士便拆开了那个小棕色袋子，将里面的东西都倒了出来。她站起身，走到附近的一张桌子旁，把那个亚麻布制成的袋子倒放在桌面上，顿时，各种各样形状和大小的成人玩具就像一座小山一样散落在桌上。这位狸猫女巫挑了几件她中意的玩具，闻了闻，然后点了点头。 看起来我所有喜欢的物品都还在那里，没错。在任务完成后才重新协商价格，这种做法确实不太妥当，但我大概能理解你的立场；不过，我也不想因为为你破例而开创一个先例。我们就把这看作是对你出色完成任务的奖励吧，嗯？ 你认为那样做就足够了——还有就是，以后在接受她安排的工作时，要更加谨慎一些。 常青女士微微一笑，然后打了个响指。她的一个女儿走过来，把桌子上弄乱的东西收拾好，她这才把注意力重新转向你。 那好吧，还有其他事情吗？ 你摇了摇头，强忍住一声叹息。当然了。不过，如果她能好心地为你提供的服务付钱的话…… 啊，当然。 常青女士发出清脆的哨声，另一个女儿拿来了一个托盘，上面放着一袋硬币。那只狸猫女巫接过袋子，塞到了你的手部里；硬币的分量恰到好处，相互碰撞时发出的声音也非常令人满意。 只要这些硬币不会在早上消失，也不会变成树叶，那就没问题了。 常青女士轻声笑了起来。 我早就不再被那种表面的光彩所吸引了。既然你想要危险津贴，那就把这个袋子也拿去吧。对你来说，它肯定比用来装我的那些小玩意儿要有用得多。 你是说……在经历了这一切之后……嗯，你根本不知道里面发生过什么…… 但你确实看到了。你亲眼看到了这一切发生，对吧？ 那只是一个反问句而已。 别这么古板嘛，里面其实挺干净的。你知道的，异维空间可不是便宜能买来的，而且它们也不会弄脏的。 如果把它翻个过来，会发生不好的事情吗？ 不，它只是被彻底弄反了而已。说真的，Estelore早就修补了这个基本的漏洞。亲爱的，你居然不知道这些历史，真是太可惜了。既然我们已经谈完了正事，或许应该找点乐子吧？我请客——当然，前提是你愿意的话。随时都可以告诉我。
