rows.original: You follow the princess outside, where a number of cow-[silly |pokes |folk ] in workers' uniforms are waiting. Varena goes to one of them, a cowgirl with thick spectacles, and quickly palms her a solid gold coin. The crowd disperses after that, and one of the Chargers clambers into the princess's carriage with the prisoner. He drives off, leaving just you, Varena, and a single bodyguard behind. The princess waves her lone protector off, then gives you a little smile. "At least we know who sent the spy now. Lord Iavari." "Tell me about him?" "House Iavari are part of the Novitauri, the newly wealthy families here in Khor'minos City. They made a name for themselves during my grandfather's reign by rebuilding aqueducts and sea tunnels that had been damaged during the big earthquakes. They have a cadre of talented geomancers in their employ, but fundamentally they're better regarded as mundane architects and engineers. I can't imagine why their patriarch would send someone after me, though. Lord Iavari's political ambitions have always been modest. He's never even run for the Senate." "What has he done recently?" Varena taps her chin. "Nothing suspicious that I can think of. I believe he worked with Senator Khaius to build the new bath houses? The senator supplied the funds, Iavari did the actual design and oversaw the work. Afterwards, I've even heard some whispers that Khaius is, um... having relations with Iavari's daughter." [var0 |Of course it comes back to Khaius. You and Calise both suspected him of being dirty, and now one of his political allies is spying on the princess. It's all coming together now. |Senator Khaius? Calise did say she suspected him of being dirty, didn't she? ] "Maybe we should look into the bath house?" you suggest. "I was thinking the same thing!" Varena says. "I've never been yet, but I hear they're remarkable. Very popular across all stratum of society. A royal visit wouldn't be out of the ordinary. First, though, I need to take possession of my cargo!" "What did you bring in anyway?" The princess gives you a cheeky grin. "I'm glad you asked. Follow me." Varena trots back inside, bends at the waist to pick up the crowbar from where it's fallen, and proves to have no trouble cranking the cargo open to reveal several neat stacks of white bags inside. She picks one up and opens it, showing off the contents: apples. Bright red apples, hundreds and hundreds of them between all the sacks in just this one box. "It's... fruit?" you wonder, looking them all over. The princess grins. "Mmhm. As much as all my money could buy. It wasn't easy getting so much through the quarantine. I had to beg an ice mage I know from Sartanni to come with the shipment and keep them fresh. But look, they're still ripe and shiny!" [pc.isDK |"All this trouble for fruit? What's the big idea?" |"So all of this was over fruit? Why?" ] "Well it doesn't matter what was in the boxes, does it? I wanted to lure out somebody who wanted to find out what was in them in the first place. So I thought, I might as well bring in something nice for the people of the city! Many of them haven't seen fruit, or anything fresh, in weeks now." Varena sinches the sack closed and slings it over her shoulder. "So now that you know the dark and terrible truth of what I was sneaking into the city... what do you say to helping me get these into the hands of the needy?"
rows.translation: 你跟随公主走到了外面，那里有好几头牛[silly |戳 |人们 ] 那些穿着工人制服的人们正在等待。瓦蕾娜走向其中一位——一位戴着厚眼镜的牛仔姑娘，迅速将一枚纯金硬币塞到了她的手部中。之后，人群渐渐散开了，其中一名“冲锋者”便带着囚犯爬上了公主的马车。 他开车离开了，只留下了你、瓦蕾娜和一名保镖。 公主挥手部让她的唯一保护者离开，然后对你微微一笑：“至少我们现在知道是谁派来了那个间谍了——是贾瓦里大人。” “请告诉我关于他的一些事情吧。雅瓦里家族属于诺维陶里家族，这是科尔米诺斯城中那些新近发家的家族。在我祖父执政期间，他们通过重建在大地震中受损的引水渠和海底隧道而声名鹊起。 他们虽然拥有一批才华横溢的风水师，但实际上，他们更应该被视作普通的建筑师和工程师。不过，我实在想不通他们的族长为什么会派人来追捕我。毕竟，贾瓦里大人的政治野心一向都很低调。 他甚至从未参加过参议院选举。 拥有 他最近做了什么吗？” 瓦蕾娜托了托下巴：“我想不出有什么可疑的地方。我听说他和凯厄斯参议员一起建造了那些新的浴场吧？资金是参议员提供的，而贾瓦里负责实际的设计和监督施工工作。后来，我还听到一些传言，说凯厄斯……嗯……似乎和某个人有关系。 关系 与贾瓦里的女儿一起。 [var0 |这一切最终都与凯乌斯有关。你和卡莉丝都怀疑他有不正当行为，而现在他的一个政治盟友还在暗中监视公主。所有这些线索终于汇聚到了一起。 |凯乌斯参议员？卡莉丝不是说过她怀疑他有不正当行为吗？ ] 也许我们应该去看看那些公共浴场吧？”你提议道。 “我也在想这个！”瓦蕾娜说，“我还没去过呢，但听说那些地方非常不错，各个社会阶层的人都很喜欢去。如果皇室成员也去的话，应该也不会显得奇怪吧。不过，首先我得去取回我的货物才行！ 做了 你反正都要带进来，对吧？” 公主调皮地笑了笑：“很高兴你问了这个问题。跟我来吧。” 瓦蕾娜快步回到屋里，弯腰捡起了掉在地上的撬棍，然后轻松地打开了货物包装，里面整齐地堆放着几叠白色袋子。 她拿起一个箱子打开它，展示里面的内容：苹果。鲜红色的苹果，仅仅在这个箱子里，就有成百上千个苹果装在各种袋子里。 “这是……水果？”你看着这些苹果，不禁疑惑道。 公主咧嘴笑了：“嗯，我的所有钱都花在这上面了。在隔离期间要把这么多东西运过来确实不容易，我甚至不得不求助于我在萨塔尼认识的一位冰法师，让他帮忙照看这些货物，确保它们保持新鲜。不过看，它们现在依然新鲜诱人，闪闪发光呢！" [pc.isDK |为了些水果搞出这么大的动静？到底图什么谋？ |所以这一切都是因为一个水果？为什么？ ] 其实，盒子里装了什么并不重要，对吧？我的目的本来就是想吸引那些想要知道盒子里有什么的人出来。所以我想，干脆为这座城市的居民准备一些好东西吧！ 他们中的许多人已经好几周没有吃到过水果，或者任何新鲜的食物了。” 瓦蕾娜把袋子系紧，然后甩到肩上。“现在你们已经知道了我偷偷潜入这座城市所背负的那些暗影而可怕的真相了。你觉得帮我把这些送到需要帮助的人手部中怎么样？
rows.raw: ' You follow the princess outside, where a number of cow-[silly |pokes |folk ] in workers' uniforms are waiting. Varena goes to one of them, a cowgirl with thick spectacles, and quickly palms her a solid gold coin. The crowd disperses after that, and one of the Chargers clambers into the princess's carriage with the prisoner. He drives off, leaving just you, Varena, and a single bodyguard behind. The princess waves her lone protector off, then gives you a little smile. "At least we know who sent the spy now. Lord Iavari." "Tell me about him?" "House Iavari are part of the Novitauri, the newly wealthy families here in Khor'minos City. They made a name for themselves during my grandfather's reign by rebuilding aqueducts and sea tunnels that had been damaged during the big earthquakes. They have a cadre of talented geomancers in their employ, but fundamentally they're better regarded as mundane architects and engineers. I can't imagine why their patriarch would send someone after me, though. Lord Iavari's political ambitions have always been modest. He's never even run for the Senate." "What has he done recently?" Varena taps her chin. "Nothing suspicious that I can think of. I believe he worked with Senator Khaius to build the new bath houses? The senator supplied the funds, Iavari did the actual design and oversaw the work. Afterwards, I've even heard some whispers that Khaius is, um... having relations with Iavari's daughter." [var0 |Of course it comes back to Khaius. You and Calise both suspected him of being dirty, and now one of his political allies is spying on the princess. It's all coming together now. |Senator Khaius? Calise did say she suspected him of being dirty, didn't she? ] "Maybe we should look into the bath house?" you suggest. "I was thinking the same thing!" Varena says. "I've never been yet, but I hear they're remarkable. Very popular across all stratum of society. A royal visit wouldn't be out of the ordinary. First, though, I need to take possession of my cargo!" "What did you bring in anyway?" The princess gives you a cheeky grin. "I'm glad you asked. Follow me." Varena trots back inside, bends at the waist to pick up the crowbar from where it's fallen, and proves to have no trouble cranking the cargo open to reveal several neat stacks of white bags inside. She picks one up and opens it, showing off the contents: apples. Bright red apples, hundreds and hundreds of them between all the sacks in just this one box. "It's... fruit?" you wonder, looking them all over. The princess grins. "Mmhm. As much as all my money could buy. It wasn't easy getting so much through the quarantine. I had to beg an ice mage I know from Sartanni to come with the shipment and keep them fresh. But look, they're still ripe and shiny!" [pc.isDK |"All this trouble for fruit? What's the big idea?" |"So all of this was over fruit? Why?" ] "Well it doesn't matter what was in the boxes, does it? I wanted to lure out somebody who wanted to find out what was in them in the first place. So I thought, I might as well bring in something nice for the people of the city! Many of them haven't seen fruit, or anything fresh, in weeks now." Varena sinches the sack closed and slings it over her shoulder. "So now that you know the dark and terrible truth of what I was sneaking into the city... what do you say to helping me get these into the hands of the needy?" '

rows.original: You've got better things to do.
rows.translation: 你还有更重要的事情要做。

rows.original:
You shake your head. "I'll pass."
    
    Varena screws up her lips. "Too important for a little charity work, huh? Tsk. Fine, I'm sure you've got Champion stuff taking up your time. I'll see you around Vitra's place later."
    
    "Until later," you say, turning back the way you'd come.
rows.translation:
你摇了摇头：“我就不参加了。”

瓦蕾娜撇了撇嘴：“对这种慈善活动来说，你确实太重要了，是吧？啧，好吧，我猜你肯定有更重要的事情要忙，比如处理那些与冠军相关的事情吧。晚点在维特拉家见。”

“回头见，”你说着，转身走回了来时的路。

rows.original: You have a strange dream this night... While you're not exactly sure how you got there in the first place, you find yourself wandering a lush, verdant hilltop, the gentle rise of the land culminating at a point in the distance. The grass is luscious but has been meticulously trimmed to a warm fuzz that tickles your bare feet as you walk on it, a soft path of packed dirt winds its way up to the peak, and a gentle, refreshing breeze constantly sweeps its way down from the cloudless heavens. The local trees are mostly peaches planted in rows, their deep pink blossoms hanging in clusters from their branches and lightly carpeting the ground in their shade. As you walk up the path in your dream, warm sunlight beats down upon your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] and sends a distinct sensation of contentment through you. Hmm... this seems oddly familiar... With a start, you realize that it's the backdrop of the mural you saw back in that chamber, the one that the Keros dedicants had apparently built. It's not an exact mirror of the scene you saw back there, but it's pretty close, and if you're not wrong, you should find a spring on top of the hill with — well, you'll just have to head on up and find out, won't you? Doubling your pace, you make it up the hill path in no time at all. Fortunately — or depending on your point of view, unfortunately — there's no vulpine orgy taking place at the moment. In fact, there aren't any kitsune hanging around; while you can see the occasional bird singing in one of the peach trees, there isn't anyone in sight. The peach grove gets thicker and thicker, trees pressing in upon the path, until they suddenly fall away and you emerge into a hilltop clearing. The sight that greets you is an interesting one, to say the least. There's the bathing spring you saw depicted in the mural, but the table with its feast is nowhere to be seen. Additionally, you're pretty sure that cabin wasn't depicted in the mural either. Built in and around a cherry blossom tree of gargantuan proportions, the entire structure rings the towering tree's hefty trunk, seamlessly blending in with the natural background. The style, the design — it's very reminiscent of that chamber you discovered the mural in, enough for you to say with certainty that they're one and the same. Yeah, while you're pretty sure that you're dreaming, everything about this hillscape just feels so real, so vivid. Did that mural make that much of an impression on you? One way or another, the hilltop cabin's the first and only sign of life that you've discovered so far. If this is a dream, nothing can really hurt you, and therefore there's no harm in going up and taking a look, is there? Squaring your shoulders, you follow the dirt path right up to the cabin, step onto the rather rustic rough-wood porch and knock on the door. Hello? Anyone home? Almost instantly, you hear shuffling from the other side, and the door opens just a crack to reveal a sliver of a face before it widens fully to reveal a mostly human fox-woman standing in the doorway. Her hair and fur is a shade of deep amber, she's dressed in what looks like a long-sleeved dress that goes all the way down to her ankles with a sash wrapped just underneath her breasts, and she's got dainty little human hands and feet. More interesting, though, is the fact that the kitsune has four tails — five short of Keros' nine, but enough to mark her as being affiliated with the trickster god, from what you can remember of your theology. Seeing you, she smiles, gives you a small bow, then speaks with an accent that you can't quite place. "Welcome, friend. I've... been hoping that you'd arrive." Why? Was she expecting you? "For a little while, yes. Would you like to come in? Speaking while standing on the doorstep is going to be a bit of a bother." Every bit the polite host, you see. Well, since this is just a dream, there can't be any harm in accepting her offer. Giving the kitsune a nod, you follow her into the rustic cabin, down a hallway and into a side chamber. There's a table in the middle of the room, knee-high and dark as ash, and she bids you sit on a floral-pattern cushion on one side while she takes up the one across from you. Now, would she be so kind as to explain what she meant by %"for a little while?"
rows.translation: 今晚你做了一个奇怪的梦…… 虽然你并不完全清楚自己是怎么做到的 得到了 首先，你会发现自己漫步在一片郁郁葱葱的山顶上，地势缓缓上升，最终在远处的某一点达到顶峰。草丛茂盛而柔软，经过精心修剪，形成一层温暖而细腻的草层，当你走在上面时，草叶会轻轻触碰你的足部背，带来一丝愉悦的感觉。一条由压实的泥土铺成的小路蜿蜒向上，通往山顶，而一阵阵清新的微风则不断从万里无云的蓝天中吹下来。 当地的树木大多是成排种植的桃树，它们深粉色的花朵成簇地挂在枝头，花瓣落下后轻轻覆盖在地面之上。 当你沿着这条小路前行时，温暖的阳光洒在你的身上 [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] 这种感觉会让你内心充满满足感。嗯……这种场景似乎有些熟悉…… 你突然意识到，这正是你在那个房间里看到的壁画背景，显然那是那些虔诚的凯罗斯信徒们创作的。这并不是一种 精确的 这应该就是你刚才看到的那个场景的镜像吧，不过两者非常相似。如果你没有弄错的话，应该在山顶上找到一个泉眼——嗯，你只需要上去亲自看看就知道了，对吧？ 你加快了足部步，很快就跑上了山坡的小路。 幸运的是——或者从另一个角度来看，也许也不幸吧——目前并没有什么狐妖们在举行狂欢活动。事实上，根本没有任何狐妖出现在附近；虽然你可以看到偶尔有鸟儿在桃树间歌唱，但确实没有狐妖的踪迹。一个 就在眼前。桃树林越来越茂密，树木将小路挤得越来越窄，直到它们突然让开道路，你便来到了一片山顶的空地上。 呈现在你眼前的景象，至少可以说，是非常有趣的。 有…… 你在壁画中看到的那处沐浴温泉确实存在，但那张摆满美食的桌子却不见了踪影。此外，你也很确定那间小屋也没有被画在壁画里。这座建筑环绕着一棵规模巨大的樱花树而建，整个结构紧密地依附在那棵参天大树的树干上，与周围的自然环境融为了一体。 这种风格、这种设计——它们让人不禁联想到你发现那幅壁画的那个房间，因此你可以肯定地说，它们其实是同一个地方。 是啊，虽然你很确定自己只是在做梦，但这个山景的一切给人的感觉实在是太 真实的真是太生动了。那幅壁画是不是让观众产生了强烈的共鸣？ 那个 这对你来说有什么特别的意义吗？ 无论如何，那座位于山顶的小屋都是你目前发现的第一个、也是唯一的生命迹象。如果这只是一个梦，那么没有什么会真正伤害到你，所以去那里看看也没什么坏处，对吧？ 你挺直肩膀，沿着那条土路一直走到小屋前，踏上那座相当简陋的木制门廊，然后敲了敲门。 “喂？有人在吗？” 几乎立刻，你就听到门另一边有足部步声传来，门被微微打开，只露出了一张脸的轮廓，随后门完全打开了，一个半人半狐的女子站在门口。 她的头发和毛发呈现出深琥珀色，她穿着一件看起来像是长袖连衣裙的衣服，这件衣服一直垂到她的足部踝处，在胸部下方还系着一条腰带。她的手部和足部都小巧得像人类的手部足部一样。 更有趣的是，这个九尾狐实际上有四条尾巴——虽然比凯罗斯的九条少五条，但根据你对相关神学的记忆，这样的特征已经足以说明她与那位善于捉弄人的神明有着关联。 看到你后，她微笑着向你轻轻鞠了一躬，然后用一种你一时无法辨认出的口音说道。 欢迎来到这里，朋友。我……其实一直在期待你的到来。 为什么？她是在等你吗？ 有那么一会儿吧。你想进来吗？站在门口说话确实有点不方便。 你真是个非常有礼貌的主人啊。嗯，既然这只是一个梦，接受她的邀请应该不会有什么坏处吧。你向那只九尾狐点了点头，然后跟着她走进了那间简朴的小屋，穿过走廊，来到了一侧的小房间。房间中央有一张桌子，高度大约和人的膝盖差不多，颜色黑得像灰烬。她让你坐在一边带有花纹的垫子上，而自己则坐在你对面的位置。 现在，她能好心解释一下“暂时”这个意思吗？

rows.original: "Ever since you picked up the orb." The orb? Oh... wait. Does she mean the amber orb you came across in the ruined chamber? "Ruined? I shouldn't be surprised it's been that long... but forgive me, where are my manners? My name is Kiyoko. I was — well, technically I still am — a kitsune, a follower of Keros the trickster god." You have heard plenty of folktales about the nine-tailed fox, none of them completely salutary. Keros has a reputation that you're sure she's full well aware of, so she won't mind if you're a little cautious, right? Kiyoko sighs, the corners of her lips turning down. "I promise not to harm you while you're in the Astral Plane, traveler. It's been so very long since I've had any kind of company while trapped here, even if I understand that time in this place isn't quite what it is on the outside. May I ask you for your name?" It's [pc.name]. The kitsune claps her hands. "Excellent. I have introduced myself. You have introduced yourself. This has been a very good start to our conversation." Well, since all this is a dream, you don't really see any harm in having a little chat with Kiyoko... "But this is no dream, [pc.name]. It may be taking place in your dreams, that's true, but our conversation right now is anything but an illusion. Regardless, you have your doubts, right?" Not knowing what exactly to say, you nod. "Then remember this, [pc.name]. When you wish to see me again, simply wear the amulet when you next go to sleep, and you will be transported here once more. Hopefully, this will convince you that this is no fever dream." [pc.isDK |Yeah, yeah. That's what all the hallucinations say. Fine, you might just give it a go sometime. After all, if she's just a figment of your imagination, then it can't hurt any. And if she's not... well, you'll cross that bridge when you get to it. |You must have appeared quite uncertain, for Kiyoko gives you a small, encouraging smile and bows again. "What can it hurt to give it a go?" Well, she's got a point there. If you're just having some kind of crazy dream, then following her advice isn't going to hurt any. And on the off-chance that you're not having some kind of crazy dream, then... well, you've already gone down enough rabbit holes in recent times. What's another crazy path explored to the likes of you? ] "I don't fault you for not fully trusting anyone or anything related to Keros," Kiyoko continues. "After all, he's not known as the trickster god for nothing. But I hope that you'll at least choose to hear me out before drawing your conclusions." "And now... I bid you good-bye, [pc.name]." With a start, the dreamscape fades away, and instead of the little forest cabin of living wood you find yourself awake and in the warm confines of [atCamp|your bedroll.|your bed in the Frost Hound.] Ugh... what dreams! Rubbing the sleep from your eyes, you remember Kiyoko's words and fumble about on your person for the amber orb. Yep, it's still there in your pocket where you left it when you turned in for the night. She told you that if you ever wanted to see her again, all you'd have to do is hold it close on your person when you went to sleep... As much as you'd like to dismiss it all and just get on with your day, there's a tiny part of you that can't help but wonder. Either way, the choice is up to you — either you can do as Kiyoko suggested in your dream and try to see her again, or you can chuck the amber orb into a storage trunk and forget it forever.
rows.translation: 从你拿到那个球体那一刻起。 那个球体？哦……等等，她是指你在那间废弃的房间里找到的那个琥珀色球体吗？ 毁了？这么久过去了，我其实也不该感到惊讶……不过请原谅我的失礼，我应该先做自我介绍。我叫清子，严格来说，我现在仍然是一只狐妖，是诡计之神凯罗斯的追随者。 你 拥有 我听过很多关于九尾狐的民间故事，但这些故事并没有一个是真正有益的。凯洛斯这个名声，她肯定心知肚明，所以如果你稍微谨慎一些，她应该也不会介意吧？ 清子叹了口气，嘴角微微下垂。 我承诺，在你身处星界的时候，绝不会伤害你，旅人。自从我被困在这里之后，已经有太久太久没有人与我相伴了……尽管我也明白，这个地方的时间流逝方式与外界不同。请问，你能告诉我你的名字吗？ 就是 [pc.name]那只狐妖拍起了手部来。 太好了。我已经做了自我介绍，你也做了自我介绍。这样我们的对话就有了一个很好的开端。 嗯，既然这一切都只是梦境，那么和清子聊聊天应该也不会有什么坏处吧…… 但这不是梦境， [pc.name]虽然这一切可能只发生在你的梦中，但我们的对话绝对不是幻觉。无论如何，你还是心存疑虑，对吧？ 不知道该说些什么，你只是点了点头。 那么请记住这一点， [pc.name]当你再次想见到我的时候，下次睡觉时只需佩戴那个护身符，你就会再次被传送到这里。希望这能让你相信，这一切并非是一场发烧引起的幻觉。 [pc.isDK |是啊，是啊。所有那些幻觉不都是这么说的吗？好吧，你不妨找个时间试试看。毕竟，如果她只是你想象中的产物，那么尝试一下也不会有什么坏处。而如果她真的存在……嗯，到那时再想办法解决就是了。 |你看起来似乎有些犹豫，于是清子给了你一个鼓励性的微笑，然后再次鞠了一躬。 试一试又有什么坏处呢？ 嗯，她说的也有道理。如果你只是在做某个疯狂的梦，那么听从她的建议也不会有什么坏处。更何况，也有可能你真的 不是 在做着某种疯狂的梦吧……嗯，最近你已经陷入太多莫名其妙的困境了。对于你这样的人来说，还有什么更疯狂的路径可以探索呢？ ] 我并不怪你不愿意完全信任与凯洛斯有关的任何人或任何事。 清子继续说道。 毕竟，他被称为‘诡计之神’可不是没有原因的。但我希望你在下结论之前，至少能听我把话说完。 现在……我要跟你们说再见了， [pc.name]." 随着一阵轻响，梦境中的景象渐渐消失，你不再置身于那座由活木搭建的小森林小屋中，而是清醒地来到了温暖而舒适的 [atCamp|你的行囊。|你在“霜猎犬”号上的床位。] 唉……真是些奇怪的梦啊！揉了揉眼睛，你想起纪代子说过的话，开始在身上翻找那颗琥珀球。没错，它还在你口袋里，就像你晚上睡觉时放好的那样。 她告诉过你，如果你以后还想再见到她，只需要在睡觉时把它紧紧抱在身边就可以了…… 无论你多么想忽略这一切，继续过你的日常生活，你内心总有那么一个小角落，会忍不住产生这样的疑问。 无论如何，这个决定由你来做——要么按照纪代子在梦中建议的那样去做，试着再次见到她；要么就把那个琥珀球扔进储物箱里，永远把它忘掉。
rows.raw: " "Ever since you picked up the orb." The orb? Oh... wait. Does she mean the amber orb you came across in the ruined chamber? "Ruined? I shouldn't be surprised it's been that long... but forgive me, where are my manners? My name is Kiyoko. I was — well, technically I still am — a kitsune, a follower of Keros the trickster god." You have heard plenty of folktales about the nine-tailed fox, none of them completely salutary. Keros has a reputation that you're sure she's full well aware of, so she won't mind if you're a little cautious, right? Kiyoko sighs, the corners of her lips turning down. "I promise not to harm you while you're in the Astral Plane, traveler. It's been so very long since I've had any kind of company while trapped here, even if I understand that time in this place isn't quite what it is on the outside. May I ask you for your name?" It's [pc.name]. The kitsune claps her hands. "Excellent. I have introduced myself. You have introduced yourself. This has been a very good start to our conversation." Well, since all this is a dream, you don't really see any harm in having a little chat with Kiyoko... "But this is no dream, [pc.name]. It may be taking place in your dreams, that's true, but our conversation right now is anything but an illusion. Regardless, you have your doubts, right?" Not knowing what exactly to say, you nod. "Then remember this, [pc.name]. When you wish to see me again, simply wear the amulet when you next go to sleep, and you will be transported here once more. Hopefully, this will convince you that this is no fever dream." [pc.isDK |Yeah, yeah. That's what all the hallucinations say. Fine, you might just give it a go sometime. After all, if she's just a figment of your imagination, then it can't hurt any. And if she's not... well, you'll cross that bridge when you get to it. |You must have appeared quite uncertain, for Kiyoko gives you a small, encouraging smile and bows again. "What can it hurt to give it a go?" Well, she's got a point there. If you're just having some kind of crazy dream, then following her advice isn't going to hurt any. And on the off-chance that you're not having some kind of crazy dream, then... well, you've already gone down enough rabbit holes in recent times. What's another crazy path explored to the likes of you? ] "I don't fault you for not fully trusting anyone or anything related to Keros," Kiyoko continues. "After all, he's not known as the trickster god for nothing. But I hope that you'll at least choose to hear me out before drawing your conclusions." "And now... I bid you good-bye, [pc.name]." With a start, the dreamscape fades away, and instead of the little forest cabin of living wood you find yourself awake and in the warm confines of [atCamp|your bedroll.|your bed in the Frost Hound.] Ugh... what dreams! Rubbing the sleep from your eyes, you remember Kiyoko's words and fumble about on your person for the amber orb. Yep, it's still there in your pocket where you left it when you turned in for the night. She told you that if you ever wanted to see her again, all you'd have to do is hold it close on your person when you went to sleep... As much as you'd like to dismiss it all and just get on with your day, there's a tiny part of you that can't help but wonder. Either way, the choice is up to you — either you can do as Kiyoko suggested in your dream and try to see her again, or you can chuck the amber orb into a storage trunk and forget it forever."

rows.original: Hmm... ... A soft, warm, and ticklish sensation is the first thing that you're aware of. As your senses slowly come to you, you realize you're lying on your back in a circle of trimmed grass, a circular clearing in a forest of peach trees. Above you, a bright blue sky burns with morning light, a few thin, wispy clouds drifting lazily from one horizon to another, but there's no sun at all. Oh. You're back. At least you haven't been dumped at the foot of the hill this time — as you sit up and get your bearings, you find your dream has been kind enough to place you right at the edge of the glade which holds Kiyoko's little cabin. Groaning and feeling just as tired as you did when you laid yourself down to sleep, you brush away the peach blossoms from your [pc.armor], push yourself to your feet, and set off towards the cabin at a brisk pace. It doesn't take long for you to close the distance to the little abode, but you're saved the trouble of having to go all the way up to the door once more. As you pass by the hilltop hot spring, you spy a familiar vulpine figure lounging about in the steaming waters. Kiyoko's eyes widen in surprise as you draw close, but soon regains her usual calm, peaceable demeanor as she watches your approach. "Oh my, I wasn't expecting you right now, [pc.name]. If I had a little advance notice, I'd have prepared a little extra in the way of lunch." She waves a hand nonchalantly at the platter of peach slices and mandarin segments on the spring's rim, a small dish of chilled sweet syrup on the side. Huh, did you catch her at a bad time? Kiyoko laughs, her voice high and musical, almost like some kind of flute. Certainly hits the right notes, that's for sure. "Oh, no, no. Not in the least — you're more than welcome to stay, or even join me in the water if you like. While we understand that other peoples are more reserved in their modesty and behave accordingly in their lands, the beloved of Keros have fewer compunctions about such matters." You think back to the orgy depicted in the mural, and have to admit that does indeed appear to be the case. "Or if you'd rather, you can just sit by the water's edge, and we can converse like this. Either way, are you now satisfied that this realm — and by extent, me — are no illusion?" You nod, then look down at the gently steaming spring waters. Like it or not, unless you were absolutely stark raving mad there's almost no chance that you'd have the same perfectly remembered dream twice in a row, and with the latter a seamless continuation of the former to boot. All right, she's real. But there's got to be a good explanation for all of this, right? Kiyoko looks thoughtful for a moment, her eyes rolling upwards as she thinks. "I'll explain it as best as I can, but it's going to take a while. You should make yourself comfortable before we begin." An invitation without explicitly inviting you. How quaint. Are you going to accept it?
rows.translation: 嗯…… …… 你首先感受到的是一种柔软、温暖且略带痒痒的感觉。当你的感官逐渐恢复功能时，你发现自己正仰躺在一片修剪整齐的草地上——这片草地位于一片桃树丛中，形成了一个圆形的空地。 你的头顶上，湛蓝的天空被晨轻型染得通亮，几片稀薄的云朵懒洋洋地从地平线这一端飘到另一端，但天空中却根本没有太阳。 哦，你回来了。至少这次你没有被丢在山足部下——当你坐起来环顾四周时，你发现梦境似乎很贴心地将你安排在了那片小树林的边缘，而基约科的小木屋就坐落在那里。 你发出一声呻吟，感到疲惫不堪，就像刚躺下准备睡觉时一样。你将那些桃花从身上拂开 [pc.armor]你强迫自己站起身来，然后快步朝着小木屋走去。 没过多久，你就赶到了那座小屋跟前，不过这次你省去了再走上一次台阶去敲门的麻烦。当你经过山顶的温泉时，你看到一个熟悉的身影正在蒸腾的水中悠闲地休息着。当你靠近时，清子的目轻型突然瞪大了，显得十分惊讶，但很快她就恢复了平时那种平静、安详的神态，静静地注视着你靠近的身影。 哦天，我本来没料到你现在会来 [pc.name]如果我能提前得到通知，我就会多准备一些午餐了。 她漫不经心地朝盘子里那些桃子片和柑橘瓣挥了挥手，旁边还放着一小碟冰镇的甜糖浆。 “哈，你是不是碰上她不高兴的时候了？” 清子笑了起来，她的笑声高亢而悦耳，简直就像某种笛声一样。毫无疑问，她的笑声确实很动听。 哦，不，不。绝对不是这样的——你完全可以留下来，甚至如果愿意的话，也可以和我一起下水。虽然我们理解在其他地方，人们会更加注重礼貌和矜持，行为也会相应地有所约束，但在凯罗斯，人们在这些方面并没有太多的顾虑。 你回想起壁画中描绘的那一幕，不得不承认，情况确实如此。 或者，如果你愿意的话，也可以坐在水边，我们就可以像这样聊天。不管怎样，你现在是否确信，这个境界——以及我本人——都不是幻觉呢？ 你点了点头，然后低头看着那股缓缓冒着热气的泉水。不管你愿不愿意承认，除非你完全失去了理智，否则几乎不可能连续两次做同一个记忆如此清晰的梦，而且后一个梦还是前一个梦的完美延续。 好吧，她确实是真实存在的。但这一切肯定有合理的解释，对吧？ 清子若有所思地沉吟了一会儿，思考时她的目轻型还微微向上翻动着。 我会尽我所能来解释，不过这需要一些时间。在我们开始之前，你不妨先放松一下。 一份没有明确邀请你的邀请函。真是别具一格啊。你会接受它吗？

rows.original: Well, that was quite the conversation, and you now think you've got a better handle on what this place is all about. Now, you know she can't get out because otherwise she'd probably have done that already, but does Kiyoko have any ideas as to how she might be freed? The kitsune averts her eyes and looks away. "Why, you would want to unleash a servant of the notorious Trickster back upon the world? Aren't you worried that I'll get up to all sorts of mischief once I'm out of my prison?" [pc.isDK |Look, you understand from what you remember of your folk legends that her patron god is some kind of asshole. Fair and fine enough. But by all accounts he wasn't an utter bastard, at least not to those who didn't deserve it in some way or the other. Even his most favored prank — granting wishes to people and then finding a loophole in the wording to pervert it against its intentions — usually tended to be carried out against the feckless, greedy, or otherwise unsavoury characters. [pc.bg acolyte|After all, you did do some reading up on each of the Living Gods during your upbringing in monastic life, although you now suppose you wish you'd paid more attention...] What you guess you're driving at is that while Keros might be mean-spirited in some aspects, perhaps even feared by the less cunning, he isn't downright cruel or evil. As such, you think you can at least hear her out. Should she ever get on your bad side, though... Rather than showing affront to the implied threat, Kiyoko just dips her head a little. "I understand; we kitsune are no strangers to cold welcomes. The way you're behaving right now isn't too different from the greeting we received upon our arrival in the north. Without mincing words, I'll admit up front that I am a monster by most definitions." "For now, all I'm requesting is for you to hear me out, give me a chance to prove that I've no ill-will. Beyond that, well, we'll see, especially after the answer that I'm going to give you regarding your earlier question." |Be as that may, you don't get the feeling that Kiyoko is a bad person. Although this admittedly is only your second meeting, you don't get from her the gut reaction someone nasty would produce — mischievous is okay, so long as it doesn't go too far. Kiyoko just rolls her eyes, smiles a thin smile and tsks. "A gut reaction. One of the easier things to fool, really. I don't know if you're being nice and trying to see the good in everyone, or just being very, very naive. I mean, all this honesty could just be setup to hide some deeper, darker secret. Admit the small sins to turn attention from the large ones and all that." Be as that may, you're still hoping you can get off on the right foot when meeting someone new. Everyone deserves a chance, so to speak. If and when that chance is blown, circumstances might change, but for now you'd like to not let her patron god's notoriety color your attitude towards her. She's been nothing but the epitome of civility and hospitality to you since you arrived in her little pocket world, and you'd like to keep it that way. Being unnecessarily mean to her would ruin that, wouldn't it? The smile vanishes from Kiyoko's face, and the kitsune lady studies you for a long time. After a minute or so, she closes her eyes and takes a deep breath. "I'm really not sure, but by all appearances you seem to be genuine in your words. If that's the case, and I haven't merely misjudged your character — well, then, thank you." No problem. "It's heartening to hear this coming from you, given what I'm about to tell you next." ] Right. Back to the point, then — does Kiyoko have any leads as to how she might be able to escape this gilded cage? By all appearances, she's tiring of her stay here. A sigh. "Now that's an understatement if I ever heard one. Not on my own, though. I had some ideas, but as I was there was no way of doing it under my own power. My suspicion is that the only way to permanently free me from this Astral Plane is to have Keros himself fix the orb of transference and put right whatever damage the dark magic did so the gate can be used. That's the first problem." "The second problem — or at least, what I suspect it to be — is that I don't think I've any material essence left, that it was ripped away by the spell that was intended to kill me. My spirit managed to get away unharmed, but as far as I can tell I don't have a body in the way you understand it. Even if the gate was still working properly, I wouldn't be able to rematerialize outside of the Astral Plane. To put it simply, I don't have a body to go back to." So she's sure that's her twofold problem? Kiyoko nods glumly. "Trust me, I've had a long time to try and work my way out of this predicament, and it always comes back to the same problems. Like I mentioned, the only real way to restore me properly would be to find Keros himself, or at least some other kitsune who could lead you to him, and have him get me out of here." "In the meantime, though... there's a temporary solution which might work, but I've never had the chance to actually try it out." And that would be? "Hmm. Do you mind if we discussed it later? I do have to go over my notes once more, just to be sure. But suffice to say that it may not be to your mores; if after I explain it you find such a thing repugnant, then I won't press." [pc.isDK |Interesting. You'll be looking forward to it, then. "Oh?" Nothing, just a thought. |You nod. It's hard to place your trust in someone who openly follows a god who goes by the moniker of the Trickster, but like you said, you'll hear her out. "By the next time you return, I'll have gathered my thoughts and will be ready to give a full explanation. After that, you can decide what to do." Sounds fair enough. ] "There is one last piece of advice that I have for you. The orb of transference and the amulet it's set in are small and easily lost — it was designed to be easily smuggled or snuck into places, after all. I would suggest that you keep a tight hold on it before it happens to lose itself again; I don't fancy another eternity stuck all alone in this realm." "You don't have to wear it all the time, of course," Kiyoko continues. "But I think it'd also help you foster a deeper connection to this place... and me." "Now, I think we've both had enough for one meeting. I'm guessing you need to mull over what I've just told you, and on my part, I need to go look for those notes..." Rising from the water, her sodden amber hair and fur clinging to her slight curves, Kiyoko steps forward and gives you a hug. "Ah, I'd almost forgotten how nice it is to receive a hug. People are so warm... well, goodbye for now, [pc.name]. I'll see you around..." You wake with a start, breathing heavily. Now that was some dream. What should you do next, though? Kiyoko did say that she'd explain her idea to you the next time you visited her in your dreams, so there's that to look forward to. Maybe you ought to ask about it when you can... for now, though, you ought to get some more sleep.
rows.translation: 嗯，那真是一次意味深长的对话，现在你应该对自己所了解的这个地方有了更清晰的认识了吧。你知道她现在无法逃脱，否则她早就行动了，但吉代有没有什么办法可以帮助她获得自由呢？ 那只狐妖移开了视线，望向了别处。 为什么，你竟然想让那个声名狼藉的恶作剧之神的仆从重新回到这个世界上来？你难道不担心我一旦摆脱囚禁，就会做出各种恶作剧吗？ [pc.isDK |你看，根据你对民间传说的记忆，她的守护神应该是个相当恶劣的角色。这倒也情有可原。但据各种描述，他其实并不是个彻头彻尾的混蛋，至少不会去针对那些在某些方面并不该受到这种对待的人。就连他最常玩的把戏——满足人们的愿望，然后却在愿望的表述中找漏洞，让这些愿望产生与原本意图相反的效果——通常也是针对那些懒惰、贪婪或者品行不端的人来实施的。 [pc.bg acolyte|毕竟，你 做了 在修道生涯中，你曾仔细研究过每一位“活神”的相关资料，但现在你或许会后悔当初没有更加用心地去了解他们……] 你的意思大概是，虽然凯罗斯在某些方面可能心胸狭隘，甚至会让那些不够精明的人感到畏惧，但他其实并不是那种彻头彻尾的 残忍的 或者 邪恶因此，你认为至少应该听她把话说完。不过，如果她真的惹你生气了…… 面对这种隐含的威胁，清子只是轻轻低下了头。 我明白；我们狐族对冷遇早已习以为常。你现在的态度，与我们初到北方时所受到的对待并没有太大区别。毫不客气地说，按照大多数定义，我确实是个怪物。 目前，我唯一的要求就是请你们先听我把话说完，给我一个机会来证明我没有任何恶意。至于其他的事情，嗯，我们到时候再看看吧，尤其是在我回答了你们之前那个问题之后。 |尽管如此，你并不会觉得清子是个坏人。虽然这确实只是你们的第二次见面，但从她身上，你并没有感受到那种让人觉得她是个坏人的直觉。 糟糕的 这样反而会显得更有趣——只要别太过火就行。 清子只是翻了个白眼，勉强挤出一丝笑容，然后轻声叹了口气。 这是一种本能的反应。其实，这也是最容易被人欺骗的地方之一。我不知道你是出于好意，试图看到每个人身上的优点，还是只是太天真了。我的意思是，所有这些坦诚之举，很可能只是为了掩盖某些更隐秘、更阴暗的真相。通过承认一些小过错，来转移人们对那些重大问题的注意力，就是这种套路吧。 无论如何，你仍然希望在与新认识的人见面时能够有一个好的开始。可以说，每个人都应该得到这个机会。如果这个机会被错过了，情况也可能会发生变化，但目前你并不想让她的那些负面名声影响到你对待她的态度。 自从你来到她这个小小的世界，她一直都以礼貌和热情的态度对待你，而你也希望这种关系能够继续保持下去。如果无缘无故地对她恶语相向，那么这一切不就会毁掉吗？ 清子的脸上原本的笑容消失了，那位狐族女子仔细地打量了你好一会儿。大约一分钟后，她闭上了眼睛，深吸了一口气。 我真的不太确定，但从你的话语来看，你似乎是真诚的。如果真是这样，而我并没有误解你的性格……那么，谢谢你。 没问题。 考虑到我接下来要告诉你的事情，听到你这么说真的让人感到欣慰。 ] 好吧，回到正题——桐子有没有什么办法可以让自己摆脱这个金笼子呢？从种种表现来看，她似乎已经厌倦了在这里的生活。 叹了口气。 这简直可以说是轻描淡写了。不过，这并不是我一个人能完成的。我确实有一些想法，但当时在现场，单凭我的力量根本无法实现。我认为，要想彻底摆脱这个星界，唯一的办法就是让凯罗斯亲自修复那个传送球，修复那些被暗影魔法造成的破坏，这样才能重新使用那道传送门。这就是第一个问题。 这个 第二 问题在于——至少我是这么认为的——我觉得自己已经没有任何实质性的存在了，那个本应杀死我的咒语把我的所有物质本质都夺走了。我的灵魂虽然侥幸逃过了伤害，但据我所知，我已经没有你们所理解的那种身体了。即使那扇通道仍然能够正常运作，我也无法在星界之外重新获得实体。简单来说，我根本没有可以回归的身体了。 所以她确定这就是她面临的双重问题吗？ 清子黯然地点了点头。 相信我，我花了很长时间试图摆脱这种困境，但问题总是反复出现。就像我之前说的，真正能让我摆脱这种处境的方法，就是找到凯罗斯本人，或者至少是另一只能够带你找到他的狐妖，让他把我从这里救出去。 不过，在此期间……有一个临时解决方案，或许可以有效，但我至今还没有机会真正试一试。 那会是什么呢？ 嗯，我们稍后再讨论这个吧？我还需要再仔细看看我的笔记，确认一下细节。不过可以先告诉你，这个想法可能不符合你的观念；如果在我解释之后，你仍然觉得这种做法令人反感，那我也不会再坚持了。 [pc.isDK |有意思。那么，你一定会很期待它的吧。 哦？ 没什么，只是随便想了一下而已。 |你点了点头。对于一个公然信奉被称为“骗子”的神明的人来说，确实很难让人信任她，但就像你说的，你还是会听她把事情讲完的。 等到你下次回来的时候，我一定会仔细思考清楚，然后准备好给出一个全面的解释。之后，你可以再决定该怎么做。 听起来挺合理的。 ] 我还有最后一条建议要告诉你。那个传送球以及镶嵌在其中的护身符体积都很小，很容易丢失——毕竟，它们本来就是被设计用来方便偷运或偷偷携带到各种地方的。我建议你一定要好好保管它们，以免它们再次丢失；我可不想再在这个领域里孤独地待上永恒的时间了。 当然，你并不一定非得一直戴着它。 清子继续说道。 但我认为，这也会帮助你与这个地方……以及与我建立更深厚的情感联系。 现在，我想我们俩在一次会议中已经讨论得够多了。我猜你需要时间仔细考虑我刚才说的那些内容，而对我来说，我也需要去把那些笔记找出来…… 从水中站起来的基约科，她那湿漉漉的琥珀色头发和毛发紧贴着她那娇美的身形，她走上前，给了你一个拥抱。 啊，我差点忘了被拥抱是多么美好的感觉。人们真是如此温暖……好吧，暂时再见了。 [pc.name]回头见…… 你突然惊醒，呼吸急促。那个梦真是够离奇的…… 不过接下来该做什么呢？纪代子确实说过，下次你在梦中拜访她时，她会向你解释她的想法，所以这个还可以期待。也许等有机会的时候应该去问问她……不过现在，还是再睡一会儿吧。
rows.raw: " Well, that was quite the conversation, and you now think you've got a better handle on what this place is all about. Now, you know she can't get out because otherwise she'd probably have done that already, but does Kiyoko have any ideas as to how she might be freed? The kitsune averts her eyes and looks away. "Why, you would want to unleash a servant of the notorious Trickster back upon the world? Aren't you worried that I'll get up to all sorts of mischief once I'm out of my prison?" [pc.isDK |Look, you understand from what you remember of your folk legends that her patron god is some kind of asshole. Fair and fine enough. But by all accounts he wasn't an utter bastard, at least not to those who didn't deserve it in some way or the other. Even his most favored prank — granting wishes to people and then finding a loophole in the wording to pervert it against its intentions — usually tended to be carried out against the feckless, greedy, or otherwise unsavoury characters. [pc.bg acolyte|After all, you did do some reading up on each of the Living Gods during your upbringing in monastic life, although you now suppose you wish you'd paid more attention...] What you guess you're driving at is that while Keros might be mean-spirited in some aspects, perhaps even feared by the less cunning, he isn't downright cruel or evil. As such, you think you can at least hear her out. Should she ever get on your bad side, though... Rather than showing affront to the implied threat, Kiyoko just dips her head a little. "I understand; we kitsune are no strangers to cold welcomes. The way you're behaving right now isn't too different from the greeting we received upon our arrival in the north. Without mincing words, I'll admit up front that I am a monster by most definitions." "For now, all I'm requesting is for you to hear me out, give me a chance to prove that I've no ill-will. Beyond that, well, we'll see, especially after the answer that I'm going to give you regarding your earlier question." |Be as that may, you don't get the feeling that Kiyoko is a bad person. Although this admittedly is only your second meeting, you don't get from her the gut reaction someone nasty would produce — mischievous is okay, so long as it doesn't go too far. Kiyoko just rolls her eyes, smiles a thin smile and tsks. "A gut reaction. One of the easier things to fool, really. I don't know if you're being nice and trying to see the good in everyone, or just being very, very naive. I mean, all this honesty could just be setup to hide some deeper, darker secret. Admit the small sins to turn attention from the large ones and all that." Be as that may, you're still hoping you can get off on the right foot when meeting someone new. Everyone deserves a chance, so to speak. If and when that chance is blown, circumstances might change, but for now you'd like to not let her patron god's notoriety color your attitude towards her. She's been nothing but the epitome of civility and hospitality to you since you arrived in her little pocket world, and you'd like to keep it that way. Being unnecessarily mean to her would ruin that, wouldn't it? The smile vanishes from Kiyoko's face, and the kitsune lady studies you for a long time. After a minute or so, she closes her eyes and takes a deep breath. "I'm really not sure, but by all appearances you seem to be genuine in your words. If that's the case, and I haven't merely misjudged your character — well, then, thank you." No problem. "It's heartening to hear this coming from you, given what I'm about to tell you next." ] Right. Back to the point, then — does Kiyoko have any leads as to how she might be able to escape this gilded cage? By all appearances, she's tiring of her stay here. A sigh. "Now that's an understatement if I ever heard one. Not on my own, though. I had some ideas, but as I was there was no way of doing it under my own power. My suspicion is that the only way to permanently free me from this Astral Plane is to have Keros himself fix the orb of transference and put right whatever damage the dark magic did so the gate can be used. That's the first problem." "The second problem — or at least, what I suspect it to be — is that I don't think I've any material essence left, that it was ripped away by the spell that was intended to kill me. My spirit managed to get away unharmed, but as far as I can tell I don't have a body in the way you understand it. Even if the gate was still working properly, I wouldn't be able to rematerialize outside of the Astral Plane. To put it simply, I don't have a body to go back to." So she's sure that's her twofold problem? Kiyoko nods glumly. "Trust me, I've had a long time to try and work my way out of this predicament, and it always comes back to the same problems. Like I mentioned, the only real way to restore me properly would be to find Keros himself, or at least some other kitsune who could lead you to him, and have him get me out of here." "In the meantime, though... there's a temporary solution which might work, but I've never had the chance to actually try it out." And that would be? "Hmm. Do you mind if we discussed it later? I do have to go over my notes once more, just to be sure. But suffice to say that it may not be to your mores; if after I explain it you find such a thing repugnant, then I won't press." [pc.isDK |Interesting. You'll be looking forward to it, then. "Oh?" Nothing, just a thought. |You nod. It's hard to place your trust in someone who openly follows a god who goes by the moniker of the Trickster, but like you said, you'll hear her out. "By the next time you return, I'll have gathered my thoughts and will be ready to give a full explanation. After that, you can decide what to do." Sounds fair enough. ] "There is one last piece of advice that I have for you. The orb of transference and the amulet it's set in are small and easily lost — it was designed to be easily smuggled or snuck into places, after all. I would suggest that you keep a tight hold on it before it happens to lose itself again; I don't fancy another eternity stuck all alone in this realm." "You don't have to wear it all the time, of course," Kiyoko continues. "But I think it'd also help you foster a deeper connection to this place... and me." "Now, I think we've both had enough for one meeting. I'm guessing you need to mull over what I've just told you, and on my part, I need to go look for those notes..." Rising from the water, her sodden amber hair and fur clinging to her slight curves, Kiyoko steps forward and gives you a hug. "Ah, I'd almost forgotten how nice it is to receive a hug. People are so warm... well, goodbye for now, [pc.name]. I'll see you around..." You wake with a start, breathing heavily. Now that was some dream. What should you do next, though? Kiyoko did say that she'd explain her idea to you the next time you visited her in your dreams, so there's that to look forward to. Maybe you ought to ask about it when you can... for now, though, you ought to get some more sleep."

rows.original: At the question, Kiyoko wiggles her large, furry ears, and her smile broadens just a little. "Why, there's one in front of you right now." Ha ha, very funny. She knows what you meant by the question, and you'd be much obliged if she would answer it. "All right, all right, no more evasions. I should've known better than to fool around." With a sigh, Kiyoko gathers up a bunch of her tails in her hands and wrings at the sodden fur. "We kitsune are the favored of the Living God Keros, also known as the Trickster God. As you can imagine, we bear his likeness." You nod. The ears and the tails, you presume. That much is as obvious to you. Can she continue? "My parents were of that number who were fairly prominent in my homeland — we just refer to it as the Old Country. I was brought up in the expectation that I would someday serve Keros, and I did. It was too good a deal to be passed up, really, or so I'm told." So all kitsune look like she does, you take it? "Why, is that meant to be a compliment?" She can take it to be, if she'd like. "Mm-hm. Well, our fur does come in different shades of color to match our hair." Kiyoko thinks a moment, then adds, "And generally, our number of tails show how mature we are and where we stand in Keros' favor. A newborn kit might have two, a child three, but after that, the number varies. As you can see, I currently have four on me. The greatest servants to Keros resemble the Trickster himself in having a whole nine tails." Do they get in the way? "I wouldn't know, I've never been without a tail in my life. But they're so good to pet and stroke and brush, especially when someone else does it for you." For a moment, Kiyoko looks past you into the distance, caught in the thrall of some distant memory before her attention returns to you once more. "What we really are under this skin is something far more animalistic — no, bestial, but couldn't that be said of all of us?" You see. Well, you don't think you have any more questions for her on this topic right now. Perhaps it's time to move the conversation along...
rows.translation: 听到这个问题，清子摇动了她那对又大又毛茸茸的耳朵，嘴角也微微上扬，露出了一丝笑容。 哦，其实现在就有一个就在你面前啊。 哈哈，真是太有趣了。她完全明白你这个问题的含义，如果她能回答的话，你一定会非常感激的。 好吧，好吧，别再逃避了。我本应该更明白事理，不该犯这种傻。 基约科叹了口气，将几条尾巴拢在手部中，用力拧了拧那些湿漉漉的毛。 我们这些狐族是生神凯罗斯的宠儿，他也被称为欺诈之神。可想而知，我们的外貌与祂十分相似。 你点了点头。那些耳朵和尾巴，你大概也明白吧？这些对你来说已经是很明显的事情了。她还能继续说下去吗？ 我的父母在我们家乡算是比较有地位的人——我们就把那个地方叫做‘旧国’。我从小就被教导，将来一定要为凯罗斯服务，而我确实这么做了。据说，这样的机会实在太好了，不容错过。 所以所有的狐妖都应该长得像她这样，你明白我的意思吧？ 哎，这算是夸奖吗？ 如果她愿意的话，她可以把这件事当作是理所当然的。 嗯，我们的毛色确实有不同深浅，这样就能与我们的毛发颜色相搭配了。 清子思考了一会儿，然后补充道： 一般来说，我们尾巴的数量能够反映我们的成熟程度，以及我们在凯罗斯麾下的地位。新生的生物可能只有两条尾巴，幼年个体则有三条，但之后这个数字就会发生变化。如你们所见，我现在一共有四条尾巴。而那些最忠于凯罗斯的生物，它们的尾巴数量甚至会达到九条，简直就像那个狡猾的戏弄者本人一样。 它们会妨碍行动吗？ 我也说不准呢，我这辈子从来都没有没有尾巴的日子。不过，这些尾巴真的非常适合让人抚摸、轻捏或者梳理，尤其是当有人帮忙来做这些事情的时候。 有那么一瞬间，清子将目光投向远方，似乎被某些遥远的回忆所吸引，但很快她的注意力又重新回到了你身上。 当我们脱去这层皮囊时，展现出来的其实是一种更为原始、更具动物性的本性——不，应该说是野性吧，但这种说法不也适用于我们所有人吗？ 你看，嗯，你现在应该不会再有关于这个话题的问题要问她了吧。也许是时候把谈话方向转移到其他事情上了……

rows.original: Just WHAT is a kitsune, anyways?
rows.translation: 那么，到底什么是狐妖呢？

rows.original: You'll admit to being curious. Here's someone who was actually involved in the Godswar, after all — could she elaborate on what she was doing up here so far away from her homeland? While Kiyoko did mention that the kitsune were here in an advisory position, you'd like to hear more details. No doubt she'd be a wealth of information on the subject. "Oh delicious fruit, what are you doing outside of my tummy? Let's fix that!" Reaching out for a slice of peach, Kiyoko dips it in the syrup and nibbles daintily as she speaks. "It feels like so long ago... it was so long ago. There were about sixty of us selected for the mission, two small dens' worth. While we tended to stay behind the front lines as Lumia's valkyries and Sorra's harpies did the brunt of the fighting, sometimes the Wraiths would take the fight to us. In such instances, we were usually prepared to defend ourselves, although none of the dens were found — up till that day." You nod and motion for her to go on. "We'd strategize, make suggestions, and go and do some sneaking around and spying when it was called for. For all their enthusiasm, Lumia and Sorra's followers weren't of any use at that. Too eager for direct confrontation, no subtlety at all." "There's nothing much to that, really. Since Keros told us to expect to be stationed there for a handful of years at the very least, we set about building accommodations for ourselves that reminded us of home. Those were guarded with the best illusory and misdirecting magics we could muster... we were confident that unless we wanted to be found, no one would ever find us. I guess that's what happened in the end; overconfidence is a slow and insidious killer." That all she has to say about the subject? The greatest conflict that Savarra had ever seen, and her involvement's condensed down to a couple of words? A shrug. "It's what it is. The greatest wars, told from the point of view of the rank and file, tends not to be glorious. Quite the opposite, in fact." [var0|That does raise the question, though. If she's been trapped in this pocket dimension for a long, long time, how does she know that the Godswar is over? "Like I told you, I'm able to vaguely discern the orb's immediate surroundings. Being stuck in a lightless, dusty corner for a long, long time gives one some sense of the passage of time outside — with the way the Godswar was going, a stalemate wasn't in the cards. That, and you speak of it in the past tense. It wasn't that much of a leap to field an educated guess that the war was indeed over, with the Seven victorious. If they hadn't, well, you wouldn't be here." Oh. Well, if you really wanted to be cynical about the whole thing, she could be trying to lull you into a false sense of security... "[pc.name], I'm not stupid, and neither are you. Attempting to deceive you would be utterly and completely not in my best interests whatsoever. Why would I want to throw away the only conversationalist I've had in a long, long time?" "Yes, I know Keros has a terrible reputation as a trickster god, but none of the Seven are squeaky clean and all hugs and kisses, either. I'm not going to ask you for a chance, but I will, given enough time, hopefully prove to you that I don't harbor ill will towards you." You'll see about that. ] Well, one way or another, it appears the conversation has come to an impasse. Perhaps you should move onto another topic...
rows.translation: 你得承认自己确实很好奇。毕竟，这里有一个人真正参与过“神战”——她能否详细说明自己为何会来到这么远离故乡的地方呢？虽然纪代子确实提到过那些狐族人只是以顾问的身份在这里，但你还是想了解更多细节。毫无疑问，她肯定能提供很多关于这个话题的信息。 哦，美味的果实啊，你们为什么不在我的肚子里呢？让我们把你们重新放回去吧！ 京子伸手拿了一片桃子，将其蘸入糖浆中，然后轻轻咬了一口，一边说着话。 感觉好像已经过去很久了 是 那是很久以前的事了。当时有大约六十人被选中执行这项任务，相当于两个小巢穴里的人数。虽然我们通常会待在前线后方，让卢米娅的英灵们和索拉的鹰女们去承担主要的战斗任务，但有时候那些幽灵也会主动向我们发起攻击。在这种情况下，我们通常是做好了防御准备的——直到那天之前，从来没有任何一个巢穴被找到过。 你点了点头，示意她继续说下去。 我们会制定策略，提出建议，在必要时还会暗中行动、进行间谍活动。尽管卢米娅和索拉的追随者们充满热情，但在这些事情上他们根本派不上用场——他们太急于直接对抗了，完全不懂如何运用策略和隐忍之道。 其实没什么特别的。既然凯洛斯告诉我们至少要在那里驻扎几年，我们就开始建造一些能让我们感受到家乡气息的住所。我们还用了我们所能掌握的所有迷惑和误导性的魔法来保护这些地方……我们相信，除非我们自己想让人找到我们，否则根本没人能找到我们。不过最终还是发生了我们预料中的事情；过度自信确实是一种缓慢而隐秘的杀手。 关于这个话题，她就只说了这些吗？萨瓦拉所见过的最激烈的冲突，而她的参与却被简化成短短几句话而已？ 她只是耸了耸肩。 事实就是如此。那些从普通士兵的角度来讲述的最伟大的战争，往往并不辉煌。事实上，恰恰相反。 [var0|那个 做 不过，这就引出了一个问题：如果她已经在这个口袋维度里被困了很长时间，她又是如何知道神战已经结束的呢？ 正如我之前所说，我能够隐约感知到那个光球周围的环境。在一片黑暗、充满灰尘的角落里被困了这么久，确实让人能够感受到外界时间的流逝——以神战目前的进展来看，僵局根本不可能出现。而且你用的也是过去时态来描述这件事。因此，我很容易就推测出，这场战争确实已经结束了，七方势力取得了胜利。如果他们没有获胜的话，你也不会在这里了。 哦，好吧，如果你真的想从消极的角度来看待这件事的话，她可能是想让你产生一种虚假的安全感…… "[pc.name]我并不傻，你也不是。试图欺骗你根本不符合我的任何利益。我为什么要放弃这么久以来唯一能与我进行正常交流的人呢？ 是的，我知道凯罗斯作为欺骗之神有着糟糕的名声，但七位神明中没有一个是真正清白的，他们也都不是什么纯洁善良的角色。我不会请求你给我一个机会，但我 会只要有足够的时间，我相信我一定能够向您证明，我并没有对您怀有任何恶意。 你就等着瞧吧。 ] 嗯，不管怎样，看来这次谈话已经陷入了僵局。或许你应该换个话题来谈……
rows.raw: " You'll admit to being curious. Here's someone who was actually involved in the Godswar, after all — could she elaborate on what she was doing up here so far away from her homeland? While Kiyoko did mention that the kitsune were here in an advisory position, you'd like to hear more details. No doubt she'd be a wealth of information on the subject. "Oh delicious fruit, what are you doing outside of my tummy? Let's fix that!" Reaching out for a slice of peach, Kiyoko dips it in the syrup and nibbles daintily as she speaks. "It feels like so long ago... it was so long ago. There were about sixty of us selected for the mission, two small dens' worth. While we tended to stay behind the front lines as Lumia's valkyries and Sorra's harpies did the brunt of the fighting, sometimes the Wraiths would take the fight to us. In such instances, we were usually prepared to defend ourselves, although none of the dens were found — up till that day." You nod and motion for her to go on. "We'd strategize, make suggestions, and go and do some sneaking around and spying when it was called for. For all their enthusiasm, Lumia and Sorra's followers weren't of any use at that. Too eager for direct confrontation, no subtlety at all." "There's nothing much to that, really. Since Keros told us to expect to be stationed there for a handful of years at the very least, we set about building accommodations for ourselves that reminded us of home. Those were guarded with the best illusory and misdirecting magics we could muster... we were confident that unless we wanted to be found, no one would ever find us. I guess that's what happened in the end; overconfidence is a slow and insidious killer." That all she has to say about the subject? The greatest conflict that Savarra had ever seen, and her involvement's condensed down to a couple of words? A shrug. "It's what it is. The greatest wars, told from the point of view of the rank and file, tends not to be glorious. Quite the opposite, in fact." [var0|That does raise the question, though. If she's been trapped in this pocket dimension for a long, long time, how does she know that the Godswar is over? "Like I told you, I'm able to vaguely discern the orb's immediate surroundings. Being stuck in a lightless, dusty corner for a long, long time gives one some sense of the passage of time outside — with the way the Godswar was going, a stalemate wasn't in the cards. That, and you speak of it in the past tense. It wasn't that much of a leap to field an educated guess that the war was indeed over, with the Seven victorious. If they hadn't, well, you wouldn't be here." Oh. Well, if you really wanted to be cynical about the whole thing, she could be trying to lull you into a false sense of security... "[pc.name], I'm not stupid, and neither are you. Attempting to deceive you would be utterly and completely not in my best interests whatsoever. Why would I want to throw away the only conversationalist I've had in a long, long time?" "Yes, I know Keros has a terrible reputation as a trickster god, but none of the Seven are squeaky clean and all hugs and kisses, either. I'm not going to ask you for a chance, but I will, given enough time, hopefully prove to you that I don't harbor ill will towards you." You'll see about that. ] Well, one way or another, it appears the conversation has come to an impasse. Perhaps you should move onto another topic..."

rows.original: What part did the kitsune play in the Godswar?
rows.translation: 在《神战》中，狐妖扮演了怎样的角色呢？
rows.raw: "What part did the kitsune play in the Godswar?"

rows.original: As pleasant a place as this so-called Astral Plane might be, you're pretty sure that spending all this time in solitude can't be healthy for one's state of mind. How's she been keeping herself from going crazy? "Tell me about it," Kiyoko replies, looking positively glum. "Oh, like you said, it's comfortable enough — whatever you might think of Keros, the Trickster does look after his own. He made sure that while we were holed up in Astral Planes, we'd want for nothing. I don't actually need to eat, but the business of obtaining, preparing and serving food helps to bring some structure to what passes for life here, helps keep me sane. I tried my hand at a bit of agriculture not too long ago, just for the fun of it." "I think you can understand just why I'm so glad to have someone to talk to." You can imagine. This might be a gilded cage, but it's a cage nonetheless; you're not entirely sure you'd have had the mental fortitude to go on for that long without any kind of contact with other people. She took up agriculture, she says? A nod. "And a whole host of other pastimes, from floral arrangements to folding paper cranes. After all, it's not time that I'm lacking. It was that without anyone else to judge my outcomes... in the end most of the efforts where I couldn't provide an objective measure of my improvement sort of began to fall apart. Let's just say there were a few trying times, and there was that." Trying times? Does she mean... "Can we not dwell on it? I know I don't want to." Wait wait wait. It's not as if you were the one who brought up the topic... look, can she tell you more about this Astral Plane? Kiyoko sighs, sinks a little lower beneath the water such that it's just her head above the water, and flattens her ears against her hair. "I think I've already told you much of what there's to tell, to be honest. You can wander away from the clearing here, and the forest just goes on forever. Kind of like an enchanted fairy-tale wood — there're plenty of glades and streams and you can explore as much as you want, but any time you want to return to the cabin it's but a short walk in any direction." "As for anything that you might need in the material sense, you'll just happen to stumble upon it. I got these —" she wiggles her ears at the sliced peaches — "off the bough. The knife ended up in a kitchen drawer where I was certain there'd been none. The same thing with the syrup, only on a shelf where there'd been only sugar the previous day." Day? You were under the impression that it was always morning around here. "It is. Until I'd like it to be evening, or night. Like I said, the Astral Plane is quite receptive to the wishes of any kitsune residing in it — to a limit, of course, but those are some pretty broad limits." It seems like quite the creation, if it can do all that just by reading her desires. Kiyoko exhales and smiles at you. "The Astral Plane was created by one of the Seven. I'm not surprised, really. Would you imagine a realm fashioned by a god to be anything less?" No, admittedly. Well, you think you've gotten the gist of what this little dream-land is all about; perhaps it's time to move the conversation on...
rows.translation: 尽管这个所谓的星界如此宜人，但你肯定知道，长时间独处对人的心理状态肯定没有好处。她究竟是怎么让自己没有发疯的呢？ 你倒是说说看吧。 清子回答道，脸上带着明显的忧郁神情。 哦，就像你说的，这里确实很舒适——无论你对凯罗斯有什么看法，这个骗子确实会照顾好自己的人。他确保了在我们躲在星界的时候，我们不会缺少任何东西。其实，我并不 需要 虽然只是为了填饱肚子，但获取、准备和提供食物这一系列活动，确实为这里的生活带来了一定的秩序，也帮助我保持了理智。不久前，我还尝试过从事一些农业活动，只是为了寻求其中的乐趣而已。 我想你应该能理解，为什么有人可以和我倾诉会让我感到如此开心。 你可以想象，这虽然可能是一个金笼子，但终究还是个笼子；你也不确定自己是否有足够的意志力，在完全不与他人接触的情况下坚持那么久。她说她开始从事农业了，是吗？ 点了点头。 还有各种各样其他的消遣活动，从插花到折纸鹤。毕竟，我并不缺时间。问题在于，没有其他人来评价我的成果……最终，那些那些我无法用客观标准来衡量自己进步程度的尝试，大多都半途而废了。可以说，确实经历了一些艰难的时刻。 遇到困难了吗？她的意思是…… 我们能不能别再讨论这个话题了？我知道我自己也不想继续谈。 等等等等，其实并不是你先提出这个话题的吧……听着，她能不能再跟你详细讲讲这个“星界”的事情呢？ 清子叹了口气，将身体再往水里沉了一些，只让头部露出水面，然后把耳朵贴在头发上。 说实话，我觉得我已经把该说的都告诉你了。你可以从这里离开这片空地，森林会一直延伸到远方。就像一个被施了魔法的童话世界——那里有许多小树林和溪流，你可以随心所欲地探索，但无论你想往哪个方向走，回到小屋都只需要走很短的距离而已。 至于你在物质上可能需要的任何东西，你总会偶然找到它们的。我买了这些—— 她看到那些切好的桃子，耳朵都动了起来 从树枝上掉下来的。那把刀最终出现在了一个厨房抽屉里，而我之前确信那里根本没有什么刀。糖浆也是同样的情况，它出现在了一个架子上，而前一天那里只有糖。 天啊？你原来以为这里永远都是早晨啊。 确实如此。只要我希望时间变成傍晚或夜晚，那就一定会成真。就像我之前说的，星界对于居住在那里的任何狐妖的愿望都相当敏感——当然，这也是有一定限度的，但这个限度其实相当宽泛。 如果它仅仅通过读取她的愿望就能做到这一切，那么这个创造物确实相当了不起。 清子呼出一口气，然后对你笑了笑。 这个星界是由七大存在之一创造的。其实我并不感到意外。试想，一个由神明创造的境界，怎么可能不是这样的呢？ 嗯，不得不承认，确实如此。你大概已经理解了这个梦幻世界的核心意义了吧；或许是时候继续讨论其他话题了……

rows.original: So, what exactly does she do all day, anyway?
rows.translation: 那么，她整天到底都在做些什么呢？
rows.raw: "So, what exactly does she do all day, anyway?"

rows.original: Well, then — perhaps she should start from the beginning. Just what exactly is this place? "This," Kiyoko begins, gesturing at your surroundings, "is what we kitsune call the Astral Plane. It's a... how should I put it? A different realm which belongs to Keros. The orbs of transference, one of which you now possess, were artifacts crafted by the trickster god to serve as gateways to his Dream. Each of the seven Living Gods possess a Dream, a realm of their shaping, and this so happens to be his." Okay. And you get here by sleeping? "That's one way to put it, I suppose. Like I said, this is going to be a long story — I understand that if I'm to earn your trust, I might as well lay everything out on the table from the get-go, right? The orbs of transference were weapons of a sort, created to serve in the Godswar. While the bulk of the fighting up in the north was conducted under the purview of Lumia and Sorra, the Trickster always prefers to have a finger in every pie — and every slice of every pie, if he can help it. I was amongst several dozen kitsune dispatched to this land in order to serve as auxiliary troops and advisors to the main fighting force, as well as to serve as Keros' eyes and ears." A weapon? Could she elaborate? "Of course. The Astral Plane itself is no weapon — indeed, it's quite the paradise, shaped to Keros' pleasing — but the ability to travel back and forth through it was a great strategic boon. A single orb of transference could hide an army; rolled into a crack, tossed over fortifications or smuggled in by a spy, an entire army of kitsune and their allies could emerge behind the enemy's defenses and lay waste to the Wraiths and their minions." "Usually, we don't enter the Astral Plane by falling asleep. But..." You expected as much; there's more to this story. "During our stay in the north, we kitsune had built a number of small bolt-holes. Just places for us to rest and perhaps give ourselves a small piece of home while in a foreign land, you see. One day — it seems so long ago — the bolt-hole I was staying in came under attack by a host of the Wraiths' minions. I'm not sure if they stumbled upon us or if we were discovered, but come they did, and we were completely unprepared and outnumbered." "While the others were caught by surprise, I... well, I'm not going to say it wasn't a cowardly thing to do, but I decided there wasn't any use in throwing my life away uselessly and attempted to escape into the Astral Plane. Which I did, just narrowly evading some kind of horrid spell one of the Wraiths' wizards had the mind to sling at me. Still, I made it, even if it was a long while before I dared to try heading back out through the orb once more." That does match up with the scene you saw back in the mural chamber, yes... the pottery shards, the blasted debris, the caved-in doorway. "Only I couldn't. Whatever the spell did to me while I was fleeing through the orb, I couldn't leave any more. Maybe it caught me at the last moment and killed my body, only leaving my spirit to flee to the Astral Plane. Maybe it did something to the magic of the orb, locking part of me inside. Maybe..." she shakes her head. "If there's no kitsune around to control things, time doesn't flow the same way in the Astral Plane. Sometimes it's faster, sometimes it's slower. I've had plenty of time to try many ways of getting out, but nothing that I can manage myself has worked. Effectively, I'm trapped. And all alone, too, until you came along." Hmm. If one has to be trapped, there are worse places to be stranded. This Astral Plane of hers is quite cozy, really. Kiyoko's expression darkens. "Trust me, being alone for so long is far from easy on the mind; it's great to finally have someone to talk to. There can be too much of a good thing, after all. I'm vaguely aware of things happening near the orb — such as being in a dusty corner for ages — but it's how I sensed you picking it up and making away with it." "We could talk here for hours, if you'd like — it's all a matter of perception, after all. Days could pass in the Astral Plane, and scarcely a few minutes would have passed where you're sleeping now." Well then. That gives you all the time you need to wrangle a few more explanations out of this foxy lady. What did you have in mind?
rows.translation: 那么，或许她应该从头开始讲起。具体该从哪里说起呢？ 正是如此 就是这个地方吗？ 这个。 清子开始说话了，她一边指着你周围的环境一边说着。 这就是我们狐妖族所称的‘星界’。可以说，它是属于凯罗斯的另一个领域。那些传送球，其中你现在就拥有一个，都是那位狡黠之神制造的法器，它们被用来作为通往他梦境的通道。七位生神每一位都拥有自己的梦境——那是他们所创造出来的领域，而这个梦境，恰好就是凯罗斯的。 好吧。那么你是通过睡觉来到这里的吗？ 我想，也可以这么说法。就像我之前说的，这个故事会很长很复杂——我明白，如果想赢得你们的信任，最好从一开始就把所有事情都讲清楚，对吧？那些传送球其实是一种武器，它们被创造出来就是为了在神战中使用。 虽然北方大部分的战斗都是在卢米娅和索拉的指挥下进行的，但那个狡猾的家伙总是喜欢插手每一件事——如果可能的话，甚至想参与到每一件事的每一个细节中。我也是被派往这片土地的几十只狐妖之一，我们的任务是作为主力部队的辅助力量和顾问，同时也为凯罗斯充当耳目和眼线。" 一件武器？她能详细说明一下吗？ 当然。星界本身并非武器——事实上，它简直就是一片天堂，完全符合凯罗斯的喜好——但能够在这片星界中自由穿梭，无疑为战略带来了巨大的优势。一个传送光球就能隐藏一支军队；如果将其滚进裂缝中，扔过防御工事，或者由间谍偷偷携带进去，那么一支由狐妖及其盟友组成的军队就能出现在敌人的防线后方，然后将那些幽灵及其爪牙彻底消灭。 通常，我们并不是通过入睡来进入星界的。但是…… 你早该料到；这件事还有更复杂的背景。 在我们住在北方的那段时间里，我们这些狐妖一族建造了许多小藏身处。这些地方只是让我们在异乡能够暂时休息，让自己感受到一丝家的温暖而已。有一天——虽然那似乎已经是很久以前的事了——我当时所在的那个藏身处遭到了那些幽灵仆从的袭击。我不确定他们是不小心发现了我们，还是我们自己被发现了，但总之他们来了，而我们完全没有任何准备，而且人数上也处于劣势。 虽然其他人都被吓了一跳，但我……嗯，我也不想说这样做不算懦弱，但我觉得没有必要白白送命，于是决定尝试逃往星界。我确实成功了，只是侥幸躲过了那些幽灵巫师们使出的可怕法术。不过，我还是花了很长时间才敢再次尝试通过那个光球返回人间。 这确实与你之前在壁画厅里看到的场景相符，没错……那些陶器碎片、被炸毁的残骸，以及坍塌的门口。 只有我没能成功。当我在那个光球中逃窜时，那个咒语一定对我做了什么，让我再也无法离开那里。也许它在最后一刻抓住了我，毁掉了我的肉体，只让我的灵魂逃到了星界。又或许它改变了那个光球的魔力，将我的一部分封印在了里面。也许…… 她摇了摇头。 如果没有狐妖在操控一切，那么在星界中时间的流逝方式就会不同。有时候时间会变快，有时候则会变慢。我花了很长时间尝试各种方法想要离开那里，但所有我自己尝试的方法都失败了。实际上，我被困住了……而且还是孤身一人，直到你的出现。 嗯，如果非得被困住的话，还有比这更糟糕的地方。她的这个星界空间其实还挺舒适的。 清子的表情变得阴沉起来。 相信我，长时间独处对心理来说绝对不是件容易的事；终于有人可以倾诉，真是太好了。毕竟，好事也可能过犹不及。我隐约感觉到在那个光球附近发生了一些事情——比如它被放在了一个积满灰尘的角落里很久——但正是通过这些线索，我才察觉到你拿走了它。 如果你愿意的话，我们可以在这里聊上几个小时——毕竟，这一切都取决于个人的感知方式。在星界中，几天可能会过去，而在你现在睡觉的地方，可能仅仅过了几分钟而已。 那好吧。这样你们就有足够的时间从这个狡猾的女士那里套出更多的解释了。你们到底打算做什么呢？
rows.raw: " Well, then — perhaps she should start from the beginning. Just what exactly is this place? "This," Kiyoko begins, gesturing at your surroundings, "is what we kitsune call the Astral Plane. It's a... how should I put it? A different realm which belongs to Keros. The orbs of transference, one of which you now possess, were artifacts crafted by the trickster god to serve as gateways to his Dream. Each of the seven Living Gods possess a Dream, a realm of their shaping, and this so happens to be his." Okay. And you get here by sleeping? "That's one way to put it, I suppose. Like I said, this is going to be a long story — I understand that if I'm to earn your trust, I might as well lay everything out on the table from the get-go, right? The orbs of transference were weapons of a sort, created to serve in the Godswar. While the bulk of the fighting up in the north was conducted under the purview of Lumia and Sorra, the Trickster always prefers to have a finger in every pie — and every slice of every pie, if he can help it. I was amongst several dozen kitsune dispatched to this land in order to serve as auxiliary troops and advisors to the main fighting force, as well as to serve as Keros' eyes and ears." A weapon? Could she elaborate? "Of course. The Astral Plane itself is no weapon — indeed, it's quite the paradise, shaped to Keros' pleasing — but the ability to travel back and forth through it was a great strategic boon. A single orb of transference could hide an army; rolled into a crack, tossed over fortifications or smuggled in by a spy, an entire army of kitsune and their allies could emerge behind the enemy's defenses and lay waste to the Wraiths and their minions." "Usually, we don't enter the Astral Plane by falling asleep. But..." You expected as much; there's more to this story. "During our stay in the north, we kitsune had built a number of small bolt-holes. Just places for us to rest and perhaps give ourselves a small piece of home while in a foreign land, you see. One day — it seems so long ago — the bolt-hole I was staying in came under attack by a host of the Wraiths' minions. I'm not sure if they stumbled upon us or if we were discovered, but come they did, and we were completely unprepared and outnumbered." "While the others were caught by surprise, I... well, I'm not going to say it wasn't a cowardly thing to do, but I decided there wasn't any use in throwing my life away uselessly and attempted to escape into the Astral Plane. Which I did, just narrowly evading some kind of horrid spell one of the Wraiths' wizards had the mind to sling at me. Still, I made it, even if it was a long while before I dared to try heading back out through the orb once more." That does match up with the scene you saw back in the mural chamber, yes... the pottery shards, the blasted debris, the caved-in doorway. "Only I couldn't. Whatever the spell did to me while I was fleeing through the orb, I couldn't leave any more. Maybe it caught me at the last moment and killed my body, only leaving my spirit to flee to the Astral Plane. Maybe it did something to the magic of the orb, locking part of me inside. Maybe..." she shakes her head. "If there's no kitsune around to control things, time doesn't flow the same way in the Astral Plane. Sometimes it's faster, sometimes it's slower. I've had plenty of time to try many ways of getting out, but nothing that I can manage myself has worked. Effectively, I'm trapped. And all alone, too, until you came along." Hmm. If one has to be trapped, there are worse places to be stranded. This Astral Plane of hers is quite cozy, really. Kiyoko's expression darkens. "Trust me, being alone for so long is far from easy on the mind; it's great to finally have someone to talk to. There can be too much of a good thing, after all. I'm vaguely aware of things happening near the orb — such as being in a dusty corner for ages — but it's how I sensed you picking it up and making away with it." "We could talk here for hours, if you'd like — it's all a matter of perception, after all. Days could pass in the Astral Plane, and scarcely a few minutes would have passed where you're sleeping now." Well then. That gives you all the time you need to wrangle a few more explanations out of this foxy lady. What did you have in mind?"

rows.original: When it comes to dreams, there're far worse things that could happen than getting into the baths with a foxy lady — and let's face it, you might be dreaming, but it'd be great to wash off the dust and grit of the Frost Marches, even if only in your mind. Quickly stripping off your [pc.armor], you lower yourself into the tepid waters and feel the heat massage your muscles and joints, gently melting away the stress of travel. On her part, Kiyoko keeps her eyes on your face and a small, pleasant smile on her lips[pc.cockRange 12 |, although you spy her gaze wandering over to your [pc.cockNoun] every now and then. Huh, wonder if she's one for size... who knows? There'll be a time and place for that, and it's not right now. |, her perky, fluffy ears twitching of their own accord as you make yourself at home. ] On your part, you get a rough view of Kiyoko's figure beneath the water's surface: a small bosom contrasted against a slight pair of hips — you get the impression that while the kitsune isn't a maiden or blushing virgin, neither does she appear old enough to be firmly ensconced within the role of mother. A young mother, perhaps — at any rate, she's very confident about the desirability of her body despite her lack of voluptuousness. It's hard to tell exactly where Kiyoko's hair ends and her fur begins, but the waterfall of orange-amber hair that cascades down her back comes up in front to frame her small nose, large jade eyes and welcoming smile in a pair of locks. Very attractive, perhaps, to those who prefer their women somewhat more slight in build, but then again, have you ever seen an ugly kitsune depicted anywhere? "I'd have added some lavender petals to the water, or perhaps some orange peel," Kiyoko quips as you settle in beneath the water's surface. "But I wanted to keep things light. Although a note for next time, since you couldn't have possibly known beforehand: you ought to scrub down before entering. There are other people in the water, after all." All right, then. Now that you've got yourself all nice and snug, maybe she could start with the explanations? Kiyoko nods, and her smile vanishes. "Immediately."
rows.translation: 说到梦境，其实还有比和一位性感的女士一起泡澡更糟糕的事情发生呢——说实话，你现在可能正处于梦境之中，但能够洗掉“霜冻荒原”带来的尘埃与污垢，哪怕只是在想象中，也是一件非常惬意的事情。快些脱掉你的 [pc.armor]你缓缓地将自己浸入温水之中，感受着温暖的水流轻柔地按摩着你的肌肉和关节，仿佛正在慢慢缓解旅途带来的疲惫。而清子则始终注视着你的脸庞，她的嘴唇上挂着一份愉悦而温柔的微笑。[pc.cockRange 12 |虽然你注意到她的目光不时转向你 [pc.cockNoun] 偶尔吧。嗯，不知道她是否喜欢按尺寸来选择……谁知道呢？总会有合适的时间和场合的，现在还不是时候。 |当你开始在这里安顿下来时，她那活泼可爱的绒毛耳朵会不由自主地动起来。 ] 从你的视角来看，你可以隐约看到水下的清子的身影：娇小的胸部与略微隆起的臀部形成对比——你会觉得，虽然这个狐妖既不是处女，也没有害羞羞怯的神情，但她看起来也不够年龄来承担母亲的角色。 或许她是一位年轻母亲——无论如何，尽管她并不拥有令人称羡的曲线美，但她对自己身体的吸引力充满信心。很难分辨清纪代子的头发究竟在何处结束，她的毛发又从哪里开始，但那倾泻而下、宛如橙琥珀般的秀发，既环绕着她的后颈，又在前方形成两道发帘，将她那小巧的鼻子、大而明亮的眼睛以及那充满亲切感的微笑衬托得格外动人。 对于那些喜欢女性体型较为纤瘦的人来说，这种设计或许很有吸引力。不过，你有没有见过任何被描绘得丑陋的狐妖呢？ 我本会在水中加入一些薰衣草花瓣，或者也许再放些橙皮。 当你潜入水底时，清子开了个玩笑。 但我本来想让气氛轻松一点。不过，作为一个提醒，因为你们之前肯定不知道这一点：在进入水里之前，应该先好好清洗身体。毕竟水里还有其他人。 好吧，那么。既然你已经准备好了，或许她可以开始解释了吧？ 清子点了点头，她的笑容也随之消失了。 立刻。

rows.original: Get into a hot spring with a foxy lady? Where do you sign up?
rows.translation: 和一位性感的女士一起泡温泉？该去哪里报名参加呢？
rows.raw: "Get into a hot spring with a foxy lady? Where do you sign up?"

rows.original: Perhaps it's just you being paranoid, but you don't quite trust the kitsune lady just yet. Finding a nice cool spot on the grass, you smooth it out and sit cross-legged on her level. Kiyoko tilts her head slightly to the side, then waggles a hand dismissively, spraying drops of water all over the spring's surface. "You'd rather not? As you will, then." No offense to her, but you don't feel like simply shedding your clothes and climbing into the spring with a foxy lady right this moment. There's a protocol to these things. A raised eyebrow, quickly replaced by a smile. "Would you like refreshments, then? I'm more than willing to share." Maybe just the explanation to begin with, if she would be so kind. "Straight down to business it is, then. I suppose I'd do the same if I were in your shoes."
rows.translation: 也许只是你多疑了，但你现在还是不太信任那位狐女。你在草地上找了一个舒适的地方，把草地弄平，然后盘腿坐下来，与她保持同一高度。清子微微侧头，随后随意地挥了挥手，水花四溅，洒在了泉水的表面。 你不愿意吗？那好吧，随你的便。 无意冒犯她，但你现在肯定没有心情脱掉衣服，和这位迷人的女士一起跳进温泉里吧。这类事情还是需要一定的礼仪和程序的。 她挑了挑眉毛，但很快又露出了微笑。 那么，您需要些点心吗？我非常乐意与您分享。 或许可以先从解释开始，如果她能这么慷慨的话。 那么，直接进入正题吧。我想如果我处在你的位置，也会做出同样的选择。

rows.original: With a sharp intake of breath, Kiyoko levers herself out of the rocking chair, planting both hands on the armrests and shaking away the last vestiges of sleep. [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4|Despite her baby bump, the kitsune mother has no problems getting to her feet. That slight frame of hers is deceptive — she has so much energy, it's practically pouring off her. |The sheer size and weight of her full, rounded belly makes the process a little awkward, but you lend a helping hand, and she's up and about in no time at all. ] She takes a few moments to smooth out her hair and fix the worst of her bedhead, then turns and gives you a small, formal bow. "Forgive my appearance, [pc.name]. I wouldn't have let myself go like this if I'd known you were coming to visit today." That's just fine. This slightly wild look suits her just as well as the carefully groomed one does, either way. She is a fox, one way or the other. Kiyoko tilts her head, as if not quite fully believing your words, then dismisses her worries with a nonchalant shrug and resuming her usual cheerful demeanor. "Well, let's not keep standing around here all day. The sun is nice, but I'd like to get inside — especially if you want to play." [kiyoko.pregStage 4|Oh? Does she want to play? "Oh yes." You don't think Kiyoko's aware of it, but the kitsune mother-to-be is biting her lower lip as her eyes dart around. I wasn't feeling it that badly when I dozed off, but since you were so kind to wake me up, I'm feeling positively frisky. I wouldn't mind it if we could have a little fun... maybe enjoy a game together..." You'll think about it. "Be careful, now." Kiyoko's lips part to show just the barest hint of pearly white, slightly pointed teeth. "Work me up too much, and I just might not be able to control myself. Who knows what I might do, then? Hee hee..." |Oh? Is she feeling frisky? Does she have — well, you can't exactly quite call it morning wood, but she knows what you mean. "Ma-aybe?" Kiyoko replies in a little sing-song voice. "You're free to do as you wish, of course, but I would really appreciate it if you could play some with me before you leave, [pc.name]. It's been a while; I want to play rough." ] Leaving her words hanging in the air, Kiyoko leads you on through the front door, down the hallway, and into the sitting room. You take a seat, then watch as the kitsune goes through the by now familiar motions of preparing the tea set and a small plate of candies. "Ah," Kiyoko murmurs with no small satisfaction as she pours herself a small cup of tea. Her large fox ears perk up as she raises the steaming liquid to her nose and takes a deep breath. "There's nothing quite like the bitter scent of tea after a long, warm nap. Now, [pc.name], shall we get started? How about I do something good to you today? Would you like that?"

rows.original:
It's a nice day, isn't it? Birds are singing, the sun is shining... days like these are just perfect, which is probably why Kiyoko tries to have such weather as much as possible. A perfect day for a visit, too... which is why you're here, isn't it? Stepping up onto the raised porch, you approach the cabin door and rap on it with your knuckles. However, there's no response, and you're about to give it another go when a soft snore from around the corner draws your attention.

    That sounds familiar... 
    
    Crossing over to investigate the source of the snoring, you don't have long to go before you find Kiyoko slumped in a rocking chair, smack in the middle of a large pool of sunlight. The kitsune mother is sound asleep, nestled securely in the chair's soft cushioning and her own many tails; the sunlight illuminates her soft features and the faint smile on her lips. The poor thing clearly hasn't brushed her hair or fur in a bit, and snuggling up in the rocking chair has only mussed up the lot even more.
    
    Come to think of it, it must be nice to nap in the warm sun on a cool day... 
    
    Back and forth, back and forth, the gentle creaking of the rocking chair on the floorboards as Kiyoko dozes away, her hands [kiyoko.pregStage 0 2 4
    |folded across her chest, her head bent to one side.
    |in front of her, cradling the growing swell of her pregnant tummy, hugging it to herself as if to make the fox kit — and herself — a little more secure while she snoozes.
    |resting atop the massive mound of her pregnancy. The front of Kiyoko's yukata is undone, allowing her bare belly to spill out of her clothes and onto her lap where it soaks up the warm sunshine; the open halves are loosely draped over the kitsune mother's milk-swollen breasts, barely covering her nipples — the outline of which are clearly still visible against the sinfully thin fabric.
    ] Every now and then, Kiyoko murmurs something in her sleep, and her large, fluffy ears twitch ever so slightly. There's a book lying on the floor beside her — she must have read herself to sleep, dropping the book to the ground when she finally nodded off.
    
    She seems so content to nap like this... but you wanted to visit, didn't you? How do you want to wake up this fluffy mommy?
rows.translation:
今天真是美好的一天，不是吗？鸟儿在歌唱，阳光明媚……这样的日子简直完美无缺，也许正因如此，清子才会尽量让这样的天气多出现一些。今天也是适合出门游玩的完美日子……所以你才会来到这里，对吧？ 走上那扇高高的门廊，你走到小屋门前，用指关节敲了敲门。然而，没有任何回应。就在你准备再敲一次的时候，从拐角处传来了轻微的鼾声，吸引了你的注意。

    这听起来有点耳熟……

当你走过去调查那阵鼾声的来源时，没过多久你就发现了静子——她瘫坐在一把摇椅里，正好处于一大片阳光的照射范围内。这位狐妖母亲正沉沉地睡着，她的身体被椅子柔软的靠垫以及自己那许多尾巴牢牢地支撑着；阳光照亮了她那柔和的面容，以及她嘴唇上那淡淡的微笑。 那可怜的小家伙显然已经有一段时间没有梳理自己的毛发了，而蜷缩在摇椅里只会让情况变得更加凌乱。

仔细想想，在一个凉爽的日子里，躺在温暖的阳光下小睡一会儿，肯定是一件非常惬意的事情。来来回回，来回来回，摇椅在木地板上发出的轻柔吱嘎声中，清子渐渐进入了梦乡，她的双手部…… [kiyoko.pregStage 0 2 4

rows.original: Smiling, you reach for Kiyoko's shoulder and take a firm grip before gently nudging her a few times. She really is a deep sleeper — your first few attempts only get you soft murmurs and ear twitches, but you work at it. She must be used to being prodded from both inside and out by now, after all, and the pool of sunlight is starting to make even you slightly drowsy...
