这种声音效果简直棒极了，远比你们两个人单独努力所能取得的效果要好得多；树叶沙沙作响，空气在向夜色中扩散时仿佛也在闪烁。你的牙齿会打颤，骨头也会发出咯咯声，但这种强烈的回声很快就会消失，留下一种清醒的感觉在你的脑海中，尽管你的身体还在抗议着这一切。 又来？ 当然。再次强调。 砰…… 两个人一起动手部，反而更容易控制节奏，大家有节奏地敲击木块与青铜器，以此迎接新年的到来。拍板撞击钟面时传来的震动既有力又令人感到宁静，这种力量感为整个仪式增添了一种庄严的氛围。 清子也确实是在全力以赴呢。[kiyoko.pregStage 2|尽管她明显已经怀孕了。]你很少看到她公开流汗，但此刻，尽管夜风清凉，她柔软的皮肤上还是冒出了汗珠。从她脸上的笑容来看，她似乎很享受这个过程……当然，这也难怪。这么多年来，她究竟有多少年是没有与任何人见面的呢？ 砰…… 最后的那一击带着一种决绝的意味，震撼着你的心灵。在那一刻，你甚至已经感觉不到自己的存在了，更不用说自己应该有多疲惫了；此刻你唯一感受到的，就是一种强烈的成就感——因为你终于松开了手部中的鼓槌，让你的那位狡猾的朋友落入了你的怀抱。 没错，这样确实比独自行动有趣多了。 看， [pc.name]," 清子在你怀里喃喃自语。 我们刚好在新年之前完成了工作，一点都不迟。 她说得对。当你转过身，从清子的肩膀后面望去，会看到地平线上浮现出一抹暗淡的琥珀色光芒，那光芒逐渐升上树梢，温暖的气息开始弥漫在这个小小的维度之中。你那可爱的朋友紧紧依偎在你身边，她的毛茸茸的身体散发着温暖，她的颜色与初升的太阳简直一模一样…… ……哈，新年快乐。 也祝你新年快乐， [pc.name]." ] 没错，新年才刚开始几分钟，情况就已经在好转了。 虽然我很希望你能多留一段时间，但我想这是不可能的，对吧？毕竟，你还有很多事情需要去做。 她是在赶你走吗？因为听起来她确实是这么做的。 不，不是的。只是想提醒你，不要过于沉迷于当下的时刻。今天我玩得很开心， [pc.name]……但这个世界上还有许多其他事物需要你的关注。毕竟，我并不想占用你所有的时间，你还有其他人需要和他们一起度过这一天，对吧？ 嗯…… 现在别争论了，快去吧。 还没等你来得及抗议，清子就凑过来，轻轻地在你的嘴唇上吻了一下，只是非常短暂的一触而已。 欢迎你下次再来拜访，好吗？ [kiyoko.numKits 1|哎呀！欢迎你们下次再来拜访哦！ 你叹了口气，又轻轻拍了拍绮奴的耳朵。有了这么早熟的女儿，你怎能不这样做呢？ ]
rows.raw: " "Well, there's a little ritual I'd like to introduce you to," Kiyoko says, a twinkle in her eye. "If you wouldn't mind?" A ritual, eh? Oh, you know she's up to something when she's got that mischievous air about her. Guess you don't mind playing along; you know that your foxy friend here would never mean you any actual harm. "Right. Follow me, please." [kiyoko.numKits 1||[pc.isChamp|You hesitate for a moment, turning back to the dirty dishes under the parasol table. She can't just leave them here, right? Then again, you're also smart enough to not break the mood — dirty dishes can be taken care of anytime, but new years' eve only comes once a year. Kiyoko's already started off at a brisk pace, and you have to jog a little to catch up with her before she starts wondering just where you've gone. ] ] The two of you eventually come to the forest's edge, a little way past the fence that marks the end of the peach orchard. You'd never noticed it before — and unsurprisingly so, considering how well hidden it is — but there's a little gazebo-like structure planted squarely on the border between civilization and wilderness. Hanging from rust-flecked chains are a huge bell and a clapper the size and length of a tree trunk; the bell itself is huge, ancient, and covered with all sorts of carvings and patches of greenish patina. "It's one of the first things I ordered the Astral Plane to fashion after I came here, a small piece of the home I lived in as a girl a long time ago. I have no way of being sure, of course, but... I'd like to think it's a pretty faithful replica." You look bell and clapper alike and give the former a rap with your knuckles. Solid bronze, indeed. So, you take it that you're supposed to ring the bell? Kiyoko nods and smiles. "A hundred and eight times, to be precise. One for each of the proscribed mental states which Lord Keros warns leads to unwholesome actions." Unwholesome actions... that's one way of putting it. A hundred and eight times... that's quite a few. [pc.toughnessRange 70|Not that you aren't going to welcome the challenge — if nothing else, it'll be a good exercise in pacing yourself.] "I'll help you, of course. No one said you were doing this alone." [pc.toughnessRange 70 |While you don't think you need the help, this'll be a lot more meaningful with two people instead of one. |Ah, right. It'll be a lot easier with two people instead of one. ] Did she use to do this a lot in the past? "During my captivity? Not so much; there wasn't a reason to observe the new year when time simply blended into a blur, one day flowing into the next like the one that came before it. Before that, though, when I was a girl in the old country... haha, three or four of us would be clamouring to have a go at the clapper under my mother's watchful eye." Sniffling a little, Kiyoko wipes a stray tear from her cheek. "It was a small wonder we ever managed to finish ringing it before the sun came up." ... "Come, now. Shall we get started?" Of course. Stepping over to the large wooden clapper, you take it under an arm and test its weight. This sure is some solid wood, and the chains, though flecked with rust, look sturdy enough. Kiyoko steps back and observes you closely as you take a deep breath to steel yourself, draw back the clapper, and send it crashing into the large bronze bell with all your might. Bong... The sound rings out through the air and out to the forest, loud and clear despite the bell's age. It resonates in your bones, bounces about in your head, and eventually leaves you, but not without leaving you feeling thoroughly rattled — but oddly enough, in a good way. By the time the last echo finally fades, you're tingling from head to toe as if you'd just been zapped with a burst of static. A small smattering of applause. "Not bad, [pc.name]. One hundred and seven more times to go, then." Phew... It's hard at first, especially when you need to stop and recover from the tremendous, clarion ringing each time, but eventually both your muscles and skull get used to it and it's not so bad by the twentieth or so strike of the bell. [pc.toughnessRange 70 |While you don't feel that out of sorts, Kiyoko insists that she take over the job after the forty-second strike and let you rest for a bit before coming back to it. The set of her face and her folded arms strongly suggest that she's not taking no for an answer. |By the forty-second strike, you're starting to feel it in your joints, and Kiyoko offers to take over for a while and let you rest a bit. It's a small mercy you eagerly accept, and you let her have it all to herself while you shake out your shoulders and waist. ] There's a nice mossy beam to one side where you can get a good view of the proceedings, and it's this you lean against while watching Kiyoko go at it. Despite being small and slight, your foxy [kiyoko.numKits 1|lover|friend]'s clearly no stranger to this; where she lacks in strength, she makes up for in technique, moving her body with the natural flow of the clapper as she strikes the bell over and over again. Kiyoko's natural wiggliness and flexibility as a kitsune comes in handy as she leverages her body weight into the equation. "Sixty-three, sixty-four, sixty-five. Phew. It's your turn once more, [pc.name]." Oh, already? She looked like she was having so much fun there. "Oh, I was, no doubt about that. However, as you're the guest tonight, it's important for you to get the best experience you can out of the ceremonies." Ha, since she put it so nicely, you guess you don't have a choice... [kiyoko.numKits 1|Just as you're about to get up and reclaim your old spot, though, you spy a small figure cresting the hilltop in the moonlight. It's not hard to recognize your firstborn daughter at a distance, not when her silvery-white hair and fur glimmer like that when the moonbeams strike them. Coming to a stop just before the gazebo, Kinu announces her presence by way of coughing gently, and gives both Kiyoko and you a small bow. Now, what is she doing here? "Ehe... well, [pc.PapaMama], Mama, I put away the dirty dishes from the new years' soba like you wanted, then I [kiyoko.numKits 2|set everyone else to sleep|made my nightly prayers] like I was supposed to. I'm not sleepy, though, so..." "...So you want to stay up all night with us and watch the sunrise?" Kinu contrives to look adorably sheepish. "That, and I wanna help bang the big bell, too. I'm old enough this year!" You look between the bell clapper, practically the size of a tree trunk, then back at Kinu. Is she sure about that? "Of course I wouldn't be doing it alone, [pc.PapaMama]. With both Mama and you around, it wouldn't be any more dangerous than handling my practice naginata." Kiyoko taps her chin. "Hmm. What do you say, love?" Well, it's only once a year, so if she's grown-up enough to not doze off she's more than welcome to join you. There're only about forty more strikes of the bell to go, and you get the feeling that things would be a lot more fun if you did this as a family. So long as you watch Kinu carefully to ensure that no accidents happen, it should be all right. So it comes to pass that the three of you arrange yourselves about the clapper as a family, with you in front, Kiyoko behind, and Kinu sandwiched between you two. Once more, you draw back the clapper by its chains and strike the bell with all your might. Bong... Kinu squeals, the sound equal parts fear and exhilaration, but your kitsune daughter keeps a tight hold on the clapper itself with her little hands. Bong... Kiyoko sure is putting her back into it, too[kiyoko.pregStage 2|, despite how obviously pregnant she is]. You don't often see her openly sweat, but there it is, beads forming on her soft skin despite the cool night air. Judging by the smile on her face, she's enjoying herself... but who wouldn't, surrounded by family like this? How many years have passed by without her seeing anyone? Bong. Has it been a hundred and eight tolls of the bell already? It doesn't feel like it — [pc.toughnessRange 70|you're still plenty energetic as it is|all that activity was far less tiring than you thought it would be]. But neither your foxy wife nor your fluffy daughter are revving up the clapper for another strike, so it must be over. You wipe the sweat from your brow, take a few deep breaths, and contemplate the matter in silence. Sure, it was a lot of hard work, and this isn't part of your own culture... but by being here with Kiyoko and Kinu, there's no doubt it's been worth your while. Kinu squirms up against you and tugs at your [pc.armor]. "Look, [pc.PapaMama], look! We made it just in time for the first sunrise of the new year!" She's not wrong. From where you stand, you can see a dull orange glow cresting the treetops, slowly pushing away the inky darkness of the starry night sky. As you watch, transfixed, Kiyoko comes up to your side and melts against your shoulder, draping herself on you with a smile. "Happy new year, [pc.name]. May it be a successful and prosperous one for you." The same for her — and of course, Kinu as well. You reach down and find the spot on Kinu's brow where she likes to be petted, then plant the heel of your palm squarely on it while chasing her ears with your fingers. |"It's just the last stretch; I have perfect confidence in your ability to finish up all one hundred and eight strikes." Well, instead of you taking over wholesale, why don't the two of you ring the bell together? It'd be more fun that way. "Hmm?" So long as it's not dangerous, why not? It's just the last stretch, isn't it? You came here to spend time with your foxy friend here, after all; this'll be better than just staring at each other taking turns at the clapper, right? Kiyoko makes a show of considering the prospect, planting a finger on her chin as she pretends to think deeply. Then, with a small smile, "I guess it can't hurt." So it comes to pass that the both of you return to the bell once more with you taking the front while Kiyoko backs you up from the rear. Affirming your grip on the heavy wooden clapper, the both of you draw it back on its chains and thrust forward to strike the bell cleanly. Bong... The sound is brilliant, far stronger than either of you could possibly have managed on your own; leaves rustle and the air itself shimmers as it travels outward into the night. Your teeth chatter and bones rattle, but the powerful reverberation soon passes, leaving a sense of clarity in the fore of your mind despite your body's protestations. "Again?" Of course. Again. Bong... With two people instead of one, you're far better able to pace yourselves, wood striking bronze at a steady pace to herald the arrival of the new year. The thump the clapper makes against your shoulder as it hits the bell is powerful yet calming, its sense of power lending a solemn air to the proceedings. Kiyoko sure is putting her back into it, too[kiyoko.pregStage 2|, despite how obviously pregnant she is]. You don't often see her openly sweat, but there it is, beads forming on her soft skin despite the cool night air. Judging by the smile on her face, she's enjoying herself... but of course. How many years have passed by without her seeing anyone? Bong... The last strike rings true with a distinctive note of finality, shaking you to the core. At this point, you can't even feel very much of yourself, let alone feel how tired you ought to be; all you're experiencing right now is a strong sense of self-satisfaction as you finally let go of the clapper and let your foxy friend fall into your embrace. Yes, that was much more fun than just going it alone. "Look, [pc.name]," Kiyoko mumbles in your arms. "We finished just in time for the new year, and not a moment too soon." She's right. Making a half-turn and looking over Kiyoko's shoulder, you spy a dull amber glow coming up upon the horizon, cresting the treetops as warmth begins to pour out over this little pocket dimension. Your foxy friend is warm and fluffy against you, and she's not that different a color as the sunrise... ... Ha. Happy new year. "Happy new year to you too, [pc.name]." ] Yep, it's been only a few minutes into the new year, and things are looking up already. "As much as I'd like you to stay longer, I suppose that's not possible, is it? After all, you still have much to do out there." Is she chasing you off? Because it sounds like she's chasing you off. "No, no. Just reminding you not to get too caught up in the moment. I had fun today, [pc.name]... but there's also a whole world out there which requires your attention. I wouldn't want to monopolize your time, after all, and there're other people you need to spend this day with, aren't there?" Well... "Don't argue now. Off you go." Before you can protest, Kiyoko leans in and smooches you lightly on the lips, just the briefest of pecks. "Come visit again soon, okay?" [kiyoko.numKits 1|"Eeee! Come visit again!" You sigh and pet Kinu's ears again. With such a precocious daughter, how could you not? ]"

rows.original: You step up onto the raised porch, making a beeline for the cabin door, but don't get that far. It opens outwards of its own accord, revealing Kiyoko framed in the entrance doorway. The kitsune gives you an elegant, formal bow, and smiles. "Excellent timing, [pc.name]. I'd foreseen your visit today, of course, but even so arriving neither too early nor too late is an art that is hard to perfect." Hey, usually it's you who arrives at the door first, not her. What's the big occasion? "[kiyoko.numKits 1 2|Kinu and I are|The kits and I are|I'm] celebrating the new year today. I'd be honored if you chose to join [kiyoko.numKits 1|us|me] in ushering in yet another year to come." Hmm. No doubt she's seen many, many years during her captivity in this gilded prison of hers. Does she do this every year, or...? Kiyoko's smile turns a little sad, the corners of her eyes crinkling. "Not... not that much before. It seemed rather hollow... half the point of celebrations is other people, after all. But now..." Ah, right. Of course you'll join in the festivities with her[kiyoko.numKits 1 2| and Kinu| and the children]. You take Kiyoko's hand in yours, and let her guide you through the door, down the hallway and to [kiyoko.numKits 0 1 2|the cabin's kitchen. Kiyoko's left a pot of noodle soup over a low fire to simmer, and even at this distance the slightly salty smell is rather appetising. |the cabin's kitchen. Kinu is standing on a stool with a wooden spoon, stirring a steaming pot of noodle soup; as you enter, she sets down the spoon, turns to you and bows deeply, clearly trying not to giggle. "Welcome, [pc.PapaMama]. It's so good that you could join us today." Ah, such a good kid. Hmm, isn't it a little dangerous for her to be tending to the cooking alone, though? Kiyoko gives you a reassuring pat on the shoulder. "Were it any other kit, yes. But you and I know our daughter is perfectly capable of handling herself." |a large dining hall. There, your children are patiently waiting at their tables; they rise and give you a bow as you enter. Up atop a low stove, a large cauldron of steaming noodle soup simmers over a muted fire, spreading a wondrous smell over the entire room. Kinu's tending to the cauldron, stirring the enormous batch of noodle broth with a long ladle and looking very pleased with herself. "That'll do," Kiyoko says, clapping her hands. As one, your children — with the exception of Kinu, of course — take their seats and await to be served. "Now that everyone's here, I think we can begin." ] With that said, Kiyoko steps up to the stove and takes a whiff of the aroma rising from the broth. "Ah, hot soba. It truly brings back memories..." Memories she'd care to share with you? Despite all this time you've been together, she hasn't really gone into her childhood in that much detail. A wan smile. "Maybe in the future. Not today, at least." All right. [kiyoko.numKits 0 1 2|Humming a gentle tune to herself, Kiyoko upends the pot into two bowls, then adds a little garnish in the form of sliced spring onions and dried shrimp. Like the kitsune herself, there's something elegant in the dish's simplicity, in her careful movements as she sets the steaming bowls on a tray and snuffs out the fire with a snap of her fingers. "Shall we eat outside? It's too nice a night to be indoors." |While your daughter prepares a garnish of sliced spring onions and dried shrimp, Kiyoko takes the steaming pot and upends its steaming contents into three bowls, humming a merry tune all the while. The way mother and daughter work together like this... it's just like the dish they're preparing, elegant and simple. "All done!" With a little flourish, Kinu sprinkles the garnishes atop the thick noodles in their light brown broth, then sets the bowls one by one on a tray. Your daughter looks up at the two of you with her big ice-blue eyes, clearly seeking approval, then squeals and squirms as she receives it in the form of headpats. Kiyoko pauses a moment as if lost in thought, her lip trembling, then snuffs out the cooking fire with a snap of her fingers and picks up the tray. "I think we should eat outside, [pc.name]; it's too fine a night to spend it indoors. Could you help clean up before coming out to join us, Kinu? Your [pc.mf|father|mother] and I would like to be alone for a little while. I promise I won't touch your share." "O-of course." |Stepping up to the cauldron, Kiyoko relieves Kinu from her post, then picks up the ladle. One by one, your kitsune children come up to their mother and are served large bowls of soba noodles, to which Kinu adds a garnish of spring onions and dried shrimp from large bins off to the side. It's an elegant, orderly affair — no doubt the fluffy kits have been warned to be on their best behavior for the day. When the last of the kits have been served and are seated, they look expectantly to Kiyoko. "Thank you for the food, Mama." "Of course. Please, begin." As your children pick up their chopsticks and get to work, Kiyoko snuffs out the cooking fire with a snap of her fingers and portions out the last of the soba noodles onto a tray — just enough for you, her, and Kinu. "I think we should eat outside, [pc.name]; it's too fine a night to spend it indoors. Could you help clean up and take care of your siblings before coming out to join us, Kinu? Your [pc.mf|father|mother] and I would like to be alone for a little while. I promise I won't touch your share." Your firstborn daughter gives the two of you a sheepish grin. "Sure, if that's what you'd like..." ] Nodding, Kiyoko picks up the tray and leads you back out of the cabin and down the path to the hilltop. Day's turned to night while you were indoors, but the gentle light of stone lanterns illuminates the path down to where the outdoor parasols are located. "Just enough time for the noodles to cool just right," Kiyoko remarks as she sets down the tray. "And just enough time for us to have a pleasant dalliance under the moonlight. I'm curious, [pc.name] — how did you observe the passing of the new year yourself?" [pc.bg noblescion courtesan minstrel|Ah, well... surely it couldn't have been that long since you came to the Marches, but you do remember the festivals in the heartland cities to the south. Big affairs, often funded by the local lord or lady with stalls lining the streets and establishments staying open till the crack of dawn. People bustling in the streets and brightly colored lanterns festooned all over the place. They were good times.[pc.bg minstrel| Of course, since you were a minstrel, it was just another workday, more haranguing than most. Festivals are never festivals for those doing the entertaining.][pc.bg noblescion| As one of the local nobility, you never lacked for anything during the festival... but here and now, sitting here with Kiyoko, you're feeling the moment far more keenly than any amount of carousal could have brought you.] ] [pc.bg soldier|Mostly being thankful for living out another year. Casualties were high in the life you led, and every year you'd see more and more of your fellow soldiers succumb to either injury or the sheer stresses of bloodshed day in, day out. The lucky ones were able to return home with perhaps a missing limb or couple of fingers; the less fortunate ended up burning in a mass grave. With Tira staring one in the face every day, simply being alive to usher in the new year was cause for celebration on what meager pay you had. ] [pc.bg hunter barbarian|Plenty of revelry and singing with the clan, that's for sure. You remember that the clan elders would break out the moonshine they'd been putting away for the entirety of the year, and everyone would gather by the bonfire's light to prepare the next year's batch while getting roaringly drunk. Even the children would be given some of the stuff after it'd been appropriately watered down — the new years' moonshine was strong, if nothing else. There'd be stories told, of course — after all these years, the tale of the moon-eating bear's one that's inexplicably stuck in your memory. The clan didn't have much in the way of material comforts those in the cities could afford, but it more than made up for it with the sheer intensity of the people participating in the celebrations. ] [pc.bg arcanist scholar acolyte|An evening of quiet repose and meditation, usually[pc.bg acolyte| followed by prayer to one or more of the Seven]. Your studies set you apart from society at large, and the revelries of new years' celebrations were often either too distant or simply didn't hold that much appeal to you. Going out into the streets of town and getting smashed with strangers just didn't seem meaningful at the time; you'd rather have spent the occasion with people you actually had meaningful relationships with. ] [pc.bg slumrat|Festivities? They were an opportunity to make a quick coin or two, whether it be from begging or less wholesome activities. Life was hard, and happiness and revelry was for other people; those were days you're glad to have left behind and never want to look back on again. ] Kiyoko listens to your recollections in silence, then heaves a little sigh when you're done. "Well, one way or the other, I'm really glad you remembered to come today. You did come because you remembered, right?" Um — Before you can reply, though, Kiyoko raises a finger to her lips and smiles. "It's okay. I'm just happy you're here with me tonight. Come on, let's have the toshikoshi soba before it gets too cold." Of course, of course... no matter how many times you try to use these sticks for eating, you can never quite get used to them. Broth and noodles alike are lukewarm by this point, and the two of you savour them in silence under the thin moonlight, a gentle breeze blowing in from the forest. Like Kiyoko herself, the food is simple and homely, evoking a strange sentiment of longing in your heart. Speaking of longing... hey, these noodles are really long... "They're made that way to symbolise long life," Kiyoko says with a small laugh, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails curling about herself. "Seven gods, I've lived long enough, or at least it feels that way." She looks pretty good for someone who's broken her second century. Why, she doesn't look a day over fifty. Kiyoko just giggles and shakes her head. Hmm... you still feel a little clumsy with these foreign utensils, but you manage to pick up a small portion of dried shrimp and hold it out in front of Kiyoko's face. Her ears wiggle and twitch as she realizes what you're doing, and your kitsune [kiyoko.fucked|wife|companion]'s cheeks color faintly. "Ehehe, I don't know, [pc.name]... I'll feel kinda embarrassed if you feed me..." Nonsense. You've known her [kiyoko.fucked|in the most intimate, carnal fashion now.| well enough to be out here celebrating the new year with her.] There's absolutely no reason for her to get all bashful over something as simple as you feeding her. Kiyoko looks askance, a small grin set in her face. "All right, all right." There's a good fluffy girl. Say aaaah. "Aaaah." Leaning forward, Kiyoko bites the shrimp off your chopsticks, then settles back, chewing. [kiyoko.numKits 1|"Eehee, that's so cute. [pc.PapaMama] and Mama feeding each other like a newlywed couple." A pair of large white ears peeks out from under the table, followed by the rest of Kinu as your firstborn daughter clambers up onto the seat between the two of you. Without waiting any further, she picks out her bowl of soba noodles and starts slurping away at a prodigious pace. "I'm soooo hungry." S-she saw everything? Kiyoko just shrugs and smiles. "I think it's better for our daughter that she sees her parents have a good relationship, don't you agree?" Well, when she puts it like that... "It's not so often that we get to do things together, [pc.name]. Let's set this aside and enjoy the moment, shall we? It is, after all, the beginning of a new year." Yeah... you pat Kinu between her ears, and your daughter wiggles in place while she continues emptying the bowl. Bit by bit, the food gradually disappears, and eventually there're three empty bowls on the tray. "Ehe, [pc.PapaMama], Mama, thanks for taking good care of me for the past year. I'll do my best in the coming year, too!" Kiyoko just smiles weakly and wipes the cold sweat off her brow. "Look, Kinu, even if we're expecting you, could you please make some noise the next time you show up like that?" "O-okay. I know you and [pc.PapaMama] want some alone time... I won't get in your way, okay? I'll just stay up and wait for the sunrise. I'll even bring back the dishes, so why don't the two of you have fun and play with each other?" "Wait!" Before Kiyoko can say anything else, though, Kinu's already run off with the tray in her hands, a small silhouette rapidly disappearing down the cabin path. "That girl... she's such a handful at times." Kinu was right, though. Didn't she want some alone time with you? What did she have in mind? |How's it taste? "Well, I did the cooking..." But it tastes better than she'd have expected, because you're here with her. "Hah." Kiyoko punches you lightly on the shoulder and chuckles. "Now it's my turn to feed you. Say aaaah." But of course. Aaaah. Giggling, Kiyoko winds an impossibly long strand of soba about a chopstick like thread on a spindle, and pops it into your mouth. You bite it off, chew, and consider flavor and texture alike. It's not quite like any other cereal you've ever tasted before — there's a clear, foreign difference compared to wheat — but Kiyoko can make anything taste good. You could get used to this. "Ehehehe. You look so adorable like this, [pc.name]." Do you, now? "Yep!" Hah. Either way, this is kind of nice. A moonlit sky, a table, just the two of you and some alone time... before you know it, you've finished off the soba noodles and set the dirty dishes back on the tray. That was really pleasant. What's next? ]
rows.translation: 你走上那扇凸出的门廊，径直走向小屋的门，但还没走多远，门就自动打开了——站在门口的，正是被门框映衬得格外清晰的清子。那只狐妖向你优雅地鞠了一躬，然后露出了微笑。 时机把握得真好， [pc.name]我当然预料到了你今天会来，但即便如此，做到既不早到也不迟到，也确实是一门很难掌握的技艺。 嘿，通常都是你先到门口的，而不是她。这次是什么特别的情况吗？ rows.raw: " You step up onto the raised porch, making a beeline for the cabin door, but don't get that far. It opens outwards of its own accord, revealing Kiyoko framed in the entrance doorway. The kitsune gives you an elegant, formal bow, and smiles. "Excellent timing, [pc.name]. I'd foreseen your visit today, of course, but even so arriving neither too early nor too late is an art that is hard to perfect." Hey, usually it's you who arrives at the door first, not her. What's the big occasion? "[kiyoko.numKits 1 2|Kinu and I are|The kits and I are|I'm] celebrating the new year today. I'd be honored if you chose to join [kiyoko.numKits 1|us|me] in ushering in yet another year to come." Hmm. No doubt she's seen many, many years during her captivity in this gilded prison of hers. Does she do this every year, or...? Kiyoko's smile turns a little sad, the corners of her eyes crinkling. "Not... not that much before. It seemed rather hollow... half the point of celebrations is other people, after all. But now..." Ah, right. Of course you'll join in the festivities with her[kiyoko.numKits 1 2| and Kinu| and the children]. You take Kiyoko's hand in yours, and let her guide you through the door, down the hallway and to [kiyoko.numKits 0 1 2|the cabin's kitchen. Kiyoko's left a pot of noodle soup over a low fire to simmer, and even at this distance the slightly salty smell is rather appetising. |the cabin's kitchen. Kinu is standing on a stool with a wooden spoon, stirring a steaming pot of noodle soup; as you enter, she sets down the spoon, turns to you and bows deeply, clearly trying not to giggle. "Welcome, [pc.PapaMama]. It's so good that you could join us today." Ah, such a good kid. Hmm, isn't it a little dangerous for her to be tending to the cooking alone, though? Kiyoko gives you a reassuring pat on the shoulder. "Were it any other kit, yes. But you and I know our daughter is perfectly capable of handling herself." |a large dining hall. There, your children are patiently waiting at their tables; they rise and give you a bow as you enter. Up atop a low stove, a large cauldron of steaming noodle soup simmers over a muted fire, spreading a wondrous smell over the entire room. Kinu's tending to the cauldron, stirring the enormous batch of noodle broth with a long ladle and looking very pleased with herself. "That'll do," Kiyoko says, clapping her hands. As one, your children — with the exception of Kinu, of course — take their seats and await to be served. "Now that everyone's here, I think we can begin." ] With that said, Kiyoko steps up to the stove and takes a whiff of the aroma rising from the broth. "Ah, hot soba. It truly brings back memories..." Memories she'd care to share with you? Despite all this time you've been together, she hasn't really gone into her childhood in that much detail. A wan smile. "Maybe in the future. Not today, at least." All right. Like the kitsune herself, there's something elegant in the dish's simplicity, in her careful movements as she sets the steaming bowls on a tray and snuffs out the fire with a snap of her fingers. "Shall we eat outside? With a little flourish, Kinu sprinkles the garnishes atop the thick noodles in their light brown broth, then sets the bowls one by one on a tray. Your daughter looks up at the two of you with her big ice-blue eyes, clearly seeking approval, then squeals and squirms as she receives it in the form of headpats. "I think we should eat outside, [pc.name]; it's too fine a night to spend it indoors. Could you help clean up before coming out to join us, Kinu? "O-of course." |Stepping up to the cauldron, Kiyoko relieves Kinu from her post, then picks up the ladle. One by one, your kitsune children come up to their mother and are served large bowls of soba noodles, to which Kinu adds a garnish of spring onions and dried shrimp from large bins off to the side. It's an elegant, orderly affair — no doubt the fluffy kits have been warned to be on their best behavior for the day. When the last of the kits have been served and are seated, they look expectantly to Kiyoko. "Thank you for the food, Mama." "Of course. Please, begin." As your children pick up their chopsticks and get to work, Kiyoko snuffs out the cooking fire with a snap of her fingers and portions out the last of the soba noodles onto a tray — just enough for you, her, and Kinu. "I think we should eat outside, [pc.name]; it's too fine a night to spend it indoors. Could you help clean up and take care of your siblings before coming out to join us, Kinu? Your [pc.mf|father|mother] and I would like to be alone for a little while. I promise I won't touch your share." Your firstborn daughter gives the two of you a sheepish grin. rows.translation: 你的手还未碰到门，门就“砰”的一声打开了，清子本人几乎是从门口冲出来，直接扑进了你的怀里。 "[pc.name]你来了！ 哇，哇，哇，哇。发生了什么大事吗？你并不是反对她见到你时这么兴奋，但是不是发生了什么事情呢？ 也许你可以自己想明白。 清子调皮地朝你眨了眨眼，同时把拥抱弄得更紧了一些。 你注意到我有什么特别的地方吗？ 嗯。 [pc.isDK|也许只是你这么觉得，但她的胸部紧贴着你的方式 [pc.skin] 它们不一样；它们给人的感觉更加……宽敞。它们的尺寸变大了吗？ 清子撅起了嘴。 "[pc.name]!" 嗯，其实 是 确实如此，不是吗？她真的正在很好地适应母亲的角色，不是吗？ 那只狐妖的脸上浮现出一丝红晕。 嗯，没错，这一点确实是真的。不过， 那个 这并不是我期望你能注意到的变化…… |你伸长脖子，想看看抱着你的那只狐妖，从而仔细观察清子。嘿，她的屁股似乎有点大了些，髋部也稍微宽了一些……但这种变化实在微乎其微，大概只是轻型线造成的错觉吧。再说，就算真的有变化 是 在这种情况下，你不会认为那就是她如此兴奋的原因吧。 ] 不，说实话。 清子撅了撅嘴，但很快就又高兴起来。 成功了！也就是说，那种精华转移的方法真的有效。 嗯，好吧，恭喜你吧？ 不，不。这些荣誉应该属于你，而不是我。我只不过是你们用来传递这些荣誉的载体罢了。 气 你的生命活力确实比任何人都更加强烈，能够收到你这样的馈赠，对我来说是一种荣幸。 但这并不是我想告诉你们的主要内容。 [pc.name]你对我一直非常友善，我希望能报答这份善意。现在你已经将你的一部分物质本质赋予了我，我相信我可以在短时间内将自己投射到这个轻型球之外，就像我在开始这项尝试时告诉你的那样。 哦？她确定吗？ 我……我已经试过几次了。虽然持续时间不长，但那些现象出现的时间足够我帮助你们作战了。其实，我也不会真正 是 那里，就算我摔倒了，也可以轻易地退回星界的安全之地。你们不必担心我的安危。 啊，你明白的。但她真的确定自己想这么做吗？ 为什么不呢？如果我能帮你清除前进道路上的障碍，你就能更快地把我送到凯罗斯那里，让我重获自由。而且，你总是来找我玩，还会送我各种礼物 气, [pc.name]作为回报，我会努力让自己变得有用！虽然…… 嗯，是吗？ 清子露出了甜美的微笑。 ……如果我表现得好，我就希望得到更多的表扬和宠爱！ 哈！嗯，现在你完全可以做这件事。当你走到菊子的面前，轻轻挠她的耳朵时，她的尾巴都会开心地摇个不停，那只狐妖还会开心地靠在你身上，发出满足的叹息。 好了好了，真是个乖女孩。 现在，这件事应该不会再有任何问题了。只要通过那个护身符联系我，我就会来帮忙的，不过我只能偶尔才能抽空去做这件事。 好的，你明白我的意思了。 现在既然 那就是 结束了…… 清子说着，从你身边走开，然后轻轻地向你行了一个正式的鞠躬。 ……欢迎回来， [pc.name]我想你了。我们进去安顿下来吧？ 你以为她永远不会问吧！在这里门廊上站了这么久，你的腿都快麻掉了。 笑声。 好吧，好吧，我们进去吧。 就这样，清子带你走进小屋，来到了那熟悉的客厅。你带着温暖的微笑，看着她一一完成准备茶点和糖果这些日常动作。 那么，你今天想做什么呢？ 从现在开始，你可以在战斗中使用“团结护符”来召唤清子协助你作战。不过，每次战斗中只能使用这一次。
rows.raw: " Scarcely has your hand come into contact with the door than it flies open with a bang, Kiyoko herself practically gushing out of the doorway and into your arms. "[pc.name]! You're here!" Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa. What's the big event? You're not against her being this excited to see you, but did something happen? "Perhaps you can figure it out for yourself." Kiyoko winks at you playfully as she tightens her hug against you. "Notice something about me?" Hmm. [pc.isDK|Maybe it's just you, but the way her breasts are pushing against your [pc.skin] are different; they feel more... ample. Did they get bigger? Kiyoko pouts. "[pc.name]!" Well, it is true, isn't it? She's quite literally growing into motherhood well, isn't she? A trace of color creeps into the kitsune's face. "Well, yes, that much is true. Still, that wasn't the change I was hoping you'd notice..." |You crane your head about the kitsune hugging you and try to get a good look at Kiyoko. Hey, her butt's a little bigger, her hips ever so slightly wider... but the change is so slight, it's probably a trick of the light or something. Besides, even if it were the case, you don't think that's what she's so excited about. ] No, to be honest. Kiyoko pouts, but brightens up again in no time. "It worked! The essence transfer, that is." Um. Well. Congratulations? "No, no. The honors are yours, not mine. I am only the receptacle you poured your chi into... there's something about your life energy that's far more intense than that of anyone else, and it's an honor to be able to receive such a gift from you. "But this isn't the main thrust of what I wish to tell you, [pc.name]. You've been very kind to me, and I wish to repay that kindness. Now that you've gifted me with a bit of your physical essence, I believe I can manifest a projection of myself outside of the orb for a short period of time, like what I told you at the outset of this endeavor." Oh? She's sure? "I... I have tried it a few times. It won't be for long, but the duration of the manifestation will be enough for me to, say, aid you in battle. Neither will I actually be there, so should I fall, I can easily retreat to the safety of the Astral Plane. You needn't worry about my safety." Ah, you understand. But is she sure she wants to do this? "Why not? If I can clear obstacles from your path, the sooner you can get me to Keros and my freedom. Besides, you always come to play with me and gift me your chi, [pc.name]; as repayment, I'll work hard to be useful! Although..." Hmm, yes? Kiyoko smiles sweetly. "...If I do well, I want to be praised and petted some more!" Hah! Well, that's something you can do plenty of right now. All of Kiyoko's tails wag happily as you step up to her and give her a good set of ear scritches, the kitsune leaning in against you with a happy sigh of blissful contentment. There, there. There's a good girl. "Now, there shouldn't be any problems with this. Simply call me through the amulet and I'll come to help, although I can only do it so often." All right, you understand. "Now that that's over with..." Kiyoko says, pulling away from you and giving you a small, formal bow. "...Welcome back, [pc.name]. I missed you. Shall we go in and get settled down?" You thought she'd never ask! You're getting pins and needles in your legs from standing out here on the porch for so long. Laughter. "All right, all right. Let's head on in." With that, Kiyoko leads you through the cabin to the familiarity of the sitting room, and you watch with a fond smile as she goes through the ritual motions of setting out the tea and candies. "So then, what do you want to do today?" From now on, you may use the amulet of union in combat to summon Kiyoko to aid you in a fight as a combat summon. This can only be done once every encounter."

rows.original: As you crest the hill, you're greeted by a familiar shape making a beeline for you at a run. Kinu's short little legs are a blur as she scampers up to you, all three of her tails flowing behind her. Finally coming to a stop by grabbing onto one of your legs, your fluffy daughter pants and sags against you, taking a moment to catch her breath. "Thank the gods I managed to catch you before you made it indoors, [pc.PapaMama]. You might have ruined everything otherwise!" Whoa whoa whoa whoa. Rewind that a moment — what was it that you would've ruined? "Oh! Ehe. Well..." Kinu looks pensive for a second or two, putting her index fingers together and twiddling them as she ponders how best to phrase her words. "Um, today is Mother's Day, you know?" That's... well, you don't really know when that happens in kitsune culture, nor do you have a solid grasp on how time flows in here compared to the waking world. Let's just say you'll take her word for it — what then? "Well... [kiyoko.numKits 2|the other kits and ]I have prepared something pretty neat for her, you know! [kiyoko.numKits 2|We|I]'d just like you to join in and keep it a secret if you can, [pc.PapaMama]!" A surprise for her mother to recognize all the effort she puts into raising them, eh? You can't say you disapprove. It's good that Kinu knows how to show gratitude for all the good things Kiyoko has showered upon her. "Eh..." [kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0 |Your daughter's smile fades, replaced by a more serious expression. "I'm only doing what's expected of me as her daughter and heir apparent, that's all. The customs and rites demand as much of me as the firstborn, no more, no less." Hey, why the sudden coldness? She's taking so much responsibility for getting all this together for her mother, and at such a young age, too. "All this? I haven't told you what I had in mind, [pc.PapaMama]." Oh no, she hasn't, but since it's her you know it's going to be good. You have that much trust in her. Kinu sniffs and looks away. "Thanks, [pc.PapaMama]." |Your daughter's smile grows even bigger and brighter. "That's really flattering... I really want to do the best I can for Mama, that's all. She works so hard to raise [kiyoko.numKits 2|us|me] right." Even so, she seems so happy about it. Well, you can't complain about your daughter being on good terms with her mother — here's to hoping it stays that way for a long time to come. Kiyoko must truly mean a lot to her for her to go all this way to preparing a surprise... "Oh? I don't remember telling you what I had in mind. How do you know it's big, [pc.PapaMama]?" With her, you can expect nothing less. "Ehe... you're making me blush..." ] You smile and pat Kinu on the head, which causes your fluffy daughter to squirm appropriately under your touch. All right... what does she need you to do, besides stay out of the way? "We'll be ready in about an hour. I just need you to distract Mama for that long, and lead her to the dining [kiyoko.numKits 8|hall|room] when that time's up. Can you do that for us, [pc.PapaMama]?" Haa... distracting Kiyoko... you can think up a few ideas. All right, she can leave it to you, then. "All right, then, I'll leave it to you!" Kinu bows, and before you know it, she's off as fast as her short little legs can take her, rapidly becoming a dot on the far side of the hill.
rows.translation: 当你爬上山顶时，一个熟悉的身影正飞快地向你奔来。绮奴那短短的小腿在奔跑中一闪而逝，它的三条尾巴在身后摇摆着。终于，它抓住你的一条腿停了下来，那身毛茸茸的身子靠在你身上，喘着粗气休息了一会儿。 谢天谢地，我在你进入室内之前及时抓住了你。 [pc.PapaMama]否则，你可能会毁掉一切！ 哇哦，等一下——你刚才说是要毁掉什么来着？ 哦！呃，嗯…… 纪奈沉思了一两秒，将食指并拢在一起，轻轻捻动着，思考着该如何最好地表达自己的意思。 嗯，今天是母亲节，你知道吗？ 那个嘛……其实你并不清楚在狐族的文化中，这种事情究竟会在什么时候发生；同时，你也不太清楚在这里，时间流逝的规律与现实世界相比有何不同。那么，我们就姑且相信她的说法吧——之后又会怎样呢？ 嗯…… [kiyoko.numKits 2|其他套件以及 ]你知道吗，我为她准备了一些相当不错的东西！ [kiyoko.numKits 2|我们|我]我只是希望你能加入进来，并且如果可能的话，帮忙保密这个秘密。 [pc.PapaMama]!" 对她母亲来说，能够认识到她为养育孩子们所付出的所有努力，真是一件令人惊喜的事情，对吧？你总不能说你不赞同这一点。好在绮奴懂得如何感激清子给予她的所有帮助与关爱。 呃…… [kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0 |你女儿的笑容消失了，取而代之的是一种更加严肃的表情。 我只不过是在履行作为一个女儿和法定继承人所应尽的责任而已。传统和习俗要求我这样做，作为长子/长女，我本就应该如此，没有更多，也没有更少。 嘿，怎么突然变得这么冷淡了呢？她这么年轻，却要承担这么多责任，为她的母亲安排这一切，真是太不容易了。 所有这些？我其实还没告诉你们我到底有什么打算 [pc.PapaMama]." 哦不，她还没准备好，但既然是她，你知道结果肯定不会差。你对她就是这么有信心。 绮奴哼了一声，然后把目光移开了。 谢谢， [pc.PapaMama]." |你女儿的笑容变得更加灿烂、更加甜美了。 这真是太让我感动了……我真的很想为妈妈尽自己最大的努力，仅此而已。她为了抚养我们付出了那么多努力。 [kiyoko.numKits 2|我们|我] 没错。 即便如此，她看起来还是非常开心。嗯，你总不能抱怨自己的女儿和母亲关系这么好吧——希望这种关系能长久保持下去。对清子来说，她肯定非常重要，否则她也不会费心准备这样的惊喜…… 哦？我不记得告诉过你我的想法是什么。你是怎么知道它很大的呢？ [pc.PapaMama]?" 有了她，你就别指望会有什么不好的事情发生。 呵呵……你让我都脸红了…… ] 你微笑着拍了拍基努的脑袋，这让你的毛茸茸的女儿在你触碰下忍不住扭动起来。好吧……除了别妨碍她之外，她还需要你做些什么呢？ 我们大约一个小时后就能准备好了。现在我只需要你在这段时间里帮我们分散妈妈的注意力，把她引到餐厅去。 [kiyoko.numKits 8|大厅|房间] 当时间到了的时候，你能为我们做这件事吗？ [pc.PapaMama]?" 哈……让纪代子分心了……你可以想出一些点子来。好吧，那这件事就交给你吧。 好吧，那这件事就交给你来处理吧！ 纪奈鞠了一躬，然后转眼间，她就以自己那双短小的腿跑得飞快，很快就变成了远处山丘上一个小点。

rows.original: Well, this should be interesting. As always, you step up to the cabin in the shade of the cherry blossom tree, knock on the door, and wait. It isn't long before the familiar sound of Kiyoko's footsteps approaches, and the door swings open; your foxy wife gives you a small [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4 |incline of her head as she greets you with her usual elegance. Laden with a kit-swollen belly, she sure is getting in the spirit of the day whether she knows or not of the surprise Kinu's got planned for her. |nod in greeting, remaining as refined as ever despite her immensely gravid condition. What timing... if Kinu's going to be organising a mother's day celebration today for her, she looks every bit the part. |bow, graceful as ever in her greeting. Looks like she doesn't suspect a thing as to what your daughter's up to. ] "Welcome, [pc.name]," she says in that lovely, lilting voice of hers, ears folding forward. "I'm glad you are able to visit today, it's always a pleasure to receive you. Before we begin, though..." Yes? "Have you seen [kiyoko.numKits 2|the children|Kinu] anywhere? I haven't caught glimpse of head or tail of [kiyoko.numKits 2|them|her] since breakfast, and it's a little concerning.[kiyoko.numKits 8 32 | Usually there're enough of our sons and daughters around that I can always spot one of them if I look hard enough, but it's like they all emptied out of the house and vanished. | I... there's always at least one of them around. Always. And now that there's absolutely no one in the house, I can feel the difference. It's... not a good feeling. ] You wouldn't happen to know where [kiyoko.numKits 2|they've|she's] gone, do you?" No, you don't know where [kiyoko.numKits 2|everyone|Kinu]'s gone off to. Did [kiyoko.numKits 2|they leave their|she leave her] tasks undone before running off to play? Kiyoko frowns. "No... I checked and the chores were all done, and far too early for them to have been completed after breakfast. My ears were twitching when I woke up this morning... I've lived long enough to be able to tell when someone's poised to play a prank on me." Well, maybe she shouldn't worry too much. The Astral Plane will keep [kiyoko.numKits 2|the kits|Kinu] safe; for the moment, she shouldn't allow this to spoil your visit. Your fox-wife tilts her head ever so slightly to the side, a calculating look in her jade-green eyes; [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4 |unthinkingly, her hands wander over to the ripening curves of her pregnant tummy, running over its taut surface |instinctively, her hands wander over to her kit-stuffed tummy and she drums on its full, taut surface with her fingertips as she thinks |they shift from side to side as she chews on her lip, clearly not quite convinced of the whole situation ]. At last, though, she sighs and takes you by the arm, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails sweeping against you as she ushers you into the house. "I guess I'll find out what they're up to eventually. Come along then, [pc.name] — let us make the most of our time together." By now, it's almost a ritual in its own right; she leads you to the sitting room, serves the tea and candies, then the two of you settle in for pleasant conversation. Considering all the excitement that goes on in the waking world, the homely atmosphere is a nice change of pace; Kiyoko is a pleasant and efficient conversationalist as always, and time sure flies when you're talking to her... [kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0 |"I wish you were around a little more for Kinu's upbringing," she tells you over a steaming cup of bitter tea. "Don't get me wrong, I know you're here as much as you can be, but sometimes handling her can get rather tiring." Is your daughter causing trouble? "Not trouble as you might call it... more irritation than anything. I don't know why, but she just seems to resent me. Always nosing around the edges, pushing at the boundaries of what's acceptable, testing the limits of my patience. Never anything outright unfilial, but I know passive-aggression when I see it. Doesn't fool me one bit." Well, there's a positive side to it, isn't there? By doing this, isn't Kinu learning to think for herself and becoming independent? She can't take care of her daughter forever, after all, and the more self-sufficient Kinu becomes, the more she'll able to [kiyoko.numKits 4|help shoulder the burden of raising her siblings|stretch her own wings without looking to her mother for guidance]. Kiyoko snorts, her fine features creasing. "Oh, it isn't that. She just wants to aggravate me, I think. Besides... a mother's task is to prepare her children for the day they will no longer need her. After that, I should hope my kits will still want me. One can be independent without going against her mother for no good or apparent reason." |"I wish you were present more often for Kinu's upbringing," Kiyoko informs you over a cup of steaming, bitter tea. "While I know you visit as often as you can, you're missing so many of the little moments that make me smile. They're good on their own, of course, but... it would be nice if you could share in them, too." Kinu's growing up well, isn't she? "Our daughter is almost everything I could ask for, really, so long as that mischievous streak of hers doesn't get out of hand. Refined, elegant, obedient — it's almost scary how much I see of my younger self in her." Well, she is her mother's daughter, after all. Besides, it reflects well on Kiyoko that she's managed to raise such a flawless daughter. "Oh, come now, I wouldn't call Kinu flawless; she can get a little lazy at times. That kind of thinking only serves to swell one's head. But despite that... I do believe that I've done quite a good job, yes." ] How long has it been since the both of you settled down together? An hour? More? Kinu's words prod at your mind... hopefully you haven't held up the proceedings. "Is something the matter, [pc.name]?" Yes. Come to think of it, you'd appreciate it greatly if she could let you taste some more of her lovely cooking. "Oh, don't flatter me..." You grin and cross over to Kiyoko's side of the table, taking her by the shoulders and helping her to her feet. [kiyoko.pregStage 1 3 |Your kitsune wife squirms and fusses in your grasp, but deigns to allow you to set her upright. "Come on, now. I'm not so pregnant that I can't stand up on my own." Well, she can think of it as more for your benefit than it is for hers. "Ehehe." Kiyoko falls in pace at your side. "I suppose." Playful, isn't she? |Her big belly makes it a little harder than it ought to be, but the weight is something she's used to at this point. "Aah, thank you," your kitsune wife sighs as she settles into a waddle at your side. rows.raw: " Well, this should be interesting. As always, you step up to the cabin in the shade of the cherry blossom tree, knock on the door, and wait. It isn't long before the familiar sound of Kiyoko's footsteps approaches, and the door swings open; your foxy wife gives you a small [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4 |incline of her head as she greets you with her usual elegance. Laden with a kit-swollen belly, she sure is getting in the spirit of the day whether she knows or not of the surprise Kinu's got planned for her. |nod in greeting, remaining as refined as ever despite her immensely gravid condition. What timing... if Kinu's going to be organising a mother's day celebration today for her, she looks every bit the part. |bow, graceful as ever in her greeting. Looks like she doesn't suspect a thing as to what your daughter's up to. ] "Welcome, [pc.name]," she says in that lovely, lilting voice of hers, ears folding forward. "I'm glad you are able to visit today, it's always a pleasure to receive you. Before we begin, though..." Yes? "Have you seen [kiyoko.numKits 2|the children|Kinu] anywhere? I haven't caught glimpse of head or tail of [kiyoko.numKits 2|them|her] since breakfast, and it's a little concerning.[kiyoko.numKits 8 32 | Usually there're enough of our sons and daughters around that I can always spot one of them if I look hard enough, but it's like they all emptied out of the house and vanished. | I... there's always at least one of them around. Always. And now that there's absolutely no one in the house, I can feel the difference. It's... not a good feeling. ] You wouldn't happen to know where [kiyoko.numKits 2|they've|she's] gone, do you?" No, you don't know where [kiyoko.numKits 2|everyone|Kinu]'s gone off to. Did [kiyoko.numKits 2|they leave their|she leave her] tasks undone before running off to play? Kiyoko frowns. "No... I checked and the chores were all done, and far too early for them to have been completed after breakfast. My ears were twitching when I woke up this morning... I've lived long enough to be able to tell when someone's poised to play a prank on me." Well, maybe she shouldn't worry too much. The Astral Plane will keep [kiyoko.numKits 2|the kits|Kinu] safe; for the moment, she shouldn't allow this to spoil your visit. Your fox-wife tilts her head ever so slightly to the side, a calculating look in her jade-green eyes; [kiyoko.pregStage 2 4 |unthinkingly, her hands wander over to the ripening curves of her pregnant tummy, running over its taut surface |instinctively, her hands wander over to her kit-stuffed tummy and she drums on its full, taut surface with her fingertips as she thinks |they shift from side to side as she chews on her lip, clearly not quite convinced of the whole situation ]. At last, though, she sighs and takes you by the arm, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails sweeping against you as she ushers you into the house. "I guess I'll find out what they're up to eventually. Come along then, [pc.name] — let us make the most of our time together." By now, it's almost a ritual in its own right; she leads you to the sitting room, serves the tea and candies, then the two of you settle in for pleasant conversation. Considering all the excitement that goes on in the waking world, the homely atmosphere is a nice change of pace; Kiyoko is a pleasant and efficient conversationalist as always, and time sure flies when you're talking to her... [kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0 |"I wish you were around a little more for Kinu's upbringing," she tells you over a steaming cup of bitter tea. "Don't get me wrong, I know you're here as much as you can be, but sometimes handling her can get rather tiring." Is your daughter causing trouble? "Not trouble as you might call it... more irritation than anything. I don't know why, but she just seems to resent me. Always nosing around the edges, pushing at the boundaries of what's acceptable, testing the limits of my patience. Never anything outright unfilial, but I know passive-aggression when I see it. Doesn't fool me one bit." Well, there's a positive side to it, isn't there? By doing this, isn't Kinu learning to think for herself and becoming independent? She can't take care of her daughter forever, after all, and the more self-sufficient Kinu becomes, the more she'll able to [kiyoko.numKits 4|help shoulder the burden of raising her siblings|stretch her own wings without looking to her mother for guidance]. Kiyoko snorts, her fine features creasing. "Oh, it isn't that. She just wants to aggravate me, I think. Besides... a mother's task is to prepare her children for the day they will no longer need her. After that, I should hope my kits will still want me. One can be independent without going against her mother for no good or apparent reason." |"I wish you were present more often for Kinu's upbringing," Kiyoko informs you over a cup of steaming, bitter tea. "While I know you visit as often as you can, you're missing so many of the little moments that make me smile. They're good on their own, of course, but... it would be nice if you could share in them, too." Kinu's growing up well, isn't she? "Our daughter is almost everything I could ask for, really, so long as that mischievous streak of hers doesn't get out of hand. Refined, elegant, obedient — it's almost scary how much I see of my younger self in her." Well, she is her mother's daughter, after all. Besides, it reflects well on Kiyoko that she's managed to raise such a flawless daughter. "Oh, come now, I wouldn't call Kinu flawless; she can get a little lazy at times. That kind of thinking only serves to swell one's head. But despite that... I do believe that I've done quite a good job, yes." ] How long has it been since the both of you settled down together? An hour? More? Kinu's words prod at your mind... hopefully you haven't held up the proceedings. "Is something the matter, [pc.name]?" Yes. Come to think of it, you'd appreciate it greatly if she could let you taste some more of her lovely cooking. "Oh, don't flatter me..." You grin and cross over to Kiyoko's side of the table, taking her by the shoulders and helping her to her feet. [kiyoko.pregStage 1 3 |Your kitsune wife squirms and fusses in your grasp, but deigns to allow you to set her upright. "Come on, now. I'm not so pregnant that I can't stand up on my own." Well, she can think of it as more for your benefit than it is for hers. "Ehehe." Kiyoko falls in pace at your side. "I suppose." Playful, isn't she? |Her big belly makes it a little harder than it ought to be, but the weight is something she's used to at this point. "Aah, thank you," your kitsune wife sighs as she settles into a waddle at your side. Hey, you put that big, healthy kit inside of her belly; it's the least you can do to help her around. |Your kitsune wife fusses a little at being pampered, playfully batting at you with her tails, but accepts the help and settles into a slow trot beside you. Frisky, isn't she? ] Come on, it's time to go. "You'd like to come along?" You won't deny it, watching her at work is a sight for sore eyes. There's just something about an elegant, cultured [kiyoko.pregStage 1|— and above all, pregnant — ]woman expertly preparing food that's calming to the nerves. "If you say so, my dear. If you say so.""

rows.original: Out of the sitting room, down the hallway to the back of the tree. It's just silence, your footsteps echoing down across wood the only sounds as you approach the entrance to the dining [kiyoko.numKits 8|hall|room]. It gets to the point where you wonder if Kinu was playing a prank on you, if there's going to be nothing waiting for you when you arrive — — Such doubts are pushed aside when you push aside the screen door and step in. There, [kiyoko.numKits 2 8 16 32 |Kinu stands at the fore of the table facing the door, bowing deeply as the two of you enter. Her siblings are seated at the table, fidgeting a little but otherwise well-behaved for the occasion. Small as she might be, Kinu has summoned up all the gravitas and solemnity her eight-year-old self can muster, as befits her position as firstborn daughter — a miniature majordomo to her mother. |Kinu stands at the fore of the head table, bowing deeply as the two of you enter. She's positioned all of her numerous siblings at the other tables, already set and waiting your arrival; they follow their eldest sister's lead in greeting the two of you. Being able to wrangle her naturally mischievous siblings like that... sheesh, your little daughter feels a lot more grown-up already, even if she doesn't look it at all. |a small army of foxen floofs stand to greet you, seated at the numerous tables laid out along the walls. Seeing all these kits... did you really impregnate Kiyoko that many times? Sure, you've seen your kits running around here and there, but for them to all be in the same place... Kiyoko certainly deserves to be honored here. Kinu stands at the fore of the head table, bowing deeply as the both of you make your entrance, her petite frame standing out against the multitude of her many siblings. |a veritable horde of kitsune kits await, seated at the numerous tables laid out in the hall. Your breath catches in your throat — sure, you knew you'd sired plenty of children on Kiyoko, but seeing them all in the same place at once is staggering. Fur ranging in color from white to black to gold to red and gray and even more turns the dining hall into a sea of color, and even though they fidget uncomfortably all of the kits are reasonably well-behaved for the occasion. Boys and girls, big and small, rowdy and quiet, every single one of them emerged from Kiyoko's womb at some point, born from your union with her. If anyone deserves to be honored on Mother's Day and given recognition for the work she's done in the name of motherhood, it's your lovely fox-wife. Kinu's standing at the fore of the head table, her many, many siblings behind her. For everything else that she is, your firstborn daughter sure knows how to take charge when her mother's not around. |Kinu awaits at the fore of the table facing the door, your daughter having summoned up all the solemnity and gravitas an eight-year-old can muster. ] She holds a silken bouquet of carnations in her hands, and standing on tiptoe, presents it gracefully and formally to Kiyoko. Her words sound overly stiff and formal, but perhaps that's how it's supposed to be between kitsune. Your firstborn daughter bows again, eyes closed, ears folded forward against her head, a clearly submissive position in front of her mother's authority. "Mother, [kiyoko.numKits 2|we are|I am] thankful for all your kindness. Today is a Mother's Day present from [kiyoko.numKits 2|us|me] to you. [kiyoko.numKits 2|On behalf of us all|With my deepest sincerity], allow me to wish for good health and a long, meaningful life for you. "Please, always be [kiyoko.numKits 2|our|my] beloved mother." Kiyoko stands over her daughter, her expression carefully neutral, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails gathered about herself. In this moment and at this time, it strikes you how absolutely and incredibly beautiful your fox-wife can be when she chooses to project such airs; even the simplest and smallest of her movements speaks of refinement and elegance. Reaching down, Kiyoko plucks the bouquet of carnations from Kinu's hands, then takes a step back to study the gift. [kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0 |It feels like forever before Kiyoko responds, but she eventually dips her head in her daughter's direction. "You have my thanks." Kinu doesn't have a reply, instead tilting her gaze to the side and away from her mother. There's a sense of awkwardness there, and then your daughter falls back on etiquette and decorum to save the situation, giving her mother another deep bow. "That will do." Pressing the bouquet close to her with her left hand, Kiyoko reaches down with her right and pats Kinu on the head, right in the space between her ears. Kinu squirms uncomfortably, grinding the balls of her feet into the ground, not daring to look her mother in the eye. |After what feels like an eternity, your kitsune wife breaks into a small smile. "Please, don't stand on ceremony." At those words, Kinu leans forward and encompasses her mother in a great big hug. [kiyoko.pregStage 1 3 |Her little arms press into the sides of Kiyoko's swollen belly as she stands on tiptoe, trying to reach around her mother — and failing quite miserably and comically at it. |There's no way her little arms can hope to reach all the way around to Kiyoko's back, so she contents with nuzzling into her mother's big pregnant belly, pressing her hands against the sides. |She has to stand on tiptoe to reach around Kiyoko's waist, but the effort is definitely worth it. ] Kiyoko returns the gesture, wrapping an arm about Kinu's shoulders while her other hand reaches to scratch between her daughter's ears. "Such an obedient child you are," she whispers, her voice choking up. "You, too... please always be my beloved firstborn.[kiyoko.numKits 2| And you all... my children, too.] The day will eventually come when you will not need me, but I hope I will have dispensed with my responsibilities well enough that you will still want me after that." ] "I will see to the final preparations. Please, Mother, [pc.mf|Father|Mother], take your seats." At that, Kinu withdraws, soft white tails swishing behind her as she makes for the kitchen. [kiyoko.numKits 4 |Two of her siblings detach themselves from their table, ushering Kiyoko and you towards the seats of honor in this little event. |Well, it looks like this is where you come in. Taking your beautiful fox-wife by the hand, you guide her towards the seat of honor in this little event. ] [kiyoko.pregStage 3 |It's a little amusing how her big, pregnant tummy gets in between her and the tabletop, requiring a bit of shifting and squeezing, but this probably isn't the time to be teasing her about it. This is her day, after all. |She slides into her seat, every bit as fine and regal as befits a woman of her station. This is her day, after all... it's very fitting that she looks the part of a fine mother in front of her children. ] Once she's settled in, Kiyoko lets out a little sigh of contentment and sets the bouquet to one side of the table. "Well, this is a pleasant surprise." You lean in and give your fox-wife a quick peck on the cheek. [kiyoko.numKits 2|The children|Kinu] must love her a lot to have gone to all this trouble for her — she's an excellent mother, and this is the day for her to be recognized. Why should it be a surprise in any way? She mulls over that. "I don't suppose you would've had any hand in all this, would you?" You? Oh no, perish the thought. With you having no idea how exactly time flows in the Astral Plane, you certainly wouldn't have any way to effectively plan something of this scale with [kiyoko.numKits 2|the kits|Kinu], right? No, all the credit goes to [kiyoko.numKits 2|them|her] for pulling it off. [kinu.kinuChildPersonality |Kiyoko sighs and contrives to look contemplative. "It's not that I don't like the proceedings, but... I do wish our daughter could be more like this in her daily life. More filial and obedient, if nothing else. Today will be today, and tomorrow she'll be back to her old self, I can tell you as much. Flowers are beautiful and all, but the greatest present she could have given me for today would be fewer gray hairs over the next year." She can't have fewer gray hairs if she doesn't have any to begin with. Your fox-wife rolls her eyes and bats at you with one of her many tails. "Please be serious for a moment. I do worry for our daughter's future if she's going to continue like this — I can already see the trouble I'm going to have finding a suitable husband-consort for her." She's growing away from her mother, becoming independent. The process began the moment she was conceived, and has only picked up in pace ever since. Kiyoko doesn't look happy at all with that answer, but that train of thought is stopped cold by Kinu returning on the scene. |Kiyoko sighs and hugs herself, looking very, very pleased as she makes herself comfortable. "Credit's where credit's due; I'm enjoying every moment of this. Kinu is already such a pleasant child... for her to have the resourcefulness to mastermind such a surprise makes me feel all giggly inside. I wonder which side of the family she gets that from?" "Kits... they grow up fast. Trust me — today she's but at your waist, tomorrow she'll be sneaking out to meet with boys in secret. My sisters used to do that all the time..." You would've said more, but that conversation is stopped cold by Kinu returning on the scene. ] Your firstborn daughter struggles under the burden of a tray piled almost comically high with food, standing on tiptoe to be able to properly present it to Kiyoko. After setting it down on the table, she steps back a respectful distance, awaiting her mother's appraisal of her offerings. Your fox-wife sniffs each of the covered crockeries daintily in turn. "Hmm. Kitsune udon, inarizushi, amazake... your know your mother's preferences well, don't you, girl?" "It wouldn't do to serve you something you disliked on the day meant to honor you, Mother." "Mm. Such a thoughtful child. Why kenchin soup, though? Isn't that your preference?" "It is, Mother. But..." "Yes?" "It's also the first thing I remember you making for me." "Ah." Kiyoko closes her eyes, her bosom heaving as she draws a deep breath and lets it out slowly. "Well then, that only leaves me to wonder how you managed to work in the kitchen without me noticing. "Mother has gone to great lengths to teach me well."[kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0| She may say that, but you can hear the strain in Kinu's voice as she forces the words forth...] "Well, then." Kinu disappears without a sound, and returns shortly after with a similar tray, sliding it onto the table. "For you, [pc.mf|Father|Mother]. "I will take my leave, then.[kiyoko.numKits 2| There are others who need to be served.]" As Kinu departs, Kiyoko gives you a sidelong glance, then sets down her chopsticks and smiles. "I suppose I should thank you too, [pc.name]" Why? This is her day, not yours. "Well, without you, I wouldn't have had the opportunity to be a mother, would I? Without you and your delectable chi to make kits with, I wouldn't be sitting here today with the people I love... [kiyoko.numKits 2 8 16 32 |our kits, and you, of course. [kiyoko.pregStage 1 3 |"Yes." Her smile turns upwards at the corners, becoming downright playful — or at least, it's best interpreted as playful.
