rows.original: You're here to look for clues as to Tollus's activities, not engage in petty theft of common items.
rows.translation: 你来到这里是为了寻找有关托卢斯活动的线索，而不是为了偷一些常见的物品。
rows.raw: "You're here to look for clues as to Tollus's activities, not engage in petty theft of common items."

rows.original:
Gweyr raises an eyebrow as you get on your knees and start unwrapping more packages in addition to checking the reinforced barrels to see if there're any that can be pried open. "Huh, really?"

        It's no different than when the two of you were getting in good on the cultist outpost; so long as you're here, you might as well take the opportunity to enrich yourselves and deny your opponents valuable resources.
        
        A huff. "You remind me of some kids I once had in the company. Couldn't even wait until the fighting was over before running to pull the boots off the dead — would always complain that the feet would swell and make getting them off in one piece hard..."
        
        [pc.isDK
        |Hey, if she wants to watch, she's more than welcome to.
        |So, it's just like old times, then?
        ]
        
        The two of you get down to it, doing your best to find the most valuable items amidst the sea of mediocrity and mundanity that stocks the cargo hold. Gweyr's nose for loot is good going — another of the many skills she no doubt picked up in her mercenary days — [party.has einin
        |but what really speeds the process along is Einin's professional eye for picking out likely marks. Darting from stack to stack, the little mecian quickly identifies promising finds, carelessly sealed containers, and oddly-shaped wrappings — it hasn't even been a few minutes before between Gweyr and her, they've rounded up all the likely suspects for searching. You can tell that Einin's really having fun getting into other peoples' stuff; even if the ship's cargo is boringly practical she nevertheless makes a game out of picking out a diamond in the rough.
        
        "All done!" she says, dusting off her hands. Between all of you, you've managed to gather the most valuable yet easily accessible ill-gotten gains from the ship's cargo. "It's not stealing if you do it from bad guys, that's what I learned from you, [pc.name]."
        
        Gweyr chuckles at that. "Cute girl, she learns fast. But yeah, I think this is the lot of it; let's move on before we run out of time here."
        |[pc.cunningRange 70
        |but your quick eye and cunning for picking out the details really speeds the process along. Together, you scour the easily accessible parts of the ship's hold, quickly identifying promising finds, carelessly sealed containers, and oddly-shaped wrappings. It takes a little time, but far less than what someone less quick on their feet would have managed, and before too long you've rounded up all the likely suspects for searching. Gweyr really does get into the spirit of things, sniffing around like the old hound that she is, and for the couple of minutes that you spend at it she does act younger than her age.
        |and together you get to searching the easily accessible parts of the cargo hold. While you try to be quick about it, Gweyr inevitably takes the lead in scouring the place for loot, quickly identifying promising finds, carelessly sealed containers, and oddly-shaped wrappings. Gweyr really does get into the spirit of things, sniffing around like the old hound that she is, and for the couple of minutes that you spend at it she does act younger than her age.
        
        It can't have taken as long as you feel it must've, but you're starting to double-guess yourself by the end of it all, wondering if this was a good idea to begin with. Eventually, though, you round up the most likely suspects from your search and split the loot.
        ]
        
        "Takes me back, this does. But yeah, I think this is the lot of it; let's move on before we run out of time here."
        ]
rows.translation:
当你跪下来开始拆开更多的包裹，同时检查那些加固过的桶，看看是否有哪个可以撬开时，格温尔挑了挑眉毛：“哈，真的吗？”

这和你们之前在那个邪教前哨基地大干一场的时候没什么两样；既然你在这里，不妨趁机多赚些好处，剥夺对手部宝贵的资源。
        
        哼，你让我想起我以前在公司里遇到的一些人。他们总是等打架结束才跑过去脱死者的靴子，还总抱怨足部肿得厉害，根本没法把靴子完整地脱下来。.."
        
        [pc.isDK
        |嘿，如果她想看的话，她完全可以来看。
        |所以，这就跟过去一样了，是吗？
        ]
        
        你们两个赶紧动手部吧，尽最大努力在货舱里那些平庸无奇的物品中找出最有价值的那些。格温尔在寻找战利品方面的天赋相当不错——这无疑也是她在当雇佣兵期间掌握的众多技能之一。 [party.has einin
        |但真正加快这一进程的是艾宁那敏锐的专业眼光——她总能迅速找出那些有可能含有目标物品的痕迹。这个小机械师在堆栈间穿梭往来，迅速识别出那些有希望的发现对象、那些被随意密封的容器，以及那些形状奇特的包装物。还没过几分钟，格温尔和她就已经收集到了所有值得搜查的疑似目标物品。 你可以看出，艾宁真的很享受翻找别人东西的乐趣；即使船上的货物都极其实用、乏味，她依然会把从中找出那颗“钻石”当作一种游戏来玩。

“全部搞定了！她说着，拍掉手上的灰尘。在你们所有人共同努力下，你们竟然从船上的货物中搜出了那些最有价值、同时也最容易获取的非法所得。” “如果是从坏人手里拿来的，那就不算偷窃，这是我从你们身上学到的。 [pc.name]格温尔听到这话笑了笑。“真是个可爱的女孩，学东西可真快。不过，我想事情就是这样的吧；我们还是赶紧继续吧，否则时间会不够用的。
        |[pc.cunningRange 70
        |但你的敏锐目光与发现细节的聪明才智确实大大加快了这一进程。你们一起仔细检查了船舱中那些容易触及的地方，迅速找出了那些可能有价值的物品、那些被随意封存的容器，以及那些形状奇特的包装物。 虽然需要一些时间，但这个时间远远短于那些行动不够敏捷的人所需的时间。不久之后，你就把所有可能成为嫌疑对象的人都找了出来。格温尔确实完全投入到了这种行动中，她像一只老猎犬一样四处搜寻，而在你花费的这几分钟时间里，她的表现确实显得比实际年龄要年轻许多。
        |于是你们一起开始搜索货舱中那些容易到达的地方。虽然你们都尽力加快速度，但格韦尔还是抢先开始在货舱里搜寻战利品，他迅速发现了那些可能有价值的物品、那些被随意密封的容器，以及那些形状奇怪的包装物。 格温尔确实完全融入了这种氛围中，她那条老猎犬般的嗅探行为，让你在陪伴她的那几分钟里，觉得她显得比实际年龄要年轻许多。

整个过程所花费的时间可能并没有你想象中那么长，但到最后，你开始开始怀疑自己当初这个决定是否正确。 最终，你还是从搜索结果中找出了最有可能的嫌疑人，然后平分了战利品。
        ]
        
        这确实让我回想起过去。不过，我想我们该继续下去了，否则时间会不够用的。
        ]

rows.original: It can't hurt. Utilize the enemy's resources against him, as the great Macah strategist once wrote...
rows.translation: 没什么坏处。利用敌人的资源来对付他们，正如伟大的马卡战略家曾经所说……
rows.raw: "It can't hurt. Utilize the enemy's resources against him, as the great Macah strategist once wrote... "

rows.original: Leaving the arbalest deck, you step through the doorway to be confronted with the ships's crew quarters — bunks, stacked upon each other, a large table in the middle with dice and cards strewn atop it, and several half-empty bottles. For a vessel crewed by demons, you're mildly surprised to find that the place doesn't stink of sex and musk, only of alcohol, and faintly at that. There're enough bunks for perhaps forty at a quick glance, but to your surprise only four or so are actually occupied, and of the remaining beds most of them have been stripped bare, clearly no in use anytime soon. The faint sound of snoring comes to you even from here as you peek in around the doorframe — well, is it so surprising that demons would need to sleep, too? "Huh, looks like we've got company." Oh yes, you do. "I prepared for as much. We could sneak past them once or twice, but it looks like we'll have to be passing through these crew quarters pretty regularly," Gweyr whispers to you. "I'm favoring a more permanent solution." Killing them? The old wolfess arches an eyebrow at you. "Not that hard a guess, but not yet; I don't want the lot up on deck spooked when they come down and find a couple of bodies, or their own missing. Just knock them out — a couple of guys with bruises might be handwaved away, a couple of deaths not so much." From what she's told of herself to you, restraint is a little surprising, coming from her. "Oh, please. Shall we begin?"
rows.translation: 离开弩炮区后，你穿过门廊，便来到了船员的宿舍。那里摆满了层层叠叠的床铺，中间有一张大桌子，上面散落着骰子和扑克牌，还有几瓶半空的酒。对于一艘由恶魔组成的船员团队来说，你有些惊讶地发现这个地方 不 空气中弥漫着性爱与麝香的气味，但也只有酒精的味道，而且还很淡。乍一看，这些铺位大概可以容纳四十个人，但令你惊讶的是，实际上只有四张铺位被占用了。而剩下的床铺大多都被掀开了被子，显然短期内不会有人使用它们。 即使从这里透过门框偷看，也能听到微弱的鼾声——嗯，恶魔也需要睡觉，这有什么好奇怪的吗？ “哈，看来我们有人来做客了。” 没错，确实有人来了。 我已经做好了各种准备。我们或许可以偷偷绕过他们一两次，但看来我们还是得经常经过这些船员宿舍。”格温尔低声对你说，“我更倾向于找一个更永久的解决办法。 杀了他们？” 老母狼挑了挑眉毛看着你。“这个答案其实并不难猜，但还不是现在的时候……我可不想那些家伙下来后，看到几具尸体，或者发现自己的同伴不见了，从而变得惊慌失措。只要把他们打晕就行了——几个身上有淤青的人，或许可以轻易地被掩盖过去，但要是有人死了，那就麻烦了。从她向你讲述的自己的经历来看，她这种克制力确实有点令人惊讶。 “哦，好了，我们开始吧？

rows.original:
As you step in to go about your business, Quin steps past you, carrying a sap in his hand. Now where did he get that? No sooner have you considered the question that he gets to work — Quin is as light-footed as his unshod feet might imply, skipping across the ship's planking with barely a noise. A grim expression on his face, he sets to the work of knocking out the helpless demons without even needing to be asked, taking a professional satisfaction but not outright glee in the unsavory act.

        Sure, they're demons, but...
        
        With such dark enthusiasm on Quin's part, any restraint you might've harbored evaporates. You head down the other side, taking care of the sleeping demon with a forceful application of your [pc.weapon]'s blunt end to their forehead, while Gweyr sweeps down the middle in an equally businesslike fashion. [pc.isChamp
            |It feels a little unsavory dealing with a helpless enemy like this, even knowing what Tollus is all about, but the situation's what it is and it's either you or them
            |Maybe you should feel something, dealing with a helpless enemy like this, but what do you really care at this point? It's either you or them, after all, and winner takes all in this game
        ]. There's a snort and half-cough followed by a sigh, and then the demon beneath you slumps into a much, much deeper sleep on the bunk.
        
        When the deed is done, the three of you meet up back by the entrance, and Quin gives you a brusque nod; his face is completely straight, his lips pressed into a thin line that tells you all you need to know.
        
        The job's done?
        
        "The job's done," both rabbit and wolf say together. They eye each other for a second, one professional sizing up and acknowledging the other, then Quin clears his throat and continues. "They should be out for an hour or so, I've done this before."
        
        "We'll be clear of this place in fifteen to twenty," Gweyr replies. "All right, then, let's get moving. There's little of value that I saw when moving through the crew bunks; Tollus was never in the habit of telling his lowest underlings more than they needed to know."
        
        "You don't say," Quin spits. "Kept in the dark and fed shit."
        
        Gweyr sniffs. "You're a funny one, bunny-man. I don't know what Tollus did to lose you from his roster, but his loss is my gain. Now, let's scram — the gods have been kind to us so far, and Tira gets tired carrying someone on her back for too long."
rows.translation:
当你正要开始自己的工作时，奎因从你身边走过，手中拿着一根树枝。他这树枝是从哪里弄来的呢？你还没来得及思考这个问题，他就开始行动了——奎因的足部步轻得惊人，赤足部走在船板上，几乎不会发出任何声响。 他脸上带着严肃的表情，开始毫不迟疑地消灭那些无助的恶魔。他从中获得了一种职业上的满足感，但并没有表现出真正的喜悦。

当然，它们只是恶魔而已……不过，还是挺让人不快的。鉴于奎因如此热切的态度，你心中可能存在的任何顾虑都烟消云散了。你走向另一侧，用力解决了那个正在睡觉的恶魔。 [pc.weapon]其中一根粗棍直刺他们的额头，而格温尔则以同样果断的方式从中间劈了下去。 [pc.isChamp
            |面对这样一个毫无反抗能力的敌人，这种做法确实让人感觉有些不妥，尽管我们已经了解了Tollus的真正目的，但现实就是如此——要么是你，要么是他们。
            |也许你应该有所感触吧，面对这样一个无助的敌人，但在这个时候，你究竟还在乎什么呢？归根结底，要么是你获胜，要么是他们获胜，而在这个游戏中，胜者通吃。
        ]一阵哼声、半声咳嗽，紧接着是一声叹息，然后你足部下的那个恶魔便在铺位上沉沉睡去了。

事情结束后，你们三个人在入口处重新会合，奎因朝你简短地点了点头；他的表情十分严肃，嘴唇紧抿成一条细线，这一点已经说明了一切。
        
        任务完成了？”

“任务完成了，”兔子和狼同时说道。他们互相对视了一秒钟，彼此都在评估对方的能力并给予认可。然后，奎因清了清嗓子，继续说道：“应该再过一个小时左右他们就会出来了，我以前做过这种事。我们十五到二十分钟就能离开这个地方了，”格韦尔回答道。“好吧，那我们赶紧出发吧。在检查船员们的铺位时，我没发现什么有价值的东西；托卢斯从来不会告诉他的下属们那些他们不需要知道的事情。真是太妙了，”奎因嗤笑道，“被蒙在鼓里，还吃着垃圾。”

格韦尔哼了一声：“你真是个有趣的人，兔子人。我不知道托卢斯做了什么才让你从他的名单上消失，但他的损失就是我的收获。 现在，我们得赶紧离开了——到目前为止，诸神还算眷顾我们，但让蒂拉长时间背着一个别人，她也累坏了。
rows.raw:
"
        As you step in to go about your business, Quin steps past you, carrying a sap in his hand. Now where did he get that? No sooner have you considered the question that he gets to work — Quin is as light-footed as his unshod feet might imply, skipping across the ship's planking with barely a noise. A grim expression on his face, he sets to the work of knocking out the helpless demons without even needing to be asked, taking a professional satisfaction but not outright glee in the unsavory act.

        Sure, they're demons, but...
        
        With such dark enthusiasm on Quin's part, any restraint you might've harbored evaporates. You head down the other side, taking care of the sleeping demon with a forceful application of your [pc.weapon]'s blunt end to their forehead, while Gweyr sweeps down the middle in an equally businesslike fashion. [pc.isChamp
            |It feels a little unsavory dealing with a helpless enemy like this, even knowing what Tollus is all about, but the situation's what it is and it's either you or them
            |Maybe you should feel something, dealing with a helpless enemy like this, but what do you really care at this point? It's either you or them, after all, and winner takes all in this game
        ]. There's a snort and half-cough followed by a sigh, and then the demon beneath you slumps into a much, much deeper sleep on the bunk.
        
        When the deed is done, the three of you meet up back by the entrance, and Quin gives you a brusque nod; his face is completely straight, his lips pressed into a thin line that tells you all you need to know.
        
        The job's done?
        
        "The job's done," both rabbit and wolf say together. They eye each other for a second, one professional sizing up and acknowledging the other, then Quin clears his throat and continues. "They should be out for an hour or so, I've done this before."
        
        "We'll be clear of this place in fifteen to twenty," Gweyr replies. "All right, then, let's get moving. There's little of value that I saw when moving through the crew bunks; Tollus was never in the habit of telling his lowest underlings more than they needed to know."
        
        "You don't say," Quin spits. "Kept in the dark and fed shit."
        
        Gweyr sniffs. "You're a funny one, bunny-man. I don't know what Tollus did to lose you from his roster, but his loss is my gain. Now, let's scram — the gods have been kind to us so far, and Tira gets tired carrying someone on her back for too long.""

rows.original:
That brings to mind something. Ryn?

        "[etheryn.highConfidence|Yes|Y-yes]?"
    
        She's trained in this sort of thing, right? As a ranger of sorts? Could she help you and Gweyr with the demons? You need to be silent, and you know she's good at that.
        
        [etheryn.highConfidence
            |Ryn nods without hesitation. "Of course."
            |Ryn swallows hard, but nods.
        ]
        
        As you step in to go about your business, Ryn hurries past you, the blunt end of her [etheryn.weapon] readied. You're reminded of that day you met her by the Wayfort, and how light-footed she can be when she puts her mind to it; your elven companion skips across the ship's planking with barely a noise, heading for the bunks on the left side of the quarters. A [etheryn.highConfidence
            |grim expression on her face
            |tremulous expression on her face as she forces herself to swallow her fear
        ], she sets to the work of knocking out the helpless demons.
            
        Seeing even Ryn put aside her hesitations and fear to get the job done, any restraint on your part evaporates. You head down the other side, taking care of the sleeping demon with a forceful application of your [pc.weapon]'s blunt end to their forehead, while Gweyr sweeps down the middle in an equally businesslike fashion. [pc.isChamp
            |It feels a little unsavory dealing with a helpless enemy like this, even a demon, but the situation's what it is and it's either you or them
            |Maybe you should feel something, dealing with a helpless enemy like this, but what do you really care at this point? It's either you or them, after all, and winner takes all in this game
        ]. There's a snort and half-cough followed by a sigh, and then the demon beneath you slumps into a much, much deeper sleep on the bunk.
        
        When the deeds are done, the three of you meet up back by the entrance, and Ryn gives you a nod; [etheryn.highConfidence
            |her face is completely straight, her lips pressed into a thin line that tells you all you need to know
            |while she looks to be on the verge of tears, she sucks it all up like the royal she should be and only allows herself a small sniffle
        ].
        
        The job's done?
        
        "[etheryn.highConfidence
            |It is.
            |I-it is. Gods, I thought I'd throw up once or twice there, just looking at a real demon from that close, wondering if he'd wake up and see me...
        ]" 
        
        Gweyr lays a hand on her shoulder. "It's not killing, but it's close. The more you practice, the easier it is to do it again, and the less it hurts."
    
        Ryn recoils as if the wolfess' hand were a hot coal. "[etheryn.highConfidence
            |That's not comforting at all! E
            |T-that's not comforting a-at all... e
        ]very time I've brought down an enemy while traveling with [pc.name]..."
        
        "It wasn't meant to be, but you clearly know what I'm talking about." Turning away from Ryn, Gweyr gives you an upnod. "They should be out for an hour or so, I've done this before."
    
        She has experience, huh?
        
        "We'll be clear of this place in fifteen to twenty," Gweyr replies. "All right, then, let's get moving. There's little of value that I saw when moving through the crew bunks; Tollus was never in the habit of telling his lowest underlings more than they needed to know."
rows.translation:
这让我想起了一件事。Ryn？[etheryn.highConfidence|是的。|是的。]她接受过这方面的训练，对吧？应该算是某种护林员吧？她能帮你和格温尔一起对付那些恶魔吗？你们需要保持安静，而你知道她很擅长这一点。
        
        [etheryn.highConfidence
            |瑞恩毫不犹豫地点了点头：“当然。
            |瑞恩艰难地咽了口唾沫，但还是点了点头。
        ]
        
        当你正要开始自己的事情时，Ryn从你身边匆匆走过，她的……那钝的一端 [etheryn.weapon] 你准备好了。你会想起那天在荒废驿堡河边与她相遇的情景，也会想起当她下定决心时，她是多么轻盈敏捷；你的精灵伙伴几乎不发出任何声响，就跳过了船板，朝着住处左侧的铺位走去。 [etheryn.highConfidence
            |她脸上带着严肃的表情。
            |她的脸上带着颤抖的表情，强忍着恐惧将那些情绪咽了下去。
        ]她开始着手消灭那些无助的恶魔。

看到就连瑞恩也抛开了犹豫和恐惧，专心致志地完成这项任务，你心中的任何顾虑也都烟消云散了。你走向另一侧，用有力的手段对付那些正在沉睡的恶魔。 [pc.weapon]一根钝器猛地击中了他们的额头，而格温尔则以同样果断的方式从中间劈了下去。 [pc.isChamp
            |面对这样一个无助的敌人，哪怕它是一只恶魔，这种行为也显得有点不地道。但现实就是如此，要么是你取胜，要么是他们得逞。
            |也许你应该有所感触吧，面对这样一个无助的敌人，但在这个时候，你究竟还在乎什么呢？归根结底，要么是你获胜，要么是他们获胜，而在这个游戏中，胜者通吃。
        ]一阵哼声、半声咳嗽，紧接着是一声叹息，然后你脚下的那个恶魔在铺位上沉沉睡去了。

当这些事情完成后，你们三个人在入口处重新会合，瑞恩向你点了点头。 [etheryn.highConfidence
            |她的脸完全绷得紧紧的，嘴唇抿成一条细线，这一幕已经说明了一切。
            |虽然她看起来快要哭出来了，但她还是像一位真正的公主一样强忍住了泪水，只允许自己轻轻抽泣了一声。
        ]工作完成了吗？[etheryn.highConfidence
            |确实如此。
            |是……天啊，我当时真觉得只要再靠近看那个真正的恶魔一眼，我就会吐出来的。我在想，如果它醒过来看到我该多可怕……
        ]格温尔把手放在她的肩上：“虽然不会致命，但也差不多了。你练习得越多，下次做起来就会越容易，疼痛也会减轻。”

瑞恩却像被狼女的手烫到一样，立刻缩了回去。[etheryn.highConfidence
            |这可一点都让人感觉不到安慰呢！真糟糕……
            |那一点都不能让人感到安慰……
        ]每次我在移动途中击倒敌人时 [pc.name]本来不是这样的，但你应该明白我在说什么。”格韦尔转过身去，朝你点了点头，“他们应该会在外面待一个小时左右，我以前也这么做过。”

她确实有经验啊……
        
        我们十五到二十分钟就能离开这个地方了，”格韦尔回答道。“好吧，那我们赶紧出发吧。在检查那些船员们的铺位时，我没有发现什么有价值的东西；托卢斯从来不会告诉他的下属们那些他们不需要知道的事情。"

rows.original: Without waiting for your reply, Gweyr's already out, her feet light on the ship's planking despite her obvious size and weight. You don't see any sap or blackjack on her, but the pommel of her dagger glints in the dim light as she makes a beeline for the bunks, a grim expression on her face. Time for you to play your part too, then; seeing Gweyr's businesslike demeanor evaporates most doubt and restraint alike on your part. You tiptoe down the other side, taking care of the sleeping demon with a forceful application of your [pc.weapon]'s blunt end to their forehead. [pc.isChamp |It feels a little unsavory dealing with a helpless enemy like this, even a demon, but the situation's what it is and it's either you or them |Maybe you should feel something, dealing with a helpless enemy like this, but what do you really care at this point? It's either you or them, after all, and winner takes all in this game ]. There's a snort and half-cough followed by a sigh, and then the demon beneath you slumps into a much, much deeper sleep on the bunk. Phew. While you don't know when your heart snuck into your throat in all of this, you nevertheless swallow it down and meet Gweyr in the middle, taking out another sleeping demon in much the same fashion as before. Every footstep you take threatens to be the one that'll set the crew to waking and screaming at the intrusion, but that dreaded moment never comes, and it's with no small amount of trepidation that you meet back up at the entrance to the arbalest deck and let out the breath you'd been holding. How does she stay so calm throughout all of this?[pc.bg soldier| It's not as if you haven't seen your share of danger as a soldier, but this is something else altogether.] "It's not killing, but it's the same idea. The more you practice, the easier it is to do it again, and the less it hurts. I don't make a bloody mess all the time, you know." Clearing her throat, Gweyr gives you an upnod. "They should be out for an hour or so, I've done this before." She has experience, huh? "We'll be clear of this place in fifteen to twenty," Gweyr replies. "All right, then, let's get moving. There's little of value that I saw when moving through the crew bunks; Tollus was never in the habit of telling his lowest underlings more than they needed to know."

rows.original: Without waiting for your reply, Gweyr's already out, her feet light on the ship's planking despite her obvious size and weight. You don't see any sap or blackjack on her, but the pommel of her dagger glints in the dim light as she makes a beeline for the bunks, a grim expression on her face. Time for you to play your part too, then; seeing Gweyr's businesslike demeanor evaporates most doubt and restraint alike on your part. You tiptoe down the other side, taking care of the sleeping demon with a forceful application of your [pc.weapon]'s blunt end to their forehead. Or that's what you intended, anyway. Maybe you breathed a little too loud, maybe you stepped on a plank that creaked, whatever the case, the demon's bleary red eyes open, fix on you, and then the poor bastard gets out half a yelp before you hurriedly clamp a hand over his mouth and smack him on the forehead with your [pc.weapon]'s blunt end. There's a snort and half-cough beneath your palm followed by a sigh, and then the demon beneath you slumps into a much, much deeper sleep on the bunk. Gods, did anyone hear that? Your heart hugs your throat for several more moments as you half-expect the sound of footsteps rushing towards the hatch and ladder, but none come just yet. Maybe the activity up top drowned out your little misstep... Swallowing hard, you force the lump in your throat back down and turn back to your task, meeting Gweyr in the middle. [pc.Weapon] raised, you take out another sleeping demon in much the same fashion as you did the first sans the yelping, but even so you can't stop your skin from crawling — every footstep you take through the crew quarters threatens to be the one that'll set the crew to waking and screaming at the intrusion, but that dreaded moment never comes. It's with no small amount of trepidation that you meet back up with Gweyr at the entrance to the arbalest deck and let out the breath you'd been holding. "Not so fast on the draw, eh, kid?" the old wolfess mutters. [pc.isDK |Yeah, yeah, she can stop gloating about it already. |Another half-second and the bastard might've very well brought down the entire ship upon you. It could've been worse... but she's also right in that you could've been better about things. ] "Practice[silly|, and I get lots of it clubbing seals over the head]. The more you practice, the easier it is to do it again, and the less it hurts. I don't make a bloody mess all the time, you know." Clearing her throat, Gweyr gives you an upnod. "They should be out for an hour or so, I've done this before." She has experience, huh? "We'll be clear of this place in fifteen to twenty," Gweyr replies. "All right, then, let's get moving; we almost certainly cut short our time here with that little mishap you had. There's little of value that I saw when moving through the crew bunks; Tollus was never in the habit of telling his lowest underlings more than they needed to know."
rows.translation: 不等你回应，格温尔就已经走了出去。尽管她的身材和体重都很显眼，但她行动起来却轻快自如，足部步毫不费力地踏在船板上。你没有看到她身上有任何武器，但在昏暗的轻型线下，她手中匕首的刀柄却闪烁着轻型芒。她面带严肃的表情，径直走向那些铺位。 那么，现在你也该发挥作用了。看到格韦尔那种雷厉风行的作风，你心中的疑虑和顾虑自然也就烟消云散了。你小心翼翼地走到另一边，用足够的力量处理掉那个正在睡觉的恶魔 [pc.weapon]那东西的钝头狠狠地砸在了他们的额头上。 至少你是这么打算的。也许你呼吸的声音太大了，也许你踩到了一块会发出吱嘎声的木板，不管是什么原因，那只恶魔那双昏暗的红眼睛突然睁开了，紧紧地盯着你。然后，那个可怜的家伙还没来得及发出一声尖叫，你就赶紧用手捂住了他的嘴，同时用你的……狠狠地敲了一下他的额头。 [pc.weapon]它的钝端……”你的手掌下传来一声轻哼和半声咳嗽，紧接着是一声叹息，然后你足部下的那个恶魔在铺位上沉沉睡去了。 天啊，有人听到吗？你的心脏还在胸口剧烈跳动着，你几乎期待着会听到有人朝舱口和梯子奔来的足部步声，但迟迟没有动静。 也许上面发生的那些事情掩盖了你的这个小失误…… 你艰难地咽了口唾沫，将卡在喉咙里的那块东西压了下去，然后继续着手你的工作，在中途与格温尔相遇了。 [pc.Weapon] 你抬手取出另一个沉睡的恶魔，过程与之前取出第一个恶魔时几乎一模一样，只不过这次没有那种尖锐的叫声。但即便如此，你还是忍不住感到一阵毛骨悚然——每当你踏入船员区，都担心这一足部会惊醒全体船员，让他们因为这种入侵而开始尖叫。然而，那个可怕的时刻始终没有到来。 当你带着几分忐忑的心情在弩炮甲板的入口处与格韦尔重新会合时，你终于松了一口气。 “拔剑的速度可真慢啊，小家伙……”那位老女狼低声说道。 [pc.isDK |是啊，是啊，她该停止为此沾沾自喜了。 |再晚半秒钟，那个混蛋很可能就会让整艘船都塌下来压在你身上。情况本可能更糟……但她说得也对，你本可以做得更好一些的。 ] 练习吧。[silly|我经常遇到这种情况，就是用棍子敲打海豹的头部。]练习得越多，以后再做同样的事情就会越容易，也不会那么痛苦了。我绝对不会把事情搞得一团糟。 所有 你知道的，就是现在这个时间。”格温尔清了清嗓子，点了点头说道，“他们应该需要一个小时左右才能回来，我以前也做过这种事。” 她确实有经验啊…… “我们十五到二十分钟就能离开这个地方了，”格温尔回答道。 好吧，那我们赶紧出发吧。因为那次小意外，我们在这里停留的时间肯定被缩短了。我在检查船员们的铺位时并没有发现什么有价值的东西——Tollus向来不会告诉他的下属们那些他们不需要知道的事情。"
rows.raw: "Without waiting for your reply, Gweyr's already out, her feet light on the ship's planking despite her obvious size and weight. You don't see any sap or blackjack on her, but the pommel of her dagger glints in the dim light as she makes a beeline for the bunks, a grim expression on her face. Time for you to play your part too, then; seeing Gweyr's businesslike demeanor evaporates most doubt and restraint alike on your part. You tiptoe down the other side, taking care of the sleeping demon with a forceful application of your [pc.weapon]'s blunt end to their forehead. Or that's what you intended, anyway. Maybe you breathed a little too loud, maybe you stepped on a plank that creaked, whatever the case, the demon's bleary red eyes open, fix on you, and then the poor bastard gets out half a yelp before you hurriedly clamp a hand over his mouth and smack him on the forehead with your [pc.weapon]'s blunt end. There's a snort and half-cough beneath your palm followed by a sigh, and then the demon beneath you slumps into a much, much deeper sleep on the bunk. Gods, did anyone hear that? Your heart hugs your throat for several more moments as you half-expect the sound of footsteps rushing towards the hatch and ladder, but none come just yet. Maybe the activity up top drowned out your little misstep... Swallowing hard, you force the lump in your throat back down and turn back to your task, meeting Gweyr in the middle. [pc.Weapon] raised, you take out another sleeping demon in much the same fashion as you did the first sans the yelping, but even so you can't stop your skin from crawling — every footstep you take through the crew quarters threatens to be the one that'll set the crew to waking and screaming at the intrusion, but that dreaded moment never comes. It's with no small amount of trepidation that you meet back up with Gweyr at the entrance to the arbalest deck and let out the breath you'd been holding. "Not so fast on the draw, eh, kid?" the old wolfess mutters. [pc.isDK |Yeah, yeah, she can stop gloating about it already. |Another half-second and the bastard might've very well brought down the entire ship upon you. It could've been worse... but she's also right in that you could've been better about things. ] "Practice[silly|, and I get lots of it clubbing seals over the head]. The more you practice, the easier it is to do it again, and the less it hurts. I don't make a bloody mess all the time, you know." Clearing her throat, Gweyr gives you an upnod. "They should be out for an hour or so, I've done this before." She has experience, huh? "We'll be clear of this place in fifteen to twenty," Gweyr replies. "All right, then, let's get moving; we almost certainly cut short our time here with that little mishap you had. There's little of value that I saw when moving through the crew bunks; Tollus was never in the habit of telling his lowest underlings more than they needed to know.""

rows.original: You step over to the maps and star charts hung up by the desk and take a closer look at them. While the writing looks vaguely similar to modern Belharan, a lot of the wording is archaic and largely illegible to you. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |Even for someone who's been blessed enough to have received a formal education like you, old Belharan isn't one of the subjects you could go into deeply enough for lack of learning material, so |Someone with the likes of your background would never have warranted any kind of formal education, let alone the kind that would've been required for reading the scrawl on this ancient parchment. Either way, ] all you're reduced to is guessing the meaning of every other word, and even that is tenuous at best. Still, it's clear as day that these navigational aids are ancient, old enough to be from the Godswar or even before it — by all rights, the constant exposure to the salt air and moist should have caused them to fall apart long ago. Even if they do crinkle, they don't fall apart at your cautious prodding, and with the way the seat has an impression in it it's implied that these have been used recently and often. The question is, of course, why would anyone still plot a course by ancient maps? Sure, much of the continent may have been devastated centuries ago, but certainly the art of cartography wasn't lost. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |You've seen your share of maps in your time given your previous profession, that's for sure, so it's not as if anyone with even a smidgen of learning doesn't know what the world looks like |You may not have seen many with your own eyes, but everyone knows that you can freely buy a map of the world in any Jassiran port city; catfolk were — and still are — sold all over the place, after all ]. There're locations marked here that don't exist any more, one or two you've only heard about in legend, and the boundaries of the nations are all wrong... or at least, you think. [party.oneComp atugia kiyoko |"Oh," Atugia says, coming up beside you to take in the maps on the wall. "Oh." Why, does she know something about these? "Carmen and I used to travel a bit just after... well, she wanted to get out of the castle for a few years after things settled down. Wanted to put the bad memories aside, you see. The maps are accurate... for their time. Teiglache's right there, you see." She jabs the map with a finger, causing it to bend and crinkle, but not tear. "And Jassira, and Tronarii... but a whole lot of these other places don't exist any more, or at least, they're not called by the same names. Especially the semi-independent city-states down by the continental coast, those got completely wiped out." So these maps are accurate for their time? "Yeah. The coastlines and all are still the same, too — except for that one where the Idejima peninsula was torn off by an earthquake from one of the bigger battles and wound up floating about in the sea until it washed up down south. Look. Just cut this bit off — " she moves her finger on the map — "and add this bit just north of Tronarii. Not much, but when you consider it moved at all..." An entire peninsula... just torn away? How is that possible? Isn't land attached to the seafloor? Wouldn't it sink? Atugia sighs. "I don't know. Those days were crazy, I'm just glad Carmen and I only saw a little bit of the chaos, being as remote as we were. But back to the point — I can tell you that these maps are real. Carmen was always a passenger aboard the ships we took, but she was always treated nice and sometimes I'd see these around when the captains invited her to dine in their cabins." Any idea why this ship might be navigating with centuries-old maps, then? "Well, many places like these were destroyed during the Godswar. My guess? They're looking for more and more of the old cities so they can loot them, bring the treasure and all to their mistress. It's the only explanation that I can see which also makes sense." |"Ah." Before you know it, your fox-wife has silently inserted herself at your side, peering at the old map. "I thought I would never see one of these again." Why, does she know something about these? "A little, beloved. Before there were torii gates, we had to come over the ocean by ship... some still do. The first ones were part of the advance fleet sent to conduct gunboat diplomacy upon our nation and annex us... we took their ships and the sailors who were brave enough to guide us back to their now torn homeland, and crossed the ocean." So these maps are accurate for their time? "Yes. I saw several of these during the month-long trip, maps and star charts, other navigational tools." Gently, Kiyoko raises a finger to the ancient, yellowed paper, and gathers a bit of dust on her fingertip before smudging it away. "Fragile, yet immensely sturdy to have survived this long. That alone would have confirmed the authenticity of this relic, if not the information on it." And she saw these personally? "The Belharan sailors used these to navigate seas unknown to us. I would imagine them quite accurate." Your fox-wife closes her eyes, clearly dredging up deep memories. "Yes. The coastlines and landmarks are identical to the ones I saw, I am sure of this. Major ports, cities, and nominally independent city-states that nevertheless paid quiet tribute to Belhar. A month on a ship is a long time to absorb information and learn, when the alternative is boredom." Any idea why this ship might be navigating with centuries-old maps, then? "My guess would be the same reason we do: to find old sites and try and excavate their treasures; no doubt this demoness of yours is highly interested in them, for all the wrong reasons. I am sure that we will find more information pertaining to this if we search a little more, that is to be sure." Kiyoko looks thoughtful a moment and taps her chin. "Komari tells me that many of the old maps the original Belharans brought along with them have been quite useful in searching for the ruins of the old empire. As far as I understand these things, the coastlines and their landmarks have not changed much since then as opposed to the interiors of the continents where much of the fighting occurred, so it would make sense to search by ship." |"Hmp." While you've been engrossed in trying to make sense of the maps and charts, Gweyr's padded over to you and started reading over your shoulder. "Don't know much about these. Do you?" [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |Some, but none this old. |Nope. ] "Still, these look pretty old. Wonder why anyone would be sailing by them... unless they're trying to find stuff that isn't on the maps of the world you can buy out of Jassira. Look at all these... well, whatever they are." The old wolfess makes to jab at the ancient, yellowed parchment, then thinks better of it. "If they were places of interest to the Belharans of old, they'd be of interest to treasure hunters like some of the folks I knew when I was younger. Wouldn't be a week going by where the earth wouldn't move and reveal yet another damned ruin or the other. Many good kids would go in and wound up never coming out..." She thinks the cult might be digging up relics of old Belhar? Gweyr blinks. "I... I wasn't thinking of that, but now that you speak of it, that's almost certainly what the damn bastards were doing. Tollus was crowing about wanting the treasures in the baroness's vaults twenty years ago... I wouldn't be surprised if he's still looking for more of the same ever since." ] That... well, that makes sense. This very ship itself is a relic that the cult's been putting to their own nefarious purposes. No doubt Kas and Tollus wouldn't be stopping at one, would they? While you've no evidence of this, it nevertheless is a conjecture that would be worth investigating. Turning away from the maps, you pause to consider this theory, what it might mean, and most importantly, how it all ties in with what's going on in the rift and Kasyrra's larger plans... assuming she and Tollus are still on the same page, that is.
rows.translation: 你走到桌边，仔细观察那些挂在那里的地图和星图。虽然上面的文字看起来与现代贝尔哈兰的语言有些相似，但很多表达方式都非常古老，几乎无法辨认。 [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |即使对于像你这样有幸接受过正规教育的人来说，古老的贝拉兰也并非那种因为缺乏学习资料而无法深入研究的课题。 |像你这样背景的人，根本就不应该接受任何形式的正规教育，更不用说那种能够帮助你理解这份古老羊皮纸上的文字的教育了。无论如何…… ] 你所能做的，就是去猜测其他所有单词的含义，而即便这样，所得到的结果也至多只是些模糊不清的猜测罢了。 不过，很明显，这些导航辅助工具已经非常古老了，它们的历史可能可以追溯到“神战”时期，甚至更早——按照常理来说，长期处于盐雾弥漫且潮湿的环境中，它们早就应该损坏报废了才对。 即使这些地图出现了褶皱，但在你轻轻触碰时，它们也不会散开。而且座椅上的使用痕迹说明，这些地图最近还被经常使用着。 当然，问题在于：为什么还有人会依靠古老的地图来规划路线呢？ 当然，虽然几个世纪前这片大陆的大部分地区可能已经遭受了严重的破坏，但制图技术肯定没有因此而失传。 [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |以你之前的职业经历来看，你肯定见过各种各样的地图，所以只要稍加学习，任何人都应该知道这个世界到底是怎样的。 |你可能没有亲眼见过很多这样的生物，但大家都知道，在贾西兰的任何港口城市，人们都可以自由购买世界地图；而猫人，过去如此，现在依然如此，到处都有出售。 ]这里标出的一些地点已经不存在了，有一两个地方你只是从传说中听说过而已，而各个国家的边界也全都错了……至少你是这么认为的。 [party.oneComp atugia kiyoko |哦，”阿图吉娅走到你身边，看着墙上的那些地图说道，“哦。” 难道她对这些了解些什么吗？ “在……嗯，事情平息之后，卡门和我曾经一起出去旅行过一段时间。她当时想离开城堡，好好过几年自由的生活。 我想把那些不好的回忆抛到一边，你知道的。这些地图在它们所处的时代来说，已经非常精确了……泰格拉赫就在那里，你看。”她用手指戳了戳地图，地图因此弯曲了一些，出现了一些褶皱，但并没有被撕破。“还有贾西拉，还有特罗纳里。但是，很多其他的地方已经不复存在了，或者至少，它们的名字已经变了。尤其是那些位于大陆海岸线的半独立城邦，它们已经被彻底消灭了。 那么这些地图在它们制作的时候是相当精确的，对吧？ “是的。海岸线之类的也都没有变化——除了那片地区：在某场大规模战役中，Idejima半岛因为地震而被撕裂，随后在海上漂浮，最终被海浪冲到了南方。看，只要把这一部分去掉——”她在地图上用手指指了指那个区域——“然后在特洛纳里以北添加这一小块就可以了。虽然变化不大，但考虑到它确实发生了位置移动…… 整整一个半岛……就这样被撕裂掉了？这怎么可能呢？陆地不应该是固定在海底的吗？这样的情况下，半岛不应该会沉入海底吗？ 阿图吉娅叹了口气：“我不知道。那些日子真是太疯狂了……幸好我们住在那么偏远的地方，所以只目睹了那一部分混乱景象。不过，这些地图确实是真实的。卡门每次都是和我们一起乘坐那些船，大家对待她都很好。有时候，当船长们邀请她去他们的船舱用餐时，我也会看到这些地图。 那么，有没有人能解释一下，为什么这艘船会使用几百年前的地图来导航呢？ “嗯，像这样的地方很多都在神战期间被毁掉了。我的猜测是：他们正在寻找那些古老的城市，以便劫掠其中的财宝，然后将所有战利品带回给他们的主子。这是我能想到的唯一合理的解释。 |啊。”还没等你反应过来，你的狐狸妻子就已经悄悄站在你身边，盯着那张古老的地图看。“我本来以为再也见不到这样的东西了。” 难道她对这些东西了解些什么吗？ “知道一点而已，亲爱的。在这一切发生之前 托里 那些大门啊，我们当初是必须乘船穿越大洋才能到达的……现在仍然有人这样做。最初那些船只，其实是作为先遣队被派来对我国实施炮舰外交、企图将我们吞并的……我们夺取了他们的船只，还有那些勇敢地愿意引导我们返回他们如今已经分裂的祖国的水手们，就这样我们穿越了大洋。 那么这些地图在它们所处的时代来说，确实是准确的吗？ “是的。在为期一个月的旅行中，我看到了很多这样的地图、星图以及其他导航工具。”清子轻轻地将手指放在那张古老而泛黄的纸上，指尖沾上了一些灰尘，随后又将它们拂去。“这些物品虽然脆弱，但却异常坚固，才能保存至今。单是这一点，就已经足以证明这些文物的真实性了，更不用说上面记载的信息了。 她这些都是亲眼所见吗？ “贝拉兰的水手们就是用这些来导航那些我们不熟悉的海域的。我想这些工具应该相当精确。”你的狐狸妻子闭上了眼睛，显然是在回忆那些往事。“是的，那些海岸线以及地标，和我当时看到的完全一样，我敢肯定。那些重要的港口、城市，以及那些名义上独立但实际上向贝拉兰表示臣服的城市国家……在船上度过一个月的时间，其实是很长的，足够让人吸收大量信息、学到很多东西的，毕竟否则的话，只会感到无聊而已。 那么，有没有人能想到为什么这艘船会使用几百年前的地图来导航呢？ “我猜原因应该和我们一样：为了寻找那些古老的遗址并尝试挖掘其中的宝藏；毫无疑问，你这位女恶魔对那些宝藏非常感兴趣，只不过她的动机绝对不纯。 我相信，如果我们再继续搜索一下，肯定能找到更多与此相关的信息。”清子若有所思地沉吟了一会儿，然后轻敲着下巴说道：“小丸告诉我，那些最初的贝拉人带来的古老地图，在寻找古老帝国的遗迹时起到了很大的帮助。 据我了解，从那以后，海岸线及其地标几乎没有发生变化，而那些发生过许多战斗的大陆内部地区则发生了很大的变化。因此，通过船只进行搜索才是合理的选择。" |哼。”当你还在专心研究那些地图和图表，试图弄清楚它们的含义时，格温尔走过来，从你肩后开始看那些东西。“我对这些不太了解，你知道吗？ [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |有些，但没有这么古老的。 |不行。 ] 不过，这些看起来确实很古老。不知道为什么会有人经过这里……除非他们是想寻找一些在贾西拉出售的世界地图上没有记载的东西。看看这些……嗯，不管它们到底是什么。那只老母狼本来想要用爪子去抓那些古老而发黄的羊皮纸，但最终还是放弃了这个念头。“如果这些地方在过去的贝尔哈兰人眼中真的有价值，那么像我年轻时认识的一些寻宝者们，肯定也会对它们感兴趣的。 不出一个星期，地球就会再次露出新的废墟……许多善良的孩子进去后，就再也没能出来……” 她认为，那个邪教组织可能在挖掘贝尔哈尔昔日的遗迹吧？ 格韦尔眨了眨眼：“我……我之前并没有想到这点，但你现在这么一说，那些该死的混蛋很可能就是在干这种事。二十年前，托卢斯就一直嚷着想要女男爵金库里的财宝。如果他从那以后还在不断寻找类似的东西，我一点也不会感到惊讶。 ] 嗯……这样想确实有道理。这艘船本身就是那个邪教组织用来谋取不正当利益的遗迹。毫无疑问，卡斯和托卢斯肯定不会只满足于使用一艘船，对吧？而你……也没有其他选择。 证据 尽管如此，这仍然是一个值得探讨的猜测。 将注意力从这些地图上移开，你停下来仔细思考这个理论：它可能意味着什么，更重要的是，它与裂隙中正在发生的事情以及卡希拉的更大计划之间究竟存在着怎样的联系……当然，前提是她和托卢斯的意见仍然一致。
rows.raw: ' You step over to the maps and star charts hung up by the desk and take a closer look at them. While the writing looks vaguely similar to modern Belharan, a lot of the wording is archaic and largely illegible to you. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |Even for someone who's been blessed enough to have received a formal education like you, old Belharan isn't one of the subjects you could go into deeply enough for lack of learning material, so |Someone with the likes of your background would never have warranted any kind of formal education, let alone the kind that would've been required for reading the scrawl on this ancient parchment. Either way, ] all you're reduced to is guessing the meaning of every other word, and even that is tenuous at best. Still, it's clear as day that these navigational aids are ancient, old enough to be from the Godswar or even before it — by all rights, the constant exposure to the salt air and moist should have caused them to fall apart long ago. Even if they do crinkle, they don't fall apart at your cautious prodding, and with the way the seat has an impression in it it's implied that these have been used recently and often. The question is, of course, why would anyone still plot a course by ancient maps? Sure, much of the continent may have been devastated centuries ago, but certainly the art of cartography wasn't lost. [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |You've seen your share of maps in your time given your previous profession, that's for sure, so it's not as if anyone with even a smidgen of learning doesn't know what the world looks like |You may not have seen many with your own eyes, but everyone knows that you can freely buy a map of the world in any Jassiran port city; catfolk were — and still are — sold all over the place, after all ]. There're locations marked here that don't exist any more, one or two you've only heard about in legend, and the boundaries of the nations are all wrong... or at least, you think. [party.oneComp atugia kiyoko |"Oh," Atugia says, coming up beside you to take in the maps on the wall. "Oh." Why, does she know something about these? "Carmen and I used to travel a bit just after... well, she wanted to get out of the castle for a few years after things settled down. Wanted to put the bad memories aside, you see. The maps are accurate... for their time. Teiglache's right there, you see." She jabs the map with a finger, causing it to bend and crinkle, but not tear. "And Jassira, and Tronarii... but a whole lot of these other places don't exist any more, or at least, they're not called by the same names. Especially the semi-independent city-states down by the continental coast, those got completely wiped out." So these maps are accurate for their time? "Yeah. The coastlines and all are still the same, too — except for that one where the Idejima peninsula was torn off by an earthquake from one of the bigger battles and wound up floating about in the sea until it washed up down south. Look. Just cut this bit off — " she moves her finger on the map — "and add this bit just north of Tronarii. Not much, but when you consider it moved at all..." An entire peninsula... just torn away? How is that possible? Isn't land attached to the seafloor? Wouldn't it sink? Atugia sighs. "I don't know. Those days were crazy, I'm just glad Carmen and I only saw a little bit of the chaos, being as remote as we were. But back to the point — I can tell you that these maps are real. Carmen was always a passenger aboard the ships we took, but she was always treated nice and sometimes I'd see these around when the captains invited her to dine in their cabins." Any idea why this ship might be navigating with centuries-old maps, then? "Well, many places like these were destroyed during the Godswar. My guess? They're looking for more and more of the old cities so they can loot them, bring the treasure and all to their mistress. It's the only explanation that I can see which also makes sense." |"Ah." Before you know it, your fox-wife has silently inserted herself at your side, peering at the old map. "I thought I would never see one of these again." Why, does she know something about these? "A little, beloved. Before there were torii gates, we had to come over the ocean by ship... some still do. The first ones were part of the advance fleet sent to conduct gunboat diplomacy upon our nation and annex us... we took their ships and the sailors who were brave enough to guide us back to their now torn homeland, and crossed the ocean." So these maps are accurate for their time? "Yes. I saw several of these during the month-long trip, maps and star charts, other navigational tools." Gently, Kiyoko raises a finger to the ancient, yellowed paper, and gathers a bit of dust on her fingertip before smudging it away. "Fragile, yet immensely sturdy to have survived this long. That alone would have confirmed the authenticity of this relic, if not the information on it." And she saw these personally? "The Belharan sailors used these to navigate seas unknown to us. I would imagine them quite accurate." Your fox-wife closes her eyes, clearly dredging up deep memories. "Yes. The coastlines and landmarks are identical to the ones I saw, I am sure of this. Major ports, cities, and nominally independent city-states that nevertheless paid quiet tribute to Belhar. A month on a ship is a long time to absorb information and learn, when the alternative is boredom." Any idea why this ship might be navigating with centuries-old maps, then? "My guess would be the same reason we do: to find old sites and try and excavate their treasures; no doubt this demoness of yours is highly interested in them, for all the wrong reasons. I am sure that we will find more information pertaining to this if we search a little more, that is to be sure." Kiyoko looks thoughtful a moment and taps her chin. "Komari tells me that many of the old maps the original Belharans brought along with them have been quite useful in searching for the ruins of the old empire. As far as I understand these things, the coastlines and their landmarks have not changed much since then as opposed to the interiors of the continents where much of the fighting occurred, so it would make sense to search by ship." |"Hmp." While you've been engrossed in trying to make sense of the maps and charts, Gweyr's padded over to you and started reading over your shoulder. "Don't know much about these. Do you?" [pc.bg scholar arcanist acolyte noblescion |Some, but none this old. |Nope. ] "Still, these look pretty old. Wonder why anyone would be sailing by them... unless they're trying to find stuff that isn't on the maps of the world you can buy out of Jassira. Look at all these... well, whatever they are." The old wolfess makes to jab at the ancient, yellowed parchment, then thinks better of it. "If they were places of interest to the Belharans of old, they'd be of interest to treasure hunters like some of the folks I knew when I was younger. Wouldn't be a week going by where the earth wouldn't move and reveal yet another damned ruin or the other. Many good kids would go in and wound up never coming out..." She thinks the cult might be digging up relics of old Belhar? Gweyr blinks. "I... I wasn't thinking of that, but now that you speak of it, that's almost certainly what the damn bastards were doing. Tollus was crowing about wanting the treasures in the baroness's vaults twenty years ago... I wouldn't be surprised if he's still looking for more of the same ever since." ] That... well, that makes sense. This very ship itself is a relic that the cult's been putting to their own nefarious purposes. No doubt Kas and Tollus wouldn't be stopping at one, would they? While you've no evidence of this, it nevertheless is a conjecture that would be worth investigating. Turning away from the maps, you pause to consider this theory, what it might mean, and most importantly, how it all ties in with what's going on in the rift and Kasyrra's larger plans... assuming she and Tollus are still on the same page, that is.'

rows.original: It's not too hard to find the ship's log — it sits on one of the stands by the desk, thick, heavy and well-thumbed. You open it to find dozens upon dozens of entries, each one meticulously written in neat handwriting; whoever penned this must have some kind of education to pay such attention to detail. How nice of the ship's captain to be so thorough for your benefit: the log is replete with everything from weather conditions, landfall, cargo taken on and offloaded, even minor altercations amongst the crew... While you only have a few minutes to flip through what entries you can, several things immediately jump out at you: Firstly, the ship moves fast; it has to, for the logs to state that landfall was made in a Jassiran port one day and then barrels were taken on in Tronarii the other. Even if the nations are neighbouring ones, that's far too fast for any reasonable ship you know... but this isn't one, is it? Secondly, it has far fewer crew than you might imagine for a vessel this size — only seven, just to get it to move. It's true that this ship doesn't have oars or sails, and without any weapons all the bunks you saw back in the crew quarters would have been defunct, but it's still hard to believe. With a ship like this, though, it wouldn't need any means of protecting itself if it can just outpace any pursuer... that, or it's got means of defense that aren't immediately obvious. Thirdly, you note that the ship's been weighing anchor at all kinds of places all over this region, funnelling... things back to — well, some of the cargo has ended up here in the rift, to be sure. But the lion's share of goods, special orders, building materials, and whatever the cult has been collecting from sites all over the world to somewhere on the Marches' east coast. While the log is quite vague about what things are being gathered, as would be natural for someone writing for themselves as opposed for someone else's elucidation, it's not hard to infer that either the cult or Kasyrra herself considers them pretty valuable, if not important. She did say she was a scientist of sorts back in the Winter City, didn't she? Amongst the most recent entries, there's one that catches your eye, though: The Master's hunch was right; we found the information we needed off the coast of the continental heartland, not too far from Willowpast where the river opens up into the sea. No one was hurt during the excavation, but it wasn't for lack of trying on the part of the things we found inside. Praise be to the Dark Lady for her blessings, that we are just as much monster now as the things that lie beneath the earth; our strength outmatched theirs. We had one casualty with a huge gash across the chest, but the wound was already half-healed by the time we returned to the boat via the dinghy. It was very clearly attempting to fester in an unnatural way, but our Dark Lady's powers outmatch those of our foes'. The total retrievable items amounted to: seven relics, sixteen manuscripts and eleven miscellaneous artifacts; I have had to stop Whelker from lifting any small items for "personal use", the bastard. Then again, she used to be one of those mouse people, same as Berach, so it only makes sense, I suppose. All are to be deliverable to Estelore, but not before allowing the Master to examine them first. We also found the inscriptions the Master instructed us to find, and I've made a rubbing of them to be delivered to him. The password is "Issal Saal Craa Gas Iskar". At least, that's how Whelker assures me they're pronounced, she's the historian here, and ever since accepting the Dark Lady's gifts her obsession with the subject has only intensified, as has her penchant for claiming bits of it for her own. Either way, the words are strange for a minotaur tongue, but it would appear that it was devised by worshippers of Nareva, so the serpentine nature of the words makes sense. At the very least, it's not something a northern minotaur would ever guess on their own; as far as I know, it's complete gibberish in any language they speak, or used to speak for that matter. But hopefully the Master will be content with this find; I've never seen him this sullen in all the years we've been together. I don't know why — the Dark Lady is everything we've hoped for and more, but it's not my place to question him. Future me, I'm writing down the password because every single one of my crew has the attention span of a gnat and the organizational habits of a — a gnat as well. If you forget, no one's going to remember this. Now hurry up to the Master and get this to him so he can finally open up the treasury. I'd have blown apart the doors myself, or tried to dig around the walls, but he said it would destabilize everything since the entire place is so deep under the ocean. I don't like it, but I guess all the other stuff we collected on the trip makes up for the bother, so fine. You thumb through the log another time, but there aren't any events recorded within the entries that jump out at you. By all appearances, this vessel is dedicated to doing milk runs for Kasyrra and her cult, even if the milk itself is pretty valuable. Kind of a shame you don't see anything of value down here in the belly of the beast, but in that case it might not be as deserted as it is... [party.has quintillus |"So, they're doing some grave-robbing." Quintillus sneers, looking very smug with himself. "Glorified grave-robbing, but grave-robbing nevertheless." It would imply that Tollus, Kas or both would be interested in artifacts of old Belhar. "Not news to me," your bunny-boy companion replies. "Like I said, he was crazy about the stuff even before all this shit started going down. He wanted the power that they represented, to deny it from others even if he couldn't figure out how to use them himself. And boy did he try, the dumbass. Ever wonder why he's bald?" You just assumed it was part of him being an asshole. But this stuff about somewhere being under the ocean, or a password in some other language — does Quin know anything about that? He shrugs. "Sorry, can't help you there. Must've been developments that happened after I booked it. He must've gotten a lot of help if he's got some kind of undersea fort or something, because that is not the kind of thing the Tollus I remember would've been capable of." Help like Kas, maybe? "Dunno. He doesn't seem to like her a lot, and I'm sure the feeling's mutual." |"So, they're doing some grave-robbing." Gweyr muses. "Glorified grave-robbing, but grave-robbing nevertheless. Not that it isn't a profitable trade, knew some myself." It would imply that Tollus, Kas or both would be interested in artifacts of old Belhar. "That he was. Remember, he was crowing about wanting to take the baroness's castle and everything that was in her vaults. I don't think she actually has any vaults, but he was certainly enamored with the idea." You just assumed it was part of him being an asshole. But this stuff about somewhere being under the ocean, or a password in some other language — does that ring any bells for her? She rubs her chin. "Sorry, can't help you there. But it sounds like he got a pretty big boost to be capable of all this... the Tollus I knew twenty years ago wouldn't have been capable of that." ] Well, that's enough for now. Maybe the rest of the ship will provide further insight into just what's going on in Tollus's mind...
rows.translation: 找到这艘船的航海日志并不太难——它就放在书桌旁的架子上，厚厚的、重型，上面还有很多人翻阅过的痕迹。当你打开它时，会看到成百上千条记录，每一条都用整洁工整的笔迹仔细记录下来；撰写这些记录的人肯定受过一定的教育，否则不可能如此注重细节。 船长真是考虑周到，为你的方便做了这么多记录：航海日志里详细记载了各种信息，从天气状况、到船只靠岸的地点、船上货物的装卸情况，甚至还包括船员之间发生的些小争执…… 虽然你只有几分钟的时间来浏览这些记录，但有几件事立刻吸引了你的注意： 首先，飞船开始移动了。 快必须这样，因为航海记录上明确记载：某天在贾西兰的一个港口登陆，而第二天又在特罗纳里港装载了货物。即便这两个国家是邻国，这样的行进速度对于任何一艘普通的船只来说都快得不可思议。.. 但这个船显然不属于这类船只，对吧？ 其次，对于一艘这么大的船来说，它的船员数量其实比你想象的要少得多——只有七个人，仅仅够让船移动而已。的确，这艘船没有桨也没有帆，而且由于没有任何武器，你在船员区看到的那些铺位本来也应该是无法使用的，但这一切还是让人难以相信。 不过，有了这样的船，就不存在这种问题了。 需要 如果它能够跑得比任何追捕者都快，那么它就拥有任何自我保护的手段……或者，它拥有一些并不显而易见的防御能力。 第三，你注意到这艘船在这个地区的各个地方都停靠过，似乎在寻找某种目标…… 各种物品 嗯，确实有一部分货物最终落在了这里的裂隙中。但大部分货物——包括特殊订单物品、建筑材料，以及那个邪教组织从世界各地收集来的各种物资——都被运到了边境东海岸的某个地方。不过，这份记录对于具体细节的描述相当模糊 各种物品 这些资料正在被收集起来，对于一个为自己写作的人来说，这样做是很自然的；而对于那些需要为他人阐明某些事情的人来说，这样做也同样合理。因此，不难推断，无论是那个邪教组织，还是卡希拉本人，都认为这些资料具有相当大的价值，甚至可以说是非常重要的。 她之前不是说过自己在冬城是一名科学家吗？ 在最近收集到的这些资料中，有一份确实特别引人注目。 大师的直觉是正确的；我们在大陆腹地的海岸附近找到了我们需要的信息，那里距离柳树镇并不远，也就是那条河流汇入大海的地方。在挖掘过程中没有人受伤，但这并不是因为人们没有付出足够的努力。 各种物品 我们在里面发现了那些东西。感谢暗影女神的恩赐，我们现在也变成了怪物，和那些埋藏在地下的事物一样；我们的力量已经超过了它们。我们中有一个人受了伤，胸前有一道巨大的伤口，但当我们乘小船返回船上时，那伤口已经愈合了一半。 很明显，这种负面影响正在以一种不自然的方式持续发展，但我们的“暗影女士”的力量远远超过了我们的敌人。 最终被找到的物品总数为：七件遗物、十六份手稿以及十一件其他杂物；我不得不阻止惠尔克把那些小物件“据为己有”，那个混蛋。 话说回来，她曾经也属于那些喜欢使用鼠标的人之一，和Berach一样，所以我想，这样也是情有可原的。所有这些东西最终都必须要交给Estelore，但在那之前，必须先让大师检查一遍。 我们还找到了大师让我们寻找的那些铭文，我已经把它们拓印下来，准备交给他。 密码是 伊萨尔·萨尔·克拉·加斯·伊斯卡至少，惠尔克是这么向我保证这些词应该这么发音的。她可是这里的专家，自从接受了那位暗影女士赠送的礼物之后，她对这一主题的兴趣就越发浓厚了，而且她还总喜欢把其中的一些内容据为己有。 无论如何，这些词语对于弥诺陶洛斯来说确实显得很奇怪，但看来它们是纳雷瓦的信徒们创造出来的，因此这些词语所具有的“蛇一般的蜿蜒特性”也在情理之中。至少，北方弥诺陶洛斯绝对不可能自己想出这样的词语；据我所知，用他们现在使用的任何语言来说，这些词语都完全是无意义的废话。 但希望大师会对这个发现感到满意；在我们共处的这些年里，我从未见过他如此沮丧。我不知道原因所在——那位暗影女士确实是我们所期望的，甚至超越了我们的期望，但质疑他的决定并不属于我的职责。未来的我，正在把这个密码记录下来，因为我的团队里每个人的注意力都像蚊子一样短暂，组织能力也同样差劲。如果你忘记了，也没人会记得这个密码的。 现在赶紧去把这个交给大师，这样他终于可以打开宝库了。我本来想亲自把门拆开，或者试着在墙壁里挖找，但他说那样会破坏整个结构的稳定性，因为这个地方位于海洋深处。虽然我不喜欢这样，但想想我们在旅途中收集到的其他东西，也算是弥补了这个麻烦，所以也就算了。 你再次翻阅了那些记录，但其中并没有任何特别引人注目的事件。从种种迹象来看，这艘船似乎专门被用来为卡希拉及其教派运送那些价值不菲的货物。可惜的是，在这艘船的内部并没有发现任何有价值的东西，但这样的话，它或许也不像看上去那么荒废…… [party.has quintillus |所以，他们正在进行盗墓活动。”昆蒂勒斯冷笑道，脸上露出得意的表情，“虽然算是‘高级盗墓’，但本质上还是盗墓而已。” 这意味着托卢斯、卡斯，或者他们俩，都对古代贝尔哈尔的文物感兴趣。 这对我来说并不意外，”你的兔子男孩伙伴回答道，“就像我之前说的，早在这一切事情发生之前，他就对那些东西充满了狂热。他渴望拥有它们所代表的力量，甚至愿意剥夺别人的这种力量，尽管他自己还不知道该如何使用它们。 这家伙真是拼命尝试啊，那个笨蛋。你们有没有想过，为什么他会秃头呢？” 你们只是认为那是他性格恶劣的表现而已。但那些关于某个地方在海洋下面，或者密码是用某种其他语言写成的说法——Quin到底知道些什么呢？ 他耸了耸肩：“抱歉，这方面我帮不上忙。肯定是在我预订之后发生了某些变化。如果他拥有某种海底堡垒之类的设施，那么他肯定得到了很多帮助，因为那样的话 不是 那种事情，我记得Tollus应该是能够做到的。” “也许需要像Kas那样的帮助吧？” “不知道。他似乎并不是很喜欢她，而且我敢肯定，她的感觉也是同样的。 |所以，他们正在从事一些盗墓活动。”格韦尔沉思道，“虽然算是高级别的盗墓行为，但本质上还是盗墓。不过这种生意确实很赚钱，我自己也认识一些从事这种行当的人。” 这意味着托卢斯、卡斯，或者他们俩，都会对贝尔哈尔时期的文物感兴趣。 “他确实有这样的打算。你们应该还记得，他曾经公然宣称想要夺取女男爵的城堡以及她地窖里的所有财物。不过我觉得她实际上 拥有 任何地窖都行，但他确实对这个想法非常着迷。” 你只是认为这是他性格中固有的坏毛病罢了。但那些关于某个地方位于海洋之下，或者密码是用某种其他语言写成的说法——这些会不会让她想起什么来呢？ 她摸了摸下巴：“抱歉，我帮不上你的忙。不过听起来，他能够做到这些，肯定是因为得到了某种强大的帮助……二十年前的那个托卢斯，是绝对做不到这些的。 ] 好了，目前就到这里吧。也许飞船上的其他部分能为我们提供更多关于托卢斯心中正在思考什么的线索……

Then again, she used to be one of those mouse people, same as Berach, so it only makes sense, I suppose. All are to be deliverable to Estelore, but not before allowing the Master to examine them first. We also found the inscriptions the Master instructed us to find, and I've made a rubbing of them to be delivered to him. The password is "Issal Saal Craa Gas Iskar". At least, that's how Whelker assures me they're pronounced, she's the historian here, and ever since accepting the Dark Lady's gifts her obsession with the subject has only intensified, as has her penchant for claiming bits of it for her own. Either way, the words are strange for a minotaur tongue, but it would appear that it was devised by worshippers of Nareva, so the serpentine nature of the words makes sense. At the very least, it's not something a northern minotaur would ever guess on their own; as far as I know, it's complete gibberish in any language they speak, or used to speak for that matter. But hopefully the Master will be content with this find; I've never seen him this sullen in all the years we've been together. I don't know why — the Dark Lady is everything we've hoped for and more, but it's not my place to question him. Future me, I'm writing down the password because every single one of my crew has the attention span of a gnat and the organizational habits of a — a gnat as well. If you forget, no one's going to remember this. Now hurry up to the Master and get this to him so he can finally open up the treasury. I'd have blown apart the doors myself, or tried to dig around the walls, but he said it would destabilize everything since the entire place is so deep under the ocean. I don't like it, but I guess all the other stuff we collected on the trip makes up for the bother, so fine. You thumb through the log another time, but there aren't any events recorded within the entries that jump out at you. By all appearances, this vessel is dedicated to doing milk runs for Kasyrra and her cult, even if the milk itself is pretty valuable. Kind of a shame you don't see anything of value down here in the belly of the beast, but in that case it might not be as deserted as it is... [party.has quintillus |"So, they're doing some grave-robbing." Quintillus sneers, looking very smug with himself. "Glorified grave-robbing, but grave-robbing nevertheless." It would imply that Tollus, Kas or both would be interested in artifacts of old Belhar. "Not news to me," your bunny-boy companion replies. "Like I said, he was crazy about the stuff even before all this shit started going down. He wanted the power that they represented, to deny it from others even if he couldn't figure out how to use them himself. And boy did he try, the dumbass. Ever wonder why he's bald?" You just assumed it was part of him being an asshole. But this stuff about somewhere being under the ocean, or a password in some other language — does Quin know anything about that? He shrugs. "Sorry, can't help you there. Must've been developments that happened after I booked it. He must've gotten a lot of help if he's got some kind of undersea fort or something, because that is not the kind of thing the Tollus I remember would've been capable of." Help like Kas, maybe? "Dunno. He doesn't seem to like her a lot, and I'm sure the feeling's mutual." |"So, they're doing some grave-robbing." Gweyr muses. "Glorified grave-robbing, but grave-robbing nevertheless. Not that it isn't a profitable trade, knew some myself." It would imply that Tollus, Kas or both would be interested in artifacts of old Belhar. "That he was. Remember, he was crowing about wanting to take the baroness's castle and everything that was in her vaults. I don't think she actually has any vaults, but he was certainly enamored with the idea." You just assumed it was part of him being an asshole. But this stuff about somewhere being under the ocean, or a password in some other language — does that ring any bells for her? She rubs her chin. "Sorry, can't help you there. But it sounds like he got a pretty big boost to be capable of all this... the Tollus I knew twenty years ago wouldn't have been capable of that." ] Well, that's enough for now. Maybe the rest of the ship will provide further insight into just what's going on in Tollus's mind... "

rows.original: Breath catching in your throat, you leave the walkway that lines the edge of the circular chamber and step onto the metal bridge that connects it to the orb's little plinth. [pc.isMage |Even if you weren't magically inclined, you'd have no problem feeling the sheer intensity of the power surging within the beam of light, and the fact that you are trained in these things only serves to set your teeth on edge all the more |While you aren't magically inclined, you don't need to be to feel the sheer intensity of the power surging through the beam of light. It makes your skin crawl — not necessarily in fear or as a danger response, but from the sheer potential that's present here. Potential for what? That's a question for someone who's more magically inclined to answer. ]. [party.has atugia |"Hey, careful there!" Tui's voice is barely audible over the thrumming. "Those runes about the base — they're clearly not good news!" She knows what they mean? "Y-yeah! They're pretty close to those we used to use in Teiglache! Look!" Atugia gestures to herself and the patterns on her skin, and now that she points it out, there's a passing similarity there — the patterns aren't exactly the same, but they're conceivably related. She is the runic expert here, though... if you do decide to get closer to investigate, she might be able to make something out of them. |"Careful, kid," Gweyr growls from behind you. "I don't know if this'll turn you into a smoking pile of dust, but... just know when to back off, okay? I've never trusted old Belharan shit since my days in the heartlands, and neither should you." Yeah, got it. ] That does bear the question, though. Do you want to get closer to the ship's engine and see what you can figure out about it? It's obviously not safe, but the insight might be worth it. You won't have time to come back to this given the fact that you're on short notice for being down here at all, so you'll have to make this decision now.
rows.translation: 你的呼吸变得急促起来，你离开了环绕着圆形大厅边缘的通道，踏上了那座将大厅与那个小球体底座连接起来的金属桥。 [pc.isMage |即使你没有魔法天赋，你也一定能感受到那道光束中蕴含的强大力量，以及这一事实本身 是 仅仅因为接受了这些方面的训练，反而会让你更加感到烦躁不安。 |虽然你并没有魔法天赋，但你也完全能够感受到那股能量通过光束传递而来的强烈冲击。这种感觉会让你不寒而栗——并非出于恐惧，也不是身体对危险的本能反应，而仅仅是因为那种能量的强度实在太过惊人了。 潜力 这就是目前所拥有的东西。那么，它具备什么潜力呢？这个问题，恐怕更适合那些对魔法更有研究的人来回答。 ]. [party.has atugia |嘿，小心点！”在嘈杂的声音中，崔的声音几乎听不见。“基地周围的那些符文……显然不是什么好兆头！” 她知道那些符文代表什么吗？ “嗯……是的！它们和我们以前在泰格拉赫使用的那些符文很相似！ 看！” 阿图吉娅指了指自己以及自己皮肤上的那些图案。现在她这么一指，确实能看出它们之间有些相似之处——这些图案虽然并不完全一样，但显然存在某种关联。毕竟，她才是这里的符文专家嘛。.. 如果你真的决定深入调查，她或许能从中发现一些线索。 |小心点，孩子，”格韦尔在你身后低吼道，“我不知道这会不会把你变成一堆灰烬，但……至少要知道什么时候该退缩，明白吗？自从我在内陆地区的时候起，我就从来不相信那个老贝尔哈兰，你也不应该相信他。” “知道了。 ] 不过，这确实引出了一个问题：你是否想靠近那艘船的引擎，看看能从中发现什么线索呢？显然这样做并不安全，但这样的尝试或许值得一试。考虑到你被紧急派到这里来，根本没有时间再回来，所以你必须现在就做出这个决定。

rows.original:
Gritting your teeth, you back away slowly from the ship's engine, the black orb still thrumming and crackling with power. You know when you're out of your league, and this is it. [pc.isMage
        |Your magical senses are all telling you to back off, and — well, who are you going to believe, your curiosity or your own lying eyes?
        |You may not be as magically attuned to this kind of stuff as an actual wizard would, but every one of your senses are screaming at you to back off.
        ] It's only when you feel your shoulders hit the wooden paneling of the engine room's walls and press yourself up against it that you feel marginally safer than you did a moment ago.
        
        "You all right?" Gweyr asks, grabbing you by under the arm and steadying you on your feet. "Looking a little pale there, [pc.mf|kid|girl]."
        
        Yeah. It was... it felt as if the magical setup was drawing you in, like a moth to a flame, but you're all right now. Best to stay in this chamber as little as possible.

rows.original: find Atugia kneeling beside you, studying the runic descriptions as intently as you were. What's she doing here? "Can't just let you stick your neck out and take all the risks when I'm the one who knows things about runes, can I? That, and you need someone to shield you if somethin' goes wrong." Well, when she puts it that way... you're glad she came up of her own volition to help out here. Now, she said earlier that the runes appeared familiar from a distance — does anything spring to mind now that she's able to have a closer look? "Give me a moment." Atugia traces the closest of the runes with her finger, and a spark of bluish-white power leaps from the light surrounding the pedestal to her — where it's absorbed into the runes on her body and dissipated harmlessly. "Yeah. It'd take a lot of explaining, but these are runes representing storm, sea and wind, almost identical to what we used in Teiglache." So she's saying that this pedestal is of Teiglachan make? "No. The runes we used didn't drive the ship like this thing is doin', they were for ensuring good weather, stayin' righted in rough seas, that kind of thing. A little country like mine didn't have this kind of power. But — " she clears her throat — "I will say that whoever made this drew a lot of inspiration from our runic system." Since the ship is of Belharan make, you'd assume that it was them who did it. "As good a guess as anyone's. The good thing about runes — " Tui points to her own body — "is that you can just draw or paint them and forget about them for a good long while. They're usually not very good focuses, though. Wonder why they used them here." Yeah, wonder why. The black crystal orb in the middle... does she know what it is? "No, but it makes my skin crawl. Like, actually tremble, my runes are going crazy just being close to it. Don't do anything too stupid, would you?" ...You'll just get a closer look. "..." The light is so blinding when you're right up against the beam, it's hard to see; yet the crystal is perfectly visible, sucking all of the radiant incandescence into its body as it hovers in the air an inch or two above the pedestal's surface, bobbing up and down ever so slowly. Or is it emitting the light? No, it couldn't be, in that case it would be going off in all directions instead of being a cleanly defined beam surrounding it, right? And yet... [pc.isMage |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all. And the Belharans had one for every one of their warships? Wow. |[pc.bg scholar acolyte |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all. And the Belharans had one for every one of their warships? Wow. |There's something about this black crystal orb that against all logic is emitting and absorbing the magical light all at once, a sense of dread and wonder that sets in just by being close to it. ] ] "Look out!" With those words, Atugia grabs you by the collar of your [pc.armor] and hauls you backwards just in time for a crackling bolt of wayward radiance to narrowly miss you. It doesn't actually cause any damage to the wooden walkway that bridges the nest of pipes or the spot where you were standing, but the scorched, chemical smell it leaves lingering in the air strongly suggests that you wouldn't want to have been hit by that. Phew, that was close. There isn't any way to shut all of this down from where you are, is there? "None of the runes looked to be related to that kind of thing, and I'm not sure that'd be a good idea anyway; the demons would notice and come runnin' down." Atugia looks you up and down, then starts leading you back to Gweyr. "I think we'd better get back before anything else like that happens."
rows.translation: 你发现阿图吉娅正跪在你身旁，和她一样专注地研究那些符文描述。 这是什么 她 我怎么可能让你一个人去承担所有风险呢？毕竟我是那个了解符文的人，对吧？而且，如果出了什么问题，你也需要有人来保护你。 嗯，既然她这么说了……你肯定很高兴她是主动过来帮忙的。刚才她说过，那些符文从远处看似乎很熟悉——现在她能够仔细观察了，有没有什么印象浮现出来呢？ 稍等片刻。”阿图吉娅用手指触碰了那些符文中最接近她的一处，顿时有一道蓝白色的能量从基座周围的轻型芒中跃向她，然后被她身上的符文吸收，无声无息地消散了。 是的。虽然需要花很多时间来解释，但这些符号代表着风暴、海洋和风，与我们之前在泰格拉赫使用的符号几乎一模一样。” 所以她是在说，这个基座是泰格拉赫人制作的吗？ 不。我们使用的符文并不能像这个东西那样驱动船只，它们只是用来确保天气良好，或在波涛汹涌的海面上保持船只的稳定方向之类的。像我这样的小国家，根本不可能拥有这样的力量。 但是 — “她清了清嗓子，说道：‘我得承认，无论是谁制作了这个东西，他们肯定从我们的符文系统中获得了很多灵感。’” 既然这艘船是贝尔哈兰人制造的，那么你很可能会认为是他们做的这件事。 和其他人的猜测一样，这也只是个猜测而已。不过，符文的好处在于——”崔指了指自己的身体——“你可以把它们画出来，然后很长一段时间都不再去想它们。不过，通常来说，这些符文并不是很好的‘专注工具’。 真不明白他们为什么在这里使用这些东西。” “是啊，也很疑惑。中间的那个黑色水晶球……她知道那是什么吗？” “不知道，但只要靠近它，我的皮肤就会发麻，甚至会颤抖，我的符文也会因此变得混乱不堪。 别做太蠢的事，好吗？” …… “……” 当你站在轻型束的正前方时，那轻型芒实在刺眼，根本看不清任何东西；然而那颗水晶却清晰地呈现在眼前——它悬浮在基座表面上一两英寸的地方，缓缓地上下晃动，将所有耀眼的轻型芒都吸收进了自己的体内。 还是说它在发轻型？不，不可能，如果是这样的话，轻型线应该会向四面八方散开，而不会形成一道清晰可见的轻型束围绕在它的周围，对吧？然而…… [pc.isMage |你只在书中读到过这种东西，但描述与实际情况完全相符：坚硬的雷晶，表面被打磨得光亮无比，红色在提纯过程中已经消失，其他方面则与自然界中的雷晶一模一样，包括那些瑕疵在内。 而贝拉尔人竟然在他们每一艘战舰上都配备了一块这样的雷晶？哇，真是令人惊叹。 |[pc.bg scholar acolyte |你只在书中读到过这种东西，但描述与实际情况完全相符：坚硬的雷晶，表面被打磨得光亮无比，红色在提纯过程中已经消失，其余部分则与自然界中存在的雷晶一模一样，包括所有的瑕疵。 而贝拉尔人竟然在他们每一艘战舰上都配备了一块这样的雷晶？哇，真是令人惊叹。 |这个黑色水晶球有着某种不可思议的特性——它既能同时释放魔法光芒，又能吸收这些光芒。仅仅站在它的附近，就会让人产生一种既恐惧又惊叹的感觉。 ] ] 当心！”说着，阿图吉娅抓住了你的衣领 [pc.armor] 然后，在那道闪烁的、方向不定的轻型芒即将击中你的瞬间，它突然将你向后拉扯，使得轻型芒与你擦肩而过。虽然这种轻型芒并没有对连接那些管道的木制走道或你刚才站立的地方造成任何实质性的损害，但空气中残留的焦灼味和化学气味，无疑让人觉得：如果真的被那道轻型芒击中，后果肯定不堪设想。 呼，真是好险。从你现在的位置来看，根本不可能彻底阻止这一切，对吧？ “那些符文看起来都与那种事情无关，而且我觉得那样做也不是个好主意；恶魔肯定会察觉到然后跑过来攻击的。阿图吉娅上下打量了你一番，然后开始带你返回格韦尔。‘我觉得我们最好在发生其他类似的事情之前赶紧回去。
rows.raw: " find Atugia kneeling beside you, studying the runic descriptions as intently as you were. What's she doing here? "Can't just let you stick your neck out and take all the risks when I'm the one who knows things about runes, can I? That, and you need someone to shield you if somethin' goes wrong." Well, when she puts it that way... you're glad she came up of her own volition to help out here. Now, she said earlier that the runes appeared familiar from a distance — does anything spring to mind now that she's able to have a closer look? "Give me a moment." Atugia traces the closest of the runes with her finger, and a spark of bluish-white power leaps from the light surrounding the pedestal to her — where it's absorbed into the runes on her body and dissipated harmlessly. "Yeah. It'd take a lot of explaining, but these are runes representing storm, sea and wind, almost identical to what we used in Teiglache." So she's saying that this pedestal is of Teiglachan make? "No. The runes we used didn't drive the ship like this thing is doin', they were for ensuring good weather, stayin' righted in rough seas, that kind of thing. A little country like mine didn't have this kind of power. But — " she clears her throat — "I will say that whoever made this drew a lot of inspiration from our runic system." Since the ship is of Belharan make, you'd assume that it was them who did it. "As good a guess as anyone's. The good thing about runes — " Tui points to her own body — "is that you can just draw or paint them and forget about them for a good long while. They're usually not very good focuses, though. Wonder why they used them here." Yeah, wonder why. The black crystal orb in the middle... does she know what it is? "No, but it makes my skin crawl. Like, actually tremble, my runes are going crazy just being close to it. Don't do anything too stupid, would you?" ...You'll just get a closer look. "..." The light is so blinding when you're right up against the beam, it's hard to see; yet the crystal is perfectly visible, sucking all of the radiant incandescence into its body as it hovers in the air an inch or two above the pedestal's surface, bobbing up and down ever so slowly. Or is it emitting the light? No, it couldn't be, in that case it would be going off in all directions instead of being a cleanly defined beam surrounding it, right? And yet... [pc.isMage |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all. And the Belharans had one for every one of their warships? Wow. |[pc.bg scholar acolyte |You've only read about it in books, but the description matches: solid ley-crystal, its surface polished to a sheen and the red color lost in the refining process but otherwise as it would be found in nature, imperfections and all. And the Belharans had one for every one of their warships? Wow. |There's something about this black crystal orb that against all logic is emitting and absorbing the magical light all at once, a sense of dread and wonder that sets in just by being close to it. ] ] "Look out!" With those words, Atugia grabs you by the collar of your [pc.armor] and hauls you backwards just in time for a crackling bolt of wayward radiance to narrowly miss you. It doesn't actually cause any damage to the wooden walkway that bridges the nest of pipes or the spot where you were standing, but the scorched, chemical smell it leaves lingering in the air strongly suggests that you wouldn't want to have been hit by that. Phew, that was close. There isn't any way to shut all of this down from where you are, is there? "None of the runes looked to be related to that kind of thing, and I'm not sure that'd be a good idea anyway; the demons would notice and come runnin' down." Atugia looks you up and down, then starts leading you back to Gweyr. "I think we'd better get back before anything else like that happens." "

rows.original: find Kiyoko kneeling beside you, studying the runic descriptions as intently as you were. What's she doing here? "Ah. Well, I can hardly allow you to walk into danger all by yourself, can I, beloved? Now then, there is no need to get too close to the engine core. The light is there to contain the energies present, but you would not want to be hit by a stray discharge." Well, when she puts it that way... you'll take a step or two back with her, then. Now, she knows about these things? "Some. I observed from a distance while one of the sailors explained it to me, although in not quite technical terms. The one or two war-wizards who came with the advanced fleet weren't so willing to talk... but sailors do." Kiyoko sighs, looking lost in thought. "This is the engine core of the ship, and is what provides the motive force to propel it through the water. Inscribed upon the base or the core holder are runes representing storm, sea and wind, based on those which the Belharans observed in Teiglache." You see. Why runes, though? "It is the same reason why both the Macahnese and we are accustomed to using paper charms for several purposes. Although they are far weaker than gems as foci, the good thing about spells based on symbology is that you can draw or paint them and forget about them for a good long while — good for places which are too dangerous to approach on a regular or extended basis, such as the engine core of a ship such as this." Right. And the black crystal orb in the middle... does she know what it is? "Refined ley-crystal, such that the natural impurities that make it red or green have been excised from the structure, turning it black." ...You'll just get a closer look. "..." The light is so blinding when you're right up against the beam, it's hard to see; yet the crystal is perfectly visible, sucking all of the radiant incandescence into its body as it hovers in the air an inch or two above the pedestal's surface, bobbing up and down ever so slowly. Or is it emitting the light? No, it couldn't be, in that case it would be going off in all directions instead of being a cleanly defined beam surrounding it, right? And yet... "Mmm. Please refrain from venturing too far, beloved. There is nothing to be gained from getting too close that I cannot tell you outright." Right. You... you were just drawn to it. Like a moth to a flame, really... but you're glad she was here to pull you back from the brink. Phew, that was close. There isn't any way to shut all of this down from here, is there? "That would be up on the ship's bridge, and I do not believe that would accomplish anything substantial towards our goal here." Kiyoko looks you up and down, her expression completely placid. "We should return to Gweyr before something worse happens."
rows.translation: 你发现清子正跪在你身旁，和她一样专注地研究那些符文描述。 这是什么 她 啊，亲爱的，我总不能让你独自去面对危险吧？现在，你不需要太靠近发动机核心。那里的灯轻型其实是用来约束那些能量的，但你肯定不希望被意外的电弧击中吧。 嗯，既然她这么说了……那你也就只好顺着她的思路来想了。现在，她已经知道这些事情了？ “知道一些。当时有水手向我解释这些，虽然用的并不是非常专业的术语，但我还是在远处观察了一下。 那些随先进舰队一同而来的军用法师们，并不太愿意开口交谈……不过水手们倒是愿意。”清子叹了口气，似乎陷入了沉思，“这就是飞船的动力核心，正是它提供了推动飞船在水中前进的动力。 在底座或核心支架上刻有象征风暴、海洋和风的符文，这些符文源自贝拉尔人在泰格拉切观察到的自然现象。 你明白的。不过，为什么要用符文呢？ “原因和马卡尼人以及我们习惯使用纸质护身符来达到多种目的是一样的。虽然这些纸质护身符作为法术的媒介，其效果远不如宝石，但基于象征符号的法术有一个很大的优点：你可以把它们画出来或者绘制出来，然后很长一段时间都不再去管它们——这对于那些过于危险、不适合经常或长时间接近的地方来说，简直再理想不过了，比如像这样的飞船的引擎核心区域。 没错。而中间那个黑色水晶球……她知道那是什么吗？ “那是经过提纯的 ley 水晶，那些让它呈现红色或绿色的天然杂质已经被完全去除，因此它变成了黑色。” ……你只要仔细看看就能明白了。 当你紧贴着那束轻型线时，轻型芒会强烈到让人无法看清周围的事物；然而，那颗水晶却清晰可见——它悬浮在基座表面上一两英寸的地方，缓缓地上下晃动，将所有耀眼的轻型芒都吸收到了自己的体内。还是说，其实是它自己在发轻型呢？不，不可能，如果是这样的话，轻型芒应该会向四面八方散开，而不会形成一道清晰可见的轻型束围绕在它周围，对吧？但事实却…… 嗯，亲爱的，請不要走得太远。靠得太近并不会带来任何我无法直接告诉你的好处。” 对吧，你……你只是被它吸引住了。就像飞蛾扑火一样……不过还好她在这里，把你从边缘拉了回来。呼，真是千钧一发啊。从现在开始，已经没有任何办法阻止这一切发生了，对吧？ 那应该是在船的桥楼上进行的，而且我认为那样做对我们实现当前的目标并没有什么实质性的帮助。”清子上下打量了你一番，表情十分平静，“在更糟糕的事情发生之前，我们还是应该回到格韦尔吧。
