rows.original:
The clear water's tempting, but ultimately it's not something you want to mess with. You've heard all sorts of horror stories about fountains in your time to be instinctively wary of them, especially in ancient ruined locations like where you're standing right now.

            Well, if you're not going to bother with the fountain, then the only way is forward, then...
rows.translation:
清澈的泉水确实很诱人，但归根结底，这种东西还是最好不要去招惹。这些年来，你肯定听过各种各样关于这些喷泉的恐怖故事，因此你本能上就会对它们保持警惕，尤其是在像你现在所处的这种古老废墟之中。

那么，如果你决定不去理会这个喷泉的话，那么唯一的出路就是……
rows.raw:
"
            The clear water's tempting, but ultimately it's not something you want to mess with. You've heard all sorts of horror stories about fountains in your time to be instinctively wary of them, especially in ancient ruined locations like where you're standing right now.

            Well, if you're not going to bother with the fountain, then the only way is forward, then..."

rows.original: Rushing up the worn granite steps[party.hasCompanions| with [party.compNames] hot on your tail], you find yourself before a large stone altar, perhaps the size of a table. Ancient pillars, crumbling under the weight of the earth until they were recently excavated. Several statues lie in various states of disrepair, all of them depicting the goddess Sorra in various appropriately grand poses. Broken marble crunches underfoot as you pass several smaller secondary shrines on your way to the altar, a small group of figures huddled together in front of it and speaking, apparently not having noticed your intrusion yet. "...All right. Make haste down the mountain and back to the base of operations. Meet up with the main group posthaste." "Yes, Master Whisper."[party.has quin| "Whisper?" Quintillus raises a brow, clutching his chin in one hand. "I don't... think I remember there being someone in charge with that name..."] The cloaked figures take off towards the back of the chamber — they must've dug out an exit on the far side of their excavation site, then. Their footsteps are loud and echo off the ruddy cavern walls as they break into a jog, clearly not expecting anyone to be around; if you used the noise to cover your approach, perhaps you could approach the lone remaining figure without being spotted. It's such a great opportunity, too. A single small figure all by itself, black-cloaked in the manner of Tollus's demon cult. A dwarf, perhaps, or a midget no more than four and a half feet tall — who knows what kind of freaks Tollus has recruited for his posse? He seems to be extremely interested in the altar's surface, examining it by torchlight and clearly absorbed in whatever he's doing. [pc.bg slumrat |You've lived long enough as a slum rat for this to be reflexive at this point, ingrained into muscle memory. Sneak up, knock him out, relieve him of any weapons, then decide what to do when all's said and done. It's not something one would be proud of, but if it meant the difference between eating and going hungry, having food in one's belly was always the better option. |[pc.cl thief |You've had training as a thief, this should be a piece of cake for you. Sneaking up on the unsuspecting and knocking them out before relieving them of their valuables is basic thieves' work, and this couldn't have been a more textbook target. |While you're not exactly trained in the arts of subtlety and assassination, this looks like it's an open-and-shut case. Creeping up and beating this little creature upside the head shouldn't be that big an issue, then you can get around to searching the chamber. ] ] [party.has quin|Quin ignores you, still mumbling to himself. "The only question is where? Wasn't that like... one of the recruits I heard about?"] [party.has einin |"I'll do it," Einin whispers, stepping ahead of you and drawing her [einin.weapon]. "Leave it to a professional." [pc.cl thief |Tch. You're a professional too, but if she wants to show off so badly, she's more than welcome to steal the show. |All right, then. You'll leave it to her, since she presumably knows what she's doing and all. ] Einin nods, and the mousegirl slinks off into the shadows, blending seamlessly with her element. Even knowing she's there, you can just make out the faint silhouette of her passing, moving at a slow but steady pace towards the altar. The cloaked figure still seems completely absorbed in his examination of the ruin — up till the moment Einin brings her weapon down in the space where he'd been a moment ago. The mousegirl looks utterly shocked, mouth half-agape as a lamp suddenly flares to life right in her face, blinding her. She squeaks, instinctively falling back to a defensive posture to buy time to recover. "Oh. Look at who it is. Now this is truly surprising." The words come in a loud, hoarse whisper, as if his vocal chords aren't quite working right. As the figure holds up the lamp in his hand, you get a good look at his features: a mecian like Einin, although possessed of considerably more rodent-like characteristics than the mousegirl. His face is fully animalistic, complete with a short muzzle, and what's exposed of his body under that dark, voluminous cloak is covered with a pelt of fine brown fur. Under ordinary circumstances, this little guy might've looked cute like so many mecians manage effortlessly, but the rows of tattoos on his muzzle that give his lips the appearance of having been stitched shut when they're together more or less ruins any hope of that. Einin steps back and brandishes her [einin.weapon], blinking furiously to clear her vision. She hisses, breath rushing through her teeth, but doesn't say anything. "And what were you hoping to do once you'd disabled me, hmm?" "Berach!" "It's been a while, Einin. And don't call me by that name anymore — I have a new name, for a new me. I don't expect you to acknowledge it, but you may call me Whisper from here on out." "That's not your name! Wha... what are you doing with these people, Berach? Don't you know that they're —" " — Causing all sorts of problems for us poor, unobtrusive mecians? Of course, it's part of why I'm with them in the first place. There you are again, always assuming I'm stupid. No, I know full well what we've been doing in Harvest Valley, and to be perfectly frank, I've been lending my expertise to most of these efforts. Master Tollus has been quite pleased with the results, I'll say." Einin closes her eyes and bites her lip, then shakes her head slowly. ".Are you insane?!" "We-ll. I'm not gibbering and foaming at the mouth in the manner one might expect of a religious zealot, if that's what you mean. We left those idiots at the river to have their fun so the actual work can get done without them mucking about in our way. But here I am, years after you left me to rot, and the first words you throw at me upon our joyous reunion are demands upon demands without so much as a hello. Oh, that cut deep, so deep." You don't know what's going on here, but Einin's clearly not herself right now, and it's not just because Whisper is one of her kind. One look at the naked terror and guilt written all over her face is enough to assure you of that. She swallows hard. "Berach... that day it wasn't- we were doing- I didn't know and I didn't mean to —" "You knew exactly what you were doing. So much for friend, folk and field. In hindsight, it was the best thing that ever happened to me." All right, time for you to step in and ask some questions of your own. |Nothing for it, then. The diminutive figure doesn't budge an inch; you barely dare to breathe as you creep through the darkness and come within arm's length of him. Raising your [pc.weapon], you bring it down upon his head — or at least where his head was but seconds ago. There's a blur in the shadows, and then the figure is standing to the side, holding up a freshly lit lamp to your face. "And what were you hoping to do once you'd bludgeoned me out cold, hmm?" The words come in a loud, hoarse whisper, as if his vocal chords aren't quite working right. Blinking furiously to clear your vision from the sudden illumination, you take in just who it is you're faced with. A tiny mouse-man — or boy; given the proportions, you're not quite sure which. Fully animalistic, complete with a muzzle, soft ears and twitching whiskers, he's covered in a fine pelt of fuzzy brown fur where he's not covered by the dark, voluminous cloak he's wearing. Perhaps under more ordinary circumstances, he might have been cute, even adorable; any hope of that is ruined by the rows of tattoos on his muzzle about his lips, giving them the impression of having being stitched shut when they're together. [pc.isDK |Why, at that point what would it matter to him? Not that he'd be able to stop you in that case, but you'd probably be satisfied with ruining his little operation here, claiming any loose artifacts he and his have been so kind to do the hard work of digging up, and generally kicking the crap out of him. |Why, just claim the artifacts he and his have been working so hard to dig up and prevent them from falling into Master Tollus's grubby little hands. A worthy cause, certainly. ] "Ah. As much as the Master warned me to take note of. He's still very much sore about you, would-be Champion." Well, you're glad you left such an impression on Tollus that you're living in his head rent-free.[party.has quin| Even now, you can't help but notice Quintillus squinting at the mouse. Is he seriously still stuck on remembering who this is when they're right here? Whisper just told you who he was!] "The Master is a touchy man. Possessing much vision and ambition, to be certain, but he does not take losses well, especially those against people he holds a grudge against." [party.has quin| At last, Quin snaps and points at the mouse. "That's it! You were the little cutie who I was thinking about fucking-" Whisper glares at Quin and you don't blame him. Yet he returns his attention to you, somewhat letting his hostility relax. Perhaps there had been more than a brief encounter between the two within the cult.] "But come, even if we are enemies, we should have at least some small measure of civility. Allow me to introduce myself — you may call me Whisper. And you?" [pc.isDK |Why, he can go fuck himself. "Ah well. I suppose for you and the Master to be so much at odds, the two of you have to be quite alike, eh? Like I said, your fame precedes you, [pc.name]. I'm sure a self-obsessed [pc.mf|man|woman] like you enjoys all the attention and recognition." |[pc.name]. A nod. "I appreciate the gesture." ] So, is this the moment he explains everything, is it? ] "Why, ask away. I'll explain everything." Why all this effort to get at an old ruin? What does Master Tollus want? Certainly he wouldn't have had hands digging into the mountain for what must have been weeks for no good reason. "Well, you're certainly right about the digging for weeks part. Even with the... ah, advanced tools we were supplied with, unearthing this place from the rockslide it'd been buried under for decades, if not centuries, involved quite a bit of effort. Without the roof holding out, our task would have been much more arduous and taken longer than the month we spent. Just our misfortune that you should arrive on the next-to-last day; I imagine that big bucket-headed brute and his barricade grew lax. Oh well, they got what they deserved. I'll pick up what's left of that lot on the way down." You shake your head. And just what does Master Tollus want from this once open-air altar? [party.has quin|Just before Whisper speaks, Quin sets his hands on his hips and interrupts. "What wouldn't he want? That bastard is a thief; all he does is desire to take, no matter who it's from." "This time," Whisper sighs. "The taeleer is on point; touchy Master may be, he is no fool. You don't think it's strange to merely be fascinated in these ancient places and their relics? The weapons of one's enemies can teach you how best to counter them." Quintillus lets his good mood entirely fall through. "The only thing Tollus should rightfully fear is the day I put him in a grave."|"Well, the Master has been taking a keen interest in such holy relics for a little while now. You don't think it's strange for a learned man like him to be fascinated by places of the past like this, and the relics they hold? After all, seeking out the weapons of your enemy and learning how they work is the first step to countering them. I'm sure you won't be the only do-gooder who thinks to gain gold and glory by stopping him, eh?"] So, he's doing all this on Kasyrra's orders? "Mm-mm." How noncommittal. That could be a yes or no... And what's his role in all of this? "Little old me? I'm merely here to oversee the dig and appraise all finds, that's all. [party.has einin |I'm sure your little mouse friend over there will be willing to tell you everything about it. Whether or not she does it truthfully is your problem. |Someone's got to be able to tell what's valuable and what's not in this entire mess of broken bits and pieces — someone with half a brain, that is. ]" And just what does he get out of all this, anyway? "You know, that's a very interesting question. Most wouldn't stop to question just why people would join up with a demon cult. It's not as if we wake up one day and tell ourselves, 'all right, this is the day I'm going to become an evil bastard and start worshipping a horrible creature that lurks in the void between the spheres.' We're just there, obstacles to be overcome. Who cares about the root causes that lure people to such extreme lengths, right? Weakness or vulnerability or temptation can't explain everything, can it?" "Well, I can't speak for others, but I can certainly speak for myself. I was recruited by Master Tollus because he's a man with a vision of how the world ought to be, and a definite plan to achieve that vision. One that I share after... ah, certain things happened to me. Not all at once — over many years, in fact. But the opportunity to do anything meaningful about it never arose until Master Tollus came along. As they used to say, 'give me a big enough lever, and I will move the world.' Master Tollus is that lever." [party.has einin |"You're not serious!" Einin manages to choke out. "I'm always serious, Einin. When have I never been serious?" ] Come to think of it, it's awfully nice of him to spill the beans to you. Is he a fan of villainous monologues? Is that something Tollus instructs his lieutenants to do, spill their life history, plans and goals at every opportunity? Whisper tsks at your jibe. "Well, as you see, sometimes it pays to play along with your enemies' games. While [party.som||the both of |the lot of ]you were so kind to stand here like [party.hasCompanions|idiots|an idiot] and listen to me speak, I imagine my underlings have made quite the distance down the mountain. Certainly far enough that you won't be able to pick up their trail, let alone stop them before they reach the Master with the prism. Meanwhile, you have no idea if everything I just told you was a fanciful figment of my imagination I conjured on the spot, a lie to send you in the exact opposite direction." Oh. Wait. The prism, he said. He wasn't here after a spear — he wasn't here to retrieve Sorra's Succor for Master Tollus in the first place. That means there might be a chance it's still around; even if you can't prevent the demon cultists from achieving their goals, you might still be able to achieve yours. If only you can get this little rodent out of the way so you can search the dig... That's at least one mistake this smug little mouse has made. [party.has einin |"All you were ever good at was stalling for time anyway, Berach!" "Ah, well. The selfish scoundrel remembers herself at last. How quaint." "We of the farms and fields —" Whisper just leers. "I don't ever remember that courtesy ever being extended to me, least of all by you, and as such I feel no obligation to pay it back. Ironic that you seek to use that false conviction against me. ] "Now then. While I would love to continue with this lovely conversation and hold you up even longer, the Master does have quite the sizable bounty out for you, would-be Champion of Hawkethorne. I'd like to see if I can't claim it for myself and get further into his good graces, maybe even get another promotion. The Master may have a few screws loose in his head, but he's no idiot." [party.has einin |"I won't let him hurt them," Einin murmurs under her breath, readying her [einin.weapon] with shaking hands. Her words seem more aimed at convincing herself than anyone else. "[pc.name], you can't let him escape. For his own good...." Right. Anyone who would willingly join Tollus's little demon cult can't be right in the head. "..." ] Before you can blink, Whisper darts forward, the tiny mousefolk moving at an incredible speed, dropping the lamp to shatter on the floor as he leaps from shadow to shadow. You have barely enough time to raise your [pc.weapon] to defend yourself as his twin daggers flash in your face, their serrated edges poised to strike. [party.hasCompanions |He certainly doesn't seem the least bit concerned with being outnumbered as he is — and with how quickly Whisper moves, you can see why. ] It's a fight!
rows.translation: 匆匆走上那些磨损的花岗岩台阶[party.hasCompanions| 与……一起 [party.compNames] 紧追不舍]你发现自己站在一座巨大的石制祭坛前，这座祭坛的大小大概与一张桌子相当。那些古老的石柱在大地的重压下早已开始崩塌，直到最近才被人们挖掘出来。几座雕像也处于不同程度的破损状态，但它们全都刻画着索拉女神，而且每一个姿势都显得极为庄严宏伟。 当你走向祭坛时，足部下踩着碎裂的大理石碎片。沿途还有几座较小的附属神龛，一小群人正聚集在祭坛前交谈，显然他们还没有注意到你的存在。 ……好吧，赶紧下山，回到行动基地，尽快与主力部队会合。 是的，低语大师。[party.has quin| 低语？”昆蒂勒斯挑了挑眉毛，一只手托着下巴。“我不太明白…… 思考 我记得当时有一个人负责这件事，他的名字就是……] 那些披着斗篷的身影向大厅的后部跑去——看来他们一定在挖掘区域的另一侧找到了出口。他们的足部步声很响，在红褐色的洞壁上回荡着，他们开始小跑起来，显然没有料到会有人在那里；如果你利用这些噪音来掩盖自己的接近声，或许就能悄悄接近那个独自留下的身影，而不被发现。 这也是一个绝佳的机会。那个独自出现的小身影，穿着托卢斯恶魔崇拜团体特有的黑色服装——或许是个矮人，又或许是个身高不超过四点五英尺的侏儒……谁知道托卢斯为他的团队招募了哪些怪人呢？ 他似乎对祭坛的表面充满了极大的兴趣，正借着火把的光仔细观察它，整个人都完全沉浸在正在做的事情中。 [pc.bg slumrat |作为贫民窟的居民，你早已习惯了这种行为方式，它已经成为了你的本能反应，深植于你的记忆之中。悄悄接近他，将他打晕，夺走他手中的任何武器，然后再决定接下来该怎么做。这种行为或许并不值得骄傲，但如果你因此能够免于挨饿，拥有食物填饱肚子，那么选择这样做总归是更好的。 |[pc.cl thief |你接受过盗贼训练，这对你来说应该易如反掌。悄悄接近毫无防备的人，将他们打晕后再抢走他们的财物，这才是盗贼的基本功啊——而这个目标简直再完美不过了。 |虽然你并不擅长运用隐秘行动和暗杀技巧，但这次的情况看起来再明显不过了。悄悄接近然后敲晕这个小家伙应该不会有什么问题，之后你就可以去搜查那个房间了。 ] ] [party.has quin|奎因没有理你，仍在自言自语：“唯一的问题是 rows.raw: " Rushing up the worn granite steps[party.hasCompanions| with [party.compNames] hot on your tail], you find yourself before a large stone altar, perhaps the size of a table. Ancient pillars, crumbling under the weight of the earth until they were recently excavated. Several statues lie in various states of disrepair, all of them depicting the goddess Sorra in various appropriately grand poses. Broken marble crunches underfoot as you pass several smaller secondary shrines on your way to the altar, a small group of figures huddled together in front of it and speaking, apparently not having noticed your intrusion yet. "...All right. Make haste down the mountain and back to the base of operations. Meet up with the main group posthaste." "Yes, Master Whisper."[party.has quin| "Whisper?" Quintillus raises a brow, clutching his chin in one hand. "I don't... think I remember there being someone in charge with that name..."] The cloaked figures take off towards the back of the chamber — they must've dug out an exit on the far side of their excavation site, then. Their footsteps are loud and echo off the ruddy cavern walls as they break into a jog, clearly not expecting anyone to be around; if you used the noise to cover your approach, perhaps you could approach the lone remaining figure without being spotted. It's such a great opportunity, too. A single small figure all by itself, black-cloaked in the manner of Tollus's demon cult. A dwarf, perhaps, or a midget no more than four and a half feet tall — who knows what kind of freaks Tollus has recruited for his posse? He seems to be extremely interested in the altar's surface, examining it by torchlight and clearly absorbed in whatever he's doing. [pc.bg slumrat |You've lived long enough as a slum rat for this to be reflexive at this point, ingrained into muscle memory. Sneak up, knock him out, relieve him of any weapons, then decide what to do when all's said and done. It's not something one would be proud of, but if it meant the difference between eating and going hungry, having food in one's belly was always the better option. |[pc.cl thief |You've had training as a thief, this should be a piece of cake for you. Sneaking up on the unsuspecting and knocking them out before relieving them of their valuables is basic thieves' work, and this couldn't have been a more textbook target. |While you're not exactly trained in the arts of subtlety and assassination, this looks like it's an open-and-shut case. Creeping up and beating this little creature upside the head shouldn't be that big an issue, then you can get around to searching the chamber. ] ] [party.has quin|Quin ignores you, still mumbling to himself. "The only question is where? Wasn't that like... one of the recruits I heard about?"] [party.has einin |"I'll do it," Einin whispers, stepping ahead of you and drawing her [einin.weapon]. "Leave it to a professional." [pc.cl thief |Tch. You're a professional too, but if she wants to show off so badly, she's more than welcome to steal the show. |All right, then. You'll leave it to her, since she presumably knows what she's doing and all. ] Einin nods, and the mousegirl slinks off into the shadows, blending seamlessly with her element. Even knowing she's there, you can just make out the faint silhouette of her passing, moving at a slow but steady pace towards the altar. The cloaked figure still seems completely absorbed in his examination of the ruin — up till the moment Einin brings her weapon down in the space where he'd been a moment ago. The mousegirl looks utterly shocked, mouth half-agape as a lamp suddenly flares to life right in her face, blinding her. She squeaks, instinctively falling back to a defensive posture to buy time to recover. "Oh. Look at who it is. Now this is truly surprising." The words come in a loud, hoarse whisper, as if his vocal chords aren't quite working right. rows.original: "Ugh..." Out of both the strength and will to keep on fighting, Whisper staggers back against a nearby toppled statue of Sorra, daggers falling from his grasp and clattering to the ground. His eyes dart this way and that in the dim light, seeking a route of escape. "...I suppose I failed to appreciate your strength. The loss is mine." [party.has einin |"It's over, Berach." Breathing hard through gritted teeth, Einin steps forward, her [einin.weapon] still leveled at Whisper. She's not taking any chances. "Surrender and... and I'll make things right. I'll show you what we were working for... and let them handle us both. . You can't be allowed to continue like this." "Not... going to finish me off? Curious. It's not as if you don't have the stomach for it." Whisper's gaze rolls back and forth between Einin and you as he lets out a rasping chuckle. "[pc.isDK|Why, do you need this would-be champion's leave to do even the smallest thing? Do you get off on being beaten down and dominated? Is that it?|Has this goody-two-shoes of a would-be champion rubbed off on you, of all people? Turned over a new leaf, have you? Using the skills you learned for the cause of good and all?] What a joke." Einin makes a frustrated noise in the back of her throat. "Berach, I'm trying to help you here! But if you won't accept that you're wrong, even with me on the line... then maybe I should just leave you here!." "Oh, so only now have you figured that you don't like me? I knew that years ago. As for your other statement... I'm not going back to that place one way or another. Trust me on that." |Hmph. Interesting that unlike his master, he can tell when he's beaten. "What... what was the saying again?" Whisper gasps in that hoarse, breathless voice of his. "Garbage in, garbage out. If you don't ever acknowledge your mistakes, you'll never improve." That's surprisingly clear-headed for a murderous demon cultist. Just why exactly is he with Tollus and his posse again? "Have you ever considered... that just as the Master sees the demoness as an opportunity, I see him as a way to achieve certain ends?" ] This is pointless. He's clearly stalling for more time while he recovers and his underlings get ever further from this place. Once bitten, twice shy; whatever you're going to end up doing to him, it's best to apprehend this little bastard first. Without letting your guard down in the slightest[party.hasCompanions| and with [party.compNames] backing you up], you approach a still-grimacing Whisper and make to grab him. What happens next is unexpected. While you were certain he would put up some kind of resistance[party.hasCompanions| and had [party.compNames] flank him], Whisper drops straight to the ground instead, hitting the stone floor with a dull thud. You immediately lower your [pc.weapon], ready for him to spring up at you in some sort of ruse, but the shape within the dark, voluminous cloak melts away in the blink of an eye, leaving behind little more than heavy cloth as you swing down upon it. Where could he — [party.has einin |"There!" Einin yells, pointing, already attacking. ] You whirl around at the sound of footsteps to find Whisper limping away into the darkness, following the footsteps of his underlings. Even with the little mecian's awkward, shuffling gait, he's covering distance at an astounding rate, and you see why: Whisper's leaping from shadow to shadow, melding into one and exiting through the other as if the patches of darkness were portals. As things are, no matter how quick you're on your feet, there's no hope of catching up to him, not in this dimly lit place beneath the earth. [party.has einin |I-is that something he could do? "No... he wasn't like me, he wasn't trained in magic. Not even my mom could do something like that. ." "Ah well, Einin." Whisper's ghastly voice echoes back through the tunnels to you. "I can't stay the same man you once knew forever. People change. "Now if you'll excuse me, I have to report our success to the Master." ] [party.has cait |"Damn it!" Cait rears back, conjuring a glowing sphere of light in a hand, the other tightly gripped about her staff. "I'm not letting him get away!" You can see where she's coming from; she's trying to dispel the shadows so Whisper can't use them to escape. It's too late for that, though, even as Cait hurls the ball of energy down the tunnel after him. It sails through the air, travels some distance, and finally explodes in a burst of brilliance, but you get the feeling that the effort was ultimately fruitless. ] Wonder if there'll be more cultists coming, or if that's the last of them. There weren't any shortages of patrols on your way up here from the camp... [party.has arona |"If there are, leave them to me," Arona growls. "That little rat bastard wasn't fun to fight in the slightest, and now I'm all worked up and ticked off with no way to let loose." ]
rows.translation: 呃…… 凭借着顽强的意志和继续战斗的力量，Whisper踉跄着退到了附近一座倒下的Sorra雕像旁，手中的匕首掉落在地，发出刺耳的声响。在昏暗的轻型线中，他的目轻型四处游移，试图寻找一条逃生之路。 ……我想，是我没有充分认识到你的实力。这次失败，确实是我的责任。 [party.has einin |一切都结束了，贝拉赫。 艾宁咬紧牙关，喘着粗气向前走去。 [einin.weapon] 她的等级仍然停留在“低语”阶段。她不想冒任何风险。 投降吧……我会把一切都弄好的。我会让你看到我们之前努力追求的目标……让他们来处理我们俩的事情。你不能再这样下去了。 不……打算把我干掉吗？真有意思。你明明有这个能力啊。 Whisper的目轻型在Einin和你之间来回扫视，同时发出了一声沙哑的笑声。 "[pc.isDK|为什么就连做最简单的事情，你也需要这个所谓的“冠军许可”呢？你是从被击败、被支配中获得快感吗？就是这个原因吗？|难道就是你，这个自以为是的伪君子，被这个所谓的“冠军”影响了吧？你终于改过自新了，是吗？开始用你所学到的技能去做好事了，对吧？] 真是个笑话。 艾宁在喉咙深处发出了一声沮丧的声音。 贝拉赫，我真的是想帮你啊！但如果你就是不肯承认自己错了，即使我也在这里劝你……那么也许我应该干脆离开你吧…… 哦，原来只是这样啊 现在 你难道还没意识到自己其实并不喜欢我吗？几年前我就已经知道了。至于你说的另外那件事……无论如何，我都不会再去那个地方了。相信我，这一点我是绝对不会改变的。 |哼，有意思的是，与他的大师不同，他知道自己什么时候被打败了。 那个……那个说法到底是啥来着？ Whisper用他那沙哑、急促的声音喘息着。 输入的是垃圾，输出的自然也是垃圾。如果你从不承认自己的错误，就永远无法进步。 对于一个嗜杀的恶魔崇拜者来说，他的头脑居然如此清醒，实在令人惊讶。那么，他究竟为什么又会跟托卢斯以及他的那些同伙在一起呢？ 你有没有想过……就像那位大师将那个女恶魔视为一个机会一样，我则把他看作实现某些目标的手段？ ] 这毫无意义。他显然是在拖延时间，好让自己有更多时间恢复体力，同时也让他的手下们有更多机会离开这个地方。一朝被蛇咬，十年怕井绳；无论你最终要对他采取什么行动，最好先抓住这个小混蛋。千万不能有丝毫松懈。[party.hasCompanions| 并且与……一同 [party.compNames] 支持你]你走近那个仍在痛苦地扭曲着面容的Whisper，准备抓住他。 然而接下来发生的事情完全出乎意料。你原本以为他会进行某种抗性[party.hasCompanions| 并且拥有 [party.compNames] 从侧面包抄他]Whisper直接掉到了地上，发出沉闷的撞击声，砸在了石质的地板上。你立刻低下了头 [pc.weapon]你本以为他会用某种诡计突然出现在你面前，但那隐藏在厚重斗篷中的身影却在一瞬间消失了，只剩下那层厚重的布料。当你俯身去抓它时，才发现……他究竟去了哪里？ [party.has einin |就是那里！ 艾宁大喊着，一边指向目标，一边发动了攻击。 ] 听到足部步声，你猛地转过身，发现Whisper正一瘸一拐地消失在暗影中，他正跟随着那些下属的足部步前进。尽管那个小小的机械生物走路时显得笨拙而摇摇晃晃，但他的移动速度却快得惊人。你现在明白为什么了：Whisper正在一片片阴影之间跳跃，时而融入其中，时而又从另一片阴影中钻出来，就好像那些暗影区域其实是传送门一样。 事实上，无论你多么迅速地行动，也根本不可能追上他——尤其是在这个昏暗的地下环境中。 [party.has einin |他真的有能力做到这件事吗？ 不……他和我不一样，他并没有接受过魔法训练。就连我妈妈也不可能做出那样的事情来…… 唉，艾宁。 Whisper那令人毛骨悚然的声音在隧道中回荡，传到了你的耳边。 我再也不能永远保持你曾经认识的那个样子了。人会改变的。 现在，请允许我离开，我必须去向大师汇报我们的成功。 ] [party.has cait |该死！ 凯特向后退了一步，一只手凝聚出一团发光的光球，另一只手则紧紧握着她的法杖。 我绝不会让他逃掉！ 你可以理解她的出发点——她是在试图驱散那些阴影，这样Whisper就无法利用它们逃脱了。然而，为时已晚。即使凯特把那团能量球扔进了隧道里，它依然在空气中飞行了一段距离，最终才爆发出一道光芒，但你能感觉到，这一切努力最终还是徒劳无功的。 ] 不知道还会不会有更多的邪教徒出现，还是说他们已经全部到齐了。从营地往这里来的路上，巡逻队可一点都没有少…… [party.has arona |如果有的话，就交给我吧。 阿罗娜低吼着。 那个小混蛋，跟它打架简直一点乐趣都没有，现在我气得不行，却找不到发泄的方式。 ]

rows.original: No point wasting time. Assuming Whisper wasn't lying through his teeth, there might be a chance you might still be able to find what Brother Sanders wants out of you now that you've driven off the maladjusted mouse. Looking about the ruins of the once open-air altar, you quickly identify several likely spots and [party.hasCompanions |direct [party.compNames] to assist you in the search for the spear. Splitting up lets you cover much more ground in as much time, and you don't want to risk reinforcements arriving while you're preoccupied. |start with the search for the spear. It's a nerve-wracking task, with you constantly worried that you're going to be ambushed while preoccupied with looking, but by good fortune or good fate no one arrives to spoil the show. ] Damn it, this is getting annoying real quickly... [party.hasCompanions |"Any luck?" [comp1.name] calls out to you. Not really. You've been sifting through several mounds of unearthed stone and pottery shards, but it looks like nothing's there. What about [comp1.himHer]? "I found several racks of spears — or at least, what used to be spears," comes the reply. "The wooden shafts have long since crumbled to dust. Nothing that looks like it's an artifact, though." Right, right. ] And then it hits you. Whisper was examining the altar when you arrived on the scene, and as it turned out, it'd been a ruse to lull you into a false sense of self-confidence. But what if it was also a ruse instead of being just one? Could it be? You'd looked over the altar before, but found not much of note on the smooth marble. Maybe it would bear further investigation... [pc.bg acolyte |your religious upbringing is enough that you're fully aware that altars are used for something; they're not just there to look grand and imposing. |while you're not too clear on the details of the worship of Sorra, you're pretty sure that altars aren't just there for decoration. ] Even so, none of the remains nearby indicate what it might have been used for... either way, maybe you should give it another look-over before committing yourself to returning empty-handed. With that thought in mind, you begin poring over the altar's dusty surface, moving your gaze from top to sides and finally to its heavyset base. Hmm. Whisper was studying the top and didn't appear to notice anything, so maybe somewhere else... oh! It's hard to see in the dim light, but there's no doubt about it: a smooth, hairline crack runs lengthwise along the side of the altar, then two more perpendicular to it on either end. There's still no sign of how to open it, but at least you're on the right track here. No doubt Whisper would have eventually spotted it had he the time for a thorough examination, but he didn't and now you're here in his place. Reinvigorated in your search, you look over the altar yet again, discovering a small piece of the decorative carvings along the base that looks like it could be moved. Without hesitation, you tug at it, and there's a dull thud from somewhere inside the stone altar. The hairline crack you spotted earlier widens, parts, and an entire section of the altar's side falls away to reveal its hollow center. There! A long, thin metal-bound case lies within, and you waste no time pulling it out and laying it on the altar's surface. The hinges are old and tarnished, but the case creaks open, and you're faced with a short spear. It's clearly ceremonial — no one would ever use such a thing in actual combat, lacking in actual reach and decorated as gaudily as it is, but if it's what Sanders wants, you're more than happy to give it to him. You don't feel any kind of magical or divine power emanating from the artifact as-is, but maybe you're just not sensitive to such things. [party.has cait |Come to think of it, does Cait feel anything coming from the relic? Your pink kitten grasps the old, dry shaft of the spear with both hands and runs her fingers up and down its length, thinning her lips. "Nope. I'd like to imagine I'm a little more sensitive than most, but I'm not getting anything, either." ] Well, you got what you came here for, and while you might not have completely ruined Master Tollus's designs on... whatever it is he's planning — assuming Whisper wasn't lying to begin with — you've at least made him pay through the nose for any gains he's made. It's not the most astounding victory you've had, but you'll take what you can get. Right. Time to get out of here. Following the tunnel forward in Whisper's footsteps eventually brings you back out into the open on the other side of the dig, amidst a bunch of abandoned scaffolding. From there, a thin trail loops back around to the front, passing back through the cultist camp and down the way you came up by. You keep your eyes peeled every step of the way, but it looks like now that they've achieved their goal, the demon cultists have all beaten a quick retreat, content to escape with their prize and lives. There's a lot of trash they left behind, especially the remains of the barricade, but that's part and parcel of a hasty withdrawal. The trip back down the trail and through the waterfall grotto is uneventful, and eventually you emerge back into the familiar sights of Harvest Valley. All that's left, you suppose, is to return the Sorran relic to Sanders and claim your reward. [party.has einin |Well, there's more than one thing that's, you suppose. Einin has been silent all the way down the mountain, the little mecian girl dragging her feet as she trails along behind you. Does she want to talk about it? "I... I don't know. Not now, at least. I... I've still got to get myself sorted out, let alone try getting it all to make sense to someone else." There's a lot she hasn't told her about herself. You'd like to hear it someday, when she feels she can trust you with it. "...[pc.name], we've all done things that we aren't exactly proud of. It's just a question of to what degree." Says the little mouse who used to make a living from being thoroughly and utterly unsavoury. But you can see where that was coming from, yes. Screwing over a big one, that's perfectly fine and dandy. But screwing over another mecian, another furred folk of the farms and fields — that's just not done, is it? Einin's awfully silent. Guess you hit the nail on the head there. Well, like she said, she'll open up about the details as and when she's gotten herself sorted out. For the moment, best head back to town. ]
rows.translation: 浪费时间毫无意义。假设Whisper没有在撒谎，那么现在你已经赶走了那个行为异常的家伙，或许还有机会找到Sanders兄弟真正想要的东西。你环顾着那座曾经用于露天祭祀的废墟，迅速找出了几个可能的地点 [party.hasCompanions |指导 [party.compNames] 为了帮助你们寻找那支长矛，我们决定分成几组行动。这样就能在相同的时间内覆盖更大的范围，而且我们也不希望因为在寻找过程中分心，而导致援军及时赶到。 |首先，开始寻找那支长矛吧。这项任务令人紧张不安，因为在全神贯注寻找的过程中，你总会担心会遭到埋伏，但幸运的是，没有人出现来破坏这个过程。 ] 该死，这种情况发展得也太快了，真是让人恼火…… [party.hasCompanions |有进展吗？ [comp1.name] 在呼唤着你。 其实并不是这样。你已经仔细检查了好几堆出土的石块和陶器碎片，但看起来里面什么都没有。那么 [comp1.himHer]? 我找到了几架装满长矛的架子——或者至少，那些东西曾经是长矛。 回复到来了。 那些木制杆子早已化为尘土，不过，其中并没有任何看起来像文物的东西。 好的，好的。 ] 然后你突然意识到了：当你赶到现场时，Whisper正在检查那个祭坛，而实际上，那只是一个诱使你产生虚假自信的诡计。但如果是这样的话 此外 其实是一种诡计罢了 只是 一个？真的有可能吗？ 你之前已经仔细检查过那个祭坛，但在轻型滑的大理石表面上并没有发现什么特别的痕迹。也许还需要进一步调查…… [pc.bg acolyte |你的宗教背景足以让你清楚地认识到，祭坛其实是 已使用 它们存在的意义不仅仅是为了显得宏伟壮观。 |虽然你对索拉崇拜的细节还不够了解，但你也清楚，那些祭坛绝对不是用来装饰的。 ] 即便如此，附近的任何遗迹都无法说明这个物体原本是用来做什么的……不管怎样，在确定最终会空手部而归之前，或许你应该再仔细检查一遍。 怀着这样的想法，你开始仔细观察祭坛那布满灰尘的表面，目轻型从顶部缓缓移到两侧，最后落在它那厚实的基座上。嗯……Whisper之前只是检查了顶部，似乎没有发现什么异常，那么也许是在其他地方……哦！ 在昏暗的轻型线下很难看清，但毫无疑问：祭坛的侧面有一条流畅的、细如发丝的裂缝，而在它的两端还各有一条与之垂直的裂缝。目前还没有发现如何打开它的方法，但至少你现在已经找到了正确的方向。 毫无疑问，如果 Whisper有足够的时间仔细检查，他最终一定会发现它的。但他没有，而现在你代替他来到了这里。重新振作起来继续搜寻，你再次仔细观察了那个祭坛，发现底座上有一小块装饰性雕刻，看起来是可以移动的。 你毫不犹豫地拉了拉它，顿时从石祭坛的内部传来一声沉闷的撞击声。你之前注意到的那道细裂缝逐渐扩大、裂开，祭坛的侧面有一整块结构随之脱落，露出了其中空的内部结构。 看到了！里面有一个长而细的金属箱，你立刻把它拿了出来，放在祭坛的表面。箱子的铰链已经老旧且生了锈，但当你把它打开时，里面是一支短矛。 这显然只是个象征性的物品——在实战中根本没人会使用这种东西，它的攻击范围实在太有限了，而且装饰得也太过花哨。但既然这是桑德斯想要的，你当然很乐意送给他。你并没有感觉到这件物品本身散发出任何神奇或神圣的力量，不过也许只是你对此类事物不够敏感罢了。 [party.has cait |仔细想来，是不是 凯特 你能感觉到那件遗物散发出的任何气息吗？ 你的粉色小猫用双手握住那根古老而干枯的长矛，用手指沿着它的长度来回滑动，同时微微抿起了嘴唇。 不。我愿意认为自己比大多数人更敏感一些，但实际上我也什么感觉都没有。 ] 嗯，你来得目的已经达到了。虽然你可能并没有完全破坏托卢斯大师的计划——假设威瑟本来就没有撒谎的话——但至少你让他为自己所取得的一切成果付出了沉重的代价。 这或许不是你取得过的最令人惊叹的胜利，但能得到什么就是什么了。 对，是时候离开这里了。 按照Whisper的足迹继续沿着隧道前进，最终你会来到挖掘工作的另一侧，那里有一堆被废弃的足部手部架，周围是一片开阔地带。 从那里开始，一条狭窄的小路蜿蜒着回到前方，穿过那些邪教徒的营地，然后沿着你来时的路线继续向下延伸。你每走一步都保持着高度警惕，但看起来，既然他们已经达到了目的，那些恶魔邪教徒们也都迅速撤退了，他们只求带着自己的战利品和性命逃走罢了。 他们留下了很多垃圾，尤其是那些路障的残余，但这种匆忙撤退的行为本身就难免会留下这些痕迹。 沿着小路返回，穿过瀑布洞穴，整个过程没有发生任何意外，最终你重新回到了熟悉的丰收谷景象之中。 你认为，现在剩下的就是把索兰的遗物归还给桑德斯，然后领取你的奖励了。 [party.has einin |嗯，其实有好几件事吧……艾宁一路上都没有说话，那个小小的梅西亚女孩拖着脚步，跟在你后面。 她是不是想谈谈这件事呢？ 我……我不知道。至少现在还不行。我……还得先把自己的事情处理好，更别提让别人能够理解这一切了。 她还有很多关于自己的事情没有告诉你。总有一天，当她觉得可以信任你时，她会愿意把这些事情告诉你。 "...[pc.name]我们每个人都做过一些让自己并不引以为傲的事情。关键在于这些事情的程度有多深而已。 那只曾经以做出一些极其难吃的东西为生的小老鼠是这么说的。不过，你也能理解它的这种想法吧……欺负一个强大的家伙，那当然没什么问题；但要是去欺负另一个机械族成员，另一个生活在田野间的有毛生物，那就真的不应该这样做了，对吧？ 艾宁显得异常沉默。看来你确实说到了点子上。嗯，就像她自己说的，等她把自己的事情理清楚了，就会详细说明情况。目前，最好的办法还是回到城里去。 ]
rows.raw: " No point wasting time. Assuming Whisper wasn't lying through his teeth, there might be a chance you might still be able to find what Brother Sanders wants out of you now that you've driven off the maladjusted mouse. Looking about the ruins of the once open-air altar, you quickly identify several likely spots and [party.hasCompanions |direct [party.compNames] to assist you in the search for the spear. Splitting up lets you cover much more ground in as much time, and you don't want to risk reinforcements arriving while you're preoccupied. |start with the search for the spear. It's a nerve-wracking task, with you constantly worried that you're going to be ambushed while preoccupied with looking, but by good fortune or good fate no one arrives to spoil the show. ] Damn it, this is getting annoying real quickly... [party.hasCompanions |"Any luck?" [comp1.name] calls out to you. Not really. You've been sifting through several mounds of unearthed stone and pottery shards, but it looks like nothing's there. What about [comp1.himHer]? "I found several racks of spears — or at least, what used to be spears," comes the reply. "The wooden shafts have long since crumbled to dust. Nothing that looks like it's an artifact, though." Right, right. ] And then it hits you. Whisper was examining the altar when you arrived on the scene, and as it turned out, it'd been a ruse to lull you into a false sense of self-confidence. But what if it was also a ruse instead of being just one? Could it be? You'd looked over the altar before, but found not much of note on the smooth marble. Maybe it would bear further investigation... [pc.bg acolyte |your religious upbringing is enough that you're fully aware that altars are used for something; they're not just there to look grand and imposing. |while you're not too clear on the details of the worship of Sorra, you're pretty sure that altars aren't just there for decoration. ] Even so, none of the remains nearby indicate what it might have been used for... either way, maybe you should give it another look-over before committing yourself to returning empty-handed. With that thought in mind, you begin poring over the altar's dusty surface, moving your gaze from top to sides and finally to its heavyset base. Hmm. Whisper was studying the top and didn't appear to notice anything, so maybe somewhere else... oh! It's hard to see in the dim light, but there's no doubt about it: a smooth, hairline crack runs lengthwise along the side of the altar, then two more perpendicular to it on either end. There's still no sign of how to open it, but at least you're on the right track here. No doubt Whisper would have eventually spotted it had he the time for a thorough examination, but he didn't and now you're here in his place. Reinvigorated in your search, you look over the altar yet again, discovering a small piece of the decorative carvings along the base that looks like it could be moved. Without hesitation, you tug at it, and there's a dull thud from somewhere inside the stone altar. The hairline crack you spotted earlier widens, parts, and an entire section of the altar's side falls away to reveal its hollow center. There! A long, thin metal-bound case lies within, and you waste no time pulling it out and laying it on the altar's surface. The hinges are old and tarnished, but the case creaks open, and you're faced with a short spear. It's clearly ceremonial — no one would ever use such a thing in actual combat, lacking in actual reach and decorated as gaudily as it is, but if it's what Sanders wants, you're more than happy to give it to him. You don't feel any kind of magical or divine power emanating from the artifact as-is, but maybe you're just not sensitive to such things. [party.has cait |Come to think of it, does Cait feel anything coming from the relic? Your pink kitten grasps the old, dry shaft of the spear with both hands and runs her fingers up and down its length, thinning her lips. "Nope. I'd like to imagine I'm a little more sensitive than most, but I'm not getting anything, either." ] Well, you got what you came here for, and while you might not have completely ruined Master Tollus's designs on... whatever it is he's planning — assuming Whisper wasn't lying to begin with — you've at least made him pay through the nose for any gains he's made. It's not the most astounding victory you've had, but you'll take what you can get. Right. Time to get out of here. Following the tunnel forward in Whisper's footsteps eventually brings you back out into the open on the other side of the dig, amidst a bunch of abandoned scaffolding. From there, a thin trail loops back around to the front, passing back through the cultist camp and down the way you came up by. You keep your eyes peeled every step of the way, but it looks like now that they've achieved their goal, the demon cultists have all beaten a quick retreat, content to escape with their prize and lives. There's a lot of trash they left behind, especially the remains of the barricade, but that's part and parcel of a hasty withdrawal. The trip back down the trail and through the waterfall grotto is uneventful, and eventually you emerge back into the familiar sights of Harvest Valley. All that's left, you suppose, is to return the Sorran relic to Sanders and claim your reward. [party.has einin |Well, there's more than one thing that's, you suppose. Einin has been silent all the way down the mountain, the little mecian girl dragging her feet as she trails along behind you. Does she want to talk about it? "I... I don't know. Not now, at least. I... I've still got to get myself sorted out, let alone try getting it all to make sense to someone else." There's a lot she hasn't told her about herself. You'd like to hear it someday, when she feels she can trust you with it. "...[pc.name], we've all done things that we aren't exactly proud of. It's just a question of to what degree." Says the little mouse who used to make a living from being thoroughly and utterly unsavoury. But you can see where that was coming from, yes. Screwing over a big one, that's perfectly fine and dandy. But screwing over another mecian, another furred folk of the farms and fields — that's just not done, is it? Einin's awfully silent. Guess you hit the nail on the head there. Well, like she said, she'll open up about the details as and when she's gotten herself sorted out. For the moment, best head back to town. ] "

rows.original:
"What are you looking at, Quin?"

        You walk up alongside him just as the taeleer stands upright, brushing off a simple-looking copper necklace. Both of his ears are drooping yet he tries to meet you with a sober smile.
        
        "Just remembering. This isn't my camp, but the cult was family for a long time."
        
        Is that necklace something important?
        
        "No," Quin drops the necklace, brushing his hands together. Instead, he sets his hands on his hips and looks at you. "But, it does bring something to mind; we don't really talk about it much... but do you know why I go around barefoot?"
rows.translation:
你在看什么，奎因？”

就在这时，那个名叫泰勒的人站直了身体，拂去了一条看起来很普通的铜项链。他的两只耳朵都耷拉着，但还是努力用一个严肃的笑容来迎接你。
        
        只是想提醒你，这里并不是我的营地，但那个邪教组织在我心中曾经就像家人一样。”

那条项链有什么特别的意义吗？

“并没有，”奎因把项链扔到地上，双手部在身前交叉。然后他双手部叉腰，看着你说道。 但是，这确实让我想起了一些事情；我们其实很少谈论这个话题……你知道我为什么总是光着脚走路吗？

Is it because of something sexual?

            "No," he chuckles, clearly quite happy with your leap. "It's because taeleer are fast; specifically, some of us only run at our best when we're barefoot. It might get cold, sure, but considering I'm a walking fireball it isn't so bad."
            
            One of Quin's ears perk up and the rabbit turns; he hastily pulls free his [quin.weapon] and snarls at a charging group of cultists.
            
            "Hold that thought! Cultists!

是因为什么与性相关的原因吗？”

rows.original:
"I'm ready to go when you are!"

    Liv's pink-tipped tail gives an excited swish behind her. "Alright! This is gonna be fun!" She gathers up her harp, adjusts her swordbelt, and tightens her little pack's cinch around her waist. "I'm ready too! C'mon, it shouldn't be too long of a walk to find one of the old waterheads."
    
    The bard waves you on towards the south gate, strumming on her instrument and starting to sing as she walks. "Oh, the merry band set forth with courage in their hearts! The horizon called, its mysteries like siren's songs..."
rows.translation:
等你准备好了，我就出发！”

莉芙那粉红色的尾巴在身后兴奋地摆动着。“好了！这次一定会很有趣！”她收拾好她的竖琴，调整好剑带，然后把小背包系紧在腰上。 我也准备好了！快走，找到那个旧水龙头应该不会花太长时间吧。”

那位吟游女朝南门的方向挥手示意，一边走一边弹奏着乐器，开始唱歌：“哦，那些快乐的伙伴们怀着勇气出发了！ 地平线在召唤，它的神秘之处宛如塞壬的歌声……

Livrea's idea of a short walk ends up being three hours at marching pace, but [pc.bg soldier barbarian hunter
            |that's nothing out of the ordinary for you or for the wandering minstrel.
            |you probably should have expected that from a wandering minstrel. Your poor calves...
        ]
        
        [party.has cait
            |Cait's sheened with sweat, eyes hazy and unfocused, breathing hard.
        ]
        
        [party.has brint
            |Brint seems unbothered by the pace, at least, though the big man's size means he's taking about half the steps Livrea is to cover the same ground.
        ]
        
        [party.has brienne
            |Brienne seems unbothered by the pace, at least, and is even swaying her hips a little to the beat of Livrea's music.
        ]
        
        [party.has atugia
            |Atugia is having to walk quicker than usual just to keep pace with the bard, and even with her impressive physique she's clearly starting to get a little winded.
        ]
        
        [party.has etheryn
            |Ryn's clearly used to long treks, though the warmer weather this far south of her homeland's left her a little sweaty and flush-faced.
        ]
        
        [party.has arona
            |Arona's treating this like a casual stroll, though from her position at the rear of the party, you're pretty sure her gaze hasn't left Livrea's ass once the entire time. Talk about bardic inspiration...
        ]
        
        [party.has azzy
            |Azzy's mostly been flying this whole time, zipping from outcropping to outcropping to keep watch for danger.
        ]
        
        [party.has kiyoko
            |While she's normally peerlessly composed in public, the sheer distance you've walked has left Kiyoko breathlessly trying to keep her footing. She looks about ready to pitch over any moment.
        ]
        
        You've been following the river for most of the trek, heading eastwards from the grassy valley and up into the foothills. There's no beaten path up this way; you're either stomping along the rocky riverbank or edging along the narrow gaps between tall stones and shattered masonry. Livrea points out the remnants of old structures now and then, parts of the old barony left broken and forgotten by war long ago. "This used to be the edge of Hawkethorne, three hundred years ago," she says, clambering over a collapsed wall on the river's edge. "I saw an old drawing of the town in its prime once. I think there used to be a mill at the top of this hill, but the waterwheel's long gone now."
        
        "Does anybody know what actually happened here?" you ask her, hefting yourself over the rubble in her wake.
        
        She shrugs. "The Godswar. It flattened just about everything from here to the Holy City. So much history and culture wiped away in just a couple of years..."
        
        You glance at the hollowed out remnants of the mill overhead. Three of its stone walls have been slammed inwards, blackened by fire, their constituent bricks scattered over the hillside. Flattened doesn't seem like it quite covers what happened to this place. 
        
        "That drawing also showed one of Khor'minos's aqueducts in the distance," Livrea says, glancing towards the horizon. "I think it should have been... there!" 
        
        She points to a trio of standing stone cairns at the top of the next hill. Three jagged, time-worn pillars are all that's left of it. The bard sighs. "This one probably lead to Hawkethorne, not the city. The waterhead it fed from should be nearby, though! And if it is, I can follow the path the water used to take into Undermountain. We just need to find it..."

        ]
        
        [party.has etheryn
            |显然，瑞恩已经习惯了长途跋涉，不过在她家乡最南端这个地区，温暖的天气让她有些出汗，脸上也泛起了红晕。
        ]
        
        [party.has arona
            |阿罗娜把这次出行当作一次轻松的散步，不过从她站在队伍后面的位置来看，你可以肯定，整个过程中她的视线几乎没有离开过莉芙蕾娅的屁股。这可真是“诗人般的灵感”啊……
        ]
        
        [party.has azzy
            |整个过程中，阿齐大部分时间都在飞行，它从一个岩石突起处迅速飞到另一个岩石突起处，时刻警惕着潜在的危险。
        ]
        
        [party.has kiyoko
            |虽然她在公开场合通常表现得十分镇定自若，但经过这么长的距离奔跑，清子已经气喘吁吁，几乎站不稳了。她看起来随时都可能倒下。
        ]
        
        在这段漫长的旅程中，你一直沿着河流前进，从那片长满草地的山谷向东行进，最终来到了山脚下。这条路上并没有被人踩出的小路；你要么在布满岩石的河岸上行走，要么在高大岩石与碎石之间狭窄的缝隙中艰难前行。 莉芙蕾娅不时会指出那些古老建筑的遗迹——那些在很久以前就被战争摧毁、被遗忘的旧领地遗迹。“三百年前，这里曾是鹰棘镇的边界，”她边说边爬上河边那座倒塌的墙壁。 我曾经看到过一张这座城镇在鼎盛时期的老地图。我想，在这座小山的顶端曾经有一座磨坊，但那水车早就不见了。
        
        有人知道这里到底发生了什么吗？”你跟在她身后，从废墟中爬了出来，问道。

她耸了耸肩：“是神战。那场战争几乎摧毁了从这里到圣城之间的所有东西。这么多的历史和文化，就在短短几年间被抹去了……
        
        你抬头望向头顶上那座磨坊的残骸。它的三面石墙已经向内坍塌，被火焰烧得通黑，那些砖块散落在山坡上。用“被压平”来形容这个地方所经历的破坏，似乎还不够贴切。 
        
        那幅画上还远处画有科尔米诺斯的一条引水渠，”莉芙蕾娅说着，目光投向地平线，“我觉得它应该就在……那里！”

她指了指下一座小山顶上那三座由石块堆成的石堆。 如今只剩下三根布满裂痕、历经岁月侵蚀的石柱了。吟游诗人叹息道：“这条通道很可能通向鹰棘镇，而不是那座城市。不过，它原本所连接的水源应该就在附近！如果真的在那里，我就能沿着那条水流曾经走过的路线，进入山腹深域了。 我们只需要找到它……
rows.raw:
"
        Livrea's idea of a short walk ends up being three hours at marching pace, but [pc.bg soldier barbarian hunter
            |that's nothing out of the ordinary for you or for the wandering minstrel.
            |you probably should have expected that from a wandering minstrel. Your poor calves...
        ]
        
        [party.has cait
            |Cait's sheened with sweat, eyes hazy and unfocused, breathing hard.
        ]
        
        [party.has brint
            |Brint seems unbothered by the pace, at least, though the big man's size means he's taking about half the steps Livrea is to cover the same ground.
        ]
        
        [party.has brienne
            |Brienne seems unbothered by the pace, at least, and is even swaying her hips a little to the beat of Livrea's music.
        ]
        
        [party.has atugia
            |Atugia is having to walk quicker than usual just to keep pace with the bard, and even with her impressive physique she's clearly starting to get a little winded.
        ]
        
        [party.has etheryn
            |Ryn's clearly used to long treks, though the warmer weather this far south of her homeland's left her a little sweaty and flush-faced.
        ]
        
        [party.has arona
            |Arona's treating this like a casual stroll, though from her position at the rear of the party, you're pretty sure her gaze hasn't left Livrea's ass once the entire time. Talk about bardic inspiration...
        ]
        
        [party.has azzy
            |Azzy's mostly been flying this whole time, zipping from outcropping to outcropping to keep watch for danger.
        ]
        
        [party.has kiyoko
            |While she's normally peerlessly composed in public, the sheer distance you've walked has left Kiyoko breathlessly trying to keep her footing. She looks about ready to pitch over any moment.
        ]
        
        You've been following the river for most of the trek, heading eastwards from the grassy valley and up into the foothills. There's no beaten path up this way; you're either stomping along the rocky riverbank or edging along the narrow gaps between tall stones and shattered masonry. Livrea points out the remnants of old structures now and then, parts of the old barony left broken and forgotten by war long ago. "This used to be the edge of Hawkethorne, three hundred years ago," she says, clambering over a collapsed wall on the river's edge. "I saw an old drawing of the town in its prime once. I think there used to be a mill at the top of this hill, but the waterwheel's long gone now."
        
        "Does anybody know what actually happened here?" you ask her, hefting yourself over the rubble in her wake.
        
        She shrugs. "The Godswar. It flattened just about everything from here to the Holy City. So much history and culture wiped away in just a couple of years..."
        
        You glance at the hollowed out remnants of the mill overhead. Three of its stone walls have been slammed inwards, blackened by fire, their constituent bricks scattered over the hillside. Flattened doesn't seem like it quite covers what happened to this place. 
        
        "That drawing also showed one of Khor'minos's aqueducts in the distance," Livrea says, glancing towards the horizon. "I think it should have been... there!" 
        
        She points to a trio of standing stone cairns at the top of the next hill. Three jagged, time-worn pillars are all that's left of it. The bard sighs. "This one probably lead to Hawkethorne, not the city. The waterhead it fed from should be nearby, though! And if it is, I can follow the path the water used to take into Undermountain. We just need to find it...""

rows.original:
"Whew! I think this is it!"

            You heft yourself up onto the top of the rocky hillside with Livrea and glance down where she's pointing. 
            
            The two of you are a good few miles from Hawkethorne now, somewhere south-east of the village and deep into the foothills between it and the mountains. The hills here have grown taller and more jagged, and you're doing more climbing than walking. There hasn't been as much in the way of ruins lately, giving way to truly untamed wilderness. 
            
            Following Livrea's gaze, you see there's a small but deep-looking lake in the caldera between three stony hills. Water collects here from small rivers all around, and... yes, there's a flow going from it straight into the side of the nearest mountain. Livrea grins ear to ear. "That's it, definitely. This dumps into the lake under the mountain. My uncle Livernus runs a barge across it — if I can just make it to the underlake I'm sure I can flag him down." She waves you forward and starts clambering down towards the waterhead.
rows.translation:
呼！我想就是这里了！”

你和莉芙蕾娅一起爬上了那座多岩石的小山的山顶，然后顺着她指的方向往下望去。

此时，你们已经距离鹰棘镇有好几英里远了，应该位于村庄的东南方向，处于村庄与山脉之间的山脚下地带。 这里的山丘变得更高、更加崎岖，你爬行的次数远远多于步行的次数。最近，遗迹的数量也减少了，取而代之的是一片真正荒芜的野外地带。

顺着莉芙蕾娅的视线望去，你会看到在三座岩石山丘之间的火山口里，有一个面积不大但看起来很深的湖泊。 这里汇集了周围小河流的水，而且……没错，这些水会直接流入最近那座山的侧面。莉芙蕾娅笑得合不拢嘴：“就是这里了，肯定就是这里。这些水最终会流入山下的湖泊里。 我叔叔利弗努斯驾驶着一艘驳船在湖上航行——只要我能赶到湖底，肯定能叫住他。”她说着，示意你跟在她后面，然后开始朝着水边爬去。

rows.original: Maybe you could open that chest?
rows.translation: 也许你可以打开那个箱子？

rows.original: Dropping that on the wyrm would be one hell of a wakeup call.
rows.translation: 把那东西扔到那条巨龙身上，绝对会让它猛然清醒过来。
rows.raw: "Dropping that on the wyrm would be one hell of a wakeup call."

rows.original: You creep up to the edge of the rocky outcropping, glancing up at the jagged pillar of wet stone hanging from the ceiling. It's pretty much directly over the wyrm's nest, though you can't quite eyeball where on the beast it might land. It's not exactly an arrow. And that's if you could dislodge it. The thing's well out of arm's reach. Plus, dropping it's definitely going to cause a lot of chaos. You better be ready for anything if you manage to get it loose...
rows.translation: 你悄悄地走到岩石突出的边缘，抬头望去，只见一根由湿漉漉的石头构成的、参差不齐的石柱悬挂在天花板上。它几乎正好位于那条巨龙的巢穴正上方，不过你无法准确判断这块石头会落在巨龙的哪个部位——毕竟它并不是一支箭啊。 就是这样。 如果 你可以把它弄下来。那个东西根本够不着。而且，如果把它掉下来，肯定会引发一阵混乱。如果你真的设法把它弄下来，最好做好应对一切情况的准备……
rows.raw: " You creep up to the edge of the rocky outcropping, glancing up at the jagged pillar of wet stone hanging from the ceiling. It's pretty much directly over the wyrm's nest, though you can't quite eyeball where on the beast it might land. It's not exactly an arrow. And that's if you could dislodge it. The thing's well out of arm's reach. Plus, dropping it's definitely going to cause a lot of chaos. You better be ready for anything if you manage to get it loose..."

rows.original: Time to give the wyrm a rude awakening. You draw a leananstone from your pouch and give it a ginger bounce in your palm, getting a good feel for the heft of the thing. It's small, but you know it's going to pack a punch — even gently palming the thing charges your hand with static electricity, making your small hairs stand upright. Livrea gives you a double thumbs-up and draws her sword from its sheath at her hip. [party.has cait |Cait folds her ears down and covers them with her hands. ] You line up a shot and hurl the leananstone straight at the hanging pillar of stone. The stormbound stone strikes true and hard, and lets loose a cacophony of thunderous force that rattles you straight to your bones. There's a scattershot of falling stone from the stalactite's base as it's violently wrenched from its hanging position, sent hurtling towards the ground with all the might of the world yanking it down. The poor sleeping wyrm under you is struck in the thigh by the falling stone, wrenched to wakefulness by deafening thunder and piercing pain. Blood paints the cavern floor crimson. The wyrm thrashes and screams, fire drooling from its slavering maw. Its tail and wings slam into the rocks beneath you, and you feel something cracking underfoot. Too late, you try and scramble backwards to safety, but already the overhang is starting to topple. The only saving grace is that it doesn't pitch over entirely, but rather is just slow enough of a collapse that your group's able to slide down rather than tumble, but there's no escaping gravity's pull. You hit the ground and roll, grabbing your [pc.weapon] as you make ready. Livrea faceplants behind you, hardly graceful with those big hooves, but you yank her back to her feet before the wyrm can fully turn to face you. Blood gushes from its seeping wound, but it's not dead yet. Not even close. It roars at you, almost as loud as the leananstone's blast, and spreads its wings menacingly.
rows.translation: 是时候让这条巨蛇彻底清醒过了。 你从口袋里掏出一把利安石剑，在掌心轻轻一弹，感受着它的重量。虽然它很小，但你知道它蕴含着巨大的力量——哪怕只是轻轻一弹，也会让你的手部掌产生静电，让细小的汗毛都竖了起来。 莉芙蕾娅也向你竖起了大拇指，然后从腰间的剑鞘中拔出了她的剑。 [party.has cait |凯特把耳朵耷拉下来，然后用双手把它们盖住。 ] 你调整好射击姿势，将那块倾斜的石头直接投向悬垂的石柱。 这块被风暴侵蚀的石头精准地击中了目标，随之迸发出震耳欲聋的巨响，那冲击力仿佛直接震到了你的骨子里。 当那根钟乳石被猛力拽离悬挂的位置时，有零星的石块从它的基部掉落下来，这些石块在重力的作用下急速向地面飞去。你足部下的那只正在沉睡的巨蛇，被掉落的石块击中了大腿，震耳欲聋的巨响和剧烈的疼痛将它从睡梦中惊醒。 鲜血将洞穴的地面染成了猩红色。 那条巨蛇剧烈地扭动身体，发出惨叫声，口中不断喷出火焰。它的尾巴和翅膀不断撞击着你足部下的岩石，而你 感受 足部下有什么东西突然断裂了。为时已晚，你试图向后爬去寻找安全的地方，但那悬垂的部分已经开始倒塌。唯一值得庆幸的是，它并没有完全倒下，而是以足够缓慢的速度崩塌，让你的小队能够滑下来而不是摔下去，不过，还是无法逃脱重力的牵引。 你摔在地上，滚了几圈，然后抓住了 [pc.weapon] 就在你准备行动的瞬间，莉芙蕾娅重重地摔在了你身后——那双巨大的蹄子让她的动作显得一点也不优雅。但你及时拉住了她，让她重新站了起来，以免那条巨龙有时间完全转过身来面对你。它的伤口正在不断流血，但它却还远没有死。远远没有。 它朝你咆哮着，声音几乎和利安斯坦石发射出的爆炸声一样响亮，同时还威胁性地展开了它的翅膀。

rows.original: If only you had a leananstone...
rows.translation: 要是你有一把利剑该多好……

rows.original: You almost snap your fingers, before you catch yourself. Don't want to risk waking the wyrm when it's in such a perfect position. That shield buried in the cave wall looks damn solid and heavy, all old bronze and discus-shaped. Perfect for [silly |cosplaying Captain America |throwing ]. You creep back, grab hold, and flex your muscles. A bit of pulling and wiggling and you're able to get it free. It's in decent shape, if badly pierced and dented — not worth much anymore as a shield, but it's still got its heft. Good enough. Taking a deep breath, you heft the battered shield up and take a running start towards the overhang's edge, waiting for the last moment to release so you can throw all your weight and momentum behind the throw. It strikes true, slamming into the pendulous stalactite and cleanly severing it at the base. There's a scattershot of falling stone from the stalactite's base as it's violently wrenched from its hanging position, sent hurtling towards the ground with all the might of the world yanking it down. The poor sleeping wyrm under you is struck in the thigh by the falling stone, wrenched to wakefulness by piercing pain. Blood paints the cavern floor crimson. rows.original: That shield lodged in the wall back behind you! It's solid and heavy, you might be able to hurl it hard enough to knock the stone free.
rows.translation: 那个盾牌卡在你身后的墙上去了！它非常坚固且重型，如果你能用力把它扔出去，或许就能把那块石头撞下来。
rows.raw: "That shield lodged in the wall back behind you! It's solid and heavy, you might be able to hurl it hard enough to knock the stone free."

rows.original: You lack the physical strength to throw anything hard enough to dislodge that stone.
rows.translation: 你没有足够的体力来抛出足够有力的力量，从而把那块石头弄掉。
rows.raw: "You lack the physical strength to throw anything hard enough to dislodge that stone."

rows.original: You point to Livrea's harp, then the stalactite, and mime an explosion. She takes a deep breath and nods, planting her feet and getting her harp nestled just right in her arms. You take the opportunity to cover your ears before the bovine bard hammers her fingers across the strings and incants a spell of sorcerous thunder that blasts like a roaring storm from her instrument into the air. The shockwave cracks the stalactite, and then a second chord sends arcs of coruscating lightning across it to finish the job. The stone breaks free with a roar of breaking earth and plummets to the ground with all of gravity's fury behind it. The poor sleeping wyrm under you is struck in the thigh by the falling stone, wrenched to wakefulness by deafening thunder and piercing pain. Blood paints the cavern floor crimson. The wyrm thrashes and screams, fire drooling from its slavering maw. Its tail and wings slam into the rocks beneath you, and you feel something cracking underfoot. Too late, you try and scramble backwards to safety, but already the overhang is starting to topple. The only saving grace is that it doesn't pitch over entirely, but rather is just slow enough of a collapse that your group's able to slide down rather than tumble, but there's no escaping gravity's pull. You hit the ground and roll, grabbing your [pc.weapon] as you make ready. Livrea faceplants behind you, hardly graceful with those big hooves, but you yank her back to her feet before the wyrm can fully turn to face you. Blood gushes from its seeping wound, but it's not dead yet. Not even close. It roars at you, almost as loud as the bard's magical blast, and spreads its wings menacingly.
rows.translation: 你指向莉芙蕾娅的竖琴，然后又指向那颗钟乳石，同时模仿爆炸的声音。她深吸一口气，点了点头，站稳身子，将竖琴牢牢地抱在怀里。你趁这个机会捂住了耳朵——因为这位“粗犷的吟游诗人”马上就要用手指敲击琴弦，释放出一道如同暴风雨般猛烈的魔法雷声了。 冲击波震碎了钟乳石，紧接着第二道电弧划过其表面，将剩余的部分彻底摧毁。石头在剧烈的震动中脱离支架，伴随着沉重的坠落声，带着全部的重力向地面急速坠落。 你足部下的那条睡眠中的巨蛇被坠落的石头击中了大腿，震耳欲聋的雷声和刺骨的剧痛将它惊醒。鲜血将洞穴的地面染成了猩红色。 这条巨蛇疯狂地挣扎着、尖叫着，从它那张张开的血盆大口中不断喷出火焰。 它的尾巴和翅膀狠狠地撞击着你足部下的岩石，而你 感受到 足部下有什么东西突然断裂了。为时已晚，你试图向后爬去寻找安全的地方，但那悬垂的部分已经开始倒塌。唯一值得庆幸的是，它并没有完全倒下，而是以足够缓慢的速度崩塌，让你的小队能够滑下来而不是摔下去，不过，还是无法逃脱重力的牵引。 你重重地摔在地上，滚了几圈，然后赶紧抓住了 [pc.weapon] 就在你准备行动的瞬间，莉芙蕾娅重重地摔在了你身后——那双巨大的蹄子让她的动作显得一点也不优雅。但你迅速将她拉了起来，以免那条巨龙有时间完全转过身来面对你。它的伤口正在不断流血，但它却远未死亡，甚至远远没有。 它朝你咆哮着，声音几乎和那位吟游士发出的魔法攻击一样响亮，同时它还威胁性地展开了翅膀。

rows.original: Ask Livrea to blast the stalactite free. Though doing so will certainly wind the bubbly bard for any upcoming encounters...
rows.translation: 让莉芙蕾娅把那些钟乳石敲掉吧。不过这么做的话，这位爱说笑的吟游诗人在未来遇到的任何对手面前，肯定都会处于劣势……
rows.raw: "Ask Livrea to blast the stalactite free. Though doing so will certainly wind the bubbly bard for any upcoming encounters..."

rows.original: "Any ideas, Liv?" you whisper. Hopefully the ruckus the wyrm's snoring makes will drown out your voices. ... Unfortunately, it really does. The bardic bovine flicks her ears and shrugs. You point up at the stalactite, and then make a cutting gesture downwards. She makes an "oh!" expression, and then hefts up her harp and mimics running her fingers aggressively over the strings, then thrusts them at the stalactite. Finally, she slumps her shoulders and breathes heavily, as though completely exhausted. You suppose that's an option, at least.
rows.translation: 有什么主意吗，莉芙？”你低声问道。希望那条巨龙发出的鼾声能掩盖你们的声音。 ……可惜，事实并非如此。 真的吗 嗯。”那位吟游诗人的女伴摇动着耳朵，耸了耸肩。 你指着钟乳石，然后向下做了一个斩击的手势。她露出“哦！”的表情，接着拿起她的竖琴，模仿着快速地用手指在琴弦上弹奏，然后又将手指朝向钟乳石的方向挥动。最后，她垂下肩膀，重重地喘着气，仿佛已经筋疲力尽。 你认为，至少这也是一个可行的选择。

rows.translation: 暂时退后一步，考虑其他选择吧。

rows.original: There's an outcropping of rock just ahead, hanging over the riverside path. [dayNight |It looks like a decently shady spot to catch your breath. Although it seems you're not the only one with the idea... |A number of bats shriek and take wing when you draw near. Wait, no, not just you... ] There's a big woman sitting herself down on top of the rocks, with battle-scarred jade skin and a long brown ponytail tossed over one shoulder. She's wearing almost nothing: just a cape and a bikini made of metal links over fur padding, leaving a tattoo in the shape of two horned wolves over her crotch bare for all to see. All that orcish muscle's proudly on display as she grins down at you, licking one of her tusks. "Well, well, [party.has arona |[arona.isExile |if it isn't the exiled kid and her loser champion." "Fuck you, Ylvid. Boot-licking whore," Arona snarls. "Come down here and say that to my face." |what brings you out this way, chief? I figured you were [arona.isDom |gonna be spending the winter balls-deep in your fucktoy there |gonna be shaking that ass for [pc.name] there all winter ]." "Ylvid!" Arona says, putting her hands on her hips. "Finally crawled out from between Thane Vulgra's thighs long enough to see the Marches, huh? You're a little late to the party." "Yeah, I heard from Hretha!" the other orc grins. "Congrats on finally proving you got a bigger dick than your brother." ] You glance at Arona. "Friend of yours?" |look at this! And the chief always said patience was for cowards, but here you are!" ] The orc slaps her hand on a war drum slung at her side. "I am Ylvid Helvasdottir, skald of the Kervus tribe! And you..." she points directly at the ginger cowgirl beside you "...must be Livrea." Your bardic companion puffs up her already-massive chest. "So you've heard of me all the way in the Sailgraves! I'm flattered." "Your line is famous in the islands, daughter of the Storm Witch," the orc sneers. "I knew our scouts' report of a bard with strawberry-colored hair poking around the foothills could only mean you!" "What?" you say. "You came chasing after the first red-headed cowgirl you heard about?" Ylvid places a hand on her drums, and the other on an axe hanging from her belt. "Of course I did! If I best the Livrea, the spirits of my clan sent beneath the waves by her witch mother will rock the veil of death with their cheers! And my legend will sing gloriously across the islands!" Livrea looks up at the orc and laughs. "So what, you want some kind of bard-off? What do they call it in orcish, a... a flyting?" "Ha, you know our language. Yes, that," Ylvid says, baring her tusks and flicking her thumb across her axehead, "or I beat you [party.som |both |all |all ] down and see how well you sing between my thighs." You put a hand on your own weapon. "You sure you want to try against [party.som |both of us |all three of us |all four of us ]?" "Ha. You're right. Not exactly a fair fight!" Ylvid says, standing. "You'd better run back to town and bring all your friends!"

rows.original:
You draw your [pc.weapon]. Livrea follows suit, pulling the short sword from the scabbard at her side.

        "Ah, I was hoping you'd pick violence!" Ylvid admits, hopping down from the rocks and pulling the axe from her belt. "Good! We'll settle this like orcs!" 
        
        "So by losing to a Minoan?" Livrea snorts. "That's what your Kervus have been doing for centuries!"
        
        Ylvid snarls. "We'll see how you sound when I'm riding those pretty lips, cow!"

“所以你是说，因为输给了米诺斯人？”莉芙蕾娅嗤笑道，“你们的凯尔维斯族几个世纪以来不就是一直在干这种事吗？”

rows.original: You're a simple [pc.mf|man|woman]. If you see an orc blocking your way, you must fight her.
rows.translation: 你真简单。 [pc.mf|男人|女性]如果你看到一个兽人挡住了你的去路，你就必须与它战斗。
rows.raw: "You're a simple [pc.mf|man|woman]. If you see an orc blocking your way, you must fight her."

rows.original:
You nod to Livrea. "Let's see how she stacks up to you."

        The bard scoffs, puffing out her chest. "Please! Nobody's more stacked than a cowgirl, and certainly not some meatheaded orc. Her kind work off all their curves pumping the oars of their tiny, sad little ships." 
        
        Ylvid howls with laughter, rapping her knuckles on her drums. "Big words for a small girl — no, that's not true. You're wide enough to block the harbor when your kins' slaver ships come sailing home. Short and stout, that's how they breed them under the mountains."
        
        Short? Livrea's six and a half foot. Matter of perspective, you guess — Ylvid's probably got another half foot on her.
        
        Livrea's fingers dance over her harp strings. "Ah, it's clear as day now: her brain's addled by islander swill, and her eyes are rotted by half a clan's seed spilled across her face." Livrea [party.has arona
            |elbows Arona with a wink
            |mimes a splash across her own face with a flourish
        ]. "A pity, Ylvid, you could almost be cute if you weren't so dull-witted."
        
        "You Minoans are so smug about your book-learning, but what have you done with it, hm? I've seen sights you can only dream of, and had women from all across the Sailgraves call me more than 'cute!' You haven't lived until you've had a pexighast priestess use her tail like your half-beast men use their flabby manhoods, and with twice the skill! And you've certainly missed out if you've never felt an orc's tusks between your nethers, kissing your lips."
        
        Livrea laughs, plucking at her harp. "Are we flirting or dueling wits, Ylvid? Though I suppose there's hardly any difference to an orcish bimbo."
        
        "It can be both," the orc skald hurries to say. Her hand slaps the top of her drum. "Every good fight deserves a little foreplay, don't you think? And what's a fight, but foreplay for what comes after!" She laughs, cupping up one of her big green tits beneath her bustier. Damn, they're really almost as big as Livrea's...
        
        The cowgirl glances at you. "And what does my heroic escort say to that?"
        
        [pc.canDance
            |You know how these duels of wits ought to go, a battle of boasts and insults until one side loses their cool. "I say one dim-witted orc will hardly be a challenge," you say, projecting your voice with confidence through the valley. "A poor skald, a mediocre flirt, and a sad fight. Even the sex would be disappointing."
            
            Ylvid puts a hand over her chest as if struck. "You're going to regret those words, [pc.boyGirl]! I'll show you both what a Kervus skald's made of!"
            |You grimace, suddenly put on the spot. "That we're gonna kick her ass?"
            
            Ylvid howls with laughter, while Livrea cringes. Did you say something wrong? "Ah, said with such conviction. I'm sure we can find something more productive for those lips to do than boast, young [pc.race]. Let me show you."
        ]
        
        The orc reaches for her axe, and leaps down from the rocks.
rows.translation:
你向莉芙蕾娅点了点头：“让我们看看她跟你比起来怎么样。”

那位吟游女嗤之以鼻，挺起胸膛说道：“得了吧！没人能比得上一名女牛仔，更别说某个头脑简单的兽人了。她们的工作就是依靠自己的曲线来划动那些又小又破的船桨罢了。伊尔维德放声大笑，用指关节敲打着鼓面。‘小姑娘也能说出这么大的话来……不，其实并不是这样。你的身材可真够壮实的，等你们家族的奴隶船归来时，你的身躯简直足以挡住整个港口呢。矮胖敦实——原来在山脚下就是这么培育这种动物的啊。矮吗？莉芙蕾娅有六英尺半高。这大概只是视角的问题吧——伊尔维德应该还要高半英尺左右。”

"[pc.isCunning |That the magic light really makes your golden eyes shine! |That you're super pretty! ]" you say, smiling disarmingly. "I don't really do big thinkies, but your big booblies are good inspiration." Livrea giggles. "And I adore you for it. But I'm starting to think there's something big and dangerous down here with us." |You nod. "There's something big down here with us." ] The bard cranes her head to the north and flicks a bovine ear. "It sounds like snarling... snarling through really huge, sharp teeth. Like a dragon warning us off." That... surely that's a minstrel's natural tendency to exaggerate, right? Still, she's not wrong. The noise coming from along the river to the west sounds dangerous. You and Livrea exchange a look, and start searching around for some sign of what's to come. All you turn up in the immediate are muddy kobold tracks on the stone beside the flowing water, and piles of discarded bones. None of them look like folk, thankfully, but there's some big damn animals in here: you recognize the skulls of an elk and a bear amongst a lot of deer and mountain lions. Whatever's down here isn't kidding around. As you're brushing your hand along the wall, searching for any further clue, you almost pitch to the side. It's almost impossible to see, even with the arcane light close by, but there's a thin crevasse in the east wall, barely big enough to squeeze through sideways — and even then Livrea's going to have some real problems. But it is another path... You point it out to your [party.som |companion |companions |party and Livrea ]. "Look what I found." Liv grimaces. "If you want to go that way, I'm gonna need to find some butter to squeeze through there after you." She'll probably be fine... Then again, you could just bravely march north and face whatever beast lurks in the dark ahead."

rows.original: You lead the way into what proves to be a fairly large and circular alcove. There's a shield half buried in a crack in the wall near the entrance, and that's only the start of the soldiering gear you find inside. There's flimsy, time-worn canvas stretched between pitons like tents, and a torn banner rests on its pole against the far wall. There are old boots, spearheads, and a broken sword scattered on the ground. "This camp is so old," Livrea points out. "Do you think it's from the war?" You point to the banner. [pc.bg scholar |"Look at that, the blue moons? This belonged to the Imperial house of Old Belhar. Nobody's flown those colors for centuries." "Good eye," she says, nodding. "Definitely from the Godswar at the latest. Maybe even earlier." |"Do you know whose colors those were?" Liv peers at the banner a moment, stopping herself from touching the blue crescent moon on it. "These were the colors of Old Belhar's royal house. It must have been carried up here by Imperial troops. It could have been brought up here during the border skirmishes with the boreal elves, but I'd put my hawks on it being from the Godswar. Definitely no later. The Imperial house was made extinct right after." ] "I wonder what they were doing in here?" you wonder. Livrea pokes at the tent pitons. "Hiding from Wraiths, maybe. Or whatever it was that blasted old Hawkethorne City to pieces back then." The ancient wood crumbles under the bard's touch, and the canvas falls to the floor. "Hey, look!" your bardic companion says, squatting down. "It was covering something." That something, it seems, is a chest. Old but still-sturdy wood, with a brass locking plate and dials on it with letters. "A wordlock chest," Liv says. "These used to be popular among Belharan nobility. You find them all over the place these days. Just gotta spin the dials to make the answer to the riddle there." [party.has cait |"Oh! My dad has one of those!" Cait says, spinning one of the letter rings. "We put our jewelry in there while we were traveling. The riddle on ours was in Old Jassiran, too, so basically nobody this side of the sea could hope to solve it... but that did not stop Tollus's goons from just stealing the whole box out of our cart." Livrea gives Cait a pat on the shoulder. ] Even if you aren't in the mood for riddles, there's plenty of miscellaneous stuff on the ground for you to collect. Fragments of old blades and spearheads can still be smelted down and made into new, useful things like nails and horseshoes by a trained smith. You gather up the goods and stow them before turning you attention back to the chest. [silly |Not Livrea's, mind you. Well, that's certainly more visually appealing, but you don't think the bard would appreciate you flicking her nips to solve the riddle of her panties just yet. Maybe in a future expansion. ]
rows.translation: 你率先走进了一个相当宽敞且呈圆形的壁龛。入口附近，有一面盾牌半埋在墙缝中，而这只是你在里面发现的军用装备中的其中一部分。还有一些破旧不堪的帆布，被固定在支架上用来搭建临时帐篷；而一面破损的旗帜则被插在远处的墙上。 地上散落着旧靴子、矛头和一把断剑。 “这个营地看起来很古老，”莉芙蕾娅说道，“你觉得这些是战争留下的吗？” 你指向那面旗帜。 [pc.bg scholar |看那个，那些蓝色的旗帜……这些旗帜曾经属于古老的贝尔哈尔皇室。几个世纪以来，再也没有人使用过这样的颜色了。” “观察得很仔细，”她点头说道，“这些旗帜肯定至少可以追溯到神战时期，甚至可能更早。 |你知道那些颜色属于谁的吗？” 莉芙盯着那面旗帜看了一会儿，忍住了想要触碰上面那轮蓝色新月图案的冲动。“这些颜色是老贝尔哈尔王室的标志。肯定是帝国军队把它们带到了这里。也有可能是在与北方精灵的边境冲突中传进来的，但我敢肯定，这些颜色肯定与‘神战’有关。绝对不可能是后来才出现的。因为帝国王室在‘神战’之后就灭绝了。 ] 我想知道他们在这里到底在做什么？”你不禁疑惑。 莉芙蕾娅拨了拨帐篷的固定桩：“也许是躲避开那些幽灵吧。又或者是为了躲避当年把鹰棘镇城炸得粉碎的那些东西。” 在吟游者的触碰下，那些古老的木桩开始腐朽，帐篷的帆布也随之掉落在地上。 嘿，看！”你的吟游诗人同伴蹲下来说道，“它之前在盖着什么东西。” 那个被盖着的物体，似乎是一口箱子。木头虽然陈旧，但依然十分结实，箱子上装有黄铜制的锁扣以及刻有字母的旋钮。 一个字谜锁箱，”莉芙说道，“这种东西过去在贝拉兰的贵族中很流行。现在到处都能看到它们，只要转动那些旋钮，就能解出里面的谜题答案。 [party.has cait |哦！我爸爸也有一个这样的东西！”凯特说着，转动着其中一个字母环。“我们旅行的时候会把首饰放进去。我们那个字母环上的谜语也是用古贾西兰语写的，所以基本上海这边的没人能解开它……但这也阻止不了托卢斯的那些手下把我们车里的整个盒子都偷走。” 莉芙蕾娅轻拍了一下凯特的肩膀。 ] 即使你没有心情猜谜语，这里也有很多其他有趣的内容。 东西 这些零碎的旧刀刃和矛头可以被收集起来，经过训练有素的铁匠的加工，仍然可以被熔炼成钉子、马蹄铁等新的、有用的物品。你把收集到的这些东西收拾好，然后再次将注意力转向那个箱子。 [silly |请注意，这并不是莉芙蕾娅的风格。嗯，这样的设计确实更美观一些，但你觉得这位吟游诗人应该不会喜欢你通过捏她的乳头来解开关于她内裤的谜题吧……也许可以在未来的扩展内容中加入这个元素。 ]
