After starting a good tale about elves coming together to put the grievances of their ancestors to rest, it's about time to milk it for all it's worth? That, and the irony of Lumian elves fighting for their cause... and pushing up Ryn's martial reputation at the same time. "It's one of the reasons why the people don't merely tolerate, but are absolutely fascinated by my [etheryn.crowned |queen |princess-regent ] taking long absences of leave from her ruling duties to be with you, Champion. Like it or not, the idea of a warrior-monarch braving exotic dangers and having daring adventures captures the imagination of the boer'alvar like nothing else. It's best to build up such a reputation while she's young to insure a more stable reign down the line." Ryn blushes a little at that. So let's get this straight. Hethia and Elthara would like you and Ryn to head on to one of the old druidic temples and do the dirty work of investigating and clearing out all the nasties, so the more spiteful of Hethia's people will be pressured to come to more reasonable terms by this show of goodwill. Amongst other issues like the housing problems, that is. "That's the long and short of it, yes, but it's not just the both of you going. I won't be able to accompany you all the way, but Elthara's agreed to represent the Lumian clergy in undertaking this adventure at your side, too." Could be worse. One question, though — if this fungal infection was able to eliminate the druids... you take it that the reason Hethia needs you and the Lumians to do this job is because it won't be able to harm you? "You catch on quickly, don't you? The problem with using diseases as weapons is that they have a tendency to spread their way back to you, which is why the legends say that it was keyed to our particular powers. The [etheryn.crowned |queen |princess-regent ], Elthara and you should be largely unaffected." And which temple would this be? Hethia smirks. "Might as well go all in, wouldn't you say? The grandest of all the druidic enclaves, Xadaron Temple itself." What was the current archdruid's last name again? Xadaron? Going straight for the sentimental value, you see. "Hit her where she'll feel it the most, yes." Why not take a contingent of elves and valkyries and clear it out, then? Oh wait, that wouldn't make a good story, would it? "That, and the hardliner druids could spin a massed effort as an invasion, a desecration, whatever. They already don't like me for trying to be reasonable with you, so..." Hethia shrugs. "Elthara says she'll have backup on standby in case you don't make it out." Very thoughtful of her. "And that's the long and short of it," Elthara says. "Hethia can bring us there, but she won't be able to enter the temple with us. We go in, clear out the remnants of the past, and return any culturally significant relics while keeping the valuables for the Crown. The druids get a show of goodwill, and confidence in the [etheryn.crowned |queen |princess-regent ]'s deeds and martial prowess grows. Everyone wins." All right, you understand what's going on here. But what about Ryn? How does she feel about being shepherded by her advisors into an adventure? [etheryn.lnhConfidence |Ryn gives you a weak smile. "You're th-the ones who've helped keep the Winter City r-running after my sister's departure. If I can't trust you to make good decisions, then that would be silly of me, w-wouldn't it? So long as you think it's for the best, then I've no objections going along with it. It feels good to hear the people cheer for me, and it might even be... f-fun." |Ryn thinks a moment. "All of you have kept the Winter City running when I wouldn't have been able to do it myself. For me to doubt you now would be quite heartless of me, wouldn't it? If you think that this would be a worthwhile venture, then I'm for it. I want to see the schism in our people healed, and while I don't exactly relish fighting for its sake like Alissa did, I'll swallow my fears if it means advancing our cause." |Ryn shrugs and gives you an easy smile. "I trust the three of you to do what's right for the future of the boer'alvar. We've come this far already, and all of you have proven to be capable and firmly on my side. To be honest, I find the idea exciting! And the less ugliness that remains buried in my family's past, the better. If that means digging it up and disposing of it, I'm all for that." ] "I know this is quite sudden to drop on you, [pc.name] — you probably have other things that you were intending on doing," Hethia says. "That being said, with the way the talks are going, there's no rush. Elthara has already made preparations for herself and the [etheryn.crowned |queen |princess-regent ]; bring up the matter with me anytime and I'll be able to take you there, as well as ask any questions pertaining to the venture." rows.original:
"All right, I'll make it as simple as possible." Hethia takes a deep breath. "I bring you, Elthara and the [etheryn.crowned
                |queen
                |princess-regent
            ] to a ruined druidic temple. All of you clear it out. You get loot, the [etheryn.crowned
                |queen
                |princess-regent
            ]'s fame spreads and people speak of her deeds, Elthara and I get a strong bargaining chip to pressure my stiff-necked boss into not sinking the reunification talks. That enough for you?"
            
            You can tell that Hethia's being more than a little mocking in that jibe of hers, but hey, you asked for it. All right, you can accept this.
            
            "And that's the long and short of it," Elthara says. "Hethia can bring us there, but she won't be able to enter the temple with us. We go in, clear out the remnants of the past, and return any culturally significant relics while keeping the valuables for the Crown. The druids get a show of goodwill, and confidence in the [etheryn.crowned
                |queen
                |princess-regent
            ]'s deeds and martial prowess grows. Everyone wins."
            
            All right, you understand what's going on here. But what about Ryn? How does she feel about being shepherded by her advisors into an adventure?
            
            [etheryn.lnhConfidence
                |Ryn gives you a weak smile. "You're th-the ones who've helped keep the Winter City r-running after my sister's departure. If I can't trust you to make good decisions, then that would be silly of me, w-wouldn't it? So long as you think it's for the best, then I've no objections going along with it. It feels good to hear the people cheer for me, and it might even be... f-fun."
                |Ryn thinks a moment. "All of you have kept the Winter City running when I wouldn't have been able to do it myself. For me to doubt you now would be quite heartless of me, wouldn't it? If you think that this would be a worthwhile venture, then I'm for it. I want to see the schism in our people healed, and while I don't exactly relish fighting for its sake like Alissa did, I'll swallow my fears if it means advancing our cause."
                |Ryn shrugs and gives you an easy smile. "I trust the three of you to do what's right for the future of the boer'alvar. We've come this far already, and all of you have proven to be capable and firmly on my side. To be honest, I find the idea exciting! And the less ugliness that remains buried in my family's past, the better. If that means digging it up and disposing of it, I'm all for that."
            ]
            
            "I know this is quite sudden to drop on you, [pc.name] — you probably have other things that you were intending on doing," Hethia says. "That being said, with the way the talks are going, there's no rush. Elthara has already made preparations for herself and the [etheryn.crowned
                |queen
                |princess-regent
            ]; bring up the matter with me anytime and I'll be able to take you there, as well as ask any questions pertaining to the venture."
            
            That'll be it for now, then. Leaving Hethia[party.has etheryn
                | and Elthara to finish up the rest of the jam waffles and wine, you leave the gardens with Ryn
                |, Elthara and Ryn to finish up the rest of the jam waffles and wine, you leave the gardens
            ] to ponder this new opportunity.

好吧，我会尽量把事情说得简单些。”赫希娅深吸一口气，继续说道，“我是来带你们，埃尔萨拉和 [etheryn.crowned
                |女王
                |摄政公主
            ] 一座被毁掉的德鲁伊神庙。你们所有人都必须把里面的东西清理干净。在那里，你们可以获得战利品。 [etheryn.crowned
                |女王
                |摄政公主
            ]她的名声传开了，人们都在谈论她的所作所为，这样一来，我和艾尔塔拉就有了一个有力的筹码，可以用来迫使那个固执的老板不要破坏重新统一的谈判。这样够了吧？”

从希西娅的这句话中，可以明显感觉到她带着一丝嘲讽的意味，不过，嘿，这也是你自找的嘛。 就是这样，”埃尔萨拉说道，“赫希娅可以带我们前往那里，但她无法和我们一起进入神庙。我们进去后，会清除过去留下的残余物，将具有文化价值的文物带回来，而将那些珍贵的物品留给我们王室。 德鲁伊们因此获得了人们的善意与信任。 [etheryn.crowned
                |女王
                |摄政公主
            ]他的功绩与武艺日益精湛，最终大家都能受益。”

好吧，你们应该明白这里发生了什么。但瑞恩呢？她对于被自己的顾问们牵着去参加这次冒险，又有什么感受呢？
            
            [etheryn.lnhConfidence
                |瑞恩勉强挤出一丝笑容：“在我姐姐离开后，是你们帮助维持了冬城的运转。如果我不能信任你们会做出正确的决定，那未免太愚蠢了，不是吗？只要你们认为这是最好的选择，我没有任何反对意见。听到人们为我欢呼，这种感觉……其实还挺不错的，甚至可能……还挺有趣的。
                |瑞恩思考了一会儿，说道：“在那些我独自无力完成的事情上，是你们所有人共同维持了冬城的运转。现在如果我怀疑你们，未免太无情了吧？如果你们认为这个尝试值得，那我支持。我希望我们族人之间的分歧能够得到化解。虽然我并不像艾莉莎那样热衷于为此而战，但如果这能推动我们的事业前进，我愿意克服自己的恐惧。
                |瑞恩耸了耸肩，然后露出了一个轻松的微笑：“我相信你们三个人会为‘布尔阿尔瓦’的未来做出正确的选择。我们已经走了这么远，而且你们所有人都证明了自己有能力，也坚定地站在我这一边。说实话，我觉得这个想法非常令人兴奋！而且，如果我的家族过去那些丑陋的事情能够被揭露并得到解决，那就再好不过了。如果这意味着需要将这些事情翻出来并加以处理，我完全支持。
            ]
            
            我知道，突然告诉你这个消息，对你来说肯定很突然 [pc.name] 你可能还有其他事情要做，”赫希娅说道，“不过就目前的谈判进展来看，也没有必要着急。埃尔萨拉已经为自己和她的同伴们做好了一切准备。 [etheryn.crowned
                |女王
                |摄政公主
            ]随时都可以跟我讨论这个问题，我会带你去那里，同时你也可以提出任何与这个计划相关的问题。”

那么，目前就到这里吧。我们离开赫希娅吧。[party.has etheryn
                | 然后和艾尔塔拉一起吃完剩下的果酱华夫饼和葡萄酒，之后你就和瑞恩一起离开花园吧。
                |艾尔塔拉和莱恩把剩下的果酱华夫饼和葡萄酒吃完后，你就离开花园吧。
            ] 思考这个新的机会。

rows.original: By the time you've reached the kennels, [flags.ELYON_MET |Elyon |one of the outriders ] has the wargs ready, and gives you a small bow as you approach. "Champion, [party.has etheryn |[etheryn.crowned |my queen |princess-regent ], your mounts are ready. Your priestess and the druid are already waiting for you by the stables." Sure enough, Elthara and Hethia |your mount is ready. The [etheryn.crowned |queen |princess-regent ] awaits your presence with her priestess and the druid by the stables." Sure enough, Ryn, Elthara and Hethia ]are already waiting for you, all of your mounts saddled and ready to go. The latter acknowledges your arrival with an upnod, then helps you up atop the warg's back and into the saddle. "I don't know if this is your first time riding, but even if it isn't you probably don't have enough experience to be comfortable with the pace at which we're going to go. Lean your weight forward, secure yourself in the saddle with your knees, and hold onto the collar like you would the reins on a horse. Don't worry about hurting the poor thing — the collars are made to sit on the shoulders, not the neck, so you won't accidentally choke him out. Got it?" Got it. "I'll be taking the lead and the wargs know to follow a leader, so just hold on and this good boy will do the rest." You glance over at [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |Cait, who is completely taken with the pony-sized canine mount she's been assigned for the trip. "Aww, isn't he just cute? Look, [pc.name]! He's wagging his tail!" Huh, you didn't know Cait was this enthusiastic about animals. Nevertheless, as much as she might want to, she can't stay petting her warg forever, you've got places to be and things to do. "Just one more pat, okay?" |Brint, who looks uncomfortable as he settles in the saddle and shifts about experimentally. Something wrong? "No, everything's quite comfortable, actually," Brint replies. "I'm just a bit surprised that there's actually a beastie in the kennels capable of carrying me without breaking a sweat." Is it really that surprising? Most boreal elves can end up pretty strapping, after all. Actually, come to think of it, do minotaurs use mounts? A grin. "Not much call for a mount when a forced march can get you most places in time. But I guess this'll be a new experience, won't it? I wanted to see the world, and I'm getting it in spades." |Brienne, who looks uncomfortable as she settles in the saddle and shifts about experimentally. Something wrong? "No, everything's quite comfortable, actually," Brienne replies. "I'm just a bit surprised that there's actually a beastie in the kennels capable of carrying me without breaking a sweat. I was worried about bouncing in the saddle, but everything's actually pretty secure once I realized I was supposed to lean forward." Is it really that surprising? Most boreal elves can end up pretty strapping, after all. Actually, come to think of it, do minotaurs use mounts? A grin. "Not much call for a mount when a forced march can get you most places in time. But I guess this'll be a new experience, won't it? I wanted to see the world, and I'm getting it in spades." |Arona, who's completely taken with the idea. "Fuck yeah!" she exclaims, petting the poor warg all over until its fur is all poofed out. Not that the beast minds, quite the opposite in fact — but it's looking quite undignified while she continues to lavish attention upon it. "Now this is a mount worthy of a chieftain! I've got to get these elves to tell me how to raise wolves like these so every single Kervus can have one! Our symbol is the wolf, right? It'd be fitting." "They're wargs, not wolves," Hethia replies dryly. "They may look similar on the outside, but that's about it. World of difference between the two, I'll have you know, the same way a dog isn't a wolf or a falcon isn't a hawk." Arona huffs. "Po-tay-to, po-tah-to. Same difference." It's an encouraging sign, though. For the first time, Arona's actually showing an interest in learning something of her own volition. That's got to have several levels of divine fuckery backing it up somehow. "Just imagine," Arona continues, spreading her hands as if describing the size of a fish that got away. "A longship pulls up on the shore, followed by a howl. Then three hundred wolves and their riders charge off the gangplanks and straight into battle! How amazing would that be?" Plenty, but if she's going to achieve that dream she's going to have to learn how to ride a warg without throwing up all over the place or something. Now then, saddle up. |Azyrran, who looks a little concerned for her mount. "Do you think he'll be uncomfortable, [pc.name]? I just realized I'll have to grip him with the harder parts of my body." It's nice of her to be concerned with the warg's comfort when she looks more unsettled by the prospect of this trip. "Well, vesparans don't have much need for mounts when we can just fly everywhere. I was tempted to ask to just be allowed to fly alongside the convoy, then remembered that it'd be best to remain fresh for the actual expedition. Besides, I'm sure that it'll be quite the experience." That's a good way to look at it. |Kiyoko, who's settled into the saddle as easily as if she was born to it. Now that's a level of familiarity which you weren't expecting from [kiyoko.married|your fox-wife|her]. Has she done this before? "There are clans of oni who raise white wolves as beasts of burden and mounts, beloved. Interesting in that while these animals are now extinct in the wild, having been crowded out by their natural competitors, the wolves themselves persist because of their relationship with these clans. I wonder, how long has it been since a warg has been spotted in the wild?" "One that wasn't traceable back to an escapee from the kennels? I don't think there's been a sighting since the Godswar." Elthara smiles. "The druids have wargs of their own, too, but they don't often cross the outriders' paths." "Mm. The relationship between people and their beasts speaks volumes about both sides." |Atugia, who's having a bit of trouble with her steed. "Whoa, whoa boy. What's gotten into you?" The warg just shakes its tail and lets out a loud whuff of breath. "Oh, I see the problem," Elthara coos, stepping up to the dullahan's side. "Try mounting him again, and hold the collar like this. The saddle spreads out your weight, but you'll still need to lean forward some more. You were treating him as if he were a horse." "Oh. Ah." Atugia tries again, and this time the warg doesn't try to throw her off. "Guess I shouldn't have squeezed so hard with my legs, huh?" "Every animal in the kennels has been trained with outriders for generations now, and even so, there're things that the wargs won't tolerate," Elthara replies. "It's quite the point of pride for them." |Quin, who looks a little uncomfortable sitting astride the giant wolf. It's not surprising and a little amusing, seeing him squirm in the saddle, but it's also fitting given his bunny nature. "Hey, I know what you're thinking," he says. "And yes, I was tempted to ask if I couldn't just run along instead. But... we're going to need every bit of our strength once we reach the temple, right? Even if it wouldn't be a problem for me, there's no need to show off in front of all these lovely elven ladies; I already know how much of a steal I am, after all." You give Quin a wink. Sure thing, sure thing. So long as he doesn't fall off... this is his first time riding a warg, after all. "This is my first time riding anything, to be honest. Unsurprisingly, taeleer don't have much call for personal mounts when we can just leg it anywhere we like. Not that there isn't any call for carts or wagons in the Tael Alliance... but there's a world of difference between sitting in a flatbed cart and riding on the back of some animal." The warg lets out a large whuff of hot breath at that. "Oh, were you upset that I called you an animal? Don't worry about it, so am I. We're both just stupid sexy animals, that's all." He laughs. "All right, [pc.name]. Let's just go before something silly happens, okay?" |Viviane, who's taken off her hat and stowed it wherever the enchantress keeps her things when they're not needed. "To be more aerodynamic, of course," she says before you can even ask. "That, and I don't want it blowing off my head and holding everyone up while I go get it." That, and would she pass by the opportunity to have her hair billow out behind her dramatically while thundering through the woods on the back of a warg? Viv's smile widens. "I say, you're painting quite the tempting picture. It wouldn't hurt to indulge myself a little, would it?" No, it wouldn't. That being said, she doesn't look too uncomfortable — has she tried this sort of thing before? Riding her spirit wolf, maybe? "Once, out of curiosity. No, it didn't work out as I'd hoped, and no, it was nothing like the warg who's under me right now. The saddle and collar really help." Good, because it looks like you're going to be traveling at quite the brisk pace. |Agni, who looks a little concerned for her mount. "Do you think he'll be uncomfortable, [pc.name]? I just realized my legs and arm-wings might get in the way and all" It's nice of her to be concerned with the warg's comfort when she looks more unsettled by the prospect of this trip. "Well, harpies don't have much need for mounts when we can just fly everywhere. I was tempted to ask to just be allowed to fly alongside everyone, then remembered that it'd be best to remain fresh for the actual expedition. Besides, I'm sure that it'll be quite the experience. Of all the things I've done over my lives, I don't remember getting to ride a warg." That's good to hear — despite her breadth of experience, going adventuring with you means she can still find plenty of novelty in the world. Bet she's never delved into the infested mess of an ancient elven temple. "Given that I'm living in one with the hellhound while not out and about with you, I'd like to know what the others are like. Shall we?" ]

rows.raw: " By the time you've reached the kennels, [flags.ELYON_MET |Elyon |one of the outriders ] has the wargs ready, and gives you a small bow as you approach. "Champion, [party.has etheryn |[etheryn.crowned |my queen |princess-regent ], your mounts are ready. Your priestess and the druid are already waiting for you by the stables." Sure enough, Elthara and Hethia |your mount is ready. The [etheryn.crowned |queen |princess-regent ] awaits your presence with her priestess and the druid by the stables." Sure enough, Ryn, Elthara and Hethia ]are already waiting for you, all of your mounts saddled and ready to go. The latter acknowledges your arrival with an upnod, then helps you up atop the warg's back and into the saddle. "I don't know if this is your first time riding, but even if it isn't you probably don't have enough experience to be comfortable with the pace at which we're going to go. Lean your weight forward, secure yourself in the saddle with your knees, and hold onto the collar like you would the reins on a horse. Don't worry about hurting the poor thing — the collars are made to sit on the shoulders, not the neck, so you won't accidentally choke him out. Got it?" Got it. "I'll be taking the lead and the wargs know to follow a leader, so just hold on and this good boy will do the rest." You glance over at [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |Cait, who is completely taken with the pony-sized canine mount she's been assigned for the trip. "Aww, isn't he just cute? Look, [pc.name]! He's wagging his tail!" Huh, you didn't know Cait was this enthusiastic about animals. Nevertheless, as much as she might want to, she can't stay petting her warg forever, you've got places to be and things to do. "Just one more pat, okay?" |Brint, who looks uncomfortable as he settles in the saddle and shifts about experimentally. Something wrong? "No, everything's quite comfortable, actually," Brint replies. "I'm just a bit surprised that there's actually a beastie in the kennels capable of carrying me without breaking a sweat." Is it really that surprising? Most boreal elves can end up pretty strapping, after all. Actually, come to think of it, do minotaurs use mounts? A grin. "Not much call for a mount when a forced march can get you most places in time. But I guess this'll be a new experience, won't it? I wanted to see the world, and I'm getting it in spades." |Brienne, who looks uncomfortable as she settles in the saddle and shifts about experimentally. Something wrong? "No, everything's quite comfortable, actually," Brienne replies. "I'm just a bit surprised that there's actually a beastie in the kennels capable of carrying me without breaking a sweat. I was worried about bouncing in the saddle, but everything's actually pretty secure once I realized I was supposed to lean forward." Is it really that surprising? Most boreal elves can end up pretty strapping, after all. Actually, come to think of it, do minotaurs use mounts? A grin. "Not much call for a mount when a forced march can get you most places in time. But I guess this'll be a new experience, won't it? I wanted to see the world, and I'm getting it in spades." |Arona, who's completely taken with the idea. "Fuck yeah!" she exclaims, petting the poor warg all over until its fur is all poofed out. Not that the beast minds, quite the opposite in fact — but it's looking quite undignified while she continues to lavish attention upon it. "Now this is a mount worthy of a chieftain! I've got to get these elves to tell me how to raise wolves like these so every single Kervus can have one! Our symbol is the wolf, right? It'd be fitting." "They're wargs, not wolves," Hethia replies dryly. "They may look similar on the outside, but that's about it. World of difference between the two, I'll have you know, the same way a dog isn't a wolf or a falcon isn't a hawk." Arona huffs. "Po-tay-to, po-tah-to. Same difference." It's an encouraging sign, though. For the first time, Arona's actually showing an interest in learning something of her own volition. That's got to have several levels of divine fuckery backing it up somehow. "Just imagine," Arona continues, spreading her hands as if describing the size of a fish that got away. "A longship pulls up on the shore, followed by a howl. Then three hundred wolves and their riders charge off the gangplanks and straight into battle! How amazing would that be?" Plenty, but if she's going to achieve that dream she's going to have to learn how to ride a warg without throwing up all over the place or something. Now then, saddle up. |Azyrran, who looks a little concerned for her mount. "Do you think he'll be uncomfortable, [pc.name]? I just realized I'll have to grip him with the harder parts of my body." It's nice of her to be concerned with the warg's comfort when she looks more unsettled by the prospect of this trip. "Well, vesparans don't have much need for mounts when we can just fly everywhere. I was tempted to ask to just be allowed to fly alongside the convoy, then remembered that it'd be best to remain fresh for the actual expedition. Besides, I'm sure that it'll be quite the experience." That's a good way to look at it. |Kiyoko, who's settled into the saddle as easily as if she was born to it. Now that's a level of familiarity which you weren't expecting from [kiyoko.married|your fox-wife|her]. Has she done this before? "There are clans of oni who raise white wolves as beasts of burden and mounts, beloved. Interesting in that while these animals are now extinct in the wild, having been crowded out by their natural competitors, the wolves themselves persist because of their relationship with these clans. I wonder, how long has it been since a warg has been spotted in the wild?" "One that wasn't traceable back to an escapee from the kennels? I don't think there's been a sighting since the Godswar." Elthara smiles. "The druids have wargs of their own, too, but they don't often cross the outriders' paths." "Mm. The relationship between people and their beasts speaks volumes about both sides." |Atugia, who's having a bit of trouble with her steed. "Whoa, whoa boy. What's gotten into you?" The warg just shakes its tail and lets out a loud whuff of breath. "Oh, I see the problem," Elthara coos, stepping up to the dullahan's side. "Try mounting him again, and hold the collar like this. The saddle spreads out your weight, but you'll still need to lean forward some more. You were treating him as if he were a horse." "Oh. Ah." Atugia tries again, and this time the warg doesn't try to throw her off. "Guess I shouldn't have squeezed so hard with my legs, huh?" "Every animal in the kennels has been trained with outriders for generations now, and even so, there're things that the wargs won't tolerate," Elthara replies. "It's quite the point of pride for them." |Quin, who looks a little uncomfortable sitting astride the giant wolf. It's not surprising and a little amusing, seeing him squirm in the saddle, but it's also fitting given his bunny nature. "Hey, I know what you're thinking," he says. "And yes, I was tempted to ask if I couldn't just run along instead. But... we're going to need every bit of our strength once we reach the temple, right? Even if it wouldn't be a problem for me, there's no need to show off in front of all these lovely elven ladies; I already know how much of a steal I am, after all." You give Quin a wink. Sure thing, sure thing. So long as he doesn't fall off... this is his first time riding a warg, after all. "This is my first time riding anything, to be honest. Unsurprisingly, taeleer don't have much call for personal mounts when we can just leg it anywhere we like. Not that there isn't any call for carts or wagons in the Tael Alliance... but there's a world of difference between sitting in a flatbed cart and riding on the back of some animal." The warg lets out a large whuff of hot breath at that. "Oh, were you upset that I called you an animal? Don't worry about it, so am I. We're both just stupid sexy animals, that's all." He laughs. "All right, [pc.name]. Let's just go before something silly happens, okay?" |Viviane, who's taken off her hat and stowed it wherever the enchantress keeps her things when they're not needed. "To be more aerodynamic, of course," she says before you can even ask. "That, and I don't want it blowing off my head and holding everyone up while I go get it." That, and would she pass by the opportunity to have her hair billow out behind her dramatically while thundering through the woods on the back of a warg? Viv's smile widens. "I say, you're painting quite the tempting picture. It wouldn't hurt to indulge myself a little, would it?" No, it wouldn't. That being said, she doesn't look too uncomfortable — has she tried this sort of thing before? Riding her spirit wolf, maybe? "Once, out of curiosity. No, it didn't work out as I'd hoped, and no, it was nothing like the warg who's under me right now. The saddle and collar really help." Good, because it looks like you're going to be traveling at quite the brisk pace. |Agni, who looks a little concerned for her mount. "Do you think he'll be uncomfortable, [pc.name]? I just realized my legs and arm-wings might get in the way and all" It's nice of her to be concerned with the warg's comfort when she looks more unsettled by the prospect of this trip. "Well, harpies don't have much need for mounts when we can just fly everywhere. I was tempted to ask to just be allowed to fly alongside everyone, then remembered that it'd be best to remain fresh for the actual expedition. Besides, I'm sure that it'll be quite the experience. Of all the things I've done over my lives, I don't remember getting to ride a warg." That's good to hear — despite her breadth of experience, going adventuring with you means she can still find plenty of novelty in the world. Bet she's never delved into the infested mess of an ancient elven temple. "Given that I'm living in one with the hellhound while not out and about with you, I'd like to know what the others are like. Shall we?" ] "

rows.original: Soon enough, the lot of you are roaring down the streets of the Winter City, attracting no small amount of attention from people about their daily lives as five wargs tear down the road, headed straight for the city gate. Good, let them gawk — part of the point of this exercise is to build Ryn's renown, after all. The guards salute your party as you pass through the gatehouse and by the tent city that's sprung up just outside the walls, heading straight into the Frostwood. The wargs' loping gait, the breakneck speed at which they barrel down the forest pathways — the wind screams in your ears, and your stomach churns. Nevertheless, you stay firm in the saddle, front half pressed against the muscular beast's thick fur as you hold on to the handled collar for dear life. [party.has arona |Arona whoops and howls off to your side, enjoying every second of it. ]Looping south around the fjord and its broken bridge, heading east through the cold bog, and then even further east than the woodland paths lead — there's little doubt that you've left familiar territory at this point, perhaps only made traversable by the wargs' swiftness and light feet, as well as Hethia's knowledge of the cold eastern bog. Eventually, though, the trees return once more, along with solid ground; the atmosphere of the woods has changed, too. You concentrate on holding on, letting your mount follow Hethia's — how long has it been? One hour? Two? Just as you think you're getting used to this, the convoy slows to a stop, and the lurching sensation in your stomach settles as Hethia dismounts. Are you there already? "It's just over that next hill," the druidess says, pointing deeper into the woods while Elthara helps everyone else off their steeds. "This is the closest any who follow the Old Wyld have been to any of the temples in a couple of centuries, now; I'm not going any further." Yeah, you get the idea. She'll be staying here with the wargs, then? "Mm-hm. If you don't return in two days, then I'll call in the reinforcements; the valkyries should be able to fly here in no time at all, right, Elthara?" "That's right. Two days, remember. If we don't return by then, you know how to call for them." Stretching herself after the long ride, Elthara turns towards you and [comp2.name]. "Are you ready?" "As ready as I think I'll ever be." "Well then. Champion, lead the way." Nothing for it. [pc.weapon] at the ready, you crest the hill and the trees part as you emerge into a large clearing. Is... is that the temple, then? And the surrounding village? Given everything that Hethia said about it, the oversized pile of rubble and rotting hovels that surround it is extremely underwhelming — you'd been expecting a grandiose temple fallen into ruin, overrun with vile life. This, though, this doesn't look any different from your average overgrown ruin. And this is supposed to be the tragic fall of the greatest of the pale elf druids in their last stand? It can't even be more than one story high, perhaps but half the size of Sanders' temple back in Hawkethorne. There's supposed to be a whole village which supported a single temple, not just a few homes... where are the fabled vineyards? The fungus that was said to have decimated the druids? Something's not right here. You don't think that Hethia would be lying to you, so... [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |"T-that's all?" Cait blinks in disbelief. "Does that mean that everything that Dad read about the boreal elf druids was also wrong?" Well, you [pc.bg scholar |know full well the ability of historians to embellish facts for one reason or the other |suppose the stories could have been exaggerated ]. On the other hand, maybe there's something else at play here, too. It's hard, but you're trying not to pre-judge the situation before investigating further, otherwise you might just turn around and tell Hethia this is going to be a waste of time. "Y-yeah." Cait perks up, a little light returning to her eyes as she grips her [cait.weapon]. "Let's take a look around, shan't we? Maybe we'll find something more." |"Looks like it'll be a bit of a squeeze," Brint says as he gazes upon the mound from afar. "I don't mind being underground, of course... but no one else ever makes things minotaur-sized, I tell you." |"Looks like it'll be a bit of a squeeze," Brienne says as she gazes upon the mound from afar. "I don't mind being underground, of course... but no one else ever makes things minotaur-sized, I tell you." |"Hey, it really does look like a burial mound," Arona says, shielding her eyes as she peers down the hill and into the ruins. "No need to get disappointed, now. The old chieftains of the isles, they could bury a whole longship and make it look like just a pile of dirt. Maybe there's a lot more temple to this than meets the eye." Does she think so? "Y'know, we're near the fjord still. I wonder if there's going to be a longship —" No. You're a good distance from the coastline, the pale elves aren't as into longships as her people are, and this is supposed to be a temple farming community. "Aww." Well, if all the druids are interred with their temple, then she's not wrong that it's a burial mound. With burial mounds comes ghosts, she knows that, right? Arona scowls. "[flags.ARONA_TOTEM |Yeah, but now I can smack them upside the head like anyone else. Doesn't make me like them any more, but at least I'm not afraid of them any more. If they want a piece of me, well, those bastards will just have to get in line. I'll teach them how to stay dead. |You just have to be a killjoy, don't you?" Hey, you can only overcome your fears by standing up to them. "That sounds like shit that Hretha would say. I'm not buying it, not one bit. ]" |As you start down the hill and towards the ruined temple, you notice that Azyrran's particularly on edge, her [azyrran.weapon] half-raised, ready to spring into action at any moment. Has she sensed some danger that you're not privy to? "Not exactly. But it's a tense feeling... as if we were walking into another queen's hive on the opening stretch of a raid. A sense of many, many things watching us and waiting to spring an ambush..." You see. Or rather, you don't see — but Azzy's quite serious, you can tell. If she gets a better handle on this imminent danger, then she should tell you posthaste. "Trust me, I will." |"Oh. Quaint." Kiyoko is clearly trying to find words to address the sight that lies before you without being impolite. "Seeing the remnants of something that once was great is always sobering, is it not, beloved?" You don't know that the sinking feeling in your stomach is so much more sobering than mildly disappointing, after Hethia talked it up so much. "Either their grand constructions fell into ruin at unprecedented speed once left untended, or there is more to this than meets the eye; my personal assessment of the situation would lean towards the latter as a more likely outcome. But even if there is not much to be had out here, the trip is not wasted, because it was with you. Perhaps thinking of it in that fashion will cheer you up? I am quite aware that people do go riding for pleasure — even if nothing happens, it will still have been a pleasant experience." Ah... that kind of thinking does require a kind of magnanimity that not everyone can be capable of all the time. Nevertheless... [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |she ] isn't wrong. It's nice to be able to spend time together, regardless of the circumstances. |"This isn't all there is to this place," Atugia says, coming up next to you and stamping her feet on the hillock. "I can feel it on my skin." Her skin. "Or more correctly, the runes. Them and the druids' magic, I don't think they're too different, or at least not in the way they're worked." W-wait. What did she mean by not too different? Does this mean she'll start growing mushrooms all over her or something? "I don't think that'll happen, or else I'd have started feeling funny already. Right? Right?" Presumably Elthara would've said something about Tui if your dullahan friend was in danger, so probably not. But what was she going to tell you? "There's more to this than meets the eye," Atugia replies, stamping on the dirt again for emphasis. "Let's go take a closer look, yeah? I'm sure we'll find something good. I'll be sure to tell you if I suddenly feel really horny, or something." |"I don't like this place." You look over your shoulder at Quin, who's continuously shifting his weight from one foot to the other. To say that the bunny-man is tense would be a grand understatement — he looks equally divided between legging it forward to meet whatever danger his instincts sense head-on, or legging it away as quickly as his feet will take him. Has he sensed some danger that you're not privy to? "Kinda?" Quin grimaces and thumbs down at the ruins below. "My legs are telling me that I should get out of here, and they're rarely wrong. Now, whether I will get out of here is another matter, given that I know this would be dangerous going in. But what I'm feeling is completely at odds with that. It damn well isn't as peaceful as it looks." You'll take his word for it, then. If he has any more concrete warnings, you'd love to hear them. "Just doing my best. Why don't we head down and take a look, then?" |"Hmm," Viv says, producing her hat and plonking it back on her head as she surveys the scene. "Doesn't appear like much at a first glance. Maybe the druids were really just telling tall tales about themselves, which grew in the telling." She finds it all underwhelming too, huh? Well, it's certainly a possibility. "Of course, we've got to keep open minds, and most of all, perform a thorough investigation — as a point of professional pride, if nothing else. Come now, it'll be an experience, if nothing else." |"That's it?" Agni blinks, shielding her eyes as she peers down the hill at the ruins. "This looks nothing like the Temple of Terrestrial Fire — the mound isn't even a quarter of its size! And this is supposed to be the greatest, grandest temple the elven druids built to the wyld?" It is odd, isn't it? The Temple of Terrestrial Fire is supposed to be a lesser temple, and it's still in relatively good shape after all these years. Xadaron Temple can't have crumbled into just a few heaps of marble bricks in two centuries and a bit, can it? If the fungus was so virulent and destructive, where is it? "I guess those are answers we're going to have to find ourselves. I don't know about you, but I'm actually pretty excited about it all." Well, that would be just like Agni, wouldn't it? All right, then — time to get a closer look at this mess. ] Indeed, your job here is to investigate, and you're not about to leave without doing just that. If nothing else, you'll be able to tell Hethia that either the druids' temples were never very great to begin with, the tale growing in the telling, or that the rate of decay that was affected upon them by this fungus was absolutely incredible. Continuing to lead the way, you draw closer to what's presumably the ruined temple. Close-up, it doesn't look too different from a lupine burial mound — the kind that jarls of ages past would bury themselves in along with all manner of valuables. As overgrown and half-buried as it is, fine marble still sticks out of the mound at various spots, and the way the ground here is much firmer underfoot. Maybe the temple sunk into the earth, and there's more to this than meets the eye? But why would that happen, though? You're already well past the bog, and if Xadaron temple had been passed from one generation of Xadarons to the next, surely the temple sinking into soft ground would've been noticed long before the Godswar. Ah, it was just a thought... At last, the lot of you wind up at the foot of the mound, where Ryn points at a half-crumbled archway leading into its depths. The remnants of a silvered gate lie half-buried in the mud and stone, torn off its hinges from the inside; the tunnel leading further into the mound is lined with stone bricks, covered in all kinds of overgrowth. Once again, you'd have expected something grander from the greatest of the druidic temples... but at least there's more to this than just disappointment. Well, you'll just have to see what lies inside, won't you?
rows.translation: 不久之后，你们这些人便沿着冬城的街道飞奔而去，五条狼族冲在前面，直奔城门而去，这一幕自然吸引了许多正在过着自己日常生活的市民的注意。 好，让他们去围观吧——毕竟，这次行动的目的之一就是提升瑞恩的声望。当你们穿过城门，经过城墙外搭建的帐篷城时，守卫们都会向你们的队伍行礼，然后你们就可以直接进入寒冰森林了。 那些狼族奔跑时的笨拙姿态，以及它们以惊人的速度在森林小径上飞奔时所带来的冲击——风声在耳边呼啸，你的胃也跟着一阵阵地抽搐。然而，你依然紧紧地坐在马鞍上，上半身紧贴着这只肌肉发达的野兽浓密的皮毛，双手则拼命地抓住马鬃不放。 [party.has arona |阿罗娜兴奋地冲到你身边，尽情享受着每一刻。 ]绕着峡湾及其断裂的桥梁向南行驶，然后穿过寒冷的沼泽地向东前进，再继续向东延伸，超越那些林间小路所能到达的范围——毫无疑问，此时你已经离开了熟悉的地域。或许只有狼族敏捷的速度和轻快的足部步，以及赫希娅对这片寒冷东部沼泽地的熟悉，才能帮助你继续前行。 然而，最终树木又一次重新生长起来，地面也恢复了坚实；森林的氛围也发生了变化。你努力保持平衡，让坐骑跟随赫希娅的步伐——已经过去多久了呢？一个小时？两个小时？就在你以为自己已经开始适应这种环境的时候，车队突然停了下来，随着赫希娅下马，你胃里那种翻腾的感觉也终于平息了下来。 就在那座小山的后面。”女德鲁伊说道，一边指向森林深处，而埃尔萨拉则帮助其他人从马背上下来。“对于那些追随古老荒野之道的人来说，这是几个世纪以来他们最接近这些神庙的地方了；我不会再往前走了。 嗯，你明白我的意思了吧。那么，她就会和那些狼族一起留在这里了？ “嗯，没错。如果你两天内没有回来，我就会召集援军；那些女武神应该很快就能飞到这里吧，对吧，埃尔萨拉？” “没错。就是两天，记住这个时间。如果到那时我们还没有回来，你知道该怎么召唤她们。”经过长途跋涉，埃尔萨拉伸了伸腰，然后转向你说道 [comp2.name]你准备好了吗？” “我已经准备得尽可能充分了。” “那好吧。冠军，你先带路吧。” 没什么好说的。 [pc.weapon] 当你冲上山顶，树木立刻分开，一片广阔的空地出现在眼前。难……难道那就是那座寺庙吗？还有周围的村庄？根据赫希娅所说的那些描述，眼前这些堆积如山的废墟和破败的房屋实在令人大失所望——你原本期待看到的应该是一座宏伟的寺庙，如今却变成了这样一片废墟，到处都是令人不快的生物。 然而，这看起来和那些普通的、杂草丛生的废墟并没有什么两样。而这竟然被认为是那些最伟大的苍白精灵德鲁伊在最后抵抗中遭遇的悲惨结局？这座建筑的高度顶多只有一个故事那么高，规模或许还不到鹰棘镇时桑德斯神庙的一半。 按理说，应该有一个整个村庄来支撑那座寺庙，而不仅仅是一些零星的房屋……那些传说中的葡萄园在哪里？还有那种据说曾经导致德鲁伊族灭绝的真菌呢？ 这里肯定有些不对劲。 你并不认为赫希娅会欺骗你，所以…… [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |就这些吗？”凯特难以置信地眨了眨眼，“难道这意味着爸爸之前读到的关于北方精灵德鲁伊的所有内容都是错的吗？” 嗯，你 [pc.bg scholar |我非常清楚历史学家们出于种种原因会夸大事实。 |或许这些故事被夸大了一些吧。 ]另一方面，也许这里还有其他的原因在起作用。这确实很难判断，但在进一步调查之前，你最好先不要妄下结论，否则你可能会直接告诉赫希娅，这件事纯粹是在浪费时间。 “嗯……是的。”凯特重新振作起来，她的眼睛里重新焕发出了轻型芒，同时紧紧握住了手中的东西。 [cait.weapon]我们先四处看看吧，怎么样？也许我们会找到更多东西。 |看起来空间有点紧张啊，”布林特远远地望着那个土堆说道，“当然，我并不介意待在地下……但说实话，从来没有人把东西做得像米诺陶尔那么大啊。 |看起来这里的空间有点拥挤啊，”布蕾妮远眺着那个土堆说道，“当然，我并不介意待在地下……但说实话，从来没有人把东西做得像米诺陶尔那么大啊。 |嘿，看起来确实像是一座坟墓啊，”阿罗娜说着，用手遮住眼睛，向下望去，望向那些废墟。“不过现在也没必要太失望。那些岛上的老首领们，就算把一整艘长船埋进去，也能把它弄得看起来就像只是一堆土而已。 也许这件事的来龙去脉远比表面上看到的要复杂得多。” 她真的是这么认为的吗？ “你知道，我们现在还在靠近峡湾的地方。我在想，会不会有长船出现…… 不。你距离海岸线还有相当的距离，而且那些淡色精灵并不像她的族人那样热衷于使用长船。 以及 这里本应该是一个用于在神庙中进行耕作的社区啊。 “哎呀。” 好吧，如果所有的德鲁伊都被安葬在他们的神庙里，那么她说这是个墓冢确实没错。有墓冢的地方就会有鬼魂出没，她应该是知道的吧？ 阿罗娜皱起了眉头。[flags.ARONA_TOTEM |是啊，但现在我可以像其他人一样揍他们的头了。这并不会让我更喜欢他们，但至少我不再害怕他们了。如果他们想得到我的东西，那这些混蛋就只能排队等候了。我会让他们知道什么叫“永远死掉”。 |你简直就是个扫兴的人，对吧？” “嘿，只有勇敢面对自己的恐惧，才能真正克服它们。” “这种话听起来就像赫蕾莎会说的……我才不信呢，一点都不会相信。 ]" |当你开始向下坡方向行进，朝着那座被毁的寺庙前进时，你注意到阿兹兰显得格外紧张不安。 [azyrran.weapon] 半蹲着，随时准备行动。她是不是察觉到了某些你并不知道的危险？ “不完全是。但这种感觉确实很紧张……就好像在开始一次突袭行动时，我们正走进另一位女王的蜂巢。有一种感觉，好像有很多很多东西在注视着我们，随时准备发动伏击……” 你懂的。或者说，你应该是懂的。 不要 看吧——不过你能看出，阿齐是相当认真的。如果她能更好地应对这种迫在眉睫的危险，那么她一定会立刻告诉你。 “相信我，我一定会的。 |哦，真是别有风味啊。”清子显然在努力寻找合适的词语，以便既能描述眼前的景象，又不会显得失礼。“看到那些曾经辉煌过的事物的遗迹，总会让人感到深思，不是吗，亲爱的？ 在赫希娅如此大力地宣扬之后，你根本不知道，那种胃里发沉的感觉，其实比轻微的失望要令人清醒得多。 “要么是那些宏伟的建筑在无人照料的情况下，以前所未有的速度毁于一旦；要么就是这件事背后隐藏着更多的真相；就我个人对形势的分析而言，后一种可能性更大。 不过，即使这次旅行并没有带来太多收获，这次经历也并没有白费，因为我是和你一起度过的。或许这样想会让你的心情好一些吧？我很清楚，有些人确实是为了享受骑行的过程而去骑马的——即使什么特别的收获都没有，那也是一次愉快的体验。啊……这种思维方式确实需要一种宽宏大量的胸怀，而并不是每个人都能时刻具备这种品质。不过…… [kiyoko.married |你的狐狸精妻子 |她 ] 没错。无论在什么情况下，能够一起度过时轻型总是件美好的事情。 |这个地方的可不止这些，”阿图吉娅走到你身边，站在小土丘上跺了跺足部说道，“我能真切地感觉到这一点。” 她的皮肤。 “或者更准确地说，是那些符文。 那些东西和德鲁伊的魔法，我觉得它们并没有太大区别，至少在运作方式上是没有区别的。 等等，她说的“没有太大区别”是什么意思？难道这意味着她的身体上会开始长出蘑菇来还是怎么回事？ 我觉得那种事情不会发生，否则我早就开始觉得不舒服了，对吧？对吧？” 如果你的那个 dullahan 朋友真的处于危险之中，想必 埃尔萨拉 会说些什么的，所以大概不会发生这种事吧。 但她究竟要告诉你什么呢？ “这件事的背后还有更多的隐情，”阿图吉娅一边说，一边再次踩在泥土上，以强调自己的话。“我们一起去仔细看看吧，好吗？我相信我们会发现一些有价值的东西的。 如果我突然感到特别欲火中烧之类的，我一定会告诉你的。 |我不太喜欢这个地方。” 你回头看了看奎因，他正不停地把体重从一只足部转移到另一只足部上。说那个“兔子人”很紧张，简直是一种轻描淡写的说法——他似乎在两种想法之间挣扎：一种是立刻迎面面对那些他的直觉所感知到的危险，另一种则是尽快逃离那里。 他是不是察觉到了某些你并不知道的危险？ “有点吧？”奎因皱了皱眉头，指了指足部下的废墟，“我的腿在告诉我，我应该离开这里，而它们的判断很少会错。现在，不管我是否该听它们的 会 从这里离开则是另一回事了，因为我知道进去会很危险。但我现在的感受与那些警告完全相反——这里根本不像看上去那么平静。” 那么，你就相信他的话吧。如果他还有其他更具体的警告，你肯定很愿意听一听。 “我只是在尽自己最大的努力而已。那么，我们还是下去看看吧？ |嗯，”薇芙说着，拿出她的帽子重新戴在头上，然后环顾四周。“乍一看，这里确实没什么特别的。也许那些德鲁伊们当初只是在自己身上编了一些故事，而这些故事在后来被人们反复讲述的过程中逐渐被夸大了。她也觉得这一切都令人失望，对吧？嗯，这种可能性确实是存在的。 “当然，我们必须保持开放的心态，最重要的是，要进行彻底的调查——至少这也是出于职业操守的考虑。 来吧，至少这也是一次难忘的经历。 |就这样？”阿格尼眨了眨眼，用手遮住眼睛，向下望着山足部下的废墟。“这根本不像是大地之火神殿的样子——那个土堆的规模甚至不到它四分之一！而据说这里可是精灵德鲁伊为野地建造的最宏伟、最壮观的圣殿啊 是 奇怪，不是吗？地火神殿本应该是一个地位较低的寺庙才对 以及 经过这么多年，它的状况仍然相当不错。毕竟，Xadaron神庙不可能在两个多世纪的时间里就变成一堆堆的大理石碎块吧？如果那种真菌真的具有如此强烈的破坏力，那它现在应该在哪里呢？ 我想这些答案我们还是得自己去寻找吧。我不知道你们怎么想，但我个人对此感到相当兴奋。” 嗯，这倒和阿格尼的性格很像，不是吗？好吧，那么——是时候仔细研究一下这个混乱的局面了。 ] 事实上，你在这里的任务就是进行调查，而你不完成这项任务是不会离开的。至少，你可以告诉赫希娅：要么是那些德鲁伊的神庙本来就没什么了不起之处，只是这些故事在流传过程中被夸大了；要么就是这种真菌对它们造成的破坏速度确实快得令人难以置信。 你继续走在最前面，逐渐接近那座想必已经毁坏的寺庙。近距离看，它与那些古代酋长用来安葬自己并存放各种贵重物品的坟墓并没有太大区别。 尽管这片土地已经杂草丛生、半被掩埋，但一些优质的大理石仍然在土堆的各个地方显露出来，而且这里的地面踩上去要坚实得多。 也许那座寺庙沉入了地下，其中隐藏着不为人知的原因？但究竟为什么会这样呢？你已经走过了那片沼泽地，如果Xadaron的寺庙真的是一代又一代Xadaron家族代代相传的遗产，那么在“神战”爆发之前，寺庙沉入松软的地面这一情况肯定早就被人们注意到了。 啊，只是随便想想而已…… 最终，你们所有人都来到了土丘的足部下。瑞恩指着一个半毁的拱门，那拱门通向土丘的深处。一扇银色大门的残骸半埋在泥石之中，门扇从内部被扯掉了铰链；而通往土丘内部的隧道两侧用石砖砌成，上面长满了各种杂草。 再一次，你本会期望从最伟大的德鲁伊神殿中获得一些更宏伟的东西……但至少，这件事并不只是令人失望而已。好吧，你总得去看看里面究竟有什么吧？
rows.raw: " Soon enough, the lot of you are roaring down the streets of the Winter City, attracting no small amount of attention from people about their daily lives as five wargs tear down the road, headed straight for the city gate. Good, let them gawk — part of the point of this exercise is to build Ryn's renown, after all. The guards salute your party as you pass through the gatehouse and by the tent city that's sprung up just outside the walls, heading straight into the Frostwood. The wargs' loping gait, the breakneck speed at which they barrel down the forest pathways — the wind screams in your ears, and your stomach churns. Nevertheless, you stay firm in the saddle, front half pressed against the muscular beast's thick fur as you hold on to the handled collar for dear life. [party.has arona |Arona whoops and howls off to your side, enjoying every second of it. ]Looping south around the fjord and its broken bridge, heading east through the cold bog, and then even further east than the woodland paths lead — there's little doubt that you've left familiar territory at this point, perhaps only made traversable by the wargs' swiftness and light feet, as well as Hethia's knowledge of the cold eastern bog. Eventually, though, the trees return once more, along with solid ground; the atmosphere of the woods has changed, too. You concentrate on holding on, letting your mount follow Hethia's — how long has it been? One hour? Two? Just as you think you're getting used to this, the convoy slows to a stop, and the lurching sensation in your stomach settles as Hethia dismounts. Are you there already? "It's just over that next hill," the druidess says, pointing deeper into the woods while Elthara helps everyone else off their steeds. "This is the closest any who follow the Old Wyld have been to any of the temples in a couple of centuries, now; I'm not going any further." Yeah, you get the idea. She'll be staying here with the wargs, then? "Mm-hm. If you don't return in two days, then I'll call in the reinforcements; the valkyries should be able to fly here in no time at all, right, Elthara?" "That's right. Two days, remember. If we don't return by then, you know how to call for them." Stretching herself after the long ride, Elthara turns towards you and [comp2.name]. "Are you ready?" "As ready as I think I'll ever be." "Well then. Champion, lead the way." Nothing for it. [pc.weapon] at the ready, you crest the hill and the trees part as you emerge into a large clearing. Is... is that the temple, then? And the surrounding village? Given everything that Hethia said about it, the oversized pile of rubble and rotting hovels that surround it is extremely underwhelming — you'd been expecting a grandiose temple fallen into ruin, overrun with vile life. This, though, this doesn't look any different from your average overgrown ruin. And this is supposed to be the tragic fall of the greatest of the pale elf druids in their last stand? It can't even be more than one story high, perhaps but half the size of Sanders' temple back in Hawkethorne. There's supposed to be a whole village which supported a single temple, not just a few homes... where are the fabled vineyards? The fungus that was said to have decimated the druids? Something's not right here. You don't think that Hethia would be lying to you, so... [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |"T-that's all?" Cait blinks in disbelief. "Does that mean that everything that Dad read about the boreal elf druids was also wrong?" Well, you [pc.bg scholar |know full well the ability of historians to embellish facts for one reason or the other |suppose the stories could have been exaggerated ]. On the other hand, maybe there's something else at play here, too. It's hard, but you're trying not to pre-judge the situation before investigating further, otherwise you might just turn around and tell Hethia this is going to be a waste of time. "Y-yeah." Cait perks up, a little light returning to her eyes as she grips her [cait.weapon]. "Let's take a look around, shan't we? Maybe we'll find something more." |"Looks like it'll be a bit of a squeeze," Brint says as he gazes upon the mound from afar. "I don't mind being underground, of course... but no one else ever makes things minotaur-sized, I tell you." |"Looks like it'll be a bit of a squeeze," Brienne says as she gazes upon the mound from afar. "I don't mind being underground, of course... but no one else ever makes things minotaur-sized, I tell you." |"Hey, it really does look like a burial mound," Arona says, shielding her eyes as she peers down the hill and into the ruins. "No need to get disappointed, now. The old chieftains of the isles, they could bury a whole longship and make it look like just a pile of dirt. Maybe there's a lot more temple to this than meets the eye." Does she think so? "Y'know, we're near the fjord still. I wonder if there's going to be a longship —" No. You're a good distance from the coastline, the pale elves aren't as into longships as her people are, and this is supposed to be a temple farming community. "Aww." Well, if all the druids are interred with their temple, then she's not wrong that it's a burial mound. With burial mounds comes ghosts, she knows that, right? Arona scowls. "[flags.ARONA_TOTEM |Yeah, but now I can smack them upside the head like anyone else. Doesn't make me like them any more, but at least I'm not afraid of them any more. If they want a piece of me, well, those bastards will just have to get in line. I'll teach them how to stay dead. |You just have to be a killjoy, don't you?" Hey, you can only overcome your fears by standing up to them. "That sounds like shit that Hretha would say. I'm not buying it, not one bit. ]" |As you start down the hill and towards the ruined temple, you notice that Azyrran's particularly on edge, her [azyrran.weapon] half-raised, ready to spring into action at any moment. Has she sensed some danger that you're not privy to? "Not exactly. But it's a tense feeling... as if we were walking into another queen's hive on the opening stretch of a raid. A sense of many, many things watching us and waiting to spring an ambush..." You see. Or rather, you don't see — but Azzy's quite serious, you can tell. If she gets a better handle on this imminent danger, then she should tell you posthaste. "Trust me, I will." |"Oh. Quaint." Kiyoko is clearly trying to find words to address the sight that lies before you without being impolite. "Seeing the remnants of something that once was great is always sobering, is it not, beloved?" You don't know that the sinking feeling in your stomach is so much more sobering than mildly disappointing, after Hethia talked it up so much. "Either their grand constructions fell into ruin at unprecedented speed once left untended, or there is more to this than meets the eye; my personal assessment of the situation would lean towards the latter as a more likely outcome. But even if there is not much to be had out here, the trip is not wasted, because it was with you. Perhaps thinking of it in that fashion will cheer you up? I am quite aware that people do go riding for pleasure — even if nothing happens, it will still have been a pleasant experience." Ah... that kind of thinking does require a kind of magnanimity that not everyone can be capable of all the time. Nevertheless... [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |she ] isn't wrong. It's nice to be able to spend time together, regardless of the circumstances. |"This isn't all there is to this place," Atugia says, coming up next to you and stamping her feet on the hillock. "I can feel it on my skin." Her skin. "Or more correctly, the runes. Them and the druids' magic, I don't think they're too different, or at least not in the way they're worked." W-wait. What did she mean by not too different? Does this mean she'll start growing mushrooms all over her or something? "I don't think that'll happen, or else I'd have started feeling funny already. Right? Right?" Presumably Elthara would've said something about Tui if your dullahan friend was in danger, so probably not. But what was she going to tell you? "There's more to this than meets the eye," Atugia replies, stamping on the dirt again for emphasis. "Let's go take a closer look, yeah? I'm sure we'll find something good. I'll be sure to tell you if I suddenly feel really horny, or something." |"I don't like this place." You look over your shoulder at Quin, who's continuously shifting his weight from one foot to the other. To say that the bunny-man is tense would be a grand understatement — he looks equally divided between legging it forward to meet whatever danger his instincts sense head-on, or legging it away as quickly as his feet will take him. Has he sensed some danger that you're not privy to? "Kinda?" Quin grimaces and thumbs down at the ruins below. "My legs are telling me that I should get out of here, and they're rarely wrong. Now, whether I will get out of here is another matter, given that I know this would be dangerous going in. But what I'm feeling is completely at odds with that. It damn well isn't as peaceful as it looks." You'll take his word for it, then. If he has any more concrete warnings, you'd love to hear them. "Just doing my best. Why don't we head down and take a look, then?" |"Hmm," Viv says, producing her hat and plonking it back on her head as she surveys the scene. "Doesn't appear like much at a first glance. Maybe the druids were really just telling tall tales about themselves, which grew in the telling." She finds it all underwhelming too, huh? Well, it's certainly a possibility. "Of course, we've got to keep open minds, and most of all, perform a thorough investigation — as a point of professional pride, if nothing else. Come now, it'll be an experience, if nothing else." |"That's it?" Agni blinks, shielding her eyes as she peers down the hill at the ruins. "This looks nothing like the Temple of Terrestrial Fire — the mound isn't even a quarter of its size! And this is supposed to be the greatest, grandest temple the elven druids built to the wyld?" It is odd, isn't it? The Temple of Terrestrial Fire is supposed to be a lesser temple, and it's still in relatively good shape after all these years. Xadaron Temple can't have crumbled into just a few heaps of marble bricks in two centuries and a bit, can it? If the fungus was so virulent and destructive, where is it? "I guess those are answers we're going to have to find ourselves. I don't know about you, but I'm actually pretty excited about it all." Well, that would be just like Agni, wouldn't it? All right, then — time to get a closer look at this mess. ] Indeed, your job here is to investigate, and you're not about to leave without doing just that. If nothing else, you'll be able to tell Hethia that either the druids' temples were never very great to begin with, the tale growing in the telling, or that the rate of decay that was affected upon them by this fungus was absolutely incredible. Continuing to lead the way, you draw closer to what's presumably the ruined temple. Close-up, it doesn't look too different from a lupine burial mound — the kind that jarls of ages past would bury themselves in along with all manner of valuables. As overgrown and half-buried as it is, fine marble still sticks out of the mound at various spots, and the way the ground here is much firmer underfoot. Maybe the temple sunk into the earth, and there's more to this than meets the eye? But why would that happen, though? You're already well past the bog, and if Xadaron temple had been passed from one generation of Xadarons to the next, surely the temple sinking into soft ground would've been noticed long before the Godswar. Ah, it was just a thought... At last, the lot of you wind up at the foot of the mound, where Ryn points at a half-crumbled archway leading into its depths. The remnants of a silvered gate lie half-buried in the mud and stone, torn off its hinges from the inside; the tunnel leading further into the mound is lined with stone bricks, covered in all kinds of overgrowth. Once again, you'd have expected something grander from the greatest of the druidic temples... but at least there's more to this than just disappointment. Well, you'll just have to see what lies inside, won't you? "

[etheryn.highConfidence
            |"Let me take a look," Ryn says, stepping up to the inscriptions. [pc.dcb
                |It's a little presumptuous for a cocksleeve to just push past you like that, but since she's being useful you'll let it slide this once.
                |You nod, and step aside to give her space to work.
                |Well, like, since she's sooo much better at this wordy stuff than you are, there's no reason for you to get in her way!
            ] "Hmm..."
            |"M-mind if I take a look?" Ryn says. "I might be able to figure something o-out."
            
            [pc.dcb
                |Well, it's nice that she's willing to prove herself useful for being more than a cocksleeve. Sure, go ahead.
                |You nod, and step aside to give her space to work. For her to take the initiative like this, you're guessing that Ryn has some interest of her own in this stuff.
                |Well, like, since she's sooo much better at this wordy stuff than you are, there's no reason for you to get in her way! Is this, like, totally important to her that she spoke up?
            ]
            
            Ryn steps up to the inscriptions and brushes off some stray plant matter. "Hmm..."
        ]
        
        [pc.isDK
            |Elthara gives you a wink from the side. "Humor her, won't you? As a favor to me, if nothing else."
            
            Oh, you already have. 
        ]Well, what does it say?
        
        Ryn suddenly blanches, and swallows hard. "It's a formal declaration of a grudge. Well, as formal as these things get."
        
        [pc.isDK
            |Really, now
            |Oh
        ]. Judging by her reaction, it's against her family, isn't it?
        
        "It's a grudge against my grandmother by the archdruid himself. The druids... they hated her for changing the faith of the boer'alvar to that of Lumia, for accepting any of the southern gods, and they hated her for what she did to her harem. They wanted future generations of boreal elves to know that she'd committed sacrilege in their eyes. Only... knowing what histories of the Godswar we have, the place must've fallen into ruin not long after this grudge was declared; I may be the first boer'alvar to see it in a long time. I knew they hated my grandmother... but after what happened in the crypt, I thought... I thought the worst of it was over."
        
        "Oh, you poor dear," Elthara sighs, gathering Ryn up into a hug. "I'm so sorry."
        
        [pc.isDK
            |Look, you get that it's upsetting, but for Ryn to come to a place like this, she can't have expected to have had a warm welcome
            |You were there, Elthara was there too. Now, once again, the both of you are here for her
        ]. By the sounds of it, a grudge sounds like a pretty serious affair; good thing that no one's bothering to uphold it in full these days, then.
        
        Ryn shakes her head and squirms out of Elthara's embrace. "The past is the past, what's done is done. Let's get to fixing what's ahead of us."

rows.original: Curious about what lies on the other side of the windows, you step up and attempt to peer through them brushing away some withered tendrils from the bars. The first change you notice isn't with your eyes, but your nose: the air that wafts in from the other end isn't merely stale, but positively musty. Part earthy, part rotten, the redolent stench assaults your nose and makes your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] crawl and feel tacky, like someone smeared something vile and sticky on it. "A-achoo!" Standing behind you, Ryn sneezes mightily, and gratefully accepts [party.randComp cait kiyoko viviane |Cait's |Kiyoko's |Viviane's |Elthara's ] offer of a handkerchief. "Sorry, something in the air. I hope we don't get more of this." "It's more than just dust," [party.has viviane |Viviane |Elthara ] muses. "I'm sure of it." Well, that much's obvious. Ignoring the byplay, you focus your eyes into the room beyond — what's lit up by the faint blue glow is eerie enough. An arboretum of sorts, it would appear, or at least, it used to be: fungal columns grow out of the lifeless husks of evergreen trees, reaching up all the way to the ceiling. Not too different from the small pinhead filaments and bracket fungi you saw earlier on in the corridor, perhaps, but merely on a matter of scale; the numerous tiny spore-creatures have amalgamated themselves into enormous living masses. There's one thing that stands out amidst the fungal overgrowth: a single massive tree that still, against all odds still stands in the midst of it all despite the fungus that infests its bark and branches. Sickly, twisted and its leaves sharp and jagged, to say that it looks unhealthy would be an understatement of the highest degree. Hmm. Taking hold of the stone bars, you give each one a firm tug, perhaps hoping that time will have loosened them enough to be pried or broken out of their holdings. [pc.strengthRange 75 |Despite your considerable strength, the stone is as solid as it seems, refusing to budge or break despite your best efforts |After a few fruitless attempts, you've no choice but to conclude that you're not getting in through the window, wide as it may be ]. [party.randComp brint brienne arona |"Why don't you let me have a go?" Brint asks. Sure, if he thinks he can pry the bars loose. You step aside and watch as your minotaur companion braces himself, puts his hefty ham-hands on the bars and pulls. Brint's muscles flex and strain, but the ancient druidic stonework holds fast. Not even a little give? Brint exhales deeply, and shakes his head. "Not even a little. We'll have to find a way around." |"Why don't you let me have a go?" Brienne asks. Sure, if she thinks she can pry the bars loose. You step aside and watch as your cowgirl companion braces herself, puts her hefty ham-hands on the bars and pulls. Brienne's muscles flex and strain, but the ancient druidic stonework holds fast. Not even a little give? Brienne exhales deeply, and shakes her head. "I'm sorry, [pc.name]. We'll have to find a way around." |"Step aside," Arona says with a chuckle. "I'll have this apart in no time at all." Sure, she can go knock herself out. You step aside and watch as your orcish companion flexes and grandstands a bit while limbering up, then braces herself and takes a firm grip on the bars. Arona's muscles flex and strain as she pulls, her expression steadily growing more strained as her exertion starts to show itself; eventually, she changes tack to hammering on the bars with her fists, then eventually resorts to pulling out her [arona.weapon] and aiming it straight at the bars. "All right, you fucker," she growls. "Time to show you who's boss." "W-wait!" Ryn begins, but it's already too late. The heavy crunch of Arona's [arona.weapon] upon stone rings in the ancient chamber, dust and dead plant matter raining down from the ceiling. She nearly loses her grip on its handle from the impact, fumbling clumsily as she staggers back, but there's nary a mark on the vine-wrapped stone bars. "Fucking sorcery," Arona mutters. "I fucking hate tree-hugger sorcery. Let's see if there's another way deeper into this place, [pc.name]." |"I don't think that's going to work," Ryn says. "Old as they are, the bars look solid and just pulling on them isn't going to pry them loose. Maybe we should try to find a way around?" ] That's probably your best bet. You spotted some other entrances on the far side of the overgrown arboretum — maybe you can see if there's a way to circle around and enter from the other end. "That's probably our best bet," Ryn agrees. "If we can't even pry the bars loose, clearing out the archway isn't an option; the roots and fungus and everything has just turned the rubble into one huge mess. Let's search the rest of this room and see if we can't find another way further into the temple."
rows.translation: 你对窗户另一边究竟有什么感到好奇，于是走上前试图透过窗户看去，同时拨开了栏杆上一些枯萎的藤蔓。你首先注意到的变化并不是视觉上的，而是嗅觉上的：从另一边吹进来的空气不仅闷热，而且散发着浓重的霉味——那种气味中既有泥土的气息，也有腐烂物的味道，这种刺鼻的气味令你的鼻子感到无比不适。 [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] 爬起来后，你会感觉身上黏糊糊的，就好像有人在你身上涂了什么又恶心又黏的东西。 “啊嚏！”站在你身后的瑞恩猛地打了个喷嚏，然后感激地接受了这个结果。 [party.randComp cait kiyoko viviane |凯特的 |清子的 |薇薇安的 |埃尔萨拉的 ] 递上一块手部帕。‘对不起，空气中有些东西……希望不会再发生这种事了。’” “这可不仅仅是灰尘而已 [party.has viviane |薇薇安 |埃尔萨拉 ] 她沉思着：“我确信这一点。” 嗯，这一点确实很明显。先不管那些旁枝末节，你把目光投向房间那头——被那种微弱的蓝光照亮的景象，已经足够令人毛骨悚然了。看起来那地方就像是一个植物园，至少是类似这样的地方 已使用 这些真菌菌柱是从常绿树木枯死的树壳中生长出来的，它们一直延伸到天花板的高度。与你在走廊里看到的那些细小的菌丝和层孔菌相比，或许并没有太大区别，只不过规模上有所不同而已；这些数以亿计的微小孢子生物共同聚集在一起，形成了巨大的生命体。 在那些茂盛的真菌丛中，有那么一棵树格外引人注目：尽管树皮和树枝上布满了真菌，但它依然顽强地矗立在那里，仿佛与一切困难抗争到底。这棵树显得病态而扭曲，树叶也变得尖锐而参差不齐。说它看起来不健康，简直都是轻描淡写的说法。 嗯，你握住那些石条，用力拉了拉每一根，或许希望时间已经让它们变得足够松动，从而可以将其撬开或弄断。 [pc.strengthRange 75 |尽管你拥有强大的力量，但这块石头依然坚如磐石，无论你如何用力尝试，它都不会移动或破裂。 |经过几次失败的尝试后，你不得不承认：尽管那扇窗户很宽敞，但你就是无法从那里进去。 ]. [party.randComp brint brienne arona |为什么不让我试试呢？”布林特问道。 “当然可以，只要他认为自己能够把那些铁条弄开的话。”你退到一边，看着你的弥诺陶洛斯伙伴做好准备，把他那双粗壮的手放在铁条上 拉动布林特的肌肉在用力收缩，但那些古老的德鲁伊石雕却纹丝不动。 连一点点松动都没有？ 布林特深深地吸了口气，然后摇了摇头：“一点都没有。我们得想办法另寻他法。 |为什么不让我试试呢？”布蕾妮问道。 “当然可以，只要她觉得自己能把那些铁条弄开的话……”你退到一边，看着你的这位女牛仔伙伴做好准备，把她那双粗壮的手放在铁条上 拉动布蕾妮的肌肉不断用力收缩，但那些古老的德鲁伊石雕却纹丝不动。 连一点点松动都没有？ 布蕾妮深吸一口气，然后摇了摇头。“对不起 [pc.name]我们得想办法解决这个问题。 |让开吧，”阿罗娜笑着说道，“我很快就能解决这个问题的。” 好吧，让她去尝试吧。你只要站在一旁，看着你的兽人伙伴活动一下四肢、展示一下自己的力量，然后做好准备，紧紧抓住那些栏杆就行了。 阿罗娜在用力拉扯时，肌肉不断收缩、绷紧，她的表情也逐渐变得愈发紧张，因为体力消耗已经开始显现出来；最终，她改变了方法，开始用拳头敲打铁栅栏，而后来干脆直接拔出了 [arona.weapon] 并将其直接对准了那些栏杆。 “好吧，你这个混蛋，”她低吼道，“是时候让你知道谁才是老大了。” “等、等等！”瑞恩试图阻止，但已经太晚了。阿罗娜那重型的拳头已经 [arona.weapon] 在那个古老的房间里，石环上积满了灰尘和枯萎的植物残渣，这些物质仿佛从天花板上不断掉落下来。她被这些物质击中，差点抓不住环的把手部，慌乱中踉跄着后退，但那些被藤蔓缠绕的石条上却丝毫没有留下任何痕迹。 “该死的魔法，”阿罗娜低声咒骂道，“我他妈讨厌这种与树木有关的魔法……看看这个地方里面是否还有其他的出路吧。 [pc.name]." |我觉得那样行不通，”莱恩说，“那些栏杆虽然老旧，但看起来非常结实，直接拉它们是根本不可能把它们弄开的。也许我们应该想办法另寻他法？ ] 那大概是我们最好的办法了。”瑞恩同意道，“如果我们连铁栅栏都弄不开，那就根本不可能清理那道拱门了——那些树根、真菌之类的东西把废墟弄得一团糟，根本无法通行。我们还是再搜搜这个房间，看看能不能找到进入神庙的别的办法。
rows.raw: " Curious about what lies on the other side of the windows, you step up and attempt to peer through them brushing away some withered tendrils from the bars. The first change you notice isn't with your eyes, but your nose: the air that wafts in from the other end isn't merely stale, but positively musty. Part earthy, part rotten, the redolent stench assaults your nose and makes your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun] crawl and feel tacky, like someone smeared something vile and sticky on it. "A-achoo!" Standing behind you, Ryn sneezes mightily, and gratefully accepts [party.randComp cait kiyoko viviane |Cait's |Kiyoko's |Viviane's |Elthara's ] offer of a handkerchief. "Sorry, something in the air. I hope we don't get more of this." "It's more than just dust," [party.has viviane |Viviane |Elthara ] muses. "I'm sure of it." Well, that much's obvious. Ignoring the byplay, you focus your eyes into the room beyond — what's lit up by the faint blue glow is eerie enough. An arboretum of sorts, it would appear, or at least, it used to be: fungal columns grow out of the lifeless husks of evergreen trees, reaching up all the way to the ceiling. Not too different from the small pinhead filaments and bracket fungi you saw earlier on in the corridor, perhaps, but merely on a matter of scale; the numerous tiny spore-creatures have amalgamated themselves into enormous living masses. There's one thing that stands out amidst the fungal overgrowth: a single massive tree that still, against all odds still stands in the midst of it all despite the fungus that infests its bark and branches. Sickly, twisted and its leaves sharp and jagged, to say that it looks unhealthy would be an understatement of the highest degree. Hmm. Taking hold of the stone bars, you give each one a firm tug, perhaps hoping that time will have loosened them enough to be pried or broken out of their holdings. [pc.strengthRange 75 |Despite your considerable strength, the stone is as solid as it seems, refusing to budge or break despite your best efforts |After a few fruitless attempts, you've no choice but to conclude that you're not getting in through the window, wide as it may be ]. [party.randComp brint brienne arona |"Why don't you let me have a go?" Brint asks. Sure, if he thinks he can pry the bars loose. You step aside and watch as your minotaur companion braces himself, puts his hefty ham-hands on the bars and pulls. Brint's muscles flex and strain, but the ancient druidic stonework holds fast. Not even a little give? Brint exhales deeply, and shakes his head. "Not even a little. We'll have to find a way around." |"Why don't you let me have a go?" Brienne asks. Sure, if she thinks she can pry the bars loose. You step aside and watch as your cowgirl companion braces herself, puts her hefty ham-hands on the bars and pulls. Brienne's muscles flex and strain, but the ancient druidic stonework holds fast. Not even a little give? Brienne exhales deeply, and shakes her head. "I'm sorry, [pc.name]. We'll have to find a way around." |"Step aside," Arona says with a chuckle. "I'll have this apart in no time at all." Sure, she can go knock herself out. You step aside and watch as your orcish companion flexes and grandstands a bit while limbering up, then braces herself and takes a firm grip on the bars. Arona's muscles flex and strain as she pulls, her expression steadily growing more strained as her exertion starts to show itself; eventually, she changes tack to hammering on the bars with her fists, then eventually resorts to pulling out her [arona.weapon] and aiming it straight at the bars. "All right, you fucker," she growls. "Time to show you who's boss." "W-wait!" Ryn begins, but it's already too late. The heavy crunch of Arona's [arona.weapon] upon stone rings in the ancient chamber, dust and dead plant matter raining down from the ceiling. She nearly loses her grip on its handle from the impact, fumbling clumsily as she staggers back, but there's nary a mark on the vine-wrapped stone bars. "Fucking sorcery," Arona mutters. "I fucking hate tree-hugger sorcery. Let's see if there's another way deeper into this place, [pc.name]." |"I don't think that's going to work," Ryn says. "Old as they are, the bars look solid and just pulling on them isn't going to pry them loose. Maybe we should try to find a way around?" ] That's probably your best bet. You spotted some other entrances on the far side of the overgrown arboretum — maybe you can see if there's a way to circle around and enter from the other end. "That's probably our best bet," Ryn agrees. "If we can't even pry the bars loose, clearing out the archway isn't an option; the roots and fungus and everything has just turned the rubble into one huge mess. Let's search the rest of this room and see if we can't find another way further into the temple." "

rows.raw: "Investigate the barred windows — what's on the other side?"

rows.original:
As you pass amidst the elven remains on the ground and atop their recliners, a sense of unease comes over you. You reach for your [pc.weapon], half-expecting the skeletons themselves to rise, or perhaps for vengeful spirits to materialize, but nothing happens just yet, merely a sense of foreboding. The cold blue aura only intensifies with each step you take, the masonry itself radiating a chill that makes your skin pucker and spine crawl.
            
            [party.has arona
                |Arona takes one look at her surroundings and stomps on a brittle skull, crushing it underfoot with a scowl on her face. "Fucking ghosts. I hate ghosts."
                
                She's sure it's ghosts?
                
                "What else could it be? Good thing we've got this big-titted elves priestess with us, eh?[flags.ARONA_TOTEM
                    | That, and these sweet duds that your witch friend cooked up for me. 
                ]I'm feeling more confident already."
            ]
            
            Conjuring a ball of light in her hand, Elthara sweeps it about the chamber, casting its radiance upon the scene as if to burn away the musty scent of mold and rot. "Oh my."
            
            The fungus devoured them, it looks like.
            
            "No wonder Hethia didn't even want to get close," Ryn says, caught between instinctive revulsion and the desire to investigate this piece of history further, sordid as it is. "I-"
            
            What's the matter?
            
            Ryn's stopped and tensed up, [ryn.lowConfidence
                |looking just about fit to run. If not for you and Elthara by her side, she probably would have
                |hunching her shoulders and thinning her lips
            ]. At last, she points into the gloom ahead.
            
            "Up ahead. You can't feel it?"
            
            Feel what, exactly? The place is most certainly unpleasant, and you're on your toes expecting the vengeful dead to rise from these mouldered bones any moment now. Is that it?
            
            Elthara wrinkles her nose. "As far as I'm concerned, there's nothing that couldn't be attributed to the mold and stale air. Oh, I don't doubt that you feel what you do for a reason, but the goddess protects, my dears."
            
            "I... something's there, in the darkness ahead. As impossible as it sounds, it recognizes me, [pc.name]. I don't know how I know this all of a sudden — it doesn't make any sense. But this thing's there and it hates me... and I've only ever felt such intense emotion like that from Alissa when she was blaming me for both Father and Mother's death."
            
            ...Ah. Now it's starting to make sense. Sounds like an exorcism's in order, once you're prepared.
            
            Are you?
rows.translation:
当你走过地上以及那些精灵座椅上残留的骸骨时，一种不安的感觉开始笼罩着你。你伸手去拿 [pc.weapon]半期待着那些骷髅会从地下爬出来，或者期待着那些复仇的灵魂会显现出来，但此刻什么也没有发生，只有一种不祥的预感。每当你迈出一步，那冰冷的蓝色轻型环就会变得更加浓烈，那些石砌的墙壁本身也在散发着令人不寒而栗的寒意，让你的皮肤紧缩，脊背发麻。
            
            [party.has arona
                |阿罗娜环顾四周，一脚踩在了一个脆弱的头骨上，面带怒容地将它踩得粉碎。“该死的鬼魂……我讨厌鬼魂。”

她真的确定那是鬼魂吗？

“还能是什么别的东西呢？幸好我们还有这位胸部丰满的精灵女祭司在身边，对吧？[flags.ARONA_TOTEM
                    | 还有你那位女巫朋友为我准备的这些美味佳肴。 
                ]我现在已经感觉更有信心了。
            ]
            
            艾尔塔拉手中凝聚出一团轻型球，在房间里四处挥动，让它的轻型芒洒满整个空间，仿佛想要驱散那些霉味与腐朽的气息。“哦，我的天啊……”

看来，那些真菌已经把它们吞没了。
            
            难怪赫希娅甚至都不想靠近它，”莱恩说道，他内心既感到本能的厌恶，又渴望进一步探究这段历史——尽管它如此肮脏不堪。“我——”

怎么了？
            
            瑞恩停下了脚步，全身变得紧张起来。 [ryn.lowConfidence
                |看起来她已经差不多可以跑步了。要不是有你和艾尔塔拉在她身边，她可能早就能够跑步了。
                |她耸了耸肩膀，嘴唇也紧抿了起来。
            ]终于，她指向前方那片黑暗。

“就在前面。你感觉不到吗？”

感觉不到什么？这个地方显然非常阴森恐怖，你随时都可能预料到那些复仇的死者会从这些发霉的骨头中重新站起来。 就我而言，所有这些现象都应该归咎于霉菌和污浊的空气吧。哦，我并不怀疑你们的感受一定有其原因，但亲爱的们，女神在保护着你们呢。”埃尔萨拉皱了皱鼻子说道。我……前方黑暗中有什么东西。虽然听起来不可思议，但它竟然认出了我。 [pc.name]我也不知道自己怎么突然就知道了这些——这根本没有任何道理。但这种感觉确实存在，而且它似乎在恨我……我以前只有一次感受到过如此强烈的情绪，那就是当艾莉莎把父母的双亡都归咎于我的时候。

……啊，现在看来，这一切似乎都有了合理的解释。听起来，如果你准备好的话，是时候进行一次“驱魔”了。

你准备好了吗？
