rows.original: Heeding Ryn's warning about the malevolence up ahead, you tread warily into the darkness, [party.compNames] close behind you; Elthara's conjured light does its best to ward off the pervasive gloom, but it presses in all the same, trying to crush your little group in its smothering presence. Hmph, malevolence indeed... The scene that lies before you is that which you just passed by in the waiting antechamber, only twice, thrice more disturbing: elven bodies lie all around you, flesh long gone and bones crumbling to shards. Fungus sprouts all over these remains — the selfsame spongy, scabby mix with pustulent blisters and fin-like protrusions growing out of it at intervals. There's not a single body that doesn't have mold creeping upon it, and their bodies are contorted as if in great pain... or some other overwhelming surge of emotion. They lie on the floor, on the stone benches and against the walls, lost to the rot. Each one is as quiet as death, a silent reminder of your mortality and your potential fate should you slip up on any one of your adventures... [party.randComp brint brienne arona quintillus atugia azyrran |"Khaak. This feels wrong," Brint says, the high ceiling in the hallway allowing the beefy minotaur to walk at his full height unimpeded. "It looks like a big battle took place... and only one side put up any kind of fight. I don't like this one bit." |"Khaak. This feels wrong," Brienne says, the thigh ceiling in the hallway allowing the beefy cowgirl to walk at her full height unimpeded. "It looks like a big battle took place... and only one side put up any kind of fight. I don't like this one bit." |"So many bodies," Arona growls, readying her [arona.weapon]. "There'll be ghosts, I tell you, there can't not be. Get ready!" |Quintillus sniffs in disdain as he surveys the bodies and the pestilent mold growing on the old bones. "Foul. Might have been something Tollus himself came up with, were he around then. It's certainly similar to ideas he's had and merely didn't have the strength to put into action back then. Now... who can say?" |"This is the work of Wraiths, or at least those who followed them," Atugia mumbles as she surveys the dead. "They always liked their victims to die in great pain... or great arousal. They craved emotion...fed upon it." You don't ask how she knows. |"I heard of this happening to other hives sometimes. Fungal infections that spoiled honey and ate away at wax, caused walls to fall..." Azyrran shakes her head slowly. "Such diseases are harder on ant-people — I forget their proper name — but it affecting people other than insect-folk is a first for me." It doesn't. Or at least, usually doesn't... you think. Right now, you're reconsidering your stance, even if Hethia says that you and your companions should be impervious to a weapon that was very specifically keyed to destroy a singular subset of people. ] As you step over the bodies and press on, you come to a fork in the path, dominated by a fountain that takes up most of the junction. rows.translation: 听从了Ryn关于前方危险势力的警告，你小心翼翼地踏入了黑暗之中。 [party.compNames] 紧随在你身后；埃尔萨拉召唤出的轻型芒竭力驱散那弥漫的黑暗，但它依然不断逼近，试图用那令人窒息的力量压垮你们这个小团队。 哼，真是充满恶意…… 你眼前呈现的景象，正是你刚才在等候厅里两次、三次经过过的场景，只不过这次更加令人毛骨悚然：精灵们的尸体遍布四周，他们的肉体早已腐烂，骨头也碎成了碎片。这些残骸上长满了真菌——那种海绵状、结痂状的物质，上面还时不时长出脓疱和类似鳍状的突起。 没有一具尸体是没有霉菌爬满它的，它们的身体扭曲着，仿佛正在承受巨大的痛苦……又或是被某种强烈的情绪所支配。 它们躺在地上，躺在石凳上，靠在墙壁上，早已被腐烂侵蚀得面目全非。 每一个都静得如同死一般，无声地提醒着你自己的渺小与脆弱，同时也警示着你：如果在任何一次冒险中稍有不慎，你将会面临怎样的命运…… [party.randComp brint brienne arona quintillus atugia azyrran |哈克，这种感觉不太对劲，”布林特说道。走廊里高高的天花板让这个魁梧的弥诺陶洛斯能够完全伸直身体行走，毫无阻碍。“看起来这里曾经发生过一场大规模的战斗……但似乎只有一方进行了抵抗。我实在不喜欢这种情况。 |哈克，这种感觉不太对劲，”布蕾妮说道。走廊里的天花板高度足够高，让这个身材高大的女牛仔能够毫无障碍地挺直身子行走。“看起来这里发生过一场大规模的战斗……但似乎只有一方进行了抵抗。我一点也不喜欢这种情况。 |这么多尸体……”阿罗娜低吼着，同时做好了行动的准备。 [arona.weapon]我告诉你，那里肯定会有鬼的。 不能 不行，马上准备！ |昆蒂勒斯不屑地哼了一声，看着那些尸体以及那些在古老骨骼上滋生的恶臭霉菌。“真恶心。要是托卢斯当时还在的话，说不定就是他想出来的这些办法。这些想法肯定和他以前想过的有些相似，只是当时他没有力量将它们付诸实践罢了。现在……谁又说得准呢？ |这是幽灵们的所作所为，至少是那些追随他们的人干的，”阿图吉娅在观察那些死者时低声说道，“他们总是喜欢让受害者在极大的痛苦中死去……或者处于极度兴奋的状态中。他们渴望情感……并以情感为食。” 你自然不会去问她是怎么知道的。 |我听说过这种事情有时也会发生在其他蜂群身上。真菌感染会破坏蜂蜜，侵蚀蜂蜡，导致蜂巢的墙壁倒塌……”阿兹兰缓缓摇了摇头，“这种疾病对那些‘蚁人’来说更加致命——我忘了他们的正式名称——但这种病会影响到非昆虫种族的人，这还是我第一次见到。并非如此。至少，通常情况下并不是这样……你认为是吧？现在，你正在重新考虑自己的立场，即使赫希娅说过，你和你的同伴应该对这种专门设计用来消灭特定人群的武器免疫。 ] 当你跨过那些尸体继续前行时，会来到一条岔路前，路中央有一个喷泉，几乎占据了整个路口。或许是出于一种病态的好奇心，瑞恩向前走了几步，俯身看向喷泉的水池，然后猛地咽了口唾沫。 里面堆满了骨头，还有一些腐烂的植物残渣，而这些地方还覆盖着厚厚的、那种海绵状、结痂状的真菌。看到这一幕以及闻到那股难闻的气味，瑞恩赶紧捂住了嘴——虽然所有的肉早就腐烂掉了，但霉菌散发出的恶臭依然令人难以忍受，于是她转过身去。 哦不……” 喷泉的深处有一具骷髅，身上佩戴着金银制成的精美饰品，头戴的帽子似乎是由石化木材制成的——在昏暗的轻型线下，实在很难分辨清楚。 那些橙色的霉菌和针头大小的真菌根本无法侵蚀这种金属，也无法使黄金生锈。由此可见，这位逝者的地位一定相当显赫。至少，可以这么说 思考 从骨骼结构来看，这是一名男性——他侧躺着，显然是在那个喷泉里被这种病毒夺去了生命。他是试图躲藏吗？还是掉进去后无法脱身了？谁知道呢？ “看起来这里是一条死路 [pc.name]这样吧，”瑞恩说道，与此同时，艾尔塔拉将她召唤出的轻型芒四处照射，试图搜寻那段被毁坏的走廊。“两个岔路口都被碎石堵住了。或许我们应该仔细检查那些墙壁，看看是否还有我们遗漏的、已经坍塌的通道……

rows.original: Her words are cut short by a gust of frigid wind, strong enough to buffet you all and send Ryn's cloak billowing. Clearly unnatural this far beneath the earth, it has you with your [pc.weapon] out and at the ready as Elthara's conjured light reveals a specter that wasn't there a moment ago. In life, he would've been a tall boreal elf, perhaps seven feet if he were standing at full height; his white linen shift rests loosely upon him in tatters, gold and silver adorning his wrists and ankles while a crown of leaves and twigs rests upon his brow, complete with carved wooden antlers. But there's little of him that remains pale to merit the name of pale elf. Clods of orange fungus infest the specter's skin like scabs from multiple wounds, spreading threads upon what parts of his body remain uncovered. The seething mass bursts with vileness and has claimed much of his twisted body; upon forcing yourself to gaze upon the specter directly, you realize that it's more than that. The druid's body is misshapen, giving the impression of so much flesh caught between forms; rampant growth unable to decide between the traditionally robust masculine or feminine figures of the boreal elves, or even the slighter figures of the half-sexed, resulting in something caught between all three. Then, of course, there's the massive, oversized dick that hangs between his legs and tents his tattered shift, and beneath that and a pair of oversized testicles, just a glimpse of a fat, gushing pussy that constantly dribbles pustulent fluids of arousal between his thighs. [etheryn.highConfidence |Ryn's eyes widen for a moment, and then her gaze hardens and she squares her shoulders. Still, she backs away warily from the revenant, holding up her hands with palms turned out. "We mean you no harm, whoever you are. Can you speak?" A terrible, hacking cough sounds from the druidic specter, spores spewing from his lips with each pained wheeze. "Pilgrims? You should not be here! Hurry, flee, flee before — " something snaps behind the spirit's gaze, a moment of cold, bitter realization before he refocuses his empty eyes on Ryn. "Synneva? No, it can't be. Synneva's... dead." "I'm not Synneva," Ryn says, continuing to back away from the ghostly druid's advance. "She rests peacefully now." "Peace? No. There was no peace for her up till the moment of her death. We know... we know what happens to those who are locked up in that... that place." The specter shudders, be it in agony of the body or the pain of remembrance. "If you can't be Synneva, then... that blood. That... that presence...!" It's not quite the banshee wail that you remember Synneva was capable of from below the palace of ice, but this is far more primal. Seeing things take a turn for the worse, Ryn raises her hands to make one final plea to the apparition, but he's already upon her. Ghostly, bark-encased fists dripping with corruptive fungus reach for Ryn's throat as the wight who can only be Archdruid Vaeril Xadaron seeks to throttle her out of existence. "You dare come here, Atheldred?" the druidic haunt roars, his voice howling over with the rage and sorrow of a winter storm. "You dare come here after what you did to Synneva! What you did to us all!" This is insane. Ryn's resemblance to her grandmother isn't that obvious... well, on the other hand, it's clear that the archdruid's specter is relying on senses other than mere sight and touch alone. As you rush to help her, Etheryn has already drawn her bow and nocked an arrow, aiming straight for the druid's scabbed-over chest. The icy arrow whistles along its path, entering Vaeril from the front and leaving through the back in a wet splotch of stinking ectoplasm. As the archdruid moves to close his bark-encrusted fists about Ryn's throat, you run him through with your [pc.weapon] — an act that takes a chunk of ectoplasm out of the haunt and leaves speckles of frost on your weapon. While it doesn't seem to have damaged him terribly much, it's enough of a distraction for Ryn to disengage and nock another arrow. "Looks like talking isn't going to calm him down, and I don't think beating him down inasmuch as you can do that to a ghost will, either." "Time for a quick exorcism, then." Elthara backs you up with a brilliant bolt of whitefire that strikes the archdruid's flank, and the twisted specter lets out another bloodcurdling scream; he raises his bark-encrusted arms to shield himself, staggering back under the impact while Elthara moves to interpose herself between Ryn and the archdruid. "Step back, [etheryn.crowned |my queen |lady regent ]!" Etheryn is already moving, taking aim while [var0 |Elthara, [comp2.name] |Elthara ] and you defend her from Vaeril's clawing, dripping grasp. |Ryn claps her hands over her mouth to stifle the gasp she knows is coming, but that doesn't matter to the wight, who has noticed her. As you rush to help her, Etheryn valiantly pulls at the fingers clawing at her throat, her eyes wide in terror and teeth gritted in desperation. Etheryn is already moving, scrambling to her feet with [etheryn.weapon] in one hand, forcing her fear down and dodging out of the way as the ghost lunges for her throat again. ] "This is your fault! Your fault! You and your human goddess created this... this thing to wipe us out, us who would not bend the knee! Did you come to see us die? Is that — " The sting of failure, the resentment over seeing one martyred, the hatred directed at a tyrant — and of course, the bodily agony of Vaeril's dying moments as the fungal infestation consumed the druids and twisted their bodies with uncontrolled, cancerous growth. All this and more form the pain and rage that animates this haunt, the tip of a spear aimed at the heart of the var Ridell line. "Treachery! Murder! I always knew that getting too intimate with those Belharans would be our undoing, Atheldred var Ridell. Now you've begun worshipping their gods as well, and bring one of their priestesses here? Treachery by the queen against her own people and the Old Wyld! I... I may have failed, but I was never traitorous!" Having composed herself, Ryn nocks an arrow and aims it at the misshapen, hermaphroditic specter charging for her. "Oh, grandmother... please let this be the last piece you've left for me to pick up." It's a fight!
rows.translation: 她的话语被一阵刺骨的寒风打断了——那股风力之大，足以让所有人都感到不适，也让瑞恩的斗篷剧烈地飘动起来。在地下这么深的地方，这样的自然现象显然很不寻常 [pc.weapon] 就在这时，埃尔萨拉召唤出的轻型芒揭示出了一个方才还不存在的幽灵。在现实生活中，他应该会是一个高大的极北精灵——如果他完全站直的话，身高或许会有七英尺；他穿着一件破烂的白色亚麻长袍，手部腕和足部踝上佩戴着金银饰品，额头上还戴着一顶由树叶和细枝编成的冠冕，上面甚至还有雕刻好的木制鹿角。 但是，他身上几乎没有任何地方还能被称为“苍白精灵”了。橙色的真菌团块像多处伤口结成的痂一样覆盖在他的皮肤上，那些未被遮盖的身体部位上也布满了这些菌丝。这些充满恶意的菌团已经侵蚀了他那扭曲的身体的大部分；当你强迫自己直视这个幽灵时，你会发现，实际情况比这还要糟糕。 这位德鲁伊的身体形态很不规则，看起来仿佛有大量的肉体被强行塞进了不同的身体结构中；这种异常的生长使得他的身体既无法呈现出极北精灵传统上那种强壮的男性化或女性化特征，也无法形成半性别的那种更为纤细的身形，最终形成了介于三者之间的某种奇怪形态。 当然，还有那根巨大得离谱的阴茎，它悬挂在他的两腿之间，将他那破烂的内裤撑得变形；而在它的下方，是一对巨大的睾丸……偶尔还能隐约看到那片肥厚的阴部，那里不断有脓状的液体渗出，这些液体代表着他的性兴奋状态。 [etheryn.highConfidence |瑞恩的眼睛瞬间睁得大大的，但很快她的目光就变得坚定起来，双肩也挺得笔直。尽管如此，她还是小心翼翼地后退着，远离那个亡魂，同时将双手举起来，手掌朝外。 “无论你是谁，我们都没有恶意。 你能说话吗？” 那个德鲁伊幽灵发出了一声可怕的、剧烈的咳嗽，每次痛苦地喘息时，都有孢子从他的嘴唇中喷出。 “朝圣者们？你们不应该在这里！快逃吧，赶紧离开这里……”就在幽灵说话的瞬间，背后发生了什么，他瞬间意识到了什么，随后又将那空洞的目光重新投向了瑞恩。 辛内瓦？不，不可能。辛内瓦的…… 死亡我不是辛内瓦，”瑞恩边说边继续后退，躲避着那个幽灵般的女德鲁伊的逼近。“她现在已经安息了。” “安息？不。在她死去的那一刻之前，她从未得到过安宁。我们知道……我们知道那些被关在那个……那个地方的人会遭遇什么。 地点那个幽灵在颤抖，无论是身体上的痛苦，还是回忆带来的伤痛。‘如果你无法成为辛内瓦，那么……那鲜血……那个 存在感……！” 这声音虽然远没有你记忆中辛内瓦在冰宫下发出的那种凄厉哀嚎，但却更加原始、更加令人毛骨悚然。看到局势正在恶化，瑞恩举起双手，向这个幽灵发出最后的恳求——但那个怪物已经扑到了她身上。 那些被腐朽真菌覆盖的、仿佛由骨爪构成的拳头，如幽灵般伸向瑞恩的喉咙——这个只能被认定为大德鲁伊瓦瑞尔·萨达伦的怪物，正试图将她扼杀在空气中。 “你竟敢来到这里，阿瑟德雷德？那片德鲁伊的领地中回荡着怒吼声，他的声音中充满了冬季风暴般的愤怒与悲伤。“你 敢 在你对辛内瓦做了那些事之后，你还敢来到这里！你对我们所有人都做出了伤害！” 这太荒谬了。瑞恩和她祖母长得太像了，这简直 那个 rows.raw: " Her words are cut short by a gust of frigid wind, strong enough to buffet you all and send Ryn's cloak billowing. Clearly unnatural this far beneath the earth, it has you with your [pc.weapon] out and at the ready as Elthara's conjured light reveals a specter that wasn't there a moment ago. In life, he would've been a tall boreal elf, perhaps seven feet if he were standing at full height; his white linen shift rests loosely upon him in tatters, gold and silver adorning his wrists and ankles while a crown of leaves and twigs rests upon his brow, complete with carved wooden antlers. But there's little of him that remains pale to merit the name of pale elf. Clods of orange fungus infest the specter's skin like scabs from multiple wounds, spreading threads upon what parts of his body remain uncovered. The seething mass bursts with vileness and has claimed much of his twisted body; upon forcing yourself to gaze upon the specter directly, you realize that it's more than that. The druid's body is misshapen, giving the impression of so much flesh caught between forms; rampant growth unable to decide between the traditionally robust masculine or feminine figures of the boreal elves, or even the slighter figures of the half-sexed, resulting in something caught between all three. Then, of course, there's the massive, oversized dick that hangs between his legs and tents his tattered shift, and beneath that and a pair of oversized testicles, just a glimpse of a fat, gushing pussy that constantly dribbles pustulent fluids of arousal between his thighs. Still, she backs away warily from the revenant, holding up her hands with palms turned out. "We mean you no harm, whoever you are. Can you speak?" A terrible, hacking cough sounds from the druidic specter, spores spewing from his lips with each pained wheeze. "Pilgrims? You should not be here! Hurry, flee, flee before — " something snaps behind the spirit's gaze, a moment of cold, bitter realization before he refocuses his empty eyes on Ryn. "Synneva? No, it can't be. Synneva's... dead." "I'm not Synneva," Ryn says, continuing to back away from the ghostly druid's advance. "She rests peacefully now." "Peace? No. There was no peace for her up till the moment of her death. We know... we know what happens to those who are locked up in that... that place." The specter shudders, be it in agony of the body or the pain of remembrance. "If you can't be Synneva, then... that blood. That... that presence...!" It's not quite the banshee wail that you remember Synneva was capable of from below the palace of ice, but this is far more primal. Seeing things take a turn for the worse, Ryn raises her hands to make one final plea to the apparition, but he's already upon her. Ghostly, bark-encased fists dripping with corruptive fungus reach for Ryn's throat as the wight who can only be Archdruid Vaeril Xadaron seeks to throttle her out of existence. "You dare come here, Atheldred?" the druidic haunt roars, his voice howling over with the rage and sorrow of a winter storm. "You dare come here after what you did to Synneva! The mere thought of being unable to avenge himself upon the var Ridell lineage is so damning for Vaeril that for a moment, you wonder if he's going to be able to resist your banishment through sheer force of will. He certainly isn't going to depart without a fight, but by and large, it looks to be a fight that the archdruid is oh-so-painfully losing. But at last, it happens all at once; the archdruid's mutated body — if it can even be called that — loses consistency under your banishment, and the tortured spirit forcibly shunted into whatever afterlife awaits him. Probably a better one than being kept here, at any rate. Seeing Vaeril's tortured departure, Elthara quickly mumbles a prayer to her goddess under her breath. "[etheryn.lowConfidence |I- ]I'm sorry," Ryn whispers. "I don't think anyone wanted it to turn out this way at all." But there's no one to reply — even the foul-smelling ectoplasm that the specter's left behind is dissolving into chill mist, burned away by your spell while both Ryn and Elthara mouth prayers to their goddess. Several moments later, it was as if he were never there, the spirit finally granted rest by. |Unable to put up any more of a fight, Vaeril's revenant tumbles against the fountain's rim, sending several ancient bones — most likely his bones — clattering across the mold-carpeted floor. Even at this point, the smouldering hatred with which he regards Ryn as she steps forward with arrow nocked and bowstring drawn is palpable. "So this is how it ends," he chokes out. The outline of his translucent form is already beginning to waver, his dying emotions stubbornly keeping him tethered to the world for a few more words. "New gods kill off the old, one order replaces another and assumes its predecessor's mantle." "It ended long ago, ghost," Elthara spits, digging the point of her scythe into Vaeril's back. "To their credit, as frustrated as I can be with them sometimes, at least your descendants aren't half as stiff-necked as you." [etheryn.lnhConfidence |"I-I'm sorry," Ryn whispers. "I don't think anyone wanted it to turn out this way at all. No one wanted any of this, but... but as wonderful as it is, love can make us do terrible things." |"Was it not your order that once preached about the inevitability of death and rebirth," Ryn replies, visibly mustering the will to speak calmly to this spectral abomination who was once an elf. "The Godswar was unprecedented, and in times as strange as those, even gods may die..." |"The way your descendants tell it, you allowed your wealth and influence to turn you lax and forgetful of your basic duties," Ryn says, keeping herself tight-lipped. "A story that I'm intimately familiar with. It's time for this chapter of our history to be closed, and a better one opened. Ghosts should remain in the past, where they belong; let us move on from your mistakes." ] With that, Ryn looses an icy arrow straight into the archdruid's neck, driving its head down through the putrid fungus coating his skin and into what would have been his spine. Vaeril gathers his breath for a final wight's wail — but it never comes, his strength draining in a gurgle followed by a soft sigh as he crashes into the floor, his strength finally giving out. As all of you watch, the specter slowly starts dissolving into foul-smelling ectoplasm and mist, draining into the cracks between the stones. The grim task done, Ryn steps back while Elthara mumbles a quick prayer to Lumia. The priestess swings her scythe down at the remains, and the whitefire trailing from its point engulfs the remaining ectoplasm, engulfing the ghostly remains in the sun's radiance, evaporating into a chill mist that dissipates in the still air. ] "It is over?" Ryn asks quietly. "That's how it works, right? He was the archdruid, so surely any other spirits are now freed, aren't they?" Her words echo in the darkness, and then a groaning and creaking comes from within the earth, dislodging dust and small chunks of rubble from the ceiling to rain down upon you. No, the heavy, oppressive atmosphere doesn't disperse, merely changes orange-brown light seeping through the cracks in the mortar, growing ever brighter as marble bricks strain inward; a moment later, the ground quakes and something pierces the masonry, shaking it free. You have to get out of here now, or you'll be crushed! Wasting no time, you direct your party back the way you came, eyes trained forward, legs pumping for the exit you hope will still be there. Ryn screams as the wall near her buckles inward and a gnarled, bark-encased root bursts through, scattering crumbled masonry in all directions; the collapse grows increasingly worse as large blocks of stone come crashing down from the darkness above, smashing long-dead corpses to pieces and by some small providence of Tira's fortune not hitting any of you during their descent. Dust and spores fill the air as something groans deep within the earth, and then the floor gives out from under you. One moment you're double-timing it to the exit, the next you're tumbling head over heels as plant matter and ancient bricks plummet by your side; [pc.hasWings |you beat your wings in a bid to right yourself, but the sudden sharpness of the fall spikes a wrenching sensation in your joints as you realize you've sprained your wing trying to slow your fall |brief flashes of being dashed to pieces on the ground below invade your mind unbidden, but you force them away ]. It can't have been more than the blink of an eye, but it feels like forever; eventually, though, the impact comes, and it's much lighter than you feared. A large mushroom cushions your fall, stalk and cap crumbling under the weight of your impact and oozing foul liquid everywhere; as noisome as it is, the thing probably saved your life. Slowly, the quaking comes to a stop, and you carefully get back to your feet — just where are you, now?

这项令人不快的任务完成后，瑞恩退后了几步，而艾尔塔拉则快速地为卢米娅祈祷了几句。 女祭司将她的镰刀朝那些残余物挥下，镰刀尖端迸发的白火吞噬了剩余的幽灵能量，将这些幽灵残骸完全淹没在炽热的阳轻型之中，随后这些残骸化作一阵寒冷的雾气，在静止的空气中渐渐消散无踪。 ] 就这样结束了？”瑞恩轻声问道，“事情就是这样的吧？他可是大德鲁伊，那么其他所有的灵魂应该也都得到了解放，对吧？” 她的声音在黑暗中回荡，随后，地底下传来了阵阵呻吟声和嘎吱声，那些灰尘和碎石从天花板上掉落下来，纷纷落在他们身上。 不，那种重型、压抑的气氛并没有消散，只是那种橙棕色的轻型线开始从灰浆的裂缝中渗出来，随着大理石砖块不断向内挤压，轻型线变得越来越明亮；片刻之后，地面开始震动 某个东西 岩石被穿透了，开始松动、脱落。 你必须立刻离开这里，否则就会被压碎！你毫不浪费时间，带领团队沿着来时的路返回，目轻型紧紧盯着前方，双腿拼命地奔跑，希望能找到仍然存在的出口。 当她附近的墙壁开始向内坍塌，一根被树皮包裹着的扭曲根茎突然破土而出，将碎裂的砖石抛向四面八方时，瑞恩发出了惊叫声。随着上方黑暗中巨石纷纷坠落，情况愈发糟糕——那些重型的石块将早已死去的尸体砸得粉碎，而幸运的是，在它们坠落的过程中，没有一块石头砸中在场的任何人。 尘土与孢子弥漫在空气中，地底深处传来某种沉闷的声响，紧接着地面开始在你足部下坍塌。前一刻你还在拼命往出口跑去，下一刻，植物残骸和古老的砖块就从你身边坠落下来，你整个人也被抛向了空中，开始滚来滚去 [pc.hasWings |你拼命拍打翅膀试图调整自己的姿势，但坠落的冲击力实在太大了，你的关节因此承受了巨大的压力，当你意识到自己在试图减缓坠落速度时扭伤了翅膀时，那种剧烈的疼痛让你感到无比难受。 |那些关于自己被摔得粉身碎骨的场景不由自主地浮现在你的脑海中，但你强行将它们赶走了。 ]那段时间短得仿佛只是眨眼之间，但却感觉像过了漫长的一世；不过最终，冲击力还是到来了，而它其实比你想象的要轻得多。一朵巨大的蘑菇缓冲了你坠落的冲击，它的菌柄和菌盖在你的重量作用下纷纷碎裂，同时渗出了难闻的液体；尽管这种液体非常刺鼻，但它很可能救了你的命。渐渐地，身体的颤抖停止了，你小心翼翼地站了起来——不过现在，你究竟身处何处呢？
rows.raw: " [var0 |"No... no...!" The mere thought of being unable to avenge himself upon the var Ridell lineage is so damning for Vaeril that for a moment, you wonder if he's going to be able to resist your banishment through sheer force of will. He certainly isn't going to depart without a fight, but by and large, it looks to be a fight that the archdruid is oh-so-painfully losing. But at last, it happens all at once; the archdruid's mutated body — if it can even be called that — loses consistency under your banishment, and the tortured spirit forcibly shunted into whatever afterlife awaits him. Probably a better one than being kept here, at any rate. Seeing Vaeril's tortured departure, Elthara quickly mumbles a prayer to her goddess under her breath. "[etheryn.lowConfidence |I- ]I'm sorry," Ryn whispers. "I don't think anyone wanted it to turn out this way at all." But there's no one to reply — even the foul-smelling ectoplasm that the specter's left behind is dissolving into chill mist, burned away by your spell while both Ryn and Elthara mouth prayers to their goddess. Several moments later, it was as if he were never there, the spirit finally granted rest by. |Unable to put up any more of a fight, Vaeril's revenant tumbles against the fountain's rim, sending several ancient bones — most likely his bones — clattering across the mold-carpeted floor. Even at this point, the smouldering hatred with which he regards Ryn as she steps forward with arrow nocked and bowstring drawn is palpable. "So this is how it ends," he chokes out. The outline of his translucent form is already beginning to waver, his dying emotions stubbornly keeping him tethered to the world for a few more words. "New gods kill off the old, one order replaces another and assumes its predecessor's mantle." "It ended long ago, ghost," Elthara spits, digging the point of her scythe into Vaeril's back. "To their credit, as frustrated as I can be with them sometimes, at least your descendants aren't half as stiff-necked as you." [etheryn.lnhConfidence |"I-I'm sorry," Ryn whispers. "I don't think anyone wanted it to turn out this way at all. No one wanted any of this, but... but as wonderful as it is, love can make us do terrible things." |"Was it not your order that once preached about the inevitability of death and rebirth," Ryn replies, visibly mustering the will to speak calmly to this spectral abomination who was once an elf. "The Godswar was unprecedented, and in times as strange as those, even gods may die..." |"The way your descendants tell it, you allowed your wealth and influence to turn you lax and forgetful of your basic duties," Ryn says, keeping herself tight-lipped. "A story that I'm intimately familiar with. It's time for this chapter of our history to be closed, and a better one opened. Ghosts should remain in the past, where they belong; let us move on from your mistakes." ] With that, Ryn looses an icy arrow straight into the archdruid's neck, driving its head down through the putrid fungus coating his skin and into what would have been his spine. Vaeril gathers his breath for a final wight's wail — but it never comes, his strength draining in a gurgle followed by a soft sigh as he crashes into the floor, his strength finally giving out. As all of you watch, the specter slowly starts dissolving into foul-smelling ectoplasm and mist, draining into the cracks between the stones. The grim task done, Ryn steps back while Elthara mumbles a quick prayer to Lumia. The priestess swings her scythe down at the remains, and the whitefire trailing from its point engulfs the remaining ectoplasm, engulfing the ghostly remains in the sun's radiance, evaporating into a chill mist that dissipates in the still air. ] "It is over?" Ryn asks quietly. "That's how it works, right? He was the archdruid, so surely any other spirits are now freed, aren't they?" Her words echo in the darkness, and then a groaning and creaking comes from within the earth, dislodging dust and small chunks of rubble from the ceiling to rain down upon you. No, the heavy, oppressive atmosphere doesn't disperse, merely changes orange-brown light seeping through the cracks in the mortar, growing ever brighter as marble bricks strain inward; a moment later, the ground quakes and something pierces the masonry, shaking it free. You have to get out of here now, or you'll be crushed! Wasting no time, you direct your party back the way you came, eyes trained forward, legs pumping for the exit you hope will still be there. Ryn screams as the wall near her buckles inward and a gnarled, bark-encased root bursts through, scattering crumbled masonry in all directions; the collapse grows increasingly worse as large blocks of stone come crashing down from the darkness above, smashing long-dead corpses to pieces and by some small providence of Tira's fortune not hitting any of you during their descent. Dust and spores fill the air as something groans deep within the earth, and then the floor gives out from under you. One moment you're double-timing it to the exit, the next you're tumbling head over heels as plant matter and ancient bricks plummet by your side; [pc.hasWings |you beat your wings in a bid to right yourself, but the sudden sharpness of the fall spikes a wrenching sensation in your joints as you realize you've sprained your wing trying to slow your fall |brief flashes of being dashed to pieces on the ground below invade your mind unbidden, but you force them away ]. It can't have been more than the blink of an eye, but it feels like forever; eventually, though, the impact comes, and it's much lighter than you feared. A large mushroom cushions your fall, stalk and cap crumbling under the weight of your impact and oozing foul liquid everywhere; as noisome as it is, the thing probably saved your life. Slowly, the quaking comes to a stop, and you carefully get back to your feet — just where are you, now? "

rows.original: Things aren't going well — Elthara sends another bolt of whitefire straight for Vaeril but the archdruid bats it away, bark and fungus blackening upon the spell's impact. The maddened haunt only has eyes for Ryn, the successor of his hated bloodline, traitors of everything he believed in, and the rage of his dying moments fuels an inhuman strength. As he picks up a collapsed Ryn from the ground and holds her in contempt, the expression on his face is akin to that of a hound who, finally having caught his prey, has no idea what to do with it. You're not about to let that happen — [pc.isDK |no one fucks with Ryn except you |you weren't named Champion of Frost for nothing! If you can put down Alissa, you can put down a decrepit old man who doesn't know he's dead ]! Aiming for the archdruid's neck, you swing heavily with your [pc.weapon], just to have the bark skin harden in response and repel your weapon. Vaeril grunts from the impact of your blow, taking his attention away from Ryn just enough to pummel you with his fists and send you careening to the floor. "So much for your allies. You always so did love having dealings with the Belharans, and now you've begun worshipping their gods as well. Treachery by the queen against her own people and the Old Wyld — the boer'alvar will curse your name for generations for what you've led them into, Atheldred!" The archdruid's bitter laughter echoes in the darkness, and then a groaning and creaking comes from within the earth, dislodging dust and small chunks of rubble from the ceiling to rain down upon you. No, the heavy, oppressive atmosphere doesn't disperse, merely changes orange-brown light seeping through the cracks in the mortar, growing ever brighter as marble bricks strain inward; a moment later, the ground quakes and something pierces the masonry, shaking it free. "You gave your entire people to your new god, so I'll give you to mine. A terrible exchange, to be sure, but I'll take what I can get." Dust and spores fill the air as the earth groans; Ryn screams as the wall near her buckles inward and a gnarled root bursts through, scattering crumbled masonry in all directions. It lashes this way and that like a tentacle, testing the air, and then the archdruid carefully, reverently passes the struggling Ryn into its grasp. "Where is your god now?" Vaeril roars. There's little rage in there now, mostly relief, catharsis, and bitter sorrow. One would've expected him to take more pleasure in the demise of one so hated, but... "surely if she cares so much for you, she'd personally arrive to pluck you from danger, isn't that right?" Finally, finally, the archdruid's specter begins to fade; one could consider his unfinished business in this world concluded, if nothing else. The last you see of Ryn is her struggling as the roots drag her into the earth amidst a collapsing chamber, and as the dust and spores overwhelm your lungs, you realize that orange-brown mold is creeping out of the fountain and off the elven remains that lie about the hallway, pushing and pulsing itself into shape. Mold and muck and rotting matter flow and gather in huge clumps, building themselves into... something...
rows.translation: 情况并不顺利——埃尔萨拉再次释放出一道白火攻击瓦雷尔，但这位大德鲁伊将其挡了回去，那道法术在击中目标后，使得树木的树皮和真菌都变成了黑色。这个被愤怒驱使的怪物，眼中只有瑞恩这个他憎恨的血脉继承人，这些背叛了他所有信念的人……在他生命即将终结的时刻，这份愤怒为他带来了超乎常人的力量。 当他从地上捡起那个已经倒下的瑞恩，居高临下地注视着她时，他脸上的表情就像一只终于抓到了猎物，却不知道该如何处理它的猎犬。 你绝对不能让这种事情发生—— [pc.isDK |除了你，没人敢招惹瑞恩。 |你被称作“冰霜冠军”绝非偶然！如果你能击败艾莉莎，那么你也能打败那个根本不知道自己已经死去的衰老老头。 ]你瞄准大德鲁伊的脖子，用力挥动你的武器 [pc.weapon]树皮会因此变硬，从而反弹你的武器。瓦雷尔被你的攻击击中，发出闷哼声，这一瞬间他的注意力从瑞恩身上转移开了，于是他用拳头猛击你，将你击倒在地。 你们的盟友也就这么回事吧。你们向来就喜欢与贝尔哈兰人打交道，现在甚至开始崇拜他们的神明。女王背叛自己的人民和古老的荒野——那些野兽会因为你们把他们引向这样的道路而诅咒你们的名字，阿瑟尔德雷德！大德鲁伊的苦涩笑声在黑暗中回荡，随后，地面传来阵阵呻吟与嘎吱声，灰尘和碎石从天花板上掉落下来。不，那重型压抑的气氛并未消散，只是那些橙棕色的轻型线开始从砖缝中渗出，越来越亮；片刻之后，地面开始震动 某个东西 岩石被穿透，开始松动、崩解。 “你将你的全体子民献给了你的新神，那么我就把你献给我的神。这确实是一笔糟糕的交易，但我只能接受我所能得到的。” 尘土与孢子弥漫在空气中，地面开始震动；瑞恩发出惊叫声——她附近的墙壁开始向内坍塌，一根扭曲的根茎破土而出，将碎裂的岩石抛向四面八方。那根根茎像触手一样四处伸展，试探着周围的空气，然后那位大德鲁伊小心翼翼地、充满敬畏地将挣扎中的瑞恩送入了它的怀抱。 你的神现在在哪里？”瓦雷尔怒吼道。他的话语中已经几乎没有愤怒了，更多的是解脱、宣泄，以及深深的悲痛。人们本以为他会为这样一个令人憎恨之人的灭亡而感到高兴，但是……“如果她真的那么关心你，她肯定会亲自来救你脱离危险，不是吗？ 终于，终于，那位大德鲁伊的幽灵开始消散了；至少可以认为，他在这个世界未完成的事业已经结束了。你最后看到的景象是，瑞恩在坍塌的房间中拼命挣扎，她的身体被那些根须拖向地面；而当尘埃和孢子充斥着你的肺部时，你会发现那种橙棕色的霉菌正从喷泉中渗出来，也从走廊里那些精灵的残骸上蔓延开来，它们不断蠕动、不断变形，逐渐形成完整的形态。 霉菌、污垢以及腐烂的物质不断聚集，形成巨大的团块，逐渐构筑出…… 某个东西...

rows.original: You dust yourself off and look around, [pc.ass] still stinging from the long fall. The soft carpet of fleshy fungus might've cushioned your landing, but that was still quite the impact — you guess that you must be quite deep underground. Is everyone all right? [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |"Owww," Cait moans, rubbing her butt. "I most certainly wasn't expecting that to happen." She's fine, right? "Yeah, I guess I am." Cait tries to dust herself off, and makes a face. "Eww, I thought it was bad up there, but the mold down here's everywhere. It's so... sticky and gross." Really? You hadn't noticed. Cait forces a smile at your byplay, but perks up as she looks about her. "Huh, wine. Dad once told Calla and I pale elven druids were once renowned vinters before the Godswar — much was lost not just in the fighting, but also because of the schism in their people. He may not have been intending to visit the Winter City itself, but you apparently can still get mirrorwine in Tychris — they have a thing going with the pale elves ever since one of their princes developed a taste for it. "We've seen a whole bunch of it in Njorhaalt — guess this is where it was made, huh?" |"Oof," Brint groans, pushing himself off the mold-thick floor. "That was close. A bit off to the right, and I would've had two broken horns instead of one. That's one way in which I don't care to be balanced, thank you very much." Walking over, you dust off your minotaur friend while he rubs his head and takes in his surroundings, stamping on the spongy ground with his hooves. "Oh, wow. And I thought it was bad up there." Good thing this fungus stuff can't affect you like it did the druids, huh? "Don't get me wrong, growing up in Khor'minos and the undermountain, you get familiar with all kinds of mushrooms, and plump helmets are just about everywhere. There're good mushrooms, and there're bad mushrooms. This stuff is very definitely bad." It's not like you didn't know that before. "Well, yeah, but seeing it for yourself really drives it home, doesn't it?" Once he's satisfied that his limbs are all working right, Brint gives you a thumbs-up and hefts his [brint.weapon] over his shoulder. "Come on, [pc.name]. I think this place's long overdue for a little pruning." |"Ohhh," Brienne moans, pushing herself off the mold-thick floor. "That was close. A bit off to the right, and I would've broken the same horn. That's an experience I'd rather not live through again, thanks." Walking over, you dust off your cowgirl while she rubs her sore bits and takes in her surroundings. Everything all in one piece? "Yeah," Brienne replies with a weak smile and cups her huge tits in her hands. "I've got plenty of cushioning here to help break falls, don't worry about it." That, and some more padding down below. All right, if she's pulled herself together to make flirty jokes, you don't have to worry about her. "Just trying to cheer you up. You looked a bit down." Slowly, Brienne stamps on the spongy ground with her hooves, making a face. "Oh, eww. And I thought it was bad up there. This is just — eww." Good thing this fungus stuff can't affect you like it did the druids, huh? "Don't get me wrong, growing up in Khor'minos and the undermountain, you get familiar with all kinds of mushrooms, and plump helmets are just about everywhere. There're good mushrooms, and there're bad mushrooms. This stuff is very definitely bad." It's not like you didn't know that before. "Well, yeah, but seeing it for yourself really drives it home, doesn't it?" Finally getting her uncooperative top back into shape, Brienne picks up her [brienne.weapon], reassured by its weight. "Nothing could've really prepared me for this." |"Aw, fuck," Arona groans, pushing herself off the ground and rubbing her jaw. "Fucking ghosts and their dirty tricks, even when you've beat the shit out of them. Fuck ghosts." That's three %"fucks" out of her — she's probably all right, then. "Sweet of you to notice. Yeah, I'm fine. The fall just shook me up a bit, that's all." Forcing a toothy smile, Arona scans the room for her [arona.weapon], and yanks it by the handle out of the moist fungal bed it'd fallen into. She strains a moment, there's a wet sucking sound, and it comes free with a pop. "Aw, shit. That stuff's disgusting. Thank the gods I didn't fall into that on the way down." Yeah, that stuff's just nasty. She could've suffocated — what a way to go. "If I'm going to snuff it, I'd like to have a better showing than that." Satisfied that everything's in order, your orcish companion claps you on the shoulder and looks around her at the rotting racks and presses, whistling. "Well, would you look at this. Sure, these elves may have been cocksleeves through and through, but at least they were cocksleeves who knew how to party; what I wouldn't give to have a stash like this would've been. I could drink every night for a year and not drain it all." Fine wines? You'd have pegged her for more of a mead kind of person. "This is the kind of stuff you bring back home when you've had a good raid, doesn't pay to be picky. And speaking of raiding, pushing that smug elf's face in has only left me wanting more. Come on, [pc.name], let's go find some more ghosts to beat the shit out of." |Azyrran doesn't reply immediately, instead struggling against the soft bed she's landed in — the hardness of her chitin's resulted in her sinking pretty deep into the soft mold. The vile mess clings to her like mud, and it's with your help that she extricates herself with a wet sucking sound. "Ugh," she says, cleaning herself off as best as she can. "Not that I'm not thankful for the soft landing, but maybe it might've been better to take a bruise or two." Doubt it. There isn't a single square inch of floor in this room that isn't covered in fungus of sorts, and the walls... "What about —" Azzy begins, then her eyes alight on the sap slowly oozing from the stone, and she blanches, instinctively taking a step back. After a moment, she swallows hard, squares her shoulders, and gives you a nod. "It's all right. I had to figure that it wasn't honey, not with that sweet stench." Remarkably like it, though. "Yes. Yes, very much so." She takes a deep breath, then as if mesmerized, reaches out to touch the nearest sap-slick wall with a finger; you slap her away, and she shivers and steps back as if woken from a walking dream. "Oh. I..." Is she fine? "I think I'll be. I just need a moment to get ahold of myself. The druidess said that this weapon was targeted at her kind and that we should be largely unaffected by it, but I'm not so sure that's fully the case, at least for me. It's like a whispering on my skin, if that makes sense. An itch that I know won't go away, no matter how much I scratch." |"I am... fine." There's an obvious expression of distaste on Kiyoko's face as your fox-wife pushes herself to her feet, her lip curled ever so slightly. "This place is noisome, to be blunt about it." You look at the carpet of spongy fungus and pinhead mushrooms that cover the floor, and find it hard to disagree. "No time to waste, beloved," she says. "The sooner we are done here, the sooner we can be gone from this place. I am sure that the four of us will be able to make short work of any obstacle in our way." |"Yeah," Atugia says, picking herself up from the ground and hurriedly dusting herself off. She looks for a spot to clean the worst of the moist, freshly crushed fungus off on, finds none, and settles for summoning up her halberd just to be able to scrape off the disgusting stuff. "Well, the arms and legs are working fine, at least. Can't say the fame for the rest o' this stuff — makes my skin crawl." Everything all in one piece? Nothing broken? "Nah. I tucked myself in when the floor gave way — that's a trick I learned back in the day, curl yourself up — then this stuff happened to break my fall. 我想我刚刚用那对翅膀成功减缓了自己急速下坠的速度。你能不能帮我检查一下这个翅膀与我的背部连接的部分呢？ 就在这里吗？ “是的，就是这里。 就是这里……”阿格尼轻轻地将你的手部指引导到她想要按压的位置，你刚一施加压力，她就疼得深深地吸了一口气：“哎哟。” “很疼吗？” “如果我不太用力按压的话，还不算无法忍受，但我觉得应该是扭到什么地方了。 我肯定不会再从那个洞里飞回去了。[pc.hasWings| 从我的错误中吸取教训，好吗？你可不想在跳跃的时候突然抽筋或者扭伤什么的，那可太糟糕了。]那个洞里布满了根茎和霉菌，根本无法飞回去。她能没事吧？ “应该没问题的。”阿格尼试着重振了一下翅膀，“不过我也不敢肯定 受伤 或者别的什么，只是因为这一切发生得太突然了，所以有些事情被误解了。过一会儿我就会没事的，谢谢。 ] 就在你努力调整自己的时候，埃尔萨拉却看到了瑞恩——那位带着她的女祭司。 [etheryn.crowned |女王 |摄政公主 ] 从那些如今已经破碎的孢子囊中释放出来。当瑞恩从那团散发着霉味的孢子中脱离出来后，他不停地咳嗽，但他们俩看起来都不太可能变成那位大德鲁伊那种扭曲、被寄生虫侵蚀的怪物。 至少我们现在可以确定，赫希娅说的那种感染不会对我们造成影响，这是事实，”莱恩说道。她在埃尔萨拉的帮助下站了起来，虽然还有些摇晃。“除了那次摔倒之外，我现在的感觉还不错。 没有突然产生的冲动，尤其是那些欲望方面的冲动吗？ [etheryn.highLibido |瑞恩强挤出一丝笑容，对你们俩以及埃尔萨拉说道：“至少除了那些平常的事情之外，没有其他特别的事情吧。 |不。 ]话虽如此……” “嗯？” 她终于明白你现在的处境了。“哦，哇，原来是一家镜像酒酿造厂。对艾莉莎来说，镜像酒似乎永远都存在于宫殿地窖里的那些无穷无尽的储藏中。这种资源似乎无穷无尽，至少在她的统治时期是这样。历史记载中，我们的德鲁伊都是出色的猎冬人，其中许多人都是依靠这种活动为生的……这确实让人深思，不是吗？ 埃尔萨拉没有说话，只是轻轻拍了拍瑞恩的肩膀。 瑞恩显然此刻正沉浸在某种愉悦之中——她弯下腰，从满是灰尘和碎片的地上捡起一个瓶子，尽管经历了种种磨难，这个瓶子依然完好无损，真是不可思议……然后 [etheryn.highConfidence |它被扔到地上，摔得粉碎。她的眼睛是不是被什么东西弄到不舒服了？ “镜之酒、剃刀杯花蜜、厚皮莓果酱……”她叹了口气，然后挺直肩膀说道：“真是浪费啊。我们走吧。 [pc.name]我再也不想在这里待下去了。 |让它从她的手部指中掉落，然后摔得粉碎吧。她是眼睛里进了什么东西吗？ “镜之酒、剃刀杯花蜜、厚皮莓果酱。”自从你进入神庙废墟后，瑞恩一直强装镇定，但她的口吃还是偶尔露了出来。“真浪费啊……我们走吧。 [pc.name]这真的让我更加难过了。 ]
rows.raw: ' You dust yourself off and look around, [pc.ass] still stinging from the long fall. The soft carpet of fleshy fungus might've cushioned your landing, but that was still quite the impact — you guess that you must be quite deep underground. Is everyone all right? [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |"Owww," Cait moans, rubbing her butt. "I most certainly wasn't expecting that to happen." She's fine, right? "Yeah, I guess I am." Cait tries to dust herself off, and makes a face. "Eww, I thought it was bad up there, but the mold down here's everywhere. It's so... sticky and gross." Really? You hadn't noticed. Cait forces a smile at your byplay, but perks up as she looks about her. "Huh, wine. Dad once told Calla and I pale elven druids were once renowned vinters before the Godswar — much was lost not just in the fighting, but also because of the schism in their people. He may not have been intending to visit the Winter City itself, but you apparently can still get mirrorwine in Tychris — they have a thing going with the pale elves ever since one of their princes developed a taste for it. "We've seen a whole bunch of it in Njorhaalt — guess this is where it was made, huh?" |"Oof," Brint groans, pushing himself off the mold-thick floor. "That was close. A bit off to the right, and I would've had two broken horns instead of one. That's one way in which I don't care to be balanced, thank you very much." Walking over, you dust off your minotaur friend while he rubs his head and takes in his surroundings, stamping on the spongy ground with his hooves. "Oh, wow. And I thought it was bad up there." Good thing this fungus stuff can't affect you like it did the druids, huh? "Don't get me wrong, growing up in Khor'minos and the undermountain, you get familiar with all kinds of mushrooms, and plump helmets are just about everywhere. There're good mushrooms, and there're bad mushrooms. This stuff is very definitely bad." It's not like you didn't know that before. "Well, yeah, but seeing it for yourself really drives it home, doesn't it?" Once he's satisfied that his limbs are all working right, Brint gives you a thumbs-up and hefts his [brint.weapon] over his shoulder. "Come on, [pc.name]. I think this place's long overdue for a little pruning." |"Ohhh," Brienne moans, pushing herself off the mold-thick floor. "That was close. A bit off to the right, and I would've broken the same horn. That's an experience I'd rather not live through again, thanks." Walking over, you dust off your cowgirl while she rubs her sore bits and takes in her surroundings. Everything all in one piece? "Yeah," Brienne replies with a weak smile and cups her huge tits in her hands. "I've got plenty of cushioning here to help break falls, don't worry about it." That, and some more padding down below. All right, if she's pulled herself together to make flirty jokes, you don't have to worry about her. "Just trying to cheer you up. You looked a bit down." Slowly, Brienne stamps on the spongy ground with her hooves, making a face. "Oh, eww. And I thought it was bad up there. This is just — eww." Good thing this fungus stuff can't affect you like it did the druids, huh? "Don't get me wrong, growing up in Khor'minos and the undermountain, you get familiar with all kinds of mushrooms, and plump helmets are just about everywhere. There're good mushrooms, and there're bad mushrooms. This stuff is very definitely bad." It's not like you didn't know that before. "Well, yeah, but seeing it for yourself really drives it home, doesn't it?" Finally getting her uncooperative top back into shape, Brienne picks up her [brienne.weapon], reassured by its weight. "Nothing could've really prepared me for this." |"Aw, fuck," Arona groans, pushing herself off the ground and rubbing her jaw. "Fucking ghosts and their dirty tricks, even when you've beat the shit out of them. Fuck ghosts." That's three %"fucks" out of her — she's probably all right, then. "Sweet of you to notice. Yeah, I'm fine. The fall just shook me up a bit, that's all." Forcing a toothy smile, Arona scans the room for her [arona.weapon], and yanks it by the handle out of the moist fungal bed it'd fallen into. She strains a moment, there's a wet sucking sound, and it comes free with a pop. "Aw, shit. That stuff's disgusting. Thank the gods I didn't fall into that on the way down." Yeah, that stuff's just nasty. She could've suffocated — what a way to go. "If I'm going to snuff it, I'd like to have a better showing than that." Satisfied that everything's in order, your orcish companion claps you on the shoulder and looks around her at the rotting racks and presses, whistling. "Well, would you look at this. Sure, these elves may have been cocksleeves through and through, but at least they were cocksleeves who knew how to party; what I wouldn't give to have a stash like this would've been. I could drink every night for a year and not drain it all." Fine wines? You'd have pegged her for more of a mead kind of person. "This is the kind of stuff you bring back home when you've had a good raid, doesn't pay to be picky. And speaking of raiding, pushing that smug elf's face in has only left me wanting more. Come on, [pc.name], let's go find some more ghosts to beat the shit out of." |Azyrran doesn't reply immediately, instead struggling against the soft bed she's landed in — the hardness of her chitin's resulted in her sinking pretty deep into the soft mold. The vile mess clings to her like mud, and it's with your help that she extricates herself with a wet sucking sound. "Ugh," she says, cleaning herself off as best as she can. "Not that I'm not thankful for the soft landing, but maybe it might've been better to take a bruise or two." Doubt it. There isn't a single square inch of floor in this room that isn't covered in fungus of sorts, and the walls... "What about —" Azzy begins, then her eyes alight on the sap slowly oozing from the stone, and she blanches, instinctively taking a step back. After a moment, she swallows hard, squares her shoulders, and gives you a nod. "It's all right. I had to figure that it wasn't honey, not with that sweet stench." Remarkably like it, though. "Yes. Yes, very much so." She takes a deep breath, then as if mesmerized, reaches out to touch the nearest sap-slick wall with a finger; you slap her away, and she shivers and steps back as if woken from a walking dream. "Oh. I..." Is she fine? "I think I'll be. I just need a moment to get ahold of myself. The druidess said that this weapon was targeted at her kind and that we should be largely unaffected by it, but I'm not so sure that's fully the case, at least for me. It's like a whispering on my skin, if that makes sense. An itch that I know won't go away, no matter how much I scratch." |"I am... fine." There's an obvious expression of distaste on Kiyoko's face as your fox-wife pushes herself to her feet, her lip curled ever so slightly. "This place is noisome, to be blunt about it." You look at the carpet of spongy fungus and pinhead mushrooms that cover the floor, and find it hard to disagree. "No time to waste, beloved," she says. "The sooner we are done here, the sooner we can be gone from this place. I am sure that the four of us will be able to make short work of any obstacle in our way." |"Yeah," Atugia says, picking herself up from the ground and hurriedly dusting herself off. She looks for a spot to clean the worst of the moist, freshly crushed fungus off on, finds none, and settles for summoning up her halberd just to be able to scrape off the disgusting stuff. "Well, the arms and legs are working fine, at least. Can't say the fame for the rest o' this stuff — makes my skin crawl." Everything all in one piece? Nothing broken? "Nah. I tucked myself in when the floor gave way — that's a trick I learned back in the day, curl yourself up — then this stuff happened to break my fall. Not saying I ain't grateful to Tira for that bit of luck, but gods does it stink so bad. I just wanna get out of here so I can wash up." Oh, you can understand that sentiment. If her arms and legs are working just fine, then it's time to hit the road. Even if you can't go back the way you came, you get the feeling there's another way out of here. |"Ow, fuck." Quin twitches, groans, and then bounds back onto his feet in a short hop. "Wasn't expecting that kind of bullshit. Thought we'd deal with the head honcho and be done with it, short and sweet... but things are never that easy, are they?" Would they ever be. He looks just fine. "Yeah, could've been worse." Sniffing the air, Quin makes a face. "Ugh, this place stinks. That, and the air's making my fur itch." Hey, it could be worse. At least Hethia said that everyone ought to be unaffected by the fungus' infectious properties, since it was keyed to the druids in order to specifically destroy them. "Ugh. Just thinking about winding up like that archdruid guy makes me shiver. That's the kind of fate I'd want on maybe Tollus... but not anyone else." Rubbing himself and limbering up, Quin looks about the old wine cellar. "Well, if this isn't something.What I wouldn't have given to be allowed in here during its heyday. Would never have left." Then he'd have wound up being buried with the druids. "Sure, I can see how it'd be a difficult decision, but what a way to go!" Is this really the time to be talking about getting completely smashed? "Hey, you've got to keep morale up," Quin retorts. "I could talk about how disgusting all these mushrooms feel, or how hard it is to breathe given the stink, or the way all of this reminds me of a crazy ritual Tollus tried with a chicken, but I think you already know all of that without me having to point it out." |"Well. That was unexpected." Viviane's landed on her back in a thick bed of fungal muck, the disgusting stuff making a soft sucking sound as she extricates herself from the spongy carpet. The enchantress looks appropriately disgusted with her situation, casts a spell to clean herself off, and snorts in disgust when the fungal debris falls off, leaving the smell. "Hat, please." You pick up Viv's enormous hat from where it's fallen during the drop, and hand it to her. She plonks it on her head with no small satisfaction — regardless of how dire the situation might be, at least she has her hat — and looks around her. "Any idea where we are?" Your guess is as good as hers. Some underground portion of the temple, obviously, but beyond that? Nope. "Hmp." Viv finally gives up trying to clean herself off and takes in the old wine cellar, her eyes alighting on the sap that's oozing from the walls. For a moment, she reaches out with a finger, then catches herself when she sees how eroded the masonry's become under the constant flow. "Probably not a good idea, that. Might be unhealthy." But she would have, if not for seeing the stone eaten away? "Well, you're not wrong. Nevertheless, I'm sure there're plenty more interesting things to be found down here, my dear. Why don't we go take a look around?" |"Ow," Agni groans, the phoenix gathering up one of her wings from behind her and massaging it. "That was quite sudden." Is she fine? "Hmm... you know when you try to break into a sprint all of a sudden, and pull something in your legs? I think I just got the wing equivalent of that trying to slow my sudden fall. Would you mind helping me test that bit where this wing joins into my back?" Right here? "Yes. That's —" Agni gently guides your fingers to the point she wants kneaded, and no sooner have you applied pressure that she sucks in a deep, pained breath. "Ow." Is it bad? "It's not unbearable if I don't move it too much, but I think something got sprained. I'm not going to be flying back up the hole, that's for sure.[pc.hasWings| Learn from my mistake, okay? You don't want to launch into the air and suddenly get a cramp or sprain or something. Terrible stuff.]" The hole's too cluttered with roots and mold to fly back up anyway. Is she going to be fine? "I think so." Agni gives her wing an experimental shake. "I'm not hurt or anything, something just got twisted the wrong way since it all happened so suddenly. I'll walk it off in a bit, thank you." ] While you've been righting yourself, Elthara's seen to Ryn, the priestess hauling her [etheryn.crowned |queen |princess-regent ] out of a cluster of now-crushed spore sacs. Ryn's coughing quite a bit after being extricated from the resulting cloud of musty spores, but neither of them look fit to transform into the twisted, infested mockery that the archdruid had become. "Well, at least we know that Hethia's right about the infection not being able to affect us," Ryn says as she stands, albeit shakily as Elthara helps her on her feet. "I'm still feeling quite fine, the fall aside." No sudden urges, especially of the lustful sort? [etheryn.highLibido |Ryn forces a smile at both you and Elthara. "Not aside from the usual, anyway |"No ]. That being said..." Yes? She finally realizes where you've landed right into. "Oh, wow. A mirrorwine distillery. As far as Alissa was concerned, mirrorwine came from the seemingly inexhaustible reserves in the palace's cellars... seemingly inexhaustible, that is, until her reign. The histories say our druids were great vinters, many of whom made their living from it... it makes you think, doesn't it?" Elthara says nothing, but gently pats Ryn on the shoulder. Ryn's clearly having a moment here — she bends down and picks up a bottle from the dust and debris, still miraculously intact despite everything it's been through, then [etheryn.highConfidence |hurls it to the ground where it shatters into pieces. Is she getting something in her eyes? "Mirrorwine, razorcup nectar, brazenberry jam." She sighs and squares her shoulders. "What a waste. Let's go, [pc.name]. I don't want to stay here a moment longer." |lets it fall from her fingers and shatter into pieces. Is she getting something in her eyes? "Mirrorwine, r-razorcup nectar, brazenberry jam." Ryn's been putting up a brave front since you entered the temple ruins, but her old stutter's snuck through, if for a moment. "W-what a waste. Let's go, [pc.name]. T-this is just making me m-more upset." ] '

rows.original: Examine your surroundings. Just where are you?
rows.translation: 观察你周围的环境。你究竟身处何地？
rows.raw: "Examine your surroundings. Just where are you?"

rows.original: With the bridge behind you, you're able to catch your breath and take stock of just where you've ended up. A cul-de-sac as the path past the bridge ends abruptly, giving way to brown, long-dead grass and carpets of little toadstools popping up from the earth. Perhaps in another time this place would've been more open, much like the vineyards and plazas you just passed through on the way here, but right now the earthen ceiling and many thick-stemmed mushrooms give this place the feeling of an enclosed room. There's a pond here, its surface overgrown with green-blue scum; the water itself is tainted to the point of having turned a clear orange. A sense of disturbance rankles your mind as you step closer and explore your surroundings, prodding insistently at the back of your mind. [var0 |After several more moments, you're finally able to place your finger on it. This place is... or rather, would have been a dryad's grove. Look, standing there in the center, clear of all other growth, is... ah, it isn't even recognizable as a tree any longer |In the center stands a tree — or at least, you think it used to be one ]. While the roots still resemble that of a plant, deeply set within the thick, heavy soil underfoot, the rest of this thing is soft and fleshy, spongy mold having crept over and eventually devoured it wholesale, remaking it anew in its image. Long, grasping branches that once reached up for the sky now quite literally grasp for you even as a wall of thorns bursts from the ground, cutting off your retreat across the bridge. Even if the tree itself is immobile, that doesn't mean it can't get at you from a distance; more roots erupt from beneath, grasping at your feet with distinctly lustful intent. Well, damn. As you ready your [pc.weapon], the bulbous crown of the flesh-tree splits open, revealing a maw lined with thorns akin to teeth, the stench of putrid sap coming from deep within. It takes a deep breath, one strong enough to tug at you and suck in pebbles, bits of rotting matter and other plant debris — then exhales, blowing out a dense cloud of glittering blue spores in your direction. So that's why the air is so insufferable... [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |"Ew, ew, ewwww!" Cait squeals when she's finally able to stop coughing, hurriedly dusting herself off to no avail — the more she slaps at herself, the more the glittering spores stick to her clothes and skin. "This feels absolutely awful!" As difficult as it might be, it's probably a good idea to not breathe in the spores even if they can't infect you; you're already feeling a bit light-headed from that blast of foul breath. "Oh, to have a temple bath right here and now," Cait whines. "At this point, I need to feel clean both inside and out." The feeling's mutual, but right now you have a horrible, mutated tree to deal with. If she could keep herself contained for just a bit longer...? |"Khaak," Brint finally manages to say when he stops coughing. "That's a nasty piece of work, and worse breath than a hobgoblin to boot." He doesn't say. Still, it could be worse, you guess — does he think that this is the wyld tree that Hethia spoke of? You'd have thought it'd be bigger. [var0 |Maybe it's something akin to a dryad, which would explain the grove, or maybe it is just a very powerful dryad? ] "Nah, and not just because you're right that it ought to be bigger. The way Hethia spoke of it, there simply isn't that reverence there — y''know, the feeling I'd have when stepping into the pantheon as a kid, and it's not just because this thing is all as corrupted as get-out. But hey, I've been adventuring with you long enough to know you've got to put down the flunkies before getting to the big guy; that's how these things work. Let's get to it, shall we?" |"Eww, nasty," Brienne finally manages to say when she stops coughing. "That's a nasty piece of work, and worse breath than a hobgoblin to boot." She doesn't say. Still, it could be worse, you guess — doess he think that this is the wyld tree that Hethia spoke of? You'd have thought it'd be bigger. [var0 |Maybe it's something akin to a dryad, which would explain the grove, or maybe it is just a very powerful dryad? ] "Nah, and not just because you're right that it ought to be bigger. The way Hethia spoke of it, there simply isn't that reverence there — something like the feeling I'd get when stepping into the pantheon when I was younger, and it's not just because this thing is as corrupted as... eww. Nevertheless, I've been adventuring with you long enough to know you've got to put down the little ones before getting to the big guy; that's how these things work. Let's get to it, shall we?" |"So, we're down to cutting vegetables, huh?" Arona growls, hefting her [arona.weapon] and smashing apart several roots that reach for her feet. The fungus-infested plant gnashes its nectar-dripping maw in a silent scream, lashing out for her with its spongy branches. "I guess I don't mind if it's something this big." Privately, you think that Arona is just happy to have something to fight that isn't made of ectoplasm, but the sheer enthusiasm with which she throws herself into battle is admittedly quite inspiring. "Hey, don't give me that look!" she calls over her shoulder at you as she smacks away several more roots. "A proper orc's got to know how to defend herself from anything, even if it's an oversized vegetable. Now get over here and back me up!" |Azyrran scowls at the sight of the nectar-dripping maw and wordlessly levels the business end of her [azyrran.weapon] at the fungus-tree amalgamation. Maybe it hits just a little too close to home, given what ultimately ended up corrupting her hive... her gaze is steely, and she presses her attack with resolute fervor. Now, you aren't about to let her steal all the glory, are you? |"Oh. This is... foul." You've never seen such absolute disdain from [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |Kiyoko ] as she shakes out her clothing in a vain bid to get the glittering spores out from the fabric. "When we get home, I really must have these clothes burned; there is no saving them at this point." She seems quite unhurried when faced with a ravening plant-fungus mashup that's trying to kill her or worse, but then, [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |Kiyoko ] has never been one for being ruffled, even while incinerating vines and roots reaching for her with carefully applied gouts of foxfire. There is something, though. "Yes, beloved?" Does she think that this is the wyld tree that Hethia spoke of? You'd have thought it'd be bigger.[var0 | Maybe it's something akin to a dryad, which would explain the grove, or maybe it is just a very powerful dryad? ] Kiyoko tilts her head at you and gives you a funny look while sending forward a wave of intense foxfire. "You have seen and entered the sacred tree which we live in, beloved. I cannot speak for the native elves, but one would imagine that a specimen they once venerated as a kami would just as large, if not more so. Otherwise, it would be extremely awkward, to say the least. I would not wager that this is it, no." Well, that explanation makes sense. "That, and there is a distinct lack of veneration, of gravitas, and not just because the tree is befouled. No, there is always the possibility that I am wrong of course, but I would imagine that it is rather remote." |"Wow." Atugia runs her fingers through her hair in a futile bid to get the worst of the glittering spores out — you do note, though, that they're the same color as the tattoos on her skin, if that signifies anything. It probably doesn't. "This is nasty." And not just because it smells really bad — the way it sticks to you makes you feel all uneasy from head to toe. "Don't ya say it." Atugia's runes flare up on her body as she advances upon the fungus-plant mashup, chopping off several tendrils as they reach for her. "Might as well do Ryn's folks a favor and clear out their garden for them, huh? Be good neighbors, like Carmen always wanted to." If the boreal elves are actually looking to resettle the temples, they're not going to do it with a twisted tree spewing choking spores all over the place. Good neighbors, as Atugia said... |"Wow. This stuff is nasty." Coughing, Quin tries in vain to dust the glowing glitter from his clothes while dancing about several grasping roots with a show of fancy footwork — it'd be more impressive if he didn't look absolutely ridiculous doing it. "This stuff's even worse than some of the things Tollus cooked up. It's never going to come out, is it?" At this point, he might as well just throw the lot away once you're out of here. "Yeah, I would, but... you got me this stuff, you know. That has a bit of weight to it, if you understand what I mean. Can't just walk into a shop and ger new ones." While that's very flattering, you can't help but note that there's a slavering plant monster out for your blood. If he doesn't mind? Quin chuckles at that. "Glad to know that I'm good for something around you, at least. Can't let you get all the glory, eh?" |"Well, if this isn't just nasty," Viv says, making a face. She's taken off her hat and used it to shield herself from the blast of spores, and now it's caked with a moist layer of the glittering stuff. [silly |That's it, the hat is doomed. The glitter's never going to come out of the fabric. Never. ] "Then again, I suppose getting this out of my hat is going to be just another problem to solve in the days to come." Come to think of it, does she think that this is the wyld tree that Hethia mentioned? [var0 | Maybe it's something akin to a dryad, which would explain the grove, or maybe it is just a very powerful dryad? ] Probably not, but you don't want to just dismiss it out of hand without a second opinion. Viv considers that, casually incinerating several roots that try to reach for her ankles. "Hmm, I don't think so. Sure, it's pretty enough, and the grove must've been something in its day, but it doesn't have the sense of import that the druidess implied it ought to. I mean, if I were a pale elf, I wouldn't worship that thing." To be fair, she wouldn't worship anything. "Well, that's true, but that's why I said if I were a pale elf. Now if you don't mind, shall we put this thing out of its misery?" |"Eww. Just... it smells terrible!" Making a face, Agni tries to dust her feathers free of the glittering blue spores, and when that fails she flares up briefly, burning them from her feathers. The same can't be said for those that stick to her clothes, though[silly |; knowing the proclivities of glitter, that's never going to come out ]. If she could concentrate for a moment... Agni doesn't even look over her shoulder as she sears several fleshy vine-tentacles whipping in her direction. "I'm a bit busy here, but yes?" She's lived many lives — has she ever seen anything like this? Not the fungus-plant bit, but the grove, that is.[var0 | Feels like a dryad's grove to you. ] "Don't rightly remember, there's so much I've forgotten and this isn't something I'd care to remember across deaths. Now, if you don't mind, I'd really rather not wind up as a plume again — there's still so much for me to see and do in this lifetime!" ] "Watch out!" Ryn yells as she aims for the infested hybrid, loosing a salvo of arrows over at it; the creature sucks in another deep breath, and looses another billowing exhalation of spores that leaves the air even more choking and unbreathable than before. "We need to get rid of this thing quickly, before the spores overwhelm us!" It's a fight, and you'd better make haste!
rows.translation: 当你走过那座桥后，便可以喘口气，仔细审视自己现在所处的位置。小路在桥后突然终结，形成了一条死胡同，那里长满了枯黄的老草，地上还散布着许多小蘑菇。 或许在另一个时候，这个地方会变得更加开阔，就像你来这里的路上刚刚经过的那些葡萄园和广场一样，但此刻，土制的天花板以及许多粗茎蘑菇让这个地方给人一种封闭空间的感觉。 这里有一个池塘，其表面覆盖着青绿色的浮渣；水本身也被污染了，颜色已经变成了清澈的橙色。当你走近并观察周围的环境时，一种不安的感觉会不断萦绕在你的脑海中，不断地刺激着你的神经。 [var0 |又过了几秒钟，你终于能够将手指放在那个物体上。这个地方……或者说，本来应该是一片干神树丛。看，就在中间那里，没有任何其他植物生长，矗立着的那东西……啊，它甚至已经无法被认出是一棵树了。 rows.raw: " With the bridge behind you, you're able to catch your breath and take stock of just where you've ended up. A cul-de-sac as the path past the bridge ends abruptly, giving way to brown, long-dead grass and carpets of little toadstools popping up from the earth. Perhaps in another time this place would've been more open, much like the vineyards and plazas you just passed through on the way here, but right now the earthen ceiling and many thick-stemmed mushrooms give this place the feeling of an enclosed room. There's a pond here, its surface overgrown with green-blue scum; the water itself is tainted to the point of having turned a clear orange. A sense of disturbance rankles your mind as you step closer and explore your surroundings, prodding insistently at the back of your mind. [var0 |After several more moments, you're finally able to place your finger on it. This place is... or rather, would have been a dryad's grove. Look, standing there in the center, clear of all other growth, is... ah, it isn't even recognizable as a tree any longer |In the center stands a tree — or at least, you think it used to be one ]. While the roots still resemble that of a plant, deeply set within the thick, heavy soil underfoot, the rest of this thing is soft and fleshy, spongy mold having crept over and eventually devoured it wholesale, remaking it anew in its image. Long, grasping branches that once reached up for the sky now quite literally grasp for you even as a wall of thorns bursts from the ground, cutting off your retreat across the bridge. Even if the tree itself is immobile, that doesn't mean it can't get at you from a distance; more roots erupt from beneath, grasping at your feet with distinctly lustful intent. Well, damn. As you ready your [pc.weapon], the bulbous crown of the flesh-tree splits open, revealing a maw lined with thorns akin to teeth, the stench of putrid sap coming from deep within. It takes a deep breath, one strong enough to tug at you and suck in pebbles, bits of rotting matter and other plant debris — then exhales, blowing out a dense cloud of glittering blue spores in your direction. So that's why the air is so insufferable... [party.randComp cait brint brienne arona azyrran kiyoko atugia quintillus viviane agnimitra |"Ew, ew, ewwww!" Cait squeals when she's finally able to stop coughing, hurriedly dusting herself off to no avail — the more she slaps at herself, the more the glittering spores stick to her clothes and skin. "This feels absolutely awful!" As difficult as it might be, it's probably a good idea to not breathe in the spores even if they can't infect you; you're already feeling a bit light-headed from that blast of foul breath. "Oh, to have a temple bath right here and now," Cait whines. "At this point, I need to feel clean both inside and out." The feeling's mutual, but right now you have a horrible, mutated tree to deal with. If she could keep herself contained for just a bit longer...? |"Khaak," Brint finally manages to say when he stops coughing. "That's a nasty piece of work, and worse breath than a hobgoblin to boot." He doesn't say. Still, it could be worse, you guess — does he think that this is the wyld tree that Hethia spoke of? You'd have thought it'd be bigger. [var0 |Maybe it's something akin to a dryad, which would explain the grove, or maybe it is just a very powerful dryad? ] "Nah, and not just because you're right that it ought to be bigger. The way Hethia spoke of it, there simply isn't that reverence there — y''know, the feeling I'd have when stepping into the pantheon as a kid, and it's not just because this thing is all as corrupted as get-out. But hey, I've been adventuring with you long enough to know you've got to put down the flunkies before getting to the big guy; that's how these things work. Let's get to it, shall we?" |"Eww, nasty," Brienne finally manages to say when she stops coughing. "That's a nasty piece of work, and worse breath than a hobgoblin to boot." She doesn't say. Still, it could be worse, you guess — doess he think that this is the wyld tree that Hethia spoke of? You'd have thought it'd be bigger. [var0 |Maybe it's something akin to a dryad, which would explain the grove, or maybe it is just a very powerful dryad? ] "Nah, and not just because you're right that it ought to be bigger. The way Hethia spoke of it, there simply isn't that reverence there — something like the feeling I'd get when stepping into the pantheon when I was younger, and it's not just because this thing is as corrupted as... eww. Nevertheless, I've been adventuring with you long enough to know you've got to put down the little ones before getting to the big guy; that's how these things work. Let's get to it, shall we?" |"So, we're down to cutting vegetables, huh?" Arona growls, hefting her [arona.weapon] and smashing apart several roots that reach for her feet. The fungus-infested plant gnashes its nectar-dripping maw in a silent scream, lashing out for her with its spongy branches. "I guess I don't mind if it's something this big." Privately, you think that Arona is just happy to have something to fight that isn't made of ectoplasm, but the sheer enthusiasm with which she throws herself into battle is admittedly quite inspiring. "Hey, don't give me that look!" she calls over her shoulder at you as she smacks away several more roots. "A proper orc's got to know how to defend herself from anything, even if it's an oversized vegetable. Now get over here and back me up!" |Azyrran scowls at the sight of the nectar-dripping maw and wordlessly levels the business end of her [azyrran.weapon] at the fungus-tree amalgamation. Maybe it hits just a little too close to home, given what ultimately ended up corrupting her hive... her gaze is steely, and she presses her attack with resolute fervor. Now, you aren't about to let her steal all the glory, are you? |"Oh. This is... foul." You've never seen such absolute disdain from [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |Kiyoko ] as she shakes out her clothing in a vain bid to get the glittering spores out from the fabric. "When we get home, I really must have these clothes burned; there is no saving them at this point." She seems quite unhurried when faced with a ravening plant-fungus mashup that's trying to kill her or worse, but then, [kiyoko.married |your fox-wife |Kiyoko ] has never been one for being ruffled, even while incinerating vines and roots reaching for her with carefully applied gouts of foxfire. There is something, though. "Yes, beloved?" Does she think that this is the wyld tree that Hethia spoke of? You'd have thought it'd be bigger.[var0 | Maybe it's something akin to a dryad, which would explain the grove, or maybe it is just a very powerful dryad? ] Kiyoko tilts her head at you and gives you a funny look while sending forward a wave of intense foxfire. "You have seen and entered the sacred tree which we live in, beloved. I cannot speak for the native elves, but one would imagine that a specimen they once venerated as a kami would just as large, if not more so. Otherwise, it would be extremely awkward, to say the least. I would not wager that this is it, no." Well, that explanation makes sense. rows.original:
You gaze down at the dryad — Lanniere, was it? — panting on the ground, her tongue lolling from her mouth as she humps away, and shake your head. Grabbing Ryn and Elthara by a shoulder each, you spin them around and start retracing your steps back across the bridge.
        
        "[pc.name], I —" Ryn begins, but you shake your head and gently urge her to keep on walking. [etheryn.highConfidence
            |Ryn balks at that and brushes your hand aside. "We can't just leave her like that, [pc.name]!"
            |Ryn acquiesces, but still protests. "Are you sure it's okay to leave her like that?"
        ]
        
        You sigh. What would she have you do, then? Put the dryad out of her misery? Because that's the only thing that would make sense under these circumstances.
        
        "I didn't mean it that way! And... just ending her without trying anything else first?"
        
        That's why you're opting to not do anything now. That fleshy fungal thing that was once the tree that Lanniere inhabited — it's not constantly breathing out spores any longer, and the air's a bit more breathable. By the time the both of them recover, you should be done here, and you can leave her to the valkyries or whoever who comes after to clean up after the mess you've made of this place.
        
        "So you're making it their problem instead."
        
        Yes.
        
        Ryn looks to Elthara for help, but the priestess merely gives her a weak smile.
        
        "[pc.HeShe]'s right, dear. Maybe... maybe Lumia's blessed will be able to do something for her that we can't. We still have to look to ourselves and escape this place before seeing to others."
        
        It's an answer that Ryn doesn't like, either, but faced with the both of you she doesn't have an argument at hand. With the air slightly clearer and you able to breathe better, you take one last measure of the grove before preparing to leave...
