rows.original: Have a chat with your daughter
Give your daughter a good petting before you say goodbye.
rows.translation: 在道别之前，好好地抱抱你的女儿吧。
rows.raw: "Give your daughter a good petting before you say goodbye."

rows.original: Take a moment to play with your daughter.
rows.translation: 花点时间陪你的女儿一起玩耍吧。
rows.raw: "Take a moment to play with your daughter."

rows.original: There is such a concept as too much of a good thing. You don't want to spoil your daughter too rotten, do you?
rows.translation: 好事过度也会适得其反。你可不想因此宠坏自己的女儿。 也 烂了吧，不是吗？
rows.raw: "There is such a concept as too much of a good thing. You don't want to spoil your daughter too rotten, do you?"

rows.original: Give Kinu some sweet fruit and spoil her rotten.
rows.translation: 给绮奴一些甜美的水果，把她宠坏吧。
rows.raw: "Give Kinu some sweet fruit and spoil her rotten."

rows.original: You don't have any sweet fruit that would make a suitable gift for Kinu here.
rows.translation: 你这里没有任何适合送给绮奴的甜果作为礼物。
rows.raw: "You don't have any sweet fruit that would make a suitable gift for Kinu here."

rows.original: Ask about your daughter's ambitions for herself.
rows.translation: 问问你女儿对自己有哪些抱负和目标。
rows.raw: "Ask about your daughter's ambitions for herself."

rows.original: Ask if she's getting along well with her mother.
rows.translation: 问问她和她母亲的关系是否融洽。
rows.raw: "Ask if she's getting along well with her mother."

rows.translation: 询问她兄弟姐妹的情况。

rows.original: Your daughter needs a few more siblings before she can say anything meaningful about them. Why don't you get to work making some more with her mother?
rows.translation: 在你的女儿有了几个兄弟姐妹之后，她才能对他们的性格和行为做出一些有意义的评价。你们为什么不和她的母亲一起努力，再生几个孩子呢？
rows.raw: "Your daughter needs a few more siblings before she can say anything meaningful about them. Why don't you get to work making some more with her mother?"

rows.original: Try and get an insight into your daughter's personality and what she's been learning in her time.
rows.translation: 试着了解你女儿的性格特点，以及她在这段时间里学到了什么。
rows.raw: "Try and get an insight into your daughter's personality and what she's been learning in her time."

rows.original: Take Kinu out to play in the forest.
rows.raw: "Take Kinu out to play in the forest."

rows.original: For the intellectually inclined. Play go or shogi with Kinu.
rows.translation: 适合喜欢思考的玩家。与绮奴一起玩围棋或将棋吧。
rows.raw: "For the intellectually inclined. Play go or shogi with Kinu."

rows.translation: 给你的女儿讲个故事吧。

rows.original: Play with Mommy — get Kiyoko out of the house for some time as a family.
rows.translation: 和妈妈一起玩吧——让纪代子暂时离开家，一家人一起度过一段时光。
rows.raw: "Play with Mommy — get Kiyoko out of the house for some time as a family."

rows.original: You crouch down so you're at eye level with Kinu, and give your fluffy daughter a look-over. She's clothed in much the same way as her mother is — the same foreign yet rather traditional light dress, a yukata, was it? Unlike Kiyoko, who goes for the more graceful, flowing look, Kinu's skirts are much shorter, ending at just below her knees. For a little fox who plays in dirt and climbs trees on a regular basis, this looks to be just about right. Her clothes are in shades of white and blue to go with her silvery-white hair and fur, and a purple anklet's been looped about her ankle, complete with a small bell. You get the feeling that there's some significance to it — it certainly isn't a bell proper, as there's no clapper within to make it ring; perhaps you should ask Kiyoko about that sometime. Long sleeves and thick hems seem to be her thing, and like her mother, the lot is bound at her waist with a large purple sash, tied into a bow about her back. Looped about Kinu's neck is a collar with yet another bell on it, made from the same material as her anklet; she really likes these things, doesn't she? When it comes to height, Kinu definitely takes after her mother in that regard. It's not correct to think of her as small — the little kitsune is more fun-sized in that regard, and is determined to prove it with a presence as big as her physical form is small. Besides, Kinu's only roughly seven or eight summers of age, she's got a lot growing left to do. In the meantime, maybe her petite stature will mean that she won't be raiding the peach grove with ease. Like all of her kind, Kinu has large, fluffy fox ears that sit atop her head, little tufts of fur sprouting haphazardly from within them; this is accompanied by a set of three tails that emerge from just above the waist of her skirts. For someone as young as her to have three is quite promising, and it can't be denied that Kinu is her mother's star pupil, either. Otherwise, though, your daughter appears almost perfectly human, if with a somewhat vulpine cast to her nose, chin, and slitted blue eyes. "I know I'm very pretty, [kinu.Dad]. Mama tells me that she comes from a line who takes good care of themselves and are exceedingly beautiful, even by kitsune standards. Is that why you chose to be with her?" Well, you didn't exactly choose to be with her — you happening across Kiyoko was a bit of a surprise, if anything else. But it was a pleasant surprise, no doubt. Kinu beams, the little kitsune's face lighting up. "One way or another, I'm very glad to have been born." Oh, of course. You give Kinu's fur a little ruffle, and then stand back up. All in all, for all the smarts she might have, she's a cute, excitable little thing all right.
rows.translation: 你蹲下来，使自己的视线与绮奴处于同一水平线，然后仔细打量了一下你那毛茸茸的女儿。她的穿着和她的母亲非常相似——同样是一件既带有异国风格又显得相当传统的轻薄连衣裙，对吧？应该叫做和服吧？与清子那种更加优雅、飘逸的穿着风格不同，绮奴的裙子要短得多，仅仅及及膝盖而已。 对于这样一只经常在泥土中玩耍、还会爬树的小狐妖来说，这样的装扮简直再合适不过了。 她的衣服采用了白色和蓝色的色调，这与她银白色的毛发和皮毛非常相配；她的脚踝上还戴着一只紫色的脚链，脚链上还挂着一颗小铃铛。 你会觉得这件事背后肯定隐藏着某种意义——毕竟这根本不是一只真正的铃铛，里面也没有可以使其发声的铃舌；或许你应该找个机会问问清子关于这件事。长袖衣服和厚重的下摆似乎是她喜欢的风格，和她母亲一样，她的衣服在腰部都用一条大大的紫色腰带系紧，然后在背后打成一个蝴蝶结。 基努的脖子上戴着一个项圈，上面还挂着一个铃铛，这个项圈和她的脚链是用同样的材料制成的；她真的很喜欢这些东西，不是吗？ 至于身高，基努在这方面确实遗传了她母亲的基因。 将她视为……是不对的。 小 — 那只小狐妖更加 小号尺寸的 在这方面，她决心用自己的存在来证明这一点——尽管她的体型娇小，但她的决心却无比坚定。此外，基努才刚刚七八岁而已，她还有很长的路要走。不过，也许正是因为她娇小的身材，她在偷摘桃子的时候反而不会那么容易被发现吧。 和同类的动物一样，基努也长着一对大而蓬松的狐妖耳朵，这两只耳朵竖立在她的头顶上，耳朵内部还随意地长着一些小簇毛发；此外，她的裙摆上方还长着三条尾巴。 对于一个年纪如此年轻的人来说，能够拥有这三个特征已经相当不错了。而且不可否认，绮奴确实是她母亲的得意门生。不过，你的女儿看起来几乎完全像人类，只是她的鼻子、下巴以及那双狭长的蓝眼睛带有一些狐妖的特征。 我知道自己非常漂亮， [kinu.Dad]妈妈告诉我，她的家族世代都非常注重自我保养，而且就算以狐族的标准来看，她们也个个都非常美丽。这就是你选择和她在一起的原因吗？ 嗯，你这么说其实有点 选择 能与她在一起——偶然遇见清子，实在是一件意外之喜，不过毫无疑问，这是一场令人愉快的惊喜。 桐人的脸上洋溢着笑容，那只小狐妖的脸庞也亮了起来。 不管怎样，能够出生在这个世界上，我感到非常庆幸。 哦，当然。你只需要轻轻弄乱绮奴的毛发，然后站回原处就可以了。说到底，尽管她可能很聪明，但她终究还是个可爱又容易兴奋的小家伙罢了。
rows.raw: " You crouch down so you're at eye level with Kinu, and give your fluffy daughter a look-over. She's clothed in much the same way as her mother is — the same foreign yet rather traditional light dress, a yukata, was it? Unlike Kiyoko, who goes for the more graceful, flowing look, Kinu's skirts are much shorter, ending at just below her knees. For a little fox who plays in dirt and climbs trees on a regular basis, this looks to be just about right. Her clothes are in shades of white and blue to go with her silvery-white hair and fur, and a purple anklet's been looped about her ankle, complete with a small bell. You get the feeling that there's some significance to it — it certainly isn't a bell proper, as there's no clapper within to make it ring; perhaps you should ask Kiyoko about that sometime. Long sleeves and thick hems seem to be her thing, and like her mother, the lot is bound at her waist with a large purple sash, tied into a bow about her back. Looped about Kinu's neck is a collar with yet another bell on it, made from the same material as her anklet; she really likes these things, doesn't she? When it comes to height, Kinu definitely takes after her mother in that regard. It's not correct to think of her as small — the little kitsune is more fun-sized in that regard, and is determined to prove it with a presence as big as her physical form is small. Besides, Kinu's only roughly seven or eight summers of age, she's got a lot growing left to do. In the meantime, maybe her petite stature will mean that she won't be raiding the peach grove with ease. Like all of her kind, Kinu has large, fluffy fox ears that sit atop her head, little tufts of fur sprouting haphazardly from within them; this is accompanied by a set of three tails that emerge from just above the waist of her skirts. For someone as young as her to have three is quite promising, and it can't be denied that Kinu is her mother's star pupil, either. Otherwise, though, your daughter appears almost perfectly human, if with a somewhat vulpine cast to her nose, chin, and slitted blue eyes. "I know I'm very pretty, [kinu.Dad]. Mama tells me that she comes from a line who takes good care of themselves and are exceedingly beautiful, even by kitsune standards. Is that why you chose to be with her?" Well, you didn't exactly choose to be with her — you happening across Kiyoko was a bit of a surprise, if anything else. But it was a pleasant surprise, no doubt. Kinu beams, the little kitsune's face lighting up. "One way or another, I'm very glad to have been born." Oh, of course. You give Kinu's fur a little ruffle, and then stand back up. All in all, for all the smarts she might have, she's a cute, excitable little thing all right."

rows.original: "You want to talk? You're like Mama, talking all the time... I'd rather play instead." Since you can't be with her all the time, you need to get to know her better. And by the same extent, your conversations with her are going to have that small ring of novelty that her mother's won't have. "I guess... but I'd still much rather play." Kinu pouts a little, and when she finally realizes that her cute act isn't going to get her what she wants, the little kitsune folds her ears and looks down. "But talking with [kinu.Dad] is fine too, I suppose." There, there. Now, what do you want to discuss with your daughter?
rows.translation: 你想聊天？你就像妈妈一样，整天都在说个不停……我还不如去玩呢。 既然你无法一直陪在她身边，那就需要更深入地了解她。这样一来，你们之间的对话也会因此而增添一些新鲜感，而这些是她的母亲所无法带来的。 我想吧……但我还是更喜欢玩游戏。 纪久微微撅起了嘴，当她终于意识到自己这种可爱的举动并不能得到她想要的东西时，这只小狐妖便把耳朵折起来，低下了头。 但是，与……交谈时 [kinu.Dad] 我想，那样也挺好的。 好了好了，现在你想和你的女儿讨论些什么呢？

Kinu pouts a little, and when she finally realizes that her cute act isn't going to get her what she wants, the little kitsune folds her ears and looks down. rows.original: [rand|"When I'm old enough, I want to be a den mother." Oh? Intending to follow in her mother's footsteps, is she? "Mama tells me that den mothers are the greatest of Keros' servants and greatly revered by all kitsune. I'd like to be admired by everyone, it feels really good to receive all sorts of nice attention." Kinu pauses a moment to think, clearly exaggerating her motions. "That, and she always looks so happy [kiyoko.numKits 4|when her tummy is big with another one of my brothers or sisters|when she's with me]. Every now and then Mama just stops what she's doing, gets so dreamy and starts stroking and petting and singing to her big tummy, it's kind of funny." Well, if she wants to be a den mother, she's going to have to start training early. Being one is more than just popping out kits, after all; anyone can do that. Others are going to look up to her for advice and leadership. Kiyoko might have had an eternity to be prepared, but Kinu doesn't. "I have to [kiyoko.numKits 4|help take care of my younger brothers and sisters|study really hard]! Mama says it'll be good practice for later on; it can get tiring, but she lets me have peaches afterwards!" That's one way to get Kinu to apply herself enthusiastically, you suppose. |"Do you know what my name means, [kinu.Dad]? 'Kinu' means 'silk' in the language of the old country where Mama came from. It's a very nice kind of cloth that's great to touch; it feels sooooo good. Mama's clothes are made from it, and so are mine." Silk, eh? Smiling, you reach down and grab one of Kinu's tails, threading the smooth fur between your fingertips. It lacks the overtly fluffy feel of Kiyoko's fur, instead more sleek and flowing to the touch. "Feels good, right?" It feels very nice. "That's the first thing which came to Mama's mind when she held me after I was born. Soft and silky. So she named me that." It's a good and fitting name for a little fusspet like her. "Hee hee!" |"Mama says that I have lots of potential, for me to have three tails when I'm so young." You don't need to know how many tails she has — with how frightfully quickly she picks up skills, anyone can easily tell that she's got plenty of potential. "Ehehe. Maybe." Kinu looks away, playing the coy little girl. "But it's a big deal to me, [kinu.Dad]. It goes to show that it's not all in my mind." There are other things tails are good for; she should ask her mother when she gets older. "They're good for pulling, and petting, and playing with!" Yep, there's still a lot she has to learn. Potential is just that until it's realized — she'll have to work really hard. Kinu huffs. "It's nothing that I'm not already doing." |You know, you've been wondering... "Hm?" When Kiyoko first introduced you to her, she was all very formal, calling the two of you "[pc.mf|father|mother]" and "mother"... and now it's just "[pc.mf|papa|mama]" and "mama." It's a little odd, this shift in language... "Well..." Kinu thinks a moment, her ears wiggling. "That time, Mama told me to be on my best behavior, and I didn't quite know how I would come across to you, so I tried to be as polite as possible. I don't like being stuffy, but if it was necessary..." Mhm, yes. And now she realizes that she can be herself around you? "That, or I realized that being cute and cuddly around [kinu.Dad] means I get lots of gifts and petting." A moment of silence. Kinu beams up at you with a big smile on her little foxy face, the very picture of innocence. "Ehehe, seeing that look on your face is priceless, [kinu.Dad]..." Well, if she's got you well and completely wrapped about her little finger, then she deserves to have as much. "You should be glad I'm not going as far as to use honorifics around you, [kinu.Dad]." |"Mama tells me I'm special; because I'm her eldest daughter, I'm capable of being a den mother like her when I grow up. She says it's something in the blood. I don't quite understand it, but that's only because I don't really have any way to find out for sure and Mama doesn't know herself..." Well, you're sure she'll find out when she gets older. "People keep on saying that... then when people get old, they start wishing they were younger again. I know that, because I read about it in books." There's more nuance to it than that, but to be fair, she isn't wrong... "It is," Kinu declares with all the authority an eight-year-old can muster, "More about the journey than the destination." |"I guess I'm not going to be growing very tall..." Sadly, if she takes after her mother — and everything points to that fact — then no; her mother is tiny compared to the other women you know, and by the looks of it Kinu is shaping up to be even more petite than her mother is. Maybe it's because her bloodline came from a foreign land; are people there shorter in general? Maybe you should ask Kiyoko sometime. "I guess it's a kitsune thing." Look, no one's going to be getting tall enough to reach the peach boughs without a ladder. She can give up that dream of hers. "Mrrrr... how is it that you can see into my head, [kinu.Dad]?" |Is there anything that she likes that isn't fruit? "I really really enjoy kenchin soup!" Now there's a dish you don't hear of on a regular basis. And what's it about this soup that makes her enjoy it so much? "I get to help Mama make it! See, we get lots and lots of tofu, then crumble it into the soup, then add lots and lots of mushrooms and root veggies and other things! Mama tries not to repeat the same recipe twice in a row, and whenever I drink it I feel so warm and good inside! Then it's all gone, and I can't have more..." |"I'm not a big fan of candy." A child who doesn't enjoy sweets? Will wonders never cease? Although, you must note, she's enough of a glutton for fruit of all kinds — aren't those sweet, too? Your daughter's eyes sidle from side to side, her face perfectly straight. "They're just so... thick; the flavor can be a little cloying and overwhelming at times. Fruit doesn't tend to have that problem, so I like it a lot more." Not that it matters, does it? Fruit or candy, she still turns into a hyperactive little pest who simply can't sit still. Kinu rubs the back of her head sheepishly. "Ehe... I can't deny that's true..." ]
rows.translation: [rand|等我长大一些，我想成为一名‘母兽’，照顾其他小动物。 哦？她是想步她母亲的后尘吗？ 妈妈告诉我，母狐是凯罗斯最伟大的仆从，所有狐族都十分尊敬它们。我也想得到大家的认可，收到各种美好的关注，这种感觉真的很棒。 纪奈停顿了一下，似乎在认真思考，她的动作明显有些夸张。 还有，她看起来总是那么开心。 [kiyoko.numKits 4|当她的肚子又怀上了我的另一个兄弟姐妹时|当她和我在一起的时候]偶尔，妈妈会停下手头的事情，陷入沉思，然后开始轻轻抚摸、亲昵地触碰她那圆滚滚的肚子，还会对着它唱歌，这种场景还挺有趣的。 嗯，如果她想担任“母兽领袖”的角色，那就必须尽早开始训练。毕竟，担任这个角色可不仅仅意味着生下幼崽——这种事任何人都能做到。其他成员会期待她能提供建议并发挥领导作用。虽然清子可能有足够的时间来准备，但绮奴却没有这样的机会。 我必须得这么做。 [kiyoko.numKits 4|帮我照顾弟弟妹妹们。|努力学习。]妈妈说，这对以后的学习会有帮助；虽然过程可能会很累，但之后她会允许我吃桃子作为奖励！ 我想，这确实是让绮奴全身心投入工作的一种方法吧。 |你知道我的名字意味着什么吗？ [kinu.Dad]在妈妈旧国的语言中，“绮奴”意味着“丝绸”。这是一种质地非常柔软、触感极佳的布料——真的感觉非常舒服 不错妈妈的衣服是用这种材料做的，我的衣服也是。 丝绸，嗯？你微笑着弯下腰，抓住基努的一条尾巴，让那光滑的毛茸茸的毛发从指缝间滑过。与清子的毛相比，它的质地没有那么蓬松，而是更加顺滑、流畅。 感觉不错吧？ 这种感觉 非常 不错。 我出生后，妈妈第一眼看到我时想到的就是这个词——柔软、丝滑。所以她给我取了这个名字。 对于她这样一个爱闹着玩的小家伙来说，这个名字确实很合适。 嘻嘻！ |妈妈说，我潜力巨大，才这么小就已经长了三条尾巴呢。 你根本不需要知道她掌握了多少种技能——只要看看她学习技能的速度有多快，就能立刻看出她拥有巨大的潜力。 呵呵，也许吧。 纪奈转开了视线，装作一副害羞的小女孩的样子。 但这对我来说意义重大。 [kinu.Dad]这恰恰证明了，那些事情并非只是我想象中的而已。 尾巴还有其他用途呢；等她长大一些，可以问问她妈妈。 它们非常适合用来拉扯、抚摸，还有一起玩耍呢！ 是啊，她还有很多东西需要学习。潜力只是潜在而已，除非真正被发挥出来——否则她就必须付出极大的努力。 绮奴叹了口气。 这本来就是我已经在做的事情罢了。 |你知道，你一直都在思考…… 嗯？ 当清子第一次把你介绍给她时，她表现得非常正式，把你们两个人都称为[pc.mf|父亲|母亲]和‘母亲’……而现在却只是[pc.mf|爸爸|妈妈]还有‘妈妈’。”这种语言上的变化，确实有点奇怪…… 嗯…… 纪久思考了一会儿，她的耳朵微微动了一下。 那次，妈妈让我一定要表现得最好，而我其实不太清楚自己在你面前会是什么样子，所以我就尽量做到有礼貌一些。我其实不喜欢拘谨的氛围，但如果有必要的话…… 嗯，是的。现在她意识到，在你面前，她可以做真正的自己了？ 要么就是，我意识到，表现得可爱、惹人怜爱其实也是一种 [kinu.Dad] 这意味着我会收到很多礼物，还会受到很多宠爱。 片刻的寂静。绮奴用她那张充满童真、带着灿烂笑容的小脸庞望着你，简直就是纯真的化身。 嘿嘿，看到你那副表情，真是太值了 [kinu.Dad]..." 嗯，如果她真的把你完全吸引到了她身边，让你对她无可抗拒，那么她确实应该得到这一切。 你应该庆幸我并没有使用敬语来称呼你。 [kinu.Dad]." |妈妈告诉我，我是特别的；因为我是她的长女，所以长大后我一定能够像她一样成为一家之主。她说这是与生俱来的天性。我其实不太明白这一点，只是因为目前还没有办法确定这一点，而妈妈自己也不太清楚…… 嗯，她长大了自然会发现的。 人们总是这么说……等到年纪大了，就会开始希望自己能再年轻一些。我是知道的，因为我在书上读到过这样的内容。 书籍." 其中其实还包含着更多的细微差别，但公平地说，她的观点并没有错…… 确实是。 基努以一个八岁孩子所能拥有的全部权威宣布道： 旅程本身比目的地更为重要。 |看来我长不高了…… 遗憾的是，如果她随她母亲的样子——而所有迹象都表明确实如此——那么她肯定不会很高。她母亲在你们认识的其他女性中已经算很矮小了，而从目前的情况来看，绮奴似乎还会比她母亲更矮。也许这是因为她的血统来自异国他乡；在那个地方，人们普遍比较矮小吧？或许你应该找个机会问问清子。 我想，这应该是狐妖的特有行为吧。 你看，没有谁不借助梯子就能够到那些桃树枝的。她还是放弃那个梦想吧。 呼……你怎么能看透我的心思呢 [kinu.Dad]?" |有没有什么她是特别喜欢的呢？ 不是 水果？ 我真的很喜欢肯钦汤！ 现在有一种菜肴，你平时并不常听说。那么，究竟是这种汤的什么特点让她如此喜爱它呢？ 我可以帮妈妈做这道菜呢！看，我们会准备很多很多豆腐，然后把它们捣碎放进汤里，再加入大量的蘑菇、根茎类蔬菜还有其他食材！妈妈总是尽量不会连续两次使用同样的食谱，每当我喝到这道汤的时候，就会觉得浑身暖洋洋的，感觉非常舒服！可惜这道汤总是很快就被吃光了，我再也吃不到啦…… |我并不是很喜欢糖果。 一个不喜欢吃甜食的孩子？世上还有奇迹存在吗？不过，你得注意，她对各种水果可是一样爱吃——那些水果不也是甜的吗？ 你女儿的眼睛左右快速转动，脸却保持着笔直的姿势。 他们就是太…… 厚实的这种味道有时会显得过于浓烈、甚至让人觉得有些腻味。而水果通常不会有这样的问题，因此我更喜欢水果口味。 其实这也无所谓吧？不管是吃水果还是糖果，她最终都会变成一个坐不住、到处乱跑的小捣蛋鬼。 纪久有些尴尬地揉了揉她的后脑勺。 呃……我不得不承认，那确实是事实…… ]

Kinu looks as skeptical as a fluffy, petite eight-year old can. |"Sometimes, Mama has me sit down with her over tea and talk with her." Ah. A lecture? "Not really." Kinu chews on her lip and looks thoughtful, her ears wiggling from side to side. "Yeah, Mama takes the opportunity to teach me about decorum, but she wants me to talk back at her, too. Said she's had enough of the sound of her own voice for centuries." Right, a conversation is a two-way street. Given what Kiyoko's been through, she's probably had enough one-sided exchanges to last several lifetimes; having someone else around to give an actual response is something she'd cherish more than most. But what about Kinu? Doesn't she like chatting with her mother? "Um, it's just that every time I try and talk with Mama, I'm reminded of just how much I don't know. So much of what she says goes over my head, so I have to nod along and pretend to understand so as to be polite. Then I have to give replies so generic that they may as well not matter..." Right. Lack of knowledge is one issue that can be resolved with hard work, but there's something else at play here. "What is it?" If you told her, that would defeat the purpose of her finding out for herself. She'll learn so much more that way. "Aw, boo..." |"Sometimes Mama will come up to me and just pick me up and cuddle. Don't tell her I told you, [kinu.Dad], but she always cries a bit when she does that." You're not surprised at that. "You're not?" Look at it this way. Your daughter might be a little terror at times, and sure, she has a tendency to raid the peach grove, but you believe that all in all, Kiyoko is very glad that she's around. Frankly speaking, an occasional cuddle is pretty low-key when it comes to things. Kinu looks thoughtful at that, idly toying with one of her three tails as she mulls over your response. "I guess... I understand it, but at the same time I don't understand it, either." Oh, you know exactly what she means. ] |[rand |Kinu winces and looks adequately guilty. "I got told off again earlier today..." You can guess, all right. Peaches? Kinu nods. You sigh. Well, at least she takes after her mother in that regard when it comes to her favorite foods... maybe Kiyoko can eventually realize that such behavior is less than perfect when it's mirrored in another individual. "Mama doesn't like peaches as much as I do." No, but there are other things she has just as great a weakness for. Your daughter's ears perk up at that. "Does that mean if I discover it, Mama will realize the error of her ways and let me have more peaches?" Oh dear. So young, and the only use for this information she can come up with is how to manipulate others for her benefit. What sort of mischievous monster are you raising here? "Eehee!" |So, now that she's got a sibling or two running around, has her mother let up on her any? "Actually, no, [kinu.Dad]. If anything, Mama's been harsher on me than before. I have to set a good example, you see — since so much has been given to me, an equal amount is going to be demanded of me." Oh, is this one of those things she understands but doesn't understand at the same time? Kinu just sighs and folds her little arms. "No, [kinu.Dad], I understand it very well. I just don't like it." You give your daughter a pat on the head. Few things worth doing were ever easy. "What makes it worse is that I can see it from Mama's point of view, and that gets into my fur so badly..." Why, it's almost as if mothers and daughters were made to ruffle each other's feathers. |"Mama has been in a good mood lately." Oh? Was there any particular reason for such? Kinu scratches her head in the most calculatedly adorable manner. "Not really... I think she just likes being around us. Mama used to have her ups and downs, but now there're more up days than down ones." Well, that's good news for her, isn't it? "Yep! Mama is so much better to get along with when she's not being all sour! She gets even happier when you visit, so you should come and see us lots!" You're here, aren't you? But is she sure she doesn't benefit from your visits in other ways? Your darling kitsune daughter gives you the biggest, most innocent smile you've ever seen. "You know that I know that you know, [kinu.Dad]. No need to tease me. Now, if you were willing to pet me a bit, I wouldn't mind..." |"Ehe, Mama brushed my hair and fur this morning. Can you tell? Can you tell?" Hmm... you're not that well-acquainted with the secrets of kitsune fur to be able to notice the differences yet. "It feels really good when Mama brushes me — I take so long when I try to do it myself, but she has it done in the blink of an eye! And she doesn't even use magic! Look! Look! Aren't my tails so glossy and lustrous?" Oh, yes. And her mother's work is going to be ruined the next time she rolls down a hill. "Heeeey... how did you know what I was doing yesterday, [kinu.Dad]?" Rolling down hills? Lucky guess? "Hmp... I don't think you do augury like Mama does, so..." On a more serious note, if she wants Kiyoko to brush her more often, maybe she should make herself useful, let her mother have a bit more free time. Then Kiyoko wouldn't have another reason to say no to demands for brushing. Kinu looks thoughtful, her ears wiggling. "That's not actually such a bad idea, [kinu.Dad] — heeeeeeey." What? |"Heeeey, [kinu.Dad]..." Yes? "So yesterday I was bringing in the laundry, and was tempted to sneak a peek in Mama's wardrobe..." Go on... "Do you know that she has fifteen sets of the exact same outfit?" That shouldn't come as a surprise to either of you. You've never seen her wear anything else, and Kinu has even less reason to be shocked by this revelation, since she does the laundry and all. Gods, even Kinu herself — you've never seen her in anything but the same yukata, right? "Wait! Wait! There's more!" Your daughter beckons you down to her level and whispers conspiratorially to you. "Mama has fifteen sets of clothes, but only six sets of smallclothes. That means... that means that some days, she's walking about the house without any panties on..." Oh dear. Kiyoko has a thing for going commando. You would absolutely have never known about Kiyoko's proclivities had your inquisitive little daughter not snooped in her mother's things. Truly, such a shocking discovery. "Somehow, [kinu.Dad], I get the feeling that you're not as intrigued about this as I am..." ] |[rand |"Mama let me help out in the kitchen today! With the sharpest knife, no less!" Hmm... if it were anyone else, you might be worried, but since it's level-headed Kiyoko supervising her it should be all right. She wouldn't saddle her daughter with anything little Kinu couldn't handle, would she? Kinu puffs up with pride, her silvery-white fur standing on end. "We're cooking bigger meals now, so I have been delegated with lighting the fires and chopping the veggies. It's fun!" Fun, she says. When viewed from the proper perspective, yes, one supposes chopping veggies could be fun... "And Mama praises me a lot when I do well..." So easily satisfied, isn't she? Well, there's her ticket. If she works hard to be useful and do well, then naturally people will want to pet and praise her. Wouldn't she like that? "Ehe. I still want to do just a bit of mischief, [kinu.Dad]..." |"Don't get in Mama's way today, okay? She'll be too polite to show it to you up front, but I've eaten leaves and dirt clods that tasted better than today's breakfast. That's how I know she's in a bad mood today." And what happened to her breakfast? "I gave it to one of my brothers and went into the forest to get some wild berries for myself... he ate it all and didn't seem to notice. But the point is that you should totally go in and cheer her up, otherwise Mama's grumpiness is going to be spreading to everyone else today." Cheer Kiyoko up, she says. Well, that's something you're certainly capable of. Indeed, a few ideas are already coming to mind. Little Kinu flicks an ear. "Mama is always in a much better mood when I'm going to be having another brother or sister. Maybe you can do... whatever it is you do, [kinu.Dad]?" |"I told off one of my little sisters for chewing on the furniture just the other day..." Chewing on... the furniture? Kinu sidles away from you, a sheepish grin on the little kitsune's face. "Yeah. I used to do it all the time when I was really little, too, but I've grown out of it since. Then I spotted my little sister doing the exact same thing and delivered a tongue-lashing, and that's when I realized..." Yes? "...Ehehe, that's when I realized I was saying the exact same things Mama would have said." Your daughter presses both palms to her cheeks in mock wide-eyed terror. "Oh no, [kinu.Dad]! I'm turning into Mama, and at such a young age, too! This can't be happening — I've got so long to live yet!" You laugh and pet Kinu on the head. There, there — Kiyoko still knows how to have plenty of fun, you can attest to that. |Now that your daughter has all these additional siblings, is her mother driving her even harder? Kinu nods glumly. "Even harder, [kinu.Dad]." She is going to be growing up into a position of considerable prestige, from what you know of kitsune society. Hence, you can understand where Kiyoko is coming from... and yet, she is also eight years old. It's hard to have to grow up so quickly[pc.bgMulti noblescion slumrat |; much was demanded of you as well because of who you were. You can just hope that Kinu takes her position more seriously than you did and not go off gallivanting on the other side of the world... |; you were forced to do much the same out of necessity. She has much that you didn't have in your miserable upbringing, if you can even call it that — she should count her blessings. | and there are times when you do wish that she could be a child for a little while longer, but things are the way they are for a reason, even if she doesn't agree with it. ] A sigh, and Kinu flattens her ears to the side. "I know, [kinu.Dad]. I know it's odd of me to say this, but I don't think I mind as much any more. It's kind of like I'm numb to it already." There, there. She deserves a hug for her hard work. "Yay, hugs..." |"Mama chewed me out a lot for getting a few scrapes while playing in the forest the other day. She was really worried." And she has every right to be. Kiyoko's her mother, after all; she'd be remiss in her duties if she didn't care when one of her children got hurt. Kinu folds her arms across her chest and pouts with all the defiance of a cute eight-year old fox kit. "Yeah, but getting a cut here and skinned knee there is important, regardless of Mama's good intentions. She can't coddle us forever, and I was doing perfectly fine up until she noticed the dried blood. I — I'm not ever going to learn to deal with pain if I don't get scratched up a bit, am I?" ... "Mama was really, really mad when I pointed this out to her, too. Thing is —" Kinu crosses her big blue eyes as she focuses on turning the gears in her head — "her job as our mother is to prepare us for the day we will no longer need her. There, I read it in one of the books she told me to study." ... "[kinu.Dad]?" If she's doing this at such a tender age, the mother-daughter arguments Kinu is going to have with Kiyoko when she gets older are going to be epic. You're tempted to watch — from a safe distance, of course. ] |[rand |"You know, [kinu.Dad], I've been thinking..." She's been thinking? Why, that's a change from her usual approach of doing things first and rationalising away her actions later. But please, do tell. Kinu sticks her tongue out at you. "Bleh! Anyways, I was thinking that Mama has it harder than any of us do. She has so many things to worry about that I don't have to, for example." That's true, yes. Although you do have to ask, what brought this on? "I... I'm not entirely sure myself. I just... I've been told so many times to wait on doing a lot of things until I'm older. But then when I look at it from another point of view — and especially ever since Mama keeps on giving me more brothers and sisters — getting older isn't all that cracked up as it's supposed to be, either. I dunno." The fact that she's realizing this of her own accord means she's getting older, in spirit if not in body. "I think I owe Mama an apology..." |"Something kinda weird happened the other day." Oh? Do tell. "I was doing the housework the other day when Mama came up from behind, hugged me and said she was glad I was born. I'm glad I was born, too, but that was all kind of sudden. And embarrassing." In that case, you'll be just as sudden in saying that you're very glad Kinu was born, in spite of all the hair-pulling, exasperating mischief she gets up to. "Eehee!" |"You want to hear something about Mama? I'll tell you, then." Kinu beckons for you to crouch down, then stands on tiptoe to whisper conspiratorially into your ear. "I was helping Mama in the kitchen the other day when I caught her sneaking away with some of the inarizushi. She doesn't think I saw her, but I did. The plate was empty when Mama got back, so there's only one reasonable conclusion to be drawn from this." Naturally. Did she think her own fondness for peaches sprang out of nowhere? That same attraction, that same desperate desire to indulge? "Now that you point it out, [kinu.Dad], it does make sense..." Heh. Like it or not, mother and daughter are more similar than either will openly admit, and in ways neither of them would prefer to consider. Now, knowing this, what is she going to do about it, if anything? Kinu rolls her eyes, adopting quite the exaggerated thinking pose. "To be honest, [kinu.Dad]? I don't know. Yeah, I could use that to try and get a treat out of Mama, but... it just feels kinda empty at this point. Petty." That's heavy stuff coming from her; there's probably no other eight-year old in all of Savarra who speaks like that. "I'll think about it later. For now, I just want to enjoy what time I have with you, [kinu.Dad]." Aww. There's a good girl. |"I think there's something wrong with my eyes, [kinu.Dad]." Hmm. You kneel down and take a good look into Kinu's big ice-blue eyes, but there's nothing there that's out of the ordinary. As far as you can tell, she seems fine[pc.cl whitemage |, and you confirm that fact with a little magic | ]. Now, is there any reason she's asking? "Then it is true! Mama is getting more... um..." Yes? Kiyoko is getting more...? "Boingy?" Boingy, she says. "Boingy. Bouncy. Uh, soft? Like, in her legs and, um... those parts..." Gods above, is your little kitsune daughter's face all red? Looks like she's also inherited her mother's weapons-grade blush, to add to all the other ways she takes after Kiyoko... "They make Mama look very regal, the way they fill out her clothes and stretch the silk fabric so smooth about her body. Then when she's brushed her hair and fur to a glossy sheen, she's absolutely stunning. I want to be like Mama and have good fur and boingy bits when I grow up, then people will fall over themselves to do what I say because I'm so pretty. And then because I'm smart, I'll know exactly what to tell them to do in order to get what I want. Hee hee!" You smile and sigh. At the end of the day, your daughter is still a scheming, mischievous, and above all, manipulative little thing. Now whose side of the family did she get that from? "I wonder why Mama is getting more boingy, though..." Um, you're sure Kiyoko will tell her when she's ready to be a full-fledged den mother. |"I'm being lectured less these days." Kinu announces proudly. There, now that's a good girl. Or is it just that with all these new siblings, her mother doesn't have that much time to scold her any more? Kinu huffs and sticks her chest out. "Of course it's because I've been good. Now that Mama delegates so much work to me, I just have more to do if I make trouble..." Ha, that's one way to solve that problem. Although there is to be said for a bit of harmless mischief every now and then, just to keep people on their toes. "I don't know about that, [kinu.Dad]." Hmm... on one hand, looks genuine. On the other hand, maybe she just wants you to think that... "Ehe. Or maybe I just don't mean anything by it, [kinu.Dad]..." ] |[rand |"I think Mama's been getting tired more easily these days, so I've been secretly helping her." You can understand her wanting to help out, but why the secrecy? "[kinu.Dad], I may not be very old yet, but even I can tell that Mama has her own pride and self-respect. If she sees me helping her out all the time when she hasn't asked me to, she's going to start feeling bad and doubting herself, and no one wants that." Oh, come on; Kiyoko's better than that. "Everyone has their moments of weakness, [kinu.Dad]. Everyone." Your precious darling daughter shifts her gaze from side to side as she chews on a thumb. "Mama may not wear her emotions on her sleeve, but I pick up more than everyone gives me credit for..." And her mother won't notice? Kinu grins. "Most times she thinks it's the astral plane doing its job despite her instructing it not to." And doesn't she imagine that her mother would find her perceived loss of control over her environment even more worrying than any feelings of inadequacy her daughter's diligence might cause? Your daughter ponders that a moment, then her ears droop and fold against her head. "Aw, [kinu.Dad]... you sure know how to ruin a good thing..." She should probably come clean with her mother. Call it a hunch, but you get the feeling that more could be achieved that way instead of trying to skirt around Kiyoko's notice. |"Um, [kinu.Dad], I know that all of us kits tend to take after Mama more than you, but my siblings are saying that I resemble her the most..." Of course, the white fox looks the most like the amber-orange one. Kinu pouts. "color aside, anyways. Well? Do I? Do I?" The likeness is there, yes, and not just in the physical sense. You get the feeling that this conversation is leading somewhere, though... "So, um... because you love Mama whole lots, and because I look like Mama, that means you love me whole lots, too! Right?" Sheesh, was that what she wanted to know? You'd absolutely adore her, even if she took after you more than Kiyoko. "Ehehe... thanks, [kinu.Dad], I love you lots too!" |"I got praised yesterday! I got praised yesterday!" Practically bubbling over with excitement, Kinu does a little hop and twirl before clutching at your legs, all three of her tails trailing behind her. "Mama praised me and said I was good!" Being complimented feels amazing, doesn't it? "It's always nice, but it didn't use to feel that way before. But the way Mama praised me, it made me all fuzzy to my stomach. Ehe..." Now that she's received something nice from her mother, she has to pay Kiyoko back. That's the way of the kitsune, after all. If she makes herself useful, studies hard and doesn't give her mother grief, you're sure there'll be more praise incoming. "I just wonder what changed... I don't really understand it myself. But I like it!" Well, guess what? So do you. |"Just the other day, Mama tried to teach me how to use makeup. Just a bit. She said I'd gotten to the point where I wouldn't just smear it all over my face or something." And by the look on her face and the cut of her ears, she didn't like it, did she? "Boo, no. Not my style, and besides, what's the point? It'd get all scuffed up when I go hunting for bugs in the woods. But the point is —" your daughter's cheerful demeanour returns to her face — "that Mama thought me able to deal with such grown-up things..." Emphasis on grown-up. After all, it's not that she doesn't know how to make herself look pretty, it's about resisting the temptation to doodle all over the place with the contents of her mother's vanity. "I-I always have good reasons for doing that..." Does she mean post-hoc justifications and rationalisations for less-than-exemplary behavior? "Boo... it's no fun with people who know you well..." |"I-I think I'm finally starting to see Mama's point of view more often than not," Kinu tells you, kicking at the dirt with the heel of her foot. "It scares me." Why should it scare her? From what you know of these things, her mother's practically an exemplar of kitsune feminine grace. "I'm herding my brothers and sisters, and then I'm thinking the exact same thoughts, doing the exact same things which Mama used to do to me. And then I don't even realize it until I have a moment to sit down and think about it. "I know I'm being pushed to grow up faster than any of my brothers and sisters so I can take on some actual responsibility, but..." your kitsune daughter searches for the appropriate words. "See, I know Mama is great and smart and pretty and has a great temperament and everything. I also know that those are pretty good things to aspire to. Question is, if I become the exact same thing as her, then what's the point of one of us existing?" All right, these are not words that should be coming out of an eight-year old's mouth. She's creeping you out, even if she doesn't mean it. "Sorry..." Sighing, you crouch down and give Kinu a warm, fluffy hug. There, even if she takes after her mother, she'll always be herself, okay? It's her job to aspire to greater things and eventually surpass Kiyoko. "I'd rather have more fun..." There, her mother wouldn't have said that. Somehow, Kinu doesn't appear very convinced, but she presses herself against you anyway. ] |[rand |"I was playing go with Mama earlier today, and we had to call it a tie. It was a really close thing." It's nice to see that even with so many brothers and sisters to take care of, the two of them still manage to eke some time out for games. A draw, was it? Neither mother nor daughter could get the upper hand on each other? Kinu looks a little embarrassed, but nods. "Funny thing is, when we were putting away the pieces, Mama laughed and said this is how so many of our arguments would turn out in the past, then she'd have to lay the law on me as my mother. It kind of made her feel guilty... but I don't blame her any more. Not that I have any regrets about being who I am, but sometimes I'm too smart for my own good." Ha. The fact that she can openly admit as much means she's wiser already, if not smarter. Besides, there are advantages to playing dumb sometimes; it can be nice to be underestimated. Either way, it's nice to hear that she's reconciled somewhat with her mother. Not that they were ever really apart in the first place, but she knows what you mean. Kinu says nothing, but you can see the gears turning in her head. |"I'm tired; I didn't even have very much energy to play today. Maybe an hour or two, tops. That's like, nothing at all." Hmm. Is this another of her plans to cajole you into giving her some more fruit? "Ehe, no. Seriously, [kinu.Dad], no." That's what someone who was planning something would say, but you'll let it slide for the moment. Why's she so tired? Kinu waves you off. "Just the same, only more of it. How does Mama get through these days without showing it on her face at all? I feel like my body's going to melt any moment. Like... like I'm going to just turn into a puddle and run downhill, or seep into the dirt." At least she now has a greater understanding of what Kiyoko goes through to raise them all, and with a smile to boot. That should help her appreciate her mother's efforts more, and maybe, just maybe, she won't work so much mischief on her mother. "Hmmm... I'll consider it deeply, [kinu.Dad]." |"I looooooove cuddling up to Mama!" Kinu exclaims, tugging at your [pc.armor] with her little hands. "Everyone wants to snuggle up to her, especially since she got so warm and boingy! We just turn into foxes and pile up until everyone just feels so fluffy and good!" Oh, you know full well how warm and comforting Kiyoko's embrace can be, especially since she's gotten more... boingy, as your daughter put it. "I will admit that I'm kinda jealous. But since I can be a den mother when I grow up, there's no doubt that I'll be getting even more warm and cuddly than Mama is right now! The foxy pile-ups I'm going to have with my children are going to be great!" Well, if nothing else, it'll be something to look forward to. "I still haven't figured out how Mama does it. But when I do — and I will, because I'm a smart girl — she'd better watch out!" |"I made some matcha for Mama this morning," Kinu tells you, beaming all the while. "She gave it a three out of ten." A three out of ten, and she's so happy about it? How harsh is Kiyoko usually? "Mama is very exacting about her tea. It's not just about the flavor, it's about..." your daughter scrunches up her face. "The visuals, the presentation, what you serve with it, even the tea set that you use. There're also a bunch of other things that matter, but I'm not going to bore you with the details, [kinu.Dad]." That might be the case, but given that she's a smart cookie she should have no problem recalling everything perfectly, right? "Nope, no problem. But see, I didn't use to care. Gulping down lukewarm tea straight from the pot was so much more fun than sitting down and making a whole ceremony out of it, hee hee." And yet she's started to care. "Ehe. I figured I owe Mama as much at this point... she gave me full marks for flavor, and nothing for everything else. That's why I got three out of ten. Then after she'd left and the pot had cooled, I gulped down everything and ate the leaves to boot." She did what? "Is there a problem, [kinu.Dad]? I wasn't going to let good tea go to waste." You sigh. No matter how intelligent your daughter might be, it's things like this that press the point that she's still a foxy child at heart. |"I asked Mama to do a divination on my future the other day." That's interesting. How did it turn out? "Ehe, Mama didn't want to do it for me." How come? "She said it's much more fun to not know what's coming at you... and even if I don't completely agree, I can tell where she's coming from." Hah. She's learning, all right. "Besides, when I thought about it, it wouldn't be that much use. Augury gets less precise the further ahead you look, so trying to figure out things when I'm all grown up wouldn't be of much use anyway." And out of pure curiosity, what did your little daughter want to know? Kinu sticks out her tongue at you. "Not telling!" ] ]'

rows.original: [kiyoko.numKits 4 8 16 32|[rand|"You know, [kinu.Dad], it was kinda lonely when it was just me and Mama, but that's not a problem anymore. I can usually find someone to play with now when I'm bored." To be fair, the decision wasn't yours alone, and given the way her mother thinks, she can expect a lot more siblings in the future. Kinu brightens at the thought, her ears perking up. "That's not too bad a proposition, [kinu.Dad]... eehee." |"Mama says that I have to be much better behaved here on out," Kinu grumps. " I'm supposed to be a role model for my siblings... if she lets me get away with things all the time, they'll be asking why Big Sis gets to do things they don't, and she doesn't want any of that." Kiyoko's not wrong, and she knows that. This is but a small responsibility compared to what she'll be asked to shoulder when she grows up; you're certain that she's capable of as much. "Boo... I'll just have to find somewhere quiet to laze about after lunch. But... but then if I walk that far out, I won't be in the mood to nap anymore... aww..." |"I'm so mad right now." Now, now. What happened to get your little fusspet all worked up? "So I was serving out the congee at breakfast, and one of my brothers said I gave him a little less. Like a complete dum-dum, I ladled out a little more for him, then one of my sisters says that she doesn't have as much. Then I keep on doling out the stuff until I catch on and start yelling for everyone to pipe down and eat... and when I go fill my own bowl there's only enough left for half a serving. Grrrr... I told Mama, and — hey, you're laughing, just like she did!" [pc.isDK|Sorry, but she did fall for it, and there's no denying it. At least it was a relatively minor prank; it'll be a good lesson for the future.|Sorry, you shouldn't have laughed. Still, this is one of the things she'll look back on with fondness when she's older.] Kinu makes an unhappy mewling sound and hugs herself. "Come on, [kinu.Dad], don't tease me... I think I might die from hunger before lunchtime comes around..." |"My brothers and sisters are always so curious about what I'm doing. I'll be putting together a charm or trying to do some painting, and then — bam! — I'll feel eyes on the back of my neck. They can never hide from Big Sis, I always know when they're around. It's like I can divine their presence without even needing to think about it!" Isn't that nice? It must be flattering to be so popular. "Ehe, I suppose. Being a star is hard work, I have to get out of the house to really be alone. It's fun for a little while, but constantly not being able to be with only myself really wears me out..." |"Our family is starting to get a little big..." That's true. "And by the looks of it, it's just going to get even bigger..." Her mother has every intention of making it so, yes. "But not every kitsune family is going to be as big as ours, Mama says. Only den mothers. Otherwise, there'd be too many of us in one place, and it'd be bad for the land." Now, where is she getting at with this train of thought? "Not much, [kinu.Dad]. Just thinking what it really means to be Big Sis. I can't shake off the feeling that I'm in over my head here." Well, she's not alone in this; she's got her mother and you, and most of all, she's a smart cookie, so it's up to her to figure something out. Which she will, you're sure. "Ehe..." ] |[rand|Does having to help take care of her brothers and sisters bother her, especially considering her mother's constantly popping out new ones? "Ehe, it's good training for the future." Kinu flicks a foxy ear your way, as if this answers everything. "That, and I'm learning the art of delegation from Mama. She delegates to me, and I delegate further down the line... it prevents me from being swamped." Still, it's a big responsibility for a child like her. "Now, [kinu.Dad], both you and me know that I'm not just any old kitsune kit." That remains to be seen. |"Usually, my brothers and sisters don't like having to do chores. They'd much rather go out to play, and I can't say I don't understand where they're coming from. Ask any of them to do any work and they get all sleepy and sluggish, but minutes later they're prancing about in the forest no problem." Ah, the vagaries of youth. The child who gets tired from mere minutes of walking manages to play outside all day without any problems whatsoever. "See, [kinu.Dad], it's all a matter of perspective. I tricked them into thinking their chores were games, and now they're much better at getting things done." Kinu thinks a moment, then grins and shrugs. "I can't say it's perfect, but it works far better than yelling at them would have." |"I don't like having to share the hot spring with my siblings. They're little foxes; you'd be more surprised if they didn't want to play in the water. "Yeah, okay, I like to play too, but not there of all places. What if something happened to her in the water and there wasn't anyone to help her? You've heard that people can get woozy and faint if they stay in too long. What if she drowned? Kinu plants her hands on her hips and pouts in the most adorable fashion. "Please, [kinu.Dad]. I'm eight years old, and smarter than that. Besides, I have a contingency going to let Mama know should any misfortune befall me." Overconfidence. That's how they get you in the end. Overconfidence. "Please, [kinu.Dad], don't tell Mama or anyone else. I just want some peace and quiet to enjoy the warm water and relax..." |"I found two of my brothers fighting over rice cakes yesterday... they couldn't decide who should get the last one, and tearing apart one of those things into equal halves is really hard because of how sticky they are." Kinu folds her arms and musters her sternest expression — which really isn't very much so. "It's utterly shameful, that's what it is. Fighting over food!" So what did she do? "I ate it myself," your daughter says, the smugness just dripping off her voice. "Since they couldn't be nice and sort it out themselves, neither of them was going to have it. I could see where they were coming from, though. Rice cakes taste pretty nice and have a really smooth texture." And she's sure she didn't just use her position as Big Sis to swipe it for herself? She couldn't have, say, given it to one of her other siblings? "[kinu.Dad]! That's... um... not true..." Reeeeeallly? "Um... oops...?" |"I like teaching my siblings things! Being a walking encyclopedia must be great, although she ought to keep in mind that she doesn't know everything in the world. "Yet. I know there's a whole world to explore, [kinu.Dad]. Mama keeps on talking about it." Humility, humility. Now, what sorts of things has she been teaching her brothers and sisters? "Oh, all sorts of things! But what they love most of all are the things I point out when we go play in the forest! Kinu nods so rapidly the little kitsune's head is a blur. "They're really good! There's this kind of grub that's as thick as a finger that you can find in old rotting bark, and it tastes really nutty when you skewer and roast it! People used to cook them in the past when they didn't have anything else to eat! Then there're those shiny beetles that crunch really well when you bite down on them, and the way they wiggle about on your tongue — what's the matter, [kinu.Dad]?" Does her mother know she's been eating bugs and teaching her siblings to do so to boot? Your daughter smiles up at you. "Mama knows that I've been reading about them..." Sigh. ] |[rand|"With so many brothers and sisters running around, I don't really bother separating out the clothes after doing laundry. Everyone wears about the same size, so they just grab what's appropriate and are off." She's got her own outfit, though... Kinu does a little twirl to better show off her yukata. "Of course! I'm Big Sister, after all. It's my duty to care so others don't have to, and as such, I need clothes befitting the station!" |Hey, there's something you need to ask... "Yes, [kinu.Dad]?" Kinu furrows her little brow. "I'm not exactly sure what you mean, [kinu.Dad]. Don't you remember all of us and our names?" No! No, you didn't mean that. It's just that, like you said, it can be hard to tell the difference between some of them at a glance. "Never had a problem myself," Kinu replies cheerily. "Maybe it's because I'm smart, maybe it's because I'm Big Sis, or maybe it's just because you're not a kitsune, [kinu.Dad]. Best to be careful, lest someone flatter their way into her heart someday. But for now, that was a very thoughtful thing she did for her siblings. "I'm a good girl, right?" Yes, yes. That she is. "Ehehe!" |"I do my little sister Kasumi's hair and tails every morning. If I didn't, she'd just run around all day looking like she just tumbled out of bed, and I won't have that. "It's not just important, it's a point of pride." Kinu puffs herself up. However, her grooming her sister's fur isn't going to impart any lessons in the long run. There has to be some way to coax her little sister into changing for the better, right? "Fine! Tell me!" "I'm not just any eight-year old kitsune, I'm Big Sis! I'm also [kinu.Dad]'s fusspet, but that's another thing. Since I'm doing good these days, do you think I deserve a reward?" "He's been following me around all day, hoping to repay the favor.
