rows.raw: " [kiyoko.numKits 4 8 16 32|[rand|"You know, [kinu.Dad], it was kinda lonely when it was just me and Mama, but that's not a problem anymore. I can usually find someone to play with now when I'm bored." To be fair, the decision wasn't yours alone, and given the way her mother thinks, she can expect a lot more siblings in the future. Kinu brightens at the thought, her ears perking up. "That's not too bad a proposition, [kinu.Dad]... eehee." |"Mama says that I have to be much better behaved here on out," Kinu grumps. " I'm supposed to be a role model for my siblings... if she lets me get away with things all the time, they'll be asking why Big Sis gets to do things they don't, and she doesn't want any of that." Kiyoko's not wrong, and she knows that. This is but a small responsibility compared to what she'll be asked to shoulder when she grows up; you're certain that she's capable of as much. "Boo... I'll just have to find somewhere quiet to laze about after lunch. But... but then if I walk that far out, I won't be in the mood to nap anymore... aww..." |"I'm so mad right now." Now, now. What happened to get your little fusspet all worked up? "So I was serving out the congee at breakfast, and one of my brothers said I gave him a little less. Like a complete dum-dum, I ladled out a little more for him, then one of my sisters says that she doesn't have as much. Then I keep on doling out the stuff until I catch on and start yelling for everyone to pipe down and eat... and when I go fill my own bowl there's only enough left for half a serving. Grrrr... I told Mama, and — hey, you're laughing, just like she did!" [pc.isDK|Sorry, but she did fall for it, and there's no denying it. At least it was a relatively minor prank; it'll be a good lesson for the future.|Sorry, you shouldn't have laughed. Still, this is one of the things she'll look back on with fondness when she's older.] Kinu makes an unhappy mewling sound and hugs herself. "Come on, [kinu.Dad], don't tease me... I think I might die from hunger before lunchtime comes around..." |"My brothers and sisters are always so curious about what I'm doing. I'll be putting together a charm or trying to do some painting, and then — bam! — I'll feel eyes on the back of my neck. They can never hide from Big Sis, I always know when they're around. It's like I can divine their presence without even needing to think about it!" Isn't that nice? It must be flattering to be so popular. "Ehe, I suppose. Being a star is hard work, I have to get out of the house to really be alone. It's fun for a little while, but constantly not being able to be with only myself really wears me out..." |"Our family is starting to get a little big..." That's true. "And by the looks of it, it's just going to get even bigger..." Her mother has every intention of making it so, yes. "But not every kitsune family is going to be as big as ours, Mama says. Only den mothers. Otherwise, there'd be too many of us in one place, and it'd be bad for the land." Now, where is she getting at with this train of thought? "Not much, [kinu.Dad]. Just thinking what it really means to be Big Sis. I can't shake off the feeling that I'm in over my head here." Well, she's not alone in this; she's got her mother and you, and most of all, she's a smart cookie, so it's up to her to figure something out. Which she will, you're sure. "Ehe..." ] |[rand|Does having to help take care of her brothers and sisters bother her, especially considering her mother's constantly popping out new ones? "Ehe, it's good training for the future." Kinu flicks a foxy ear your way, as if this answers everything. "That, and I'm learning the art of delegation from Mama. She delegates to me, and I delegate further down the line... it prevents me from being swamped." Still, it's a big responsibility for a child like her. "Now, [kinu.Dad], both you and me know that I'm not just any old kitsune kit." That remains to be seen. |"Usually, my brothers and sisters don't like having to do chores. They'd much rather go out to play, and I can't say I don't understand where they're coming from. Ask any of them to do any work and they get all sleepy and sluggish, but minutes later they're prancing about in the forest no problem." Ah, the vagaries of youth. The child who gets tired from mere minutes of walking manages to play outside all day without any problems whatsoever. "See, [kinu.Dad], it's all a matter of perspective. I tricked them into thinking their chores were games, and now they're much better at getting things done." Kinu thinks a moment, then grins and shrugs. "I can't say it's perfect, but it works far better than yelling at them would have." |"I don't like having to share the hot spring with my siblings. They always splash and play about in the water; it's impolite and undignified to create such a ruckus in what should be a place of serene comfort." They're little foxes; you'd be more surprised if they didn't want to play in the water. "Yeah, okay, I like to play too, but not there of all places. It's gotten bad enough that I have to slip out at night to get a good soak without anyone disturbing me." Isn't that dangerous? What if something happened to her in the water and there wasn't anyone to help her? You've heard that people can get woozy and faint if they stay in too long. What if she drowned? Kinu plants her hands on her hips and pouts in the most adorable fashion. "Please, [kinu.Dad]. I'm eight years old, and smarter than that. Besides, I have a contingency going to let Mama know should any misfortune befall me." Overconfidence. That's how they get you in the end. Overconfidence. "Please, [kinu.Dad], don't tell Mama or anyone else. I just want some peace and quiet to enjoy the warm water and relax..." |"I found two of my brothers fighting over rice cakes yesterday... they couldn't decide who should get the last one, and tearing apart one of those things into equal halves is really hard because of how sticky they are." Kinu folds her arms and musters her sternest expression — which really isn't very much so. "It's utterly shameful, that's what it is. Fighting over food!" So what did she do? "I ate it myself," your daughter says, the smugness just dripping off her voice. "Since they couldn't be nice and sort it out themselves, neither of them was going to have it. I could see where they were coming from, though. Rice cakes taste pretty nice and have a really smooth texture." And she's sure she didn't just use her position as Big Sis to swipe it for herself? She couldn't have, say, given it to one of her other siblings? "[kinu.Dad]! That's... um... not true..." Reeeeeallly? "Um... oops...?" |"I like teaching my siblings things! They're all so amazed when I point out useful little facts that they didn't know and praise me for being smart like Mama does!" Being a walking encyclopedia must be great, although she ought to keep in mind that she doesn't know everything in the world. "Yet. I know there's a whole world to explore, [kinu.Dad]. Mama keeps on talking about it." Humility, humility. Now, what sorts of things has she been teaching her brothers and sisters? "Oh, all sorts of things! But what they love most of all are the things I point out when we go play in the forest! Like the leaves of that plant are good for fevers, where to find the big mushrooms that grow between the roots of oak trees, and how to catch yummy bugs!" Yummy... bugs? Kinu nods so rapidly the little kitsune's head is a blur. "They're really good! There's this kind of grub that's as thick as a finger that you can find in old rotting bark, and it tastes really nutty when you skewer and roast it! People used to cook them in the past when they didn't have anything else to eat! Then there're those shiny beetles that crunch really well when you bite down on them, and the way they wiggle about on your tongue — what's the matter, [kinu.Dad]?" Does her mother know she's been eating bugs and teaching her siblings to do so to boot? Your daughter smiles up at you. "Mama knows that I've been reading about them..." Sigh. ] |[rand|"With so many brothers and sisters running around, I don't really bother separating out the clothes after doing laundry. Everyone wears about the same size, so they just grab what's appropriate and are off." She's got her own outfit, though... Kinu does a little twirl to better show off her yukata. "Of course! I'm Big Sister, after all. It's my duty to care so others don't have to, and as such, I need clothes befitting the station!" |Hey, there's something you need to ask... "Yes, [kinu.Dad]?" She sure has a lot of brothers and sisters, right? Yet she can always tell them apart at a glance. Just how does she manage to do it, especially when they're all so similarly dressed? Kinu furrows her little brow. "I'm not exactly sure what you mean, [kinu.Dad]. Don't you remember all of us and our names?" No! No, you didn't mean that. It's just that, like you said, it can be hard to tell the difference between some of them at a glance. "Never had a problem myself," Kinu replies cheerily. "Maybe it's because I'm smart, maybe it's because I'm Big Sis, or maybe it's just because you're not a kitsune, [kinu.Dad]. It can be hard to tell the fine differences between people who look kinda alike, so you've got to pay extra attention." |So, what exactly are her duties as Big Sis? "Many things! Too many to count! Mama says I must be prepared for any eventuality, and I agree with her!" All right, perhaps you could rephrase that. What are her more prominent duties? "I oversee and delegate, that is most important! Then I also help serve everyone at mealtimes, and make sure everyone scrapes into the pig bin properly! I also help Mama lead in our daily devotions to Keros, and replace the charms when they wear out! I am also responsible for making sure everyone is accounted for when I give my daily report to Mama, and..." Right, right. Kinu gives you a wink and swish of her three tails. "If you don't want the answer to a question, [kinu.Dad], maybe it's better not to ask in the first place. Oh, and I'm not allowed to use magic while doing any of these, otherwise I won't learn anything from it. It's said that play is supposed to be training for grown-up duties, but I don't seem to be getting much play in these days... or at least, as much as I used to..." |"I asked Mama to help me make candy for everyone yesterday!" Wow, really? "It was pretty fun! I used a spell so I wouldn't accidentally burn myself, then Mama got a big pot and we filled it with all kinds of nuts and things! Then we boiled syrup until it got thick, and I had to keep stirring it with a big ladle so it wouldn't burn! Stirring is tiring." Doesn't she hate candy, though? "Ehe, yep." Your daughter puts her forefingers together and sheepishly shifts her eyes from side to side, ears wiggling all the while. "I kinda almost puked a couple times, since the smell filled the kitchen... "But it was worth it! We poured out the syrupy stuff and let it cool, then cut it up and gave all of my brothers and sisters a piece! Then they all thanked and praised me, and all of it made me really warm and giddy! Hee hee!" She really is a sucker for praise, isn't she? Best to be careful, lest someone flatter their way into her heart someday. But for now, that was a very thoughtful thing she did for her siblings. "I'm a good girl, right?" Yes, yes. That she is. "Ehehe!" |"I do my little sister Kasumi's hair and tails every morning. If I didn't, she'd just run around all day looking like she just tumbled out of bed, and I won't have that. If I can manage to keep up my appearance while rolling down hills and climbing trees, anyone can!" Keeping her hair and fur neat and glossy is important to her, isn't it? "It's not just important, it's a point of pride." Kinu puffs herself up. "Sure, you might think that there's no point in propriety when you're all alone, [kinu.Dad], but it's what we do when we think no one's watching that really shows who we are." She has a point there. However, her grooming her sister's fur isn't going to impart any lessons in the long run. There has to be some way to coax her little sister into changing for the better, right? "Fine! Tell me!" Oh, but if you did, she'd learn nothing. "Hmph..." ] |[rand|"I have so many brothers and sisters now!" Indeed, and thanks in no small part to her mother's... ah... enthusiasm on this issue. Judging by the big smile your little fusspet has on her face, she doesn't seem to mind in the slightest, yes? "Ehe, it's okay. Having to help Mama take care of everyone is going to teach me responsibility and managing large groups of people. That is what I'll need to do in the future as a den mother. Maybe I'll even have more children than Mama!" You shudder. Ye gods, the girl's ambitious, if nothing else. Kiyoko's got a pretty solid head start on her, but if she's determined to see this through... it's hard to think of your daughter doing what he mother does. "Sure, trying to play with a lot of people at once tires me out really quickly. But I know where to go if I want a quick nap, the same way Mama sends us all out to play when she wants to be alone for a bit. It just requires you be an excellent manager and to learn how to properly entrust people with delegated authority." Those are some awfully big words for an eight-year old to use... "I'm not just any eight-year old kitsune, I'm Big Sis! I'm also [kinu.Dad]'s fusspet, but that's another thing. Since I'm doing good these days, do you think I deserve a reward?" Ah, some things never change. |"Since there're so many of us, we're all good at different things. Seems like there isn't a skill or job that one of my brothers or sisters isn't talented in. I, of course, am the super-duper best!" Oh, really? Kinu nods enthusiastically. "See, like it's great to be talented at things. But it's really great to be talented at learning things, because then you can be great at everything! So long as you put in the effort, that is. Some days, I'd rather nap." If she's got that much potential, she'd better not waste it. "Hee hee, how do you think so many of my brothers and sisters know what they do? I taught them, of course! Teaching is a great way to reinforce what you yourself have learnt, it's great! You should try it sometime, [kinu.Dad]!" |"One of my brothers came up this morning and asked really nicely if I could darn a hole in his sock for him. So I did! He was really thankful, and that made me happy as well!" It's nice to know that she's making herself useful to everyone, not just her mother. "I don't know why, especially since I'd have been pretty annoyed at anyone who asked before, but it's all good. Still, there's one thing that's bothering me..." And what would that be? "He's been following me around all day, hoping to repay the favor. I know we are commanded by Lord Keros to pay back any genuine kindness shown to us, but maybe that's taking it a little too far... if anything, he's doing the exact opposite by annoying me, but I still haven't the heart to tell him to go away." On one hand, patience is a virtue. On the other, she needs to stand up for herself. |"So, I heard Mama make a really odd joke..." Yes? "She said that she's had enough kids to field both sides of a sporting event, if not more. I'm not exactly sure why this is supposed to be funny, but it had her in stitches for a good while. Having this many siblings is a thing I take quite seriously." Perhaps, but it's also good to be able to see the funny side of things. A little levity goes a long way, especially on the longer days. "I don't get it..." |"When I look back on every day, it really strikes me as to how well I'm doing," Kinu tells you proudly. "I didn't really realize it until I put things down to paper, but there's sooooo much work involved in feeding, clothing, wrangling and instructing everyone. Mama calls it logistics, and says that it's good practice for what I'll be doing later in life." Is it? "Must be, because I don't really notice it anymore. I just gotta say a few words, and things kinda run by themselves now that everyone knows what they have to do." Your daughter reaches up and scratches a large, furry ear. "It's all one big mess, but it's an orderly mess, and I don't think I'd have it any other way. Did you know how much everyone eats every day? It surprised me when I sat down to do the numbers." ] ]"

rows.original: [rand|"Hey, don't tell Mama that I told you, but she used to be terrible at cooking." Did she? The way she's so proficient in the kitchen, you'd never have guessed. "Yep! When she was younger, Mama was so busy studying magic and divination that she didn't have time for anything else. Besides, as the den mother's firstborn daughter, she always had other people around to do the cooking for her, so she never quite needed it... all that changed, of course, and she suddenly had a lot of time on her hands and no one around to prepare meals." And what of little Kinu? Will she learn to cook, too? Kinu broadens her stance a little and gives you the most serious look her adorable round face can muster. "[kinu.Dad], I will learn all the things. It would be a shame to waste my inheritance, wouldn't it?" Haha. There's a clever girl. Kinu preens at the praise, looking very pleased with herself. |"There's an underground river that flows beneath the roots of the home tree; we have a basement so we can get to it. The water there's really cold and clear, so we use it for all sorts of things! Not bathing, though! Hot water is for bathing, cold water is for drinking! "Oh! Also, we put fresh-picked veggies from the fields in netted boxes, then put those into the stream to chill! Veggies taste so much better when they've been chilled with cold clean water!" |"Did you know that dried persimmons are really yummy? You wouldn't know it, especially since they're really sour when fresh. But then there's something about the drying process that takes out all that tartness and leaves only a delicious fruity flavor. It's amazing, hee hee!" |"Noon is the most awful time of day," your daughter declares. This ought to be good. You're all ears. "Mm-hm. My tummy gets growly and rumbly, then I feel tired and don't want to do anything but wait for lunch. But then after I've eaten, I feel all nice and full, and don't want to do anything but nap in the sun. Of course, there's always chores to be done around then, so I don't get to do any of that... and then by the time I can go out to play or nap, the feeling's passed." Very convincing, except for the fact that you know that eating's not much of a necessity on the astral plane, and that Kiyoko mostly does mealtimes to give structure to her day. Kinu huffs and folds her arms, sulking. "Maybe it is to you and Mama, but I get awfully hungry..." |"I like it when [kinu.Dad] visits because I get petted lots!" Ha! You reach down and tousle Kinu's hair, ruffling her large ears, and the little kitsune squeals in delight. Closing her eyes and bowing her head towards you, Kinu luxuriates in the simple bliss of affectionate human contact. "See? See?" She's as sensitive as her mother is, that's for sure; you have no doubt she'll make some other kitsune very happy when she grows up. Kinu looks a little disappointed when you finish petting her, but settles back with a wiggle of her ears and swish of her three tails. "I like it when [kinu.Dad] visits because I get petted lots!" She already said that. "I know!" |"Growing taller takes so long," Kinu grumps. Let's guess... she wants to be taller because then it'll be easier for her to reach the peaches on the higher branches? "I'm not saying anything..." She knows that there are other kinds of fruit which don't grow on trees, right? Maybe she could try planting a berry bush or two? Or how about some melons? Those are pretty good and grow close to the ground... "I'll think about it. Mama gets mad with me if I dig in the dirt too much." |"Are you going to play with Mama again today?" You're going to see her, yes. After all, you wouldn't come all this way onto the astral plane and leave without paying Kiyoko a visit, would you? "I didn't mean visit, I meant play." Now... what exactly does your foxy little darling daughter mean by play? "I'm not exactly sure, but I know you have a lot of fun because Mama only raises her voice like that when she's enjoying herself. It's okay, I like to play alone or just with someone else, too. Too many people at once tires me out quickly." Kinu thinks a moment. "Every time Mama is done playing with you, she becomes very happy for days on end... I'd like to see her happy more often. That's another way how I know you have lots of fun playing together." Uh, you most definitely do. "I like playing with you too, [kinu.Dad]." Okay, this conversation just got awkward. Time to change the subject. |"No one will play any board games with me," Kinu grumps, the little kitsune's ears drooping. Oh? Why's that? [kiyoko.numKits 0 2|A sigh. "Mama's always busy with... whatever it is she does. Half the time I see her, it's for lessons; the other half, it's for mealtimes and scolding me for getting myself all dirty. Well, if she doesn't want me to be dirty, maybe she should take a little while to play with me, right? Otherwise, I'm just going to dig in the dirt or find some peaches, because playing both sides of go gets really boring after a while..." |Kinu looks away, unwilling to meet your gaze. "My siblings won't play with me; they say I always win at go and shogi, and that it's not fun if they haven't even a chance at coming out ahead." You can understand where they're coming from, yes. Can't blame them for not wanting to throw themselves against an insurmountable wall like that. "Nor is it fun for me to walk all over them and win so easily. Mama's the only one who's capable of putting up any real opposition, and she can't play with me all the time, so I'm right back where I started." ] Well, now that you're here to visit, maybe you can entertain your fluffy daughter for a bit before going to be with her mother. It might not necessarily be a board game, but you definitely can spare a little time to play with her — after all, as you understand things, the passage of time in the astral plane doesn't quite completely map to that in the waking world. "I would really like that, [kinu.Dad]." [kiyoko.numKits 4|Although there is one thing... "What is it?" Why doesn't she coach her siblings in those games? Kinu blinks. Look, she herself admits that defeating an opponent who can barely fight back is boring, right? Clearly, the thing to do is to help her siblings get better, like a farmer fattening calves for the slaughter. That way her eventual triumph will be truly fulfilling, instead of the meaningless walkovers she's been having to date. As if on cue, Kinu's ears start wiggling. "Ooooooh. That's not a bad idea, [kinu.Dad]..." Of course, there's always the danger of the students surpassing the master, which is why she's got to improve as well. But she's a smart little thing; you're sure she can manage it. ] |"So the other day, I was sorting through where Mama keeps the spices..." That sounds interesting. Did she discover anything of note? "Yes! Yes! I discovered wasabi. Have you tasted the stuff, [kinu.Dad]? It's super-duper amazing!" No, not yet. Can she tell you what it tastes like? "Ehe. Kinda sorta..." Oh, from the furrowed brow on your little fusspet, this is going to be a good one. "See, [kinu.Dad], I was going to try, so I put a big whole dollop of it on my tongue, and then my tongue went numb. Then Mama noticed what I was doing, and made me wash out my mouth... my tongue's still numb, though. It feels kinda funny." Hah. Whatever this wasabi thing is, it's probably not something to be eaten directly, especially if it's a condiment of some sort. "I dunno about that, [kinu.Dad]. It's really great." ]
rows.translation: [rand|嘿，别告诉妈妈是我告诉你的，但她以前做饭可真不怎么样。 她真的会吗？看她做饭那么熟练，根本没人会想到这一点。 没错！她小时候，妈妈一直忙于研究魔法和占卜，根本没时间做其他事情。而且，作为族长的长女，总是有人帮她做饭，所以她其实从来不需要自己动手……当然，后来情况完全变了，她突然有了很多空闲时间，却再也没有人帮她准备饭菜了。 那小堇呢？她也会学会做饭吗？ 堇稍微调整了一下站姿，然后用她那张可爱的圆脸露出了最认真的表情。 "[kinu.Dad]我会学习的。 所有这些事情浪费我的遗产未免太可惜了，不是吗？ 哈哈，真是个聪明的女孩。 绮奴听到这样的赞美后，显得非常得意，脸上洋溢着满足的笑容。 |在房子所在那棵树的根部下面，有一条地下河流；因为我们有地下室，所以能够到达那里。那里的水非常寒冷且清澈，所以我们用它来做各种各样的事情！不过不是用来洗澡的！热水是用来洗澡的，冷水则是用来饮用的！ 哦！我们还把刚从田里采摘的蔬菜装进网袋里，然后把它们放到小溪里冷却！用干净冷水冷却过的蔬菜味道会好很多呢！ |你知道吗？干柿子其实非常美味哦！刚开始吃的时候可能不会觉得，因为新鲜的柿子味道其实挺酸的。但经过晾干的过程后，那些酸味全都消失了，只剩下美味的果香，真是太神奇了，嘿嘿！ |中午是一天中最糟糕的时刻。 你的女儿宣布道： “这肯定很有趣。大家都洗耳恭听吧。 嗯，没错。我的肚子会开始咕咕叫，然后我就觉得浑身无力，什么都不想做，只想等着吃午饭。但吃完饭后，我又会感到很满足、很饱，然后就只想在阳光下小睡一会儿。当然，这个时候总是有各种家务要做，所以我根本没时间做那些事……等到我可以出去玩或者小睡的时候，那种感觉就已经过去了。 说得很有道理，不过你知道在星界层面，进食其实并不是什么必需的事情。而清子之所以会安排用餐时间，只是为了给自己的日常生活增添一些规律罢了。” 绮奴生气地哼了一声，双臂交叉在胸前，显得很不高兴。 也许这对你和妈妈来说是这样，但 我 饿得厉害…… |我喜欢……的时候。 [kinu.Dad] 人们会来看我，因为大家都很喜欢抚摸我！ 哈！你伸手部揉了揉绮奴的头发，弄乱了她那大耳朵，小狐妖高兴地尖叫起来。绮奴闭上眼睛，把头靠在你的身上，尽情享受这种人类给予的关爱与温暖。 看到了吗？看到了吧？ 她肯定和她母亲一样敏感；毫无疑问，等她长大后，一定会让其他狐妖们也非常开心。当你抚摸完绮奴后，她看起来有点失望，但很快就会摇摇耳朵、甩动三条尾巴，重新放松下来。 我喜欢……的时候。 [kinu.Dad] 人们会来看我，因为大家都很喜欢抚摸我！ 她已经这么说了。 我知道！ |长高真的需要花费很多时间啊 长," 绮奴嘟起了嘴。 我们来猜猜看……她是不是想长得高一点，这样就能更容易地拿到高树枝上的桃子了？ 我什么都没说…… 她知道还有其他种类的水果并不是长在树上的，对吧？也许她可以试着种一两株浆果灌木？或者种一些瓜类植物怎么样？那些果实味道很好，而且生长在离地面不高的地方…… 我再考虑考虑吧。要是我太爱玩泥巴，妈妈会生我的气的。 |你今天还要和妈妈一起玩吗？ 你确实会见到她的。毕竟，你大老远来到这个星界，总不会不去拜访一下清子吧？ 我并不是说去参观，而是想玩游戏。 现在……你那个狡黠可爱的小女儿到底是什么意思呢？ 进行游戏? rows.original: [rand|"Mama is teaching me her mother tongue. It's very different from the one that we usually speak in, [kinu.Dad]. Very different, but I'm managing." Now that's interesting. [pc.bg scholar noblescion courtesan|You did have the opportunity to learn some foreign languages in the past, but with Belharan being the general trade tongue of the continent you didn't really see the need. After all, anyone who didn't know Belharan wasn't worth talking to, as the saying went.|You didn't have the chance to learn any foreign languages, and even if you did they wouldn't have been much use in the life you led back then.] Still, you can see why Kiyoko would insist on her daughter learning her mother tongue, and not just for the purposes of spellcrafting. "Kitsune aside, I don't think there'll be anyone who speaks or writes it once we get out of here..." But it's nevertheless important for understanding where she came from. That, and it can be fun to have a conversation in front of others who can't understand the language. It makes you feel like you're in a secret club, doesn't it? Kinu brightens. "Yeah... when you put it that way, it kind of sounds fun, [kinu.Dad]. Now, if only there were people who didn't understand the kitsune tongue to try this on — you excepted, of course." You'll just have to work harder on that "getting everyone out of here" thing, won't you? "Yep! Although no need to rush, I suppose. After all, Mama tells me that time doesn't flow the same way here it does outside..." |"I hate swimming," your daughter declares with an unmistakable note of finality. Does that mean that she can't swim, she won't swim, she doesn't know how to swim, or some combination of the above? Kinu pouts and plants her hands on her hips. "Eh. I can swim, [kinu.Dad]. A bit. And then I don't want to any more." That's not very reassuring. What if she fell into a river someday and couldn't swim back out? "Hot springs are okay. Playing in the shallows is okay. What's not okay is cold water that goes in over my head. It gets in my ears and saps all my strength. Seriously, [kinu.Dad]. Less than a minute in that kind of water, and I might as well be a log." One way or the other, this is rather concerning. The danger posed to her from large bodies of water aside, this refusal to even try to overcome this weakness is rather uncharacteristic of Kinu. Maybe you should speak to her mother about this. A sniff. "Do whatever you want, [kinu.Dad]. It doesn't change the fact that it is what it is." Maybe, but you'd like to understand the situation better, if nothing else. |"Mama says that it's vital for me to develop a steady and organized mind that isn't prone to panic. Only then will I be ready to deal with large numbers of screaming, crying, mischievous kits, all of whom will do their best to drive me to my wits' end." Amusingly enough, the way Kiyoko's training her for that is to have her daughter deal with large numbers of screaming, crying, mischievous kits, all of whom will do their best to drive her to her wits' end. In a controlled setting, of course. When she has kits of her own, she won't be able to run crying to her mother whenever a problem that's too big for her to handle crops up. "Ehe. Or maybe I will, anyway. Mama does tell me stories from when she was a girl." Maybe you'll even get to hear them someday. But back to the point — Kinu is a level-headed little thing most of the time, which is more than what you can say for some of the other kits. There's nothing like having to deal with utter chaos on a daily basis to hone one's mental strength. "Ehe, it feels good to be praised. Although if I don't cry that often... when I do cry, people will think I'm faking it to earn sympathy, since it's so out character for me. Maybe I should do it a bit more, or at least fake it?" Oh dear. Whatever are you going to do with her? |"I don't think I'm too bad at cooking, [kinu.Dad]." Now, what brought this up? "Well, for some time now I've been helping Mama in the kitchen, and I can do some simple meals — nothing fancy like what Mama can cook up, yet. And while everything seems fine when I taste the end result myself, [kiyoko.numKits 3 |my brothers and sisters always balk whenever I serve up something I've prepared. Is there something I'm missing, or is my sense of taste just off?" Has she tried asking them exactly why they dislike her food? Kinu shrugs. "I've tried, but they're all just too polite to tell Big Sister when she asks. Either that, or they're afraid I'll take umbrage if they criticise me." |Mama always manages to find fault with the dish, and is able to tell me exactly why. Is there something I'm missing, or is my sense of taste just off?" ] Heh. There are drawbacks to being her mother's right hand, it seems. Well, if she's going to try preparing an actual dish for you — not just roasting chestnuts and mushrooms over a fire — you'd be more than willing to help. With the way things are, though, you suspect it's not about the taste or the presentation, but something else that's possibly unrelated to the food. This is a good exercise in discreetly gathering information if you ever saw one; best to start small with these things. |"I'm doing excellently in my spellcrafting studies." Oh? And who's the judge of that? "Mama, of course. That, and when I do fail at it, I tend to do so in rather spectacular and obvious ways that don't leave me any room to rationalise away my mistakes." That's... one way to put it. [pc.bg arcanist scholar|You've learned enough about these things to know that the most miniscule spell gone wrong can have the most... obvious effects.|While you haven't had much history with all things arcane, you'd like to think you know enough to figure out your daughter isn't exaggerating.] It's a good thing that her mother insists on all the proper precautions before giving lessons. "My calligraphy is perfect, if I may say so," Kinu continues, turning up her little nose in the air. "That, and the actual physical assembly of the scroll's components. What I'd really like to see, though..." Yes? "...Is some foreign magic. Mama tells me people in your part of the world use things like staves and totems as spell foci, [kinu.Dad]. The underlying principles may be the same, but I really want to see the forms in their proper context, take them apart to see what makes them work." Now that's an idea. Maybe you should drop in the next time they have a lesson... if you can time your arrival right, that is. |"Mama sure is teaching me a lot of things... she wants to impart all that she knows to me so that I can teach my brothers and sisters, too!" Is she okay with this? Kinu looks a little uncertain, but nods. "There's no better way to reinforce what you've learned than teaching it to someone else." In that case, she needs to be more confident in what she's learned. Book teaching will only go so far, after all; experience will take her the rest of the way. That being said, you're sure that she'll get better at it with time. "I hope so, [kinu.Dad]. But I'll do my best nevertheless!" Best is one thing. Whether it's sufficient is another. |"It seems like I inherited Mama's talent for magic." [pc.bg acolyte scholar|And yours as well, given your training and background. |Along with most of her other fetching qualities, you note. ] Kinu huffs. "I can only hope so. Mama says we'll only know for sure when I get older, although I'm not certain what she means by that. Either way, I seem to be really really good with magic." Why then, might she cast a spell for you, perhaps show you what she's learned? "Hee hee, of course!" Kinu balls her hands and waves them about in the air. "I cast fist!" Umm... "Sorry. That was a lot funnier when I went over it in my head." A lot of things are, you tell Kinu, tweaking the little kitsune's downcast ears. Maybe she ought to save that demonstration for when her mother's around. "Aww, boo. There is one thing I really want to learn, though, and Mama won't teach me..." Oh? "I wanna learn how to grasp things from afar." Uh, no. Both she and you know that she'll pick the peach grove clean the moment she learns that trick. Both you are Kiyoko are standing together on this point. "Awww..." Maybe when she's older and better able to control her appetites. |While you have little doubt that Kinu's mental faculties are being developed under her mother's careful supervision, does she get any physical training? "Hmm..." Kinu looks a little unsure at that. "Mama says I get enough exercise with all the running around and climbing trees I do..." It's not just the exercise. It's the way she handles herself. Kinu is quick to catch on. "Do you mean you want me to learn how to handle weapons like you do, [kinu.Dad]?" Hey, you didn't say anything about that — she brought that one up herself. You'll have to see the extent of her physical abilities, and it's not likely that she'll be able to do much while this young. But there's always room for working on her constitution and stamina even at a young age. You don't want a frail daughter by any means, after all. Kinu huffs. "Do I look frail to you, [kinu.Dad]? I'm not made out of porcelain, after all. Maybe I should dig around in the dirt more." Maybe she should do just that — after she learns a spell to clean herself up so Kiyoko doesn't have to bemoan a dirty daughter. |Does she ever forget anything she's learned? It's no good filling one's head with things if it's all going to flow right out again like trying to fill a sieve with water. Kinu considers the question deeply, her kitsune instincts no doubt warning her of a potential snare here. Eventually, she shakes her head and gives you a weak smile. "Um... no?" Is she sure? She never forgets anything? "Yes, [kinu.Dad]!" Good, good. Since she's got such an excellent memory, you'll take it that any misbehavior on her part is wholly deliberate, instead of her simply having forgotten to be good in the heat of the moment. Kinu's ears fold forward, and she pouts. "Aw, boo..." |"Mama is putting me on what she calls a 'classical education.' I'm not exactly sure what that means, but it's not for lack of trying, that's for sure." You'll trust Kiyoko with these things — she was trained from childhood to see to the raising of children, after all. But what does your daughter learn all day? "A whole bunch of things from where Mama came from, which is very far away!" And she's not bothered by the fact that she's learning subjects from a land she might never see? "Don't be silly, [kinu.Dad]. I have to know where I came from, if I'm going to figure out where I'm going. Besides, I'm going to live a decently long time. Who's to say I won't be able to make the trip?" Well, if she has that much confidence in herself, there's no reason she wouldn't be able to eventually do so. |"Mama has been trying to teach me the poetry of the place where she came from..." [pc.bg scholar noblescion|You nod. Much can be inferred about a people and their values from the literature they hold dear. You yourself had the opportunity to study some old Belharan poetry during your younger days, thanks to your position in society; regardless of the subject matter, it offered insights into the way people of that time went about their lives and what they thought important. |Literature's not really your thing, but you're not going to let your own lack of understanding get in the way of your daughter's education. ] "I keep on forgetting that haiku poetry is different from traditional waka poetry. Waka poetry has verses in five, seven, five, seven and seven syllables, and is always on the subject of people or scenery. Haiku poetry verses are in five, seven, and five syllables, and they always tout the beauty of the seasons with required seasonal words. Then Mama gets mad at me for not recalling the difference..." Wait, didn't she just remember — Kinu blinks, realization dawning upon your daughter's face. "Oh. Ehe. Maybe you should help me study sometime, [kinu.Dad]... I might do better if you're around." Or maybe she never forgot it at all, and just couldn't bring it to mind until given sufficient incentive. |[kinu.kinuWeapon| [rand| "Mama is so amazing when she goes through the forms with her naginata. Her steps and motions are so dignified and flowing, she looks like a fire dancing in the hearth. I know I was a bit reluctant when I first began learning it from her... but seriously, [kinu.Dad], after you've seen enough of that you really, really start to appreciate the naginata for what it is." After what happened, you're glad to see that she's having a more positive attitude about learning a martial art. Still, it's important not to overdo it, okay? She's still young and you don't want her to get sick again; her mother was worried enough the first time. Kinu bites her lip and shifts her eyes from side to side. "I don't want to be sick like that again, either. It wasn't nice." That's making an understatement of the grossest degree. "For the time being, Mama's keeping me on the practice one she made out of bamboo so I can do the forms easily. She says she'll graduate me to a proper naginata when I'm stronger in my arms." That's perfectly fine. It'll be some years before she'll actually need to put what she's learning here into practice anyways — she'll no longer be a child at that point. | "The more I learn about the history of the naginata and its meaning to the kitsune people, [kinu.Dad], the more I feel inspired to get better at wielding one. You were right that day — knowing the whys and wherefores has given me a greater appreciation for the weapon." That's great to hear. "Isn't it? Even when I'm holding the practice naginata Mama made for me, I can feel a connection to the den mothers and matrons of old who defended their homes with one of these. I may never visit the land where she came from, but I feel braver already just imagining myself as one of them. Even Mama who doesn't favor it as a weapon still knows the forms; they're something that's handed down from mother to daughter. "As they say, this is an art with history, and I'm enjoying it more and more." You pet Kinu on the head, and your daughter squeals in delight as you ruffle her fur. On your part, you're glad that she took your words so deeply to heart. She just has to remember to pace herself and not make her mother worry by falling sick again, okay? "Okay!" ] | [rand| "Mama says I may never be able to use another bow besides the hankyu. It's not just the draw strength of the bow, it's the sheer size..." Sure, Kinu might be a petite thing, but isn't it a little too early to say how tall she'll eventually be in the future? "Oh come on, [kinu.Dad]. By the looks of it, I'll be even tinier than Mama is when I'm grown-up. There's no need to not be realistic about things." Ah, such fatalism from one so young, and especially from one so usually cheerful at that. Kinu sniffs. "Back to the point, [kinu.Dad]. I think it fits me, anyway. It's small and compact, but there's a lot of energy in the bowstring. I can't quite imagine me doing any of that with a bigger one... with the hankyu, I feel pretty quick and nimble." Can she reliably hit things, though? "Yeeeah..." Kinu looks a little sheepish and grinds her toes against the dirt. "I'm working on that part." | Say... maybe it's just your imagination, but has Kinu gained a little more bulk in her arms? Maybe not since the last time you saw her, but she's definitely changed from how you remember her from a while back. "Eh, you're not wrong, [kinu.Dad]. Mama's had me working out my arms, giving me more physical chores from day to day. Nowadays, she shoos me out of the house if she catches me loafing about indoors. 'Go play outside!'." Hmm. It's probably not a good idea to bulk up too much when one's as young as she is, but she oughtn't worry; she'd have to actually work out pretty hard to raise any concern. Why this, though? "Well, after I took ill... both you and Mama were quite worried about me." Yes. It was rather upsetting. You take it Kiyoko's found a decent way to develop her daughter's arm strength; it certainly looks like she's been getting results, at any rate. "Ehe. At least I can draw the bowstring without my arms shaking all over the place. That's a good start, isn't it?" Indeed. Now, she has to try and actually hit something instead of all her arrows going wild... "Like I said, [kinu.Dad], I'm working on it..." ] ] |[kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0| [rand| "Learning how to keep my brothers and sisters in line is tiring, I don't know how Mama manages it so effortlessly. Sometimes I wonder if it's some mystical den mother power I'll only come into when I get older." Keeping them in line is tiring, huh? What's the problem, exactly? Maybe you can offer some advice, and if not, encouragement at least. "Well, you told me it was important to try and find out why people did bad things before passing judgement. So each time this kind of thing happens, I try to dig out the underlying problem...and once I unearth it, I just can't rest well until it's resolved. It just gnaws at me." Hmm, you don't know what to think about this, and it's not exactly what you envisioned happening when you said those words back then. Being affectionate isn't wrong in and of itself, but as with anything, there's always a risk of overdoing it. She doesn't want to develop a reputation for being a nosy meddler or smother her siblings, does she? Kinu looks a little worried at that. "I think I understand what you're getting at, [kinu.Dad], but it's very hard to step back and simply not do anything when someone's in trouble. It...it doesn't make me feel good at all." So is this about helping other people, or is it about making herself feel good? Your foxy daughter mumbles something not quite under her breath and turns askance, refusing to look you in the eye. "Can't it be both?" She just needs to remember not to spread herself too thinly. Can't help others if she herself is indisposed, or if people instinctively reject her approaches. "I need to think about this, [kinu.Dad]. I'm getting conflicting messages here." That would be a good idea, yes. | "I'm learning how to properly go about doing agriculture!" Oh, really? So she can have a never-ending supply of peaches on which to gorge herself on? And the way she put it — "doing agriculture" — it makes simple farming sound so... well, formal. "Heeey, unlike Mama, I'm taking this seriously. The peach grove is the only real thing she tried her hand at, and that was as a hobby. I, on the other hand —" she puffs out her chest at you — "am learning what crops flourish in what seasons, when to leave land fallow and how to keep it productive without wearing it out. That sort of thing. And I'm learning it myself out of books, instead of Mama teaching." Fascinating. Why the sudden interest in working the land, though? "Wellll... ehe... I'd say that pulling up veggies is lots of fun, but that's just a small part of it. I kinda like seeing things grow, and while I do enjoy them being pretty, there's also the practical aspect to consider. Flower arrangements are a soothing sight, but flowers get cut down first when hunger sets in." Putting her learning into practice is a lot of hard physical labor. Is she sure someone as slight as her is up to it? Kinu winks at you. "Oh, not to worry, [kinu.Dad]. That's what I have brothers and sisters for — and when I get old enough, kits of my own. In the meantime, I'm doing what I can on a smaller scale. You're not wrong in that it's a lot of sweaty work, but I think it's worth it." | "I told Mama I wanted to learn an instrument in addition to just singing, and she offered to teach me how to play the koto. It's not quite my style, though, so I turned her down. It's too cramped for me, for a lack of a better word to describe it." What has she taken up, then? You know your daughter well enough to know that she wouldn't stop there. "Ehe. I'm learning the shakuhachi!" The what? "Um, uh, it's kind of a flute?" Kinu scratches the back of her head, ears wiggling as she thinks. "I guess it is a flute, by the way you would understand the word, [kinu.Dad]. But the important thing is that it's got this nice, meditative tone, and I can carry it around when I go about my daily work. I feel it's more flexible that way." Hmm. Her mother's teaching her the ins and outs, you take it? "Nope, she doesn't know anything of it. Which means I have to make do with the manuals I have, try and figure things out on my own. If Mama could do it for so many other subjects, I don't see why I can't at least give it a go." She thinks a moment. "Progress is pretty slow, though. Everyone keeps on telling me that my playing is awful, so I don't think I'm going to be showing off anytime soon. Learning by yourself is a lot different from learning from a teacher." Naturally, and she doesn't have to worry about progress being slow — what's important here is that she's learning an additional skill in the bargain — that of autodidactism. When one learns to learn effectively, so many possibilities open up, and one can explore them at one's own pace. "Hmm... I like the sound of that, [kinu.Dad]. Exploring. That's a pretty exciting way to put it. I don't know if everyone else will find it that exciting, though. From their reactions so far, it's more annoyance than anything else; I keep on telling them it's only to be expected when one's trying to learn a new instrument but Mama makes me do my practice outside where I won't burst everyone's eardrums. Which, to be frank, suits me just fine." | "I wish I had more people to talk to." Oh? Is she feeling lonely? "No, I'd just like to talk to more kinds of people. For example, I notice that your manner of speech is different than Mama's, but it doesn't end there. It's the way you move when conversing with other people, [kinu.Dad]." The way you move, huh... "Yep. Most people don't even bother thinking about it, so you can tell a lot about what they're really thinking while they're speaking. The same goes for a bunch of animals I see in the forest, too, except they don't talk. I think Mama's the only person who's aware of this, but she doesn't bother trying to conceal it most of the time." So, can she read your mood right now? Your daughter frowns. "Not very well. Like I said, [kinu.Dad], you're different. It's kind of hard to make generalisations when all I have to practice on is Mama and my brothers and sisters. That's why I'd like to have the chance to converse with many different kinds of people and observe them while they're speaking. The more people I get to observe, the better I'll be at reading them in general. Makes sense, right?" It always boils down to that, doesn't it? You're working on it — finding a deity can be a little tricky at times. "Oh? I didn't say anything about that at all, [kinu.Dad]. You came up with that by your very own self." She sticks her tongue out at you. "I think I'm getting a better hold of you already." | You're seeing Kinu outside a lot these days. Does her mother not want her in the house? "There is that, but I don't mind it so much these days, [kinu.Dad]. I feel more comfortable outside and with fresh air, even when playing shogi or go. Besides, it gives me plenty of opportunities to practice my magic — I feel a lot more confident experimenting with spells when I'm in the peach grove or veggie garden. It's like the plants there are cheering me on." Hmm... is she showing druidic tendencies? "From the way you described them, [kinu.Dad], no. Druids worship nature, from what I'm told — agriculture is the most direct union of civilization and nature. The forest is nice, but I don't get the same feeling from it that I do from the growing veggies... we've been together with them for so long that the both of us have changed each other. They trust me enough to lend me power to be repaid later; the plants in the forest are either too mean or too scared of me to even want to talk." She certainly is growing apart from her mother's way of doing things... Kiyoko's bound to blame you for this. "Ehehe. Can't I just be my own person, [kinu.Dad]? Learning by experimentation is so much more fun than sitting down and listening to Mama lecture away." She eyes you shiftily, then leans in to stage-whisper. "You know what we need?" What? "We need a rice paddy. Like, just a wide expanse of golden rice..." Kinu claps her hands together and goes all starry-eyed. "Imagine how amazing I'd look framed against it. But Mama says no, a veggie garden's already enough trouble to tend as it is." If she's trying to play you off against Kiyoko, the answer is no. You're standing with her mother on this. "Boo..." ] | [rand| "Keeping my siblings in line is important, both for them and for Mama's sanity. It's been a lot of trial and error and understanding what makes them tick individually, but I think I'm getting the hang of making sure they behave." She sighs and gives you a little wry smile. "Being Big Sister is hard. They may not fully understand why it's important to behave beyond an I-said-so, but I'm sure they'll thank me in the days to come." [pc.isDK|Certainly. You hope that she's adequately impressing upon them the importance of following her leadership and authority. "Um, [kinu.Dad], that's not exactly what I meant... but you do have a point there. Why shouldn't they follow me when Mama's not around? I'm the smartest and oldest, after all — it naturally follows that they should listen to my direction whether they like it or not. I only have their best interests in mind, after all!" You smirk and tousle Kinu's hair. The little kitsune may look like her mother in body, but she's truly a fox after your own heart.|That might be true, but she shouldn't stop trying to explain the whys and wherefores to them. Even if her siblings can't comprehend the reason she's disciplining them, they ought to be able to realize there that she isn't doing it just on a whim. Kinu gives you a wry smile and plants her little hands on her hips. "Isn't it all the same, [kinu.Dad]? Train them up when they're young, and they'll be set in their ways when they're older?" That's one way to put it...] "Either way, this is a part of my education that Mama can't guide me the whole way through. Being a den mother isn't just about making kits, it's also about raising them to be decent and useful people who live in accordance with Keros' teachings. Hence, I really can't be easy on any of them, even if they cry and pout." And when her own mother reprimands her, does she take the lesson with grace? "I do my best to, [kinu.Dad]; I'd be a hypocrite otherwise. It's not that I don't get peeved — I do — but I realize what I'm doing is wrong, and try to get over myself to understand why Mama is ticked off at me. It's not perfect, but I think it's an important experience. After all, which is better — to be born as a perfectly good girl, or to have some flaws but carefully work to overcome them?" | "I'm learning to cultivate flowers!" Huh. You're not quite sure if flowers needed cultivating. "Weell... when I do flower arrangement with Mama, going out to the forest to get flowers is a pain. Not the going out part, but the finding part. It's so hard to get one that matches exactly what I need — and I'm not going to let Mama just tell the plane to conjure one. That would defeat the point..." Ah, you see where this is going. If she raises them from scratch, she'll get exactly what she needs. "That. Finding blossoms of a particular color, size, and shape is hair-tearing, but if I raise them myself I can influence them as they grow and mould them into something suitable for my arrangements. Although I'll say, [kinu.Dad], that I've discovered there's something pleasing about raising them in and of itself." Indeed. Raising something and seeing the effects of your care on it can be one of the most fulfilling or terrible things in the world, depending on how well of a job one does. You're glad that she's getting to experience this first-hand on a smaller scale in a controlled setting. Kinu pulls her brows together and looks thoughtful. "I get the feeling that you're trying to be deep and meaningful here, [kinu.Dad], but I can't place my finger on it..." | "I told Mama I wanted to learn an instrument in addition to just singing, so she's started teaching me the koto. It's what she's been playing since she was a girl, or so Mama says, so I have the benefit of a good teacher to draw experience from." The koto, huh? What sort of instrument is that? "It's..." Kinu pauses. "It has strings, and you pluck them to make music. I have very slender and nimble fingers, so Mama said it was a good choice for me." A string instrument, eh? Kind of like a lute? "What's a lute?" There's a moment's awkward silence, and then your daughter brushes off the faux pas and continues, ever the cheery fox kit. "I think Mama's kind of proud that I'm following in her footsteps. She's definitely putting more into these lessons than she usually does for other subjects." Well, you know what they say: imitation is the sincerest form of flattery. | "I've decided it's important for a lady-to-be like me to be eloquent in both speech and writing. As a den mother, my children will be looking up to me the same way my brothers and sisters do for Mama, so I'll have to set a good example for them." That's nice, although deciding on a matter is easy; carrying it out to fruition takes a little more effort. What's she doing about it? "Well, Mama's busy enough already, so I've taken to reading some of the old classics she's got lying about in the upper branches of the tree. I don't think she's touched them for a long, looong time, [kinu.Dad]." No, ever since she and her siblings came on the scene, you don't imagine Kiyoko has had much in the way of spare time, especially when she's doing what she truly enjoys. "That's just the beginning, of course," Kinu continues. "Studying how the people of that time strung together words not just to convey meaning in no uncertain terms, but knowing which ones to use to evoke the proper impressions and emotions in whoever reads your words or listens to you speak — and of course, knowing when to use which." That's rather eloquent for something coming out of an eight-year-old's mouth. Kinu smiles. "See? It's working already! Sure, it's important to be outwardly pretty, but that image is going to be ruined if you embarrass yourself the moment you open your mouth. Mama is pretty great in that regard — she always knows the right thing to say in any situation. I know I've still got a looong way to go before I get anywhere approaching her level..." | "The arcane magic Mama uses for divination is fascinating. I can't help but imagine the things I could do if I could just get better... Mama is pacing my lessons so I don't get ahead of myself, but I really want to know more and it's bugging me to no end." Her mother must be pretty happy her daughter's chosen to follow in her footsteps so closely. "Ehe. I'm doing it because I want to, not because Mama's forcing me to do anything. The feel of old scrolls, tomes and manuals beneath my fingers... there's something that's lovely and exquisite about them that I can't put into words." Kinu folds her ears forward and smiles, going all starry-eyed. "I like to think they can speak to me with the voices of the people who wrote them. Isn't that amazing?" [pc.bg arcanist scholar|Well, with both sides of the family into this sort of thing, it's little surprise your daughter turned out this way. At least it's something you know Kiyoko and you can cope with...|Hmph. It's a small relief that your relative inexperience with these things hasn't dampened the enthusiasm your daughter's apparently inherited from her mother.] "Guess patience is one of those virtues Mama wants to cultivate in me," Kinu grumps. "Hmph. I'm smart enough to handle more than what she's willing to teach..." ] ] ]
rows.translation: [rand|妈妈正在教我她的母语。这种语言和我们平时说的那种语言非常不同 [kinu.Dad]非常不同，但我正在努力应对。 这可真有意思。 [pc.bg scholar noblescion courtesan|你过去确实有机会学习一些外语，但由于贝尔哈兰语是这片大陆上通用的语言，你觉得并没有必要去学习其他语言。毕竟，正如那句俗话所说，任何不懂贝尔哈兰语的人都不值得与你交谈。|你当时根本没有机会学习任何外语，即使学会了，那些语言在你当时的生活环境中也几乎派不上什么用场。] 不过，你也可以理解为什么清子会坚持让女儿学习她的母语——这不仅仅是为了魔法施放的需要。 除了 狐妖，我想等我们离开这里之后，应该不会再有人会说或写这种语言了…… 但这对于了解她的背景来说仍然很重要。而且，在那些听不懂这种语言的人面前进行对话，也会是一件有趣的事情。这样会让你觉得自己仿佛属于一个秘密俱乐部，不是吗？ 绮奴的笑容变得更加灿烂了。 是啊……你这么一说，听起来还挺有趣的。 [kinu.Dad]现在，要是有那些不懂狐语的人来试试这个该多好啊——当然，你除外。 rows.original: Kinu squeals the moment you reach out and down, knowing what you're after. "I wanna be petted! I wanna be petted!" My, she sure is enthusiastic about it. "You should know, [kinu.Dad]. Someday when I'm older, I'll pet you back. It'll be repayment for all the times you petted me, so you should pet me more now!" Why not now? "I'm not tall enough..." All right, girl, hold your horses. Firmly planting the heel of your palm on Kinu's forehead, you give your daughter a noogie right between the eyes. The little white kitsune's ears perk up at your touch, then begin wiggling uncontrollably, as do her three tails. "Eheehee! It tickles!" Of course. You wouldn't do it if it didn't tickle. "Come on! Pet more! Pet more!" Grinning madly, Kinu pushes her head against your hand, nuzzling against you to and fro. Now, now. She can't rush these things. Just like with fruit, she's got to learn how to stop and savor the pleasantries of life instead of wolfing them down with wanton abandon. Now that your palm is secure, you lay your fingers down atop your daughter's head and dig them into the smooth, flowing hair and fur, then begin rubbing with a gentle back-and-forth motion. "Aaah..." Heh. Pushing back against you like this, Kinu looks more like a fox than a human, eyes closed and head nodding back and forth as you continue to pet away. The little kitsune's mouth opens and closes wordlessly as you lavish affection upon her; she's clearly luxuriating in the simple joy of being pampered, taking it in for everything it's worth. Now, if she wants to properly repay you for your petting, she has to be good and obey her mother when you're not around, okay? "Mmm..." Also, she mustn't stuff herself with fruit until she gets sick from overeating. "Aww..." That's a non-negotiable, and being cute isn't going to help her any. "Okay... if you'll pet me some more, [kinu.Dad]." It's a deal, then. You finish up the simple head-petting, and move on to Kinu's ears. They're less fluffy to the touch than her mother's, but far, far more sensitive; Kinu doesn't have fluffy tufts in her large fox ears, but makes little incoherent yips of delight as your fingertips brush against the hairs within. Little Kinu sighs, then slumps against you and gives you a big hug as you shower every exposed bit of your daughter's ears with plenty of affection. Meanwhile, you hook your fingertips around her ears, scratching at their sensitive backs in turn. Kinu's three tails wrap around her and curl about your feet, their silken fur siding back and forth as she embraces you with everything she has. There, there. When you finally pull away and push a clingy Kinu off you, your daughter has a big, dreamy smile on her face, eyes half-lidded and unfocused until she gathers her wits again. "That was fun." Wasn't it? You'll give her another petting if she continues being a good girl until the next time you visit. "Okay, I will, [kinu.Dad]! Bye bye now! Make Mama happy, okay!"
rows.translation: 当你伸手去拿的时候，绮奴立刻发出了尖叫，因为它知道你在想要什么。 我想让人抚摸我！我想让人抚摸我！ 哎呀，她对这件事真是充满热情啊。 你应该知道， [kinu.Dad]等我长大了，一定会反过来抚摸你。那将是对你一直以来抚摸我的回报，所以现在你应该多抚摸我一些哦！ 为什么不是现在呢？ 我的个子还不够高…… 好了，姑娘，先别急。你把手掌的根部紧紧按在绮奴的额头上，然后用力敲了她的太阳穴一下。那只小白色的狐妖听到你的触碰后，耳朵立刻竖了起来，接着它的三条尾巴也开始不受控制地扭动起来。 嘿嘿嘿！真好玩啊！ 当然。如果这件事不能让你感到有趣、感到开心，你也不会去做它。 来吧！多摸摸它吧！多摸摸它吧！ 基努疯狂地笑着，把头往你的手上蹭来蹭去，紧紧依偎在你身边。 现在，她不能急于求成。就像品尝水果一样，她必须学会停下来，细细品味生活中这些美好的时刻，而不是肆无忌惮地狼吞虎咽。现在你的手掌已经稳稳地放在她头上了，你用手指轻轻抚摸她那顺滑柔亮的头发和毛发，然后开始有节奏地轻轻按摩起来。 啊…… 呵呵，像这样对你撒娇的绮奴，看起来更像只狐妖而不是人类——她闭着眼睛，不断地点头回应你的抚摸。当你给予她关爱时，她的小嘴无声地张开又闭上，显然她正在尽情享受这种被宠爱的快乐，把每一刻都珍视不已。 现在，如果她想好好报答你对自己的关爱，就必须在你不在的时候听妈妈的话，乖巧地表现出来，好吗？ 嗯…… 另外，她也不能吃太多水果，否则会因为吃得太多而生病。 哎呀…… 这是没有商量余地的，而且长得可爱对她来说也毫无帮助。 好吧……如果你再多摸摸我一会儿的话 [kinu.Dad]." 那就这么定了。你先完成那些简单的抚摸动作，然后再继续抚摸绮奴的耳朵。她的耳朵摸起来没有她妈妈的耳朵那么柔软蓬松，但敏感度要高得多；绮奴那对大大的狐妖耳朵上并没有柔软的绒毛，但当你的指尖轻轻触碰到里面的毛发时，她就会发出一些愉悦的、断断续续的叫声。 小希努轻轻叹了口气，然后靠在你身上，给了你一个紧紧的拥抱。而你则用充满爱意的手抚摸着女儿耳朵的每一个部位。与此同时，你也用指尖轻轻挠了挠她耳朵后面那些敏感的地方。 基努的三条尾巴环绕着她的身躯，又盘绕在你的足部边，它们那柔软的毛皮不断地来回摆动，而她则用自己全部的力量紧紧拥抱着你。 好了，好了。 当你终于拉开距离，将这个黏人的基努从自己身上推开时，你的女儿脸上露出了灿烂而梦幻般的笑容，她的眼睛半闭着，目光有些呆滞，直到她重新恢复了清醒。 那真是太有趣了。 不是吗？如果她下次你来访之前继续表现得好，你就会再抚摸她一次的。 好的，我会的。 [kinu.Dad]好了，现在要走了哦！要让妈妈开心，好吗？
rows.raw: " Kinu squeals the moment you reach out and down, knowing what you're after. "I wanna be petted! I wanna be petted!" My, she sure is enthusiastic about it. "You should know, [kinu.Dad]. Someday when I'm older, I'll pet you back. It'll be repayment for all the times you petted me, so you should pet me more now!" Why not now? "I'm not tall enough..." All right, girl, hold your horses. Firmly planting the heel of your palm on Kinu's forehead, you give your daughter a noogie right between the eyes. The little white kitsune's ears perk up at your touch, then begin wiggling uncontrollably, as do her three tails. "Eheehee! It tickles!" Of course. You wouldn't do it if it didn't tickle. "Come on! Pet more! Pet more!" Grinning madly, Kinu pushes her head against your hand, nuzzling against you to and fro. Now, now. She can't rush these things. Just like with fruit, she's got to learn how to stop and savor the pleasantries of life instead of wolfing them down with wanton abandon. Now that your palm is secure, you lay your fingers down atop your daughter's head and dig them into the smooth, flowing hair and fur, then begin rubbing with a gentle back-and-forth motion. "Aaah..." Heh. Pushing back against you like this, Kinu looks more like a fox than a human, eyes closed and head nodding back and forth as you continue to pet away. The little kitsune's mouth opens and closes wordlessly as you lavish affection upon her; she's clearly luxuriating in the simple joy of being pampered, taking it in for everything it's worth. Now, if she wants to properly repay you for your petting, she has to be good and obey her mother when you're not around, okay? "Mmm..." Also, she mustn't stuff herself with fruit until she gets sick from overeating. "Aww..." That's a non-negotiable, and being cute isn't going to help her any. "Okay... if you'll pet me some more, [kinu.Dad]." It's a deal, then. You finish up the simple head-petting, and move on to Kinu's ears. They're less fluffy to the touch than her mother's, but far, far more sensitive; Kinu doesn't have fluffy tufts in her large fox ears, but makes little incoherent yips of delight as your fingertips brush against the hairs within. Little Kinu sighs, then slumps against you and gives you a big hug as you shower every exposed bit of your daughter's ears with plenty of affection. Meanwhile, you hook your fingertips around her ears, scratching at their sensitive backs in turn. Kinu's three tails wrap around her and curl about your feet, their silken fur siding back and forth as she embraces you with everything she has. There, there. When you finally pull away and push a clingy Kinu off you, your daughter has a big, dreamy smile on her face, eyes half-lidded and unfocused until she gathers her wits again. "That was fun." Wasn't it? You'll give her another petting if she continues being a good girl until the next time you visit. "Okay, I will, [kinu.Dad]! Bye bye now! Make Mama happy, okay!" "

rows.original: A big, open-mouthed smile crosses Kinu's face at the mere thought of receiving a petting. "Pet my tails! Pet my tails! I spent all morning brushing out all the loose hairs and tangles, so they should be really super-duper great to pet!" Hopping on the spot, your daughter does a twirl and a flourish, her three tails flowing in her wake. The glossy, silvery-white hairs catch the sunlight and glisten faintly, lending Kinu's tails a vaguely ethereal sheen. Now, now, one step at a time. She's got to take these things slowly, else her heart might burst from sheer excitement. Besides, you don't want to accidentally yank her tails while you're petting them — that would be bad for everyone involved. "Okay, okay!" Kinu settles down a little — for a definition of settling down, considering she's practically vibrating on the spot — and offers you one of her lovely tails, the appendage snaking around from behind her and coming within reach. It's almost as long as she is tall, and it's clear that your daughter takes as good care of her tails as her mother does. Trying to take hold of it is an uphill task — each time you reach for the proffered tail, its lustrous hairs just flow through your fingers like water, leaving you grasping at empty air. One supposes that her name is well-deserved, isn't it? "I'm warm like silk, as lovely and precious as silk, and as smooth as silk! What other name should Mama have given me? Now pet my tails!" It takes a few more tries, but you finally manage to catch hold of Kinu's tail by its core. Her fur is definitely different from her mother's — instead of being all floofy and fluffy, your daughter's tail fur is sleek to the touch, not unlike a brush or a whisk. Twisting and squirming in your grasp, Kinu's tail instinctively tries to escape your fingers, not too unlike your hyperactive daughter herself. "Eehee. Sorry, [kinu.Dad]. Sometimes, they just don't do what I want them to. They're like my ears in that regard..." It's okay. Starting off with long, languid strokes, you trail your fingers through the proffered tail, running its entire length from base to furry tip. After the first pass, your daughter's expression has softened considerably; after the fifth, her knees have begun to grow weak and trembling. A quiet yip escapes her throat as she falls against you with a thud, pupils dilated and expression dreamy. Gods, she's even worse than her mother when it comes to this particular weakness. "Pet more! Pet more! Don't stop!" Sure, but she needs to sit down first before she falls over. "Naaaah!" With a roll and flop, Kinu is belly-down on the ground, her three tails waving in the air. "This is more fun! Now pet more!" Ah, there's no way you can deny an adorable little fusspet like her. Kneeling down, you grab all three of Kinu's tails at the base, wrap your hands about them to form a bunch, and start stroking the silken, lustrous mess all at once. "Eeeee!" Three tails are much more of a handful to wrangle than one, especially when they're so silky and smooth, but there's enough mass there that you can't help but be petting something when you move your fingers through the lot. Under your tender ministrations, your daughter begins to whimper and pant as you lavish her tails with all the love and affection you have to give; as you watch, Kinu slowly melts into a gooey puddle of saccharine happiness, big vulpine ears pressed flat against her head as every muscle in her body goes limp. Right now, she looks more like a fox kit than a little girl, especially with the wordless barks and yips that're escaping from her mouth. There, there. That's a good girl. This really brightened her day, didn't it? "I love you, [kinu.Dad]... this feels so good..." It's a good thing that kitsune can't pet their own tails, otherwise they'd just sit around all day stroking their tails and nothing would ever get done. Even Kinu's tails have stopped trying to squirm away from your touch, choosing instead to curl about your fingers and wrists in a bid to get as much contact with you as they can. You'd go on for a bit longer, but after a while your fingers start to get all tingly and your wrists start to ache; best to stop now so that you can put her the next time you come around. Kinu herself is in no shape to do much of anything else, either; the little kitsune has been reduced to a blubbering, giggling mess, and as you watch she curls up into a little ball on the grass, tucks her tails about herself, and begins to snore. That'll do. That'll do. Now, perhaps you should pay her mother a visit?
rows.translation: 一想到会被人抚摸，绮奴的脸上立刻浮现出灿烂而开心的笑容。 摸摸我的尾巴吧！摸摸我的尾巴吧！我整个早上都在仔细梳理那些松散的毛发和打结的地方，所以现在摸起来肯定超级舒服的！ 你的女儿在原地跳着脚，转了个圈，然后挥动着自己的三条尾巴，那些闪亮的银白色毛发在阳光下微微闪烁，让她的尾巴呈现出一种仿佛来自天界的光泽。 好了，好了，一步一个脚印来。她必须慢慢来，否则她的心脏可能会因为太过兴奋而“爆炸”掉。另外，你在抚摸她的尾巴时可千万不能不小心拉到它们——那对大家都不好。 好吧，好吧！ 基努稍微安静了一些——不过考虑到她实际上还在原地不停地颤抖，这个“安静”也算是一种相对的状态吧——然后她把那条漂亮的尾巴伸了过来，那条尾巴从她身后蜿蜒而来，正好落在你可以触及的范围之内。 它的长度几乎和她的身高一样长，很明显，你的女儿和她母亲一样，非常细心地照顾着自己的尾巴。想要抓住它简直是一件不可能完成的任务——每次你试图抓住那条柔软的尾巴，它那闪亮的毛发就会像流水一样从你的手部指间滑过，让你只能徒劳地抓住空气。 人们会认为，她的这个名字确实名副其实，不是吗？ 我柔软如丝绸，美丽而珍贵，触感也像丝绸一样顺滑！妈妈还能给我起什么别的名字呢？现在来摸摸我的尾巴吧！ 经过几次尝试，你终于成功地抓住了绮奴尾巴的根部。她的毛发确实与她母亲的不一样——那些柔软蓬松的毛发在绮奴身上显得格外光滑，摸起来就像一把刷子或一根鸡毛掸子。在你的手部中扭动挣扎着，绮奴的尾巴本能地想要逃脱你的手部指，这一幕与你那个活泼好动的女儿简直一模一样。 嘿嘿，抱歉 [kinu.Dad]有时候，它们就是不会按照我的意愿来行动。在这方面，它们简直就像我的“耳朵”一样…… 没关系。刚开始时，你可以用缓慢、轻柔的动作，用手部指沿着那条柔软的尾巴从根部一直滑到毛茸茸的尾尖。第一次触摸之后，你女儿的表情就已经变得柔和了许多；到了第五次触摸时，她的膝盖已经开始发软、颤抖起来。她轻轻叫了一声，然后重重地靠在你身上，瞳孔放大，神情仿佛陷入了梦境。 天啊，在这种事情上，她甚至比她妈妈还要严重呢。 多摸摸它吧！再摸摸它！别停下来！ 当然可以，但她在坐下之前得先站稳，否则会摔倒的。 才不呢！ 随着一声翻滚和扑通，绮奴整个人趴在了地上，她的三条尾巴在空气中挥动着。 这样更有趣了！现在多摸摸它吧！ 啊，对于这么可爱、喜欢闹着玩的小家伙，你根本无法拒绝她的请求。你蹲下来，抓住基努三条尾巴的根部，双手部将它们握在一起，然后开始同时抚摸那些柔软、有光泽的尾巴。 哎呀！ 三条尾巴可比一条尾巴难对付多了，尤其是当它们如此柔软光滑的时候……不过，由于它们的体积足够大，你还是忍不住会想要抚摸它们。 某个东西 当你用手部指轻轻抚摸她的时候，在你充满爱与关怀的抚摸下，你的女儿开始呜咽着、喘着气，而你则将所有的心爱与关怀都倾注在她的尾巴上。看着她，绮奴渐渐融化成了一滩甜蜜幸福的黏液，她那大大的狐妖耳朵紧紧贴在头上，她身体的每一块肌肉都变得软软的、无力地垂着。 现在看来，她更像一只小狐妖，而不是一个小女孩，尤其是当那些无声的吠叫和叫声从她嘴里冒出来时。 好了，好了，真是个好孩子。这确实让她的这一天变得愉快多了，不是吗？ 我爱你， [kinu.Dad]……这种感觉真是太棒了…… 幸好狐妖无法抚摸自己的尾巴，否则它们整天都会坐着不停地舔自己的尾巴，根本什么事情也做不成。就连绮奴的尾巴也不再试图摆脱你的触碰，反而会缠绕在你的手部指和手部腕上，尽可能地与你保持接触。 你可以再继续一会儿，但过不了多久，你的手部指就会开始发麻，手部腕也会开始疼痛；所以最好现在就停下来，这样下次来的时候就可以继续帮她了。至于绮奴本身，她也根本无力做任何其他事情了——那只小狐妖现在已经变成了一团哭哭笑笑、乱七八糟的家伙。当你看着它蜷缩在草地上，把尾巴围在身上，开始打呼噜的时候，你会觉得它真的已经无能为力了。 这样就可以了。这样就可以了。现在，或许你应该去看看她的母亲吧？
