rows.original: Well, you don't feel up to running around and getting yourself all winded and dirty — after all, you're intending to see her mother later on and ought to at least look decent. How about a nice board game out in the open? "Are you sure, [kinu.Dad]?" Kinu clasps her hands together and starts rubbing away, impish glee written all over her adorable face. "Are you absoluuuutely sure?" Yes, you know how strategy games are her forte. Yes, you know how even her mother has trouble beating her at times. But she's your darling daughter, and [pc.cunningRange 0 50 80 |even if you're not the best at these kinds of games, you still want to entertain her. Who knows, you might even improve with time. Kinu seems to have realized something, and stops her hand-rubbing. "Yeah, about that, [kinu.Dad]... the thought is really appreciated, but when I turn it over in my head some more it doesn't really seem appealing to me anymore. Don't take this the wrong way or anything, but there really isn't fun in walking all over an opponent." So, she doesn't want to play today? "Not like this. It would be unfair, and besides, I want you to have fun too, not suffer in silence for my sake over something so trivial. Why don't we play something else?" Sheesh, when she puts it that way... it's hard not to feel guilty, too. All right, then — maybe you'll find another game to play with her... |you think you can put up a good fight, even if you're likely to lose. Who knows, you might even get lucky and pull an unexpected move over on her. "There are some who say playing against beginners can be enlightening at times," Kinu replies matter-of-factly. "They may even attempt gambits more seasoned players would deem too risky or not worth one's time." Haha, that's one way to put it. You don't think you're that bad, though... "It's all — ahem — relative. At least you're not a walkover like some of my siblings are, [kinu.Dad]. Come on, let's get started!" |besides, you think you have a decent-to-good chance of winning, even if she's your opponent. Kinu whistles, her ears perky and ever so innocent. "If that's how you feel, [kinu.Dad]. If that's how you feel. Maybe I'll go easy on you and let you win." No, absolutely not. If you're going to come out on top, it's going to be in spite of her doing her best, and you absolutely forbid her from throwing the game just because she feels sorry for you. She's got to be honest and give it her all, okay? Kinu grins. "I had a feeling that you'd say that, [kinu.Dad]; I just wanted to hear it from you in no uncertain terms. Okay, I won't hold back!" ]
rows.translation: 嗯，你大概没精力到处跑来跑去，弄得自己气喘吁吁、满身脏兮兮的吧——毕竟你之后还打算去见她的母亲，至少应该看起来整洁一些。不如在户外玩一款不错的桌游怎么样？ 你确定吗？ [kinu.Dad]?" 纪奈双手部交叠，开始搓来搓去，她那可爱的脸上洋溢着调皮的笑容。 你真的确定吗？ 没错，你们都知道策略游戏才是她的强项。没错，就连她的母亲有时也很难战胜她。但她毕竟是你们的宝贝女儿啊 [pc.cunningRange 0 50 80 |即使你不是这类游戏的高手，你仍然想逗她开心。谁知道呢，随着时间的推移，你说不定还会进步呢。 绮奴似乎意识到了什么，于是停止了揉手的行为。 是的，关于那个 [kinu.Dad]……这个想法确实很值得考虑，但再仔细想一想，我觉得它并没有那么吸引人。别误会我的意思，但真的，一路追着对手部跑来跑去并没有什么乐趣可言。 所以，她今天不想玩了吗？ 不是这样的。那样太不公平了，而且，我也希望你能开心地玩，而不是因为这么琐碎的事情而默默忍受。我们为什么不玩点别的吧？ 哎呀，她这么一说……确实会让人感到内疚啊。好吧，那你就再找别的游戏和她一起玩吧…… |你觉得自己就算很可能失败，也能好好抗争一番。谁知道呢，说不定你还会走运，使出某个意想不到的招数，反而战胜她呢。 有些人认为，与初学者对战有时也会让人有所收获。 纪久回答得非常淡然。 他们甚至可能会尝试那些经验更丰富的玩家认为风险太大或不值得花费时间的策略。 哈哈，这么说也有道理。你难道不觉得自己 那个 不过，这也挺糟糕的…… 这一切啊——咳——都是相对的。至少你不像我的一些兄弟姐妹那样，那么容易就被击败。 [kinu.Dad]来吧，我们开始吧！ |此外，你认为自己即使面对她这样的对手部，也有相当大的胜算。 绮奴吹着口哨，她的耳朵竖得高高的，显得格外天真无邪。 如果你是这么想的， [kinu.Dad]如果你是这么想的的话，也许我会放你一马，让你赢吧。 不，绝对不行。如果你想取得胜利，那就必须是在她尽了最大努力的情况下依然取得胜利；你绝对不能因为她同情你而让她放弃比赛。她必须诚实面对，全力以赴，明白吗？ 绮奴露出了微笑。 我就觉得你会这么说 [kinu.Dad]我只是想从你口中明确听到这个答案。好吧，我不会再犹豫了！ ]
rows.raw: " Well, you don't feel up to running around and getting yourself all winded and dirty — after all, you're intending to see her mother later on and ought to at least look decent. How about a nice board game out in the open? "Are you sure, [kinu.Dad]?" Kinu clasps her hands together and starts rubbing away, impish glee written all over her adorable face. "Are you absoluuuutely sure?" Yes, you know how strategy games are her forte. Yes, you know how even her mother has trouble beating her at times. But she's your darling daughter, and [pc.cunningRange 0 50 80 |even if you're not the best at these kinds of games, you still want to entertain her. Who knows, you might even improve with time. Kinu seems to have realized something, and stops her hand-rubbing. "Yeah, about that, [kinu.Dad]... the thought is really appreciated, but when I turn it over in my head some more it doesn't really seem appealing to me anymore. Don't take this the wrong way or anything, but there really isn't fun in walking all over an opponent." So, she doesn't want to play today? "Not like this. It would be unfair, and besides, I want you to have fun too, not suffer in silence for my sake over something so trivial. Why don't we play something else?" Sheesh, when she puts it that way... it's hard not to feel guilty, too. All right, then — maybe you'll find another game to play with her... |you think you can put up a good fight, even if you're likely to lose. Who knows, you might even get lucky and pull an unexpected move over on her. "There are some who say playing against beginners can be enlightening at times," Kinu replies matter-of-factly. "They may even attempt gambits more seasoned players would deem too risky or not worth one's time." Haha, that's one way to put it. You don't think you're that bad, though... "It's all — ahem — relative. At least you're not a walkover like some of my siblings are, [kinu.Dad]. Come on, let's get started!" |besides, you think you have a decent-to-good chance of winning, even if she's your opponent. Kinu whistles, her ears perky and ever so innocent. "If that's how you feel, [kinu.Dad]. If that's how you feel. Maybe I'll go easy on you and let you win." No, absolutely not. If you're going to come out on top, it's going to be in spite of her doing her best, and you absolutely forbid her from throwing the game just because she feels sorry for you. She's got to be honest and give it her all, okay? Kinu grins. "I had a feeling that you'd say that, [kinu.Dad]; I just wanted to hear it from you in no uncertain terms. Okay, I won't hold back!" ]"

rows.original: With that, Kinu breaks off into a quick jog for her home, motioning for you to wait here. The little kitsune can be fast when she puts her mind to it — you don't think more than fifteen minutes have passed before she returns with the board and pieces in her arms, ears all perky and her three silky tails having taken a life of their own with her excitement. "All right, then! Let's find a nice place to sit down and play! There're few things better in life than enjoying a game out with a hilltop breeze caressing your skin; I hope you can share in this simple pleasure, [kinu.Dad]!" So it comes to pass that you and your kitsune daughter wind up in the shade of a parasol, facing each other down over a game of [rand|go|shogi]. You're not exactly sure where the tea and rice crackers came from — one moment they weren't there, the next moment they were — but it's not done to question things too deeply around here. At least the tea is hot and the crackers passable, if very bland and dry. To you, it's like eating paper, but Kinu doesn't seem to mind in the least. For the next hour or so — time is rather indeterminate in the astral plane — all that can be heard is the clacking of pieces against the board, broken every so often by the gentle tinkling of wind chimes. [var0|Kinu's usually cheerful and carefree expression has gathered into one of absolute concentration, brows furrowed as her ice-blue eyes flick back and forth. Those aren't just gears turning in that cute little head of hers — it's an entire assembly of deviously complex mechanisms. Seconds tick by between each of your moves, a strange gravitas suffusing the board as pieces are picked up and set down with grim finality. [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|Though you're not too familiar with the game itself, you've had plenty of chances to play chess and other strategy board games in the past, and the principles are eerily similar to what you're facing now. Some things truly are universal, one supposes. |Although you really haven't had the chance to play such board games in the past, you nevertheless manage to intuitively connect some of the strategies to your experiences growing up as [a] [pc.background], and a number of possibilities become open to you. Maybe you're just talented at this kind of stuff. ] The game continues to drag on. At this point, even Kinu's ears have stilled, stiff and alert on her head as she studies the pieces on the board. Then at last, the endgame. [rand|"I believe I've won, [kinu.Dad]." Why yes, she has. She has indeed won, although by the looks of things it was a very close game. Thinking back on it, there were a couple of points back there where making a slightly different move would have radically changed the game's outcome. Kinu purses her lips and eyes the board once more. "I'm not going to deny that; you gave me a run for my money. Ehehe, Mama is the only other person who can do that, and she doesn't have all the time in the world to play with me all day. "Either way, this was a good game. It was fun! I think I learned a few things I want to try out next time." Of course. You've enjoyed your time with her, too. |"I believe you've won, [kinu.Dad]." Why, so you have. That's actually rather surprising. "Is it? I'm just good at this, I never quite said I was unbeatable." She looks down at the board again and wiggles in her seat. "Yeah, I see it now, [kinu.Dad]. I could've won if I'd done this —" she jabs at the board with a finger — "and this and this twenty moves ago." Thinking with a clear head is hard enough. Doing so under pressure is a skill one needs to cultivate over time. She may be talented, but experience is something that can't be rushed. That being said, you've no doubt she'll be a force to be reckoned with in the future. "Ehe. This is kinda embarrassing... I'm not sure I deserve the praise if I still lost in the end. It was fun, though. I learned a lot!" So long as she remembers that there generally are more opportunities to learn from loss and failure than from coming out ahead, she'll do just fine. And yes, you quite enjoyed your time with her. ] |[rand|The picture of peaceful serenity doesn't last long, though. Within a handful of moves, your kitsune daughter has completely outmaneuvered you and has free rein of the board. It's not long after that you're forced to admit defeat, perhaps a little relieved that this wasn't dragged out any longer than it needed to be. On her part, Kinu looks a little disappointed at the easy victory, chewing her lip as she looks over what pieces remain on the board. Eventually, she sighs and shakes her head, mumbling to herself. "Well, guess you had a bit of bad strategy back there, [kinu.Dad]. Unless I intentionally went easy on you, I don't think there was any way you could've salvaged the situation past the twelfth move back —" she jabs a finger on the board — "there." And you absolutely refuse to let her go easy on you, otherwise what would be the point? "Ehe. I like to think that I'm not the kind of person to enjoy cat-and-mouse games and drag out someone's loss when it's clear there's not much point to doing so. Those get boring fast." Still, did she have fun? "Not from the game itself, I'll admit to that. But spending time with you is always great, [kinu.Dad]." Now there's a honey-tongued little flatterer if you ever saw one. |As the game proceeds, your kitsune daughter gradually becomes a pinpoint of intense focus, her ice-blue eyes narrowing as she studies the board. Almost unconsciously, Kinu's three tails sweep out to her front, and she hugs her own silken fur close to herself as her moves become much more methodical and much less lackadaisical. "Hmm..." It's almost as if she's enjoying being decently challenged — or at least, more of a challenge than [kiyoko.numKits 3|her siblings usually put up|she gets from playing against herself]. You're going to give it your all, too — if you lose, it's not going to be from lack of trying. The state of the battlefield that's the wooden game board shifts from moment to moment, the tides of war turning at seemingly a whim; it's hard to discern who exactly has the upper hand until seemingly out of nowhere, Kinu pulls off a series of moves that has you completely outmaneuvered in moments. "...And there. Good show, [kinu.Dad], but seems like I win in the end. For a moment I thought that gambit wasn't going to work, but then that, more than anything else, was the time to take a risk." A desperation move, huh? [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|You've had some time to do things like chess and checkers in your youth, and some of the strategies do carry over to these games of hers, if not completely. Hopefully, you've been able to give a new perspective on various plays that Kiyoko's home culture wouldn't be familiar with. "Weeeelll... that's one way of putting it, [kinu.Dad]. I'm very thankful for the time you've taken to play with me. I think I learned something from all this. Maybe I'd learn more if you played with me again some other time." Heh. Is that an invitation? Well, you'll see. "Well, I always enjoy the time I get to spend with you, [kinu.Dad], so you should definitely take me up on that offer!" |Well, considering that you didn't have much chance to play these sorts of games in your youth, being able to back her into a corner like this must be some kind of achievement in and of itself. Kinu looks up at you, her expression inscrutable. "Well, if you got to play more, [kinu.Dad], who knows how you might improve? Perhaps you should play more strategy games with me in the future?" Oh, she doesn't have to couch it like that — you'll gladly play with her any time she wants. "Well, Mama says that people are more likely to agree with you if you point out how your actions are going to benefit them." ] Psh, isn't that just adorably devious. |Kinu starts off with a strong opening and bold play, but quickly falls into a far more conservative strategy when you stymie her opening gambit. Your daughter's brows knit and furrow as she considers each move deeply, perhaps realizing that she's gotten in ahead of herself, perhaps due to simple overconfidence. Still, she gives as good as she takes. The tides of war shift back and forth on the battlefield of the wooden game board, each move by either party slow and deliberate. Untouched, the tea grows cold and the rice crackers lie forlornly on their plate, but neither of you have time for such trivialities. By this point, Kinu's lips are a thin, straight line as she cups her chin in a hand, those ice-blue eyes of hers darting back and forth across the board. When it happens, it surprises you almost as much as it does her; with a final, resounding clack, you set the piece in your hand down on the board and claim victory over your daughter. "Congratulations, [kinu.Dad]. It appears that you've won." So you have. That doesn't mean anything, though — you could have gotten lucky, or she could have been careless. "Oh, please. Don't undersell yourself, [kinu.Dad]. Now then, perhaps you ought to play with me more at another time to show that this wasn't a fluke." You grin. Is she really that starved for competent players to challenge? "It's more than that. Not only did I learn a few things today, but I always enjoy the time we spend together. We don't get to play all the time, so that makes it extra special, you know? Absence, fondness, and all that good stuff." He, she doesn't need to lay it on that thick. ] ] "Either way, thank you once more. I'll stay here, finish up the tea, and pick up the board later, okay? For now, I'd like to go over the game we just had, review our moves and see what could have been done better." You nod, stand and give her a pat on the head. She really takes these games seriously, doesn't she? Kinu squirms under the petting. "Ehe, you don't get good at anything by taking it lightly, [kinu.Dad]. Eee! Not there, it tickles! Um, maybe you should go and see Mama now, okay? I can't think straight with you petting my ears like this." Ha! You give Kinu's hair one final run-through, then say goodbye to your foxy daughter. She'll be here the next time you drop by to visit her mother.
rows.translation: 说完，绮奴便快步跑向了她的家，同时示意你在这里等着。这个小小的狐妖真是 快 只要她下定决心去做，你绝对不会觉得过了十五分钟，她就会抱着棋盘和棋子回来，耳朵竖得高高的，那三条柔软的尾巴也因为她的兴奋而不停地摆动着。 好吧，那我们就找个舒服的地方坐下来玩吧！生活中没有什么比在山顶的微风中享受游戏更惬意的了；希望你也能体会到这种简单的乐趣。 [kinu.Dad]!" 于是，你和你的九尾狐女儿便坐在遮阳伞下，面对面地开始玩起这个游戏来。 [rand|开始吧|将棋]你其实并不确定这些茶和米饼是从哪里来的——前一刻它们还不存在，下一刻就出现了——但在这里，人们并不会深入探究这些事情。至少茶是热的，米饼也还算可以，虽然味道很淡，也很干。 对你来说，这就像在吃纸一样，但绮奴似乎一点也不在意。 在接下来的一个小时左右的时间里——在星界中，时间的概念其实并不明显——所能听到的只有棋子落在棋盘上发出的咔嗒声，偶尔还会被风铃轻柔的叮当声打断。 [var0|通常开朗无忧的纪努此刻却全神贯注地盯着棋盘，眉头紧锁，冰蓝色的眼睛不停来回转动。在她那可爱的小脑袋里，运转的不仅仅是简单的思维机制——而是整套极其复杂、精巧的思维系统。每当你做出一个动作，几秒钟的时间就会悄然流逝，而当棋子被小心翼翼地拿起又放下时，整个棋盘似乎都被一种庄严而凝重的气氛所笼罩。 [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|虽然你对这款游戏本身并不太熟悉，但过去你有很多机会去玩国际象棋和其他策略类棋盘游戏，而这些游戏的规则与你现在面临的挑战有着惊人的相似之处。或许，有些东西确实是普遍存在的吧。 |虽然你过去确实没有机会玩过这类棋盘游戏，但你也能够凭借自身的成长经历，直觉地将其中的一些策略与自己的实际体验联系起来。 [a] [pc.background]这样一来，许多可能性就会向你敞开。也许你天生就擅长这类事情。 ] 这场游戏依旧在拖延时间。此时，就连基努的耳朵也静止了下来，她将耳朵紧紧贴在头上，仔细观察棋盘上的棋子。终于，游戏进入了最后阶段。 [rand|我想我赢了。 [kinu.Dad]." 没错，她确实赢了。虽然从比赛情况来看，这场对决其实非常胶着。回想起来，有那么几个关键时刻，如果当时采取稍微不同的策略，整个比赛的结果可能会完全不同。 绮奴抿了抿嘴唇，再次注视着棋盘。 我不得不承认，你确实让我费了一番功夫才打败你。嘿嘿，妈妈也是唯一一个能做到这点的人，不过她也没那么多时间整天陪我玩。 不管怎样，这确实是一款很棒的游戏。玩起来非常有趣！我觉得自己学到了一些东西，下次玩游戏时一定会尝试这些新方法。 当然。你和她在一起的时光也应该很愉快吧。 |我认为你已经赢了。 [kinu.Dad]." 哦，原来如此。这确实有点令人惊讶。 是吗？我只是在这方面比较擅长而已，从来没说过自己是无敌的。 她再次低头看着棋盘，在座位上扭来扭去。 是的，我现在明白了。 [kinu.Dad]如果我当时这么做了，我本可以获胜的—— 她用手指戳着那块板子—— 还有这些等等。 这个 二十步之前。 保持头脑清醒地进行思考已经很困难了，而在压力下依然能够做到这一点，则是需要通过长时间的努力来培养的一项能力。她或许天赋异禀，但经验这种东西是无法速成的。不过，可以肯定的是，她将来必定会成为一股不可小觑的力量。 嘿嘿，这有点尴尬……如果最后还是输了，我真不确定自己是否配得到这些赞美。不过过程确实很有趣，我也学到了很多！ 只要她记住，从失败和挫折中学习到的机会通常要比从成功中获得的机会更多，她就会一切顺利的。而且，你确实很享受与她相处的时光。 ] |[rand|然而，这种宁静祥和的局面并没有持续太久。仅仅经过几步操作，你的九尾狐女儿就已经完全掌控了局局主动权，让你完全无法应对。不久之后，你就不得不承认失败了——或许还暗自庆幸这场战斗并没有拖得太久。 对于基努来说，这场如此轻易取得的胜利似乎让她有些失望。她咬着嘴唇，看着棋盘上剩下的棋子，最终叹了口气，摇了摇头，自言自语起来。 嗯，看来你的策略确实有点欠考虑啊。 [kinu.Dad]除非我是故意放水让你，否则我觉得在第十二步之后，你根本不可能挽回局势了—— 她用手指在板上点了一下—— "就在那里。 而你却坚决不让她对你手下留情，否则这样做还有什么意义呢？ 呵呵，我总觉得自己不是那种喜欢玩捉迷藏游戏、或者明明没有意义还要故意拖延别人失败的人。那种游戏很快就会变得无聊起来。 不过，她玩得开心吗？ 不得不承认，这并不是游戏本身带来的。但和你在一起度过时光，总是非常愉快的。 [kinu.Dad]." 这可真是个嘴甜舌滑、会讨好人的家伙，你见过这样的吗？ |随着游戏的进行，你的九尾狐女儿逐渐成为了众人关注的焦点——她那冰蓝色的眼睛紧紧盯着棋盘，目光愈发专注。几乎是在无意识的情况下，她的三条尾巴伸到了身前，她将自己那柔软的毛皮紧紧抱在身上，此时的她的行动变得有条不紊，再没有之前那种漫不经心的样子了。 嗯…… 似乎她真的很享受这种有一定难度的挑战——或者说，这种挑战确实比那些简单的任务要有趣得多。 [kiyoko.numKits 3|她的兄弟姐妹通常都会配合。|她是在与自己的较量中取得进步的。]你也会全力以赴的——因为如果你失败了，那肯定不是因为没有努力。战场上的局势，也就是那块木制的游戏棋盘，每时每刻都在发生变化，战争的局势似乎会随着一时的冲动而改变；在看似毫无征兆的情况下，绮奴会突然使出一连串的招数，让你在瞬间陷入被动，完全被其牵制住。 ……就是那里。干得不错。 [kinu.Dad]不过看起来最终我还是赢了。有那么一刻，我以为那个策略不会奏效，但后来我想，此刻正是冒险的时候。 真是孤注一掷的举动啊，嗯？ [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|你在年轻时有过一段时间来练习国际象棋和跳棋这类游戏，其中的一些策略，即使不能完全适用，也确实可以运用到她玩的这些游戏中。希望你能够为各种棋局提供新的视角——那些清子所处的文化环境可能并不熟悉这些策略。 嗯……也可以这么说法吧。 [kinu.Dad]我非常感谢你花时间与我一起玩游戏。我觉得从这些经历中我学到了一些东西。如果你们能在其他时间再和我一起玩，我想我会学到更多。 呵呵，这算是一种邀请吗？嗯，等着瞧吧。 嗯，我总是很享受能和你在一起的时光。 [kinu.Dad]所以你绝对应该接受我的这个提议！ |嗯，考虑到你在年轻时并没有太多机会玩这类游戏，能够把她逼到这种境地，本身就已经算是一种成就了。 绮奴抬头看着你，她的表情难以捉摸。 嗯，如果你能多玩一会儿的话 [kinu.Dad]谁知道呢，也许你可以通过多和我一起玩策略游戏来取得进步呢？ 哦，她没必要说得那么委婉——只要她想玩，你随时都乐意陪她一起玩。 嗯，妈妈说，如果你说明自己的行为会给他们带来什么好处，人们就更有可能同意你的观点。 ] 哼，这简直太狡黠可爱了，不是吗？ |绮奴一开始采取了强势的开局和大胆的策略，但当你挫败了她的先发制人之举后，她很快便转为更为保守的打法。你的女儿眉头紧锁，仔细思考着每一步棋，或许她意识到自己有些过于冒进了，或许只是因为过于自信而已。 不过，她也是以牙还牙的。在这块木质游戏棋盘上，战争的局势不断变幻，双方的每一步行动都显得缓慢而谨慎。茶水渐渐变凉，米饼也孤零零地躺在盘子里，但你们俩根本没有时间去在意这些琐事。 此时，绮奴双手托着下巴，嘴唇紧闭成一条细细的直线，那双冰蓝色的眼睛在棋盘上来回扫视。 当那一刻真正来临时，对你来说，和对她来说一样令人惊讶；随着最后一声清脆的碰撞声，你将手中的棋子放在棋盘上，宣告自己战胜了女儿。 恭喜你， [kinu.Dad]看来你赢了。 所以你得到了它。不过，这并不意味着什么——你可能只是运气好，或者她可能只是粗心大意而已。 哦，求你了。千万不要低估自己的能力。 [kinu.Dad]那么，也许你应该改天再和我一起玩，这样就能证明这并不是偶然发生的。 你笑了。她真的那么急需有能力的玩家来挑战她吗？ 不仅仅如此。今天我不仅学到了一些东西，而且我也非常享受我们共度的时光。我们并不总是有时间一起玩耍，所以这样的时刻就显得更加特别了，你懂我的意思吧？那种因为分离而更加珍惜彼此的感觉，以及所有这些美好的情感。 他/她没必要把事情说得那么夸张。 ] ] 无论如何，还是要再次感谢你。我会留在这里，喝完茶，稍后再去把棋盘拿过来，好吗？现在，我想回顾一下我们刚才进行的这局游戏，仔细分析一下我们的每一步行动，看看有哪些地方可以做得更好。 你点了点头，站起身来，轻轻拍了拍她的头。她真的是把这些游戏当得很认真啊，不是吗？ 绮奴在被人抚摸的时候扭来扭去，显得很不自在。 呵呵，如果什么事情都掉以轻心，是永远不可能掌握它的。 [kinu.Dad]哎呀！不是那里，这里会被挠痒的！嗯，也许你现在应该去找妈妈吧，好吗？你这样不停地挠我的耳朵，我根本没法集中注意力思考了。 哈！你再最后检查一下绮奴的头发，然后跟你的漂亮女儿道别吧。下次你去看她妈妈的时候，她还会在这里的。
rows.raw: " With that, Kinu breaks off into a quick jog for her home, motioning for you to wait here. The little kitsune can be fast when she puts her mind to it — you don't think more than fifteen minutes have passed before she returns with the board and pieces in her arms, ears all perky and her three silky tails having taken a life of their own with her excitement. "All right, then! Let's find a nice place to sit down and play! There're few things better in life than enjoying a game out with a hilltop breeze caressing your skin; I hope you can share in this simple pleasure, [kinu.Dad]!" So it comes to pass that you and your kitsune daughter wind up in the shade of a parasol, facing each other down over a game of [rand|go|shogi]. You're not exactly sure where the tea and rice crackers came from — one moment they weren't there, the next moment they were — but it's not done to question things too deeply around here. At least the tea is hot and the crackers passable, if very bland and dry. To you, it's like eating paper, but Kinu doesn't seem to mind in the least. For the next hour or so — time is rather indeterminate in the astral plane — all that can be heard is the clacking of pieces against the board, broken every so often by the gentle tinkling of wind chimes. [var0|Kinu's usually cheerful and carefree expression has gathered into one of absolute concentration, brows furrowed as her ice-blue eyes flick back and forth. Those aren't just gears turning in that cute little head of hers — it's an entire assembly of deviously complex mechanisms. Seconds tick by between each of your moves, a strange gravitas suffusing the board as pieces are picked up and set down with grim finality. [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|Though you're not too familiar with the game itself, you've had plenty of chances to play chess and other strategy board games in the past, and the principles are eerily similar to what you're facing now. Some things truly are universal, one supposes. |Although you really haven't had the chance to play such board games in the past, you nevertheless manage to intuitively connect some of the strategies to your experiences growing up as [a] [pc.background], and a number of possibilities become open to you. Maybe you're just talented at this kind of stuff. ] The game continues to drag on. At this point, even Kinu's ears have stilled, stiff and alert on her head as she studies the pieces on the board. Then at last, the endgame. [rand|"I believe I've won, [kinu.Dad]." Why yes, she has. She has indeed won, although by the looks of things it was a very close game. Thinking back on it, there were a couple of points back there where making a slightly different move would have radically changed the game's outcome. Kinu purses her lips and eyes the board once more. "I'm not going to deny that; you gave me a run for my money. Ehehe, Mama is the only other person who can do that, and she doesn't have all the time in the world to play with me all day. "Either way, this was a good game. It was fun! I think I learned a few things I want to try out next time." Of course. You've enjoyed your time with her, too. |"I believe you've won, [kinu.Dad]." Why, so you have. That's actually rather surprising. "Is it? I'm just good at this, I never quite said I was unbeatable." She looks down at the board again and wiggles in her seat. "Yeah, I see it now, [kinu.Dad]. I could've won if I'd done this —" she jabs at the board with a finger — "and this and this twenty moves ago." Thinking with a clear head is hard enough. Doing so under pressure is a skill one needs to cultivate over time. She may be talented, but experience is something that can't be rushed. That being said, you've no doubt she'll be a force to be reckoned with in the future. "Ehe. This is kinda embarrassing... I'm not sure I deserve the praise if I still lost in the end. It was fun, though. I learned a lot!" So long as she remembers that there generally are more opportunities to learn from loss and failure than from coming out ahead, she'll do just fine. And yes, you quite enjoyed your time with her. ] |[rand|The picture of peaceful serenity doesn't last long, though. Within a handful of moves, your kitsune daughter has completely outmaneuvered you and has free rein of the board. It's not long after that you're forced to admit defeat, perhaps a little relieved that this wasn't dragged out any longer than it needed to be. On her part, Kinu looks a little disappointed at the easy victory, chewing her lip as she looks over what pieces remain on the board. Eventually, she sighs and shakes her head, mumbling to herself. "Well, guess you had a bit of bad strategy back there, [kinu.Dad]. Unless I intentionally went easy on you, I don't think there was any way you could've salvaged the situation past the twelfth move back —" she jabs a finger on the board — "there." And you absolutely refuse to let her go easy on you, otherwise what would be the point? "Ehe. I like to think that I'm not the kind of person to enjoy cat-and-mouse games and drag out someone's loss when it's clear there's not much point to doing so. Those get boring fast." Still, did she have fun? "Not from the game itself, I'll admit to that. But spending time with you is always great, [kinu.Dad]." Now there's a honey-tongued little flatterer if you ever saw one. |As the game proceeds, your kitsune daughter gradually becomes a pinpoint of intense focus, her ice-blue eyes narrowing as she studies the board. Almost unconsciously, Kinu's three tails sweep out to her front, and she hugs her own silken fur close to herself as her moves become much more methodical and much less lackadaisical. "Hmm..." It's almost as if she's enjoying being decently challenged — or at least, more of a challenge than [kiyoko.numKits 3|her siblings usually put up|she gets from playing against herself]. You're going to give it your all, too — if you lose, it's not going to be from lack of trying. The state of the battlefield that's the wooden game board shifts from moment to moment, the tides of war turning at seemingly a whim; it's hard to discern who exactly has the upper hand until seemingly out of nowhere, Kinu pulls off a series of moves that has you completely outmaneuvered in moments. "...And there. Good show, [kinu.Dad], but seems like I win in the end. For a moment I thought that gambit wasn't going to work, but then that, more than anything else, was the time to take a risk." A desperation move, huh? [pc.bg acolyte noblescion arcanist scholar|You've had some time to do things like chess and checkers in your youth, and some of the strategies do carry over to these games of hers, if not completely. Hopefully, you've been able to give a new perspective on various plays that Kiyoko's home culture wouldn't be familiar with. "Weeeelll... that's one way of putting it, [kinu.Dad]. I'm very thankful for the time you've taken to play with me. I think I learned something from all this. Maybe I'd learn more if you played with me again some other time." Heh. Is that an invitation? Well, you'll see. "Well, I always enjoy the time I get to spend with you, [kinu.Dad], so you should definitely take me up on that offer!" |Well, considering that you didn't have much chance to play these sorts of games in your youth, being able to back her into a corner like this must be some kind of achievement in and of itself. Kinu looks up at you, her expression inscrutable. "Well, if you got to play more, [kinu.Dad], who knows how you might improve? Perhaps you should play more strategy games with me in the future?" Oh, she doesn't have to couch it like that — you'll gladly play with her any time she wants. "Well, Mama says that people are more likely to agree with you if you point out how your actions are going to benefit them." ] Psh, isn't that just adorably devious. |Kinu starts off with a strong opening and bold play, but quickly falls into a far more conservative strategy when you stymie her opening gambit. Your daughter's brows knit and furrow as she considers each move deeply, perhaps realizing that she's gotten in ahead of herself, perhaps due to simple overconfidence. Still, she gives as good as she takes. The tides of war shift back and forth on the battlefield of the wooden game board, each move by either party slow and deliberate. Untouched, the tea grows cold and the rice crackers lie forlornly on their plate, but neither of you have time for such trivialities. By this point, Kinu's lips are a thin, straight line as she cups her chin in a hand, those ice-blue eyes of hers darting back and forth across the board. When it happens, it surprises you almost as much as it does her; with a final, resounding clack, you set the piece in your hand down on the board and claim victory over your daughter. "Congratulations, [kinu.Dad]. It appears that you've won." So you have. That doesn't mean anything, though — you could have gotten lucky, or she could have been careless. "Oh, please. Don't undersell yourself, [kinu.Dad]. Now then, perhaps you ought to play with me more at another time to show that this wasn't a fluke." You grin. Is she really that starved for competent players to challenge? "It's more than that. Not only did I learn a few things today, but I always enjoy the time we spend together. We don't get to play all the time, so that makes it extra special, you know? Absence, fondness, and all that good stuff." He, she doesn't need to lay it on that thick. ] ] "Either way, thank you once more. I'll stay here, finish up the tea, and pick up the board later, okay? For now, I'd like to go over the game we just had, review our moves and see what could have been done better." You nod, stand and give her a pat on the head. She really takes these games seriously, doesn't she? Kinu squirms under the petting. "Ehe, you don't get good at anything by taking it lightly, [kinu.Dad]. Eee! Not there, it tickles! Um, maybe you should go and see Mama now, okay? I can't think straight with you petting my ears like this." Ha! You give Kinu's hair one final run-through, then say goodbye to your foxy daughter. She'll be here the next time you drop by to visit her mother."

rows.original: the traditional brave adventures/knights in shining armor. Group arcanist/scholar/acolyte in another, stories about gods and spirits and magicians. Barbarian/hunter in another, focus on mysticism/animism/paganism-esque stories. Slum rat/courtesan for urban myths and tales focused around the cities and injustice. Dig around for various myths/fairy tales. "Hooray, a story! I love stories! Mama tells me stories from her homeland, but it's nice to hear tales from all kinds of places! Will you tell me a story from where you grew up?" From where you grew up, eh? Let's see if you can't recall anything good... but first, might as well get comfortable, since this is probably going to take a while. Kinu excitedly leads the both of you over to a mossy tree stump, and you take a seat on the grassy soil with your backs to it, your daughter snuggling up to you. Now, let's see... stories you remember from your youth...
rows.translation: 传统的勇敢冒险故事，以及那些身披闪亮铠甲的骑士们。还有另一类故事，讲述的是法师、学者和学徒们的传奇经历，其中充斥着关于神灵、精灵和魔法师的故事。再有就是以野蛮人或猎人为主角的故事，这类故事侧重于神秘主义、万物有灵论或异教风格的主题。而对于都市传说来说，则以贫民窟居民或妓女作为主角，讲述发生在城市里那些与不公相关的故事。当然，我们还可以挖掘各种不同的神话和童话故事。 太好了，有故事听了！我超爱听故事的！妈妈会给我讲她家乡的故事，不过听到来自各种各样地方的故事也真是太有趣了！你能给我讲讲你成长的地方的故事吗？ 在你成长的地方，对吧？让我们看看你是否还能想起一些美好的回忆……不过首先，还是先放松下来吧，因为这个过程可能会花一些时间。绮奴兴奋地带着你们俩来到一棵长满苔藓的树桩旁，你靠在树桩旁的草地上坐下，你的女儿则依偎在你身边。 那么，现在让我们来想想……你年轻时记得的一些故事吧……
