rows.original: As you crest the hilltop, Kinu comes jogging up to greet you, arms hidden behind her back. From the way her three tails are swishing all over the place, your daughter's up to something — good or bad, that remains to be seen. "[kinu.Dad]! You're here! I did a divination and you showed up just like it said you would, so I went ahead and made preparations!" Ooh, preparations — that sounds ominous enough, all right. Now, what was she preparing for, and what does she have hidden behind her back? "It's — it's a present! For you! Because you've been giving me things... and Mama says that it's very important to Keros that we kitsune repay good deeds done for us out of the kindness of one's heart. I know you can't really take things out of this place with you when you leave, so I tried to think up a present that you can enjoy here!" Ah, so it's a religious duty to pay back this karma thing which Kiyoko sometimes talks about. Kinu makes a pouty face at that. "But it's more than that, [kinu.Dad]. I always feel really happy when you get me sweet fruit as presents. Now I want to make you feel happy too, so, um, here's the present. Ta-daaaah!" With that, Kinu brings out her hands from behind her back, letting you take in the surprise she's planned for you. [rand|There's... nothing? Half-suspecting a mischievous trick or some sort, you eye your little kitsune daughter, who simply beams at you and pounces forward to grab your legs in a wide-armed hug. "Not nothing, silly! As repayment for all the things you've given me, you get one fluffy kitsune kit!" Kinu makes a happy little noise in the back of her throat and begins rubbing the side of her head against you, white-furred foxy ears brushing up against your [pc.skinFurScales]. "I'm so amazing, I make a great gift for anyone who wants to be healed with fluffiness!" Healed with fluffiness, eh? It's hard to argue with that, especially when Kinu's three tails have come around to her front and have started massaging away at your ankles. Sheesh... do kitsune know how to do this by instinct, or has her mother taught her a few things? Either way, while Kinu is less fluffy than her mother is, her fur has a flowing texture to it that reminds you of a warm breeze's caress. "Ehe... am I doing it right, [kinu.Dad]? Can you feel my happiness passing on to you?" Well, even if she weren't, there's enough happiness being generated here that you can't tell the difference. "Eeheehee!" Kinu rubs herself against you a few more times for good measure, then pulls away with a sigh, her three tails swishing so quickly you're amazed they're not bumping into each other. |Held in her hands is a little black bowl, complete with lid — the kind that Kiyoko serves soup in. Proudly, your kitsune daughter presents it to you in both hands, and you receive the gift with all due grace, careful not to spill any. It's warm but not hot, and as Kinu withdraws her hands brush against yours — my, they're just as toasty as the soup bowl itself. Just how long has she been keeping it warm for you? Kinu giggles. "That doesn't matter, [kinu.Dad]. I could have held it all day and not gotten tired. Have some, okay?" Hm, that's a very savoury smell coming from within. It's kind of foreign, and yet familiar at the same time — earthy, inasmuch as mushrooms are. You give it another sniff, more exacting this time, and [pc.ra lupine|a heartwarming scent of at least several different types of root vegetables rises from the lid to greet you. It's not as fine or distinct as a soup made with meat stock would be, but it's about as good as a wholly vegetable soup could ever get.|the fine, warm scent of a medley of vegetables rises from the lid to greet you.] No time like the present, then. Indeed, when you uncover the lid, a warm, clear broth with several kinds of root vegetables you recognize — and more that you don't — greets you while Kinu hops around and helpfully offers you a spoon. "It's kenchin soup, [kinu.Dad]! One of the bestest things to eat after sweet fruit! It always makes me feel happy inside whenever I have some, so this is a great way to repay some of the happiness you always give me!" Sheesh. With her so enthusiastic and bubbly about it, there's no need to push the stuff on you. As Kinu stares expectantly, you take the spoon and have an experimental sip. The flavor's definitely not something you'd usually find in the Frost Marches, rich and hearty, yet without the characteristic heaviness that accompanies similar meat-based soups. The first sip is followed by another, and another, until even the root veggies are gone. "Well, was it good, [kinu.Dad]? Was it?" You finished it all, didn't you? "Yeah, but you might have done so to be polite... don't want to be rude, but I want to be sure." All right, all right. Some of the foreign veggies were definitely an acquired taste, but the rest was pretty good. It wasn't bad, just something that your palate isn't used to. Kinu gives you a weak smile and twiddles her thumbs. "Right, so it wasn't anything I could really control..." If anything, it's an impetus for her to start exploring things on her own rather than just learning what's already been covered. Sooner or later, she'll have learnt all there is to be reasonably taught on a subject, and then the world itself will have to be her teacher. |"I'm going to sing for you, [kinu.Dad]!" Sing, huh? That's a pretty neat gift. "Yep! I'm going to sing, and share my happiness that way!" Without further ado, Kinu takes a deep breath, and bursts into song, a wordless, melancholic melody. Hey, your daughter's got a pretty good voice. It'll probably change once she's no longer a child and it's not exactly the same flute-like tone as her mother's, but it's high-pitched and sweet, not too different from when she gets really excited. [pc.bg minstrel|She's not half-bad, actually. There're some parts where she goes off-key — whether it be from excitement, nervousness or otherwise — but your daughter can generally keep a tune together. Maybe you could teach her a thing or two when she's older, or when you have the time.|You don't know enough about music to be able to provide any meaningful criticism, but in your layman's opinion it's really, really soothing.] The singing doesn't last very long — perhaps a handful of minutes — but Kinu looks absolutely intense by the end of it all, every single muscle in her little body unwinding as she finishes the last verse and looks up to you for approval. Has her mother been teaching her much in the way of vocal control? "Ehe. A bit? Well, Mama hasn't much time to teach me much in the way of music outside of the koto. I think she much prefers poetry as an art form." Ah. Well, either way, you have to thank her for the music. That was quite lovely — if she'd meant to share her happiness with you, then it worked. |Cradled in your daughter's cupped hands is an orange-brown fruit about the size of a large apple. Smiling from ear to ear, Kinu stands on tiptoe and presents it to you in the most reverent fashion a hyperactive eight year-old kitsune can. "It's a persimmon! For you!" A persimmon, eh? The fruit feels firm and crisp under your fingers, the skin smooth and without blemish. There's a certain something or the other to it that you can't quite place, though... "I spent so long picking one out for you, [kinu.Dad]! It's got just the right size, shape, color and smell! It's a pretty great persimmon, and I always get the warm fuzzies when I eat one like this, so you will too!" Honestly speaking, it's not as if you could tell, what with not having that much experience with persimmons of this sort, but there's no reason to let Kinu know that. You thank your daughter, give her a pat on the head, and study the fruit once more. "I washed it just before I came out to greet you, so it's clean! You can eat it just as it is!" Well, no reason to put it off any longer, then. It might have been better had this been sliced, but whole is just fine; there's a certain tartness to the peel as you bite into it, but it's otherwise very sweet. Kinu watches with rapt attention as you devour the persimmon, peel and all — with her intense gaze on you like this, you would've eaten the whole thing even if you'd hated it... "It's good, isn't it?" Oh, it's good. But the reason you're happy isn't because the persimmon was good, it's because it came from her. Your daughter just squeals and claps her hands to her cheeks, her big, fluffy ears twitching all over the place as a light blush creeps into her cheeks. Gods, Kiyoko really taught her well when it comes to laying on the flattery. "Really?" Yep! The blush deepens. "Ehehe. You really know how to lay on the flattery, [kinu.Dad]." It takes one to know one. Still, that was a great persimmon she had there. |There's... nothing? You peer into Kinu's cupped hands, which are perfectly and utterly empty save for a couple of calluses and healed-over scratches, no doubt from playing in the forest. "Oh, it's there, [kinu.Dad]. You just have to look closer. Like, really close." Oh? Deciding to play along, you stoop down and eye Kinu's cupped hands up close. Nope, still nothing... "Just a bit closer, [kinu.Dad]..." Like this? "Ah-ha! Now you're completely defenseless and vulnerable! Mwah!" Standing on tiptoe, your little kitsune daughter inches her head up to plant a kiss on your cheek, then quickly hops back, looking a little bashful. Ah, so that was her gift. "Eehee!" Gods, who's supposed to be receiving the gift here, you or her? She's at least twice as excited about this as you are. ] "See? See? It was a great gift, wasn't it? Even if you can't take anything material with you when you leave, you can still bring the memories along! And that's great! Mama always says it's not so much the exact nature of the gift, but the thought and effort that goes into it, but I personally suspect that she just says that so she can be cheap when giving gifts." Hah... now she's just making you want to get your daughter out of here all the faster so you can actually receive more kinds of gifts from her. Kinu preens a little at the praise. "I wouldn't mind! So, now that you're here and I've given you your gift, can we play now before you go in and see Mama? Pleasepleaseplease?"
rows.translation: 当你爬上山顶时，绮奴慢跑着过来迎接你，双手部背在身后。从她那三条尾巴乱晃的样子来看，你的女儿肯定在搞什么名堂——是好是坏，那就有待观看了。 "[kinu.Dad]你来了！我之前做了占卜，结果果然如占卜所言，你会出现，所以我就提前做好了准备！ 哦，准备工作啊——这听起来确实挺不祥的，好吧。那么，她到底在准备什么？又隐藏了什么不可告人的把戏呢？ 这是——这是一份礼物！是给你的！因为你一直都在给我送东西……妈妈说，对凯洛斯来说，我们作为狐妖，一定要回报那些出于善意为我们所做的一切。我知道你离开的时候不可能把这些东西带走，所以我就想了一份你在这里就可以享受的礼物！ 啊，所以偿还这种“因果报应”之类的东西，似乎是一种宗教义务吧？清子有时候也会提到这个。 听到这里，绮奴露出了不高兴的表情。 但不仅如此， [kinu.Dad]每当你送我甜美的水果作为礼物时，我总是感到非常开心。现在我也想让你开心起来，所以，嗯，这就是我的礼物。瞧——送给你啦！ 说着，绮奴将双手部从背后抽了出来，让你看到了她为你们准备的这个惊喜。 [rand|什么都没有？你半信半疑地怀疑这可能是个恶作剧，于是看向你那可爱的小狐女儿，只见她开心地朝你跑过来，张开双臂紧紧抱住了你的腿。 可不是什么小礼物，傻瓜！作为对你为我做过的所有事情的回报，你将得到一只毛茸茸的狐妖小精灵！ 绮奴在喉咙深处发出愉悦的声音，然后开始用头蹭你，她那白色毛茸茸的狐狸耳朵轻轻触碰到你的身体。 [pc.skinFurScales]. 我太棒了，对于那些希望拥有柔软触感、获得治愈的人来说，我简直是完美的礼物！ 被柔软的毛茸茸触感治愈了，嗯？这一点确实很难反驳，尤其是当绮奴的三条尾巴围到她身前，开始轻轻按摩你的脚踝时。天啊……难道狐妖天生就会这样，还是她的母亲教了她这些技巧？不管怎样，虽然绮奴的毛没有她母亲那么浓密，但她的毛发质地柔软顺滑，让人感受到如同温暖微风轻拂般的舒适感。 呃……我这样做对吗？ [kinu.Dad]你能感受到我的快乐正在传递给你吗？ 嗯，即使她不是这样，这里产生的快乐也已经足够多，以至于你根本无法分辨其中的差别了。 嘻嘻嘻！ 基努又蹭了你几次，以确保效果，然后叹了口气拉开距离，她的三条尾巴摆动得如此之快，让你惊讶于它们竟然没有互相碰撞。 |她手部中捧着一个小小的黑色碗，还配有盖子——就是那种千代子用来盛汤的碗。你的狐女儿骄傲地用双手部将这个碗递给你，你也优雅地接过了这份礼物，小心翼翼地防止汤洒出来。汤的温度适中，不冷也不热。当纪奈收回双手部时，她的手部触到了你的手部——天啊，她的手部和那个汤碗一样温暖。她究竟为你们保温了这么久呢？ 纪奈咯咯地笑了起来。 那没关系， [kinu.Dad]我可以一整天都这样坚持下去，而不会感到疲倦。来，吃点吧，好吗？ 嗯，从里面传出来的这种气味真是非常诱人。它有点陌生，却又让人感到熟悉——那种属于大自然的气息，毕竟蘑菇本来就属于大自然的一部分。你再闻一次，这次更加仔细地闻 [pc.ra lupine|从锅盖中散发出来的，是一种由多种根茎类蔬菜混合而成的、令人感到温暖的气息。这种味道虽然没有用肉汤熬制的汤那么浓郁、那么层次分明，但就已经算是纯蔬菜汤所能达到的最佳境界了。|从锅盖中散发出来的那种浓郁而温暖的蔬菜混合香气，会迎面扑来，让你立刻感受到它的存在。] 现在正是最好的时机。的确，当你揭开盖子时，一股温暖清亮的汤汁便会迎面扑来——其中含有几种你熟悉的根茎类蔬菜，也有一些你并不认识的材料。而绮奴则会在一旁蹦来跳去，热心地递给你一把勺子。 这是肯钦汤。 [kinu.Dad]在吃了甜水果之后，这绝对是最好的食物之一！每当我吃到它的时候，总会让我感到内心充满快乐，所以，这真的是一种回报你一直带给我的快乐的绝佳方式啊！ 哎呀，她这么热情洋溢地推荐，实在没必要再强迫你尝试了。在绮奴充满期待的目轻型注视下，你拿起了勺子，试着尝了一口。这种味道绝对不是你在霜冻之地能尝到的——浓郁醇厚，却又没有那种类似肉汤才会有的油腻感。第一口尝下去后，你又接连喝了几口，直到那些根茎类蔬菜也被吃轻型了。 嗯，觉得怎么样？好玩吗？ [kinu.Dad]是吗？ 你把所有事情都完成了，对吧？ 是啊，但你这么做可能只是出于礼貌……我并不是想冒犯你，只是想确认一下而已。 好吧，好吧。有些外国蔬菜确实需要一段时间来适应，但其他的还是相当不错的。并不是说全部都不行 糟糕只是某些你们的味觉还不习惯的东西罢了。 绮奴露出一个淡淡的微笑，开始玩弄着自己的拇指。 没错，这件事其实并不是我能够控制的…… 如果说这有什么作用的话，那就是促使她开始自主探索事物，而不仅仅局限于学习那些已经被讲授过的内容。迟早，她会学到关于某个主题所有可以被合理教授的知识，而到了那时，整个世界本身才会成为她的老师。 |我要为你歌唱， [kinu.Dad]!" 唱歌，哈？这真是份相当不错的礼物。 没错！我要唱歌，通过这种方式来分享我的快乐！ 毫不迟疑，绮奴深吸一口气，开始唱起歌来——那是一段无词而充满忧郁旋律的歌声。嘿，你女儿的歌声还挺不错的。等她长大后，她的嗓音可能会发生变化，也不会再像她母亲那样拥有那种类似长笛的音色，但她的音调依然高亢而甜美，尤其是在她感到非常兴奋的时候，这种音色几乎不会有什么变化。 [pc.bg minstrel|其实，她唱得还不错。虽然有时候会跑调——不管是因为太兴奋、太紧张，还是其他原因——但总体来说，你女儿的唱功还是不错的。等她长大一些，或者你有空的时候，或许可以教她一些技巧。|你对音乐的了解还不够深入，因此无法给出任何有意义的评价，但以一个外行的角度来看，这段音乐确实非常、非常舒缓。] 这首歌的演唱时间并不长——大概只有几分钟而已——但当她唱完最后一段歌词，抬起头期待你的赞许时，绮奴的神情显得无比专注，她那小小的身体里的每一块肌肉似乎都在随着歌声的结束而逐渐放松下来。 她的母亲是否在声乐控制方面对她进行了很多指导呢？ 呵呵，有点吧？其实妈妈除了教我弹古筝之外，并没有太多时间来教我关于音乐的知识。我觉得她更喜欢将诗歌作为一种艺术形式来欣赏。 啊，不管怎样，你都得感谢她提供的这些音乐。真的非常棒——如果她真的是想与你分享她的快乐，那么她的目的就达到了。 |被你女儿那双小小的手部捧在掌心里的，是一个颜色呈橙棕色的水果，大小大概和一个大苹果差不多。绮奴笑得合不拢嘴，踮起脚来，以一个活泼好动的八岁狐妖所能表现出的最虔诚的方式，将这个水果递给了你。 这是一个柿子！是给你的！ 柿子，嗯？这种水果在手部指间摸起来紧实而脆嫩，果皮轻型滑且没有任何瑕疵。不过，它身上似乎还带着某种难以言喻的特殊味道或特质…… 我花了这么长时间来为你挑选一个， [kinu.Dad]它的大小、形状、颜色和味道都恰到好处！这是一个非常棒的柿子，每当我吃到这样的柿子时，总会感到一阵暖意涌上心头，你吃了一定也会有同样的感觉！ 说实话，由于你对这种柿子并没有太多经验，其实也很难分辨出来，不过也没有必要让纪奈知道这一点。你只需要感谢女儿，轻轻拍拍她的头，然后再仔细观察一下这种水果就行了。 在我出来迎接你之前，我刚刚把它洗过了，所以现在很干净！你可以直接吃它哦！ 那么，再拖延下去也没意义了。如果把这个果实切成小块可能会更好吃，但整个吃下去也完全没问题；咬下去的时候果皮会带有一丝酸味，不过整体来说还是非常甜的。当你把整个柿子连果皮一起吃掉的时候，绮奴正全神贯注地注视着你——在她这样热切的目轻型注视下，即使你真的不喜欢这个柿子，也会把它吃轻型的…… 挺好的，不是吗？ 哦，确实不错。但你开心的原因并不是因为那个柿子有多好吃，而是因为它来自她。 你的女儿兴奋得尖叫起来，还用手部拍着自己的脸颊，她那又大又蓬松的耳朵不停地抖动着，脸上也逐渐浮现出一抹红晕。天啊，在讨好别人这方面，清子真的把她教得很好啊。 真的吗？ 没错！ 那种红晕变得更加明显了。 呵呵，你还真会说些奉承话呢。 [kinu.Dad]." 知己难求。不过，她手部里的那个柿子确实很不错。 |什么都没有？你仔细观察绮奴那双合拢的双手部，里面空空如也，只有几处老茧和已经愈合的划痕，这些划痕无疑是她在森林里玩耍时留下的。 哦，它在那里。 [kinu.Dad]你只需要再仔细看一看，真的，要看得再近一些。 哦？既然你决定配合了，我就弯下腰，仔细看了看绮奴那合拢的双手部……还是没有东西…… 再近一点就好， [kinu.Dad]..." 就这样吗？ 啊哈！现在你完全处于无防备的状态，毫无抵抗力了！哇哈哈！ 你那小狐女儿踮起脚尖，把头凑过来在你脸上轻吻了一下，然后迅速跳了回去，看起来有点害羞。啊，真是这样啊 那个 这是她送给我的礼物。 嘻嘻！ 天啊，这个礼物到底应该是谁来收呢？是你还是她？她对这件事的兴奋程度至少是你的一倍。 ] 看到了吧？这确实是一份很棒的礼物，对吧？即使离开的时候不能带走任何实物，但那些回忆却可以永远留在心中，这难道不是一件很棒的事情吗？妈妈总是说，礼物的价值并不在于它的物质形态，而在于送礼人的心意和付出，但我个人觉得，她这么说其实只是为了在送礼的时候能少花点钱罢了。 哈……现在她这样做，只会让你更想尽快把女儿带离这里，这样你就能收到她送来的更多礼物了。 绮奴听到这样的赞美，不禁有些得意起来。 我完全不介意！既然你现在已经来了，而且我也已经给了你礼物，那在我们进去见妈妈之前，我们现在能开始玩吗？求求你啦？
rows.raw: " As you crest the hilltop, Kinu comes jogging up to greet you, arms hidden behind her back. From the way her three tails are swishing all over the place, your daughter's up to something — good or bad, that remains to be seen. "[kinu.Dad]! You're here! I did a divination and you showed up just like it said you would, so I went ahead and made preparations!" Ooh, preparations — that sounds ominous enough, all right. Now, what was she preparing for, and what does she have hidden behind her back? "It's — it's a present! For you! Because you've been giving me things... and Mama says that it's very important to Keros that we kitsune repay good deeds done for us out of the kindness of one's heart. I know you can't really take things out of this place with you when you leave, so I tried to think up a present that you can enjoy here!" Ah, so it's a religious duty to pay back this karma thing which Kiyoko sometimes talks about. Kinu makes a pouty face at that. "But it's more than that, [kinu.Dad]. I always feel really happy when you get me sweet fruit as presents. Now I want to make you feel happy too, so, um, here's the present. Ta-daaaah!" With that, Kinu brings out her hands from behind her back, letting you take in the surprise she's planned for you. [rand|There's... nothing? Half-suspecting a mischievous trick or some sort, you eye your little kitsune daughter, who simply beams at you and pounces forward to grab your legs in a wide-armed hug. "Not nothing, silly! As repayment for all the things you've given me, you get one fluffy kitsune kit!" Kinu makes a happy little noise in the back of her throat and begins rubbing the side of her head against you, white-furred foxy ears brushing up against your [pc.skinFurScales]. "I'm so amazing, I make a great gift for anyone who wants to be healed with fluffiness!" Healed with fluffiness, eh? It's hard to argue with that, especially when Kinu's three tails have come around to her front and have started massaging away at your ankles. Sheesh... do kitsune know how to do this by instinct, or has her mother taught her a few things? Either way, while Kinu is less fluffy than her mother is, her fur has a flowing texture to it that reminds you of a warm breeze's caress. "Ehe... am I doing it right, [kinu.Dad]? Can you feel my happiness passing on to you?" Well, even if she weren't, there's enough happiness being generated here that you can't tell the difference. "Eeheehee!" Kinu rubs herself against you a few more times for good measure, then pulls away with a sigh, her three tails swishing so quickly you're amazed they're not bumping into each other. |Held in her hands is a little black bowl, complete with lid — the kind that Kiyoko serves soup in. Proudly, your kitsune daughter presents it to you in both hands, and you receive the gift with all due grace, careful not to spill any. It's warm but not hot, and as Kinu withdraws her hands brush against yours — my, they're just as toasty as the soup bowl itself. Just how long has she been keeping it warm for you? Kinu giggles. "That doesn't matter, [kinu.Dad]. I could have held it all day and not gotten tired. Have some, okay?" Hm, that's a very savoury smell coming from within. It's kind of foreign, and yet familiar at the same time — earthy, inasmuch as mushrooms are. You give it another sniff, more exacting this time, and [pc.ra lupine|a heartwarming scent of at least several different types of root vegetables rises from the lid to greet you. It's not as fine or distinct as a soup made with meat stock would be, but it's about as good as a wholly vegetable soup could ever get.|the fine, warm scent of a medley of vegetables rises from the lid to greet you.] No time like the present, then. Indeed, when you uncover the lid, a warm, clear broth with several kinds of root vegetables you recognize — and more that you don't — greets you while Kinu hops around and helpfully offers you a spoon. "It's kenchin soup, [kinu.Dad]! One of the bestest things to eat after sweet fruit! It always makes me feel happy inside whenever I have some, so this is a great way to repay some of the happiness you always give me!" Sheesh. With her so enthusiastic and bubbly about it, there's no need to push the stuff on you. As Kinu stares expectantly, you take the spoon and have an experimental sip. The flavor's definitely not something you'd usually find in the Frost Marches, rich and hearty, yet without the characteristic heaviness that accompanies similar meat-based soups. The first sip is followed by another, and another, until even the root veggies are gone. "Well, was it good, [kinu.Dad]? Was it?" You finished it all, didn't you? "Yeah, but you might have done so to be polite... don't want to be rude, but I want to be sure." All right, all right. Some of the foreign veggies were definitely an acquired taste, but the rest was pretty good. It wasn't bad, just something that your palate isn't used to. Kinu gives you a weak smile and twiddles her thumbs. "Right, so it wasn't anything I could really control..." If anything, it's an impetus for her to start exploring things on her own rather than just learning what's already been covered. Sooner or later, she'll have learnt all there is to be reasonably taught on a subject, and then the world itself will have to be her teacher. |"I'm going to sing for you, [kinu.Dad]!" Sing, huh? That's a pretty neat gift. "Yep! I'm going to sing, and share my happiness that way!" Without further ado, Kinu takes a deep breath, and bursts into song, a wordless, melancholic melody. Hey, your daughter's got a pretty good voice. It'll probably change once she's no longer a child and it's not exactly the same flute-like tone as her mother's, but it's high-pitched and sweet, not too different from when she gets really excited. [pc.bg minstrel|She's not half-bad, actually. There're some parts where she goes off-key — whether it be from excitement, nervousness or otherwise — but your daughter can generally keep a tune together. Maybe you could teach her a thing or two when she's older, or when you have the time.|You don't know enough about music to be able to provide any meaningful criticism, but in your layman's opinion it's really, really soothing.] The singing doesn't last very long — perhaps a handful of minutes — but Kinu looks absolutely intense by the end of it all, every single muscle in her little body unwinding as she finishes the last verse and looks up to you for approval. Has her mother been teaching her much in the way of vocal control? "Ehe. A bit? Well, Mama hasn't much time to teach me much in the way of music outside of the koto. I think she much prefers poetry as an art form." Ah. Well, either way, you have to thank her for the music. That was quite lovely — if she'd meant to share her happiness with you, then it worked. |Cradled in your daughter's cupped hands is an orange-brown fruit about the size of a large apple. Smiling from ear to ear, Kinu stands on tiptoe and presents it to you in the most reverent fashion a hyperactive eight year-old kitsune can. "It's a persimmon! For you!" A persimmon, eh? The fruit feels firm and crisp under your fingers, the skin smooth and without blemish. There's a certain something or the other to it that you can't quite place, though... "I spent so long picking one out for you, [kinu.Dad]! It's got just the right size, shape, color and smell! It's a pretty great persimmon, and I always get the warm fuzzies when I eat one like this, so you will too!" Honestly speaking, it's not as if you could tell, what with not having that much experience with persimmons of this sort, but there's no reason to let Kinu know that. You thank your daughter, give her a pat on the head, and study the fruit once more. "I washed it just before I came out to greet you, so it's clean! You can eat it just as it is!" Well, no reason to put it off any longer, then. It might have been better had this been sliced, but whole is just fine; there's a certain tartness to the peel as you bite into it, but it's otherwise very sweet. Kinu watches with rapt attention as you devour the persimmon, peel and all — with her intense gaze on you like this, you would've eaten the whole thing even if you'd hated it... "It's good, isn't it?" Oh, it's good. But the reason you're happy isn't because the persimmon was good, it's because it came from her. Your daughter just squeals and claps her hands to her cheeks, her big, fluffy ears twitching all over the place as a light blush creeps into her cheeks. Gods, Kiyoko really taught her well when it comes to laying on the flattery. "Really?" Yep! The blush deepens. "Ehehe. You really know how to lay on the flattery, [kinu.Dad]." It takes one to know one. Still, that was a great persimmon she had there. |There's... nothing? You peer into Kinu's cupped hands, which are perfectly and utterly empty save for a couple of calluses and healed-over scratches, no doubt from playing in the forest. "Oh, it's there, [kinu.Dad]. You just have to look closer. Like, really close." Oh? Deciding to play along, you stoop down and eye Kinu's cupped hands up close. Nope, still nothing... "Just a bit closer, [kinu.Dad]..." Like this? "Ah-ha! Now you're completely defenseless and vulnerable! Mwah!" Standing on tiptoe, your little kitsune daughter inches her head up to plant a kiss on your cheek, then quickly hops back, looking a little bashful. Ah, so that was her gift. "Eehee!" Gods, who's supposed to be receiving the gift here, you or her? She's at least twice as excited about this as you are. ] "See? See? It was a great gift, wasn't it? Even if you can't take anything material with you when you leave, you can still bring the memories along! And that's great! Mama always says it's not so much the exact nature of the gift, but the thought and effort that goes into it, but I personally suspect that she just says that so she can be cheap when giving gifts." Hah... now she's just making you want to get your daughter out of here all the faster so you can actually receive more kinds of gifts from her. Kinu preens a little at the praise. "I wouldn't mind! So, now that you're here and I've given you your gift, can we play now before you go in and see Mama? Pleasepleaseplease?""

rows.original: "Aww, you're leaving already?" Indeed. It's been fun catching up with her, but you've got to go and see her mother. There're some matters you have to discuss with Kiyoko, as well as a handful of other grown-up things you might be doing with her. "Oh. Those sorts of things. Well, have fun playing with Mama! Make her happy, okay? Me, I'm going to run around in the forest and find a nice tree to climb. Bye bye!" With that, Kinu turns around and scampers for the trees. Her three tails flowing behind her are the last you see of your daughter, and she's gone.
rows.translation: 哎呀，你就要走了吗？ 确实，和她聊天真的很愉快，但你现在得去见见她的母亲了。有些事情你需要和清子讨论，还有一些其他成年人才会处理的事情，也可能需要和她一起解决。 哦。 那些 各种有趣的事情吧。好了，和妈妈一起玩得开心点！让她开心起来，好吗？而我呢，要去森林里跑跑，找一棵好树爬上去。再见啦！ 说完，绮奴便转身朝树林跑去。她那三条尾巴在身后摇摆着，那是你最后一次看到你的女儿了，之后她就消失在了树林中。
rows.raw: " "Aww, you're leaving already?" Indeed. It's been fun catching up with her, but you've got to go and see her mother. There're some matters you have to discuss with Kiyoko, as well as a handful of other grown-up things you might be doing with her. "Oh. Those sorts of things. Well, have fun playing with Mama! Make her happy, okay? Me, I'm going to run around in the forest and find a nice tree to climb. Bye bye!" With that, Kinu turns around and scampers for the trees. Her three tails flowing behind her are the last you see of your daughter, and she's gone."

rows.original: As you approach Kinu, your daughter brightens immediately and runs up to you, shaking all over with excitement. The little kitsune looks fit to start running in circles any moment now but manages to hold herself in through an act of superhuman willpower, instead settling from grabbing your [pc.armor] and alternating between tugging and pushing. Oh dear. Has she gotten into the peaches again? "Ehehe, no. But I did an augury this morning and it said you'd be coming today, so I went and got everything prepared! Come and see!" Prepared for — oh. Ah. Well! As Kinu drags you away and towards the hillside, you see waiting for you a large firepit ringed with stones, dry leaves and twigs already packed in its recesses and waiting to be set alight. A large plate has been set out on a low bench, heaped with the pine mushrooms you'd picked with Kinu the last time; even uncooked, a tantalising scent of earthy spiciness rises from the spread on offer.
rows.translation: 当你靠近纪努时，你的女儿立刻变得兴奋起来，跑向你，全身都在颤抖。那只小狐妖看起来随时都会开始绕圈奔跑，但它凭借超乎常人的意志力克制住了自己，只是紧紧地抓住你的手。 [pc.armor] 不断地拉扯和推搡着。 哦天哪，她又把那些桃子弄乱了吗？ 嘿嘿，不是的。不过今天早上我做了个占卜，结果说你今天会来，所以我就把所有东西都准备好了！快来看看吧！ 准备好了——哦，啊，太好了！ 当绮奴拉着你往山坡走去时，你看到那里有一个被石头、干叶子和细枝围成的大篝火坑，那些燃料已经堆放在坑里，随时可以点燃。一张大盘子被放在低矮的长凳上，上面堆满了你上次和绮奴一起采到的松茸；即使还没有煮过，这些松茸散发出的浓郁香气也已经让人垂涎欲滴了。

Oh dear. Has she gotten into the peaches again? "Ehehe, no. But I did an augury this morning and it said you'd be coming today, so I went and got everything prepared! Come and see!" Prepared for — oh. Ah. Well! A large plate has been set out on a low bench, heaped with the pine mushrooms you'd picked with Kinu the last time; even uncooked, a tantalising scent of earthy spiciness rises from the spread on offer. "

rows.original: Oh, and Kiyoko's there too. Your fox-wife is carrying a large metal pot, [kiyoko.pregStage 3|waddling over from the cabin as she balances her burden in front of her huge pregnant belly. |balancing it in front of her as she carefully makes her way over from the cabin.] Steam seeps out from under the lid, wafting up and away — goodness, they really knew you were coming, didn't they? "My greetings," Kiyoko says with a small smile as she sets the pot down on the bench. "I hope you don't mind me being here as well. Our daughter wanted to make matsutake rice for this, but she hasn't got the process down just yet. It's more than simply following a recipe, after all." "Mama! Mama!" "There was a little too much for just rice, too, so I made some other things with our daughter's help. And then I realized we'd made too much for just two... so I thought you wouldn't mind having another mouth around to finish up all the food. [kiyoko.pregStage 1|Or two, for that matter," she adds, rubbing the rising swell of her pregnancy. "]You don't mind, do you?" Oh, of course not. This'll be a great family picnic. Kiyoko laughs and pats Kinu on the scruff of her neck. "I'm not sure it qualifies as a picnic, considering it's so close to home, but I'm sure it'll be wonderful nonetheless. You've been very good to Kinu of late, and I myself appreciate you taking the little rapscallion out of my fur every now and then." "Can we eat already? I'm huuuuungry." Okay, okay. While Kiyoko takes a seat, Kinu lights the firepit with a flick of her fingers, almost carelessly tossing a glob of foxfire into the twigs and tinder to set it alight. Once the flames are licking away merrily, she pads over to the plate of marinated mushrooms, spears one of the mushroom halves on a long stick, and offers it to you. "You go first, [kinu.Dad]! This is to thank you for always petting and playing with me!" Aw, shucks. You take the wooden skewer from Kinu and hold the mushroom half over the fire, watching hot air waver over the leaf fire as the matsutake begins to cook. Kinu takes a seat besides you on the bench, her big blue eyes fixed on the shroom as you turn it about in the fire. Before long, the sauce and oil on it starts to sizzle and pop, the matsutake itself turning a golden-brown as a delightful smell begins to waft into the air. "This brings back memories," Kiyoko says with a small sigh[kiyoko.pregStage 3|, her hands resting on her big pregnant belly]. "My mother and I would go out in the fall to pick matsutake in the pine forest — mid-autumn was one of the few times when she'd get a reprieve from her hectic schedule. We'd fill baskets with the delicacies, then head home happy... and now my own daughter is doing it with me." Kinu wiggles and squirms as Kiyoko pets her ears. "Hee hee!" "You will do the same with your own children when you have them, yes? I'm not the biggest fan of roasted and grilled food... but I will say that the best way to bring out the flavor of matsutake is simple preparation. Look, it's nearly done." And so it is. The once white portions of the halved mushroom are now a wonderful golden-brown, and the signature spicy aroma has been well and truly brought out by the cooking. Mother and daughter alike watch you intently as you raise the mushroom, and take a bite. Gods above. [pc.bg noblescion|The only thing that might compare to this are the truffles you once sampled in the heartlands.|You've never had the opportunity to taste anything this good.] And the fact that you have your foxy, floofy family at your side — that just makes it all the more intense. Ah... now this is happiness. The mushroom is firm and chewy — meaty, even, and possessed of a certain spicy flavor that's not peppery. A little like cinnamon, to be honest. "Was it good, [kinu.Dad]? I'm pretty awesome with soy sauce and rice wine!" You finished it, didn't you? "Yaaaaaaay!" "Now, now, both of you. There's plenty to be had, so there's no need to rush things. In addition to our daughter's offerings, I made some matsutake rice and egg custard as well. Why don't you try some as well? It'll certainly be a change from your usual fare." And so it goes. While Kinu sets to roasting the mushrooms in the fire, Kiyoko and you scoop out hearty servings of rice into big bowls. Your foxy wife wasn't kidding when she said she'd made a lot — one of these matsutake mushrooms sure goes a long way, especially with how thinly she can slice them. As the three of you settle down to eat on the warm hillside, part of you wishes that this could go on forever, that you wouldn't have to eventually return to the waking world and deal with the chaos Kasyrra's creating... [rand| "There, there," Kiyoko chides gently, pulling a finely embroidered handkerchief out of her yukata and wiping off Kinu's face. "Your mouth is covered in food, daughter... here, let me clean you off." Kinu wiggles and squirms. "Mwa! Thank you!" "You too, [pc.name]. Your mouth is all oily... there." Kiyoko finishes cleaning you off, then thinks a moment and giggles. "How interesting. Not only do you and our daughter share similar auras, but you make the same messes as well. I wonder if there's any connection there?" | "Eat slower, Kinu. You'll choke if you don't chew your food properly. Besides, matsutake is made to be savoured slowly, not wolfed down." "Ehe. But then I have to eat lots! That way I can grow up fast and be a den mother like you!" No, really, it doesn't work that way. Overstuffing herself on peaches only makes her sick — what would cause her to think anything else would be any different? Kiyoko sighs good-naturedly and rubs her temples. "Well, to be fair, our daughter does eat her weight in food every day, or at least that's how it feels like.[kiyoko.numKits 4| Cooking for her alone is tiring enough, but feeding her and all of her siblings is truly a feat worthy of heroes. ]" | Kiyoko picks up a small piece of matsutake with her chopsticks and pets Kinu between the ears. "Now, daughter dearest, say 'aaaah'." You watch as your little kitsune daughter opens up obediently to be fed by her mother, then starts chewing away with great glee. Isn't she a little too old for that? "Hmm, I don't know about that. I've always found that it's good to retain some youthful tendencies, otherwise you tend to get old and cynical about things. Optimism, you know?" "Yay! Now it's my turn to feed [kinu.Dad]! Food always tastes better when it's served by someone who loves you, so come on! Aaaaaah!" [pc.isDK|If you must.|Gladly]. Kinu holds out a skewer with a bit of mushroom on it, and you pick it off with your teeth. It really is very good. "Well, then." Kiyoko smiles a little smile and turns the full force of her sea-green eyes on you, all [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] of her tails sweeping back and forth behind her. "I suppose you'll just have to feed me now, [pc.name]." "Yay! Feed Mama! Feed Mama!" Kiyoko's smile turns into a little mischievous grin. "Come on, now. Aaaaah." Oh, just for this you'll be feeding her something else later on when the two of you can get some time alone. | "Eat everything, okay?" Kiyoko says, eyeing Kinu's bowl. "Don't just eat the things you like, or eat them first before everything else. It's impolite. I made the egg custard for a reason." Kinu makes a whiny little noise in the back of her throat, but settles down and acquiesces without putting up a fight. Guess she knows that kitsune tricks don't work on themselves, eh? "There's a good girl. Food is precious. You may take it for granted here in the astral plane, but this won't always be the case." Indeed. Come to think of it, she said she made the egg custard for a reason — what is it? Your foxy wife sets down her bowl and chopsticks and thinks a moment. "It's... well, what you consider home cooking would be what you grew up eating, right? No matter where you came from, or your station in life... suffice to say that when I think of my own mother, egg custard and kenchin soup always come to mind. Come now, why don't you have some yourself, [pc.name]?" With that, Kiyoko reaches in with the large spoon and scoops out a chunk of wobbly, pale-yellow egg custard, plonking it straight into your bowl. You can see the bits of minced matsutake inside along with some kind of minced shellfish... it's soft, smooth and slippery, and the flavor's certainly not something one would find common in the Frost Marches, or even the heartlands. Even with the taste of matsutake dominating most of the mouthful, though, it's a bit of an acquired taste. ] Time passes, the food diminishes, and eventually the fire itself dies to a heap of embers and charred ashes. Ever calm and collected, Kiyoko picks up the dirty dishes and stacks them into the now-empty pot before giving the both of you a nod. "I'll be taking these back, then. [pc.name], occupy our daughter for a little while longer, won't you? There'll be plenty of time for us to be together alone after you've sent this little rascal on her way." With that, your foxy wife ups and leaves with the dishes, disappearing over the crest of the hill and into the cabin in the cherry blossom tree. Kinu watches her retreating form for a little while, then steps forward and rubs her side and tails against your legs. "Mmm, thank you so much for having fun with me today, [kinu.Dad]. I feel so warm and full!" Oh, she came up with everything with her mother; all you had to do was participate. "And that's what made the difference! Don't undersell yourself!" Kinu looks around, then leans in on tiptoe and kisses you at a level she's comfortable with — which happens to be somewhere just above your waist. "Okay, then! I'll put out the embers and clean everything else up! Go and play with Mama, I'll stay out of your fur, promise!" With that, your daughter turns her attention to throwing sand into the firepit, leaving you alone to make your move. Now that was fun... hopefully Kiyoko will be done with the dishes by the time you reach the cabin.
rows.translation: 哦，清子也在那里。你的狐妖妻子正拿着一个巨大的金属锅。 [kiyoko.pregStage 3|她摇摇晃晃地从小屋走过来，那巨大的怀孕腹部使她不得不在行走时小心翼翼地平衡手中的负担。 |她小心翼翼地从小屋中走出来，将那个东西放在她面前，努力保持它的平衡。] 蒸汽从盖子下面渗出来，缓缓升腾而上——天哪，他们真的做到了。 知道 你本来是要来的，对吧？ 我向您致以诚挚的问候。 清子微微一笑，将锅放在长凳上说道。 希望你们不会介意我也在这里。我们女儿想用这种方法来做松茸饭，但她还没掌握具体的制作流程。毕竟，这可不仅仅是一套简单的食谱那么简单。 妈妈！妈妈！ 光是用来做米饭的话，这些材料似乎有点多了，所以在我们女儿的帮助下，我又做了一些其他的菜。后来我发现，这些食物对于两个人来说确实有点多余……所以我想，你应该不会介意再多一个人来帮忙把剩下的食物吃完吧。 [kiyoko.pregStage 1|或者两个，也完全没问题。 她边说边揉着逐渐凸起的腹部。 "]你不会介意吧？ 哦，当然不会。这一定会是一次很愉快的家庭野餐。 清子笑着，轻轻拍了拍纪奈的脖子。 考虑到地点离家里这么近，我不太确定这算不算真正的野餐，但不管怎样，我相信一定会很愉快的。最近你对绮奴一直很好，而且我也真的很感激你偶尔能帮我照看那个调皮的小家伙。 我们能开始吃饭了吗？我饿死了。 好的，好的。当清子坐下来时，纪奈随手部一弹，就点燃了火堆，几乎漫不经心地把一团狐火扔到树枝和引火物上，火立刻燃烧了起来。当火焰欢快地跳动起来时，她走到装着腌蘑菇的盘子旁，用一根长棍子把其中一枚蘑菇串起来，然后递给了你。 你先走吧， [kinu.Dad]这是为了感谢你一直陪伴我、陪我玩耍！ 哎呀，真遗憾。你拿过绮奴给的木签，把蘑菇的一半架在火上，观察着热空气在蘑菇叶片上袅袅升起，这时松茸就开始慢慢煮熟了。绮奴坐在你旁边的长凳上，她那双大大的蓝眼睛紧紧地盯着正在火上烤的蘑菇。不久之后，蘑菇上的酱汁和油脂开始发出“嘶嘶”声，蘑菇本身也变成了金黄色，一股美妙的香味逐渐弥漫在空气中。 这唤起了许多回忆。 清子轻叹着说道。[kiyoko.pregStage 3|她的双手放在自己隆起的孕肚上。]. 每到秋天，我和母亲就会一起去松林里采摘松茸——仲秋时节是她难得能从繁忙的日程中抽空出来的时候之一。我们会把采到的美味装满篮子，然后开心地回家……现在，我的女儿也和我一起做这件事了。 当清子轻抚她的耳朵时，纪久不停地扭动身体、挣扎着。 嘻嘻！ 你 会 等你自己有了孩子，也要用同样的方法来对待他们，对吧？我其实并不是特别喜欢烤制或烧烤类的食物……但不得不说，要真正凸显松茸的味道，最简单的方法就是采用简单的烹饪方式。看，差不多煮好了。 果然如此。那原本呈白色的蘑菇部分，现在已经变成了美妙的金棕色，而那种特有的辛辣香气也通过烹饪过程被充分激发了出来。母女俩都紧紧地注视着你，看着你将蘑菇举到嘴边，然后咬下了一口。 天啊 [pc.bg noblescion|唯一能与这种味道相媲美的，恐怕就是你曾经在内地品尝过的松露了。|你从未有机会品尝过如此美味的东西。] 而且，有你那些可爱又毛茸茸的家人陪伴在身边，这一切就变得更加美好了。 啊……这才是真正的幸福。这种蘑菇口感紧实、有嚼劲，甚至还有些肉质感，同时还带有一种并不辛辣的香味。说实话，这种味道有点像肉桂。 好玩吗？ [kinu.Dad]我对酱油和米酒的使用可是相当在行的呢！ 你终于完成了，对吧？ 耶耶耶耶耶！ 好了好了，你们俩别急。食物多得很，没必要这么着急。除了我们女儿准备的饭菜，我还做了些松茸饭和蛋奶羹，你们也尝尝吧？肯定和你们平时吃的不一样哦。 事情就是这样。当绮奴在火上烤蘑菇的时候，清子和你会把满满一碗米饭盛到大碗里。你那位机灵的妻子说她准备了很多食物，这话可一点不假——这些松茸确实非常管用，尤其是她能把它们切成那么薄的片之后。 当你们三个人在温暖的山坡上坐下来吃饭时，内心深处总会有那么一丝愿望：希望这一切能永远持续下去，希望自己永远不必回到现实世界，去面对卡希拉所引发的那一片混乱…… [rand| 好了，好了。 清子轻声责备道，然后从和服里拿出一块绣着精美图案的手帕，为纪奈擦去了脸上的泪水。 女儿，你的嘴巴里全是食物……来，让我帮你清理干净。 基努扭动着身体，不停地蠕动着。 哇！谢谢你！ 你也是 [pc.name]你的嘴巴上全是油……就在那儿。 清子帮你擦干净后，想了一会儿，然后咯咯地笑了起来。 真有意思。你和我们的女儿不仅拥有相似的气场，还会把事情弄得一团糟。我在想，这两者之间会不会有什么联系呢？ | 慢点吃，绮奴。如果不仔细咀嚼，你会噎到的。而且，松茸这种食物就是用来慢慢品味的，而不是狼吞虎咽地吃掉的。 嘿嘿，不过那样我就得吃很多很多东西才行！这样我就能快速长大，然后像你一样成为母兽啦！ 不，真的不是这样的。吃太多桃子只会让她生病——那还有什么理由让她认为其他东西会有不同的效果呢？ 清子无奈地叹了口气，然后揉了揉太阳穴。 嗯，公平地说，我们的女儿确实每天会吃掉与她体重相当的食物量，至少应该是这样。 感觉起来…… 就像那样。[kiyoko.numKits 4| 仅仅为她一个人做饭就已经够累的了，而还要同时喂养她和她的所有兄弟姐妹，这真是一项值得英雄们去完成的壮举。 ]" | 清子用筷子夹起一小块松茸，然后轻轻抚摸着犬的耳朵。 现在，我最亲爱的女儿，说‘啊啊啊’吧。 你看着你那只小狐女儿乖乖地张开嘴让母亲喂食，然后开心地开始咀嚼起来。她这个年纪，不应该再吃这种东西了吧？ 嗯，这个我不太确定。我一直认为，保持一些年轻时的特质是件好事，否则人就会变得老迈和愤世嫉俗。乐观主义，你知道的吧？ 耶！现在轮到我喂食了！ [kinu.Dad]当那些爱你的人为你准备食物时，味道总是会更好吃的，所以快来吧！啊…… [pc.isDK|如果非得这样的话。|很乐意]绮奴递过来一根插着少许蘑菇的烤肉签，你用牙齿把它拔下来吃掉，真的非常美味。 那好吧。 清子微微一笑，然后用她那双海绿色的眼睛紧紧地注视着你。 [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] 她的尾巴在身后来回摆动。 我想现在你只能喂我了 [pc.name]." 耶！喂妈妈！喂妈妈！ 清子的笑容变成了一个略带调皮的笑容。 快点，现在就来。啊…… 哦，就为了这个，等你们有单独相处的时间时，你之后可以给她喂点别的东西。 | 把所有东西都吃掉，好吗？ 清子看着纪久的碗说道。 不要只吃自己喜欢的东西，也不要总是先把它们吃掉。那样很不礼貌。我做这个蛋奶羹是有原因的。 绮奴在喉咙深处发出了一声抱怨般的轻哼，但最终还是安静下来，没有再反抗。看来她知道，狐妖的把戏对自己是没用的吧？ 真是个好姑娘。食物可是很珍贵的。在星界这里你可能觉得这很平常，但情况并不总是如此的。 确实。仔细想来，她说自己做蛋奶糊是有一定原因的——究竟是什么原因呢？ 是 它？ 你的那个狡猾的妻子放下碗和筷子，思考了一会儿。 这……嗯，你所说的家常菜，其实就是你从小吃到大的食物，对吧？无论你来自哪里，无论你的社会地位如何……总之，每当我想到我的母亲，蛋奶糊和肯钦汤就会浮现在我的脑海中。来吧，你也尝尝看吧。 [pc.name]?" 说着，清子便用那把大勺舀起一块软软的、淡黄色的蛋奶糊，直接把它放进你的碗里。你可以看到里面有一些切碎的松茸，还有某种切碎的贝类……这种蛋奶糊质地柔软、顺滑，味道绝对不是在霜冻边境地区，甚至是在内陆地区也能经常尝到的。不过，尽管松茸的味道占据了口腔中的大部分味道，这种口味还是需要一段时间才能适应的。 ] 时间流逝，食物逐渐减少，最终火焰也熄灭了，只剩下一堆余烬和烧焦的灰烬。基约科始终保持着冷静与沉着，她将那些脏盘子捡起来，整齐地堆放在那个已经空了的锅里，然后向你们两个人点了点头。 那这些我就拿回去了。 [pc.name]再陪我们的女儿一会儿吧，好吗？等把这个调皮鬼送走之后，我们就有很多时间可以单独相处了。 说着，你那位狡黠的妻子便端着盘子走开了，消失在山丘的另一侧，走进了那座位于樱花树下的小屋。绮奴盯着她远去的背影看了一会儿，然后走上前，用身体蹭你的腿，还用尾巴轻触你的腿部。 嗯，非常感谢你今天能和我一起享受这些欢乐时光， [kinu.Dad]我感到无比温暖，内心也充满了满足感！ 哦，这些都是她和妈妈一起想出来的；你所要做的就是参与进来而已。 正是这一点才带来了不同的结果！千万不要低估自己的能力！ 纪久环顾四周，然后踮起脚尖，以她觉得合适的距离吻了你——那个位置恰好在你的腰部以上。 好吧，那我就把余火熄灭，把其他地方都清理干净！你去和妈妈一起玩吧，我肯定不会去打扰你们的，保证！ 说完，你的女儿便把注意力转移到往火坑里扔沙子上去了，这样你就独自一人可以采取行动了。刚才真是太有趣了……希望等你赶到小屋的时候，清子已经洗完盘子了。
rows.raw: ' Oh, and Kiyoko's there too. Your fox-wife is carrying a large metal pot, [kiyoko.pregStage 3|waddling over from the cabin as she balances her burden in front of her huge pregnant belly. |balancing it in front of her as she carefully makes her way over from the cabin.] Steam seeps out from under the lid, wafting up and away — goodness, they really knew you were coming, didn't they? "My greetings," Kiyoko says with a small smile as she sets the pot down on the bench. "I hope you don't mind me being here as well. Our daughter wanted to make matsutake rice for this, but she hasn't got the process down just yet. It's more than simply following a recipe, after all." "Mama! Mama!" "There was a little too much for just rice, too, so I made some other things with our daughter's help. And then I realized we'd made too much for just two... so I thought you wouldn't mind having another mouth around to finish up all the food. [kiyoko.pregStage 1|Or two, for that matter," she adds, rubbing the rising swell of her pregnancy. "]You don't mind, do you?" Oh, of course not. This'll be a great family picnic. Kiyoko laughs and pats Kinu on the scruff of her neck. "I'm not sure it qualifies as a picnic, considering it's so close to home, but I'm sure it'll be wonderful nonetheless. You've been very good to Kinu of late, and I myself appreciate you taking the little rapscallion out of my fur every now and then." "Can we eat already? I'm huuuuungry." Okay, okay. While Kiyoko takes a seat, Kinu lights the firepit with a flick of her fingers, almost carelessly tossing a glob of foxfire into the twigs and tinder to set it alight. Once the flames are licking away merrily, she pads over to the plate of marinated mushrooms, spears one of the mushroom halves on a long stick, and offers it to you. "You go first, [kinu.Dad]! This is to thank you for always petting and playing with me!" Aw, shucks. You take the wooden skewer from Kinu and hold the mushroom half over the fire, watching hot air waver over the leaf fire as the matsutake begins to cook. Kinu takes a seat besides you on the bench, her big blue eyes fixed on the shroom as you turn it about in the fire. Before long, the sauce and oil on it starts to sizzle and pop, the matsutake itself turning a golden-brown as a delightful smell begins to waft into the air. "This brings back memories," Kiyoko says with a small sigh[kiyoko.pregStage 3|, her hands resting on her big pregnant belly]. "My mother and I would go out in the fall to pick matsutake in the pine forest — mid-autumn was one of the few times when she'd get a reprieve from her hectic schedule. We'd fill baskets with the delicacies, then head home happy... and now my own daughter is doing it with me." Kinu wiggles and squirms as Kiyoko pets her ears. "Hee hee!" "You will do the same with your own children when you have them, yes? I'm not the biggest fan of roasted and grilled food... but I will say that the best way to bring out the flavor of matsutake is simple preparation. Look, it's nearly done." And so it is. The once white portions of the halved mushroom are now a wonderful golden-brown, and the signature spicy aroma has been well and truly brought out by the cooking. Mother and daughter alike watch you intently as you raise the mushroom, and take a bite. Gods above. [pc.bg noblescion|The only thing that might compare to this are the truffles you once sampled in the heartlands.|You've never had the opportunity to taste anything this good.] And the fact that you have your foxy, floofy family at your side — that just makes it all the more intense. Ah... now this is happiness. The mushroom is firm and chewy — meaty, even, and possessed of a certain spicy flavor that's not peppery. A little like cinnamon, to be honest. "Was it good, [kinu.Dad]? I'm pretty awesome with soy sauce and rice wine!" You finished it, didn't you? "Yaaaaaaay!" "Now, now, both of you. There's plenty to be had, so there's no need to rush things. In addition to our daughter's offerings, I made some matsutake rice and egg custard as well. Why don't you try some as well? It'll certainly be a change from your usual fare." And so it goes. While Kinu sets to roasting the mushrooms in the fire, Kiyoko and you scoop out hearty servings of rice into big bowls. Your foxy wife wasn't kidding when she said she'd made a lot — one of these matsutake mushrooms sure goes a long way, especially with how thinly she can slice them. As the three of you settle down to eat on the warm hillside, part of you wishes that this could go on forever, that you wouldn't have to eventually return to the waking world and deal with the chaos Kasyrra's creating... [rand| "There, there," Kiyoko chides gently, pulling a finely embroidered handkerchief out of her yukata and wiping off Kinu's face. "Your mouth is covered in food, daughter... here, let me clean you off." Kinu wiggles and squirms. "Mwa! Thank you!" "You too, [pc.name]. Your mouth is all oily... there." Kiyoko finishes cleaning you off, then thinks a moment and giggles. "How interesting. Not only do you and our daughter share similar auras, but you make the same messes as well. I wonder if there's any connection there?" | "Eat slower, Kinu. You'll choke if you don't chew your food properly. Besides, matsutake is made to be savoured slowly, not wolfed down." "Ehe. But then I have to eat lots! That way I can grow up fast and be a den mother like you!" No, really, it doesn't work that way. Overstuffing herself on peaches only makes her sick — what would cause her to think anything else would be any different? Kiyoko sighs good-naturedly and rubs her temples. "Well, to be fair, our daughter does eat her weight in food every day, or at least that's how it feels like.[kiyoko.numKits 4| Cooking for her alone is tiring enough, but feeding her and all of her siblings is truly a feat worthy of heroes. ]" | Kiyoko picks up a small piece of matsutake with her chopsticks and pets Kinu between the ears. "Now, daughter dearest, say 'aaaah'." You watch as your little kitsune daughter opens up obediently to be fed by her mother, then starts chewing away with great glee. Isn't she a little too old for that? "Hmm, I don't know about that. I've always found that it's good to retain some youthful tendencies, otherwise you tend to get old and cynical about things. Optimism, you know?" "Yay! Now it's my turn to feed [kinu.Dad]! Food always tastes better when it's served by someone who loves you, so come on! Aaaaaah!" [pc.isDK|If you must.|Gladly]. Kinu holds out a skewer with a bit of mushroom on it, and you pick it off with your teeth. It really is very good. "Well, then." Kiyoko smiles a little smile and turns the full force of her sea-green eyes on you, all [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] of her tails sweeping back and forth behind her. "I suppose you'll just have to feed me now, [pc.name]." "Yay! Feed Mama! Feed Mama!" Kiyoko's smile turns into a little mischievous grin. "Come on, now. Aaaaah." Oh, just for this you'll be feeding her something else later on when the two of you can get some time alone. | "Eat everything, okay?" Kiyoko says, eyeing Kinu's bowl. "Don't just eat the things you like, or eat them first before everything else. It's impolite. I made the egg custard for a reason." Kinu makes a whiny little noise in the back of her throat, but settles down and acquiesces without putting up a fight. Guess she knows that kitsune tricks don't work on themselves, eh? "There's a good girl. Food is precious. You may take it for granted here in the astral plane, but this won't always be the case." Indeed. Come to think of it, she said she made the egg custard for a reason — what is it? Your foxy wife sets down her bowl and chopsticks and thinks a moment. "It's... well, what you consider home cooking would be what you grew up eating, right? No matter where you came from, or your station in life... suffice to say that when I think of my own mother, egg custard and kenchin soup always come to mind. Come now, why don't you have some yourself, [pc.name]?" With that, Kiyoko reaches in with the large spoon and scoops out a chunk of wobbly, pale-yellow egg custard, plonking it straight into your bowl. You can see the bits of minced matsutake inside along with some kind of minced shellfish... it's soft, smooth and slippery, and the flavor's certainly not something one would find common in the Frost Marches, or even the heartlands. Even with the taste of matsutake dominating most of the mouthful, though, it's a bit of an acquired taste. ] Time passes, the food diminishes, and eventually the fire itself dies to a heap of embers and charred ashes. Ever calm and collected, Kiyoko picks up the dirty dishes and stacks them into the now-empty pot before giving the both of you a nod. "I'll be taking these back, then. [pc.name], occupy our daughter for a little while longer, won't you? There'll be plenty of time for us to be together alone after you've sent this little rascal on her way." With that, your foxy wife ups and leaves with the dishes, disappearing over the crest of the hill and into the cabin in the cherry blossom tree. Kinu watches her retreating form for a little while, then steps forward and rubs her side and tails against your legs. "Mmm, thank you so much for having fun with me today, [kinu.Dad]. I feel so warm and full!" Oh, she came up with everything with her mother; all you had to do was participate. "And that's what made the difference! Don't undersell yourself!" Kinu looks around, then leans in on tiptoe and kisses you at a level she's comfortable with — which happens to be somewhere just above your waist. "Okay, then! I'll put out the embers and clean everything else up! Go and play with Mama, I'll stay out of your fur, promise!" With that, your daughter turns her attention to throwing sand into the firepit, leaving you alone to make your move. Now that was fun... hopefully Kiyoko will be done with the dishes by the time you reach the cabin. '

rows.original: Not bad. Not bad at all. Did she prepare this all by herself? "Not really, Mama did help me out a lot. Even so, though, she couldn't come today and I'm not allowed to use the steamer by myself, so instead of what I wanted to make, I got this!" With that, Kinu scoots under the bench and pulls out a large basket full of sweet potatoes and chestnuts, holding it over her head to present it to you with a flourish. "See? See? It's really good to eat things which are in harmony with the season. Matsutake are very iconic of the fall, so I prepared some other things which are thematically appropriate, too!" That's not all, of course. Along with the basket of goodies is a long-handled pan — for the chestnuts, no doubt — and two plates for each of you. "I brought more than what we needed," Kinu continues, looking up at you with her big blue eyes. "So please help yourself, [kinu.Dad]. I've thought of everything, so I'm a great girl, right?" Yes, yes. You don't know about great — that really depends on who she's comparing herself to — but she's definitely a thoughtful child who deserves to be repaid in kind. You reach out and pet Kinu on her forehead, and the little kitsune purrs, wiggling under your touch. "Okay! Okay! We can get started now, right?" Of course. Let the games begin! "Yaaaaay!" Your daughter claps her hands, and a glorious plume of pale blue flame erupts from the firepit, rising into the sky. Left in its wake is a merry little fire, a gentle fragrance rising into the air alongside pale gray smoke as flames lick at the stones on the edge of the firepit. No time like the present, then. You step over to the bench, spear one of the marinated mushroom halves on the wooden skewers, and take a seat by the fire to let it cook. An exquisite spicy fragrance rises from the matsutake as it cooks, and before your eyes, the white flesh turns a beautiful golden-brown as you turn it in the fire. "It's done! You need to be sure not to overcook it, so it's done! Try it! Try it!" How could you not, especially with a little foxy daughter egging you on? You blow on the freshly roasted mushroom to cool it off, and then take a bite — warm, rich juices burst straight onto your tongue the moment your teeth sink into the meaty mushroom flesh. Ah... now this is happiness. The mushroom is quie chewy, and the flavor is truly as unique as its smell, a strange blend of spiciness and earthiness that leaves you wanting more. Gods above. [pc.bg slumrat |If anyone had ever told you growing up on the streets that you'd taste such delicacies, you'd have spat in their face.|You can see why Kinu was so excited to go out and hunt for this stuff.] And the fact that you have a your little foxy daughter by your side egging you on makes it taste even better. Now, it's not right that you're eating this all by yourself, especially when Kinu worked so hard for it. Smiling, you raise the half-eaten matsutake to your darling daughter's mouth, and tell her to open wide. "Aaaah!" You pop the rest of the mushroom in, and Kinu chews and swallows. A look of pure contentment spreads over the little kitsune's face, and her three tails begin to swish about behind her. "I'm the bestest cook ever! Soy sauce and rice wine work really well!" Is that what's in the marinade? It certainly isn't like anything you've tasted before. The rest of the food is all-natural, though. "Yep! To be honest, [kinu.Dad], I like most of my food as-is and simply cooked, but Mama made me marinate the matsutake. I'm just a simple girl, you see!" A simple girl with very complex tastes in mischief. But enough of that. There's still more to be cooked up here, much, much more, and there's no point sitting around! Hop to it! Kinu does so with unrestrained enthusiasm. While you fill the grilling pan with chestnuts, Kinu stokes the fire to a merry blaze, then sets up a little tripod over the firepit to hang the pan from. Soon enough, you have sweet potatoes and matsutake mushrooms roasting in the open flames, while the chestnuts pop and rattle in the pan. The aroma that wafts through the air and down the hill... yeah, seasonal would be the only way to put it; there's simply no other word that would do this lovely scent justice. [kiyoko.numKits 4| And with such a heavenly smell... oh yes, here they come. Foxy ears peek out over the crest of the hill, and a trio of Kinu's two-tailed siblings come rushing up in short order, all looking bright-eyed and hopeful as they sniff the air. "Big Sis! Big Sis! Are you cooking something with [kinu.Dad]?" "It smells so goooood!" "Can we have some? Pleasepleasepleaseplease?" Kinu looks a little unsure. "Eh, I dunno... this is supposed to be between me and [kinu.Dad]..." "Awww..." Now, now. Didn't she just say that she'd prepared more than enough for two? There's no reason why she shouldn't share — [pc.isDK|it just means that they'll be ingratiated to her later on. Important to build leverage early, eh?|and things'll be more fun with more folks around. You want to impress upon her the importance of sharing, after all.] Kinu sniffs. "Okay, you can have some, since [kinu.Dad] is so nice. Don't mess things up, okay?" "We won't!" You smile and give Kinu a pat on the head. Yes, you understand that she wanted to have some alone time with you, but she's going to be following in her mother's footsteps someday. Learning to improvise and deal with unexpected situations is going to be a big boon for her. Besides, the cooking will go much faster with three more pairs of hands to help, won't it? "Hmp..." You pass out some more skewers with sweet potatoes on them, and your little kitsune children squeal with glee as they hold them out over the open fire. The chestnuts themselves are coming along very well, and it's not too long before you hear the pop-pop-pop of them signaling that they're cooked and ready to be eaten. [rand| "There, there, careful with that," Kinu says as she eases one of her little brothers away from the firepit. "If that sweet potato ends up burned, you'll have to eat it regardless. So don't burn it, okay?" "Okay, Big Sis..." "Good boy." Your kitsune daughter gives her brother a pat on the head, and in that moment you're struck by how much she does resemble her mother in that regard. "It can be hard to tell sometimes, especially over an open fire — you don't want the insides to be all raw and yucky, but neither do you want the outsides burned to a crisp. Call for me if you need help, okay?" | Kinu's ears perk up, and she leans over the firepit to unhook the pan from the tripod. The heat doesn't seem to bother her at all — she's holding the no doubt scorching thing with her bare hands — and with great care and deliberation, uncovers the pan and begins shelling the chestnuts. Oh? She's not having any of her own? "Eh, not until I've made enough for those three, [kinu.Dad]. Otherwise, they'll just keep on bugging me for some and sour the taste in my mouth." Is she suuuure? "Yes, [kinu.Dad]." Finishing up with the last of the handful she's picked apart, Kinu pads over to her trio of siblings and holds their wide-eyed gazes. "Now then, Tatsumi. Say 'aaaaah'." "Aaaah?" While the little kitsune kit's mouth is open, Kinu carefully pops in one of the freshly roasted chestnuts. He chews, and his ears stiffen as his eyes light up. "Mfffmfmfmf." "Now, it's rude to talk with your mouth full. Chew, swallow, then speak. Now, what did you want to say?" "Thank you, Big Sis." The kit thinks a moment, then speaks again, this time more stiffly as if reciting from rote memory: "As Lord Keros has taught, I must repay you someday." "Good boy. You can do as much by not giving Mama a big headache. Now then, little sis, it's your turn..." One by one, Kinu's little trio of siblings receive mouthfuls of still-warm chestnuts, looking very pleased with themselves. Finally done, your daughter returns to her seat on the bench and starts tucking into her own meal. The way she handled that was quite impressive. She's got her mother's touch, that's for sure. "It's nothing, [kinu.Dad]. Live with these little scamps for long enough, and you get to know what drives them without even needing to think about it; I pick up on that quickly enough." | "Careful, careful," Kinu mutters as she watches one of her little sisters break open a baked sweet potato, steam rushing out of its now mushy core. "It's still very hot, so give it a little time to cool. Here, let Big Sis blow on it for you." "Okay!" Kinu takes the sweet potato from her little sister, then huffs and puffs a bit before handing it back, the rising steam now gone. "Just don't get overexcited, okay? It's probably still warm inside — I'd never hear the end of it from Mama if you burned your tongue on my watch." ] She's being a really good big sister to her brothers and sisters, isn't she? While Kinu has yet to perfect the technique, she definitely has to beginnings of her mother's deft hand when it comes to dealing with children. "I have to be, [kinu.Dad]. Who else is going to help Mama deal with all of this craziness?" Kinu puffs out her chest proudly and straightens to her full, petite height, all four feet of it. Well, maybe a little less, but just a little. Ha! Ha! Well, she'd better take a seat and start eating, or all the food's going to be gone before long. The first batch of chestnuts are already all gone, and her siblings are eyeing the cooking matsutake with the kind of gaze only perpetually ravenous children can muster. "Yeah..." The rest of the little cookout passes in silence, the five of you simply enjoying each other's company amidst a medley of aromas and flavors. Kinu helps her siblings roast up batch after batch of chestnuts, and before long even the little bottomless pits are satiated and looking content, if not happy. The matsutake is spicy and amazing, the sweet potatoes are delightfully starchy, and the chestnuts... well, Kinu and her siblings ate them all. Kinu cleans off her plate with a happy sigh, then turns to her siblings. "Are you all done?" "Yes, big sis," they reply as one. "Good, good. I'd be worried about spoiling your appetites for dinner, but I know better than that. Clean yourselves off now... and what do you say after you've eaten?" "Thank you for the food, big sis." The kits turn to you, and bow far more formally than young children should have any right to do. "Thank you, [kinu.Dad]." No, thank you for the wonderful company. "All right, that's enough out of the lot of you. Run along now." Kinu steps up and gives each of her siblings a headpat between the ears, then shoos the happy kits out and away before turning back to you. "I guess we didn't get to eat as much as we intended, [kinu.Dad], but I guess that's okay." She doesn't have to guess, you know it's okay. The company of her brothers and sisters more than makes up for any deliciousness you might have missed out on. Cooking out under an open sky is so much better when it's done with other people, even if you don't talk much; just being there is fine. "Sheesh, you're getting sappy, [kinu.Dad]..." Heh heh. | Since there's just the two of you, it takes a while for things to get going. The halved matsutake are quick to cook, the sweet potatoes less so; you busy yourself with the former while Kinu handles the latter. Time passes as the two of you sit side by side in silence, a gentle breeze carrying the fragrance of your cooking downhill, simply enjoying each other's company. Pity her mother couldn't make it, huh? Should you skip out on seeing her today? "Mama said she had something to attend to, and that she should be done by the time we're done, too. You can go ahead and visit no problem. Oh, look! They're done!" And so they are. Kinu sets the next batch of fall-themed goodies to roasting, while you take the current one off the fire and set them to cool. The sweet potatoes are a bit burnt on the outside, but you've otherwise got quite the appetising spread before you, with more on the way. [rand| Kinu takes a big bite out of a baked sweet potato and sighs, foxy ears wiggling. "This is truly good, isn't it?" It's very... idyllic. Representative of the simpler pleasures of life, if you might say so. "Thanks, [kinu.Dad]. I worked pretty hard to put this all together — it's not just the food which has to complement each other, but also the mood and theme as well! Sure, most people won't notice it consciously, but they sure will feel it! You noticed, which makes you extra-special, [kinu.Dad]!" Well, isn't that just precocious of her. You pat Kinu on the head, taking care to fold down each ear as your palm runs across it, eliciting a happy squeal from your daughter. | "This firepit is pretty new," Kinu says. "Mama says it wasn't here before I was born." Why would that be the case? "Because according to Mama, this sort of open-air cooking is supposed to be done with other people. She says that she could do it by herself, but it wouldn't have been the same, and then that would defeat the point of the exercise. She didn't want her memories to be tarnished by bad attempts to recreate them." Kinu pops a couple of shelled roasted chestnuts into her mouth, chews, and swallows. "But then you came along, and then I came along. Now that there're more people about, it isn't so pointless any more." You can see where her mother's coming from. Cooking over an open-air fire like this is nice, but it definitely wouldn't be the same without your daughter by your side. "Say, [kinu.Dad]..." Yes? "Do you think more people will be coming along soon?" More... people? "Mama says that she thinks more children like me will be arriving soon... I'm not sure exactly what she means, but I don't really mind, so long as I have more people to play with. I mean, it's ok when Mama takes out some time to play with me, but then she also lectures me and keeps me in line... I dunno. I'd like to have more people my age about here. "Do you think Mama is correct, that there'll be more kids arriving soon? She didn't say how she knew, though, so I think she did an augury or something." Kinu's face is the very expression of wide-eyed innocence. Just what exactly has her mother been telling her? Actually, guess what? If her mother keeps this up, there's a very good chance that little prediction of hers will come true. Kinu perks up. "Really? I'll go tell her that, then!" Yes, she can go do just that. | "Do you think there's an elegance to all this, [kinu.Dad]?" Elegance? Hmm... you're not sure about elegance. Charm, yes. Beauty of the natural sort, yes. Elegance... not quite. But does it need that? "Well, Mama is fancy and elegant. That's her thing and I know I can't compete with her in that regard, so I want to be simple and elegant. That way we won't have to step on each other's toes." You laugh. Well, if she wants to work on her elegance, she's got a ways to go from crawling around on the forest floor hunting mushrooms buried in dirt and pine needles. Or is it possible to do that with any measure of elegance? Kinu sniffs. "Everything has its proper time and place, [kinu.Dad]. Forests are for playing and getting all dirty in. A meal with the family? Simple elegance." And come to think of it, her mother's not that fancy, either — or at least, not by some of the standards you've heard of. So if she's going to be simple compared to that... maybe it'd be better to shoot for that when she's older. For now, just charm will do. "Mmmmmh... I'm not so sure I like that answer, [kinu.Dad]." Well, she shouldn't ask questions she's not ready to receive answers to. ] Compared to Kiyoko's finely prepared and presented cooking, this is but plain fare, but there's something about sharing food with a hyperactive kitsune child that makes it taste better than it should. As you expected, the sweet potatoes are a little burnt, but it's easy enough to simply scoop out the soft, mushy insides and toss the burnt bits into the fire.
