rows.original: Wordlessly, you take out the apprentice staff and pass it over the low table to Kiyoko. Seeing this, your kitsune wife's smile broadens just a little, and she takes the simple wooden staff in hand, examining the focusing crystal. "It's fascinating, isn't it? Both rely on the same basic principles, but the emergent forms they take are quite different, colored by the environments they evolved in. Hah... the sight of this brings back memories, and not all good ones." She hasn't spoken that much about her past before she got trapped in here, that's true. "Mostly because it wasn't a pleasant time for anyone involved. While there's something to be said for learning the lessons of the past, there's also not much point in dredging up bad memories for their own sake. Unless you're the kind who likes wallowing in that kind of moroseness, I suppose. Now then, I'll go call Kinu in — I'm sure she'll appreciate the change in her schedule. In the meantime, why don't you make yourself comfortable upstairs?" Upstairs? "If you please." [var0|Would she like you to take a more active part in the lesson? You've had some formal training in matters arcane in the past; if the object of this exercise is to impress upon Kinu the comparisons and contrasts between the native magics of Kiyoko's homeland and that of Belhar's legacy, then this is something you can help out with. "Yes, I'd be delighted to have someone share in the burden of answering our precocious daughter's questions, thank you very much. In fact, I'd like to see you take up the bulk of the task. It'll be a change of pace for me." |You'll acquiesce, but you're not exactly sure what you can do here. Magic's not quite your area of expertise at the moment. A smile. "As before, mostly for moral support. I'd like Kinu to know that even if you can't be with us that often, you're nevertheless interested in her education. I... well, she's been growing distracted and listless of late, as children do from time to time, and a couple of changes should help her focus her interest, at the very least." ] All right, then. While your foxy wife leaves the cabin in search of your daughter, you head upstairs and make yourself comfortable in the room she mentioned; clearly one that Kinu uses for magic lessons. [var0|With you being alone, you're able examine in detail the setup Kiyoko has placed over its entirety. She certainly knows what she's doing — there's a simple elegance that you easily recognize in the wards and charms that line the walls and ceiling. With your expertise, you're able to quickly figure that nothing short of a major magical mishap would escape the containment. Sure, you might not understand the language used in the calligraphy, but this doesn't need words to get the point across. |Once again, you're reminded how out of depth you are here in this place. Even as magically illiterate as you are, you're able to sense the strength of the wards in place here, a constant crawling sensation on your [pc.skinFurScales]. It's unsettling, but you can understand why Kiyoko isn't taking any chances with Kinu. ] It's not long before you hear footsteps on the stairs, and then the screen door slides open to admit both mother and daughter into the room. Kinu is a little scuffed up from playing outside, but by the spring in her step all the enthusiasm from running around in the fields has seamlessly transferred to the prospect of learning more about a subject she enjoys. "...Is this the day you finally teach me how to retrieve objects at a distance, Mama? Is that what you meant by doing something different today?" "Not until you've learned some self-control. But I've managed to rope your [pc.mf|father|mother]'s help in your education. You've been growing a little listless during lessons, so..." Kinu stops and clears her throat self-consciously when she sees you seated in the corner of the room. "Oh. Hello, [kinu.Dad]." Right. You're not sure how long your visit will be, so perhaps getting started would be a good idea. And so it is. [var0|For what feels like the next handful of hours, you sit down at the low table with Kinu while Kiyoko takes a back seat and observes the impromptu lesson. While you haven't forgotten that much theory you've learned, recent events have necessitated an emphasis on the practical, and it's this you attempt to impress upon your daughter as the lesson proceeds, using the apprentice staff as a learning tool. It's not an easy task by any means, especially with convincing Kinu to temporarily go back to basics and discard and preconceptions she's acquired. Your daughter is quick to draw parallels between your style of doing things and hers, and has more than one question that you feel rather uneasy answering — perhaps it's something that shouldn't be coming out of an eight-year-old's mouth, or simply something that you didn't pay close enough attention to during your training. At the end of it all, though, she's picked up using the simple staff as a focus with her trademark ease, sputtering around with the simple fire spells that come so naturally to her, and with no major mishaps to boot. Kiyoko comes up behind you with a smile and a small cup of tea, which you take gratefully — talking to Kinu in this kind of setting is certainly draining, to say the least. Kinu waves the staff about in the air a bit, conjuring a small ring of flames that dance about her feet before extinguishing themselves. "I see what you were getting at, [kinu.Dad]. Can I keep this for more practice?" You don't see why not. It's not as if its real-world counterpart is going to vanish if you let Kinu have this one, right? |With a nod, Kiyoko sits everyone down at the low table and begins the lesson. Most of the stuff she's saying is going straight over your head — you've heard Cait use a few of the terms from time to time, but otherwise it's all unintelligble to you. It doesn't help that your foxy wife is simply speaking so fast, one word rolling into the other like a gushing spring. Kinu is perfectly fine with this, though, listening to her mother with rapt attention. The amorphous blob of energy she was when playing outside has been honed into a fine-pointed needle; even her ears and tails are largely still as Kiyoko brings out the apprentice staff you brought in and starts with the practical demonstrations. You're given opportunities to help in the lesson — admittedly, mostly as a practice dummy, but hey, your daughter's education is worth it, right? Right? "This is fun!" Kinu squeals as she conjures a small ring of flames about your feet with the staff. There's no heat thanks to the wards, but it's still unnerving, to say the least. "I don't know if it's easier to use than a scroll would be, but it's certainly different." "Which is the point of the exercise," Kiyoko replies. "I hope you enjoyed yourself too, [pc.name]." It was something, all right. You're not sure how much you contributed to the lesson, but at least you appreciated being able to spend time with your foxy wife and daughter. "Oh! Do you mind if I keep the staff with me? I'd like to — uh — experiment with it some more." There's no reason to deny Kinu as much, is there? ] "Thank you, [kinu.Dad]. And thank you for being here today. I really appreciate it." And you really appreciate her being in here despite this being her playtime. She should be out there having fun, shouldn't she? Kinu looks a little sheepish and scratches the back of her head. "Ehe. If you want to do it, it counts as fun, [kinu.Dad]." "All right, all right. It's not that often that we're all able to get together to do something... I kind of wish I could come up with something that could involve the entire family, but that would be a bit of a logistics nightmare. In the meantime, thank you for coming, [pc.name]. I sincerely hope that you'll continue to be more involved in Kinu's education in time to come. It might be a bit hard because of when and how you can visit, but the effort is nevertheless appreciated." Of course, of course. Well, it's about time for you to leave. You give Kiyoko a final kiss on the cheek and Kinu a pat between her ears, then bid them goodbye as you head down and out of the cabin. The sun's still shining down as warmly as it was when you entered the Astral Plane, and there's a smile on your face as you head off into the waking world. With how effortlessly she picked up Behlaran magic, surely your daughter will grow up to be as fine an arcanist as her mother when she comes of age, if not more...
rows.translation: 你默默地取出那根学徒用的木杖，将其放在矮桌上递给清子。看到这一幕，你的九尾妻子嘴角微微上扬，她接过那根简单的木杖，仔细端详着上面的聚光水晶。 真是太有趣了，不是吗？它们都基于相同的基本原理，但最终形成的形态却大相径庭，这些差异完全取决于它们所处的环境。哈……看到这一幕，不禁让人回忆起许多往事，不过那些回忆并不都是美好的。 确实，在被关到这里之前，她很少谈论自己的过去。 主要是因为那段时光对所有相关人员来说都并不愉快。虽然从过去的事故中吸取教训确实很有意义，但仅仅为了重温那些糟糕的记忆而刻意去翻旧账，其实也没什么意义。除非你就是那种喜欢沉溺在这种消极情绪中的人……好吧，我去叫绮奴过来吧——我相信她一定会很高兴自己的日程安排有所改变的。与此同时，你不妨去楼上休息一下吧。 楼上吗？ 如果可以的话。 [var0|她是否希望你能更积极地参与这次教学活动呢？你过去接受过一些关于神秘学方面的系统训练；如果这次练习的目的是让绮奴了解清子的故乡与Belhar的传统魔法之间的异同，那么你肯定能够提供帮助。 是的，如果有人能帮忙分担回答我们这个早熟女儿问题的重任，我会非常感激的。事实上，我希望你能承担大部分工作——这样对我来说也会是一种不同的体验。 |你会同意的，但你也并不清楚自己能在这里做些什么。目前来说，魔法确实不是你的专长领域。 一个微笑。 和以前一样，主要是为了给予她精神上的支持。我想让绮奴知道，即使你不能经常陪伴在我们身边，但你依然非常关心她的教育。嗯……最近她确实有些心不在焉、提不起精神，孩子们有时候就是会这样。做一些小小的改变，至少应该能帮助她重新集中注意力吧。 ] 好吧，那么。当你那位狡猾的妻子离开小屋去寻找你的女儿时，你就上楼去，到她提到的那个房间里休息吧；显然，那个房间是绮奴用来上魔法课的。 [var0|当你独自一人时，你便能够仔细观察清子为整个空间所做的布置。她显然非常清楚自己在做什么——那些排列在墙壁和天花板上的护符与咒术中，蕴含着一种简洁而高雅的设计风格，这种风格你是很容易就能辨认出来的。凭借你的专业知识，你很快就能意识到：除非发生极其严重的魔法意外，否则没有任何东西能够突破这些防护措施。当然，你可能无法理解那些书法中使用的文字，但这些设计本身就已经足以传达其意义了。 |再一次，你被提醒了：在这个地方，你究竟是多么的无知。即便你如此“缺乏魔法知识”，你也能够感受到这里设置的防护结界的强大力量——那种持续存在的、仿佛有东西在身上爬动的感觉，让你清晰地意识到它们的存在。 [pc.skinFurScales]这确实让人感到不安，但你也能够理解为什么清子对纪久如此谨慎、不敢轻易采取任何行动。 ] 没过多久，你就听到楼梯上传来了足部步声，接着纱门被推开了，母女俩一起走进了房间。绮奴因为在户外玩耍，身上有些脏兮兮的，但她那充满活力的步伐清楚地表明：在田野里奔跑带来的兴奋，已经完全转移到了她学习自己感兴趣的知识的兴趣上了。 ……妈妈，今天就是你终于要教我如何远距离取物的日子吗？你今天说要‘做一些不同的事情’，指的就是这个吗？ 除非你学会自我控制才行。不过，我倒是想办法把你给 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲]感谢你在我学习过程中给予的帮助。最近你在上课时显得有点无精打采，所以…… 当金看到你坐在房间的角落里时，她不由自主地停下了足部步，清了清嗓子。 哦，你好， [kinu.Dad]." 没错。你也不确定自己会待多久，所以开始行动或许是个好主意。 果然如此。 [var0|在接下来的几个小时里，你和绮奴一起坐在那张矮桌旁，而清子则在一旁观察这堂即兴进行的课程。虽然你并没有忘记所学过的那些理论知识，但最近发生的一些事情使得实践操作变得更为重要。因此，在这堂课上，你便利用学徒用的法杖作为教学工具，努力将这些实践知识传授给你的女儿。 这绝非易事，尤其是要说服绮奴暂时回归基础，摒弃她一直以来形成的那些固有观念和先入之见。你的女儿总是很快就会将你的行事方式与她自己的方式进行比较，而且她会提出一些让你感到相当尴尬的问题——有些问题本不该出自一个八岁孩子的口中，或者有些问题其实是你自己在训练过程中没有足够重视的。 不过，最终她还是熟练地运用那根简单的法杖，以她特有的从容姿态施展那些对她来说再自然不过的简单火系法术，而且完全没有出现任何失误。清子微笑着走到你身后，递给你一小杯茶，你心怀感激地接过了它——在这种环境中与纪久交谈，说实话，确实让人感到非常疲惫。 纪奈将法杖在空气中挥动了几下，顿时有一圈小火苗在她脚边跳动着，随后便熄灭了。 我明白你的意思了。 [kinu.Dad]我可以留这个用来多练习吗？ 你为什么不试试呢？反正现实世界中的对应物品并不会因为你让绮奴得到了这个物品就消失掉，对吧？ |基代子点了点头，让大家坐在那张矮桌旁，然后开始上课。她说的内容大多数你们根本听不懂——你们偶尔会听到凯特使用其中一些术语，但除此之外，这一切对你们来说都像天书一样。更糟糕的是，你们那位狡黠的妻子说话的方式实在让人难以理解 快一个个词语如同潺潺流淌的泉水般连绵不断地流淌出来。 不过，绮奴对此却毫无异议，她全神贯注地聆听着母亲的讲解。当初在户外玩耍时还只是那个毫无形态的能量团，如今已经被锤炼成了一根锋利无比的“针”；就连她的耳朵和尾巴，也几乎保持在了原来的样子。当清子拿出你带来的学徒法杖，开始进行实际操作演示时，绮奴更是认真地观察着每一处细节。 你有机会参与到这次教学活动中来——虽然大多数时候你只是充当练习对象而已，但话说回来，你女儿的教育毕竟很重要，对吧？ 对吧？ 这太有趣了！ 基努用法杖在你足部边召唤出一圈小火苗，发出尖叫声。由于有防护结界的存在，这些火焰并不会产生热量，但即便如此，也足以让人感到不安了。 我不知道是不是 更简单 使用它肯定比使用滚动条更方便，但确实如此。 不同." 这样做的意义何在呢？ 清子回答道。 希望你也能玩得开心。 [pc.name]." 这确实是一件值得珍惜的事情。虽然你不确定自己为这个“教训”贡献了多少，但至少你很开心能和你的妻子以及女儿一起度过那些时光。 哦！你介意我把这根棍子带在身边吗？我想再拿它做些实验。 没有理由拒绝给予绮奴这么多吧？ ] 谢谢， [kinu.Dad]也非常感谢大家今天能够来到这里，我真心感到十分感激。 你真的很感激她能留在这里，尽管现在应该是她的玩耍时间。她应该在外面开心地玩耍才对，不是吗？ 绮奴显得有点害羞，挠了挠后脑勺。 呵呵，如果你愿意去做的话，那也算是一种乐趣吧。 [kinu.Dad]." 好吧，好吧。我们能够聚在一起做些什么的事情其实并不常见……我真希望能想出一些能让全家人都参与其中的活动，但那样的话，后勤安排肯定会变得非常复杂。不过，还是感谢大家能来参加这次聚会。 [pc.name]我真心希望你们将来能继续更多地参与绮奴的教育。虽然由于你们访问的时间和方式可能会有一些困难，但无论如何，我们都非常感谢你们的付出。 当然，当然。嗯，是时候让你离开了。你最后在清子的脸颊上亲了一下，在纪奈的耳朵旁轻拍了一下，然后向她们道别，走下了小屋。阳光依然像你进入星界时那样温暖地照耀着大地，当你走向现实世界时，脸上也带着微笑。你的女儿如此轻松地掌握了贝拉兰的魔法，那么等她长大后，她肯定也会成为一名像她母亲一样出色的秘术师，甚至可能会更出色……
rows.raw: " Wordlessly, you take out the apprentice staff and pass it over the low table to Kiyoko. Seeing this, your kitsune wife's smile broadens just a little, and she takes the simple wooden staff in hand, examining the focusing crystal. "It's fascinating, isn't it? Both rely on the same basic principles, but the emergent forms they take are quite different, colored by the environments they evolved in. Hah... the sight of this brings back memories, and not all good ones." She hasn't spoken that much about her past before she got trapped in here, that's true. "Mostly because it wasn't a pleasant time for anyone involved. While there's something to be said for learning the lessons of the past, there's also not much point in dredging up bad memories for their own sake. Unless you're the kind who likes wallowing in that kind of moroseness, I suppose. Now then, I'll go call Kinu in — I'm sure she'll appreciate the change in her schedule. In the meantime, why don't you make yourself comfortable upstairs?" Upstairs? "If you please." [var0|Would she like you to take a more active part in the lesson? You've had some formal training in matters arcane in the past; if the object of this exercise is to impress upon Kinu the comparisons and contrasts between the native magics of Kiyoko's homeland and that of Belhar's legacy, then this is something you can help out with. "Yes, I'd be delighted to have someone share in the burden of answering our precocious daughter's questions, thank you very much. In fact, I'd like to see you take up the bulk of the task. It'll be a change of pace for me." |You'll acquiesce, but you're not exactly sure what you can do here. Magic's not quite your area of expertise at the moment. A smile. "As before, mostly for moral support. I'd like Kinu to know that even if you can't be with us that often, you're nevertheless interested in her education. I... well, she's been growing distracted and listless of late, as children do from time to time, and a couple of changes should help her focus her interest, at the very least." ] All right, then. While your foxy wife leaves the cabin in search of your daughter, you head upstairs and make yourself comfortable in the room she mentioned; clearly one that Kinu uses for magic lessons. [var0|With you being alone, you're able examine in detail the setup Kiyoko has placed over its entirety. She certainly knows what she's doing — there's a simple elegance that you easily recognize in the wards and charms that line the walls and ceiling. With your expertise, you're able to quickly figure that nothing short of a major magical mishap would escape the containment. Sure, you might not understand the language used in the calligraphy, but this doesn't need words to get the point across. |Once again, you're reminded how out of depth you are here in this place. Even as magically illiterate as you are, you're able to sense the strength of the wards in place here, a constant crawling sensation on your [pc.skinFurScales]. It's unsettling, but you can understand why Kiyoko isn't taking any chances with Kinu. ] It's not long before you hear footsteps on the stairs, and then the screen door slides open to admit both mother and daughter into the room. Kinu is a little scuffed up from playing outside, but by the spring in her step all the enthusiasm from running around in the fields has seamlessly transferred to the prospect of learning more about a subject she enjoys. "...Is this the day you finally teach me how to retrieve objects at a distance, Mama? Is that what you meant by doing something different today?" "Not until you've learned some self-control. But I've managed to rope your [pc.mf|father|mother]'s help in your education. You've been growing a little listless during lessons, so..." Kinu stops and clears her throat self-consciously when she sees you seated in the corner of the room. "Oh. Hello, [kinu.Dad]." Right. You're not sure how long your visit will be, so perhaps getting started would be a good idea. And so it is. [var0|For what feels like the next handful of hours, you sit down at the low table with Kinu while Kiyoko takes a back seat and observes the impromptu lesson. While you haven't forgotten that much theory you've learned, recent events have necessitated an emphasis on the practical, and it's this you attempt to impress upon your daughter as the lesson proceeds, using the apprentice staff as a learning tool. It's not an easy task by any means, especially with convincing Kinu to temporarily go back to basics and discard and preconceptions she's acquired. Your daughter is quick to draw parallels between your style of doing things and hers, and has more than one question that you feel rather uneasy answering — perhaps it's something that shouldn't be coming out of an eight-year-old's mouth, or simply something that you didn't pay close enough attention to during your training. At the end of it all, though, she's picked up using the simple staff as a focus with her trademark ease, sputtering around with the simple fire spells that come so naturally to her, and with no major mishaps to boot. Kiyoko comes up behind you with a smile and a small cup of tea, which you take gratefully — talking to Kinu in this kind of setting is certainly draining, to say the least. Kinu waves the staff about in the air a bit, conjuring a small ring of flames that dance about her feet before extinguishing themselves. "I see what you were getting at, [kinu.Dad]. Can I keep this for more practice?" You don't see why not. It's not as if its real-world counterpart is going to vanish if you let Kinu have this one, right? |With a nod, Kiyoko sits everyone down at the low table and begins the lesson. Most of the stuff she's saying is going straight over your head — you've heard Cait use a few of the terms from time to time, but otherwise it's all unintelligble to you. It doesn't help that your foxy wife is simply speaking so fast, one word rolling into the other like a gushing spring. Kinu is perfectly fine with this, though, listening to her mother with rapt attention. The amorphous blob of energy she was when playing outside has been honed into a fine-pointed needle; even her ears and tails are largely still as Kiyoko brings out the apprentice staff you brought in and starts with the practical demonstrations. You're given opportunities to help in the lesson — admittedly, mostly as a practice dummy, but hey, your daughter's education is worth it, right? Right? "This is fun!" Kinu squeals as she conjures a small ring of flames about your feet with the staff. There's no heat thanks to the wards, but it's still unnerving, to say the least. "I don't know if it's easier to use than a scroll would be, but it's certainly different." "Which is the point of the exercise," Kiyoko replies. "I hope you enjoyed yourself too, [pc.name]." It was something, all right. You're not sure how much you contributed to the lesson, but at least you appreciated being able to spend time with your foxy wife and daughter. "Oh! Do you mind if I keep the staff with me? I'd like to — uh — experiment with it some more." There's no reason to deny Kinu as much, is there? ] "Thank you, [kinu.Dad]. And thank you for being here today. I really appreciate it." And you really appreciate her being in here despite this being her playtime. She should be out there having fun, shouldn't she? Kinu looks a little sheepish and scratches the back of her head. "Ehe. If you want to do it, it counts as fun, [kinu.Dad]." "All right, all right. It's not that often that we're all able to get together to do something... I kind of wish I could come up with something that could involve the entire family, but that would be a bit of a logistics nightmare. In the meantime, thank you for coming, [pc.name]. I sincerely hope that you'll continue to be more involved in Kinu's education in time to come. It might be a bit hard because of when and how you can visit, but the effort is nevertheless appreciated." Of course, of course. Well, it's about time for you to leave. You give Kiyoko a final kiss on the cheek and Kinu a pat between her ears, then bid them goodbye as you head down and out of the cabin. The sun's still shining down as warmly as it was when you entered the Astral Plane, and there's a smile on your face as you head off into the waking world. With how effortlessly she picked up Behlaran magic, surely your daughter will grow up to be as fine an arcanist as her mother when she comes of age, if not more... "

rows.original: Knocking on the door, you're greeted by Kiyoko as usual. Your foxy wife is looking rather pleased with herself today, [kiyoko.pregStage 1|even more than the usual cheery demeanour that tends to accompany her when she's with child|but it's not the kind of sly smile that precedes events getting... uh, intense]. Rather, it's the kind of eager grin that bodes childish excitement, the kind that only looks good on someone as foxy as she is. "There you are, [pc.name]. I'd a feeling you'd turn up today; our firstborn daughter was quite excited at the prospect of your visit. She's been bouncing off the walls since yesterday." Not literally bouncing, you hope. A dry laugh. "I don't know about that, especially after she's gotten too much sweet fruit in her. But no, our daughter's just been rather enthusiastic about showing you what she's learned of late." You nod, close the door behind you, and follow Kiyoko into the cabin down familiar hallways. Oh? Why you? "Well, [pc.name]... call it a hunch, but I think Kinu looks up to you. She wants your approval more than she does mine — I'll admit I'm kind of jealous." And you'll admit you're somewhat flattered. One can only wonder why, though. "My guess is that you come by so infrequently that praise from you is a rare thing to behold," Kiyoko replies with a small sigh. "While I merely do the job of feeding and clothing our daughter, not to mention the small task of raising her to be a decent and useful person. You know, things that cause her to grow overfamiliar with me." Ha. As Kiyoko pushes aside the screen door to the sitting room, you're greeted by the sight of [ kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0 |Kinu sitting cross-legged on a cushion in a corner, right next to the chest of drawers that contains her mother's divination materials. She's got what looks like a long, thick flute nestled in both her hands like a prized possession, and stands to give the both of you a bow as you enter. "[kinu.Dad], Mama. Umm..." Kinu hesitates, your daughter's face coloring a little, then she puffs herself up as best as a petite eight year-old can, gathering confidence in the face of stage fright. "I'll be playing Call of the Swan for the both of you today. I hope you enjoy what I have to offer." "Hmph." Kiyoko tosses her head — she doesn't actually sniff derisively, but she conceivably could have any moment. "Come and sit at the table, [pc.name]. I'll serve us some tea while our daughter entertains us." While Kiyoko's back is turned getting the tea set, Kinu gives you a pleading look, her ice-blue eyes all big and wide. You... you're not exactly sure what's expected of you here. The best you manage is an encouraging nod, which appears to be enough; your daughter turns back to her preparations just as her mother saunters over and plonks the tea set down on the low table, serving up cups of bitter draught for you and herself. That's an interesting make of flute, you note as you sip the tea Kiyoko offers you. Something from Kiyoko's homeland, is it? "It's a shakuhachi. I don't really know much about them, save that one of my many brothers took it up as a hobby. I spent my years as a kit learning to play the koto from my mother, a properly elegant instrument." You're sensing a bit of conflict here. Did Kinu make it herself? "Ha, no. Those things take up to ten years to fashion from scratch. The astral plane must have conjured one for our daughter — but I didn't order it to do such..." Which means that it's starting to obey Kinu, too. Ah, you're starting to see the beginnings of why your daughter's progress is starting to get your foxy wife just the slightest bit worried. "I'm not resentful, just worried. It could cause problems if the astral plane started giving into her demands — can you imagine our daughter just conjuring up a never-ending supply of peaches to stuff her face with? I simply don't like unexpected developments sneaking in under my nose, you know? Especially when it concerns our daughter?" Hmm... Slowly, music begins to fill the room as Kinu starts playing, her fingers dancing over the flute's length as she closes her eyes in concentration. The tune is solemn with a deep and rich timbre — practically meditative and spiritual, when you focus a bit. It's calming, perhaps a little too much so, threatening to lull you to sleep if you don't keep your guard up... About the playing itself, though... not the best, to be honest. [ pc.bg minstrel |Listening to Kinu work the flute, you're pretty sure your daughter's missed a couple notes here and there, and ugh — that one was off-key, no doubt about it. The tune's still holding together, but there's little doubt in your mind there's plenty of room for improvement. If you knew the instrument yourself, you might've the mind to take her aside afterwards. |You may not know how to play music, but you've definitely heard enough in your time to tell if something's off, and the expression of disapproving distaste on Kiyoko's face is enough to suggest that it's indeed the case. Did Kinu just miss a note there? ] She's trying, gods knows she is, but perhaps she could've practiced a little bit more before choosing to perform for you... "Like I said, one of my many brothers used to play the shakuhachi back in the day," Kiyoko says with a sniff. "Our daughter has quite a ways to go yet, I'd say. Why, when I asked her the reason for choosing that over the koto where I'd be able to give her a proper education and guidance, she told me that I was too good at it and wanted to do something where she wouldn't be smothered." Hmm... is that animosity you're hearing from her? Kiyoko tightens her lips and sips her tea. "I don't know, I think I raised our daughter better than to pass over a perfectly good opportunity instead of stubbornly demanding to take the hard road." Eventually, the music dies down, Kinu lowers the bamboo flute, and she breaks the steady rhythm of her breathing with a small sigh. Turning your gaze from mother to daughter and back again, you clear your throat and tell Kinu you'll see her outside. "Yes, [kinu.Dad]." Wrapping her three tails about herself, Kinu shuffles out of the sitting room and into the hallway beyond. You follow suit, and it's only when the screen door's shut behind the two of you that your daughter looks askance and grinds her heels into the floor. So... "That wasn't very good, was it?" It could have been better, yes. If she knew she wasn't at a presentable level yet, why did she insist on performing in front of her mother and you? "I..." Kinu's lip trembles, but she catches herself and turns it into a pout. "I wanted you to recognize me." And so you are. She's catching flak for disobeying her mother, isn't she? "It's not disobeying. I... I just don't want to play the koto, [kinu.Dad]. It's not me, and I don't want to end up as a miniature copy of Mama, anyway. If two people are the same and agree on everything, one of them is unnecessary. Yes, I'm having a harder time learning the shakuhachi than I would the koto, but it's worth it. I want to find my way of expressing myself, not do it because it's what Mama does." ...So, at the end of the day, she wants to be more independent and her mother doesn't like it because she's interpreting it as disobedience. And yet the same argument she made for not wanting to learn the koto could arguably be applied to anything she was too lazy to bother with... "Are you on my side or not, [kinu.Dad]?" You're on no one's side. In fact, you'd like to see how this plays out — you'll tentatively support her efforts for now, but she should know you'll also be keeping a close eye on this situation. Hopefully, she'll conduct herself in a manner that'll reflect well on her and be able to perform again for you sometime down the road. "Boo." Kinu sniffs. "Well, I'm going to practice some more, then. Can't let you down, can I?" With that, she's off, eyes locked straight ahead and very definitely not eyeing you out of the corner of her vision. You watch your daughter disappear around a corner, her footsteps fading into the distance, then slip back into the sitting room where Kiyoko's waiting. "So? Were you able to coax anything out of our daughter?" Somewhat. There're some issues to be worked out with Kinu, but it was time you took a more active role in your daughter's life, anyway. You should also make some time to talk to Kiyoko about this, but not right now when tempers are running high. Maybe during another visit, when everyone's cooled down enough to be able to think more rationally about the issue. "You do that," Kiyoko says with a sigh as she pours herself another cup of tea. "It would really be nice if you helped with that handful of fluff from time to time. But enough about our daughter's misbehavior — let's have some alone time, [pc.name]. What's on your mind?" |Kinu kneeling on a cushion in one corner, right by the chest of drawers that contains her mother's divination materials. Set out in front of her is... well, it would look a little like a lute of the kind that little bard-boy in the Frost Hound plays, if a lute were flat, placed on the floor and raised on one end. All right, strings aside, it looks absolutely nothing like a lute. [ pc.bg minstrel |Now that you're thinking about it, you've vaguely heard of these kinds of instruments — a whole family of them, if you're not wrong. Zithers, were they? For some reason, they never seemed to catch on amongst any of your fellow minstrels. Probably a combination of them being less portable and local customs, if anything. ] "Hello, [kinu.Dad]," your firstborn fox-daughter pipes up. "And Mama, too." Indeed. What's this all about? "Well." Kinu looks a little uncertain for all of a moment, then puffs herself up as best as an eight year-old fox-child can. "I've been learning the koto from Mama, and um... I'd like to show you how far I've progressed. That, and I really want you to be able to enjoy some relaxing music, [kinu.Dad]. You always seem so stressed when you come. Think of it as thanks for always petting and playing with me." Kiyoko purrs and leans against you, one of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] foxy tails caressing your leg. "Such a sweet little thing, isn't she? Come, sit down; I'll bring us some tea." Faced with such an invitation by both wife and daughter, it's hard to say no. You take your usual place at the low table, Kiyoko brings up the tea set before settling in beside you, and she pours you a steaming cup of fresh, bitter brew as Kinu begins to play. You're not quite sure what to think. The melody's definitely foreign to your ears — [ pc.bg minstrel |as someone trained in the musical arts yourself, it's always nice to hear something that's out of the ordinary, perhaps pinch some of the better ideas in it for your own use |but that isn't about to dampen your enjoyment of your daughter's performance, though ]. It's lively, flowing and energetic, while still oozing elegance from every note Kinu plucks from the strings. She's putting a lot of feeling and soul into her playing, that's for sure. Beside you, Kiyoko has a big smile on her face as she sips at her tea, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails swishing back and forth as she savours the melody. Your foxy wife is looking immensely self-satisfied, and gives you a wink as you catch her eye. "It's very good, isn't it? She's better than I was when I was her age; it's almost frightening how quickly she picked it up. And she's playing one of my favorites, too." Mm-hm. But a clever child must have had an excellent teacher and mother to have gotten anywhere, right? "By Keros' name, you're such a flatterer," Kiyoko purrs. "In that case, your seed must have been exceptionally strong to produce such a precocious daughter, because that didn't come from my side of the family, I can tell as much." Oof, that was a good one. Your attention turns back to Kinu as your daughter's playing reaches a peak, music filling the room and seeping into your bones. Kinu is completely focused and alert, her large fox ears perked up, the intensity of her presence palpable as her fingers fly in a blur across the koto's strings. Amazing, she hasn't missed a single note — [ pc.bg minstrel |you'd like to think that this is something Kinu got from you as well, but that's probably patting yourself on the back a little too hard. You aren't that great of a minstrel — yet |or maybe she might have, but if she did you damn well couldn't tell ]. At last, though, the music dies down, and Kinu looks up uncertainly at the both of you. Poor thing's clearly seeking approval; smiling, you stand, step up to your daughter and pet her between the ears. She did good there. Your little floof daughter does her best to remain composed and elegant, but the color that creeps into her cheeks is obvious as you fluff her ear fur while she bows. "Thank you, [kinu.Dad]. I-I'll be going now." Before you can protest, little Kinu's picked up her instrument under and arm and is high-tailing it out in a flash. Kiyoko just laughs, sips her tea and folds her arms[kiyoko.pregStage 1| on her kit-swollen belly]. "Oh dear, seems like you embarrassed her. I remember feeling much the same when performing for the first time in front of someone who wasn't my mother. Don't worry, it'll pass." She gestures for you to take up your seat back at the table. "That was entertaining, wasn't it?" Indeed, it was. For Kinu to throw together a performance like that... A smile. "Like I said, [pc.name], she really, really wants your approval. But enough about that, it's a lovely day. Why don't we enjoy some time together?" ]

一个微笑。 就像我之前说的， [pc.name]她真的 真的吗 需要你的同意。不过，先不说这个了，今天是个美好的日子，我们为什么不一起享受一些时光呢？ ]
rows.raw: " Knocking on the door, you're greeted by Kiyoko as usual. Your foxy wife is looking rather pleased with herself today, [kiyoko.pregStage 1|even more than the usual cheery demeanour that tends to accompany her when she's with child|but it's not the kind of sly smile that precedes events getting... uh, intense]. Rather, it's the kind of eager grin that bodes childish excitement, the kind that only looks good on someone as foxy as she is. "There you are, [pc.name]. I'd a feeling you'd turn up today; our firstborn daughter was quite excited at the prospect of your visit. She's been bouncing off the walls since yesterday." Not literally bouncing, you hope. A dry laugh. "I don't know about that, especially after she's gotten too much sweet fruit in her. But no, our daughter's just been rather enthusiastic about showing you what she's learned of late." You nod, close the door behind you, and follow Kiyoko into the cabin down familiar hallways. Oh? Why you? "Well, [pc.name]... call it a hunch, but I think Kinu looks up to you. She wants your approval more than she does mine — I'll admit I'm kind of jealous." And you'll admit you're somewhat flattered. One can only wonder why, though. "My guess is that you come by so infrequently that praise from you is a rare thing to behold," Kiyoko replies with a small sigh. "While I merely do the job of feeding and clothing our daughter, not to mention the small task of raising her to be a decent and useful person. You know, things that cause her to grow overfamiliar with me." Ha. As Kiyoko pushes aside the screen door to the sitting room, you're greeted by the sight of [ kinu.kinuChildPersonality 0 |Kinu sitting cross-legged on a cushion in a corner, right next to the chest of drawers that contains her mother's divination materials. She's got what looks like a long, thick flute nestled in both her hands like a prized possession, and stands to give the both of you a bow as you enter. "[kinu.Dad], Mama. Umm..." Kinu hesitates, your daughter's face coloring a little, then she puffs herself up as best as a petite eight year-old can, gathering confidence in the face of stage fright. "I'll be playing Call of the Swan for the both of you today. I hope you enjoy what I have to offer." "Hmph." Kiyoko tosses her head — she doesn't actually sniff derisively, but she conceivably could have any moment. "Come and sit at the table, [pc.name]. I'll serve us some tea while our daughter entertains us." While Kiyoko's back is turned getting the tea set, Kinu gives you a pleading look, her ice-blue eyes all big and wide. You... you're not exactly sure what's expected of you here. The best you manage is an encouraging nod, which appears to be enough; your daughter turns back to her preparations just as her mother saunters over and plonks the tea set down on the low table, serving up cups of bitter draught for you and herself. That's an interesting make of flute, you note as you sip the tea Kiyoko offers you. Something from Kiyoko's homeland, is it? "It's a shakuhachi. I don't really know much about them, save that one of my many brothers took it up as a hobby. I spent my years as a kit learning to play the koto from my mother, a properly elegant instrument." You're sensing a bit of conflict here. Did Kinu make it herself? "Ha, no. Those things take up to ten years to fashion from scratch. The astral plane must have conjured one for our daughter — but I didn't order it to do such..." Which means that it's starting to obey Kinu, too. Ah, you're starting to see the beginnings of why your daughter's progress is starting to get your foxy wife just the slightest bit worried. "I'm not resentful, just worried. It could cause problems if the astral plane started giving into her demands — can you imagine our daughter just conjuring up a never-ending supply of peaches to stuff her face with? I simply don't like unexpected developments sneaking in under my nose, you know? Especially when it concerns our daughter?" Hmm... Slowly, music begins to fill the room as Kinu starts playing, her fingers dancing over the flute's length as she closes her eyes in concentration. The tune is solemn with a deep and rich timbre — practically meditative and spiritual, when you focus a bit. It's calming, perhaps a little too much so, threatening to lull you to sleep if you don't keep your guard up... About the playing itself, though... not the best, to be honest. [ pc.bg minstrel |Listening to Kinu work the flute, you're pretty sure your daughter's missed a couple notes here and there, and ugh — that one was off-key, no doubt about it. The tune's still holding together, but there's little doubt in your mind there's plenty of room for improvement. If you knew the instrument yourself, you might've the mind to take her aside afterwards. |You may not know how to play music, but you've definitely heard enough in your time to tell if something's off, and the expression of disapproving distaste on Kiyoko's face is enough to suggest that it's indeed the case. Did Kinu just miss a note there? ] She's trying, gods knows she is, but perhaps she could've practiced a little bit more before choosing to perform for you... "Like I said, one of my many brothers used to play the shakuhachi back in the day," Kiyoko says with a sniff. "Our daughter has quite a ways to go yet, I'd say. Why, when I asked her the reason for choosing that over the koto where I'd be able to give her a proper education and guidance, she told me that I was too good at it and wanted to do something where she wouldn't be smothered." Hmm... is that animosity you're hearing from her? Kiyoko tightens her lips and sips her tea. "I don't know, I think I raised our daughter better than to pass over a perfectly good opportunity instead of stubbornly demanding to take the hard road." Eventually, the music dies down, Kinu lowers the bamboo flute, and she breaks the steady rhythm of her breathing with a small sigh. Turning your gaze from mother to daughter and back again, you clear your throat and tell Kinu you'll see her outside. "Yes, [kinu.Dad]." Wrapping her three tails about herself, Kinu shuffles out of the sitting room and into the hallway beyond. You follow suit, and it's only when the screen door's shut behind the two of you that your daughter looks askance and grinds her heels into the floor. So... "That wasn't very good, was it?" It could have been better, yes. If she knew she wasn't at a presentable level yet, why did she insist on performing in front of her mother and you? "I..." Kinu's lip trembles, but she catches herself and turns it into a pout. "I wanted you to recognize me." And so you are. She's catching flak for disobeying her mother, isn't she? "It's not disobeying. I... I just don't want to play the koto, [kinu.Dad]. It's not me, and I don't want to end up as a miniature copy of Mama, anyway. If two people are the same and agree on everything, one of them is unnecessary. Yes, I'm having a harder time learning the shakuhachi than I would the koto, but it's worth it. I want to find my way of expressing myself, not do it because it's what Mama does." ...So, at the end of the day, she wants to be more independent and her mother doesn't like it because she's interpreting it as disobedience. And yet the same argument she made for not wanting to learn the koto could arguably be applied to anything she was too lazy to bother with... "Are you on my side or not, [kinu.Dad]?" You're on no one's side. In fact, you'd like to see how this plays out — you'll tentatively support her efforts for now, but she should know you'll also be keeping a close eye on this situation. Hopefully, she'll conduct herself in a manner that'll reflect well on her and be able to perform again for you sometime down the road. "Boo." Kinu sniffs. "Well, I'm going to practice some more, then. Can't let you down, can I?" With that, she's off, eyes locked straight ahead and very definitely not eyeing you out of the corner of her vision. You watch your daughter disappear around a corner, her footsteps fading into the distance, then slip back into the sitting room where Kiyoko's waiting. "So? Were you able to coax anything out of our daughter?" Somewhat. There're some issues to be worked out with Kinu, but it was time you took a more active role in your daughter's life, anyway. You should also make some time to talk to Kiyoko about this, but not right now when tempers are running high. Maybe during another visit, when everyone's cooled down enough to be able to think more rationally about the issue. "You do that," Kiyoko says with a sigh as she pours herself another cup of tea. "It would really be nice if you helped with that handful of fluff from time to time. But enough about our daughter's misbehavior — let's have some alone time, [pc.name]. What's on your mind?" |Kinu kneeling on a cushion in one corner, right by the chest of drawers that contains her mother's divination materials. Set out in front of her is... well, it would look a little like a lute of the kind that little bard-boy in the Frost Hound plays, if a lute were flat, placed on the floor and raised on one end. All right, strings aside, it looks absolutely nothing like a lute. [ pc.bg minstrel |Now that you're thinking about it, you've vaguely heard of these kinds of instruments — a whole family of them, if you're not wrong. Zithers, were they? For some reason, they never seemed to catch on amongst any of your fellow minstrels. Probably a combination of them being less portable and local customs, if anything. ] "Hello, [kinu.Dad]," your firstborn fox-daughter pipes up. "And Mama, too." Indeed. What's this all about? "Well." Kinu looks a little uncertain for all of a moment, then puffs herself up as best as an eight year-old fox-child can. "I've been learning the koto from Mama, and um... I'd like to show you how far I've progressed. That, and I really want you to be able to enjoy some relaxing music, [kinu.Dad]. You always seem so stressed when you come. Think of it as thanks for always petting and playing with me." Kiyoko purrs and leans against you, one of her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] foxy tails caressing your leg. "Such a sweet little thing, isn't she? Come, sit down; I'll bring us some tea." Faced with such an invitation by both wife and daughter, it's hard to say no. You take your usual place at the low table, Kiyoko brings up the tea set before settling in beside you, and she pours you a steaming cup of fresh, bitter brew as Kinu begins to play. You're not quite sure what to think. The melody's definitely foreign to your ears — [ pc.bg minstrel |as someone trained in the musical arts yourself, it's always nice to hear something that's out of the ordinary, perhaps pinch some of the better ideas in it for your own use |but that isn't about to dampen your enjoyment of your daughter's performance, though ]. It's lively, flowing and energetic, while still oozing elegance from every note Kinu plucks from the strings. She's putting a lot of feeling and soul into her playing, that's for sure. Beside you, Kiyoko has a big smile on her face as she sips at her tea, her [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] tails swishing back and forth as she savours the melody. Your foxy wife is looking immensely self-satisfied, and gives you a wink as you catch her eye. "It's very good, isn't it? She's better than I was when I was her age; it's almost frightening how quickly she picked it up. And she's playing one of my favorites, too." Mm-hm. But a clever child must have had an excellent teacher and mother to have gotten anywhere, right? "By Keros' name, you're such a flatterer," Kiyoko purrs. "In that case, your seed must have been exceptionally strong to produce such a precocious daughter, because that didn't come from my side of the family, I can tell as much." Oof, that was a good one. Your attention turns back to Kinu as your daughter's playing reaches a peak, music filling the room and seeping into your bones. Kinu is completely focused and alert, her large fox ears perked up, the intensity of her presence palpable as her fingers fly in a blur across the koto's strings. Amazing, she hasn't missed a single note — [ pc.bg minstrel |you'd like to think that this is something Kinu got from you as well, but that's probably patting yourself on the back a little too hard. You aren't that great of a minstrel — yet |or maybe she might have, but if she did you damn well couldn't tell ]. At last, though, the music dies down, and Kinu looks up uncertainly at the both of you. Poor thing's clearly seeking approval; smiling, you stand, step up to your daughter and pet her between the ears. She did good there. Your little floof daughter does her best to remain composed and elegant, but the color that creeps into her cheeks is obvious as you fluff her ear fur while she bows. "Thank you, [kinu.Dad]. I-I'll be going now." Before you can protest, little Kinu's picked up her instrument under and arm and is high-tailing it out in a flash. Kiyoko just laughs, sips her tea and folds her arms[kiyoko.pregStage 1| on her kit-swollen belly]. "Oh dear, seems like you embarrassed her. I remember feeling much the same when performing for the first time in front of someone who wasn't my mother. Don't worry, it'll pass." She gestures for you to take up your seat back at the table. "That was entertaining, wasn't it?" Indeed, it was. For Kinu to throw together a performance like that... A smile. "Like I said, [pc.name], she really, really wants your approval. But enough about that, it's a lovely day. Why don't we enjoy some time together?" ]"

rows.original: Somewhere else and some time ago... Warm sunlight breaks through the forest canopy in bright rays, warm against your skin as you clamber over roots and fallen logs. The soft, crumbly soil is just as cool, sticking to your bare feet and toes and feeling very, very pleasant. Mother'll kick up a fuss when you get back into the house if you don't wash your feet first... ...Come to think of it, you've got to be further into the forest than you've ever been before. Sure, home's always but a short distance away if you put your mind to it, but there's the thrill of adventure at going so deep, past the familiar landmarks... Does it ever end? The sound of flowing water catches your ear, and you slink through the pines and maples to investigate its source. Gradually,the trees fall away to reveal a small forest pond, its clear surface sparkling with reflected warmth, its bottom clearly visible even from where you stand. That's not all that there is to the place, though: flowers of every shape and color cluster about the water's edge, butterflies and moths flitting about their many-hued petals. A small stream flows outwards from whatever underground spring feeds the pool, trickling over mossy rock as it vanishes into the forest. This is perfect. A place to sit and rest your feet, plus Mother said she wanted you to gather some choice specimens for tomorrow's flower arrangement lessons. You've been walking for what feels like hours in search of something like this, and just when you were about to give up, such a scene of natural beauty happens to present itself... Is this what Mother means when she speaks of fate? Either way, there's no rest for someone as responsible as you! Getting on your hands and knees so that your face is level with the multitudes of blossoms strewn about the clearing, you set to sniffing and searching, doing your best to find the flower that's the prettiest. Tall grass tickles your tails and pollen gets in your nose, making you sneeze and your eyes water, but that's fine. Good things come to those who persevere, after all. One by one, you spend the rest of the afternoon picking through the options available to you, sniffing scents and munching on petals as you make your way around the forest glade. No, that one's blemished and wilted. No, that one's off; each flower in the arrangement must harmonise with the others, Mother says. No, that kind won't stay fresh for very long once you break it from its roots; the point is to keep the flowers pristine for as long as possible. One bad choice could ruin the entire arrangement... Hmm... Eventually, you get tired enough that you stop for a moment and soak your smarting feet in the pond's cool waters. So much time spent searching, and nothing to show for it... it's then that you spy a bunch of lilies growing in the soft, wet dirt by the water's edge. Those large, showy blooms with their elegant white petals and gentle fragrance make your heart skip a beat — sweet enough to be alluring, yet not so much that you dislike them. Kind of like peaches, really. If you cut them properly, they'd make a great centerpiece for tomorrow's lesson. Yes, this will certainly do. As you start towards the lilies, though, a flash of yellow catches your eye. Not five paces from them stands a clump of dandelions, their bright yellow color advertising itself, begging for your attention. Sure, they look a little scraggly, but you're sure they'd stay fresh a long time and moreover, you can feel new ideas for arrangements worming their way into your mind just by looking at them. Such resilience, such vigor, it can only spark inspiration even as it warms your heart. The two won't work together, though. Their colors, their auras — they simply clash too much, refusing to work together. Each one demands to be its own centerpiece, setting the theme for which the rest of the arrangement should take shape around. Dignified, alluring, fragrant — by all rights, you should take the lilies home for your lesson tomorrow. Yet there's a quiet resilience to the dandelions' simple beauty, one that draws the eye and makes your ears twitch. Mother won't be happy you brought home a weed, but she's never seen the appeal in such things — and besides, you can eat the dandelion when you're done with it. Which flower will you pick for your flower arrangement lesson with Mother?
rows.translation: 在某个地方，某个时候…… 温暖的阳光穿透森林的树冠，洒下明亮的光芒，当你攀爬着树根和倒下的原木时，这些光线温暖地抚触着你的皮肤。而那柔软、松软的泥土也同样凉爽，粘在你的赤足部上，感觉非常舒适。如果你不先洗足部就回到家里，妈妈肯定会大发雷霆的…… 仔细想想，你这次进入森林的范围肯定比以往任何时候都要深。当然，只要你想回去，家其实永远都在不远处，但深入森林，越过那些熟悉的地标，那种冒险的刺激感确实是非同寻常的…… 这种状态究竟何时才会结束呢？ 潺潺的流水声传入你的耳中，你悄悄地穿过松树和枫树林，去探寻它的源头。渐渐地，树木消失了，出现了一个小森林池塘——它清澈的湖面反射着温暖的光芒，即使站在那里，也能清楚地看到湖底。 不过，这个地方的可观赏之处还不止这些：各种形状和颜色的花朵簇拥在水边，蝴蝶和飞蛾在它们五彩斑斓的花瓣周围飞舞。有一条小溪从为这个水池提供水源的地下泉眼中流出，它蜿蜒流过长满苔藓的岩石，最终消失在森林之中。 这简直太完美了。这里既可以坐下来休息，而且妈妈还说让你采集一些优质的标本，用来准备明天的插花课。你似乎走了好几个小时才找到这样的地方，就在你准备放弃的时候，这样一片自然美景竟然出现在你面前…… 母亲所说的命运，难道就是这个意思吗？ 无论如何，对于你这样一个责任心强的人来说，根本不可能有休息的机会！你跪倒在地，让脸与空地上散落的那些花朵处于同一水平线上，开始仔细嗅闻、寻找，竭力找出最漂亮的那朵花。高高的草丛会挠你的尾巴，花粉也会进入你的鼻子，让你打喷嚏、眼睛流泪，但这些都没关系。毕竟，坚持到底的人总会得到好的回报。 一个下午的时间，你逐一挑选那些可供选择的鲜花，穿梭在森林的小径间，闻着花香，品尝着花瓣的芬芳。不，这一朵有瑕疵，已经枯萎了；不，这一朵也不行——母亲说过，插花时每一朵花都必须与其他花朵相协调。不，这种花一旦从花茎上摘下来，很快就不会新鲜了；关键是要让这些花朵保持最新鲜的状态。一个错误的选择，就可能会毁掉整个插花作品…… 嗯…… 最终，你累得实在受不了了，便停下来，将发痛的双足部浸入池塘清凉的水中。花了这么多时间寻找，却一无所获……就在这时，你注意到水边柔软潮湿的泥土中长着一丛丛莲花。 那些大型、醒目的花朵，拥有优雅的白色花瓣和淡淡的香气，会让你的心跳加速——它们甜美诱人，却又不会让人感到反感。其实，它们和桃子有点相似。如果处理得当，它们完全可以成为明天课程中完美的装饰品。 是的，这样肯定就可以了。 然而，当你朝着百合花的方向走去时，一道黄色的光芒吸引了你的目光。距离百合花仅有五步之遥的地方，有一丛蒲公英，它们那鲜艳的黄色色彩格外显眼，仿佛在吸引你的注意。虽然这些蒲公英看起来有点杂乱无章，但你相信它们一定能够保持很长时间的新鲜状态。更重要的是，仅仅是看着它们，你就会产生一些关于如何搭配花束的新想法。这种生命力、这种活力，不仅能激发你的灵感，还能温暖你的心。 然而，这两者是无法协同工作的。它们的颜色、它们所散发的气场——这些元素之间的冲突实在太过剧烈，根本无法协调一致。每一部分都坚持要成为整个组合的核心，都试图让自己成为整个布局的主题，而其他部分则必须围绕这个主题来展开。 高贵、诱人、芳香——按常理来说，你应该把这些百合花带回家，作为明天的学习素材。然而，蒲公英那种朴素的美中蕴含着一种默默的力量，这种美能够吸引人们的目光，让人忍不住想要仔细欣赏。妈妈肯定不会高兴你带了一株野草回家，但她从来没见过这类东西的魅力所在……更何况，你总可以 吃 用完之后，就把蒲公英扔掉吧。 那么，在和妈妈一起做插花练习时，你会选择哪朵花呢？

rows.original: You give the dandelions one last look, then decide against them. As nice and energetic as they may be, they simply lack the propriety needed to go into a flower arrangement; plants like that belong out in the fields and woods where they ought to be. A flower arrangement is supposed to be something refined and carefully curated; weeds like these have no place in one. Now these lilies, though, that's another matter. Even just taking one of the petals and rubbing it between thumb and forefinger makes you feel serene and happy; you're sure that Mother will approve of your choice. Good thing you brought everything you needed out all this way — filling a small vase with water from the pond, you cut the lilies near the base of the stem and quickly transfer them to the porcelain vase. That should keep them fresh and perky for as long as possible. It's odd. The more you look at the lilies, the more you like them; before long, there's a big smile on your face as you trundle back home. It's obvious these blossoms have a unique magnetism of their own, and Mother's sure to like them as much as you do. No matter how deep you venture into the forest, home is always but a thought away. Within minutes, the trees part and fall away to open up into the familiar sight of the hilltop once more. Mother's on the porch as you approach the door, a broom in her hands as she sweeps away fallen leaves and cherry blossoms. "Kinu!" You stop and give Mother a small bow. "Mama." "Ah, you're back, and I see you brought something for tomorrow's lesson. Wash your feet before you step into the house, okay? I just finished cleaning, and don't want you tracking dirt all over the place." "Yes, Mama." "Now, shall we see what you brought home?" Happily, you bounce up to Mother and push your tiny, fluffy body against hers, then hold out the vase for inspection. "Now, where'd you find these?" "Oh, here and there." "Really." A sly smile spreading on her face, Mother sets aside her broom and kneels down so her face is level with yours.[kiyoko.pregStage 3| It's a bit of a stretch considering how big her pregnant belly is, but Mother is surprisingly flexible for her current gravid state.] Slowly, she cups her chin in her hands and turns the full force of her jade-green eyes on you. "Well then, this is quite the pleasant surprise. It'll make a pretty good centerpiece for what we're going to be doing in tomorrow's lesson. You have a good eye for these things, Kinu." "Ehehehe. I wanted to make you a present, Mama." "Oh?" You flush a little and start fingering your braid. "I just wanted to thank you for all the good things you've done for me, Mama, starting with being born and everything since that." Upon hearing this, Mother lets out a little dry laugh. "I'm glad you were born too, even if it was the most difficult birth I've had to date. You had a big head even as a newborn; just make sure it's not the only thing that gets bigger as you get older, okay? It's easy to be full of yourself, especially when you don't just think, but know you're smart. It would be a pity if nothing but your head grew." "Ehehe." You clasp your hands together, and contrive to look a little sheepish. "Always be my mother, and never change, okay?" "That much I can do. All right then, I'll take these off your hands until tomorrow's flower arrangement lesson. Hmm, I know exactly where to put this, too — we have a bit of wall that's looking a little bare. Maybe we'll have to do a little calligraphy and make a scroll to hang up behind the flowers; that would look good." Mother takes the lilies from you, gives them a sniff, and sighs happily. "They're good, aren't they?" "So adorable. Just don't be like your mother and turn all grouchy and moody when you get to a difficult age, okay? I know I caused my mother all sorts of grief back in the day. Come here, let Mother pet you." You obediently bow your head, ears tilted forward, and squeal aloud as Mother dispenses affectionate headpats. Her fingers slide through your silky hair, firm against your scalp; your three tails wag so fast they're practically a blur. "Ehehehehehe." "Now then, off with you. Wash your feet, then get ready to help with dinner."
rows.translation: 你最后再看了一眼那些蒲公英，但还是决定不选用它们。尽管它们看起来很漂亮、充满生机，但它们确实缺乏制作花束所需的品质；这样的植物应该被种在田野和树林里，它们属于那里。花束应该是精致而经过精心挑选的物品，而这类杂草根本不适合用来制作花束。 不过，这些百合花就另当别论了 那就是 另一件事是，哪怕只是摘下一片花瓣，用拇指和食指轻轻揉搓，也会让你感到宁静而愉悦；你肯定相信，母亲会认可你的选择。幸好你一路上都带上了所需的一切——从池塘里取水装满一个小花瓶，然后在莲花的茎部附近将花剪下，迅速将它们移栽到那个瓷花瓶里。 这样就能让它们尽可能长时间地保持新鲜和活力。 奇怪的是，你越看这些百合花，就越喜欢它们；不久之后，当你欢快地走回家时，脸上一定会露出灿烂的笑容。显然，这些花朵本身就有一种独特的魅力，妈妈肯定也会和你一样喜欢它们的。 无论你走进森林多深，家始终就在咫尺之间。几分钟之内，树木就会让开道路，让你再次看到那熟悉的山顶景象。当你走近家门时，母亲会站在门廊上，手部里拿着一把扫帚，正在清扫落下的树叶和樱花花瓣。 基努！ 你停下来，向母亲微微鞠了一躬。 妈妈。 啊，你回来了，我看你带了些东西准备明天的课程用。进屋之前先洗洗足部，好吗？我刚打扫完，可不想让你把脏东西带得到处都是。 是的，妈妈。 现在，让我们来看看你带回了什么吧？ 幸运的是，你立刻跑向妈妈，将自己那柔软、毛茸茸的小身体贴在她身上，然后把花瓶拿出来让她看。 那么，你是在哪里找到这些的？ 哦，到处都是吧。 真的吗。 她脸上露出狡黠的笑容，放下扫帚，跪了下来，让自己的脸与你平视。[kiyoko.pregStage 3| 考虑到她怀孕后肚子已经变得那么大了，她还能保持这样的灵活性，确实有点不可思议。不过，以她目前的孕期状态来看，她的柔韧性确实相当不错。] 她缓缓地将下巴托在双手部之间，然后用那双翠绿色的眼睛紧紧地注视着你。 那么，这真是个令人愉快的惊喜。它将会成为我们明天课程中讨论内容的绝佳切入点。绮奴，你在这些方面确实有独到的眼光。 嘿嘿嘿，妈妈，我想送你一份礼物。 哦？ 你稍微冲洗了一下，然后开始摆弄自己的辫子。 妈妈，我只是想感谢你为我做过的所有好事，从你让我出生开始，到之后发生的每一件事。 听到这话，母亲发出了一声干涩的笑声。 我很高兴你也能来到这个世界上，尽管那是我经历过的最艰难的分娩过程。你刚出生的时候脑袋就很大；不过要记住，随着年龄的增长，不要让只有脑袋变得越来越大哦，好吗？人很容易变得自高自大，尤其是当你不仅会思考 知道 你真聪明。要是你只有脑袋能长出来，那就太可惜了。 嘿嘿。 你双手部交叠在一起，努力做出一副有点害羞的样子。 永远做我的妈妈，永远不要改变，好吗？ 这些我就能帮忙处理了。好吧，那这些就由我来帮您保管，等到明天的插花课再还给您。嗯，我也知道该把它们放在哪里——我们家里有段墙看起来有点空荡荡的，或许我们可以写些书法，制作一幅卷轴挂在花后面，那样会看起来很漂亮。 母亲从你手部中接过百合花，闻了闻，然后开心地叹了口气。 它们很不错，对吧？ 太可爱了。只是别像你妈妈那样，到了青春期就变得脾气暴躁、情绪多变，好吗？我知道是我造成的 我的 过去，它总是惹来各种麻烦。过来吧，让妈妈抱抱你。 你乖乖地低下头，耳朵向前倾，当妈妈温柔地轻拍你的头时，你发出了欢快的叫声。她的手部指穿过你柔软的头发，轻轻触碰着你的头皮；而你的三条尾巴则快速地摇动，几乎看不清它们的动作了。 嘿嘿嘿嘿。 好了，你现在可以走了。去洗洗足部，然后准备帮忙准备晚餐吧。
rows.raw: ' You give the dandelions one last look, then decide against them. As nice and energetic as they may be, they simply lack the propriety needed to go into a flower arrangement; plants like that belong out in the fields and woods where they ought to be. A flower arrangement is supposed to be something refined and carefully curated; weeds like these have no place in one. Now these lilies, though, that's another matter. Even just taking one of the petals and rubbing it between thumb and forefinger makes you feel serene and happy; you're sure that Mother will approve of your choice. Good thing you brought everything you needed out all this way — filling a small vase with water from the pond, you cut the lilies near the base of the stem and quickly transfer them to the porcelain vase. That should keep them fresh and perky for as long as possible. It's odd. The more you look at the lilies, the more you like them; before long, there's a big smile on your face as you trundle back home. It's obvious these blossoms have a unique magnetism of their own, and Mother's sure to like them as much as you do. No matter how deep you venture into the forest, home is always but a thought away. Within minutes, the trees part and fall away to open up into the familiar sight of the hilltop once more. Mother's on the porch as you approach the door, a broom in her hands as she sweeps away fallen leaves and cherry blossoms. "Kinu!" You stop and give Mother a small bow. "Mama." "Ah, you're back, and I see you brought something for tomorrow's lesson. Wash your feet before you step into the house, okay? I just finished cleaning, and don't want you tracking dirt all over the place." "Yes, Mama." "Now, shall we see what you brought home?" Happily, you bounce up to Mother and push your tiny, fluffy body against hers, then hold out the vase for inspection. "Now, where'd you find these?" "Oh, here and there." "Really." A sly smile spreading on her face, Mother sets aside her broom and kneels down so her face is level with yours.[kiyoko.pregStage 3| It's a bit of a stretch considering how big her pregnant belly is, but Mother is surprisingly flexible for her current gravid state.] Slowly, she cups her chin in her hands and turns the full force of her jade-green eyes on you. "Well then, this is quite the pleasant surprise. It'll make a pretty good centerpiece for what we're going to be doing in tomorrow's lesson. You have a good eye for these things, Kinu." "Ehehehe. I wanted to make you a present, Mama." "Oh?" You flush a little and start fingering your braid. "I just wanted to thank you for all the good things you've done for me, Mama, starting with being born and everything since that." Upon hearing this, Mother lets out a little dry laugh. "I'm glad you were born too, even if it was the most difficult birth I've had to date. You had a big head even as a newborn; just make sure it's not the only thing that gets bigger as you get older, okay? It's easy to be full of yourself, especially when you don't just think, but know you're smart. It would be a pity if nothing but your head grew." "Ehehe." You clasp your hands together, and contrive to look a little sheepish. "Always be my mother, and never change, okay?" "That much I can do. All right then, I'll take these off your hands until tomorrow's flower arrangement lesson. Hmm, I know exactly where to put this, too — we have a bit of wall that's looking a little bare. Maybe we'll have to do a little calligraphy and make a scroll to hang up behind the flowers; that would look good." Mother takes the lilies from you, gives them a sniff, and sighs happily. "They're good, aren't they?" "So adorable. Just don't be like your mother and turn all grouchy and moody when you get to a difficult age, okay? I know I caused my mother all sorts of grief back in the day. Come here, let Mother pet you." You obediently bow your head, ears tilted forward, and squeal aloud as Mother dispenses affectionate headpats. Her fingers slide through your silky hair, firm against your scalp; your three tails wag so fast they're practically a blur. "Ehehehehehe." "Now then, off with you. Wash your feet, then get ready to help with dinner."'

rows.original: Pick some of the lilies. Calm and elegant is your style.
rows.translation: 摘一些百合花吧。宁静而优雅，这才是你的风格。
rows.raw: "Pick some of the lilies. Calm and elegant is your style."

rows.original: You've made your decision — the dandelions it is. Rolling up your sleeves, you take a firm grip on the stems near the base of the choicest specimen, and pull. The weed is stubborn, but you're even more so; it fights you every step of the way, clinging to the ground with surprisingly strong roots. Little wonder Mother's so aghast when one of these happens to take root in the vegetable garden; it just refuses to give up when other, lesser weeds would've surrendered long ago. In a way, you can't help but feel a grudging respect for your foe even as it resists you to the very end, even though the outcome is clearly no longer in doubt. But you win — at long last, you win. Clods of dirt still clinging to its roots, the dandelion comes free of the earth and into your hands. Your fingers sting and the scent of sap is heavy in the air, but you've nevertheless won. Phew. Were you supposed to put it in water? Eh, you've forgotten to bring a bowl or vase or something to put it in; you simply can't move in the woods with something like that weighing you down anyway. Best to get it home as quickly as possible, then. Despite you having been rooting about in the forest for hours, finding your way back to the big tree is always a simple matter of minutes, and you practically bump into Mother on your way in. She's sweeping the porch of fallen leaves and cherry blossoms, and looks up at you sharply as you try to push past her. "Kinu!" "Can't talk, Mama. I need to put down this flower in some water before it starts to wilt!" "No, young lady, you're stopping right there. You're not going to track dirt into the house when I've just finished cleaning it." Mother stops, looks you up and down, then curls her lip. "You needed to get water, you said? Well then, march yourself over to the well and draw yourself a bath. You're filthy from head to toe, and there's pollen all over your hair and fur." Eeeeh... you never noticed. But now that Mother's pointed it out, there's no denying it. You are pretty dirty. Guess you were a little too into the spirit of things... "You did get something for tomorrow's flower arrangement lesson, didn't you?" "Like I said, Mama, I have to put this flower in some water!" Mother blinks at the brilliant yellow dandelion you have in your hands, its roots still attached to a clod of earth. What's with the disappointment? Surely she can see why you made your choice, can't she? "Why a dandelion?" she says at last. "I like it! It's very strong and vibrant!" "And... ?" "And you can use it for many things! The flower, the roots, the stem and leaves..." "I spend hours trying to teach you the language of flowers, and this is what you come up with?" You pout. "I know the language, Mama. Trust me, I do. But sometimes I find that it isn't able to speak the words I want to say. That's why... that's why I want this one!" This dandelion, it's yours. You found it. If Mother makes you throw it out and get another one from the forest, you'll... you'll... You'll what, exactly? A small sigh. Then, to your surprise, Mother's hand finds its way to your head and begins ruffling the scruffy hair between your ears. "Fine, do as you wish. Just go and wash that dirt off you now, understand? That, and check in on the daikon radishes while you're behind the house; we'll be having some for dinner." Strange. You'd expected Mother to put up more of a fight than that, but you're not going to question her change of heart. Dandelion still clasped in your cupped hands, you turn tail and head for the rear of the tree. Some things never change... but sometimes, they do.
rows.translation: 你已经做出了决定——要拔掉那些蒲公英。你卷起袖子，紧紧抓住那株最茂盛的蒲公英的茎部，开始用力拔拉。这种杂草非常顽固，但你也毫不退缩；它在每一个环节都在与你抗争，那些根系紧紧地抓住地面，让人感到十分难以拔除。 难怪当这种杂草在菜园里扎根时，妈妈会如此惊慌失措——因为它会顽强地坚持下去，而那些比较普通的杂草早就放弃了抵抗。在某种程度上，你甚至会不由得对这种敌人产生一种莫名的敬意，尽管它一直在与你抗争到底，尽管结果早已显而易见。 但你赢了——终于，你赢了。那些粘在蒲公英根部的泥土还未完全脱落，但它已经从土里钻了出来，落在了你的手部中。你的手部指被刺痛了，空气中弥漫着浓重的汁液气味，但无论如何，你还是赢了。 呼…… 你是不是应该把它放在水里呢？呃，你忘了带碗或者花瓶之类的容器来装它吧；直接这样放是不对的。 移动 当有这样的东西压在身上时，待在树林里实在不是什么好事。所以，最好尽快把它带回家。尽管你在森林里找了几个小时，但找到回到那棵大树的路其实只需要几分钟而已。而当你往回走的时候，几乎一下子就碰到了妈妈。她正在打扫门廊上落下的树叶和樱花花瓣，当你试图从她身边经过时，她猛地抬头看了你一眼。 基努！ 妈妈，我现在不能说话。我得把这朵花放在水里，否则它就会开始枯萎了！ 不行，小姐，您就停在这里吧。我刚把房子打扫干净，您可不能把灰尘带进屋里去。 母亲停下来，上下打量了你一番，然后撇了撇嘴。 你说你需要去取水，是吧？那就好好走到井边去打些水来洗个澡吧。你从头到脚都脏兮兮的，头发和毛皮上还沾满了花粉。 呃……你之前从来都没有注意到这一点。但既然妈妈指了出来，那就无可否认了。你 是 相当过分啊。看来你真是太投入其中了…… 你 做了 你为明天的插花课准备了一些东西，对吧？ 就像我说的，妈妈，我必须把这朵花放在水里才行！ 母亲看着你手部中那朵亮黄色的蒲公英，它的根部还紧紧地粘着一块土。你为什么看起来这么失望呢？她肯定能够理解你做出这个选择的原因，对吧？ 为什么选蒲公英呢？ 她终于开口说道。 我喜欢！它非常有力，充满活力！ 然后……？ 而且它的用途非常多！花、根、茎、叶……都可以用来做各种事情。 我花了数小时的时间试图教你理解花语，而你给出的却是这样的结果？ 你撅起了嘴。 妈妈，我会说这种语言。相信我，我真的会。但有时候，我发现这种语言无法表达我想说的话。所以……所以我才想要这个！ 这种蒲公英啊，真是 你的你找到了它。如果妈妈让你把它扔掉，然后去森林里再找一个，你就会……你就会……” “你到底会怎么样呢？” 轻轻叹了口气。然后，令你惊讶的是，妈妈的手部伸到了你的头上，开始拨弄你耳边那些乱糟糟的头发。 好吧，随你的便。现在就去把身上的脏东西洗干净，明白吗？另外，在你去屋后的时候顺便看看那些大根萝卜吧，我们晚饭要用它们。 奇怪。你本以为母亲会抵抗得更激烈一些，但你也不会质疑她态度的转变。手部中依然紧握着那朵蒲公英，你转身朝树的后方走去。有些事情永远都不会改变……但有时候，它们也会改变的。
