rows.original: Praise Kinu and tell her to keep up the good effort. Even with a natural advantage, she's going to have her work cut out for her if she's aiming to be a stunner when she grows up.
rows.translation: 表扬绮奴，告诉她要继续保持这样的努力。即使她拥有天生的优势，但如果她立志将来成为一名出色的模特，她仍然需要付出很多努力。
rows.raw: "Praise Kinu and tell her to keep up the good effort. Even with a natural advantage, she's going to have her work cut out for her if she's aiming to be a stunner when she grows up."

rows.original: Rubbing your chin, you take a step back and adopt a thoughtful expression. Hmm... "Is something the matter, [kinu.Dad]?" Well, being attractive and charismatic is all well and good, but has she stopped to think this all the way through? She may be a smart cookie, but she needs to have the wisdom to consider a matter from different angles here. For example, sure, flaunting what she's got all over the place is sure to attract attention like she plans, but not all of the attention she'll receive that way is going to be of the good kind. Here in the Astral Plane it's just her mother and siblings around, but it's a far less safe world out there filled with all manner of creeps, asses, and clingy losers who can't take no for an answer — and that's just the scum floating on the top of the barrel. Kinu just looks confused. "I'm not completely sure what you're getting at, [kinu.Dad]. Are you saying that I shouldn't be pretty so as not to attract unwanted attention?" No, you're not telling her that she shouldn't strive to make herself as alluring and captivating as possible — given how long you've been with her mother, you know that she has a natural propensity for that, being a kitsune and all. What you're saying is that there are different approaches to what she wants without being blatant about it; if she plays her hand right, she can avoid a good portion of the drawbacks of being a looker. [pc.bg courtesan|Given what you used to do for a living as a courtesan, you should know as much. She should definitely not have to experience the uglier portions of your past if you can help it. While it might not have personally happened to you — or it might have and you're not telling Kinu — some of the higher-class, more in-demand courtesans would be harassed off-hours by those who simply didn't understand the nature of the job, by those who mistook the feigned affection for real. Then there was the endless backbiting that took place against them by others in the same profession - Looking back on it, being run out of town was the best thing that happened to you.|] "[kinu.Dad]?" Right, sorry for the silence — you were just thinking. "If what I'm doing is going to get me into trouble, what do you suggest, then?" Well, less is more, for one. There's something to be said for the value of subtlety and surprise, a blade in the dark. Perhaps she could try and make her approach a little more incidental; being all up in someone's face would increase the risk of her actual intentions coming to light — and that would defeat the purpose of such, wouldn't it? "Eh..." A modest outfit, a homely countenance to disguise herself, conceal and camouflage her true nature. But with a slight shift of posture, a smile, or when the light just happens to hit her fur right — the shiv comes out when it's least expected, enrapturing all who look upon her and leaving them wondering how they couldn't have seen it earlier. And all while being plausibly deniable. Your foxy daughter's face brightens as realization gradually dawns, her ears wiggling with excitement as she looks positively impish. "I think I see what you're getting at, [kinu.Dad] and it's not a bad idea at all. Not a bad idea at all. Also, this way I won't have to intrude on Mama's particular expertise... even come up with a style of my own! I know I can't compete with her on her own turf... plus this way I'll still get to dig about in the dirt and hop into leaf piles and do all sorts of other fun things!" Now she's coming around to your way of thinking, eh? "Eeheehee. I'm going to be one of those rural beauties, strike when it's least expected! Draw the gazes of people, then make them feel ashamed for staring at such a wholesome girl! Oh, growing up is going to be so fun!"
rows.translation: 你摸了摸下巴，后退一步，露出若有所思的表情。嗯…… 出了什么问题吗？ [kinu.Dad]?" 嗯，拥有吸引人的外貌和迷人的魅力固然很好，但她有没有认真思考过这一切呢？她可能是个聪明人，但在这个问题上，她需要具备从不同角度进行分析的智慧。 比如说，她把自己的优势到处展示，确实会像她预想的那样吸引注意力，但这样得到的关注并不全是积极的。在这里的星界，周围只有她的母亲和兄弟姐妹，但外面的世界却危险得多，那里到处都是各种卑鄙小人、混蛋，还有那些死缠烂打、连拒绝都接受不了的失败者——而这些只不过是表面现象罢了。 纪久只是显得有些困惑而已。 我不太明白你到底想表达什么 [kinu.Dad]你是说，我应该不要长得漂亮，这样就不会吸引那些不必要的注意了吗？ 不，你并不是在告诉她不应该努力让自己变得尽可能吸引人、迷人——毕竟你和她母亲相处了这么久，你应该知道她天生就具备这样的特质，毕竟她可是一只狐妖啊。你的意思是，要想实现她的目标，可以采取不同的方法，而不必过于直白地表现出来；如果她处理得当，就可以避免那些因为外貌出众而可能带来的种种麻烦。 [pc.bg courtesan|鉴于你曾经以妓女为职业，你应该很清楚这些事情。她肯定也应该知道。 不是 如果可以避免的话，人们确实应该尽量避免面对自己过去那些不堪回首的经历。虽然这些事情可能并没有真正发生在你身上——或者虽然发生了但你并没有告诉绮奴——但那些属于上层社会、备受追捧的妓女们，往往会在工作时间之外遭到那些根本不了解这份工作本质的人的骚扰；那些将她们表面的柔情误认为是真感情的人，也会对她们进行骚扰。 然后，还有同行业其他人对他们进行的无休止的诽谤与中伤—— 回想起来，被赶出那个城市其实是发生在你身上最幸运的事情。|] "[kinu.Dad]?" 好吧，抱歉刚才没说话——你当时可能在思考些什么吧。 如果我这样做会给我带来麻烦，那你有什么建议呢？ 嗯，首先，少即是多。巧妙与惊喜确实具有很大的价值，就如同暗中的利刃一样。或许她可以尝试让自己的行动显得更自然、更偶然一些；如果总是直接暴露在别人的视线中，就很容易让别人察觉到她的真实意图——而那样就违背了这样做的初衷，不是吗？ 呃…… 一身朴素的装束，一张平凡的面容，这些都是她用来伪装自己、隐藏真实本性的手段。然而，只要她稍微调整一下姿势，露出一丝微笑，或者当轻型线恰好照射在她的毛发上时——她那隐藏的特质就会在最不经意的时候显现出来，吸引所有注视她的人，让他们不禁疑惑：自己之前怎么就没发现呢？ 而这一切，都可以被合理地否认。 当你那狡黠的女儿逐渐明白过来时，她的脸上露出了灿烂的笑容，耳朵也因为兴奋而不停地动来动去，看上去简直坏心眼十足。 我想我明白你的意思了 [kinu.Dad] 这确实是个不错的主意。真的不错。而且这样我就不必去干扰妈妈的专业领域了……甚至还可以发展出属于自己的风格呢！我知道，在她的专业领域里，我根本无法与她竞争……但这样我仍然可以继续在泥土里挖来挖去，跳进落叶堆里，做各种各样有趣的事情！ 现在她也开始认同你的观点了，是吧？ 嘻嘻嘻，我一定要成为那种乡下美女，总是在最意想不到的时候出现！吸引所有人的目轻型，然后让他们为自己盯着这么纯洁可爱的女孩而感到羞愧！哦，成长一定会非常有趣呢！
rows.raw: " Rubbing your chin, you take a step back and adopt a thoughtful expression. Hmm... "Is something the matter, [kinu.Dad]?" Well, being attractive and charismatic is all well and good, but has she stopped to think this all the way through? She may be a smart cookie, but she needs to have the wisdom to consider a matter from different angles here. For example, sure, flaunting what she's got all over the place is sure to attract attention like she plans, but not all of the attention she'll receive that way is going to be of the good kind. Here in the Astral Plane it's just her mother and siblings around, but it's a far less safe world out there filled with all manner of creeps, asses, and clingy losers who can't take no for an answer — and that's just the scum floating on the top of the barrel. Kinu just looks confused. "I'm not completely sure what you're getting at, [kinu.Dad]. Are you saying that I shouldn't be pretty so as not to attract unwanted attention?" No, you're not telling her that she shouldn't strive to make herself as alluring and captivating as possible — given how long you've been with her mother, you know that she has a natural propensity for that, being a kitsune and all. What you're saying is that there are different approaches to what she wants without being blatant about it; if she plays her hand right, she can avoid a good portion of the drawbacks of being a looker. [pc.bg courtesan|Given what you used to do for a living as a courtesan, you should know as much. She should definitely not have to experience the uglier portions of your past if you can help it. While it might not have personally happened to you — or it might have and you're not telling Kinu — some of the higher-class, more in-demand courtesans would be harassed off-hours by those who simply didn't understand the nature of the job, by those who mistook the feigned affection for real. Then there was the endless backbiting that took place against them by others in the same profession - Looking back on it, being run out of town was the best thing that happened to you.|] "[kinu.Dad]?" Right, sorry for the silence — you were just thinking. "If what I'm doing is going to get me into trouble, what do you suggest, then?" Well, less is more, for one. There's something to be said for the value of subtlety and surprise, a blade in the dark. Perhaps she could try and make her approach a little more incidental; being all up in someone's face would increase the risk of her actual intentions coming to light — and that would defeat the purpose of such, wouldn't it? "Eh..." A modest outfit, a homely countenance to disguise herself, conceal and camouflage her true nature. But with a slight shift of posture, a smile, or when the light just happens to hit her fur right — the shiv comes out when it's least expected, enrapturing all who look upon her and leaving them wondering how they couldn't have seen it earlier. And all while being plausibly deniable. Your foxy daughter's face brightens as realization gradually dawns, her ears wiggling with excitement as she looks positively impish. "I think I see what you're getting at, [kinu.Dad] and it's not a bad idea at all. Not a bad idea at all. Also, this way I won't have to intrude on Mama's particular expertise... even come up with a style of my own! I know I can't compete with her on her own turf... plus this way I'll still get to dig about in the dirt and hop into leaf piles and do all sorts of other fun things!" Now she's coming around to your way of thinking, eh? "Eeheehee. I'm going to be one of those rural beauties, strike when it's least expected! Draw the gazes of people, then make them feel ashamed for staring at such a wholesome girl! Oh, growing up is going to be so fun!" "

rows.original: Tell Kinu that being pretty is all well and good, but it might have unforeseen — and unwanted — side effects. Less is more
rows.translation: 告诉绮奴，漂亮固然很好，但这也可能会带来一些意想不到的、甚至是不希望出现的副作用。少即是多。
rows.raw: "Tell Kinu that being pretty is all well and good, but it might have unforeseen — and unwanted — side effects. Less is more"

rows.original: As you approach the hill's crest, stepping into the shade of the massive cherry blossom tree that houses Kiyoko's cabin, you're greeted with a curious sight: Kinu is sitting cross-legged on the grassy earth, her back propped against one of the tree's thick roots, a thin stick of charcoal in hand and a workbook in her lap. Your kitsune daughter's big blue eyes are glued intently to the pages in front of her, her little fingers are all smudged several times over, and there's a bowl of what might have once been some kind of cold iced dessert, only it's all melted into a pink and white mess, smelling distinctly of peach. Looks like she's been here for a while, then. Completely engrossed, Kinu doesn't even notice you as you approach — not until you're standing right next to her and plant a hand on her head right between her twitching foxy ears. A squeal of surprise escapes your kitsune daughter's mouth as her fluffy ears stiffen, her three tails poof up and swish to and fro, knocking over the dessert bowl and sending beans, cubed peaches and melted ice all over the grass. "I... I..." her hand's gripping the charcoal stick so tightly, it's a small wonder it hasn't snapped in twain already. "That wasn't nice, [kinu.Dad]... oooohh..." Back and forth your hand moves, quelling any complaints Kinu might have as you reduce your white-furred kitsune daughter into a mewling mush. You smooth over her ears and tousle her hair, watching as her head bobs with your movements. Kinu opens and shuts her mouth several times as if to voice complaint, but always stops short of actually doing so, eventually settling for being handled like a limp fox kit. "What's the occasion, [kinu.Dad]? Ooh, I just lost my train of thought there..." Not much; you saw your best daughter sitting here and thought you'd stop to greet her before heading on in to see her mother. What's in her lap that's so gripping, she forgot to eat her sweets? Wordlessly, Kinu picks up the workbook from her lap and shows it to you. [pc.bg noblescion arcanist scholar|One page is full of illegible scrawl, while the other has a couple of diagrams pencilled in. Looks like Kiyoko's setting her on basic geometry here. Well, basic for you, that is. Maybe not so much for an eight-year-old. |Scribbles in Kinu's hand fill the right page, while the left is occupied by a number of neatly-drawn circles and triangles, clearly her mother's work. You peer at the lot for a bit, but they might as well be written in Kiyoko's native tongue where you're concerned. ] Looks like her mother's set her some math problems. "She told me to take these and go outside for a bit. I think Mama's in one of her moods again." Kinu puts her fingers together and starts twiddling them. "Somehow, though, I think that mood will clear right up when you show your face at the door, [kinu.Dad]." Hmm. And she finds these quite gripping, does she? "Ehe. I can't quite seem to figure this one out..." You look back down at the workbook again, take in the utter mess of charcoal scrawlings that Kinu's made of the paper. [pc.bg noblescion arcanist scholar|It's with some difficulty that you follow the working and thought processes she's laid down — in no small part due to her atrocious handwriting when she's frustrated — but after some time you figure out where exactly in the problem Kinu's gone wrong. No wonder she can't solve it if she's simply brought the error forward throughout the problem. |Without the educational backing to understand what's going on here, you're just as lost and hopeless as your kitsune daughter is.] "I solved most of the problems without even needing to put any working down on paper," Kinu declares with no small amount of pride. Sniffling, she picks up the dessert bowl and licks it clean of what little syrup and cream's left in the bottom, muffling her voice as she speaks. "This one, though..." Hmm... "It's driving me crazy, [kinu.Dad]. I'm beginning to suspect Mama just gave me an unsolvable problem just to get me out of her hair." [pc.bg noblescion arcanist scholar| No, she hasn't. You can vouch for that, having worked it out yourself; besides, Kiyoko's not the kind of person who would do that. Effective as it might be in tying up her most precocious daughter, you're sure her mother would understand the damage deliberately setting an impossible problem for her would do. Kinu sighs, sets down the dessert bowl, and leans back against the tree root. "I guess... what do I do now, then?" | You don't know about that, but you have full faith Kiyoko wouldn't do something like that to her own daughter and risk spoiling her daughter's learning spirit. That would be counterproductive, and by far not worth a few hours of getting Kinu out of the house. "You have a lot of faith in Mama, [kinu.Dad]." Well, of course you do. How does she imagine she came about in the first place? "Hmph... well. What do I do now, then?" ]
rows.translation: 当你即将登上小山的顶峰，走进那棵巨大的樱花树的荫蔽之下——那里正是清子的小屋所在——你会看到一幅奇特的景象：纪奈正盘腿坐在草地上，背部靠在树根上，手中拿着一根细炭笔，腿上放着一本练习册。 你那只狐妖女儿那双大大的蓝眼睛紧紧地盯着眼前的书页，她的小手指因为反复翻阅而被弄得满是污迹。还有一个碗，里面原本可能是某种冰镇甜点，但现在都已经融化了，变成了一团粉白相间的糊状物，还散发着明显的桃子香味。 看来她已经在这里待了一段时间了。 绮奴完全沉浸在游戏之中，甚至没有注意到你的靠近——直到你站在她旁边，将手放在她那两只不停抽动的狐妖耳朵中间时，她才注意到你。 你的九尾狐女儿惊讶地尖叫起来，她那毛茸茸的耳朵立刻竖了起来，三条尾巴也一下子翘了起来，来回摆动，结果把装甜点的碗打翻了，豆子、切块的桃子和融化的冰块全都洒在了草地上。 我……我…… 她的手紧紧地握着那根炭笔，真不可思议它居然还没有折断。 那样做可不太好。 [kinu.Dad]……哦哦哦…… 你来回移动着手，安抚着基努可能发出的任何抱怨，将你那身白色毛发的狐妖女儿揉成一团呜咽的肉团。你轻抚她的耳朵，拨弄她的毛发，看着她的脑袋随着你的动作一颠一簸。基努几次张嘴似乎想要抱怨，但最终都没有真正说出来，只能任由你像对待一只无力的小狐妖一样摆布她。 有什么特别的原因吗？ [kinu.Dad]哦，我刚才有点走神了…… 没什么特别的；你看到自己最疼爱的女儿坐在这里，就想着先停下来跟她打个招呼，然后再去见她的母亲。她腿上拿的是什么东西，让她看得如此入迷，甚至忘记了吃甜点？ 金无言地从自己腿上拿过练习册，递给了你。 [pc.bg noblescion arcanist scholar|其中一页上写满了难以辨认的潦草字迹，而另一页上则画了几张简陋的图表。看来清子正在通过这些图表向他讲解基础几何知识。嗯，也算是基础吧 你也就是说，对于一个八岁的孩子来说，可能就不是那么适用了。 |希努手写的涂鸦占据了右边的页面，而左边则画满了整齐排列的圆圈和三角形，这些显然是她母亲的作品。你仔细观察了那些图案一会儿，但对你来说，它们简直就像是用清子的母语写出来的一样，完全无法理解其中的意思。 ] 看来她妈妈给她布置了一些数学题。 她让我拿这些东西然后出去走一会儿。我觉得妈妈又进入那种情绪不好的状态了。 纪奈将手指并拢，开始不停地摆弄它们。 不过，我觉得只要你出现在门口，那种阴郁的情绪就会立刻烟消云散的。 [kinu.Dad]." 嗯，她觉得这些内容相当吸引人，是吧？ 呵呵，这个我实在搞不太明白…… 你再次低头看着那本练习本，看着绮奴在纸上留下的那些乱七八糟的炭笔痕迹，心中不禁感到一阵无奈。 [pc.bg noblescion arcanist scholar|要理解她所阐述的解题思路和思考过程确实有些困难——这在很大程度上是因为她在感到沮丧时字写得非常潦草——但过了一段时间后，你终于弄清楚了绮奴在问题的哪个环节出了错。难怪她无法解决这个问题，因为她只是把错误一直延续到了问题的最后阶段而已。 |如果没有相应的知识背景来理解这里发生的事情，你也会和你那个狐妖女儿一样感到迷茫和无助。] 我甚至都没有把解题过程写在纸上，就解决了大部分问题。 纪奈带着毫不掩饰的骄傲说道。她抽着鼻子，拿起甜点碗，把碗底剩下的糖浆和奶油舔得干干净净，说话时声音也低了下去。 不过这个…… 嗯…… 这真要把我逼疯了 [kinu.Dad]我开始怀疑，妈妈其实是故意给我一个根本无法解决的问题，只是为了让我别再来烦她。 [pc.bg noblescion arcanist scholar| 不，她并没有那么做。你自己也参与过解决这个问题，所以你可以为此作证；再说，清子也不是会做出那种事的人。虽然这种方法确实能够约束她那个最早熟的女儿，但她的母亲肯定能够理解，故意给她设置一个无法解决的问题，会给她带来多大的伤害。 纪奈叹了口气，放下甜点碗，然后靠在树根上。 我想……那我现在该做什么呢？ | 你可能不知道，但你完全相信清子不会对自己的女儿做出那样的事，她绝不会冒着破坏女儿学习积极性的风险去这么做。那样的做法只会适得其反，绝对不值得为了把纪奈从家里弄出去而花费几个小时的时间。 你对妈妈充满了信任， [kinu.Dad]." 嗯，你当然这么认为了。她究竟是怎么想象自己会出现在这个世上的呢？ 哼……那么，我现在该做什么呢？ ]

rows.original: You tell Kinu that she should try to work out the problem by herself, even if it takes her the rest of the day. "That's what I've been doing since morning, [kinu.Dad]. Is it even going to help?" [pc.bg noblescion arcanist scholar| Yes, it is going to help. You've looked through her working, followed her thought processes, and you've figured out exactly where she went wrong in the geometry involved. Being able to backtrack and uncover one's mistakes is an important skill, one that she needs to cultivate before she grows up. Her mother won't be giving her lessons for the rest of her life; autodidactry is vital to her future going forward. "And that means struggling with this stupid problem for the rest of the day." Yes. Kinu looks from you to the workbook, then to the charcoal in her hand, then back to you again. Ears folding down against her head, your daughter heaves an impressively loud sigh for someone of her petite stature. "All right, all right, [kinu.Dad]. I'll take your word for it. This thing had better not be unsolvable..." You could give her the answer, but that would defeat the point of the exercise. She'd learn nothing, and then her time would be truly wasted. | She won't like your answer, but yes, it's going to help. Being able to think back on one's actions, identify mistakes, and most of all, admit their existence so they can be fixed, is an important skill to have, perhaps the most important one she'll ever learn. Gods, it might even be the foundation of education itself, or at least, that which stretches beyond mere book learning. She's got to tackle this by herself — it'll only make her stronger in the long run. Kinu looks at the workbook in her lap, up at you, then back at the workbook. "Is that just adult talk for 'I can't solve this problem', [kinu.Dad]?" She's right, you can't solve the problem, you were never trained in... more complex mathematics, so you're even less capable than her at eventually figuring out this headscratcher. But that doesn't diminish the truth of what you just said. "Eeeeh." Kinu's ears flatten against her head, and she scowls back down at the workbook in her lap. "Maybe I'll go ask Mama after you've visited and cheered her up..." She could ask for her mother's guidance, you suppose. The problem with that is, she's going to grow up someday — what's she going to do, come running back to Kiyoko every time something crops up? No, she's got to learn to figure things out for herself — best it be a math problem rather than something more dire. ] Kinu doesn't seem to like your answer at all, her lips set into a childish pout, but she nods reluctantly and turns back to her workbook, gaze burning as if she intends to force the answer from the paper through sheer willpower alone. You give your kitsune daughter a final pat between the ears — breaking her concentration yet again — and let her know in no uncertain terms that you have utmost confidence that she'll figure it out. "I wish I had that kind of confidence..." Well, it only comes with not just achieving success, but knowing that one actually deserves that success instead of being handed it. If she'd like to be more confident, that she needs to hit that book of hers and actually solve that problem instead of putting it off. "Boo..."
rows.translation: 你告诉绮奴，她应该试着自己解决这个问题，即使这会耗费她一整天的时间。 从早上开始，我一直在做这件事。 [kinu.Dad]这真的会有帮助吗？ [pc.bg noblescion arcanist scholar| 是的，可以。 是 这会对她有所帮助的。你仔细研究了她的解题过程，跟随她的思维轨迹，从而准确地找出了她在几何问题中出错的地方。能够回溯自己的思路并发现自己的错误，是一项非常重要的能力——这是她在未来成长过程中必须掌握的技能。她的母亲不可能一辈子都给她辅导功课；自学能力对她未来的发展来说至关重要。 这意味着接下来一整天都得为这个愚蠢的问题而烦恼。 是的。” 金努将目光从你身上移到工作簿上，又看向手中的木炭，最后再次回到你的身上。她把耳朵贴在脑袋旁，对于这样一个身材娇小的人来说，她的叹息声实在显得格外响亮。 好吧，好吧， [kinu.Dad]我相信你的话。这件事最好真的有解决办法…… 你 可以 告诉她答案的话，那就违背了这项练习的初衷了。她根本什么也学不到，而且这样也会浪费她的时间。 确实如此 白白浪费了。 | 她可能不会喜欢你的回答，但没错，这确实会有帮助。能够回顾自己的行为、认识到错误，尤其是能够承认这些错误的存在以便加以改正，这是一项非常重要的能力——或许也是她将会学到的最重要的能力。 天啊，这甚至可能是教育的根本所在，或者至少是超越了单纯书本学习的范畴。她必须自己解决这个问题——从长远来看，这只会让她变得更强大。 金看着膝上的练习册，先看着你，然后又把目光转回到练习册上。 那其实就是成年人用来表达‘我解决不了这个问题’的说法罢了。 [kinu.Dad]?" 她说得对，你根本解决不了这个问题——你从来就没有接受过关于更复杂数学知识的训练，所以比起她来，你更没有能力弄清楚这个让人头疼的难题。不过，这并不会改变你刚才所说的话所蕴含的真相。 呃…… 绮奴的耳朵贴在脑袋上，她皱着眉头重新低头看着腿上的练习册。 也许等你们去探望她、让她高兴起来之后，我再去问问妈妈吧…… 她 可以 你大概是想让她向母亲寻求指导吧。但问题在于，她总有一天会长大独立的——到时候，每次遇到问题就跑回清子身边吗？不，她必须学会自己解决问题，最好是从解决数学问题开始，这样总比遇到更严重的问题要好。 ] 纪久似乎一点也不喜欢你的答案，她的嘴唇微微撅起，露出孩子气般的表情，但最终还是不情愿地点了点头，然后又继续翻阅她的练习册，目光中充满了决心，仿佛只要凭借足够的意志力，就能从纸面上找出正确的答案。你最后轻轻拍了拍你那只狐妖女儿的耳朵——又一次打断了她的注意力——然后明确地告诉她，你非常相信她一定能够解决这个问题。 我真希望自己也有那样的自信…… 嗯，成功带来的不仅仅是成就感，更重要的是让人明白自己确实是值得获得那些成功的，而不是这些成功是别人赐予的。如果她想变得更加自信，那就必须认真钻研那些书籍，真正解决那些问题，而不是把它们一直拖下去。 嘘……

Is it even going to help?" [pc.bg noblescion arcanist scholar| Yes, it is going to help. You've looked through her working, followed her thought processes, and you've figured out exactly where she went wrong in the geometry involved. Being able to backtrack and uncover one's mistakes is an important skill, one that she needs to cultivate before she grows up. Her mother won't be giving her lessons for the rest of her life; autodidactry is vital to her future going forward. "And that means struggling with this stupid problem for the rest of the day." Yes. This thing had better not be unsolvable..." You could give her the answer, but that would defeat the point of the exercise. She'd learn nothing, and then her time would be truly wasted. | She won't like your answer, but yes, it's going to help. rows.original: Perhaps she could ask her mother for help? "I don't think that's going to work very well, [kinu.Dad]. If Mama's in one of her moods again and she gave me these problems to get me out of her hair, then going back to her probably isn't going to do much good." Oh, but Kiyoko's bound to cheer right up once you visit, you're sure of that. Once you've left, her mother is sure to be in a far more amenable mood. Kinu looks a little unsure at that, reaching up with a thumb to bite her nail; you gently slap her hand away, and she lowers it with a clearly shameful look on her face. Nervous or not, no kitsune daughter of your is going to cultivate such bad habits. But back to the point — there shouldn't be any shame in asking others for help, if there's ample cause. She's clearly been racking her brains over this particular problem for some time now — there's tenacity, and then there's being too proud to admit defeat. "I-I'm not too proud to know when I'm beaten!" Then why is she still here instead of trying another approach to the problem? "I just said that Mama was in one of her moods —" And you just said you'd take care of the problem for her. You may not be a diviner like Kiyoko is, but somehow you get the feeling she'll be a lot more amenable after you're through with her. So... what's the problem? Silence. You take a seat on the tree root, Kinu at your feet, and slowly close the workbook. Kinu looks a little pensive at that, staring down at her charcoal-stained hands, but no matter how tense the silence becomes, your daughter refuses to break it. Now then. There's no need to go about re-inventing the wheel; the whole point of civilization is that people build up upon the successes of those who came before them. Sure, there's being needy and bothersome, and then there're legitimate requests for help. So just ask. What's the worst that could happen? Kiyoko's her mother — if she's not going to answer, who would? "I... I just feel like I should be able to do this by myself." Is she really that committed to autodidactry, or is she just ashamed and desiring to keep up her image as the smart one? Can't have the smart one admitting she can't figure things out, can she? Kinu winces as if you'd struck her. "I... now you've put me in a mood, [kinu.Dad]..." So your guess was right. When you're done visiting Kiyoko, you want her to go find her mother and ask for help on her lesson. All it'll take is swallowing her pride. You kitsune daughter doesn't say anything, simply picking up workbook, charcoal and bowl before stomping away. She's so much like her mother in several respects... like when they get mad. Still, you hope she'll take your rather blunt advice to heart.
rows.translation: 或许她可以向母亲寻求帮助？ 我觉得那样做效果不会很好。 [kinu.Dad]如果妈妈又进入了她那种坏脾气状态，然后给我布置这些任务只是为了让我别去烦她，那么回去找她大概也不会有什么好处。 哦，不过你可以肯定，只要你去拜访基代子，她一定会立刻高兴起来的。而等你离开后，她妈妈的情绪肯定也会变得好很多。 然而，纪奈看起来有些犹豫，她抬起手部用拇指咬着自己的指甲；你轻轻拍了拍她的手部，她立刻把手部放了下来，脸上露出明显的尴尬表情。 不管你是不是紧张，你的那个九尾狐女儿绝对不应该养成这种坏习惯。不过，归根结底，如果有充分的理由，向别人求助根本没有什么可羞愧的。很明显，她已经为这个难题绞尽脑汁好一段时间了——她既有坚持的精神，又过于骄傲，不肯承认失败。 我……我并不介意承认自己被打败了！ 那么，她为什么还留在这里，而不是尝试其他解决方法来处理这个问题呢？ 我只是说妈妈当时正处于她那种情绪状态中…… 你刚才还说会帮她解决这个问题。你可能没有清子那样的预知能力，但不知为何，你感觉在你处理完这件事之后，她应该会变得容易相处多了。那么……到底是什么问题呢？ 沉默。 你坐在树根旁，让绮奴坐在你足部边，然后缓缓合上工作簿。此时，绮奴显得有些若有所思，她低头凝视着自己那些被炭笔染黑的手部掌，但无论这种沉默变得多么紧张，你的女儿始终拒绝打破它。 那么，其实没有必要重复前人已经做过的事情；文明的本质就在于人们能够在前人取得的成就基础上继续前进。当然，也会有一些人表现得过分依赖他人、惹人烦扰，但也会有一些人确实是需要帮助的。 所以，尽管问吧。最坏的结果又能怎样呢？清子毕竟是她的母亲——如果她都不愿意回答，还有谁会愿意呢？ 我……我只是觉得这件事应该能够自己完成。 她真的是那么热衷于自学吗？还是只是因为羞于承认自己不懂某些事情，所以才想维护自己“聪明人”的形象呢？毕竟，一个聪明人是不应该承认自己搞不懂某些问题的，对吧？ 金努吓得缩了一下身子，就好像你打了她一样。 我……现在你把事情搞得这么复杂了 我 有心情的时候。 [kinu.Dad]..." 那么，你的猜测是 是 没错。当你陪清子玩完之后，你就希望她能去找她的母亲，向母亲寻求帮助来完成她的功课。其实，她只需要放下自己的骄傲罢了。 你的这个狐妖女儿什么也没说，只是拿起了练习本、炭笔和砚台，然后就气呼呼地走了。在很多方面，她真的和她母亲很像……比如当她们生气的时候。不过，你还是希望她能认真考虑你这个直率的建议。

rows.original: Well, if she isn't able to solve the problem herself and she doesn't want to ask her mother, why don't you help her with the problem instead? Kinu's eyes widen, and her ears perk up. "You, [kinu.Dad]?" Why not? You've already looked over her working, and you know where the problem lies. She can walk you through her reasoning, and while you won't give her the answer outright, you can definitely guide her in the right direction. "Well... I guess there's nothing to lose at this point. All right!" Excellent. You prop up Kinu's workbook on the tree root and begin, asking her to explain her approach to figuring out the geometry involved and solving the problem. Your kitsune daughter complies as best as she's able, picking up the dessert bowl in her black-smudged hands and licking up what's left in the bottom. [pc.bg noblescion|This brings back memories... you might have been the spare and not the heir to your house, but even so, you had the benefit of private tutors, faithfully hired by your parents to oversee your education. The dusty old men and wrinkled old women who trundles through the halls of your house to impart what they had to teach — some of the lessons were interesting, others less so. Today, you're finding the positions reversed here... and perhaps you're beginning to understand what all those learned tutors must have thought of you.][pc.bg arcanist|Geometry, huh... seems like Kiyoko has high hopes for your daughter, then. Any idiot can fix a gem onto one end of a stick, but the dazzling arrays used in the complex rituals of the old Belharan mages had to be perfect in their exaction. Even one citrine out of place could easily spoil the spell... though you'd almost certainly never have enough gems on hand for a multilayered spell foci, let alone actually create one, you still studied the theory with a ravenous dedication. How odd that today, the most important practical use you'd get out of those hours of study would be to pass that knowledge along to your daughter.][pc.bg scholar|In your days as a scholar, occasionally your colleagues would receive requests from the local noble houses to go tutor their children. While you never personally had the chance to do so, the complaints about the local youth that your seniors often expressed in the safety of the lyceum were scathing, to say the least. Odd that sitting here with Kinu and guiding her through all this, you don't feel stressed in the least bit. Maybe it's because she's talented... or maybe it's because she's your daughter.] "See, [kinu.Dad], I joined those two points on the circle to form a triangle, and from there —" Perhaps she should slow down there and think about that last step, the one before this one. Kinu picks up the workbook and turns it over in her hands. "I've no doubt there's nothing wrong with that one, [kinu.Dad]. I don't need to go over what I'm certain is right." Still, you'd urge her to take another look. "I..." Kinu turns the workbook upside-down, then blinks. "Oh. Oh." Yes. Oh. "This is so embarrassing..." She may be smart, but that doesn't preclude her from being careless. Overconfidence is a slow and insidious killer. Now if she looks there - "Where I carried the error forward —" Yes. "..." Oh, and she gets no credit for error carried forward. Were this to be a practical matter, the results might very well be catastrophic. Kinu doesn't say anything, instead chewing on her lip as she studies her working. She wrinkles her nose, twitches her ears, then strikes out with the charcoal and pens down the correct answer to the problem. All too easy — or at least, she makes it look that way. "And that solves that. Thank you, [kinu.Dad]. I think I learned an important lesson today." Your kitsune daughter shuts her workbook with a final-sounding thump, then clambers up onto the tree root to curl up with her three fluffy tails. "I think I'm going to stay here awhile. The sun is very warm today." She's not heading back in? "After you, [kinu.Dad]." Oh, right. There's the issue of her mother to be settled. "You go ahead and cheer her up, and I'll sneak back in when Mama's in a better mood. For now, though, I feel like I need a nap. Don't mind me, [kinu.Dad]."
rows.translation: 嗯，如果她自己无法解决这个问题，又不想向妈妈求助，那为什么不 你 为什么不帮她解决这个问题呢？ 绮奴的眼睛瞪得大大的，耳朵也竖了起来。 你， [kinu.Dad]?" 为什么不呢？你已经看过她的工作成果了，也知道问题出在哪里。她可以向你解释她的思考过程，虽然你不会直接告诉她答案，但肯定可以给她指明正确的方向。 嗯……我想现在也没什么可失去的了。好吧！ 太好了。你把绮奴的工作簿放在树根上，然后开始让她解释自己是如何理解其中涉及的几何知识并解决这个问题的。你的狐妖女儿尽她最大的努力来回答你的问题，她用那些被黑色污迹弄脏的手部拿起甜点碗，把碗底剩下的东西都舔干净了。 [pc.bg noblescion|这唤起了许多回忆……你或许并不是家中的继承人，而只是个备选者，但即便如此，你的父母还是专门聘请了私人教师来指导你的学习。那些年迈的男教师和女教师，他们拖着疲惫的身体在宅邸的走廊里来回穿梭，传授他们所掌握的知识——有些课程确实很有意思，而有些则不尽如人意。 今天，你会发现这里的职位顺序被颠倒了……或许你开始明白那些受过专业训练的导师们当时一定是怎么看待你的了。][pc.bg arcanist|几何结构，啊……看来清子对你的女儿寄予了很高的期望。任何傻瓜都能把宝石固定在棍子的一端，但那些被用于贝尔哈兰老法师们复杂仪式中的璀璨图案，其制作精度必须达到极致才行。 哪怕只有一颗位置摆放不当的黄水晶，都很容易破坏这个法术的效果……虽然你几乎肯定永远没有足够的宝石来制作多层结构的法术核心，更不用说真正完成这个法术了，但你仍然以极其专注的态度研究着相关的理论。 真是奇怪，如今，你花费那些时间学习所获得的最重要的实际意义，竟然只是将这些知识传授给你的女儿。][pc.bg scholar|在你作为学者的那些日子里，偶尔你的同事们会收到当地贵族家庭的邀请，去为他们的女儿们辅导功课。虽然你自己从未有机会这样做，但你的前辈们经常在学院里抱怨当地那些年轻人的状况，用词之严厉，简直可以说是刻薄至极。奇怪的是，现在和绮奴坐在一起，指导她学习这些知识，你却丝毫没有感到压力。也许是因为她很有天赋……又或许是因为她是你的女儿。] 看， [kinu.Dad]我在圆上将那两点连接起来，从而形成了一个三角形，然后从那里开始…… 或许她应该放慢脚步，仔细思考那最后一步——也就是在这一步之前的那一步。 纪奈拿起练习册，在手部中翻来翻去。 我毫不怀疑那个东西没有任何问题。 [kinu.Dad]那些我确信是正确的事情，自然就不需要再重复说明了。 不过，你还是会劝她再看一遍。 我…… 绮奴把练习本翻了个个儿，然后眨了眨眼。 哦。 哦。" 是的。哦。 这太尴尬了…… 她可能很聪明，但这并不意味着她就不会犯粗心大意的错误。过度自信其实是一种缓慢而隐秘的“杀手部”。现在，如果她看向那里的话 就在那里，我继续将这个错误延续下去…… 是的。 "..." 哦，而且她因为之前的错误而没有得到任何惩罚。如果这种情况在现实中发生，后果可能会非常严重。 绮奴什么也没说，只是咬着嘴唇仔细思考着题目。她皱了皱鼻子，动了一下耳朵，然后拿起炭笔在纸上写下了这个问题的正确答案。这对她来说太容易了——至少她自己是这么认为的。 看 就这样吧。 这样就解决了问题。谢谢。 [kinu.Dad]我想，今天我学到了一堂非常重要的课。 你的九尾狐女儿“砰”的一声关上了她的练习本，然后爬到树根上，蜷缩起来，三条蓬松的尾巴也跟着盘了起来。 我想我会在这里待上一会儿，今天的阳光真的很温暖。 她不打算回去了吗？ 你先来吧。 [kinu.Dad]." 哦，对了，还有她母亲的问题需要解决。 你去安慰她吧，等妈妈心情好一些的时候，我再悄悄溜进去。不过现在，我有点想小睡一会儿。别介意我 [kinu.Dad]."
rows.raw: " Well, if she isn't able to solve the problem herself and she doesn't want to ask her mother, why don't you help her with the problem instead? Kinu's eyes widen, and her ears perk up. "You, [kinu.Dad]?" Why not? You've already looked over her working, and you know where the problem lies. She can walk you through her reasoning, and while you won't give her the answer outright, you can definitely guide her in the right direction. "Well... I guess there's nothing to lose at this point. All right!" Excellent. You prop up Kinu's workbook on the tree root and begin, asking her to explain her approach to figuring out the geometry involved and solving the problem. Your kitsune daughter complies as best as she's able, picking up the dessert bowl in her black-smudged hands and licking up what's left in the bottom. [pc.bg noblescion|This brings back memories... you might have been the spare and not the heir to your house, but even so, you had the benefit of private tutors, faithfully hired by your parents to oversee your education. The dusty old men and wrinkled old women who trundles through the halls of your house to impart what they had to teach — some of the lessons were interesting, others less so. Today, you're finding the positions reversed here... and perhaps you're beginning to understand what all those learned tutors must have thought of you.][pc.bg arcanist|Geometry, huh... seems like Kiyoko has high hopes for your daughter, then. Any idiot can fix a gem onto one end of a stick, but the dazzling arrays used in the complex rituals of the old Belharan mages had to be perfect in their exaction. Even one citrine out of place could easily spoil the spell... though you'd almost certainly never have enough gems on hand for a multilayered spell foci, let alone actually create one, you still studied the theory with a ravenous dedication. How odd that today, the most important practical use you'd get out of those hours of study would be to pass that knowledge along to your daughter.][pc.bg scholar|In your days as a scholar, occasionally your colleagues would receive requests from the local noble houses to go tutor their children. While you never personally had the chance to do so, the complaints about the local youth that your seniors often expressed in the safety of the lyceum were scathing, to say the least. Odd that sitting here with Kinu and guiding her through all this, you don't feel stressed in the least bit. Maybe it's because she's talented... or maybe it's because she's your daughter.] "See, [kinu.Dad], I joined those two points on the circle to form a triangle, and from there —" Perhaps she should slow down there and think about that last step, the one before this one. Kinu picks up the workbook and turns it over in her hands. "I've no doubt there's nothing wrong with that one, [kinu.Dad]. I don't need to go over what I'm certain is right." Still, you'd urge her to take another look. "I..." Kinu turns the workbook upside-down, then blinks. "Oh. Oh." Yes. Oh. "This is so embarrassing..." She may be smart, but that doesn't preclude her from being careless. Overconfidence is a slow and insidious killer. Now if she looks there - "Where I carried the error forward —" Yes. "..." Oh, and she gets no credit for error carried forward. Were this to be a practical matter, the results might very well be catastrophic. Kinu doesn't say anything, instead chewing on her lip as she studies her working. She wrinkles her nose, twitches her ears, then strikes out with the charcoal and pens down the correct answer to the problem. All too easy — or at least, she makes it look that way. "And that solves that. Thank you, [kinu.Dad]. I think I learned an important lesson today." Your kitsune daughter shuts her workbook with a final-sounding thump, then clambers up onto the tree root to curl up with her three fluffy tails. "I think I'm going to stay here awhile. The sun is very warm today." She's not heading back in? "After you, [kinu.Dad]." Oh, right. There's the issue of her mother to be settled. "You go ahead and cheer her up, and I'll sneak back in when Mama's in a better mood. For now, though, I feel like I need a nap. Don't mind me, [kinu.Dad].""

rows.original: You don't have the educational background to make sense of this math problem...
rows.translation: 你的教育背景显然不足以理解这道数学题……
rows.raw: "You don't have the educational background to make sense of this math problem..."

rows.original: You look to the humongous pile of round moon cakes, down at Kinu, then back to the cakes. Hopefully she's taken what you've just tried to impress upon her to heart; she shouldn't let her status as a future den mother get to her head. "Ehe. Don't worry about that, [kinu.Dad] — I'll remember what you said today." Promise? "Promise." That's your girl. You give Kinu one last pat on the head, which elicits a happy squeal from your kitsune daughter, and chuckle. "Oh! One more thing, though..." Yes? "For all this to pass, you have to get everyone out of here first, don't you?" Well. Yes. You're working on that... unfortunately, her mother's memories are likely to be outdated and of little use in this regard, so you're left with precious few leads. For her sake, though, and that of everyone here... you'll rescue her mother. "Okay, okay!" Kinu wags her tails again, and looks up at the huge pile of moon cakes. "I just want... I just want someone to walk with during the moon-viewing festival when the time comes, you know?" Of course. A little girl dreaming of romance. "I think I'm going to take a nap now. I'm going to be allowed to stay up late tonight, and I don't want to waste any moment of it." With how excited she is, is she sure she's going to be able to sleep? Kinu sticks her tongue out at you. "Don't underestimate me, [kinu.Dad]. I'm a pro napper, I can sleep anywhere I want. Just watch me. And..." Yes? "Have fun playing with Mama." Winking at you, Kinu turns tail and scampers off before you can demand an explanation for that last line. Although given that she has been getting into her mother's reading... maybe you should bring it up with Kiyoko when you see her.
rows.translation: 你望着那一大堆圆润的月饼，低头看了看绮奴，然后又把目光转回到那些月饼上。希望她能够把你刚才试图让她明白的事情牢记在心；她不应该因为自己将来会成为群体的领导者而变得自高自大。 呵呵，别担心那个， [kinu.Dad] 我会记住你今天说的话的。 承诺？ 我保证。 那就是你的女儿了。你最后轻轻拍了拍绮奴的脑袋，她立刻开心地尖叫起来，你也跟着笑了起来。 哦！不过还有一件事…… 嗯？ 要想让这一切发生，首先你必须把所有人都从这里弄出去，对吧？ 嗯，是的，你正在处理这件事……可惜，她母亲的记忆可能已经过时了，在这方面几乎没什么用处，所以你能获得的线索非常有限。不过，为了她，也为了在场的每一个人……你必须救出她的母亲。 好吧，好吧！ 金子又一次摇起了尾巴，抬头望向那堆巨大的月饼。 我只是希望……只是希望在中秋节那天，有个人能陪在我身边，你知道吗？ 当然。一个梦想着浪漫的小女孩。 我想我现在要去小睡一会儿了。今晚我可以熬夜，所以我可不想浪费任何时间。 她这么兴奋，真的能睡着吗？ 绮奴对着你吐了吐舌头。 别小看我， [kinu.Dad]我可是个“睡神”，想在哪里睡觉就能在哪里睡觉。你们就看着吧……还有…… 嗯？ 和妈妈一起玩得开心吧。 金乌向你使了个眼色，然后在你还没来得及要求她解释最后一句话之前，就转身逃跑了。不过，考虑到她的性格 拥有 她最近开始读她母亲的书籍了……也许你应该在见到清子的时候跟她提一下这件事。

rows.original: As you come upon the hilltop, Kinu comes running up to you, her legs a blur as she barrels forward in your direction. To her credit, your foxy daughter tries to slow down when she realizes she's going to collide with you, but there's no way she's going to be able to stop in time. Indeed, your bodies meet with quite the forceful crash, and the both of you end up sprawled on the grass in a furry, fuzzy mess. "[kinu.Dad]! You're here! You're here!" Oww... so you are. Picking yourself off the soft earth, you reach out and pinch Kinu's cheeks, eliciting a giggle from your foxy daughter. All right, so what's the big occasion? Usually she lets you come up to her before starting with the enthusiastic greetings. "Well, um, I —" Kinu looks unsure of herself for a moment, then swallows her indecision and forges on. "I wanted to have you to myself for a bit before you went in to see Mama today. I... well, I just wanted you to see something, and to ask you something." And what's this question about, that she can't let her mother know about it? More hesitation. Color rises to Kinu's cheeks as she puts her fingers together and starts fidgeting, her soft white fox ears curling in upon themselves as she looks quite sheepish. "It's... it's kind of awkward, [kinu.Dad]. It'll make sense when I ask it, okay?" You can see as much; it's written all over her face. All right, then — lead the way. Kinu does so with great gusto, taking you by the hand and dragging you around the side of the hill. By the time you reach another set of benches, you see the table that's been set out: elaborately carved wood, a beautifully embroidered tablecloth, and a large plate piled high with white, ball-shaped pastries. Arranged in a neat pyramid, the pastries practically gleam in the sunlight, and even from this far away you can still smell a faint sweet aroma that rises from the spread. "We're having the moon-viewing festival tonight, [kinu.Dad]. I know you usually can't stay until when Mama makes it night, so I wanted you to see this. Mama and I spent the better part of yesterday making all these cakes. Then, when Mama makes it night, we're going to sit out here on the benches and admire the splendour of the full moon... or at least, how Mama remembers it. "I know it's not the real thing... but Mama says it's important to keep these practices alive, and that I'll be able to better understand why when I grow older. That, and I'm not allowed to touch the cakes until afterwards..." [kiyoko.numKits 2 16 32| That's great. She won't fight with her siblings over the cakes when it's time to eat them, will she? "Please, [kinu.Dad]. Squabbling over food is so childish. Do you honestly think I'd stoop to something like that?" Yes. Kinu's face colors, and she winces, looking very guilty. "Well... fine. I promise not to fight over the cakes, [kinu.Dad]." There's a good girl. | Looks like there's plenty to go around — she must be tired from helping her mother all day yesterday. Kinu preens. "Oh, that was nothing. The real challenge's going to be in getting everyone to sit still and be quiet while appreciating the moon's natural beauty. I just hope I don't have to raise my voice too much." Her mother really is preparing her daughter to follow in her footsteps, isn't she? "It's only natural, [kinu.Dad]. Besides, given how much fun she has, being like Mama isn't going to be that much worse than what I'm already doing, can it?" | It's good that she made so much — with so many mouths to feed, you're not sure there're going to be enough cakes for all her brothers and sisters. "There's going to be enough," Kinu says confidently, folding her arms over her little chest. "I know, because I counted. Everyone gets one, except for Mama and I, who get two." You can understand her mother, but why does she get more? "Because I earned it, [kinu.Dad]. Have you any idea how sore your wrists get when you roll dough all day? By the time I was done, I was minded to eat all of them by myself, even if I knew I'd get sick from that." | That's a lot of cakes there. Is she and her mother going to be able to finish them all before they go bad? "Ehe. Probably not, but it won't be for lack of trying." Kinu looks up at you and flutters her eyes oh-so-innocently. "Don't give me that stern face, [kinu.Dad]. I earned them!" By making them? Your foxy daughter nods so fast, her head's a blur. "You have no idea how badly your wrists can ache after the fiftieth moon cake you've rolled together, [kinu.Dad]. I think I deserve as much, even if I'm thoroughly sick afterwards. Besides, I'm not going to eat more than Mama is going to." Using her mother as cover isn't doing her any favors, she knows that, right? "Ehe..." ] Right. So, about this question she wanted to ask you... "Um, so, the moon-viewing festival isn't just about appreciating natural beauty, it's about... um, well..." Come on, she can spit it out now. "It's about, um, when people who like each other go out once a year under the moonlight and take walks, and um, uh, do other things like what I read in the novels Mama sometimes has lying around — "— Look, all I want to ask is how you and Mama met, okay? That's all!" And that's the question she wanted to get you to herself for? "Yes! Because it'd be really awkward for the both of you if I asked you while she was around, and then the both of you would clam up and I'd get nothing! There! I asked it!" Pouting, Kinu stomps her little foot on the grassy ground and folds her arms, as if daring you to make fun of her. Admittedly, it's sorely tempting, but you decide to humor your foxy daughter and lead her by the hand to one of the benches. Well, it's time for her to get comfortable, because it's going to be a very long story... Kinu takes a seat beside you, legs dangling off the ground, and listens as you recount the tale in full, all the way from when you discovered the broken-down shrine in the Old Forest and the sealed cave in the rear. Gods, has it really been that long? It doesn't feel like it... in fact, with how well it sticks out in your memory, it could've been just yesterday that Kiyoko first appeared in your dreams. Her mother asking you for help in escaping her prison, asking for the very essence of your life, and you giving it to her... her announcing that she's carrying your kit in her womb, Kinu's birth... Your foxy daughter listens in rapt fascination, starry-eyed and breathing hard while you take her for a walk through your memories. When you finally conclude the tale, she practically squeals in excitement, bouncing up and down in her seat while her three tails swish wildly behind her. "I knew it! I knew it! It's just like in those novels Mama had lying around! [kinu.Dad], all that's left is for you to free Mama from the Astral Plane, and it'll be the perfect story! I know it'll be!" She pauses a moment to catch her breath before she passes out. "I... I want to have someone like that when I grow up and get to have a consort! To sweep me off my feet like you did to Mama!" Seems like Kinu getting into her mother's romance novels has put ideas into your daughter's head, and she seems fairly enamored of them. Sure, it might be an idealised form of love, but ideals exist for a reason — as a goal to work towards, even if they can't be reasonably achieved. All this being said... is this something that you want to encourage in Kinu?
rows.translation: 当你登上山顶时，金努飞快地朝你跑来，她的双腿在奔跑中快速移动，几乎看不清轮廓。值得称赞的是，当你的女儿意识到自己即将撞上你时，她确实试图减速，但显然已经来不及阻止碰撞了。果然，你们两个猛地相撞，一起倒在草地上，形成了一团毛茸茸的混乱景象。 "[kinu.Dad]你来了！你终于来了！ 哎哟……原来是这样。你从柔软的泥土中爬起来，伸手捏了捏绮奴的脸颊，惹得你那个调皮的女儿咯咯笑了起来。好吧，那么到底发生了什么大事呢？通常情况下，她都会先热情地跟你打招呼，才会让你靠近她啊。 嗯，我—— 基努有那么一刻显得有些犹豫不决，但最终她克服了这种犹豫，继续前进了。 在你们今天去见妈妈之前，我想单独和你待一会儿。我……其实，我只是想让你看一些东西，然后问你一些问题。 那么，这个问题到底是关于什么的呢？为什么她不能让妈妈知道这件事呢？ 她再次犹豫起来。金子的脸颊渐渐泛红，她把手指交叉在一起，开始坐立不安，那对柔软的白色狐狸耳朵也紧紧地贴在脸上，看起来显得非常害羞。 这……有点尴尬吧， [kinu.Dad]等我问清楚了，你就会明白的，好吗？ 你一看就明白了，这一切都写在她的脸上。好吧，那你就带路吧。 绮奴兴致勃勃地牵着你的手，带你绕过山坡。当你来到另一组长椅旁时，你看到了已经摆好的桌子：精美的木雕、漂亮刺绣的桌布，还有满满一盘白色球形点心。 这些糕点被整齐地堆成金字塔状，在阳光下闪闪发光；即使从这么远的距离，你仍然能闻到从这些糕点散发出来的淡淡甜香。 今晚我们要举行赏月节活动， [kinu.Dad]我知道你通常无法等到妈妈说“天黑了”的时候才离开，所以我想让你看看这个。昨天，妈妈和我花了大半天的时间制作了这些蛋糕。等到妈妈说“天黑了”，我们就坐在这里的长椅上，欣赏满月的美丽……至少，是妈妈记忆中的那种景象。 我知道那并不是 真实的 嗯……但是妈妈说，保持这些传统很重要，等我长大了，就能更好地理解其中的原因了。另外，还规定在仪式结束之前，我是不允许碰那些蛋糕的…… [kiyoko.numKits 2 16 32| 太好了。到时候吃蛋糕的时候，她就不会和兄弟姐妹们抢了吧？ 拜托了， [kinu.Dad]为食物争吵真是 所以 太幼稚了。你真以为我会做出那种事吗？ 是的。 纪奈的脸颊顿时变红了，她皱起了眉头，看起来显得非常内疚。 嗯……好吧。我保证不会为了那些蛋糕而争吵。 [kinu.Dad]." 有个好女孩。 | 看起来还有很多事情要做呢——她昨天一整天都在帮助母亲，肯定累坏了。 绮奴正在整理自己的羽毛。 哦，那没什么的。真的。 真实的 最大的挑战在于让所有人都能安静地坐着，欣赏月亮的自然之美。我只希望自己不必太大声地说话。 她的母亲确实是在为女儿铺路，让她能够走自己的道路，不是吗？ 这是很自然的。 [kinu.Dad]而且，考虑到她现在玩得这么开心，扮演妈妈应该也不会比我现在做的更糟糕吧？ | 她能做出这么多东西真是太好了——家里有那么多人要吃饭，真不知道她做的蛋糕是否够分给所有的兄弟姐妹们。 应该够用了。 纪奈自信地说道，双臂交叉在胸前。 我知道，因为我已经数过了。每个人都能得到一个，除了妈妈和我，我们能得到两个。 你能理解她母亲的做法，但为什么 她 想要更多吗？ 因为我想 获得的 它。 [kinu.Dad]你知道吗，整天揉面团会让手腕变得多么酸痛吗？当我忙完这些活儿后，我甚至想把那些面团都吃掉，尽管我知道那样会让自己生病。 | 那些蛋糕可真不少啊。她和她的妈妈能在它们变质之前全部吃完吗？ 呵呵，大概不会吧，但至少我会尽力尝试的。 纪久仰望着你，用那双纯真无邪的眼睛眨了眨眼。 别摆出那种严肃的表情来， [kinu.Dad]这些都是我靠自己的努力赚来的！ 是通过让她们这么做吗？ 你那个狡黠的女儿连连点头，她的头都快转晕了。 你拥有 不行。 你能想象，在包了第五十个月饼之后，你的手腕会有多疼吧？ [kinu.Dad]我觉得我理应得到这些，即使之后会感到非常难受。再说，我也不会吃得比妈妈还多。 她利用母亲作为掩护，其实并没有帮到自己什么，她心里明白这一点，对吧？ 呵呵…… ] 好的。那么，关于她想问你的这个问题…… 嗯，其实，赏月节并不仅仅是为了欣赏大自然的美景，它还意味着……嗯，总之…… 快吧，她现在可以把话都说出来了。 就是那种，嗯，彼此喜欢的人每年会在月光下一起出去散步，还会做一些我在妈妈有时会放在家里的小说里读到的那些事情…… ——听着，我只想知道你和妈妈是怎么认识的，好吗？ 就这样吧！" 这就是她想让你亲自告诉她的那个问题吧？ "好的！ 因为如果她在场的时候我问你，你们俩都会变得很尴尬，然后就会都不说话了，我也就什么也问不出来！好了，我终于问出来了！ 金努撅着嘴，把小足部踩在草地上，双臂交叉抱在胸前，似乎在挑衅你去取笑她。诚然，这种样子实在让人忍不住想笑，但你还是决定迁就你这个调皮的女儿，牵着她的手走向其中一张长椅。 嗯，现在是时候让她放松下来听故事了，因为这个故事会很长…… 纪奈坐在你旁边，双腿悬在半空，听你从头到尾讲述这个故事——从你发现旧森林里那座破败的神社，到后面那个被封住的洞穴，一切都被你详细地讲了出来。 天啊，真的已经过去这么久了吗？感觉并不像……事实上，既然这件事在你的记忆中如此清晰，那么或许纪代子第一次出现在你的梦中，其实就发生在昨天而已。她的母亲向你求助，请求你帮助她逃离监狱，请求你给予她你生命中最珍贵的东西，而你也就这么做了。……当她宣布自己正在怀中孕育着你的后代，当绮奴诞生之时…… 你那聪明伶俐的女儿全神贯注地聆听着这个故事，双眼充满惊奇，呼吸也变得急促起来。当你带着她一起回顾那些回忆时，当故事终于结束时，她兴奋得几乎尖叫起来，在座位上上下跳动，她那三条尾巴也在她身后剧烈地摆动着。 我就知道！我就知道！这跟妈妈家里那些小说里描述的一模一样！ [kinu.Dad]现在所剩下的，就是你要把妈妈从星界中解救出来，这样这个故事就会变得完美无缺了！我相信一定会这样的！ 她停顿了片刻，喘口气，然后才昏了过去。 我……等我长大后，也想要拥有这样一个伴侣！希望她能像你那样让我为之倾倒，让我的生活变得充满幸福！ 看来绮奴读了她母亲的言情小说后，这些故事影响了你女儿的想法，她似乎对这些故事非常着迷。当然，这种爱情观念可能是一种理想化的形式，但理想之所以存在，正是因为它们代表着我们可以追求的目标，即使这些目标可能难以真正实现。不过，话又说回来……你真的希望绮奴继续保持这种想法吗？
rows.raw: " As you come upon the hilltop, Kinu comes running up to you, her legs a blur as she barrels forward in your direction. To her credit, your foxy daughter tries to slow down when she realizes she's going to collide with you, but there's no way she's going to be able to stop in time. Indeed, your bodies meet with quite the forceful crash, and the both of you end up sprawled on the grass in a furry, fuzzy mess. "[kinu.Dad]! You're here! You're here!" Oww... so you are. Picking yourself off the soft earth, you reach out and pinch Kinu's cheeks, eliciting a giggle from your foxy daughter. All right, so what's the big occasion? Usually she lets you come up to her before starting with the enthusiastic greetings. "Well, um, I —" Kinu looks unsure of herself for a moment, then swallows her indecision and forges on. "I wanted to have you to myself for a bit before you went in to see Mama today. I... well, I just wanted you to see something, and to ask you something." And what's this question about, that she can't let her mother know about it? More hesitation. Color rises to Kinu's cheeks as she puts her fingers together and starts fidgeting, her soft white fox ears curling in upon themselves as she looks quite sheepish. "It's... it's kind of awkward, [kinu.Dad]. It'll make sense when I ask it, okay?" You can see as much; it's written all over her face. All right, then — lead the way. Kinu does so with great gusto, taking you by the hand and dragging you around the side of the hill. By the time you reach another set of benches, you see the table that's been set out: elaborately carved wood, a beautifully embroidered tablecloth, and a large plate piled high with white, ball-shaped pastries. Arranged in a neat pyramid, the pastries practically gleam in the sunlight, and even from this far away you can still smell a faint sweet aroma that rises from the spread. "We're having the moon-viewing festival tonight, [kinu.Dad]. I know you usually can't stay until when Mama makes it night, so I wanted you to see this. Mama and I spent the better part of yesterday making all these cakes. Then, when Mama makes it night, we're going to sit out here on the benches and admire the splendour of the full moon... or at least, how Mama remembers it. "I know it's not the real thing... but Mama says it's important to keep these practices alive, and that I'll be able to better understand why when I grow older. That, and I'm not allowed to touch the cakes until afterwards..." [kiyoko.numKits 2 16 32| That's great. She won't fight with her siblings over the cakes when it's time to eat them, will she? "Please, [kinu.Dad]. Squabbling over food is so childish. Do you honestly think I'd stoop to something like that?" Yes. Kinu's face colors, and she winces, looking very guilty. "Well... fine. I promise not to fight over the cakes, [kinu.Dad]." There's a good girl. | Looks like there's plenty to go around — she must be tired from helping her mother all day yesterday. Kinu preens. "Oh, that was nothing. The real challenge's going to be in getting everyone to sit still and be quiet while appreciating the moon's natural beauty. I just hope I don't have to raise my voice too much." Her mother really is preparing her daughter to follow in her footsteps, isn't she? "It's only natural, [kinu.Dad]. Besides, given how much fun she has, being like Mama isn't going to be that much worse than what I'm already doing, can it?" | It's good that she made so much — with so many mouths to feed, you're not sure there're going to be enough cakes for all her brothers and sisters. "There's going to be enough," Kinu says confidently, folding her arms over her little chest. "I know, because I counted. Everyone gets one, except for Mama and I, who get two." You can understand her mother, but why does she get more? "Because I earned it, [kinu.Dad]. Have you any idea how sore your wrists get when you roll dough all day? By the time I was done, I was minded to eat all of them by myself, even if I knew I'd get sick from that." | That's a lot of cakes there. Is she and her mother going to be able to finish them all before they go bad? "Ehe. Probably not, but it won't be for lack of trying." Kinu looks up at you and flutters her eyes oh-so-innocently. "Don't give me that stern face, [kinu.Dad]. I earned them!" By making them? Your foxy daughter nods so fast, her head's a blur. "You have no idea how badly your wrists can ache after the fiftieth moon cake you've rolled together, [kinu.Dad]. I think I deserve as much, even if I'm thoroughly sick afterwards. Besides, I'm not going to eat more than Mama is going to." Using her mother as cover isn't doing her any favors, she knows that, right? "Ehe..." ] Right. So, about this question she wanted to ask you... "Um, so, the moon-viewing festival isn't just about appreciating natural beauty, it's about... um, well..." Come on, she can spit it out now. "It's about, um, when people who like each other go out once a year under the moonlight and take walks, and um, uh, do other things like what I read in the novels Mama sometimes has lying around — "— Look, all I want to ask is how you and Mama met, okay? That's all!" And that's the question she wanted to get you to herself for? "Yes! Because it'd be really awkward for the both of you if I asked you while she was around, and then the both of you would clam up and I'd get nothing! There! I asked it!" Pouting, Kinu stomps her little foot on the grassy ground and folds her arms, as if daring you to make fun of her. Admittedly, it's sorely tempting, but you decide to humor your foxy daughter and lead her by the hand to one of the benches. Well, it's time for her to get comfortable, because it's going to be a very long story... Kinu takes a seat beside you, legs dangling off the ground, and listens as you recount the tale in full, all the way from when you discovered the broken-down shrine in the Old Forest and the sealed cave in the rear. Gods, has it really been that long? It doesn't feel like it... in fact, with how well it sticks out in your memory, it could've been just yesterday that Kiyoko first appeared in your dreams. Her mother asking you for help in escaping her prison, asking for the very essence of your life, and you giving it to her... her announcing that she's carrying your kit in her womb, Kinu's birth... Your foxy daughter listens in rapt fascination, starry-eyed and breathing hard while you take her for a walk through your memories. When you finally conclude the tale, she practically squeals in excitement, bouncing up and down in her seat while her three tails swish wildly behind her. "I knew it! I knew it! It's just like in those novels Mama had lying around! [kinu.Dad], all that's left is for you to free Mama from the Astral Plane, and it'll be the perfect story! I know it'll be!" She pauses a moment to catch her breath before she passes out. "I... I want to have someone like that when I grow up and get to have a consort! To sweep me off my feet like you did to Mama!" Seems like Kinu getting into her mother's romance novels has put ideas into your daughter's head, and she seems fairly enamored of them. Sure, it might be an idealised form of love, but ideals exist for a reason — as a goal to work towards, even if they can't be reasonably achieved. All this being said... is this something that you want to encourage in Kinu?"

rows.original: You smile and give Kinu a pat on the head, turning your already bubbly kitsune daughter into an effervescent mess of energy. Yes, yes she should have someone like that. Someone suave and exciting to simply barge into her life, turn it upside-down, and quite literally carry her away. Sure, it doesn't happen often and she'll have to get rather lucky, but the truly fortunate create their own luck and besides, she already has a leg up on the competition. If anyone is going to have a fairy-tale romance, it ought to be your darling daughter. "Ehehehe. What do you mean though, [kinu.Dad]? That bit about me having a leg up on the competition?" Well, she wants to be a den mother just like Kiyoko when she comes of age, right? "That's right..." Now, you don't have any experience of larger kitsune society, but given what you understand from talking to her mother, she's going to be in quite high demand by virtue of who she is, if nothing else. Not that she won't have to work on her natural talents, but she won't have any shortage of suitors lining up to try and sweep her off her feet. Kinu's big blue eyes widen even further as she tries to process this, then her already big smile becomes positively stupid as her mind takes that particular fantasy and runs away with it, cartwheeling into the distance. You ruffle Kinu's hair and ears a bit longer, then give her a few light pats on the cheek. All right, all right, no need to get too carried away. "Do... do you mean it, [kinu.Dad]? That this sort of fairy-tale romance can happen outside of books?" It's not exactly common, but it's more than possible. Like you said, she's got a better chance than most, even if it won't just fall into her lap. She just has to look at what happened between you and her mother... what kind of coincidences had to happen, what kind of trust did the both of you have to place in each other for this particular chain of events to occur that eventually led to her birth? "I see where you're coming from, [kinu.Dad]. It's just..." your kitsune daughter's words trail off as her mind shifts into gear. "Hmm..." An ideal may be unattainable in its entirety — that's why they're called ideals, after all — but that says nothing of whether it's a good idea to work towards it or not. If she wants to have a life like one of her mother's romance novels, then she'd better make herself worthy of it. Following one's dreams was never easy, after all. "Okay, [kinu.Dad]. I think... I think I get it." Kinu takes a few deep breaths to try and calm herself down, an effort that's ultimately futile as she bursts out into a fresh giggling fit. "I'll do my best, okay?" There's a good girl.
rows.translation: 你微笑着拍了拍绮奴的脑袋，你那已经充满活力的九尾狐女儿立刻变得兴奋不已，活力四射。没错，她确实需要这样的人——一个风度翩翩、充满魅力的人，能够突然闯入她的生活，把一切都搅得天翻地覆，然后真正地将她带往一个全新的世界。 当然，这种事情并不经常发生，她得运气非常好才行，但真正幸运的人总能自己创造机会。而且，她已经比其他人有了更大的优势。如果真有人能拥有童话般的浪漫爱情，那一定应该是你亲爱的女儿。 嘿嘿嘿，不过你这话是什么意思呢 [kinu.Dad]就是说我比其他竞争者有优势这一点吧？ 嗯，她长大后肯定也想成为像清子那样的“母兽”，对吧？ 没错…… 现在，你还没有接触过规模更大的九尾狐社群，但根据你和她母亲的谈话，仅凭她的身份，就会有人争相追求她。当然，她仍然需要不断磨练自己的天赋，但追求她的人肯定不会缺少。 当基努试图理解这一切时，她那双大大的蓝眼睛睁得更加大了，而她原本就灿烂的笑容此时更是显得无比可爱，因为她的想象力已经开始疯狂地驰骋在那个美好的幻想世界中。你又轻轻揉了揉她的头发和耳朵，然后轻轻拍了拍她的脸颊。 好了好了，没必要这么激动。 太 变得过于兴奋或沉迷其中。 你…你是认真的吗？ [kinu.Dad]难道这种童话般的浪漫故事真的会发生在现实生活中吗？ 这种情况虽然不算常见，但完全有可能发生。正如你所说，她的机会比大多数人都要大，不过这一切并不会轻易降临到她身上。她只需要仔细想想你和她母亲之间发生的事情……究竟需要多少巧合，你们彼此之间又需要建立多大的信任，才能让这一系列事件最终促成她的诞生？ 我明白你的意思了。 [kinu.Dad]就是…… 你那只狐妖女儿的话语渐渐消失了，因为她的思绪已经开始转移，进入了另一个状态。 嗯…… 一个理想可能无法完全实现——毕竟它们本来就被称作“理想”嘛——但这并不意味着追求这个理想是否是一件好事。如果她想要过上像她母亲笔下的爱情小说里描述的那种生活，那么她最好先让自己配得上这样的生活。毕竟，追求梦想从来都不是一件容易的事。 好的， [kinu.Dad]我想……我想我明白了吧。 纪奈深吸了几口气，试图让自己平静下来，但这一努力最终还是徒劳的——她又忍不住爆发出一阵笑声。 我会尽我最大的努力的，好吗？ 有个好女孩。

rows.original: Indulge Kinu's dreams of romantic love. Sometimes dreams do come true, don't they? If anyone's dreams could become reality, they should be Kinu's.
rows.translation: 让绮奴实现她对浪漫爱情的梦想吧。有时候，梦想本身就是最重要的东西。 做 变成现实了，不是吗？如果有什么人的梦想真的能够实现，那一定应该是绮奴的梦想。
rows.raw: "Indulge Kinu's dreams of romantic love. Sometimes dreams do come true, don't they? If anyone's dreams could become reality, they should be Kinu's."

rows.original: You shake your head and give Kinu a firm pat on the shoulder. Stories are all very well and good for what they are, escapist fantasy — stories written for bored housewives to while away the time with. If she tries to live her life according to one of her mother's romance novels, though, she's only going to set herself up for disappointment. Kinu winces as she senses you prying at the seams of her fantasy. "[kinu.Dad]..." Those romance novels, they either never show you what happens after the end, or everything seems to magically work itself out without any effort on either party in the relationship. Happily ever after doesn't happen, not without a lot of work put into it; if she sets herself unrealistic expectations, she's going to have to be prepared to be disappointed time and again. "All right, then." Kinu folds her arms and glares up at you challengingly. "Tell me how it's done." After the novelty wears off, after the first rush of infatuation fades, what's left? It's easy to get caught up in the heat of the moment, but whoever she picks will have to be someone she can wake up to every morning for the rest of her life. That's not something that should be taken lightly, not is it something that "just happens." You and her mother, you've put in effort to work on your relationship, to build trust, to make and reciprocate sacrifices for one another. You didn't have to give her mother any of your life essence; you could simply have thrown the amulet away and forgot about it. Stories are just that, stories. This is real life, and in order to make good things last, they have to be worked on and cultivated. One good disagreement or argument, and the plots of those silly novels would fall apart. "But — but you just told me —" You just told her that no matter how magical your start with her mother was, it wouldn't have lasted if either one of you hadn't been willing to trust the other and work together, as well as work out your differences. Look, she's going to be a den mother when she grows up, right? "Yes...?" You haven't had that much exposure to the intricacies of larger kitsune society, but judging from what her mother's told you, she's going to be a pretty hot item when she's older. In that kind of position, it'll be really easy for her to get carried away... before making any decisions, she needs to sit down, calm down and think about whether this is the right choice to make. "I don't understand all of that, [kinu.Dad], and I'm supposed to be the smart one." Well, she needs to be a little older to put it all in perspective. Before then, though, you hope that she'll keep what you've told her today in mind. Not to say she can't enjoy her mother's trashy novels if she can get her little paws on them, but she has to keep in mind that ultimately, they're just fiction and she shouldn't expect her life to follow the narrative of some escapist tale. Kinu looks away and scratches at one of her ears. "If you say so, [kinu.Dad]."
rows.translation: 你摇了摇头，然后轻轻拍了拍绮奴的肩膀。故事本身确实很有意义，它们属于那种能够帮助人们逃避现实、沉浸在幻想中的文学形式——这类故事本来就是为那些无聊的家庭主妇们消磨时间而创作的。不过，如果她真的试图按照自己母亲写的那些言情小说来安排自己的生活，那么她只会让自己陷入失望之中。 绮奴感到你的话语正在刺破她那美好的幻想世界，不由得皱起了眉头。 "[kinu.Dad]..." 那些言情小说，要么根本不会描述故事结局之后的发展，要么就会把所有问题都描绘得好像双方都不需要付出任何努力就能顺利解决一样。幸福美满的结局从来都不是轻轻松松就能得到的；如果她对自己抱有不切实际的期望，那么她就必须做好一次又一次失望的准备。 那好吧。 纪奈双臂交叉，挑衅地抬头看着你。 告诉我到底是怎么做到的。 当新鲜感消退，最初的迷恋之情也慢慢褪去之后，剩下的究竟是什么？人们很容易被一时的热情所冲昏头脑，但无论她最终选择谁，那个人都必须是她愿意余生每天早晨一起面对的人。 这件事绝不能掉以轻心，更不是“偶然发生”的事情。你和她母亲，都为改善彼此的关系、建立信任、为对方做出牺牲而付出了努力。 你完全没有必要将自己的生命精华给予她的母亲；你完全可以把那个护身符扔掉，然后就此忘掉这件事。 故事终究只是故事而已。而现实生活则不同，要想让美好的事物长久持续下去，就必须不断地去努力、去经营、去培育它们。 只要发生一次激烈的争执或争论，那些愚蠢小说的情节就会彻底崩塌。 但是——但是你刚才才告诉我—— 你刚刚告诉她，无论你们与她母亲的初次相遇有多么美好，如果其中任何一方不愿意信任对方、不愿意共同努力、不愿意解决彼此之间的分歧，那么这种美好关系是无法持续下去的。你看，她长大后也会成为一个母亲，对吧？ 是吗……？ 你还没有深入了解那些复杂的狐族社会结构，但根据她母亲告诉你的那些话，等她长大后，她一定会成为非常抢手的人选。处于那样的地位，她很容易就会失去理智……在做出任何决定之前，她需要先冷静下来，仔细思考这是否真的是正确的选择。 我完全不明白那些内容， [kinu.Dad]而我却应该被认为是那个聪明的人。 嗯，她还得再长大一些，才能正确理解这一切。不过在此之前，你希望她能记住你今天告诉她的那些话。并不是说她不能读那些她妈妈写的低俗小说，但如果有机会的话，她还是应该记住：那些毕竟只是虚构的故事，她不应该把自己的生活想象成那些逃避现实的故事情节。 绮奴把目光移开，开始挠自己的耳朵。 如果你这么认为的话 [kinu.Dad]."
rows.raw: " You shake your head and give Kinu a firm pat on the shoulder. Stories are all very well and good for what they are, escapist fantasy — stories written for bored housewives to while away the time with. If she tries to live her life according to one of her mother's romance novels, though, she's only going to set herself up for disappointment. Kinu winces as she senses you prying at the seams of her fantasy. "[kinu.Dad]..." Those romance novels, they either never show you what happens after the end, or everything seems to magically work itself out without any effort on either party in the relationship. Happily ever after doesn't happen, not without a lot of work put into it; if she sets herself unrealistic expectations, she's going to have to be prepared to be disappointed time and again. "All right, then." Kinu folds her arms and glares up at you challengingly. "Tell me how it's done." After the novelty wears off, after the first rush of infatuation fades, what's left? It's easy to get caught up in the heat of the moment, but whoever she picks will have to be someone she can wake up to every morning for the rest of her life. That's not something that should be taken lightly, not is it something that "just happens." You and her mother, you've put in effort to work on your relationship, to build trust, to make and reciprocate sacrifices for one another. You didn't have to give her mother any of your life essence; you could simply have thrown the amulet away and forgot about it. Stories are just that, stories. This is real life, and in order to make good things last, they have to be worked on and cultivated. One good disagreement or argument, and the plots of those silly novels would fall apart. "But — but you just told me —" You just told her that no matter how magical your start with her mother was, it wouldn't have lasted if either one of you hadn't been willing to trust the other and work together, as well as work out your differences. Look, she's going to be a den mother when she grows up, right? "Yes...?" You haven't had that much exposure to the intricacies of larger kitsune society, but judging from what her mother's told you, she's going to be a pretty hot item when she's older. In that kind of position, it'll be really easy for her to get carried away... before making any decisions, she needs to sit down, calm down and think about whether this is the right choice to make. "I don't understand all of that, [kinu.Dad], and I'm supposed to be the smart one." Well, she needs to be a little older to put it all in perspective. Before then, though, you hope that she'll keep what you've told her today in mind. Not to say she can't enjoy her mother's trashy novels if she can get her little paws on them, but she has to keep in mind that ultimately, they're just fiction and she shouldn't expect her life to follow the narrative of some escapist tale. Kinu looks away and scratches at one of her ears. "If you say so, [kinu.Dad].""

rows.original: Disabuse Kinu of the notion. Love is nothing like what she imagines it to be; letting her get unrealistic ideas is setting her up for unhappiness.
rows.translation: 要让绮奴认清这个事实：爱情根本不是她想象中的那样；如果让她抱有不切实际的幻想，只会让她陷入不幸。
rows.raw: "Disabuse Kinu of the notion. Love is nothing like what she imagines it to be; letting her get unrealistic ideas is setting her up for unhappiness."

rows.original: It's a fine, warm day as you crest the hilltop, coming into the shade of the cherry blossom tree; it suddenly gets a lot warmer when something small and fluffy sneaks up on you from behind and [pc.hasTail|grabs you by the tail|hugs your legs]. [pc.cunningRange 70|Oh, you could've turned and called out Kinu at any moment, but it's so much more fun to let her imagine she's successfully sneaking up on you. |Instincts kick in, and you've half-turned, at the ready when you realize it's just Kinu. ] Your foxy daughter beams up at you, her three tails wagging like mad, moving so fast they're a blur. "Hiiiiiiiii [kinu.Dad]!" [pc.cunningRange 70| And there you were, wondering when she'd show up. "Aww, you figured I was there?" And a good thing, too. Given the reflexes you've had to cultivate of late, things might've become less than pleasant if she'd actually surprised you. | Not that you don't appreciate the enthusiastic greeting, but can she please make some noise when she moves in the future? You almost... well, you don't want to think about what you might've done, but could she not scare you like that? "Ehe..." Oh, looking at her face like that, you can't stay upset with her. But really, it's not a good idea to scare people with sharp objects about their person. ] You're not one of her siblings, after all. "Okay, okay, I'm sorry..." That's better. Gently reaching down, you pry a hyperactive fox kit off your person and set her down on the grass. Now, what's gotten her all worked up like this? "Eehee. I just wanted to show you something, [kinu.Dad]. You see, I've noticed that when I put on my best smile, people around me tend to follow suit, too. It worked on Mama, it works on most of my siblings, and I wanted to see if it works on you too!" And that required her sneaking up on you? "Well! If I scared you, [kinu.Dad], then you'd be mad at me, right? That way, I'd know if the power of my smile really works, because then you wouldn't just be randomly in a good mood, but also have to overcome your annoyance to smile back at me. I've got to be sure when I'm doing these things, can't leave them up to chance, you know." Beaming with all the innocence of an eight-year-old fox-child, Kinu clasps her hands together, closes her eyes, and squeals happily, her foxy ears wiggling to and fro. By the Seven, she's good. She's really good. Just looking at your daughter's face like this makes it practically impossible to get or stay mad at her; even when you know she's openly yanking on your heartstrings and manipulating you like... well, something that's easily manipulated. That ring of authenticity to her actions? Oh, it's there all right, very cleverly and convincingly faked; if you didn't know she was pretending... Gods. Did she get this from you, or her mother? Or, more likely, is it some ungodly whole that's emerged from the combination of such, a whole far greater than the sum of the parts? "Eeheehee. You're smiling, [kinu.Dad]." Damn, so you are. It's a good thing she's got going over there. Kinu sticks her tongue out at you. "Don't worry, [kinu.Dad]. I promise to use this amazing power only for the cause of good." She promises, yes? "I double-dog promise. Really though, [kinu.Dad]... it's very gratifying to be able to spread joy just like this, even when I'm faking it. Then I get happy for real, and that only makes it better." Your foxy daughter sighs and squirms on the spot, color rising to her cheeks. "Or worse, depending on your point of view." Because when you actually become the mask, what's even the point of bothering to wear one, right? She'll never be a properly cunning heartstring-tugger if she's so easily falling victim to her own machinations... "Ehehehe. I don't know, [kinu.Dad], I kind of like it this way." So she does. Still... cute as it is, should she be doing this? Putting on an emotional show for other people? Sure, it's not intrinsically bad, but knowing what you do, even if she's not doing such for manipulative and self-serving ends — would it be right to put this sort of emotional labor on an eight-year-old child?
rows.translation: 当你爬上山顶，走进樱花树的荫凉之下时，天气晴朗而温暖；然而，当有某个小巧而柔软的东西从背后悄悄靠近你时，气温突然变得暖和了许多 [pc.hasTail|直接抓住你的把柄|抱着你的腿]. [pc.cunningRange 70|哦，你其实随时都可以转身叫住绮奴，但让她以为自己已经成功地悄悄接近了你，这样反而有趣多了。 |本能立刻驱使你转过身去，准备应对任何可能的威胁，直到你意识到来人其实是绮奴。 ] 你那只机敏的女儿欢快地朝你奔来，她的三条尾巴疯狂地摇动，速度快得让人看不清它们的轮廓。 嗨 [kinu.Dad]!" [pc.cunningRange 70| 你就这么坐着，心里琢磨着她什么时候会出现。 哇，你居然猜到我就在那里？ 这也是件好事。考虑到你最近不得不培养出来的那些反应能力，如果她真的突然出现的话，情况可能会变得相当不愉快。 | 并不是说你不喜欢她那热情的问候，但以后她移动的时候能不能稍微注意点声音呢？你差点就……嗯，你肯定不想去想自己当时可能会做出什么反应，但她真的不能这么吓人吗？ 嘿嘿…… 哦，看到她那样的表情，你就不会再生她的气了。不过说真的，用尖锐的物品来吓唬别人，确实不是个好主意。 ] 毕竟，你又不是她的兄弟姐妹之一。 好吧，好吧，我很抱歉…… 这样就好多了。你轻轻地将那只过于活跃的小狐狸从自己身上抱下来，放在草地上。那么，究竟是什么事情让它变得如此兴奋呢？ 嘻嘻，我只是想给你看点东西而已 [kinu.Dad]你知道吗，我注意到，每当我露出最灿烂的笑容时，我周围的人也会跟着我一起笑。这个方法对妈妈有效，对我的大多数兄弟姐妹也有效，所以我想看看对你是否也有效呢！ 这就需要她偷偷接近你吗？ 哎呀！如果我吓到你了 [kinu.Dad]那样的话，你肯定会生我的气的，对吧？这样我就能知道我的笑容是否真的有效了——因为如果你只是随便心情好了一点，而并非克服了烦恼才选择对我微笑，那我就可以确定我的笑容确实有用了。我必须知道这个答案。 当然可以。 当我做这些事情的时候，就不能把它们交给运气来决定，你懂我的意思吧。 金努带着八岁小狐狸特有的纯真，双手部合十，闭上眼睛，开心地尖叫起来，她那狐狸般的耳朵还不停地晃动着。天啊，她真棒……她真的做得很好。 真的吗 太好了。只要看到你女儿这样的脸，就根本不可能生她的气，或者继续生她的气；即使在你 知道 她明明在故意触碰你的敏感神经，操纵你……嗯，就像在操纵一个很容易被影响的人一样。她那些行为所表现出的“真实性”呢？哦，当然存在，只不过是被她巧妙而逼真地伪造出来的；如果你没有仔细观察的话，根本就发现不了。 知道 她在装模作样…… 天啊，这是她从你这里学来的，还是她妈妈教的？或者，更有可能的是，这是某种由这些元素组合而成的、完全全新的东西——其整体效果远远超过了各个部分相加所带来的结果？ 嘻嘻嘻，你在笑呢 [kinu.Dad]." 该死，原来如此。幸好她去了那边。 绮奴对着你吐了吐舌头。 别担心， [kinu.Dad]我承诺，只会将这种强大的力量用于善良的事业。 她答应了，对吧？ 我郑重承诺。真的，绝对没有骗你。 [kinu.Dad]…能够以这样的方式带来快乐，即使我是在假装，也让我感到非常有成就感。这样一来，我才会真正感到开心，而这种感觉只会让一切变得更加美好。 你那个调皮的女儿在原地坐立不安，脸颊渐渐涨红了。 或者更糟糕的情况，这取决于你的观点。 因为当你真正成为了那个“面具”的化身时，再戴上面具还有什么意义呢？如果她这么容易就被自己设下的圈套所害，那她永远也成不了一个真正高明、善于牵动别人情感的人…… 嘿嘿嘿，我也不清楚 [kinu.Dad]我其实挺喜欢这样的方式的。 她确实这么做了。不过……虽然这样挺可爱的，但她真的应该这样做吗？为了取悦别人而刻意表现出某种情绪吗？当然，这本身并没有什么坏处，但既然她知道自己在做什么，而且即使她这样做的目的并不是为了操控别人或满足自己的私欲，那么让一个八岁的孩子承担这种“情感劳动”，真的合适吗？

rows.original: Smiling your best smile, you shake your head and pat Kinu right between her large fluffy ears, making your daughter squeal in delight. It's good that she likes smiling a lot, because the world could do with a lot more smiling people than sad ones. Even if her own smiles aren't always genuine to start with, as she pointed out, lifting someone else's spirits only serves to give oneself joy to match. "Mmm... so you like it, [kinu.Dad]?" You do, and you're personally hoping that you'll get to see Kinu smile a lot more. Her mother was alone in this place for so long, and having someone smile up at her — well, you can guess how much it means to her mother. Kinu considers that for a moment through all the wriggling and squirming she's doing. "Eehee. You know, [kinu.Dad], I feel like it's some kind of miracle that people are able to spread their joy like this. Don't you think so?" A miracle? You don't know about that. It's simply just being with the people you love, that's all — you just want to see them happy, and when they are, you are too. See, you'll demonstrate right here... Reaching down, you scoop up Kinu by under her arms and pull your kitsune daughter into your embrace. She kicks and wiggles, her three tails tickling your nose, but eventually settles into the hug and lets out a sigh of utter satisfaction. "Okay, [kinu.Dad], I get it, I really do." Does she? "Oh yes, very much so. I'll take this lesson to heart." Kinu fluffs up a little when you set her back down, but quickly pats herself down to her usual sleek form. "Just watch me!" With that, she's bounding off away from you, practically bouncing all the way back home. Heh, here's to hoping she doesn't overdo it and end up ticking off her mother... although the thought of Kiyoko trying to explain that Kinu's too happy is quite an amusing one.
rows.translation: 你露出最灿烂的笑容，摇摇头，然后轻轻拍了拍基努那两只蓬松的大耳朵，这让你的女儿开心地尖叫起来。幸好她很喜欢微笑，因为这个世界上，需要更多微笑的人，而不是那些总是面带愁容的人。虽然正如她自己指出的那样，她的微笑并不总是发自内心，但只要自己的行为能够让别人的心情变得愉快，那么自己也会感到无比快乐。 嗯……所以你喜欢它啊 [kinu.Dad]?" 你确实这么希望，而且你也真心希望自己能经常看到绮奴露出笑容。她的母亲在这里独自生活了太久，而当有人对她微笑时——嗯，你可以想象这对她的母亲来说意味着什么。 在那些扭动、挣扎的动作中，绮奴也有那么一刻想到了这一点。 嘻嘻，你知道的 [kinu.Dad]我觉得，人们能够以这样的方式传递自己的快乐，简直就像是一种奇迹。你不这么认为吗？ 奇迹？你根本不懂那是什么。其实，只要能和自己爱的人在一起，那就足够了——你只是希望看到他们开心，而当他们开心的时候，你也会感到无比幸福。看，你现在就在这里证明了这一点…… 你俯身将绮奴的双臂从下方抱住，将这个拥有三条尾巴的狐灵女儿紧紧搂在怀里。她不停地踢腿扭动，那三条尾巴轻轻挠着你的鼻子，但最终还是安静下来，满足地叹了口气。 好的， [kinu.Dad]我明白了，真的明白了。 她是这样吗？ 哦，是的，我一定会牢记这个教训的。 当你把绮奴放回原地时，她会稍微蓬松一下，但很快又会恢复到她那惯常的光滑形态。 就看我的吧！ 说完这句话，她就蹦蹦跳跳地离你走了，几乎是一路小跑着回到了家。呵呵，希望她不会做得太过火，以免惹恼她的妈妈……不过，想象着清子试图向妈妈解释关于纪奈的事情，还是觉得有点好笑。 太 happy”这个词用在这里确实挺有趣的。
