You do, and you're personally hoping that you'll get to see Kinu smile a lot more. Her mother was alone in this place for so long, and having someone smile up at her — well, you can guess how much it means to her mother. Kinu considers that for a moment through all the wriggling and squirming she's doing. "Eehee. You know, [kinu.Dad], I feel like it's some kind of miracle that people are able to spread their joy like this. Don't you think so?" A miracle? You don't know about that. It's simply just being with the people you love, that's all — you just want to see them happy, and when they are, you are too. See, you'll demonstrate right here... Reaching down, you scoop up Kinu by under her arms and pull your kitsune daughter into your embrace. She kicks and wiggles, her three tails tickling your nose, but eventually settles into the hug and lets out a sigh of utter satisfaction. "Okay, [kinu.Dad], I get it, I really do." Does she? "Oh yes, very much so. I'll take this lesson to heart." Kinu fluffs up a little when you set her back down, but quickly pats herself down to her usual sleek form. "Just watch me!" With that, she's bounding off away from you, practically bouncing all the way back home. Heh, here's to hoping she doesn't overdo it and end up ticking off her mother... although the thought of Kiyoko trying to explain that Kinu's too happy is quite an amusing one."

rows.original: A smile like hers spreads joy. Even if she isn't feeling it herself, she should be fully expressive and help others be happy.
rows.translation: 像她这样的微笑总能带来欢乐。即使她自己并没有感到开心，她也应该尽情地表达出来，让别人感受到快乐。
rows.raw: "A smile like hers spreads joy. Even if she isn't feeling it herself, she should be fully expressive and help others be happy."

rows.original: Sighing, you squat down so you're on eye level with Kinu, and give her a small pat on the head. Her smile is beautiful and all, but perhaps she should be a little more circumspect in where and how she utilises it. "You're not saying that I shouldn't smile, are you, [kinu.Dad]?" No, you're not saying that. What you're getting at is that wearing her heart on her sleeve is far more effective if she doesn't do it all the time, and she's genuine about it. If she's overwhelmingly cheery and chirpy all the time, then people are going to get tired of it — one can be pleasant and courteous without being overbearing. "I don't quite understand..." Hmm. Does she like sweets? "Oh yes! The hardened candies that Mama and I make together are —" Now, if she would let you finish this train of thought. Could she eat them every day, all day? Kinu considers this question a minute or two; you spy the mischievous tic in her face as she considers saying yes. She thinks better of it, though, instead folding her arms and shaking her head. "I guess not... I'd get sick after a day or two." And what about rice? What's so special about it that she[kiyoko.numKits 3 |, her mother and her siblings| and her mother] eat it every day for almost every meal? "Eh... nothing much, I guess... it kinda just fills the belly... oh." You take it she's figured out the point you're getting at. "Yes, [kinu.Dad]..." You smile, hook your hands under Kinu's arms, and pluck your kitsune daughter off the ground into a warm embrace. She squeals and kicks for a bit, then sinks against you while you pet her head; her trio of tails tickle your face in return. More is less, less is more. Good times like these... if you have too many of them, you start to take them for granted, they lose their appeal, you keep needing more to try and recreate that first joy. You don't realize how important they are, not until they're gone — her mother learned that the hard way. Simply speaking to another person, human contact, having someone who actually cares about you — they're not important until you don't have them, whereupon they become vitally so. You're not telling her not to smile; rather, when she does, you want the gesture to be meaningful and genuine; faking it for the sake of cheering others up is noble, but it's not going to be as effective if she does it too much. Does she get it? "Yeah, [kinu.Dad]. I think I do. It's a lot to process, though... even if I feel like I should be able to get it instinctively." You know she's a bright cookie, so she'll be able to figure it out soon enough. Sometimes, the most obvious answer isn't the one she needs. All right, that's enough — carefully, you set Kinu back down on the ground, where she tries to smooth out her fluffed-up hair and fur. "Aww..." One can't enjoy the good without the bad; you'd have to let go of her eventually. Now like you said, she needs to think about what you told her today. "Okay. I'll go out to the river and reflect on it, maybe catch some fish. I don't really like it, but it kinda makes sense when I follow your line of reasoning..." Good girl. Although to be frank, you'd rather her figure it out from first principles. All right then, off she goes. "Say hi to Mama for me, okay? I'll be back before dinner! Have fun playing together!" With that, Kinu's off, rapidly disappearing into the forest and leaving you alone on the hill. With a child like her, the only way she'll forget what you said is if she chose to do so... and you get the feeling that she's not about to do that any time soon.
rows.translation: 你叹了口气，蹲下来与绮奴平视，轻轻拍了拍她的头。她的笑容确实很美，但或许她应该更加注意在什么场合、以什么样的方式展现这种笑容。 你并不是说我不应该微笑，对吧？ [kinu.Dad]?" 不，你并不是这个意思。你想要表达的是：如果她不总是把感情表露得过于明显，而是真正发自内心地表现出来，那么这种做法会显得更加有效。如果她总是表现得过于开朗、活泼，人们反而会对此感到厌烦——一个人完全可以保持友善和礼貌，而不必表现得过分夸张。 我不太明白…… 嗯，她喜欢甜食吗？ 哦，对了！妈妈和我一起制作的那些硬糖—— 现在，如果她能让你把这个想法说完整的话……她真的能每天、一整天都吃这些东西吗？ 基努思考了一两分钟；当你看到她脸上浮现出那种调皮的神情时，你几乎可以断定她想答应这个请求。不过，她最终还是改变了主意，只是双臂交叉，摇了摇头。 我想不行……撑一两天我就会生病吧。 那大米呢？它有什么特别之处，让她[kiyoko.numKits 3 |她的母亲以及她的兄弟姐妹们| 以及她的母亲] 每天几乎每顿饭都吃这个吗？ 呃……也没什么特别的，就是能填饱肚子而已…… 哦。" 她应该已经理解你想要表达的意思了。 是的， [kinu.Dad]..." 你微笑着，将手部搭在纪奈的臂弯上，然后将你的九尾狐女儿从地上抱起来，紧紧拥在怀里。她先是尖叫着、踢蹬着，但很快就在你轻抚她头发的时候靠在了你身上；她的三条尾巴轻轻挠着你的脸，仿佛在回应你的爱抚。 越多反而越少，越少反而越有意义。像这样的美好时光……如果它们太过频繁，人们就会开始把它们视为理所当然，它们的魅力也会随之消失。人们会不断追求更多，试图重新体验最初的那种喜悦。直到这些时光真正离我们而去，人们才会意识到它们究竟有多重要——她的母亲就是通过惨痛的经历才明白了这个道理。 简单来说，与人建立联系、拥有真正关心你的人——这些在平时可能并不会被你视为多么重要，但一旦你失去了它们，你就会意识到它们是多么不可或缺。 你并不是在告诉她不要微笑；相反，当你 进行……操作你希望这种举动能够富有意义且发自内心；为了让别人开心而假装这样做固然高尚，但如果她做得太过频繁，效果就会大打折扣。她明白这一点吗？ 是啊， [kinu.Dad]我想我是懂的。不过，这些信息确实需要花一些时间来消化……尽管我觉得自己应该能够凭直觉理解它们。 你知道她是个聪明的女孩，所以她很快就能弄明白的。有时候，最显而易见的答案并不是她所需要的。好了，够了——你小心翼翼地把绮奴放回地上，她试图整理自己那些蓬乱的毛发和皮毛。 哎呀…… 没有坏事，也就不会有好事；你最终还是得放她走。就像你说的，她现在需要认真思考你今天告诉她的那些话。 好吧，我去河边好好想想，或许还能抓些鱼。其实我并不是很喜欢这个主意，但按照你的逻辑来想，倒也挺有道理的…… 好姑娘。不过说实话，你还是希望她能从基本原理出发自己去弄明白这件事。好吧，那她就可以去尝试了。 代我向妈妈问好，好吗？晚饭前我就会回来！一起玩得开心点！ 就这样，绮奴离开了，迅速消失在森林中，把你独自留在了山上。对于这样一个孩子来说，她唯一能忘记你说的话的方法，就是 选择了 要做这样的事情……但你会觉得，她短期内并不会真的去这么做。

rows.original: Familiarity breeds contempt, and it's important to be honest in one's feelings. If she smiles only when she means it, people will appreciate it more.
rows.translation: 熟能生厌，因此坦诚表达自己的感受非常重要。如果她只有当真心实意的时候才会微笑，人们会更加欣赏这样的态度。
rows.raw: "Familiarity breeds contempt, and it's important to be honest in one's feelings. If she smiles only when she means it, people will appreciate it more."

rows.original: Some time ago and somewhere else... Bringing in the laundry is quite the tiresome task, especially since [kiyoko.numKits 8|there's so much of it|you're so small]. These days, the basket is practically half your size, but you really seem to be taking your time in growing taller. Mother says it'll be good exercise and you can't deny the truth of that, but even so... Well, at least you're almost done; there's just Mother's clothes left to deal with. Pushing open the screen door leading to her private chambers, you lug in the laundry basket after you and stop to catch your breath. Everything's simply so big when you're this tiny, and it's all so tiring... come to think of it, you haven't seen Mother indoors all day since morning. Did she go to run an errand? Well, it's not your business, you've got to get these clothes folded and put away. Just as you're about to get back on the job, though, you can't help but notice that a couple things have been left on Mother's vanity. Usually, that kind of stuff's kept away safely, but she must've left it in a hurry when she went wherever she was going. Now that you're thinking about it, you can smell the fragrance of aromatic herbs even from across the room, enticement and allure squeezed into one tight package. Ehehehe... Like it or not, your ears and tails start wiggling of their own accord, and before you know it, your feet have drawn you over to the big mirrored vanity. Mother's cosmetics smell really nice... you know she always has that faint floral scent about her. You've always wondered how these grown-up things work... well, knowing is one thing, but practical experience is another, and since Mother's not in right now...
rows.translation: 很久以前，在另一个地方…… 把洗好的衣服拿进来确实是一件相当烦人的事情，尤其是 [kiyoko.numKits 8|数量非常多。|你太小了。]这些天，那个洗衣篮的大小几乎只有你原来的一半了，不过你长个子的速度确实挺慢的。妈妈说这样有助于锻炼身体，这一点确实无可否认，但即便如此…… 好吧，至少你已经快完成了；现在只剩下妈妈的衣服需要处理了。你推开门走进她的私人房间，把洗衣篮拖了进去，然后停下来喘口气。一切都进行得如此顺利 大的 当你这么小的时候，做这些事情真的太累了……仔细想想，从早上到现在，你一天都没有在室内见过妈妈。她是去办什么事了吗？不过，这与你无关，你现在的任务就是把这些衣服叠好并收好。 然而，就在你准备继续工作时，你不禁注意到母亲梳妆台上还留着几样东西。通常，这类物品都会被妥善收好，但她肯定是匆忙离开时忘带了它们。 现在仔细想来，即使隔着整个房间，你也能闻到那些芳香草药的气息——这种诱惑与吸引力仿佛被紧紧地包裹在了一起。 呵呵呵呵…… 不管你愿不愿意，你的耳朵和尾巴都会不由自主地动起来，而不知不觉间，你的足部步就已经将你引向了那面巨大的镜前梳妆台。 妈妈的化妆品味道真的很好闻……你知道，她身上总是带着那种淡淡的花香。你一直很好奇这些成人的化妆品到底是怎么用的……嗯，知道原理是一回事，但实际使用又是另一回事了。而且现在妈妈又不在家……..

rows.original: Ehehe. You've always wondered how this works. While you vaguely know that the powder inside that box's supposed to make one's skin appear lighter, you've never quite figured out how it does that; that's not the kind of thing you'd learn from a book. Then there's the matter of the eyeshadow... Mother doesn't use it much, that kind of thing doesn't really suit her. Doesn't go well with her fur color or something, you weren't listening that time... Still... Carefully, you creak open the wooden box, and are rewarded with a puff of sweet-smelling powder. Yes, it's definitely that floral scent that clings to Mother, you can tell as much. But oh, how it tickles your nose — a-ah — "Achoo!" Eyes wide, ears perked, you listen for footsteps in the hallway outside, but all is silent. Heaving a sigh of relief, you turn your attention back to Mother's vanity and take a pinch of the soft cream-colored powder between your fingers, rubbing away and wondering at the smooth, crumbly feel and perfumed smell. Mother puts some of this on her face, doesn't she? Why does she need it, anyway? Maybe you'll find out of you experiment a little... Hee hee. This is so much fun! "Kinu?!" You freeze, oily, powder-caked fingers half-raised to your face. "Mama?" "What are you doing?" Your eyes dart from the vanity, to the laundry basket, then back to Mother. "Um..." "Keros' tails, look at you." In a few strides, she's crossed the room and is towering over you, arms folded. "You're a frightful mess." "Ehehehe, I don't know, Mama. I think I look quite pretty." Mother quirks an eyebrow. "Have you even looked at yourself in the mirror, young woman?" "Eh... yes. Why? Is it bad?" A sigh. "You look no different from one of those barbarian foreigners with war-paint on their faces. What possessed you to smear your cheeks all over with eyeshadow?" "Um... it was fun?" "I'd tell you to stay out of my things in the future, but I know that isn't going to work with you. By all rights, you're too young to start even thinking about dolling yourself up like this, but knowing you, you just want to understand it all. Am I right? "If you're going to play with my makeup, you might as well learn to apply it correctly. That way I don't have to teach you how to do it all over again when you're old enough to put what you've learned into practice. What are you giggling at, young woman?" "Ehe... I was expecting to be scolded, and that would be the end of that. But with you offering to teach me how to look nice, I think I came out ahead." Mother just sighs and claps a hand to her forehead. "Such a precocious child; whatever will I do with you? If teaching you will sate your curiosity and keep you out of my things, I'm willing to do it." "Yaaaaay!" "But first, clean off your face! Then, the laundry!" "Yes, Mama."
rows.translation: 嘿嘿，你一直很好奇这是怎么发挥作用的吧？虽然你大概知道那个盒子里的粉末能让皮肤看起来更白，但具体原理你其实并不清楚——这种东西可不是通过读书就能弄明白的。 然后还有眼影的问题……妈妈不太常用那种眼影，那种风格真的不适合她。她的毛色之类的和它不太搭，你当时根本没在听…… 不过…… 你小心翼翼地打开那个木箱，顿时闻到了一阵芳香扑鼻的粉末。没错，那正是母亲身上散发着的那种花香气息。不过，这种味道真的让人鼻子发痒啊——啊 阿嚏！ 你瞪大眼睛，竖起耳朵，试图听清外面走廊里是否有脚步声，但四周一片寂静。你松了一口气，又将注意力转向母亲的梳妆台，用手指取了一点点那种柔软的奶油色粉末，仔细揉搓着，同时思考着它那细腻、易碎的质地以及那芬芳的气味。母亲不是也会在脸上涂抹这种东西吗？她究竟为什么需要它呢？也许你可以通过自己尝试一下来找到答案…… 嘻嘻，真是太有趣了！ 基努？！ 你的手指僵硬着，沾满了油污和粉末，半举着靠近脸庞。 妈妈？ 你在干什么？ 进行中?" 你的目光在梳妆台、洗衣篮之间来回移动，最后又回到了母亲身上。 嗯…… 凯罗斯的尾巴，看看你。 她几步就走到了你的面前，双臂交叉站在你面前，显得比你高大许多。 你简直是一团糟。 嘿嘿嘿，妈妈，我也不确定呢。不过我觉得自己看起来还挺漂亮的吧。 母亲挑了挑眉毛。 你到底有没有 看起来 年轻的女士，你是在镜子前审视自己吗？ 呃……是的。为什么？有什么不好的地方吗？ 一声叹息。 你看起来和那些脸上涂着战涂的野蛮外国人没什么两样。究竟是什么驱使你把眼影涂得满面都是的？ 嗯……还挺有趣的吧？ 我本想告诉你以后别管我的事情，但我知道你对这种劝告根本不会听。按常理来说，你年纪还太小，根本不应该开始考虑打扮得这么花枝招展，但了解你之后，我就知道你就是非得弄明白这一切才行。对吧？ 如果你要玩弄我的化妆品，那就最好先学会正确地使用它们。这样等你长大到可以实践自己所学的知识时，我就不用再一遍一遍地教你了。姑娘，你在笑什么啊？ 呵呵……我本来以为会被人责骂，然后这件事也就到此为止了。但既然你主动提出要教我如何打扮得漂亮些，我想我反而占了上风。 母亲只是叹了口气，然后用手拍了拍自己的额头。 这么早熟的孩子……我该拿你怎么办呢？如果教导你能够满足你的好奇心，同时让你不要乱动我的东西，那我愿意这么做。 耶耶耶！ 但首先，把脸上的东西擦干净！然后再去洗衣服！ 是的，妈妈。

You freeze, oily, powder-caked fingers half-raised to your face. "Mama?" "What are you doing?" Your eyes dart from the vanity, to the laundry basket, then back to Mother. "Um..." "Keros' tails, look at you." In a few strides, she's crossed the room and is towering over you, arms folded. "You're a frightful mess." "Ehehehe, I don't know, Mama. I think I look quite pretty." Mother quirks an eyebrow. "Have you even looked at yourself in the mirror, young woman?" "Eh... yes. Why? Is it bad?" A sigh. "You look no different from one of those barbarian foreigners with war-paint on their faces. What possessed you to smear your cheeks all over with eyeshadow?" "Um... it was fun?" "I'd tell you to stay out of my things in the future, but I know that isn't going to work with you. By all rights, you're too young to start even thinking about dolling yourself up like this, but knowing you, you just want to understand it all. Am I right? "If you're going to play with my makeup, you might as well learn to apply it correctly. That way I don't have to teach you how to do it all over again when you're old enough to put what you've learned into practice. What are you giggling at, young woman?" "Ehe... I was expecting to be scolded, and that would be the end of that. But with you offering to teach me how to look nice, I think I came out ahead." Mother just sighs and claps a hand to her forehead. "Such a precocious child; whatever will I do with you? If teaching you will sate your curiosity and keep you out of my things, I'm willing to do it." "Yaaaaay!" "But first, clean off your face! Then, the laundry!" "Yes, Mama."'

rows.original: Play with your mother's eyeshadow and foundation.
rows.translation: 乱用你妈妈的眼影和粉底吧。
rows.raw: "Play with your mother's eyeshadow and foundation."

rows.original: Grinning to yourself, you pick up Mother's hairbrush and turn it over in your hands. Gee... while you've seen Mother brushing out her hair and fur with this thing, you've never had the opportunity to examine it up close... it's so exquisite, the wood a golden-brown, the bristles delightful against your skin as you test them with a finger. It's really like something a fine lady would use — no, a queen. Ehehehee... laundry all but forgotten, you can't help but curl one of your tails around and give the brush an experimental run through the fur, practically squealing in delight as bristles part the silken hairs. This feels so much better than the lousy old brush you get to use! Sure, maybe it's just because the brush is Mother's and you're not supposed to use it — the allure of forbidden fruit — but there's also a sense of weight and history to it that makes you feel so big and refined. Like a grown-up, even! How much better would it be if you used that herb oil as well? Time to find out! It's a bit of a struggle to pry open the earthenware jar, but you eventually manage it and are greeted with a strong, pungent odour. It's slightly musky, but mostly medicinal; thick and colorless, the oil roils in its jar as you swirl it about gently. Eeeee! You can't take it any more! Quickly undoing your braid, you shake your hair out and dip Mother's hairbrush in a bit of the oil. Your little body shivers in delight as you brush out your hair, feeling the tangles and snarls give way before the amazing bristles — it's practically like being petted! With this in mind, you can't wait and immediately turn the brush to your sleek tails, your lips parted in a silly, open-mouthed smile as Mother's hairbrush practically flows through fox-fur, the oil spreading evenly and leaving a lustrous sheen in its wake. Sheesh... did you really have that many grass bits caught up in your tails? They must've gotten in when you were out at the clothesline... Back and forth, back and forth, feeling your usually sleek tail fur fluff up and stand on end, the soft tingling of static that accompanies glorious warmth. All of it conspires to leave you wide-eyed and drooling like an idiot — little wonder that given the time, Mother can brush all [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] of her tails for hours on end... "Kinu?" That voice... uh-oh. Your ears flatten themselves against your head, but caught mid-brush as you are, there's no way to hide what you've been doing. "You're using my hairbrush, aren't you?" It's all you can do to smile weakly. "Ehehe. Sorry, Mama." "Really. I go out to run an errand, forget to put away my things, and here you are. Do you really like that brush so much?" "It's... very good. It looks so elegant, with all those carvings on it. Oh, and it feels so good in my hair and fur. How do you make that oil? Is that how you get your tails so fluffy?" A pause, and then finally, a sigh. "I suppose the day would eventually come; a girl must play with her mother's things, mustn't she? Finish up putting away the laundry first, then go and get your own brush. I'll teach you how to compound the herbal oil and apply it properly. Look at you, you're a complete mess." A mess? You don't get it, you spread the oil evenly, didn't you? "I feel just fine, Mama..." "That's exactly what I mean. Now, laundry!"
rows.translation: 你暗自笑着，拿起母亲的梳子，在手部中仔细端详起来。哎呀……虽然你经常看到母亲用这个梳子梳理自己的头发和毛发，但却从未有机会仔细观察它……真是太精致了——木头呈金棕色，刷毛触在皮肤上感觉无比舒适，用手部指轻轻一试，那种感觉简直棒极了。这种刷子真的像是只有高贵的女士才会使用的东西……不，应该是女王才会用的。 呵呵呵呵……洗衣服的事早就被抛到九霄云外去了，你忍不住拿一根尾巴缠住刷子，在自己的皮毛上试了试，当刷毛轻轻分开那些丝滑的毛发时，你简直高兴得叫了起来。 这个感觉比那个破旧的旧刷子好多了。 你 可以用啦！当然，也许只是因为那支笔是妈妈的，你不应该使用它——这就是“禁果”的诱惑吧——但除此之外，还有一种别的感觉 重量 以及 历史 正是这种感觉让你觉得自己如此成熟、如此有内涵，简直就像个成年人一样！ 如果你也使用这种草本精油，效果会好多少呢？是时候去试试看了！虽然打开那个陶罐有点费劲，但最终你还是成功了，顿时一股浓烈、刺鼻的气味扑面而来。这种精油带有淡淡的麝香气息，但主要还是药香味；它质地浓稠、无色透明，当你轻轻摇晃罐子时，精油会在里面流动。 哎呀！你实在受不了了！你迅速解开发辫，把头发抖散开来，然后取母亲的那把梳子，蘸上一点油。当你用这把梳子梳理头发时，你的小身体兴奋得微微颤抖——那些缠结的头发在梳子的作用下纷纷散开，这种感觉简直就像有人在抚摸你一样！ 想到这里，你迫不及待地用刷子轻轻梳理自己光滑的尾巴，嘴唇微微张开，露出一个傻乎乎的微笑——妈妈的梳子仿佛在狐狸的毛皮上滑行一般，油脂均匀地被涂抹开来，留下了一层亮泽的光泽。 哎呀……你的尾巴上真的缠了那么多草屑吗？肯定是在你把衣服挂在晾衣绳上的时候粘上去的…… 来回摩擦着，感受着自己原本光滑的尾巴毛变得蓬松起来，那种伴随着温暖感觉的轻微静电刺激，真的会让你目瞪口呆、流口水……难怪过了一段时间，妈妈就能把那些草屑都刷干净了。 [kiyoko.kiyokoTails] 她尾巴不停地摆动，持续了好几个小时…… 基努？ 那个声音……哦不。你的耳朵会紧紧贴在头上，但在这种情况下，已经无法隐藏你刚才在做什么了。 你正在用我的梳子，对吧？ 你只能勉强挤出一丝微笑。 嘿嘿，对不起，妈妈。 真的吗？我出去办点事，结果忘了把东西收起来，结果你就来了。你真的那么喜欢那支笔吗？ 太……太好了。上面那些雕刻看起来如此精美，而且涂在头发和皮毛上感觉也非常舒服。你们是怎么制作这种油的？是不是因为用了这种油，你们的尾巴才会那么柔软蓬松呢？ 一阵停顿，终于，一声叹息。 我想这样的日子终究会到来的；女孩子总得玩玩妈妈的东西，不是吗？先把洗好的衣服收好，然后再去拿你自己的刷子。我会教你如何配制这种草药油以及正确使用它。看看你现在的样子，简直一团糟。 一团糟？你根本没搞懂，你应该把油均匀地涂开才对吧？ 妈妈，我完全没事…… 我说的就是这个意思。现在，去洗衣服吧！

rows.original: Play with your mother's brush and herb oil.
rows.translation: 用你妈妈的画笔和草本精油来创作吧。
rows.raw: "Play with your mother's brush and herb oil."

rows.original:
Curiously, you pick up both powder box and brush off the dresser, shaking them a bit before setting them down again. Eh, these don't look as fun close up as they were at a distance... not to mention they smell funny, too. You know from personal experience the value of a brush in getting the leaves, tangles and dead bugs out of your fur at the end of the day, but the rest is just a big bother. It'll give away your scent to rabbits and squirrels, and besides, all that stuff will wash off the moment you go for a swim.

        Who are you going to be looking pretty for, anyway?
        
        Shaking your head, you step away from the vanity and back towards your laundry basket. Daydreaming is fine — no, it isn't fine. It's wasting time, and you've got better things to do than contemplating playing with Mother's personal effects. You're a future den mother... you're above that sort of childish thing. There's laundry to be put away, and it's not going to do that by itself.
rows.translation:
奇怪的是，你把那个粉盒和刷子都从梳妆台上拿下来，稍微晃了晃它们，然后又把它们放了回去。嗯，近距离看的话，这些东西似乎没有远看时那么有趣了……更不用说它们还散发着奇怪的气味。 你肯定有过这样的亲身经历：在一天结束时，用刷子把毛发上的树叶、缠结物和死虫子清除掉，确实非常方便。但除此之外，使用刷子反而会带来很多麻烦——它会让兔子和松鼠闻到你的气味，而且一旦你去游泳，那些东西很快就会被水冲掉。

        你到底想给谁打扮得漂漂亮亮的呢？

你摇摇头，走开梳妆台，回到了放洗衣物的篮子旁。做白日梦倒也无妨——不，其实并不好。这只是在浪费时间，你还有更重要的事情要做，而不是去琢磨母亲的个人物品。 你以后可要像个家庭主妇一样了……这种幼稚的事情不应该再发生了。还有衣服要洗好并收好，这些事情可不会自己完成哦。

It's wasting time, and you've got better things to do than contemplating playing with Mother's personal effects. You're a future den mother... you're above that sort of childish thing. There's laundry to be put away, and it's not going to do that by itself."

rows.original: While all of this is interesting, none of it looks particularly fun.
rows.translation: 虽然这一切都很有趣，但看起来并没有哪一项真正有趣味性。
rows.raw: "While all of this is interesting, none of it looks particularly fun."

rows.original: Warm smells fill the kitchen as Mother stirs the pot. [kiyoko.numKits 2 8 16|She always seems at her best and happiest in this part of the house; their auras mesh well. It's clear that unlike you, Mother doesn't see the task of feeding your hungry mouth as a burden at all; to be quite frank, it makes you a little jealous. |Lunchtime is always a treat, mostly because you get to lord it over your siblings. Sure, you have to take responsibility if something goes wrong, but that's a small price to pay for the glorious title of Big Sister. It makes you feel all warm and good inside, even without having just eaten. |It's big — it has to be in order to feed not just the two of you, but all your brothers and sisters as well — but she always takes such joy in the simple act of cooking that the sheer magnitude of the act dwindles to nothing. |Even though it's just the two of you, she always takes the time to prepare a full course without fail; there are no rushed, quick meals in this household. One always sits and eats until one's warm and full inside, no exceptions.] Today, she's cooking congee, thick rice porridge — or at least, that's what it'll eventually be. Right now, the stock's simmering in the pot, a mixture of various mushrooms, bones and sauces, steam slowly rising out and up with an almost mystical sense of wonder to it. It's just like magic. There's also chickpeas, but that comes in with the rice. "Have you finished slicing the onions? The stock's almost ready." "Yes, Mama." She doesn't supervise you while you handle the knife these days. It's a small point of pride, but one nevertheless. "I don't think we have enough rice in the kitchen. Would you go out to the storehouse and get me the half-sack from last week?" [kiyoko.pregStage 2|Sighing, Mother rubs her aching back, offsetting the weight of her big, swollen belly. "I'd go get it myself, but..." ] You bow ever so slightly. "Yes, Mama." "Don't spill any, you hear me?" Mother's voice follows you out of the kitchen and into the dining hall as you make your exit. "Food is precious!" "I promise to get it all back, Mama!" You know the way well by now: out the front door, circle around to the side of the tree, into the door by its roots and down into the cellar. Mama says that cellars weren't really a thing in her homeland because earthquakes were really common, but the ground's much more stable in this part of the world and they picked up some things from the natives. Either way, cool darkness rushes up to greet you as you descend the stairs; you light a tiny blue flame with a snap of your fingers and set it to hover by your head before heading beneath the earth. So many things — dried persimmons, salt, garlic — but what you want is laid near the back of the room. Picking up the half-full rice sack is a bit of a struggle, but you make it out with the weighty thing in your arms. As you head back for the kitchen, though, you get the sensation that you're being watched — your ears are wiggling and twitching like mad, although you don't think you're in any danger. It's then that you spy it: a little speckled sparrow hopping through the freshly trimmed grass behind you, looking up hopefully at the sack in your arms. "Eh?" The sparrow chirps and flutters about. "Do you want some of this?" Almost as if understanding you, the little bird bobs its head. It chirps again, and two more sparrows swoop down from a nearby branch, huddling together in a small flock. Peeping and tweeting, they start hopping after you, looking every bit as hopeful as the first. It's clear that you're not going to be rid of these little creatures unless you give them a clear answer — what's it going to be?
rows.translation: 当母亲在厨房里搅拌锅中的食物时，一股股温暖的气味弥漫开来。 [kiyoko.numKits 2 8 16|她似乎总是在房子的这一部分表现得最好、最开心；她们的气场也非常契合。很明显，与你不同，母亲根本不认为喂饱你的肚子是一件负担；说实话，这让你有点嫉妒。 |午餐时间总是一件让人开心的事，主要是因为你可以对弟弟妹妹们发号施令。当然，如果出了什么问题，你也得承担责任，但为了获得“姐姐”这个光荣的头衔，这个代价其实并不高。即使没有真正吃到什么好东西，这个头衔也会让你感到内心暖洋洋的、非常开心。 |这份工作量确实很大——不仅要养活你们两个人，还要照顾所有的兄弟姐妹——但她在烹饪这个简单的过程中总是能感受到如此大的快乐，以至于这份工作的艰巨性在她的眼中就变得微不足道了。 |尽管只有你们两个人，她总是会花时间准备一顿丰盛的饭菜；在这个家里，从不会有什么匆忙草率地解决的餐食。每个人都会坐下来认真吃饭，直到自己感到温暖且吃饱为止，从来没有任何例外。] 今天，她正在煮粥——至少最终会变成粥。现在，各种蘑菇、骨头和调味料熬成的汤汁正在锅里慢慢炖煮，热气缓缓升起，营造出一种仿佛充满魔力的氛围。简直就像在变魔术一样。其中还加入了鹰嘴豆，不过这些食材会和米一起被煮进去。 你切好洋葱了吗？高汤差不多准备好了。 是的，妈妈。 这些天你使用刀具的时候，她并没有监督你。这虽然只是件小事，但总归是一件值得骄傲的事情。 我觉得厨房里的米不够用了。你能去仓库把上周剩下的那半袋米拿过来吗？ [kiyoko.pregStage 2|母亲叹了口气，轻轻揉着她那疼痛的背部，试图缓解自己那大而隆起的腹部的重量。 我本来想自己去拿的，但是…… ] 你微微鞠了一躬。 是的，妈妈。 千万不要弄洒了，听清楚了吗？ 当你走出厨房进入餐厅时，母亲的声音仍在你身后回荡。 食物是宝贵的！ 妈妈，我保证会把一切都弄回来！ 你现在应该已经很熟悉这条路了：从前门出去，绕到树旁，从树根处进入那扇门，然后下到地窖里。妈妈说，在她的家乡，地窖其实并不存在，因为那里经常发生地震；但这个地区的地面要稳定得多，所以他们从当地人那里学习了一些制作地窖的方法。 无论如何，当你走下楼梯时，清凉的黑暗会迎面扑来；你只需打个响指，就能点燃一小团蓝色的火焰，让它悬在你的头顶上方，然后继续朝着地底前进。 房间里摆放着许多东西——干柿子、盐、大蒜——但你真正想要的东西，被放在房间的最里面。 提起那个装了半袋米的袋子确实有点费劲，但你还是设法将它抱在了怀里。 然而，当你往厨房走去的路上，你突然感觉到有人在注视着你——你的耳朵不停地抽动着，尽管你并不认为自己处于任何危险之中。 就在这时，你看到了它：一只身上带着斑点的麻雀，在你身后刚修剪过的草丛中蹦来跳去，它满怀期待地抬头望着你怀中的那个袋子。 嗯？ 麻雀叽叽喳喳地叫着，飞来飞去。 你要来点这个吗？ 那只小鸟似乎真的理解了你的意思，它点了点头，又发出了一声鸣叫。紧接着，又有两只麻雀从附近的树枝上飞了下来，它们聚在一起，形成了一个小鸟群。这些小鸟一边窥视着你，一边发出鸣叫声，然后开始跟着你跳跃，它们的眼神中充满了与最初那只小鸟一样的期待。 显然，除非你给它们一个明确的答案，否则你是无法摆脱这些小生物的……你会选择什么呢？

It makes you feel all warm and good inside, even without having just eaten. |It's big — it has to be in order to feed not just the two of you, but all your brothers and sisters as well — but she always takes such joy in the simple act of cooking that the sheer magnitude of the act dwindles to nothing. |Even though it's just the two of you, she always takes the time to prepare a full course without fail; there are no rushed, quick meals in this household. One always sits and eats until one's warm and full inside, no exceptions.] Today, she's cooking congee, thick rice porridge — or at least, that's what it'll eventually be. Right now, the stock's simmering in the pot, a mixture of various mushrooms, bones and sauces, steam slowly rising out and up with an almost mystical sense of wonder to it. It's just like magic. There's also chickpeas, but that comes in with the rice. "Have you finished slicing the onions? The stock's almost ready." "Yes, Mama." She doesn't supervise you while you handle the knife these days. It's a small point of pride, but one nevertheless. "I don't think we have enough rice in the kitchen. Would you go out to the storehouse and get me the half-sack from last week?" [kiyoko.pregStage 2|Sighing, Mother rubs her aching back, offsetting the weight of her big, swollen belly. "I'd go get it myself, but..." ] You bow ever so slightly. "Yes, Mama." "Don't spill any, you hear me?" Mother's voice follows you out of the kitchen and into the dining hall as you make your exit. "Food is precious!" "I promise to get it all back, Mama!" You know the way well by now: out the front door, circle around to the side of the tree, into the door by its roots and down into the cellar. Mama says that cellars weren't really a thing in her homeland because earthquakes were really common, but the ground's much more stable in this part of the world and they picked up some things from the natives. Either way, cool darkness rushes up to greet you as you descend the stairs; you light a tiny blue flame with a snap of your fingers and set it to hover by your head before heading beneath the earth. So many things — dried persimmons, salt, garlic — but what you want is laid near the back of the room. Picking up the half-full rice sack is a bit of a struggle, but you make it out with the weighty thing in your arms. As you head back for the kitchen, though, you get the sensation that you're being watched — your ears are wiggling and twitching like mad, although you don't think you're in any danger. It's then that you spy it: a little speckled sparrow hopping through the freshly trimmed grass behind you, looking up hopefully at the sack in your arms. "Eh?" The sparrow chirps and flutters about. "Do you want some of this?" Almost as if understanding you, the little bird bobs its head. It chirps again, and two more sparrows swoop down from a nearby branch, huddling together in a small flock. Peeping and tweeting, they start hopping after you, looking every bit as hopeful as the first. It's clear that you're not going to be rid of these little creatures unless you give them a clear answer — what's it going to be?"

rows.original: You look back and forth between the sparrows and the woven sack in your arms, silently wishing the sparrows would just give up and go away so you don't have to make this choice. They don't. "All right, all right. Don't look so sad. Here, have some." You untie the sack, reach into its dry-smelling depths and draw out a handful of raw rice grains. Setting down your burden and squatting close to the ground, you hold it out to the little birds. "This is all I can give you, else Mama will notice." The sparrows don't need any further encouragement — all three of them surge forward in a flutter of wings, jostling at each other as they eat out of your hand. Their little beaks nip at your palm and fingers in their excitement, and it's not long before most of the rice is gone. You dust off your hands, scattering the remaining grains onto the grass, and the birds hop after them, pecking at the ground. Looking at them, you can't help but smile. Even if you did promise Mother... a handful of rice won't be missed, and the sparrows look so happy. Even if Mother somehow manages to find out and scolds you for wasting food on mere animals... it'll have been worth it. Picking up the sack once more, you head on back to the kitchen. Lunch isn't going to cook itself!
rows.translation: 你目光在那些麻雀和怀中的编织袋之间来回移动，心中默默地希望这些麻雀能放弃离开，这样你就不用做出这个选择了。 然而，它们并没有。 好了好了，别这么难过。来，吃点这个吧。 你解开袋子，将手部伸进袋子里面，从那里取出一把干巴巴的稻谷。放下手部中的负担，蹲在地面附近，然后将这些稻谷递给那些小鸟。 这就是我所能给你的了，否则妈妈会发现的。 这些麻雀根本不需要任何鼓励——三只鸟一起振翅飞了过来，一边抢着吃你手部里的食物，一边互相推挤。它们那小小的喙在兴奋中不停地啄你的手部掌和手部指，不一会儿，大部分米粒就已经被吃光了。 你拍掉手部上的灰尘，将剩下的米粒撒在草地上，那些鸟儿立刻飞过来，争相啄食那些米粒。 看着它们，你不禁笑了起来。即使你之前答应过妈妈……失去一把米也不会有什么大不了的，而这些麻雀看起来真是太开心了。 即使妈妈 somehow发现了这件事，然后因为你把食物浪费在那些动物身上而责骂你……那也是值得的。 你再次拿起那个袋子，朝着厨房走去。午餐总不能自己做饭吧！

rows.original: Feed the sparrows just a handful of rice. You know it'll be too little for Mother to notice.
rows.translation: 给那些麻雀喂一把米吧。你知道，这样的量妈妈根本不会注意到。
rows.raw: "Feed the sparrows just a handful of rice. You know it'll be too little for Mother to notice."

rows.original: "I can't give you any of my rice. I promised Mama I'd get it all to her." The sparrows just continue to look hopeful. "Please don't put me in a bind here. I really can't break a promise I made, even if it's a small one. Even if it's only a handful that wouldn't be missed. If I find an excuse to break a promise... I'm sure I'll find another one next time. Please don't make me do that." Flutter, flutter, peck, peck. "I'm so sorry... but I still won't give you any!" As much as it hurts you to do this, if you have to do this, you will. Steeling yourself, you raise a foot and stamp down on the grass perilously close to one of the sparrows; the little bird chirps in alarm and hops back. "Go away, okay? Just go away already! Stop bothering me!" Startled, the sparrows scatter, taking flight and seeking refuge in the nearest high branch. Well, you've made your choice, for good or for ill; even at this distance, you can still feel the little birds staring down at you. Let them stare all they like; it's at times when one thinks no one's watching or when a loss won't be missed that the true test of one's word comes to the fore. Now, back to the kitchen. Mother's going to have an earful for you if you don't hurry up!
rows.translation: 我没办法把我的米分给你。我答应过妈妈要把所有的米都给她。 那些麻雀依然显得充满希望。 请不要让我陷入这种两难境地。我真的无法违背自己做出的承诺，哪怕是再微小的承诺也好。即使只是那一点点、不会被任何人注意到的东西。如果我找到了一个借口来违背承诺……我相信下次我一定会再找到另一个借口。请不要逼我这么做。 扑腾，扑腾，啄啊啄啊。 我真的很抱歉……但我还是不会给你任何东西的！ 尽管这样做会让你感到痛苦，但如果你必须这么做，你就必须去做。你强忍住痛苦，抬起一只脚，重重地踩在那片草地上——而那片草地正好位于一只麻雀的附近；那只小鸟立刻发出惊恐的叫声，跳开了。 走开，好吗？赶紧离开吧！别再来打扰我了！ 受惊的小麻雀们四散飞开，纷纷躲到了附近的高树枝上寻求庇护。好吧，你已经做出了选择，无论结果是好是坏；即使距离这么远，你依然能感觉到那些小鸟正在注视着你。让它们看着吧……有时候，正是在人们以为没有人在注视自己、或者认为某个损失不会被注意到的时候，一个人承诺的诚意才会真正受到考验。 现在，回到厨房吧。如果你不快点，妈妈肯定会训你的！

I'm sure I'll find another one next time. Please don't make me do that." Flutter, flutter, peck, peck. "I'm so sorry... but I still won't give you any!" Stop bothering me!" Startled, the sparrows scatter, taking flight and seeking refuge in the nearest high branch. Let them stare all they like; it's at times when one thinks no one's watching or when a loss won't be missed that the true test of one's word comes to the fore. Now, back to the kitchen. Mother's going to have an earful for you if you don't hurry up!"

rows.original: Mother trusts you to get all of the rice back to the kitchen. You're not about to break your promise, even for a good reason.
rows.translation: 妈妈信任你，把所有的米都送回厨房。即使有再好的理由，你也不会违背自己的承诺吧。
rows.raw: "Mother trusts you to get all of the rice back to the kitchen. You're not about to break your promise, even for a good reason."

rows.original: Some time ago and somewhere else... It's been a great day in the forest so far. Since lunch, you've climbed several trees, swum in the stream, spotted an eel as thick as your leg and rolled downhill all the way from the gulley. Even though it seems like forever since you've gone out to play, you've still plenty of hours' worth of daylight remaining, if you've judged the sun's position correctly. Ehh... what to play now? [kiyoko.numKits 4|Sure, you could head back and get some of your siblings, but you don't really feel like going indoors at the moment. Besides, Mother might catch sight of you and saddle you with some task or the other...] It's then that it catches your eye: the most beautiful sweet potato plant you've ever seen growing in the wild. Growing on a little mound above the grasses and underbrush, illuminated by a patch of warm sunlight that's wormed through the maples and pines — it's a majestic sight to behold. The perfectly shaped arrow-headed leaves, the thick, lush vines, the sweet scent of sap rising from the plant itself, and it's even begun to flower with tiny purple-white buds. You haven't even begun to dig, and you already know this is going to be great. So you do. Foxes are no stranger to digging with their hands; the dirt is crumbly and gives way easily beneath your fingers. Within minutes, you've unearthed a lovely half-dozen wild tubers, slender and without blemish on their purple skin. Sweet potato. Oh, piping hot sweet potato. Sweet without any of the cloying ickiness that candy has, you can already taste them. All you'd need is to gather enough leaves to start a fire, a good skewer... maybe a bit of oil, but that'd mean going back to the house, and you don't want that. The more you look at the dirt-covered sweet potatoes dangling in your hand, the more you just want to get started already. Then again... You don't have to eat these now. Such perfect sweet potatoes... what a taste they promise to have once baked, but there's not much body to them; you'd have to have all six of them at once to feel warm and full inside like you love to be. But if you didn't eat them now... you could take the tubers back home, cut them up into slips and let them sprout. Then you could plant them... you wouldn't just have these six sweet potatoes, you'd have so many more! Enough for everyone to have some, probably! Then maybe you could work on making these more full-bodied and filling... Only one problem, though: growing sweet potatoes from slips would take months. Cross-breeding them and growing new plants from seeds would take even longer, and enough years would probably have passed by the time you'd made the truly perfect sweet potato. You wouldn't be a carefree girl any more, not with the frame of mind to bake sweet potatoes in leaves... or at least not with the wonder of a child. This most uncharacteristic thought is sobering. Little kitsune kits shouldn't have such notions. Either way... what to do now?
rows.translation: 很久以前，在另一个地方…… 今天在森林里真是度过了非常愉快的一天。从午餐后开始，你爬上了好几棵树，在小溪里游泳，还看到了一条有你大腿那么粗的鳗鱼，甚至还从沟壑里滚了下来。虽然感觉出去玩的时间似乎已经很久了，但如果你判断正确的话，现在天还亮着呢，还有很多时间可以继续玩耍呢。 呃……现在该玩什么呢？ [kiyoko.numKits 4|当然，你可以回去叫上你的兄弟姐妹们，但此刻你实在没有兴趣待在室内。再说，妈妈可能会看到你，然后派你去做这个或那个任务……] 就在这时，你的目光被它吸引了——那是你见过的最美丽的野生红薯植株。它生长在草丛和灌木丛上方的小土堆上，一片温暖的阳光穿透枫树和松树的枝叶，照在了它身上，使得这一景象显得格外壮观。那形状完美的箭头状叶子，茂密而坚韧的藤蔓，从植株本身散发出来的甜腻香气，甚至它已经开始绽放出那些紫白色的小花蕾……你甚至还没有开始挖掘，但就已经被它迷住了。 知道 这一定会非常有趣。 你试试看吧。狐妖们早就习惯了用爪子挖土；那些泥土松软易碎，在你的手部指下很容易就被挖开。短短几分钟内，你就挖出了半打漂亮的野生块茎，它们细长而结实，紫色的表皮上没有一点瑕疵。 红薯。哦，热气腾腾的红薯。它们的甜味毫不黏腻，也没有糖果那种令人不适的甜腻感，你只需采集足够的树叶生火，准备一根好的烤签……或许再加点油，但那样就得回到房子里去了，而你肯定不想那么做。 当你越看手部中那些被泥土覆盖的红薯，你就越迫不及待想要立刻开始动手部了。 不过，另一方面…… 你 不要 现在必须把这些吃掉。这些红薯实在太完美了……等烤熟后肯定会有美妙的口感，不过它们的肉质并不是很丰富；要想真正感受到那种暖洋洋、饱饱的满足感，恐怕得一口气吃掉六个才行。 但如果你现在不把它们吃掉的话……可以把这些块茎带回家，切成小段然后催芽。之后再把它们种下去……这样你得到的就不只是这六颗红薯了，还会有很多很多！足够让每个人都能分到一些呢！ 那么，也许你可以尝试让这些作物变得更加浓郁、更加能带来满足感…… 不过只有一个问题：用插条种植红薯需要花费数月的时间；而通过杂交育种、再用种子培育新的植株，所需的时间会更长。等到你最终成功培育出这些新品种时，可能已经过了很多年。 确实如此 完美的红薯啊……有了想要用叶子包裹红薯来烘烤的念头，你就再也不是那个无忧无虑的女孩了……至少不再拥有孩子般的纯真与好奇了。 这种完全不符合自己性格的想法，实在令人清醒。小狐妖本来就不应该有这样的想法啊……不管怎样……现在该怎么办呢？

rows.original: Ah, bother. All sorts of things could happen in between you planting the potatoes and the harvest months down the line. Weather. Bugs. Bratty little siblings. Mother making you share. Here and now, you've got a half-dozen sweet potatoes in your hand, and they promise to be the best-tasting snacks you've had all week. No, all month. You're going to gain weight, the annoying little voice of reason rings in the back of your mind. You ignore it. Children shouldn't care about gaining weight; you'll have plenty of time to worry about that when you're a young woman, if Mother's admonishments are any indication. Being in the middle of the forest, it doesn't take you very long to scrounge together a sizable pile of fallen leaves. Then it's off to the stream you were swimming in to wash off your find, plus get a handful of nice, water-smoothed rocks. You remember seeing a few while you were there... Odd how time flies when you're having fun, but before you know it, you've put it all together. Leaves over sweet potatoes within a ring of stones, and a couple nice long sticks for skewers. A bit of wood and tinder to get the fire going, and you set it all alight with a snap of your fingers. If there's anything that comes naturally to kitsune, it's fire magic. Heavy white smoke billows out from the small leaf pile, and you slowly add more dry leaves as time passes; taking one's time is crucial when baking sweet potatoes like this, else the outside gets charred and the insides get all icky. The oil would've been really nice, but you're confident in your ability to do this with nothing more than what you can scavenge up yourself. Time ticks by as you squat by the little firepit you've built, watching the leaves burn; to keep track of how long the potatoes have been baking, you sing a little rhyme in your head over and over again. By the thirtieth time, they'll be done... not that you can't smell that delicious aroma wafting out into the air with the smoke. Just being in the vicinity makes you painfully aware of how long it's been since you ate, far too long. You turn over the sweet potatoes every now and then, making sure they're evenly baked, then settle back with a happy sigh. Eventually, though, time's up and they're done. Sweet potatoes... such sweet simplicity, and the sight that greets you as you pull the skewers out of the leaf fire is glorious. Spots of soot stain the purple skins here and there, but the yellow-white flesh is untouched, yet soft and starchy. You pick up the most appetising one on its skewer, blow on it for a while to help it cool, then take a small bite. It's so good, you could start crying; it's almost as good as having your head and tail petted at the same time. [kiyoko.numKits 4| While some of your siblings like to put honey or butter on their baked potatoes, whyever would you do such a thing? Why would you adulterate such wonderful taste and texture with... with... oh, it hurts to just think about it! ] Only the prospect of burning your tongue keeps you from scarfing down the entire thing like some kind of rabid creature; since you're forced to eat slowly, you close your eyes and concentrate on the act of chewing, of the joy that's been sparked on your tongue, of the sigh after you swallow, only to repeat it all over again... Of course. [kiyoko.numKits 4|"Only Kinu nee-sama would be able to be so happy with a sweet potato." That's what they'd say. Well, you have yours now, and frankly, is it that bad to savour life's little pleasures that much? It makes it so much easier to be happy and thankful with less.] Sweet potato. Oh, piping hot sweet potato. Before you know it, all the yellow-white flesh has disappeared into your tummy, but you still want more. The skin is still warm and you're tempted to eat that too, but there're still five more of the slender wild tubers waiting for your whole and undivided attention. Mother's going to yell at you for ruining your appetite for dinner... Gluttony might be a sin, but with something this good you're sure that Lord Keros will forgive you given the extraordinary circumstances. Maybe you should save one of these as an offering, as difficult as it'll be. In the meantime, though... turning your attention to the next baked potato on the skewer, you lick your lips and prepare to dig in. That sensation of feeling all warm and good inside... oh, you missed it so much.
rows.translation: 啊，真是麻烦。从你种下土豆到几个月后收获，期间可能会发生各种各样的事情：天气变化、害虫侵袭，还有那些调皮的小兄弟姐妹，甚至妈妈还会让你分享食物。而此刻，你手里拿着半打红薯，它们绝对会成为你这周——不，是这整个月来最美味的零食。 你会变胖的。 你脑海中总会响起那个烦人的理性声音。但你选择忽略它——孩子们根本不应该担心体重问题；你以后还有足够的时间去为此烦恼。 那个 当你还是个年轻女孩的时候，如果母亲们的告诫能说明什么的话…… 既然身处森林之中，你很快就能收集到一大堆落叶。然后，你就会前往你之前游泳的那条小溪，把收集到的落叶冲洗干净，同时再捡一些表面光滑、被水冲得圆润的石头。你记得当时在那里的时候确实看到过几块这样的石头…… 时间在欢乐中过得真是飞快，不知不觉间，你就已经把所有东西都准备齐全了——用石头围成一个圈，把红薯和树叶放在里面，再准备几根长棍子用来串烤。再找些木头和引火物，轻轻一捻手指，火就燃起来了。 对狐妖来说，没有什么比火系魔法更得心应手了。当那些干树叶被点燃后，浓重的白烟便袅袅升起。随着时间的推移，你会慢慢添加更多的干树叶——在这种制作红薯的方法中，耐心是至关重要的，否则外皮就会烤焦，而内部则会变得黏糊糊的，一点都不好吃。 那种油本来会非常有用，但你有信心仅凭自己能收集到的材料就能完成这项任务。 时间一分一秒地流逝，你蹲在自己搭建的小火堆旁，注视着燃烧的树叶；为了记录土豆烘烤了多久，你不断在脑海中重复着那句小谣曲。等到第三十次重复的时候，土豆应该就烤好了……虽然你也说不准到底要多久。 气味 那种美妙的香气随着烟雾飘荡在空气中。仅仅站在附近，你就会清楚地意识到自己已经有多久没有吃东西了——实在太久了。你不时地翻动那些红薯，确保它们能够均匀受热，然后满意地叹了口气，放松下来。 然而，时间终究到了，他们的工作也完成了。红薯……如此纯粹而美好，当你将烤肉串从火中取出时，呈现在眼前的景象实在令人赞叹。紫色的红薯皮上偶尔会沾上一些烟灰，但那黄白色的果肉却完好无损，依然柔软且富含淀粉。 你拿起串在烤肉签上最诱人那块，吹一会儿让它凉快些，然后轻轻咬一小口。 简直太美味了，吃到眼泪都快出来了；这种味道简直比……还要棒。 以及 尾巴也同时摆动着。 [kiyoko.numKits 4| 虽然你们有些兄弟姐妹喜欢在烤土豆上涂蜂蜜或黄油，但究竟为什么呢 你 为什么要做出这种事呢？为什么要把如此美妙的口感和风味破坏掉，用……用……哦，光是想到这一点就让人难受。 思考 快行动吧！ ] 只有想到会烫到舌头这种恐惧，才能让你不会像某种疯狂的生物一样狼吞虎咽地吃光所有东西；因为你必须慢慢咀嚼，所以你会闭上眼睛，专注于咀嚼的过程，专注于那种在舌头上引发的愉悦感，以及吞下食物后所感受到的满足……然后，这一切又会重新开始…… 当然。 [kiyoko.numKits 4|只有绮奴 nee-sama才会因为一个红薯而如此开心。 他们就是会这么说。不过，现在你有了自己的选择，说实话，过分追求生活中的小乐趣，真的有那么糟糕吗？这样，即使拥有得不多，也会让我们更容易感到幸福和满足。] 红薯。哦，热气腾腾的红薯。还没等你反应过来，那些黄白色的果肉就已经全都进入了你的肚子，但你还是想再吃一些。红薯皮依然温热，你甚至忍不住想把它们也吃掉，不过还有五颗这样的细长红薯在等着你全心全意的品尝呢。 妈妈会因为你破坏了自己吃晚餐的胃口而责骂你的…… 虽然暴食可能是一种罪过，但面对这么美味的食物，考虑到这种特殊情况，凯罗斯大人肯定会原谅你的。 也许你应该把其中一个留下来作为祭品，尽管这会相当困难。不过，在此之前……把注意力转移到烤土豆上吧，你舔了舔嘴唇，准备大快朵颐。那种让人感到全身温暖、心情愉悦的感觉，真是太美妙了。.. 哦，你真的错过了太多啊。
rows.raw: " Ah, bother. All sorts of things could happen in between you planting the potatoes and the harvest months down the line. Weather. Bugs. Bratty little siblings. Mother making you share. Here and now, you've got a half-dozen sweet potatoes in your hand, and they promise to be the best-tasting snacks you've had all week. No, all month. You're going to gain weight, the annoying little voice of reason rings in the back of your mind. You ignore it. Children shouldn't care about gaining weight; you'll have plenty of time to worry about that when you're a young woman, if Mother's admonishments are any indication. Being in the middle of the forest, it doesn't take you very long to scrounge together a sizable pile of fallen leaves. Then it's off to the stream you were swimming in to wash off your find, plus get a handful of nice, water-smoothed rocks. You remember seeing a few while you were there... Odd how time flies when you're having fun, but before you know it, you've put it all together. Leaves over sweet potatoes within a ring of stones, and a couple nice long sticks for skewers. A bit of wood and tinder to get the fire going, and you set it all alight with a snap of your fingers. If there's anything that comes naturally to kitsune, it's fire magic. Heavy white smoke billows out from the small leaf pile, and you slowly add more dry leaves as time passes; taking one's time is crucial when baking sweet potatoes like this, else the outside gets charred and the insides get all icky. The oil would've been really nice, but you're confident in your ability to do this with nothing more than what you can scavenge up yourself. Time ticks by as you squat by the little firepit you've built, watching the leaves burn; to keep track of how long the potatoes have been baking, you sing a little rhyme in your head over and over again. By the thirtieth time, they'll be done... not that you can't smell that delicious aroma wafting out into the air with the smoke. Just being in the vicinity makes you painfully aware of how long it's been since you ate, far too long. You turn over the sweet potatoes every now and then, making sure they're evenly baked, then settle back with a happy sigh. Eventually, though, time's up and they're done. Sweet potatoes... such sweet simplicity, and the sight that greets you as you pull the skewers out of the leaf fire is glorious. Spots of soot stain the purple skins here and there, but the yellow-white flesh is untouched, yet soft and starchy. You pick up the most appetising one on its skewer, blow on it for a while to help it cool, then take a small bite. It's so good, you could start crying; it's almost as good as having your head and tail petted at the same time. [kiyoko.numKits 4| While some of your siblings like to put honey or butter on their baked potatoes, whyever would you do such a thing? Why would you adulterate such wonderful taste and texture with... with... oh, it hurts to just think about it! ] Only the prospect of burning your tongue keeps you from scarfing down the entire thing like some kind of rabid creature; since you're forced to eat slowly, you close your eyes and concentrate on the act of chewing, of the joy that's been sparked on your tongue, of the sigh after you swallow, only to repeat it all over again... Of course. [kiyoko.numKits 4|"Only Kinu nee-sama would be able to be so happy with a sweet potato." That's what they'd say. Well, you have yours now, and frankly, is it that bad to savour life's little pleasures that much? It makes it so much easier to be happy and thankful with less.] Sweet potato. Oh, piping hot sweet potato. Before you know it, all the yellow-white flesh has disappeared into your tummy, but you still want more. The skin is still warm and you're tempted to eat that too, but there're still five more of the slender wild tubers waiting for your whole and undivided attention. Mother's going to yell at you for ruining your appetite for dinner... Gluttony might be a sin, but with something this good you're sure that Lord Keros will forgive you given the extraordinary circumstances. Maybe you should save one of these as an offering, as difficult as it'll be. In the meantime, though... turning your attention to the next baked potato on the skewer, you lick your lips and prepare to dig in. That sensation of feeling all warm and good inside... oh, you missed it so much."

rows.original: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush. Cook up these beauties and eat them.
rows.translation: 一鸟在手，胜过二鸟在林。把这些美味的食物做出来吃掉吧。
rows.raw: "A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush. Cook up these beauties and eat them."

rows.original: You take a long, hard look at the half-dozen sweet potatoes hanging from your grubby hand, a tightness welling up in the pit of your stomach. Sure, anything could happen in the months in between planting and harvest: bugs, heavy rain, [kiyoko.numKits 4|annoying little siblings, ]hungry pregnant mothers. To be sure would be to bake these on the spot and stuff yourself until you're sticky to the eyebrows, but the payoff should you manage to see this through... Like you read in those stuffy old books, civilization entails doing things you don't want to because they're necessary. Besides, as delicious as these sweet potatoes promise to be, they're lacking a certain fullness of body. With some keeping, you think you might be able to fix that... The mere thought of big and plump sweet potatoes baked in an oven or in leaves, with that taste, instead of these slender things... it's more than enough to tempt any old fox. Or maybe you could slice the lot and steam them with rice... Aaaah! Is this what you want to be known for when you become a young woman? The girl who spent her childhood creating the perfect sweet potato? Yes! You get so giggly and giddy at the prospect that you have to sit down on a nearby rock and catch your breath. Oh dear oh dear oh dear. Right, right. You have to get these home posthaste; the faster you do it, the better the chance you'll get more sproutlings from each root. All right, all right. Steady, now. Put one foot in front of the other, don't fall over, and think about going home. As expected, you haven't walked so much as ten minutes before the familiar sight of home draws into view. You've got to get to the kitchen, get the knife and clear the greens from the tubers and roots, then find a nice nursery planter to let them sprout in. Then you'll have to see to clearing the garden ahead of time, since the vines will need plenty of space — "Kinu, what are you doing? And why are you carrying that stool? I hope you're not intending to climb somewhere you're not supposed to be." Ehhhh... Mother could be bad news. "I'm getting the knife, Mama." "And why do you need the —" Mother's eyes dart between your filthy, dirt-smeared clothes, the stool in one hand, and the sweet potato plant in your hand, vines, leaves, roots and all. Raising her hand to rub her temples, she sighs. "And here I was thinking you were playing outdoors. All right, I'll get the knife, but you're only using it while I'm watching. Didn't you think to just ask me instead of climbing up the cupboard to get it?" "The idea never crossed my mind, Mama." "I —" Mother opens her mouth to say something, then shakes her head and folds her ears downwards. "No, you aren't stupid; you're smarter than that. So that just leaves being plain silly, or — you know what? Never mind, let's just do this." Under Mother's supervision, you cut off the greens, which she takes away to wash for dinner later. Then it's on outside to the garden and planter, which you half fill with water from the well; one by one, all half-dozen tubers end up half-submerged, held in place by bits and pieces of old chopsticks you've cobbled together. Then it's off to prepare the soil; the plot'll be needed in a handful of days when the tubers start sprouting and you're to transplant the slips... Kneeling on cool dirt with warm sun beating down upon you, drinking in the light while surrounded by the rustle of leaves and green growing things — any regret you might've had at not cooking up the sweet potatoes and eating them on the spot is washed away by the simple, repetitive labor. A simple hand hoe does the heavy lifting of preparing the earth, but it feels so much better to dig with your fingers like a fox ought to. The soil's got to be loose for sweet potatoes to grow as big as they can. Mother's been hovering over you all this while, watching you work. "You really like this, don't you, Kinu?" "Ehehehe. It's almost as good as cooking and eating the final result, Mama." Something flickers in Mother's eyes, something about the slant of her ears — what did you say something wrong again? Eh, whatever. Mother's in one of her moods again[kiyoko.pregStage 1| — she sometimes gets this way when she's got a kit in her tummy —|,] and you're not about to let it ruin your good mood. Sweet potato, sweet potato, piping — hot — sweet — potato — Mother just shakes her head at your singing and steps away. "All right, then. I've got other things to do today, so I'll just leave you to it. Take a good bath before you head back in, you're filthy from head to toe and there's dirt stuck in your tails. I'm not having a wild animal in the house." "Yes, Mama." Sweet potato, sweet potato, piping — hot — sweet — potato — This is going to be great.
rows.translation: 你仔细地看了看自己那双脏兮兮的手上挂着的半打红薯，顿时感到胃里一阵发紧。当然，在从播种到收获的这段时间里，任何事情都可能发生：虫害、暴雨 [kiyoko.numKits 4|烦人的小弟弟妹妹们， ]饥饿的孕妇们……真是令人心疼。 当然可以。 最好的办法就是当场把这些烤出来，然后大吃特吃，吃到眉毛都粘在一起为止。不过，如果你能坚持做下去，得到的回报一定会值得的…… 就像你在那些陈旧的书里读到的那样，文明意味着要做那些你并不想做，但却必不可少的事情。另外，尽管这些红薯看起来非常美味，但它们的口感还是有些欠缺。如果你能多保存一些，或许就能改善这个问题…… 一想到那些又大又胖的红薯被放在烤箱里或者用叶子包裹着烘烤出来，那种美味的滋味……与这些细长型的红薯相比，这种诱惑力简直足以让任何狐狸都动心。或者，也可以把它们切成片，和米饭一起蒸着吃…… 啊啊啊！难道这就是你长大后想要别人记住你的样子吗？那个从小就致力于制作完美红薯的女孩？ 是的！ 一想到这个，你就忍不住笑得前仰后合，甚至不得不坐在附近的石头上喘口气。哦天啊，真的得赶紧把这些带回家才行；你行动得越快，每个根系长出更多幼苗的机会就越大。 好了，好了。慢慢来，一步一个脚印地走，别摔倒了，想着要回家吧。果然，还没走十分钟，熟悉的家园景象就已经出现在眼前了。你得先去厨房，拿把刀把那些块茎和根茎上的叶子清理干净，然后找一个合适的育苗盆让它们发芽生长。接下来，你还得提前把花园整理好，因为这些藤蔓需要足够的空间来生长呢。 纪夫，你在干什么？为什么拿着那把凳子？希望你不会打算去一些不该去的地方吧。 呃……妈妈带来的消息可能不太好。 妈妈，我去拿刀来。 那你为什么需要这个—— 母亲的目轻型在你的那件脏兮兮、沾满泥土的衣服、你手中拿着的凳子，以及你手中的那株红薯苗之间来回移动——包括那些藤蔓、叶子、根茎等等。她抬起手揉了揉太阳穴，然后叹了口气。 我还以为你是在外面玩呢。好吧，我去拿刀，但你只能在我看着的时候使用它。你难道没想过可以直接 询问 为什么不是我去把那个东西从橱柜里拿出来呢？ 妈妈，我从来没想过这个主意。 我—— 母亲张开嘴想说些什么，但随后又摇了摇头，把耳朵耷了下来。 不，你并不傻，你比那要聪明得多。那么，就只剩下两种可能了：要么是纯粹的愚蠢行为，要么就是……算了，我们还是继续做这件事吧。 在母亲的监督下，你把那些绿叶摘下来，母亲会把它们拿去清洗，用来做晚饭。然后，这些食材就被拿到外面的花园和种植箱里，你用井里的水把种植箱灌满一半；一个接一个，那六块块茎都被浸在水中，而它们则被你用一些旧筷子拼凑起来的小支架固定在那里。 接下来就是准备土壤了；再过几天，当块茎开始发芽时，就需要这块土壤来移植幼苗了…… 跪在凉爽的泥土上，温暖的阳轻型洒在身上，周围是树叶的沙沙声和正在生长的绿色植物，这种简单的、重复性的劳动让之前那些没有把红薯煮熟当场吃掉的遗憾都烟消云散了。 虽然一把简单的手锄就能完成翻土这项繁重的工作，但用手指像狐狸一样挖土，那种感觉确实要好得多。只有让土壤保持疏松的状态，红薯才能长得又大又甜。 这段时间，妈妈一直都在你身边，看着你工作。 你真的很喜欢这个，对吧，绮奴？ 嘿嘿嘿，这感觉简直和亲自烹饪然后品尝最终成果一样棒呢，妈妈。 母亲的眼中闪过一丝轻型芒，她耳朵的形状似乎也发生了一些变化……你刚才说什么来着？又说错什么了吗？ 唉，算了。母亲又进入她那种情绪状态了。[kiyoko.pregStage 1| — 当她肚子里“装着一套装备”时，她有时就会变成这样 —|,] 你肯定不会让它毁掉一切的。 你的 好心情。红薯，红薯，热乎乎的红薯…… 妈妈只是摇摇头，然后走开了。 好吧，那我就先走了。今天我还有其他事情要处理，所以就留给你们自己处理吧。回去之前好好洗个澡，你们从头到脚都脏兮兮的，尾巴里还沾满了灰尘。我可不想家里到处都是野生动物。 是的，妈妈。 红薯，红薯，热乎乎的红薯…… 这一定会很棒。 很棒.

rows.original: Take the sweet potatoes home and plant them. You'll have more in the future.
rows.translation: 把这些红薯带回家种吧，以后就能有更多的了。
rows.raw: "Take the sweet potatoes home and plant them. You'll have more in the future."

rows.original: Some time ago and somewhere else... It's one of those days again, a warm, sunny day when you don't want to do anything but lie in the sun. You know you ought to be doing something more constructive with your precious free time, but all the energy has fled your limbs and you don't want to move, save for your tails swishing idly as you lie belly-down on the bench. You've set up a go board just in front of your chin, but playing against yourself gets boring fast... "[silly|Nee-Sama|Big Sis]?" One of your ears swivels towards the voice. A shadow falls over you, short and thin. Tilting your head, you roll your gaze upwards to meet your little brother's. "[silly|Nee-Sama|Big Sis]? Are you awake?" "Eh?" Even on a day like this, Tatsumi's wrapped up well. You don't like the cold either — no one in your family does, except maybe your [pc.mf|father|mother] — but your little brother's always been extra sensitive to chills. Summer might be the only time of year when he doesn't bundle up, even though he doesn't trim his coat after winter... Reaching out, Tatsumi grabs you by the shoulder and pushes you back and forth. "C'mon, wake up, [silly|Nee-Sama|Big Sis]!" "Mmmmh." The effort involved in sitting up is monumental, as if someone had tied boulders to your arms and legs. "What's the matter, Tatsumi? Do you want to play go with me?" Your little brother visibly recoils at that, holding out his hands in front of him as if intending to shield himself from a savage blow, terrified fox noises escaping his lips as his ears turn downward. "No..." "Then? What's the matter?" It takes a little while for Tatsumi to calm his nerves enough for him to speak coherently again, but you're a patient creature. "Well, it's my scarf, the one you gave me some time ago..." Some time... must have been years ago now. You were really little then, and Tatsumi was even more so. The memory is faint, even though children are supposed to remember things better than grown-ups, right? Certainly you weren't that young... Yeah, you should've noticed it earlier. He's not wearing it today... he's always wearing that scarf. "What about it?" "Um, well." Your little brother shuffles about on his feet. "It's starting to go... can you darn up a hole or two for me? I can't go to Mama for that, she'll just tell me to throw it out and I don't want to do that." "Hmm. Let me see it." Tatsumi glances around guiltily, perhaps looking for any trace of your mother. When there's none, he reaches behind him and pulls out the long piece of thick purple fabric, handing it to you. Sighing softly, you take the worn old thing in your hands and give it a look-over. Well damn. When Tatsumi said this was starting to go, he made an immense understatement. The cloth isn't just worn, it's started to go all hole-y. It's been washed so many times, the color's started to run... that, and the repeated applications of dirt, sap and sweat have conspired to make the purple uneven, to put it lightly. It's a small miracle that moths haven't already gotten to it, if anything. At least it's regularly washed, so it doesn't smell... A better garment would have lasted longer, but this was one of your early creations. Just looking at it makes you a little embarrassed... "Eh, is there any reason you want to save this scarf? It's not that I can't fix it, but it would be a lot easier to get a new one." "You gave it to me..." A lantern lights in your head. "Ah, so it has sentimental value for you, is that it?" "Sen-ti...?" "What I'm saying is, it means a lot to you, right?" Tatsumi nods so fast his head's a blur. Keros' tails, he's still a little kid... but you suppose you can't expect anything else, can I? Still, what should you do about this? Tatsumi really likes his scarf, true, and it would be pretty mean for you to take it away from him even if it's for a good reason. You, too, can understand that people can have deep attachments for things that look simple on the surface. On the other hand, you can't just let him grow overly attached to an object like this. He's got to properly understand what it is that's important... Eh, what to do, what to do... "[silly|Nee-Sama|Big Sis]?"
rows.translation: 很久以前，在另一个地方…… 又是一个这样的日子——温暖而阳光明媚，你根本不想做任何事，只想躺在阳光下休息。你知道自己应该利用这段宝贵的空闲时间去做一些更有意义的事情，但你的四肢仿佛失去了所有的力气，根本不想动弹；唯一能做的，就是仰面躺在长椅上，让尾巴闲散地摆动着。你就在下巴前面放了一个棋盘，但和自己对战很快就变得无聊起来…… "[silly|妮萨玛|大姐]?" 你的其中一只耳朵自动转向了那个声音传来的方向。一道阴影投了下来，那道阴影又短又细。你微微歪着头，将目光向上移，与弟弟的目光对上了。 "[silly|妮萨玛|大姐]你醒了吗？ 嗯？ 即使是在这样的日子里，龙美也把自己裹得严严实实。你也不喜欢寒冷吧——你家里没有人喜欢寒冷，也许除了你的 [pc.mf|父亲|母亲] 但是你弟弟对寒冷总是特别敏感。夏天可能是他一年中唯一不会裹得严严实实的时候，尽管冬天的毛皮他也不会修剪……” 龙美伸出手部，抓住你的肩膀，轻轻地将你推来推去。 快醒醒吧， [silly|妮萨玛|大姐]!" 嗯…… 要坐起来所需要付出的努力实在巨大，就好像有人在你四肢上绑上了沉重的巨石一样。 怎么了，龙美？想和我一起下围棋吗？ 你弟弟看到这一幕明显吓了一跳，他双手部在身前摊开，仿佛想要挡住某次猛烈的攻击；他的耳朵耷了下来，嘴里还不停地发出惊恐的叫声。 不…… 然后呢？怎么了？ 过了一会儿，龙司才终于平静下来，能够再次条理清晰地说话了——你真是个有耐心的家伙。 嗯，这是我的围巾，就是你前段时间送给我的那条…… 那应该是很多年前的事了。那时你还很小，而龙美更是小得可怜。那些记忆已经变得模糊不清了——虽然一般来说，孩子们应该比成年人记得更清楚才对吧？你肯定也记不清了。 那个 年轻…… 是啊，你早该注意到的。他今天没有戴它……他 总是 戴着那条围巾。 那又怎样？ 嗯，好吧。 你的弟弟正摇摇晃晃地站着。 它开始坏了……你能帮我挖一两个洞吗？我不能去找妈妈帮忙，她只会让我把东西扔掉，而我可不想那么做。 嗯，让我看看吧。 龙美内疚地环顾四周，似乎在寻找你母亲的任何踪迹。当一无所获时，他从身后拿出一大块厚厚的紫色布料，递给了你。你轻轻叹了口气，接过这件破旧的衣服仔细端详起来。 真是见鬼了。当龙美说这块布料开始损坏的时候，他其实大大低估了实际情况。这块布料不仅被反复穿着，还出现了很多破洞；由于被洗得太多次，颜色也已经开始褪色……更糟糕的是，污垢、树液和汗水的反复侵蚀，使得这块紫色布料变得参差不齐，用轻描淡写的说法来说，就是已经彻底损坏了。 如果没有什么其他害虫的话，蛾子还没有侵蚀它，已经算是小小的奇迹了。至少这件衣物会定期被清洗，所以也没有发臭…… 一件质量更好的衣物本来可以使用更久，但这件毕竟是你早期制作的作品之一。 光是看着它，就会让人感到有点尴尬…… 呃，你为什么非得保存这条围巾呢？其实我完全可以把它修好，但买一条新的的话，肯定会更方便吧。 是你把它给我的…… 你的脑海中突然浮现出一个念头。 啊，所以这对你来说具有情感价值，是吗？ 森-蒂……？ 我的意思是，这对你来说意义重大，对吧？ 龙司连连点头，头都快晃成了一团模糊。 凯罗斯的尾巴……他还只是个小孩子而已……不过，我想也没什么别的办法了吧，对吧？不过，面对这种情况，你到底应该怎么做呢？诚然，龙司真的很喜欢那条围巾，如果因为某个正当理由而拿走它，未免也太残忍了。 你也可以理解，人们往往会对那些表面上看似简单的东西产生深厚的感情。不过，你不能让他对这样的物品产生过度的依赖。他必须真正明白什么才是真正重要的东西。.. 呃，该怎么办呢…… "[silly|妮萨玛|大姐]?"

rows.original: You consider what you're about to do, then thin your lips. This is something that has to be done for Tatsumi's good. Leaning forward, you grab your little brother's cheeks with both hands and force his eyes to meet yours. "I think you should throw away the scarf. Not just because it's getting too old and threadbare to be mended any more, but also because you're getting your priorities wrong." "I-I don't understand. Didn't [silly|Nee-Sama|Big Sis] give me this scarf? I —" Time to nip the situation in the bud before it spins out of control. "Look, Tatsumi. You like this scarf because I was the one who made it for you, right?" He nods, blinking back tears. "You wouldn't have placed so much importance on it if it weren't me who had given it to you, right?" "N-no?" "Then you're placing the wrong emphasis on things. It's not the scarf that's important in and of itself, it's the feelings between us as siblings which it represents that's important. Don't ever mistake one for the other or get things wrong... and a big sister who cares for her little siblings makes sure they dress properly. I'll make you a new scarf, Tatsumi, and it'll be as good as this one, because it's not the threads that matter, it's the bonds, and that hasn't changed." Tatsumi just stares at you unblinkingly, and you know he's trying desperately to understand you, but coming up short. No points are given for effort, but if they were, he'd be scoring high. Shaking your head with a smile, you let go of your little brother's cheeks and take hold of his hand. "Come on. Help me pack up the go board, and we can head back into the house." "Where are we going?" "To make you a new scarf, of course. What color do you want?"
rows.translation: 你仔细考虑着自己即将要做的事情，然后抿紧了嘴唇。为了龙司的好，这件事必须得做。你向前倾身，用双手部抓住弟弟的脸颊，迫使他的目光与自己的对视。 我觉得你应该把这条围巾扔掉。不仅仅是因为它已经破旧到无法再修补了，更因为你的优先事项搞反了。 我……我不明白。难道不是 [silly|妮萨玛|大姐] 把这个围巾给我好吗？我—— 现在是时候在事情失控之前将其扼杀在萌芽状态了。 看，龙美。你喜欢这条围巾，是因为是我为你制作的，对吧？ 他点了点头，强忍着泪水没有让它们流出来。 如果不是我给了你这个东西，你也不会这么重视它吧？ 不……不？ 那么你把重点放在了错误的地方。重要的并不是围巾本身，而是它所象征的我们兄妹之间的感情。千万不要把两者混为一谈，否则就会犯错……而一个关心弟弟妹妹的姐姐，一定会确保他们穿得妥当。我会为你重新织一条围巾，Tatsumi，它会和这条一样好，因为重要的不是线材，而是我们之间的感情，而这一点永远不会改变。 龙美只是直直地注视着你，一言不发，而你 知道 他正在拼命努力去理解你，但却始终未能成功。虽然努力本身并不会带来任何奖励，但如果真的有奖励的话，他的分数肯定很高。 你微笑着摇了摇头，松开了弟弟的脸颊，然后握住了他的手部。 来吧，帮我把棋盘收拾好，然后我们就可以回屋去了。 我们要去哪里？ 当然，我会为你制作一条新的围巾。你想要什么颜色呢？
