rows.original: "So," Gweyr eventually says after a moment's pause to let the story sink in. "That's what happened. Am I a monster, [pc.name]?"
rows.translation: 所以，”格温尔在稍作停顿，让听众有时间消化这个故事之后，终于开口说道，“事情就是这样的。我是不是一个怪物 [pc.name]?"
rows.raw: '\n            "So," Gweyr eventually says after a moment\'s pause to let the story sink in. "That\'s what happened. Am I a monster, [pc.name]?"'

rows.original:
You can't deny that she did some monstrous things, that's true. Killing more than half of fledgeling Hawkethorne's youth in one night — that's a monstrous deed, to be sure. But whether it makes her a monster or not... she may be a necessary monster if you're going to dismantle Tollus's cult. She hasn't crossed that line.
            
                "I guess that's about as good as an answer I'm getting," Gweyr says with a sigh. "Well then, [pc.name]... if you're still in despite knowing everything I've done, talk to me about the matter again in an hour or two. For now, I think I just want to have a little time to myself."
rows.translation:
你不得不承认，她确实做了一些极其残忍的事情，这是事实。在一个晚上就杀害了鹰棘镇家族中超过一半的年轻成员——这无疑是一桩残忍至极的罪行。但究竟这是否意味着她本身就是一个怪物……如果你想摧毁托卢斯的邪教组织，那么她或许就是那个必须被利用的“怪物”。她并没有越过那条界限。

“我想，这应该算是我得到的最合理的答案了吧，”格温尔叹了口气说道，“那么，就这样吧。 [pc.name]……如果你在知道我做过的一切之后仍然愿意继续和我在一起，那么一两个小时后再和我谈谈这件事吧。现在，我想我只是需要一些属于自己的时间。

rows.original: This must be how Tollus and Leold escaped. Flee yourself, before it's too late!
rows.translation: 看来托卢斯和莱奥德就是这么逃走的。快逃吧，否则就太晚了！
rows.raw: "This must be how Tollus and Leold escaped. Flee yourself, before it's too late!"

rows.original: As you step through the old jotun halls, a chill runs down your spine. Something is very, very wrong here... "Look alive!" Gweyr says, a scowl on her face. "They're coming." The cultists are coming at you from behind pillars and from the shadows, eyes set with fanatical fury, legs pumping tirelessly as they dash towards you. No rest for the [pc.isDK|wicked|brave], alas — you have barely enough time to recover and hold your [pc.weapon] at the ready before battle is joined. The hows and whys can wait — here and now, you've got business to deal with. It's a fight!
rows.translation: 当你穿过那些古老的巨人之厅时，一阵寒意顺着脊椎传了下来。这里肯定出了什么大问题…… “快躲起来！”格温尔面带怒容说道，“他们来了。” 那些邪教徒们正从柱子后面以及阴影中朝你冲来，他们眼中燃烧着狂热的怒火，双腿不停地奔跑着，朝着你猛扑过来。这些人根本不会休息 [pc.isDK|邪恶的|勇敢的]唉——你几乎根本没有足够的时间来恢复体力，也没有足够的时间来保持 [pc.weapon] 在战斗开始之前，必须做好充分的准备。各种原因和细节可以稍后再考虑——此刻，你首要的任务就是完成手头的工作。 这是一场激烈的战斗！

rows.original: Carefully, you make your way across the ancient stone bridge, following Gweyr's lead. The tiles underfoot are wet and slick with water and moss, and every now and then you find yourself stepping into a puddle you didn't know was there, kicking up water and sending small creatures scurrying out of your way. There doesn't seem to be any sign of Tollus's cultists yet, though... Thing is, you've put so much of yourself into looking around that you've neglected to pay attention to what's going on underfoot. Even though Gweyr makes a slow yet steady pace, tapping her path with the haft of her spear all the time, she must've weakened the bridge or something when she first passed over it. When you follow in her footsteps, splashing into one of the small pools where water dripping from the ceiling has gathered, an ominous crunching and grinding sounds from underfoot, muffled by the damp and wet all about you. Still, it's enough for Gweyr to whirl around[party.hasCompanions | and for [party.som||[comp1.name]|[comp1.name] and [comp2.name]] to leap back ], the old wolfess' hand outstretched as the ancient bricks crumble beneath your feet. Jagged chunks of masonry break free from the underside of the bridge, falling away into the dark water beneath with large splashes; you only barely manage to close your fingers about Gweyr's before the ground below you gives way. [pc.hasWings |You flap your wings desperately for all the good they're going to do you from a sudden standing start, but better something that nothing... | ] Even with Gweyr holding onto you, gravity still drags you forward against the rough, jagged edges in the newly-made hole in the bridge, scraping at your chin and arms. It's a second or two of heart-pounding and gut-wrenching terror before you've realized that everything's stabilized... even if it's with your legs dangling out over a perilous drop into open water. Slowly, Gweyr pulls you up[party.hasCompanions | with [party.compNames true]'s aid ], grunting with effort as she hauls you up and over the edge onto firm ground once more. "You all right there, [pc.mf |kid |girl ]?" You wipe the blood off your stinging forearms and grimace[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] looking on in concern ]. Nothing too bad, some scrapes on your chin, arms and knees... you've suffered worse. Was that a trap set by the cult? "Don't think so. I've run through my share of these places in my youth... old places get unstable. That, and with all this water around..." She waves a hand. "I've saved my share of friends from these, and lost more. Should've realized it before you stepped there... I'm getting old. You sure you're fine?" Does it change anything? You're not about to backtrack now. "It does. Trust me on that." Yeah, you can go on. All that noise no doubt has alerted every demon in this place to your presence, and you've got to move fast. Once you've [party.hasCompanions |carefully edged [party.compNames true] around the gaping hole in the bridge |checked yourself over and are ready ], you press on, taking care to circle around any more pools of stagnant water on the masonry.
rows.translation: 你小心翼翼地跟在格韦尔的后面，穿过那座古老的石桥。足部下的瓷砖被水和苔藓弄得湿滑不已，不时会踩到一些你之前没有注意到的水坑，溅起水花，惊得一些小生物慌忙躲开。不过，目前看来，还没有任何托卢斯的信徒出现的迹象…… 问题在于，你在寻找这些信徒的过程中，已经投入了太多精力。 周围 你显然没有注意到足部下发生的事情。尽管格温尔行走的速度很慢，但却始终用长矛的柄部敲击着路面，因此当她第一次穿过那座桥时，肯定已经对桥体造成了某种程度的损坏。 当你跟随她的足部步，踏入那些因天花板滴水而形成的小水坑时，足部下会传来令人不寒而栗的嘎吱声和摩擦声——这些声音被周围潮湿的环境所减弱，但却依然清晰可闻。 不过，这对格温尔来说已经足够让他旋转起来了。[party.hasCompanions | 也是为了 [party.som||[comp1.name]|[comp1.name] 以及 [comp2.name]] 向后跳退 ]老狼女伸出了手，而古老的砖块却在你的足部下纷纷碎裂。桥身底部的碎石块纷纷脱落，落入下方暗影的水中，激起巨大的水花；你在地面彻底坍塌之前，才勉强抓住了格韦尔的手。 [pc.hasWings |你拼命地拍打翅膀，希望这能让你在突然开始奔跑的情况下获得一些优势，但其实什么帮助也没有…… | ] 即使格韦尔紧紧抓住你，重力依然会把你向前拉，让你的身体擦过桥上那那些粗糙、锋利的边缘，你的下巴和手臂都会被刮伤。有那么一两秒钟，你会陷入令人心惊胆战的恐惧之中，直到你意识到一切都已经稳定下来……尽管此时你的双腿还悬在下面，下方是危险的深渊。慢慢地，格韦尔将你拉了上来。[party.hasCompanions | 与……一起 [party.compNames true]他的帮助 ]她费力地哼着气，将你拉上来，终于让你重新站在了坚实的地面上。 “你没事吧 [pc.mf |小孩 |女孩 ]你擦去刺痛感从前臂上传来的血液，脸上露出痛苦的表情。[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] 忧心忡忡地注视着 ]也没什么大碍，下巴、手臂和膝盖都擦伤了一点……你经历过更糟糕的情况吧。那是不是那个邪教设下的陷阱？” “我不这么认为。我年轻时经常在这些地方活动……那些老旧的建筑确实很容易发生危险。 就是这个，再加上周围有这么多水……”她挥了挥手，“我好不容易才救出一些朋友，但也有很多人没能幸免。在你走到那里之前，我就应该意识到这一点的……我年纪大了，你确定你没受伤吗？” 这样会有什么不同吗？ 你现在可不能退缩了。 “确实不行。相信我。” 好吧，你继续吧。所有那些噪音肯定已经把这里所有的恶魔都引来了，你必须尽快行动。一旦你 [party.hasCompanions |边缘处理得非常精细 [party.compNames true] 在桥上那个巨大的洞洞周围 |你已经检查了自己的情况，现在准备就绪了。 ]你继续前进，同时注意避开石砌结构上那些积水的区域。
rows.raw: " Carefully, you make your way across the ancient stone bridge, following Gweyr's lead. The tiles underfoot are wet and slick with water and moss, and every now and then you find yourself stepping into a puddle you didn't know was there, kicking up water and sending small creatures scurrying out of your way. There doesn't seem to be any sign of Tollus's cultists yet, though... Thing is, you've put so much of yourself into looking around that you've neglected to pay attention to what's going on underfoot. Even though Gweyr makes a slow yet steady pace, tapping her path with the haft of her spear all the time, she must've weakened the bridge or something when she first passed over it. When you follow in her footsteps, splashing into one of the small pools where water dripping from the ceiling has gathered, an ominous crunching and grinding sounds from underfoot, muffled by the damp and wet all about you. Still, it's enough for Gweyr to whirl around[party.hasCompanions | and for [party.som||[comp1.name]|[comp1.name] and [comp2.name]] to leap back ], the old wolfess' hand outstretched as the ancient bricks crumble beneath your feet. Jagged chunks of masonry break free from the underside of the bridge, falling away into the dark water beneath with large splashes; you only barely manage to close your fingers about Gweyr's before the ground below you gives way. [pc.hasWings |You flap your wings desperately for all the good they're going to do you from a sudden standing start, but better something that nothing... | ] Even with Gweyr holding onto you, gravity still drags you forward against the rough, jagged edges in the newly-made hole in the bridge, scraping at your chin and arms. It's a second or two of heart-pounding and gut-wrenching terror before you've realized that everything's stabilized... even if it's with your legs dangling out over a perilous drop into open water. Slowly, Gweyr pulls you up[party.hasCompanions | with [party.compNames true]'s aid ], grunting with effort as she hauls you up and over the edge onto firm ground once more. "You all right there, [pc.mf |kid |girl ]?" You wipe the blood off your stinging forearms and grimace[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] looking on in concern ]. Nothing too bad, some scrapes on your chin, arms and knees... you've suffered worse. Was that a trap set by the cult? "Don't think so. I've run through my share of these places in my youth... old places get unstable. That, and with all this water around..." She waves a hand. "I've saved my share of friends from these, and lost more. Should've realized it before you stepped there... I'm getting old. You sure you're fine?" Does it change anything? You're not about to backtrack now. "It does. Trust me on that." Yeah, you can go on. All that noise no doubt has alerted every demon in this place to your presence, and you've got to move fast. Once you've [party.hasCompanions |carefully edged [party.compNames true] around the gaping hole in the bridge |checked yourself over and are ready ], you press on, taking care to circle around any more pools of stagnant water on the masonry. "

rows.original:
Now that you've crossed the bridges, the actual entrance to the ancient jotun keep draws into view — and it's been heavily fortified. Would it be that it were a mere palisade, but alas, stone and mortar barricades have been built into the wide, jotun-sized gates, a properly entrenched position with a narrow killzone in front of it. Tollus's cultists have had a good long while to prepare for any kind of intrusion, and your arrival in particular has not gone unnoticed.
    
    "It's [pc.himHer]!"
    
    That's all the warning you get before arrows and firebolts alike sail through the air in arcs, raining down on your position and forcing you out of the gateway. Gweyr drops onto the ground instinctively, then takes cover behind a chunk of fallen rubble while [party.combatNames true] duck around a corner. Someone's designed this killbox very well... and it's your only way in as far as you can tell, unless you're willing to dig through gods know how much rock there is without accidentally breaking out into the open sea and flooding the whole place.
    
    You swallow hard, and consider your options...
rows.translation:
现在你已经穿过了那些障碍，那座古老的巨人之堡的真正入口终于出现在眼前了——而且它被加固得极为严密。本来以为那可能只是一道简单的栅栏，但实际上，那些宽大的、足以容纳巨人的大门上竟然筑起了石墙和砖垒，形成了一个防御工事严密的据点，其前方还设有狭窄的防御区域。托卢斯的信徒们已经有足够的时间来准备应对任何形式的入侵，而你的到来更是没有被他们忽视。

“就是这里了 [pc.himHer]就在这时，你只收到了这一声警告，紧接着，箭矢与火球便划着弧线飞向空中，如倾盆大雨般落在了你的所在位置，迫使你不得不离开那个通道。格温尔本能地跌落在地上，然后迅速躲到了一块倒塌的碎石后面 [party.combatNames true] 拐过那个角落。有人把这个陷阱设计得非常精妙……就你目前所知，这是你进入这里的唯一途径，除非你愿意挖开那些堆积如山的岩石，而不用担心会不小心挖到外面的大海，导致整个地方被水淹没。

你艰难地咽了口唾沫，开始思考自己的选择……

[var0 |Arona snaps into action, the burly orcess pulling her shield out and holding the massive thing up at an angle as she takes point ahead of the party. She's clearly more than eager to get into the action but not so much as to arrive there a pincushion, your thoughts are cut short as she grabs you by the scruff of your neck and pulls you into the cover of her pavise. "Stop fucking around and get in close with me!" Once you're safely pressed against her, Arona [party.som | |angles her shield to cover both Gweyr and you as you advance. It's a tight fit, sandwiched between two burly women, but if you weren't in imminent danger maybe it wouldn't be so bad after all |reaches for [companion2.name] and helps [companion2.himHer] into the cover her shield affords, Gweyr bringing up the back. Wide as it is and with you all in single file, her shield is still barely enough to afford you as much cover as it does, and you hear Gweyr grunt as a barbed arrow nicks her pelt ]. "Gonna be a bit of a squeeze, but better than nothing." As if proving her point, a bolt of magical fire whistles down and lands smack in Arona's shield, the runes carved into hide and wood flaring up but still leaving an ugly scorch mark upon its face. She snarls and roars a curse [pc.ora orc |that would have made your mother blush |in suitably ferocious orcish ], then breaks into a broad-shouldered charge straight for the fortifications, dragging the rest of you in her wake to avoid being exposed to the missile fire coming from the cultists. She doesn't even bother to duck and weave, instead taking the straightest and most direct route into the defenses; a last desperate salvo of arrows and flame manages to singe Arona's arms and legs, painting her green skin with blood and soot. That only enrages her more as she bowls straight into the barricade and shoulders the nearest demon, snarling toothily in genuine orcish battle-rage. "Demons? You aren't worth the fucking after I'm done with you!" Looks like Arona's got her blood up. Bringing up the rear, the lot of you move to back up the orcess as the cultists drop their bows and draw blades and daggers alike. It's a fight! |"Come on!" Brint says, hefting his shield of ice. "I'll lead." With him in his suit of ice armor, you have to admit he's best suited for the task of facing down arrows and fireballs. As Brint takes point, [party.som | |Gweyr and you |Gweyr, [companion2.name] and you ] fall in line behind him, using the column of safety that his massive ice shield creates to advance upon the cultists' position. It's a bit of a squeeze, especially with both Brint and Gweyr having to take cover behind his shield, but maybe being squeezed between two slabs of meat isn't all that bad... Slow but resolute and utterly inexorable, Brint advances upon the fortifications like a mighty glacier, keeping an even pace and his shield raised; barbed arrows and bolts of flame rain down upon his shield and armor with vitriolic hissing aplenty, but it doesn't shatter or melt. His sheer size means that one or two firebolts clip his shoulders from an angle, but ice armor is arguably the best defense against such missiles, and nothing manages to stop his advance despite him not even bothering to take any kind of evasive action and simply absorbing everything with his shield. "You know, you shouldn't overrely on that thing," Gweyr mutters as an arrow clips her shin, whistling through her fur and narrowly avoiding drawing blood. "It's strong, but not infinitely so." "It's strong enough," Brint replies through gritted teeth. With the last handful of steps upon the fortifications, Brint breaks into a sudden sprint, dragging the rest of you along with him lest you be exposed to the cultists' fire. Barrelling straight for the nearest demon who's fumbling to draw a jagged-edged sword, he tackles the cultist, sending the line into disarray while the lot of you back him up, spreading out to take advantage of the chaos. Seeing their defense fail, the remainder of the cultists drop their bows and draw blades and daggers alike, ready to enter the melee. You briefly wonder what she's doing, then realize her intentions as the next salvo of missiles hurtle through the air at her — and are stopped cold by a crackling bubble of runic energy. With her making down the hallway, [party.som | |Gweyr and you |Gweyr, [companion2.name] and you ] fall in line behind Atugia, entering the glimmering blue bubble before it seals entirely. It's a bit of a squeeze given what your dullahan companion can manage, but better some cover than nothing at all. How long can she keep this up for? "Not too long now!" "Then we'd better move fast." Atugia yelps, then settles down when she realizes what Gweyr is about and concentrates on maintaining the runic barrier while Gweyr brings up the fore. Seeing your advance speed towards their position, the demon cultists redouble their efforts; flame and arrowhead alike slam into the shield of runic light, hairline cracks starting to run across its surface as you close the distance. It's just your good fortune, but the exact moment Atugia's shield gives out is the exact moment [silly |Gweyr throws her like a caber into the nearest demon cultist, bowling over their ranks as your dullahan companion lands squarely in his chest |you close the distance, weapons drawn ]; splinters of the magical barrier fall away like a broken window pane before dissolving into nothingness, blinding you for a moment. Breaking into a sprint as the fortifications draw near, you soon close the distance[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] hot in your wake ], and the cultists drop their bows and pull out blades and daggers to meet you in the melee. "Now this is something that's more my style," Gweyr snarls as she slams the haft of her spear into one of the demons' sides. "Up close and personal." It's a fight! |"Shit," Gweyr snarls. "No easy way forward, no easy way back, and they outrange us. I've survived worse... but I'm not as young as I used to be, and luck's carried me enough through my younger years that I don't want push her." Nothing for it, then. "Keep close to the ground!" rows.raw: " Motioning to [party.som |Gweyr |Gweyr and [party.compNames true] |Gweyr, [party.compNames true] ] to spring at a moment's notice, you wait for a lull in the barrage headed your way before giving the signal. [var0 |Arona snaps into action, the burly orcess pulling her shield out and holding the massive thing up at an angle as she takes point ahead of the party. She's clearly more than eager to get into the action but not so much as to arrive there a pincushion, your thoughts are cut short as she grabs you by the scruff of your neck and pulls you into the cover of her pavise. "Stop fucking around and get in close with me!" Once you're safely pressed against her, Arona [party.som | |angles her shield to cover both Gweyr and you as you advance. It's a tight fit, sandwiched between two burly women, but if you weren't in imminent danger maybe it wouldn't be so bad after all |reaches for [companion2.name] and helps [companion2.himHer] into the cover her shield affords, Gweyr bringing up the back. Wide as it is and with you all in single file, her shield is still barely enough to afford you as much cover as it does, and you hear Gweyr grunt as a barbed arrow nicks her pelt ]. "Gonna be a bit of a squeeze, but better than nothing." As if proving her point, a bolt of magical fire whistles down and lands smack in Arona's shield, the runes carved into hide and wood flaring up but still leaving an ugly scorch mark upon its face. She snarls and roars a curse [pc.ora orc |that would have made your mother blush |in suitably ferocious orcish ], then breaks into a broad-shouldered charge straight for the fortifications, dragging the rest of you in her wake to avoid being exposed to the missile fire coming from the cultists. She doesn't even bother to duck and weave, instead taking the straightest and most direct route into the defenses; a last desperate salvo of arrows and flame manages to singe Arona's arms and legs, painting her green skin with blood and soot. That only enrages her more as she bowls straight into the barricade and shoulders the nearest demon, snarling toothily in genuine orcish battle-rage. "Demons? You aren't worth the fucking after I'm done with you!" Looks like Arona's got her blood up. Bringing up the rear, the lot of you move to back up the orcess as the cultists drop their bows and draw blades and daggers alike. It's a fight! |"Come on!" Brint says, hefting his shield of ice. "I'll lead." With him in his suit of ice armor, you have to admit he's best suited for the task of facing down arrows and fireballs. As Brint takes point, [party.som | |Gweyr and you |Gweyr, [companion2.name] and you ] fall in line behind him, using the column of safety that his massive ice shield creates to advance upon the cultists' position. It's a bit of a squeeze, especially with both Brint and Gweyr having to take cover behind his shield, but maybe being squeezed between two slabs of meat isn't all that bad... Slow but resolute and utterly inexorable, Brint advances upon the fortifications like a mighty glacier, keeping an even pace and his shield raised; barbed arrows and bolts of flame rain down upon his shield and armor with vitriolic hissing aplenty, but it doesn't shatter or melt. His sheer size means that one or two firebolts clip his shoulders from an angle, but ice armor is arguably the best defense against such missiles, and nothing manages to stop his advance despite him not even bothering to take any kind of evasive action and simply absorbing everything with his shield. "You know, you shouldn't overrely on that thing," Gweyr mutters as an arrow clips her shin, whistling through her fur and narrowly avoiding drawing blood. "It's strong, but not infinitely so." "It's strong enough," Brint replies through gritted teeth. With the last handful of steps upon the fortifications, Brint breaks into a sudden sprint, dragging the rest of you along with him lest you be exposed to the cultists' fire. Barrelling straight for the nearest demon who's fumbling to draw a jagged-edged sword, he tackles the cultist, sending the line into disarray while the lot of you back him up, spreading out to take advantage of the chaos. Seeing their defense fail, the remainder of the cultists drop their bows and draw blades and daggers alike, ready to enter the melee. It's a fight! |"It's okay," Atugia says, stepping out from the corner. "Behind me!" You briefly wonder what she's doing, then realize her intentions as the next salvo of missiles hurtle through the air at her — and are stopped cold by a crackling bubble of runic energy. With her making down the hallway, [party.som | |Gweyr and you |Gweyr, [companion2.name] and you ] fall in line behind Atugia, entering the glimmering blue bubble before it seals entirely. It's a bit of a squeeze given what your dullahan companion can manage, but better some cover than nothing at all. How long can she keep this up for? "Not too long now!" "Then we'd better move fast." Without another word, Gweyr grabs Atugia by about the waist, lifting her clean off the ground and starting off into a brisk jog. Atugia yelps, then settles down when she realizes what Gweyr is about and concentrates on maintaining the runic barrier while Gweyr brings up the fore. Seeing your advance speed towards their position, the demon cultists redouble their efforts; flame and arrowhead alike slam into the shield of runic light, hairline cracks starting to run across its surface as you close the distance. It's just your good fortune, but the exact moment Atugia's shield gives out is the exact moment [silly |Gweyr throws her like a caber into the nearest demon cultist, bowling over their ranks as your dullahan companion lands squarely in his chest |you close the distance, weapons drawn ]; splinters of the magical barrier fall away like a broken window pane before dissolving into nothingness, blinding you for a moment. Seeing their defense being breached, the remainder of the cultists drop their bows and draw blades and daggers alike, ready to enter the melee. It's a fight! |You don't have time to waste. Taking advantage of the lull in the barrage headed your direction, you take a defensive half-crouch and raise your [pc.offhand] at an angle to meet the next impending salvo. Barely have you steadied yourself before an arrow lands smack into your [pc.offhand], making your forearm jerk from the sharp impact as the barbed head digs into the shield's surface. Yeowch, that looks like it'd have been nasty had it actually managed to find its mark. [party.hasCompanions |Looking around, you shout for [party.compNames true] to get in under the cover of your shield. Once you're sure everyone's as safe as can be given the circumstances |There's nothing for it. Breaking into a brisk, braced walk ], you press ahead resolutely with your shield raised. You've got to close the distance before those bastards can loose more arrows at you, or even worse, strike you dead-on with a firebolt! Not that the demons are slacking any. Seeing you come at them, the cultists loose another salvo, and another — some fall wide, others slam into your shield, and one or two nick your skin, stinging as the barbed heads manage to draw blood. Whatever, better a scrape or two's than being turned into a pincushion[pc.isDK | — but you'll be sure to make them pay dearly for this ]. Breaking into a sprint as the fortifications draw near, you soon close the distance[party.hasCompanions |, [party.compNames true] hot in your wake ], and the cultists drop their bows and pull out blades and daggers to meet you in the melee. "Now this is something that's more my style," Gweyr snarls as she slams the haft of her spear into one of the demons' sides. "Up close and personal." It's a fight! |"Shit," Gweyr snarls. "No easy way forward, no easy way back, and they outrange us. I've survived worse... but I'm not as young as I used to be, and luck's carried me enough through my younger years that I don't want push her." Nothing for it, then. "Keep close to the ground!" [pc.agilityRange 70 |You drop to the old flagstones and turn into a roll, scrambling to your feet in short order, keeping yourself as low as possible. Knowing every moment out in the open hallway counts, you make a mad dash for the barricade, zigzagging as erratically as you can while still making expedient progress towards your goal. Fortunately for [party.compNames], the cultists have figured that you're the biggest threat here and are focusing their fire on you in an attempt to bring you down. Flattering, perhaps, and you definitely don't need to worry that much about anyone besides yourself, but on the other hand there's a lot of pressure on you to stay standing. It's but a few seconds, but those are harrowing seconds indeed. More than once, an arrow comes within inches of burying its cruel, barbed head into your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun], but you're light enough on your feet and blessed with quick enough reflexes to catch yourself in the nick of time and hurl yourself the other way. A firebolt singes your hair and chars your skin, but fortunately doesn't do any real damage even if you feel like your flesh is being seared alive. Several of the barbed heads catch in your [pc.armor] and draw blood, but at least you don't suffer wounds any more serious than a couple of stinging grazes. The cultists were clearly depending too much on quantity instead of quality in their attempt to bring you down, and are paying the price for it. Eventually, you're finally within arm's reach of the barricade, but the fight's not over yet. Drawing your [pc.weapon] with [party.compNames] hot on your heels, you shoulder-check the nearest demon and leap over him with your superior agility. Time slows as you plant your feet squarely on another of the cultist bowmen's chests, sending him sprawling off his post and to the castle's ancient stones with an %"oomph"; alas, neither stay down for long, their demonic constitutions having them up and on their feet in no time. Unperturbed by your flamboyant entrance, the remaining cultists drop their bows and draw wicked-looking blades and daggers, closing in to engage you in melee. |You drop to the old flagstones and turn into a roll, scrambling to your feet in short order, keeping yourself as low as possible. The cultists have been smart enough to clear the approach of debris and any other potential cover, but with retreat being out of the question, it's either move in or wait to be turned into a roasted pincushion, and you're not giving these bastards the satisfaction of the latter. Though you move in as erratic a fashion as possible and zigzag as much as you can, you've simply nowhere near the impressive speed and reflexes someone would need in order to evade the hail of magic and missile alike aimed at you simply by dodging. Fortunately for [party.compNames] — and unfortunately for you — the cultists have figured that you're the biggest threat here and are focusing their fire in an attempt to bring you down. Flattering, perhaps, and you definitely don't need to worry that much about anyone besides yourself, but on the other hand there's a lot of pressure on you to stay standing. While your [pc.armor] saves you from certain death, you're far from unscathed as you finally close the last of the distance to the barricades, [party.compNames] quickly bringing up the rear. "Not today," Gweyr snarls as slams the haft of her spear into one of the demons' sides. "Not today, you bastards." The cultists are prepared for this move, and drop their bows to brandish serrated blades and daggers, moving in to meet you in melee. Their actions are quick and disciplined, and it's clear they've been trained for this. Who supplied the training is a question that's dashed from your mind as the battle begins in earnest. ] It's a fight! ] "

rows.original: There's nothing for it, evaluate your options and charge the fortification.
rows.translation: 别无选择，仔细权衡各种方案，然后全力攻占那座堡垒吧。
rows.raw: "There's nothing for it, evaluate your options and charge the fortification."

rows.original: [var0 |If there's one thing you've learned about Tollus's demons from your experiences with them, it's that they're all incorrigibly horny. Grabbing a vial of wyvern venom from your possessions, you find a lull in the suppressive fire and give it a good toss towards the cultists' entrenched position. It doesn't take long for the tinkle of shattering glass to echo down to you, followed by coughing and a bit of grunting and moaning. While these demons are actually a bit more disciplined than the others you've come across and haven't been outright sent into an orgy by the scent of the aphrodisiac cloud, the lull in the offense is something you can take advantage of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. With the momentum of the encounter turned, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they try to shake off the venom cloud's lingering effects. |If there's one thing you've learned about dug-in foes, it's that smoking them out tends to work. Grabbing a jug of naphtha from your possessions, you stuff a rag into the neck and light it as a wick, then find a lull in the suppressive fire to give it a good toss towards the cultists' entrenched position. It doesn't take long for the crash of shattering ceramic to echo down to you, followed by shouts and the sounds of people attempting to beat out a fire. While the effect's bound to be limited in a place this incorrigibly damp, the lull in the demons' offense is something you can take advantage of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. With the momentum of the encounter turned, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they step away from the flames. |Sure, Tollus's goons may have entrenched themselves pretty well, but you have ideas of your own. Grabbing a leananstone from your possessions, you find a lull in the suppressive fire and give it a good toss into the air, timing it so it'll discharge above the barricade. Even with your eyes averted and ears covered, the flash of light and deafening boom that echoes down from the corridor shakes you to the bone. While these demons have resilience that surpasses that of ordinary people and probably aren't going to be outright disabled by the charged magical trinket, shockwave of storm energies creates a lull in the offense that you waste no time in making good use of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. Rubbing watering eyes and struggling to stand on unsteady legs, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they try to shake off the leananstone's lingering effects. |It's an expenditure of a precious resource, but if not now, then when? Grabbing the ley-crystal grenade from your possessions, you twist the two halves of the orb, feeling something within snap and give way. From there, it's just a matter of finding a lull in the suppressive fire to give it a good toss towards the cultists' entrenched position. Your breath catches in your throat, then the roar of heat and light comes down the corridor to you, punctuated by a scream or two. While the defenses have absorbed most of the blast and now lie in ruins, the demons' firing line has been thrown into disarray by the blast and the lull in the offense is something you can take advantage of. Rallying [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] to your side while Gweyr bursts out from where she's taken cover, all |Gweyr to your side, the two ] of you charge the cultists' entrenched position, weapons drawn. With the momentum of the encounter turned, the demons drop their bows and scramble to join the melee, meeting you in battle even as they struggle to stand and form a defensive line. ] It's a fight!
rows.translation: [var0 |如果说从与托卢斯恶魔们的交手中你学到了什么的话，那就是它们全都无可救药地好色。你从自己的物品中拿出一小瓶双足飞龙毒液，在压制性火力的间隙，将它狠狠扔向那些邪教徒的据点。 不一会儿，玻璃碎裂的声音便传到了你的耳边，紧接着是咳嗽声以及一些哼哼声和呻吟声。虽然这些恶魔实际上比你之前遇到的那些要守纪律一些，没有因为那股催情云的气味而陷入疯狂，但这种进攻的暂时停歇正是你可以利用的机会。 集结 [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] 就在这时，格温尔从她藏身的地方冲了出来，所有人都…… |格韦尔站在你身边，两人一起…… ] 你们向那些盘踞在据点的邪教徒发起了攻击，所有人都拔出了武器。随着战局形势的逆转，那些恶魔也放下了弓箭，纷纷加入近战，他们在试图摆脱毒云的持续影响的同时，也与你们展开了激战。 |如果说关于那些顽固的敌人，你有什么体会的话，那就是把他们引出来通常是个有效的办法。从你的物品中拿出一壶石脑油，把一块布塞进瓶口并点燃它作为导火索，然后趁敌方压制性火力有所减弱的时候，把这个燃烧的容器扔向那些邪教徒的据点。 不一会儿，破碎陶瓷撞击地面发出的声响便传到了你的耳边，紧接着是人们的呼喊声以及试图扑灭大火的声音。虽然在这种潮湿的环境中，这些措施的效果必然会大打折扣，但恶魔的攻击暂时停止了，这正是你可以利用的机会。 集结 [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] 就在这时，格温尔从她藏身的地方冲了出来，所有人都…… |格韦尔站在你身边，两人一起…… ] 你们向那些盘踞在阵地上的邪教徒发起了攻击，所有人都拔出了武器。随着战局形势的逆转，那些恶魔也放下了弓箭，纷纷加入近战，即使他们刚刚才从火焰中逃出来，也立刻加入了战斗。 |当然，Tollus的手下们可能已经把守得非常严密，但你自己也有办法。你从随身携带的物品中拿出一块长石，在压制性火力暂时停歇的瞬间，将它高高抛向空中，确保它能够落在路障的上方。 即使你闭着眼睛、捂着耳朵，从走廊里传来的闪轻型与震耳欲聋的爆炸声依然会让你浑身发抖。这些恶魔的恢复力远超常人，那些带电的魔法饰品很可能无法彻底击败它们，但风暴能量的冲击波确实为你的反击创造了机会，你毫不犹豫地抓住了这个机会。 集结 [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] 就在这时，格温尔从她藏身的地方冲了出来，所有人都…… |格温尔站在你身边，两人一起…… ] 你们冲向那些占据有利位置的邪教徒，拔出了武器。那些恶魔眼中含泪，脚步不稳，但他们还是放下了弓，匆忙加入近战，试图在摆脱那些石块带来的影响的同时与你们展开战斗。 |这是一种对珍贵资源的消耗，但如果不现在行动，那还要等到什么时候呢？从自己的物品中取出那颗能量水晶手雷，你扭动球体的两半，感觉到里面的某个部件突然断裂、松开了。接下来，只需要在敌方密集的火力间隙中，将手雷狠狠扔向那些邪教徒的据点即可。 你的呼吸瞬间变得急促起来，紧接着，一阵由热浪与轻型芒构成的巨响沿着走廊朝你袭来，其间还不时传来一两声尖叫。虽然防御设施已经吸收了大部分冲击力，如今早已沦为废墟，但那些恶魔的攻击线也因为这次爆炸而陷入混乱，这种进攻上的停滞正是你可以利用的机会。 集结 [party.hasCompanions |[party.compNames true] 就在这时，格温尔从她藏身的地方冲了出来，所有人都…… |格韦尔站在你身边，两人一起…… ] 你们向那些盘踞在据点中的邪教徒发起了攻击，所有人都拔出了武器。随着战局形势的逆转，那些恶魔也放下了弓箭，纷纷加入近战，他们在努力站稳脚跟、组成防御阵型的同时，也与你们展开了激战。 ] 这是一场激烈的战斗！

rows.original: You whirl around, expecting more foes to emerge from the shadows and blind corners of the fortifications, but there aren't any more cultists for your [pc.weapon] to meet. Looking at the battlefield laid out before you with broken arrow shafts and scorch marks peppering the masonry walls and floor, you heave a sigh of relief and finally let your guard drop for just a moment to catch your breath. "Impressive," Gweyr mumbles, the old wolfess crouching down to examine the barricade and other defenses. "The entire hallway funnelled us into a killzone that we had no way to avoid taking. If it weren't for the grace of the gods and our own strength... hm. I'm not sure that I could've done much better in my heyday given the circumstances." Is that implying that Tollus has had mercenary training for his goons? "I can't say it was mercenary training for sure, but you saw what they did. The moment they realized that they couldn't win, they disengaged instead of fleeing. A retreat instead of a rout. That doesn't happen with greenhorns you pull in off the street, and it's not something you'd expect from members of a crazy cult. It's professional. Whether this means Tollus has acquired the backing of some kind of state or he's managed to charm someone with actual skill into his ranks, I don't know. What I do know is that it's bad." Well, damn. The demons who fled... they're going to tell their fellows that you're here. "We'd best not give them time to prepare. I'll sweep this position, but we should be ready to move shortly." [party.randComp viviane cait brint brienne arona atugia quintillus kiyoko einin azyrran etheryn |You note a distracted look on Viviane's face, and approach the witch. Is something wrong? "[viv.isDemon|Ah, just quieting some thoughts. During the fight, I started to ask questions of myself that I hadn't in a long time. Years, even. I'm just attempting to figure out what caused them.|I... I'm not sure. During that fight and since, I've just been... thinking, I suppose. Asking questions whose answers I thought I'd found years ago. Questions of purpose, and the like.]" What does she mean? "[viv.isDemon|Well, I spent a lot of time alone over the years. During that, I sometimes found myself wondering if I was making the right choice, doing the right thing with my life, things like that. But I eventually overcame those and other metaphorical demons that plagued me. But something brought those to the surface again. Be on your guard. I may have learned not to listen to the voices in my head years ago, but something tells me the others may not be so fortunate.|I spent a lot of time on my own, just traveling the woods. Time would pass and pass, and I'd find myself asking if I was really doing what I wanted. If I was a researcher and enchantress and the like because I wanted to be or because it's all I'd known. When you go so long in silence that the first time you talk to someone to trade, you feel for those opening moments as if they'd invented speech for the first time, those sorts of questions start to really dig at you. Over the years, I found my answers to them in the joy of discovery and experimentation. But something about this place makes me question again. Despite... what it is. How excited I should be. We're in ancient ruins, and I can't help but ask myself what I'm doing here. Something is wrong with this place.]" |Stepping over to Cait, you give her a light punch on the shoulder. Is she fine? She looks a little downcast. "I-I'm fine. I only took scratches back there." You can see that she doesn't have any real injuries from that scrap. What you're worried about is up there — she looks morose all of a sudden. What's up? Cait squirms a bit, then folds her ears against her head and curls her tail about a leg. "I — I just had a thought. What if all of this was pointless?" What does she mean? "I just... What if we go through all this and don't find anything that'll help me get my sister back? What if I never get Calla back? What if all of this is pointless, and there's really no way to save her? S-she could already be dead, wherever she was sent to, or worse! Oh, Mallach, seeing those twisted people... what they've become. Is that what'll happen to Calla, too? It's been so many days, weeks, since she was dragged through that portal. What if time doesn't work the same way wherever she's gone, and when we do get her back she's a withered old woman? I — " Cait screams, clutching her head and ears; it's not a pretty sound. You grab her by the shoulders and shake her until she stops, but even then tears are still pouring down her cheeks, flowing from her big blue eyes. What's gotten into her all of a sudden? |Just as you're about to join Gweyr in her search, Brint steps over to you, placing a gentle hand on your shoulder. "[pc.name]. C-could I ask you a question?" What's up? He's not the kind to be hesitant. "Y-you're okay with me, aren't you?" What kind of question is that? Of course you're okay with him, you're more than okay with him. You've placed your life in his hands more than once, and are doing so right now. Why... why this question all of a sudden? It's most unlike him. "I left home because wanted to see the world, and now that I've seen the world I've only come to understand what it was I threw away. I know my mom and sis would always take me back if I wanted to go home and stay home... but they'd also take back my dad if he showed up on the doorstep one day. Because they want to... or because they're obligated to?" You study Brint's face; he's clearly not himself, his eyes wide, his expression terrified. And yet, the fear is very, very real. "Remember when we first met, [pc.name]? I didn't know if I'd fit into Hawkethorne, even with you backing me up; all the other places I'd been to outside of the undermountain weren't the same way. Garth smiles at me every morning — but is that because I'm just a paying customer and he has to do it? How do I know he's genuine, [pc.name]? "How do I know?" |Just as you're about to join Gweyr in her search, Brienne steps over to you, placing a gentle hand on your shoulder. "[pc.name]. C-could I ask you a question?" What's up? She's not the kind to be coy about what she wants. "Do you love me?" What's gotten into her all of a sudden? Why this question, here and now? "A-answer me! Do you love me? Sure, you'll fuck all kinds of people, but you won't ever throw me away, will you?" The words are on your lips, but she's not listening. Fingers trembling, her eyes wide and darting from side to side as she [pc.heightRange 80 |clutches |looms over ] you, Brienne shivers from head to toe, and it's not from the cold. "It's okay if I'm not your first, [pc.name]. Or your second. Or your third. But I'll — I'll even be your last, if it means I can be with you forever. Say it, [pc.name]. Say you'll be with me forever!" Brienne! This isn't — "Say it!" Her scream echoes down the halls of the ancient jotun castle, ringing in your ears; the breath rushes from your lungs as she grabs you by the shoulders with sweaty palms and slams you into the wall. Then finally realizing what she's done, Brienne recoils from you in horror, tears welling up in her eyes as she clutches her head. |You look around, checking your surroundings for any traces of Tollus's goons, and find none. What you do discover, though, is Arona staring off down the corridor, her eyes looking as if they're fit to pop free of their sockets, her mouth slightly agape. This isn't Arona. Definitely not when she should be flush with the heat of battle, cooling off after a bout of exhilaration — stepping up, you're just about to ask if she's okay when Arona snaps to you and grabs you by the shoulders. "[pc.name]. I just realized." W-what? Maybe she should calm down a bit. What's gotten into her? "I'm going to grow old someday. I'm going to get old and weak and stupid like my brother did, and... and I won't be able to do anything any more. I won't be able to fight. I won't be able to drink. I won't even be able to get it up — all that I'll be able to do is sit or lie around all day and have some slave feed me gruel water or something while I waste away." She just beat a whole bunch of demons! What's she talking about?! "No, no, you don't see." Her breath whistles through her tusks. "I — I even if I conquer everything. If I beat everything. That means that one day, there won't be anything left to do. I'll have beaten everyone. And that'll be me. Sitting miserable and alone on my throne, an ancient piece of shit who's just waiting for someone with the balls to kick me off. Just like my brother. Oh no, oh no, oh fuck. "I've got to find something worth dying to. Or better yet, dying for before that happens! I can't just sit around waiting for Tira's crows to peck my old bones. I want to go out like an orc! A Kervus!" You watch in horror as Arona raises her [arona.weapon] and turns towards the darkness, ready to charge off alone howling into the void. There's a brief struggle between the both of you, and it's for the best that she's off-kilter — your orcish companion's weapon clatters to the ground she staggers forward, breathing heavily. Before Arona can try to go get herself killed in glorious battle, you kick it out of her reach and thump her hard on the head. |You move to help Gweyr in securing the area, but gradually become aware of a gentle tugging at your [pc.armor]. Half-turning, you find Atugia gazing [pc.heightRange 65 |up |over ] at you, biting her lip. "Hey. You got a second??" Sure. What's gotten into her all of a sudden? "I just... never mind. Gods, this feels just like back then. I just need you to tell me that I'm not a monster, okay?" Sure, she's not a monster. Why should she be? The dogged dullahan looks uncertainly at the walls, the ceiling, anywhere but directly at you. She looks as if she wants to talk, but every time she starts she stops to look around again. Finally she manages to lock eyes with you, but instead of her usual determination you see a shadow of something unlike her. It's personal. But thanks. I needed to hear that." Tui lets out the breath she's been holding, and you notice for the first time that she's been balling her fists all this while. Her knuckles have turned white by the time she relaxes and lets you go. "I mean it when I say thank you. More than you know." |As Gweyr moves to secure the area, you spy Quin staring down the hallway, eyes trained in the direction the cultists fled in; he's breathing heavily and raggedly, gaze not leaving the darkness that lurks in the eaves of the ancient jotun castle. What's up? Worried that they might circle around for a counterattack? "No, no. I just — " given the confident demeanor that Quin tends to project, or at least tries to, seeing him openly rattled is a rare moment of open weakness indeed. "I was just thinking." [pc.isDK |Thinking, huh? Well, he does a lot of that, to be sure, but it's never at the opportune moments where it would be useful. It's at this moment where you'd have expected a cocky or dirty glare from Quin, but none's forthcoming |Penny for his thoughts? Quin demurs ]. "I... shit, [pc.name]. Looking at those dumbasses who ran off... sure, Tollus is an asshole, most of the big shots are assholes... but those were probably just decent people minding their own business until Tollus and his posse came along and swept them up. And even though I'm supposed to have turned my back on them, I still played along with Tollus and his shit for too long, far too long. "I helped him get to where he is today, [pc.name]! Sure, I told myself I was just in it for the sex and the fun, but when it came down to it he's only here because me, and people like me thought the same way for all these years!" Quin makes to grab for your collar, but his hands are so shaky, his movements so uncoordinated that you see it coming a mile away and slap his hands to the side. He looks as if he might make another pass at you, then slumps his shoulders and hangs his head. "It's my fault. I made all this possible. He mightn't have reached the tipping point if not for me and the people and other stuff I helped bring in. We're down here because of me, and I get the feeling that no matter what I do to try and make things right people won't ever forgive me. That damnable pink kitten of yours won't, for one. How many people out there are like her?" Yes, but he himself acknowledged it — you gave him a chance when no one else in Hawkethorne would. Even if no one else believes in his intentions, you do enough in order to actually entrust your life into his hands and to have his back against yours. He's demonstrated as much to your satisfaction. "But that's not the point!" Quin's voice rises to a hysterical, rabbit-like whining scream that echoes down the halls of the ancient jotun castle. "I — if all this shit spreads beyond the Marches, who knows who and what — " You've had enough of this. Drawing back a hand, you give Quin a good hard slap on the cheek, enough to sting but hopefully not enough to cause any actual hurt. Quin just stares at you blankly, dumbfounded in the throes of his hysterics, then shivers and settles down a little. "Fuck." You won't have him putting himself down like this, and more than that, you won't have him dragging not just you, but everyone else who gave him enough credit to try a do-over through the mud. If he wants to stop the thing he helped to set into motion, if he doesn't want Tollus influence to spread to those he actually cares about, then Tollus's ass still needs kicking and he's going to pull himself together in order to do just that. "Fuck," Quin says again, this time a little less morosely. He clenches and unclenches his fists several times, then rubs his cheeks, lingering on the spot where you slapped him. "Shit. I guess... I guess you're right. We still should talk about this once we've dealt with the skinny bastard, though." |You're just about to join Gweyr in looking over the remainder of the fortifications when you hear a choked sob from Kiyoko. Your fox-wife is trying hard to hide it in the usual polite fashion of her people, but either she's getting lax, or the emotion roiling within her is too much for her to keep a lid on. ...What's the matter? "Beloved, have you ever wondered if we're doing [kiyoko.numKits 2 |our kits |Kinu ] justice by being away for so long? I do know what we are doing is necessary to give [kiyoko.numKits 2 |them |her ] a world that's worth growing up in, but... I know you have your qualms and regrets about missing so much of our daughter's early life. One one hand, we want to protect those we love, but at the same time, we know they need to experience life on their own... ah, it is so hard to let go, for a mother who defines herself so much by her children..." ... "Ah, it is so hard to not give in to selfish desires." Look, she raised [kiyoko.numKits 2 |your kits |Kinu ] for ten years in your absence. Whatever she may think of herself or the circumstances surrounding that absence, that's an accomplishment in its own right. If something happens while you're out... Kinu is a grown woman now. She'll be able to handle it on her own. The two of you put what you had and did what you could to raise her in the proper way that you believed she should go, and that's that. Sure, you wish you could be with your family more, but if you don't go through with this there won't be a future for them. And that's what's important — it hurts, of course, oh how it hurts, but someone's got to do it and it may as well be the both of you. Does she understand? |Just as you're about to join Gweyr on her search, you find Einin curled up into a little mousy ball in a corner, hugging her knees and mumbling to herself. She doesn't look too scuffed up from the fight, but there's clearly something up with her. Something the matter? "[pc.name], have I been in the wrong all my life?" What? You understand that she's a thief, that she relishes the joy of the job, the itch of fiddling with things that she shouldn't. So long as she uses her talents for good like she's doing now, it shouldn't be a problem, should it? "But... but all the things I did, I told myself it was because I was in the right, that I needed to support Dad and the others, that they were rich and wouldn't miss it or... or... but then they'd take out their anger at being robbed on those under them, or raise their rents, or... when it comes down to it, [pc.name], how many people have I actually harmed unknowingly?" She can't possibly know that. Why worry about it? And she really needs to take a breath before she passes out from that last run-on sentence. Despite your attempt at humor, Einin isn't buying it. She claps her hands to her cheeks, shaking her head furiously, desperately. "I won't ever be forgiven for it... will I? E-Even if Dad says so... if Mom says so... it won't matter, will it?" Look. You don't know the full tale of what she did before she tried to cut your purse, nor do you ever expect her to tell you every last detail. In the same way, she'll go mad if every single possible smidge of genuine harm she might have done in her past thieving ways tries to haunt her. What she needs to do is to trust in you going forward to do the right thing. You'll make sure of that. |As you go about the cleanup, helping Gweyr search the remnants of the fortifications for anything nasty the demons might have left, you spy Azzy sitting on a sack of sand, chin cupped in her hands. If she doesn't mind, would she help you and Gweyr secure the place? "I..." Azyrran blinks her dark eyes, and her gaze snaps into focus. "Of course." Is something the matter? She looks like she's on the verge of tears right now — this isn't her. "You won't ever leave me, right?" What kind of question is that to be asking, here and now? "Just answer me! You won't ever leave me, won't you?" You've no intention of doing so, especially not here and now. What brought this on? "I... I don't know why. I just started thinking back to before we met, when I was all alone in that garden just south of the bridge. All my life, I'd had Mother, my sisters, even my brothers by my side. And then in a blink of an eye, they weren't themselves anymore. I couldn't save them... "All my life I'd taken their company, their presence for granted; it was only when they weren't around, when I felt alone, that I realized what it was. I didn't even know what it was I was missing because I didn't have any idea that it could be such a thing! I might've, should've given up after all those days, wondering, not knowing, terrified of the faces of my own family — " But she didn't. She pushed on and conquered that fear and came out on the other side stronger for it. "Thanks, [pc.name], but I'm not going to lie to myself. I didn't do it all on my lonesome — I tried, and failed. If not for you coming along, Mother wouldn't have had any chance of being saved. And as much as I was afraid of losing them back then, now I have to worry about losing you, too. There's just so much — so much — " she raises chitin-plated hands to her cheeks and shudders — "I can't help but wonder if it'd been better if I'd never known anyone, that way I don't have to fear being alone because I'd be used to it — " As sternly as you can, you grab the stooped-over Azyrran by the shoulders and shake some sense into her. Does she even know what she's saying? That she was seriously considering giving up the companionship of her mother, sisters and brothers just so that she didn't have to fear their loss? |Feeling the heat of battle leave your blood, you decide to let Gweyr get on with the search and check your surroundings. While you don't find any of Tollus's goons lurking in the shadows, ready to spring out at a moment's notice, what you do find is Ryn looking at her own hands morosely. Ryn? Is something the matter? "[pc.name]... am I fit to rule?" Where did that come from... and what kind of question is that, anyway? Of course she's fit to rule. She stood up to her sister, went all the way down alone to look for help, and finally returned to set things right in the Winter City. Of course she's fit to rule! "But... that's got nothing with actual ruling. In just the short time since Alissa's deposal, I've realized just how little I actually know — you know what Alissa was really keeping me for, as so-called Duchess of the Rim. If I didn't have Elthara to do everything for me, I'd have expended the goodwill of the people long ago." Ryn stares down at her own feet. "I-I don't know, [pc.name]. My grandmother messed up even while she tried to fix things. My parents followed in their footsteps, and Alissa... well, you know. There's so much bad blood in the var Ridells that maybe... maybe it would be better for everyone if I just abdicated and let everything start on a new leaf! Elthara does most of the work, anyway! Look at me, I'm down under the ocean gallivanting away when I should be actually trying to steward what precious little is left of the pale elves! How can I rule when I'm not even in the place to do it? All the peoples of the rift hate us! I-I — " Etheryn's flailing about now in a fit of abject panic that's most unlike her, and doesn't stop until you catch your elven companion and give her a good shake. Look, she's not abdicating anything, either her throne or her responsibilities by being down here with you. Only she can actually face down this threat to her lands and people, so she needs to be here for the Winter City. Does she understand you? Those words coming from her mouth — that's not her, that's the madness talking, and you won't have any of it. |You're about to answer Gweyr when a sudden sensation of cold clamminess comes over you, a feeling like an eel, frog or fish wet against your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun]. Without warning, you find it hard to breathe, doubling over and wheezing, coughing as you splutter and paw at your throat. The air's just so thick that it feels like molasses, that the mere act of drawing breath is an effort; Gweyr immediately notices this and drops what she's doing to rush over and thump you hard on the back and sides. "Breathe, damn it!" In that moment, your throat burns and you feel like your eye are going to pop clean of their sockets, but with a final splutter whatever that was constricting your airway loosens and you heave a tremendous sigh of relief. Air, sweet air... as cold and miserable as it is, it's still welcome. ] "It's this place," Gweyr growls as she grabs you by the arm. "When I was young digging around in the heartlands with Garth, they called it ruin sickness. When people go far down below the earth, away from the sun for hours, days, weeks... their minds start going crazy. No one really knows what causes it. This, though, it's more than that. We haven't been down here for that long, and already..." The demons looked and acted perfectly fine. "Those bastards were already insane, and you know it." You... you can feel it. A whisper on the edge of your hearing, yet you can swear you haven't heard a word. There's something about this place that's getting to you, probing your mind for weaknesses, trying to find a fracture, a fault to wrench open. "We should get a move on. If we stay here too long, who knows what might happen to us even if we win. I've got precious few of my years remaining to me, and I don't intend to spend them cippled with the shakes." You have no idea what the shakes are, but they don't sound like anything you'd want to contract. Yes, time to get a move on before your thoughts can start straying again...

真是令人印象深刻，”格韦尔低声说道。那头老母狼蹲下来仔细检查那些路障和其他防御设施。“整个走廊的设计简直把我们逼入了一个必死的区域，我们根本没有任何办法可以避开它。多亏了诸神的恩典，以及我们自身的力量，才能成功逃脱。嗯……在那种情况下，我不确定自己在巅峰时期能否做得更好。” 这是不是意味着Tollus让他的手部下接受了雇佣兵训练？ “我不能肯定地说确实如此。 雇佣兵 |你注意到薇薇安的脸上带着心不在焉的神情，于是走过去询问那位女巫：“是不是出了什么问题？[viv.isDemon|啊，只是在整理一些思绪。在战斗的过程中，我开始问自己一些很久以来都没有问过的问题——甚至是好几年的时间都没有问过的问题。我只是在试图弄清楚，究竟是什么导致了这些疑问的产生。|我……我不太确定。在那场战斗之后，我一直都在……思考，大概可以这么说吧。我在追问一些问题，而那些答案，我原以为自己早在多年前就已经找到了。关于人生目标之类的问题。]她这话是什么意思？[viv.isDemon|这些年来，我确实花了很多时间独自一人。在那些日子里，我有时会怀疑自己是否做出了正确的选择，是否在正确地度过自己的人生，诸如此类的问题。但最终，我战胜了那些困扰我的念头以及其他各种心理障碍。然而，现在有些事情让它们再次浮上了表面。你们要提高警惕——虽然多年前我就学会了不再听那些内心中的声音，但我有预感，其他人可能就没有那么幸运了。|我花了很多时间独自在森林里漫游。时间一点点流逝，我开始质疑自己是否真的在做自己想做的事情。我是真的想成为一名研究者或一位女巫呢，还是仅仅因为我想成为那样的人，又或者因为那是我一直以来所熟悉的生活方式呢？ 当你长时间保持沉默，直到第一次与他人交谈进行交易时，你会感受到那些最初的对话时刻，仿佛人们是第一次发明了语言一样。这类问题会开始不断地萦绕在你的脑海中。这些年来，我是在探索与尝试的乐趣中找到了这些问题的答案。 但这个地方有些地方让我再次产生了疑问。尽管……原因是什么。究竟为什么呢？ 兴奋不已 我确实是这么想的。我们现在身处古老的废墟之中，我不禁会问自己，自己究竟为什么会来到这里。肯定有什么原因 把卡拉救回来？但如果这一切都是徒劳的，真的没有任何办法救她的话怎么办？她可能已经死了，无论被送到了哪里，甚至可能会遭遇更糟的事情！哦，马拉克，看到那些被扭曲的人们……他们已经变成了那样。卡拉也会变成那样吗？自从她被送进那个传送门之后，已经过去了好多天、好多周了。如果在她去到的那个地方，时间的流逝方式与我们这里不同，那么当我们 做 把她弄回来，她不过是个枯萎的老女人罢了……我——” 你对他应该没有意见才对。你不止一次将自己的生命交到他手部中，现在也是如此。为什么……为什么突然会提出这样的问题？这完全不符合他的性格。 “我离开家是因为想看看这个世界，而现在当我真正看到了这个世界之后，我才意识到自己究竟放弃了什么。 我知道，如果我想回家的话，妈妈和姐姐一定会接我回去……但要是爸爸有一天出现在家门口，她们也会接他回去。是因为她们愿意这么做，还是因为觉得有这个责任呢？ rows.raw: " You whirl around, expecting more foes to emerge from the shadows and blind corners of the fortifications, but there aren't any more cultists for your [pc.weapon] to meet. Looking at the battlefield laid out before you with broken arrow shafts and scorch marks peppering the masonry walls and floor, you heave a sigh of relief and finally let your guard drop for just a moment to catch your breath. "Impressive," Gweyr mumbles, the old wolfess crouching down to examine the barricade and other defenses. "The entire hallway funnelled us into a killzone that we had no way to avoid taking. If it weren't for the grace of the gods and our own strength... hm. I'm not sure that I could've done much better in my heyday given the circumstances." Is that implying that Tollus has had mercenary training for his goons? "I can't say it was mercenary training for sure, but you saw what they did. The moment they realized that they couldn't win, they disengaged instead of fleeing. A retreat instead of a rout. That doesn't happen with greenhorns you pull in off the street, and it's not something you'd expect from members of a crazy cult. It's professional. Whether this means Tollus has acquired the backing of some kind of state or he's managed to charm someone with actual skill into his ranks, I don't know. What I do know is that it's bad." Well, damn. The demons who fled... they're going to tell their fellows that you're here. "We'd best not give them time to prepare. I'll sweep this position, but we should be ready to move shortly." "I've got to find something worth dying to. Or better yet, dying for before that happens! I can't just sit around waiting for Tira's crows to peck my old bones. I want to go out like an orc! A Kervus!" You watch in horror as Arona raises her [arona.weapon] and turns towards the darkness, ready to charge off alone howling into the void. There's a brief struggle between the both of you, and it's for the best that she's off-kilter — your orcish companion's weapon clatters to the ground she staggers forward, breathing heavily. Before Arona can try to go get herself killed in glorious battle, you kick it out of her reach and thump her hard on the head. |You move to help Gweyr in securing the area, but gradually become aware of a gentle tugging at your [pc.armor]. Half-turning, you find Atugia gazing [pc.heightRange 65 |up |over ] at you, biting her lip. "Hey. You got a second??" Sure. What's gotten into her all of a sudden? "I just... never mind. Gods, this feels just like back then. I just need you to tell me that I'm not a monster, okay?" Sure, she's not a monster. Why should she be? The dogged dullahan looks uncertainly at the walls, the ceiling, anywhere but directly at you. She looks as if she wants to talk, but every time she starts she stops to look around again. Finally she manages to lock eyes with you, but instead of her usual determination you see a shadow of something unlike her. It's personal. But thanks. I needed to hear that." Tui lets out the breath she's been holding, and you notice for the first time that she's been balling her fists all this while. Her knuckles have turned white by the time she relaxes and lets you go. "I mean it when I say thank you. More than you know." |As Gweyr moves to secure the area, you spy Quin staring down the hallway, eyes trained in the direction the cultists fled in; he's breathing heavily and raggedly, gaze not leaving the darkness that lurks in the eaves of the ancient jotun castle. What's up? Worried that they might circle around for a counterattack? "No, no. I just — " given the confident demeanor that Quin tends to project, or at least tries to, seeing him openly rattled is a rare moment of open weakness indeed. "I was just thinking." [pc.isDK |Thinking, huh? Well, he does a lot of that, to be sure, but it's never at the opportune moments where it would be useful. It's at this moment where you'd have expected a cocky or dirty glare from Quin, but none's forthcoming |Penny for his thoughts? Quin demurs ]. "I... shit, [pc.name]. Looking at those dumbasses who ran off... sure, Tollus is an asshole, most of the big shots are assholes... but those were probably just decent people minding their own business until Tollus and his posse came along and swept them up. And even though I'm supposed to have turned my back on them, I still played along with Tollus and his shit for too long, far too long. "I helped him get to where he is today, [pc.name]! Sure, I told myself I was just in it for the sex and the fun, but when it came down to it he's only here because me, and people like me thought the same way for all these years!" Quin makes to grab for your collar, but his hands are so shaky, his movements so uncoordinated that you see it coming a mile away and slap his hands to the side. He looks as if he might make another pass at you, then slumps his shoulders and hangs his head. "It's my fault. I made all this possible. He mightn't have reached the tipping point if not for me and the people and other stuff I helped bring in. We're down here because of me, and I get the feeling that no matter what I do to try and make things right people won't ever forgive me. That damnable pink kitten of yours won't, for one. How many people out there are like her?" Yes, but he himself acknowledged it — you gave him a chance when no one else in Hawkethorne would. Even if no one else believes in his intentions, you do enough in order to actually entrust your life into his hands and to have his back against yours. He's demonstrated as much to your satisfaction. "But that's not the point!" Quin's voice rises to a hysterical, rabbit-like whining scream that echoes down the halls of the ancient jotun castle. "I — if all this shit spreads beyond the Marches, who knows who and what — " You've had enough of this. Drawing back a hand, you give Quin a good hard slap on the cheek, enough to sting but hopefully not enough to cause any actual hurt. Quin just stares at you blankly, dumbfounded in the throes of his hysterics, then shivers and settles down a little. "Fuck." You won't have him putting himself down like this, and more than that, you won't have him dragging not just you, but everyone else who gave him enough credit to try a do-over through the mud. If he wants to stop the thing he helped to set into motion, if he doesn't want Tollus influence to spread to those he actually cares about, then Tollus's ass still needs kicking and he's going to pull himself together in order to do just that. "Fuck," Quin says again, this time a little less morosely. He clenches and unclenches his fists several times, then rubs his cheeks, lingering on the spot where you slapped him. "Shit. I guess... I guess you're right. We still should talk about this once we've dealt with the skinny bastard, though." |You're just about to join Gweyr in looking over the remainder of the fortifications when you hear a choked sob from Kiyoko. Your fox-wife is trying hard to hide it in the usual polite fashion of her people, but either she's getting lax, or the emotion roiling within her is too much for her to keep a lid on. ...What's the matter? "Beloved, have you ever wondered if we're doing [kiyoko.numKits 2 |our kits |Kinu ] justice by being away for so long? I do know what we are doing is necessary to give [kiyoko.numKits 2 |them |her ] a world that's worth growing up in, but... I know you have your qualms and regrets about missing so much of our daughter's early life. One one hand, we want to protect those we love, but at the same time, we know they need to experience life on their own... ah, it is so hard to let go, for a mother who defines herself so much by her children..." ... "Ah, it is so hard to not give in to selfish desires." Look, she raised [kiyoko.numKits 2 |your kits |Kinu ] for ten years in your absence. Whatever she may think of herself or the circumstances surrounding that absence, that's an accomplishment in its own right. If something happens while you're out... Kinu is a grown woman now. She'll be able to handle it on her own. The two of you put what you had and did what you could to raise her in the proper way that you believed she should go, and that's that. Sure, you wish you could be with your family more, but if you don't go through with this there won't be a future for them. And that's what's important — it hurts, of course, oh how it hurts, but someone's got to do it and it may as well be the both of you. Does she understand? |Just as you're about to join Gweyr on her search, you find Einin curled up into a little mousy ball in a corner, hugging her knees and mumbling to herself. She doesn't look too scuffed up from the fight, but there's clearly something up with her. Something the matter? "[pc.name], have I been in the wrong all my life?" What? You understand that she's a thief, that she relishes the joy of the job, the itch of fiddling with things that she shouldn't. So long as she uses her talents for good like she's doing now, it shouldn't be a problem, should it? "But... but all the things I did, I told myself it was because I was in the right, that I needed to support Dad and the others, that they were rich and wouldn't miss it or... or... but then they'd take out their anger at being robbed on those under them, or raise their rents, or... when it comes down to it, [pc.name], how many people have I actually harmed unknowingly?" She can't possibly know that. Why worry about it? And she really needs to take a breath before she passes out from that last run-on sentence. Despite your attempt at humor, Einin isn't buying it. She claps her hands to her cheeks, shaking her head furiously, desperately. "I won't ever be forgiven for it... will I? E-Even if Dad says so... if Mom says so... it won't matter, will it?" Look. You don't know the full tale of what she did before she tried to cut your purse, nor do you ever expect her to tell you every last detail. In the same way, she'll go mad if every single possible smidge of genuine harm she might have done in her past thieving ways tries to haunt her. What she needs to do is to trust in you going forward to do the right thing. You'll make sure of that. |As you go about the cleanup, helping Gweyr search the remnants of the fortifications for anything nasty the demons might have left, you spy Azzy sitting on a sack of sand, chin cupped in her hands. If she doesn't mind, would she help you and Gweyr secure the place? "I..." Azyrran blinks her dark eyes, and her gaze snaps into focus. "Of course." Is something the matter? She looks like she's on the verge of tears right now — this isn't her. "You won't ever leave me, right?" What kind of question is that to be asking, here and now? "Just answer me! You won't ever leave me, won't you?" You've no intention of doing so, especially not here and now. What brought this on? "I... I don't know why. I just started thinking back to before we met, when I was all alone in that garden just south of the bridge. All my life, I'd had Mother, my sisters, even my brothers by my side. And then in a blink of an eye, they weren't themselves anymore. I couldn't save them... "All my life I'd taken their company, their presence for granted; it was only when they weren't around, when I felt alone, that I realized what it was. I didn't even know what it was I was missing because I didn't have any idea that it could be such a thing! I might've, should've given up after all those days, wondering, not knowing, terrified of the faces of my own family — " But she didn't. She pushed on and conquered that fear and came out on the other side stronger for it. "Thanks, [pc.name], but I'm not going to lie to myself. I didn't do it all on my lonesome — I tried, and failed. If not for you coming along, Mother wouldn't have had any chance of being saved. And as much as I was afraid of losing them back then, now I have to worry about losing you, too. There's just so much — so much — " she raises chitin-plated hands to her cheeks and shudders — "I can't help but wonder if it'd been better if I'd never known anyone, that way I don't have to fear being alone because I'd be used to it — " As sternly as you can, you grab the stooped-over Azyrran by the shoulders and shake some sense into her. Does she even know what she's saying? That she was seriously considering giving up the companionship of her mother, sisters and brothers just so that she didn't have to fear their loss? |Feeling the heat of battle leave your blood, you decide to let Gweyr get on with the search and check your surroundings. While you don't find any of Tollus's goons lurking in the shadows, ready to spring out at a moment's notice, what you do find is Ryn looking at her own hands morosely. Ryn? Is something the matter? "[pc.name]... am I fit to rule?" Where did that come from... and what kind of question is that, anyway? Of course she's fit to rule. She stood up to her sister, went all the way down alone to look for help, and finally returned to set things right in the Winter City. Of course she's fit to rule! "But... that's got nothing with actual ruling. In just the short time since Alissa's deposal, I've realized just how little I actually know — you know what Alissa was really keeping me for, as so-called Duchess of the Rim. If I didn't have Elthara to do everything for me, I'd have expended the goodwill of the people long ago." Ryn stares down at her own feet. "I-I don't know, [pc.name]. My grandmother messed up even while she tried to fix things. My parents followed in their footsteps, and Alissa... well, you know. There's so much bad blood in the var Ridells that maybe... maybe it would be better for everyone if I just abdicated and let everything start on a new leaf! Elthara does most of the work, anyway! Look at me, I'm down under the ocean gallivanting away when I should be actually trying to steward what precious little is left of the pale elves! How can I rule when I'm not even in the place to do it? All the peoples of the rift hate us! I-I — " Etheryn's flailing about now in a fit of abject panic that's most unlike her, and doesn't stop until you catch your elven companion and give her a good shake. Look, she's not abdicating anything, either her throne or her responsibilities by being down here with you. Only she can actually face down this threat to her lands and people, so she needs to be here for the Winter City. Does she understand you? Those words coming from her mouth — that's not her, that's the madness talking, and you won't have any of it. |You're about to answer Gweyr when a sudden sensation of cold clamminess comes over you, a feeling like an eel, frog or fish wet against your [pc.skinFurScalesNoun]. Without warning, you find it hard to breathe, doubling over and wheezing, coughing as you splutter and paw at your throat. The air's just so thick that it feels like molasses, that the mere act of drawing breath is an effort; Gweyr immediately notices this and drops what she's doing to rush over and thump you hard on the back and sides. "Breathe, damn it!" In that moment, your throat burns and you feel like your eye are going to pop clean of their sockets, but with a final splutter whatever that was constricting your airway loosens and you heave a tremendous sigh of relief. Air, sweet air... as cold and miserable as it is, it's still welcome. ] "It's this place," Gweyr growls as she grabs you by the arm. "When I was young digging around in the heartlands with Garth, they called it ruin sickness. When people go far down below the earth, away from the sun for hours, days, weeks... their minds start going crazy. No one really knows what causes it. This, though, it's more than that. We haven't been down here for that long, and already..." The demons looked and acted perfectly fine. "Those bastards were already insane, and you know it." You... you can feel it. A whisper on the edge of your hearing, yet you can swear you haven't heard a word. There's something about this place that's getting to you, probing your mind for weaknesses, trying to find a fracture, a fault to wrench open. "We should get a move on. If we stay here too long, who knows what might happen to us even if we win. I've got precious few of my years remaining to me, and I don't intend to spend them cippled with the shakes." You have no idea what the shakes are, but they don't sound like anything you'd want to contract. Yes, time to get a move on before your thoughts can start straying again... "

rows.original:
A sharp jolt of magic knocks your [pc.weapon] from your hand, and as you scramble to retrieve it more and more of the demon cultists pile onto you, stabbing away as they drag you down to the cold stone floor. Gweyr manages to hold out a little longer, but without you to back her up the sheer number of cultists soon manages to overwhelm her in much the same fashion.
    
    "We'll be taking you to see the master now," one of them hisses before delivering a sharp blow to the back of your head.
    
    The world goes dark...
rows.translation:
一阵强烈的魔法冲击力将你 [pc.weapon] 它从你手中掉落，而当你拼命试图抢回它时，越来越多的恶魔教徒扑了上来，他们一边刺你，一边将你拖向冰冷的石地面。格温尔勉强坚持了一会儿，但没有了你的支援，庞大的崇拜者人数最终还是让她陷入了同样的困境。

“我们现在要带你去见大师了，”其中一个人嘶声道，随后猛地一击打在了你的后脑勺上。

世界陷入了暗影……
